intro.heading: Four ways the marks go, and what each costs to fix
paragraphs: Almost every Diploma student who needs outside teaching is losing marks in one of four specific ways, and knowing which one changes the price of the solution. The first is command terms: an answer that is factually right but structured for the wrong verb, so an evaluate question collects describe marks. The second is time: a student who knows the content and never reaches the last extended-response question. The third is internal assessment, where a sound investigation loses criterion marks in the write-up. The fourth is foundation, usually algebra.

These are not equally expensive to repair. Command-term work is the cheapest thing in this market, because it is technique rather than content and a handful of marked papers usually move it. Foundation repair is the most expensive, because rebuilding two years of algebra while new Higher Level content keeps arriving takes a term and sometimes two. Internal assessment feedback sits in the middle and has a hard deadline attached. Timing work is cheap but only useful once the content is actually there.

That is why a single hourly rate tells a family almost nothing. The honest question is not what an hour costs but how many hours the named failure needs, and whether the tutor can diagnose which failure it is. A provider quoting one number for every enquiry has not asked. Advertised rates in the Kingdom run from around SAR 35 on budget platforms to SAR 220 on premium Higher Level tracks, and the spread is mostly about scarcity and marking experience rather than quality.

One-to-one is being compared here against a group class and against doing nothing. Against nothing, the argument is simply that these four failures do not resolve on their own: a student who has misread command terms for a year will keep doing it, because nobody has ever shown them the mark scheme. Against a group class, the argument is per useful minute. A group covers content; only one-to-one teaching can sit on one student's own marked paper for forty minutes. That is also the honest limit of the comparison: where the problem really is missing content across a whole topic, a well-taught group class covering it is cheaper and perfectly adequate, and a family should not be sold an hourly rate for something a revision course would fix.

Lessons for Saudi families are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, on Arabia Standard Time. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a Saudi address; home visits are a service we offer only in India. The practical effect on price is worth naming: no travel loading is built into the rate, and the specialist pool is not limited to whoever lives a short drive from the house, which matters most for scarce Higher Level subjects.

1-to-1-ib-tutor.programmesIntro: The programme decides how much of the grade is still movable, which is the first input into whether one-to-one teaching is worth buying at all.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, assessed mainly by written papers in the May session with internally assessed work in nearly every subject. Almost all one-to-one demand sits here, because the papers are external and the technique is coachable.
programmes.countryNote: Higher Level specialists are the scarce resource in the Kingdom, and scarcity is what the rate reflects. A Mathematics Analysis and Approaches or Physics Higher Level request costs more than a Standard Level one in every listing we have seen.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Criterion-marked rather than examined, ending in the Personal Project. Rates sit below Diploma levels because the assessment is internal and the content less specialised, but the value is in building writing technique before it is examined under time.
programmes.countryNote: Families in the Kingdom often treat the final middle-years year as the cheap moment to fix writing structure, which is sound. Repairing the same weakness during the Diploma costs more because it competes with new content.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: No external examinations and descriptive reporting, so there is no grade to move. Useful one-to-one work here is narrow: number fluency, reading stamina, and writing at length in English where it is a second language.
programmes.countryNote: Short sessions at this age are better value than long ones, and advertised primary rates in Riyadh guides sit near the bottom of the range at around SAR 50. Buying a Diploma specialist for a Year 4 student is spending for nothing.

1-to-1-ib-tutor.subjectsIntro: Subjects are priced by scarcity, not by difficulty. These are the ones Saudi families request most, with the failure mode that usually drives the enquiry.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The classic foundation case. Weak algebra from two years earlier surfaces here, and repair takes a term. The scarcest Higher Level specialism in this market.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Marks go in interpretation and written commentary, not calculation. A cheaper repair than Analysis and Approaches, because the failure is technique.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Definitions examined strictly, extended responses wanting linked reasoning. Higher Level specialists are scarce enough to sit at the top of advertised bands.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The internally assessed investigation carries a fixed school deadline, so feedback work is time-boxed and priced as a block.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Mostly a command-term failure dressed as a content failure. Candidates who reread lose marks on evaluate and distinguish.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy decides the lower band, evaluation the upper one. A cheap repair, because both are structural.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: A defensible argument earns more than vocabulary. Second-language students need structure work, which is technique and not expensive.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study papers punish generic answers, and the internally assessed commentary needs a real organisational issue. Both are coachable in weeks.

sections.heading: Command terms: the cheapest failure to fix
paragraphs: A mark scheme does not pay for information. It pays for a structure, and each command term names a different one. Describe wants features. Explain wants a mechanism. Evaluate wants a judgement with weighed evidence and usually an acknowledged limitation. Distinguish wants a comparison on a stated basis, not two paragraphs side by side. A candidate who answers an evaluate question with two accurate descriptions has written nothing false and has still scored in the lower band.

This is the most common reason a strong student brings home disappointing paper marks, and it is also the cheapest thing in this market to repair. The work is mechanical: take marked answers the student has already written, put the published mark scheme beside them, and show where the verb was ignored. Four or five marked pieces usually produce visible movement, which means a fixed technique block rather than an open weekly slot is the honest thing to sell.

It is worth being specific about what the parent should hear in a trial lesson. Hand the tutor a question the student lost marks on and ask what the scheme wanted. A good answer names the command term and the structure, and often points at a phrase in the student's own answer that was almost right. A weak answer re-teaches the topic, which is what the school already did and what the student already knows. Ask for that comparison in writing afterwards, so the student can repeat the exercise without a tutor present.

sections.heading: Timed papers: the failure that looks like weak knowledge
paragraphs: A student who never reaches the final extended-response question loses those marks entirely, and the report card reads as a content problem. It usually is not. The pattern is recognisable: full marks on early short-answer questions, thin answers in the middle, nothing at the end. Marking the paper by question number rather than by total makes it visible in one sitting, and no amount of further content teaching will touch it.

The repair is whole papers under examination conditions, marked, and then walked through. Not questions, papers. Students who practise in ten-minute fragments never build the pacing judgement the examination demands, and a tutor who sets fragments is making the session easier to run rather than more useful. Between attempts there has to be marking time, which is why two shorter sessions a week beat one long one in the final weeks before a series.

Priced honestly, this is a block of six to eight sessions rather than a term. It also has a prerequisite: timing work only pays once the content is actually there. Buying pacing practice for a student with genuine topic gaps produces faster wrong answers. That is why the diagnostic matters more than the start date, and why a provider should be willing to say that this particular student needs content work first, even though it is the slower and less impressive sale. Past papers held in the school's own archive are the cheapest source of material for all of this, and the examinations officer will usually release them on request.

sections.heading: Internal assessment: marks lost in the write-up, not the laboratory
paragraphs: Internally assessed components are marked against published criteria, and the criteria reward things students systematically underestimate. A focused research question scores better than an ambitious one. A clearly stated method with acknowledged limitations scores better than a flawless-sounding account. Evaluation of the data earns more than more data. A sound investigation written up loosely routinely loses several marks that were available to it, and the student never knows which ones.

What a tutor may do here is narrow, and the limit is the point. A tutor can explain what a criterion strand is asking for, question a research design before data collection starts, say that a section does not yet answer the strand it is meant to answer, and teach the writing conventions the component rewards. No tutor writes, completes or rewrites the work. Any provider offering to produce the component is offering academic malpractice, and schools do notice.

The pricing follows the deadline rather than the calendar. Because the school sets a submission date, this is a block of scheduled sessions with a fixed end, usually concentrated in the weeks before the draft is due. The most valuable session is the earliest one, before a research question is locked and before data has been collected around a question that cannot carry the criteria. Families who come late are paying for damage limitation instead. Ask the school for the criteria document before the first session, because it is published, it is short, and most students have never read it.

sections.heading: Foundation gaps: the expensive repair nobody budgets for
paragraphs: Mathematics Analysis and Approaches is where this shows up first, because every topic assumes the algebra of the one before. A student who passed IGCSE by memorising procedures hits Higher Level content and the procedures stop generalising. The same pattern appears in Physics, where algebraic rearrangement is assumed rather than taught, and in Chemistry calculations. The symptom is a student who follows the lesson and cannot start the homework.

This is the slow repair, and the honest conversation at the start is that it takes a term and sometimes two. The tutor is doing two jobs at once: rebuilding the missing foundation and keeping the student afloat in content that keeps arriving weekly. Trying to do only the second produces a term of apparent progress followed by the same wall. Trying to do only the first means falling further behind the class, which no family will accept for long.

Because of that, foundation work is the one case where an open weekly slot is the right purchase rather than a block. Nobody can quote a fixed number of sessions honestly at the start, and a provider who does is guessing. What can be promised is visible intermediate evidence: a list of the specific gaps found, and that list shortening in writing every four weeks. If it is not shortening by the second review, the diagnosis was wrong and the plan should change. Holiday weeks are the best value available for this particular repair, because no new content is arriving from school to compete with it.

sections.heading: What one-to-one costs in the Kingdom, and what moves the number
paragraphs: Advertised rates in Saudi Arabia span roughly six times from bottom to top, and the spread has little to do with quality. At the bottom, budget platforms list IGCSE one-to-one online from around SAR 35 an hour, and general non-specialist online tutoring from around SAR 55. Riyadh tutor-marketplace guides put general primary tuition near SAR 50 and senior-school examination subjects at SAR 200 and above. Tutoring-company listings price IB subject tutoring from around SAR 180.

Higher Level and premium tracks appear at roughly SAR 200 to 220 in those same listings, and some international providers quote in dollars at around $60 an hour. Every figure in the table below is a rate a provider advertises about itself. None of them is a market average, none is a verified price, and none is what IB Gram charges. Our own rate is quoted in riyals before any trial lesson, with the reasons for it stated.

What actually moves the number, in order of weight: subject scarcity first, because a Higher Level Physics or Mathematics Analysis and Approaches specialist is harder to find than a Standard Level one anywhere; then marking or examining experience; then level, where Higher sits above Standard which sits above the middle years and IGCSE; then whether the tutor travels, which adds a loading that online delivery removes; and last, the length of the block committed to. Ask any provider which of those five factors their quote reflects, and roughly in what proportion, because the answer is revealing.

sections.heading: Arriving from another curriculum: pricing the repair
paragraphs: A student joining the Diploma from a Cambridge, CBSE, ICSE or American school is not simply behind. They have been trained to write answers of a different length, for mark schemes with different expectations, often in a subject sequenced differently. The cost of the repair depends almost entirely on which of the four failure modes the switch produces, and that is knowable in one session by comparing two schemes of work side by side.

Skills transfer better than content. A History student brings source technique and needs one prescribed topic rebuilt, which is a block. A Mathematics student whose algebra was taught procedurally brings the expensive problem, because that is foundation work. An American-curriculum student joining Higher Level sciences usually needs depth in two or three topics rather than breadth, plus the internally assessed investigation, which may already be close to its school deadline.

Two practical points save money. Get the receiving school's coordinator to confirm in the first week what internally assessed work can be carried over and what restarts, because a restart changes the whole plan and its cost. And be realistic about level: dropping a subject from Higher to Standard after a late transfer is sometimes the cheapest intervention available, and a tutor who will say so is worth more than one who sells the hours to defend the original choice. Both schemes of work should be requested in writing, because a verbal summary from either school reliably misses topics.

sections.heading: The first month, priced: what four weeks should buy
paragraphs: A free trial lesson should produce a diagnosis, not a quotation. It opens with work the student has already had marked, because real marked answers show in twenty minutes what a purpose-written assessment would not. It should end with a short written finding: which of the four failure modes is dominant, which topics are secure, and whether the recommended shape is an open slot or a fixed block. That document is what the first month is then measured against.

Four weeks of weekly one-to-one is a small number of hours, so what it can honestly buy is limited and specific. For a command-term failure, it should buy measurably better marks on marked written work. For a timing failure, it should buy two or three full papers attempted and marked, with pacing visible in the question-by-question breakdown. For a foundation failure, it should buy a gap list that is shorter than it was. None of those is a grade.

At the end of the month the report should be specific enough to disagree with: what was taught, what the marked work showed, what remains, and what the next four weeks target. If nothing moved, the diagnosis, the focus, the frequency or the tutor changes, and the provider should name which. Recommending more hours without changing anything else is the clearest signal in this market that a provider is selling time rather than teaching. Keep every report, because the second month's argument depends on the first one existing on paper.

faqs.question: How many one-to-one sessions a week can a Diploma student absorb without losing school homework time?
faqs.answer: Two is usually the ceiling during term, across all subjects combined, and one is often enough. A Diploma student already has written work from six subjects plus the core. A third weekly session tends to be paid for by school homework going undone, which costs more than the lesson bought. Density above two sessions makes sense in a holiday block or in the final weeks before a series, not in the middle of a term.

faqs.question: Is a sixty-minute session or a ninety-minute one better value for a timed-paper lesson?
faqs.answer: Ninety minutes, if the paper is being attempted in the session. A full paper plus any discussion will not fit into an hour, and splitting it across two weeks loses the pacing effect the exercise exists for. For command-term work on already-marked answers, sixty minutes is the better buy because attention fades and the material is dense. Match the length to the task rather than booking one length for everything.

faqs.question: Can two Diploma subjects run on the same evening back to back?
faqs.answer: It is possible and rarely a good idea during term. Three hours of concentrated one-to-one after a school day produces a strong first session and a wasted second, and the written work set by both lands in the same week. Where a student genuinely needs two subjects, separating them by two or three days gives the marked work from each somewhere to go. In a holiday block, back-to-back scheduling works far better.

faqs.question: What notice does changing a fixed weekly time need, and why?
faqs.answer: A couple of weeks is reasonable, because a scarce Higher Level specialist's week is built around committed slots and the alternative times may already be held by other students. Single-lesson rescheduling for a school examination or trip is normally straightforward with a few days' notice. Permanent moves are harder in the subjects where specialists are thin, which is also where families least want to lose the tutor they have.

faqs.question: Does a one-to-one slot survive the long summer break, or is it given away?
faqs.answer: It depends what is agreed at the start, so agree it. A paused slot can be held where the tutor expects the student back, and many families use part of the break for foundation work precisely because nothing new is arriving from school. Where a slot is released, getting the same tutor and the same evening back in the autumn term is not guaranteed in scarce subjects. State the intention in writing before the break.

faqs.question: What does a CBSE or ICSE student find hardest about IB internal assessment?
faqs.answer: The open-endedness. A student trained on prescribed practicals and set questions is suddenly asked to choose a research question, justify a method and evaluate their own data against published criteria. The science and the mathematics are usually not the problem. What has to be built is the judgement about scope, because an ambitious question that cannot be answered well scores below a narrow one that can, and that inversion feels wrong at first.

faqs.question: How long does a student moving from a Cambridge school take to stop writing IGCSE-length answers?
faqs.answer: Four to six marked pieces, in most cases. The habit is strong because it was rewarded for two years: compact, complete answers that collect the available marks quickly. Diploma extended responses want development, linked reasoning and evaluation, which takes more length and a different shape. The fix is marking the student's own work against the published scheme until the gap between what they wrote and what was paid for becomes obvious to them.

faqs.question: Which Diploma subjects are the most expensive to repair after a curriculum switch?
faqs.answer: Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, followed by Higher Level Physics. Both assume a foundation taught earlier and taught in a particular order, so a mismatch means rebuilding underneath while new content arrives. History and Geography are cheaper, because the transferable skill is source and case-study technique and only the content needs replacing. Biology is cheapest of the sciences, since its content blocks stand largely alone.

faqs.question: Does a student switching boards mid-year need a different tutor from one who is simply behind?
faqs.answer: Often yes. A student who is behind needs depth in known gaps. A student who has switched needs a comparison first: two schemes of work set against each other to find out what was never taught at all, which is a different and slightly unusual skill. Ask a prospective tutor how they would start with a transfer case. If the answer is a topic test rather than a document comparison, they have not done it before.

faqs.question: Is Standard Level the honest choice after a late transfer into Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth hearing from someone with no reason to sell you hours. Higher Level carries topics with no Standard Level equivalent, so a very late arrival may be trying to learn material taught once, months ago, while keeping up with current content. Where university entry does not require the Higher Level subject, dropping can be the cheapest and calmest intervention available. The school and the coordinator decide what is still possible.

faqs.question: What should a family refuse to pay for in a first one-to-one session?
faqs.answer: A session that produces no written finding. The first hour exists to identify which failure mode is dominant and what shape of work fits it, and that conclusion should arrive on paper. Refuse a quotation given before any marked work has been read, refuse a recommended number of hours attached to no named gap, and refuse any offer to produce assessed work. Also refuse a target grade promised in the first hour.

faqs.question: How is a target set honestly when the student has one marked paper to go on?
faqs.answer: It is not, and a provider should say so. One marked paper gives a position, not a trajectory, and grade boundaries move between series so the mark itself is not fixed in meaning. What can be set honestly after one paper is a process target: the specific error type that should stop appearing within four weeks. Grade targets become defensible once three or four marked pieces exist and a direction is visible.

faqs.question: What does a parent do between one-to-one sessions that actually helps?
faqs.answer: Make sure the set work is attempted before the session rather than during it, and that it arrives with the tutor early enough to be marked. Beyond that, the useful contribution is protecting the slot and the quiet room, and reading the session notes rather than asking the student how it went. Checking the content is the tutor's job, and a parent who starts teaching alongside usually introduces a second method and more confusion.

faqs.question: When is the right moment to stop one-to-one support for a subject?
faqs.answer: When the named failure has stopped appearing in marked work for several weeks and the student can diagnose their own errors. That is the measurable end point, and a provider should raise it before a family does. Stopping is easier after a fixed block than after an open slot, which is one argument for buying technique work as a block. Foundation work usually ends with a reduction in frequency rather than a clean stop.

1-to-1-igcse-tutor.tutorsIntro: The specialists below are matched to a syllabus code and a tier rather than to a subject label, because an Extended Chemistry 0620 candidate sitting Papers 2, 4 and 6 needs a different hour from a Core candidate sitting Papers 1, 3 and 6. Tell us the code and the component list and the match gets much narrower.

intro.heading: Start with the entry sheet, because the entry sheet decides the teaching
paragraphs: Almost every family who searches for a 1-to-1 IGCSE tutor in Saudi Arabia opens with the subject name. Chemistry. Maths. English. The examination board does not work in subject names. What exists on the entry your school submits is a syllabus code, a tier, a numbered component list and a variant digit, and those four facts govern every hour of teaching that follows. A student entered for Chemistry 0620 at Core tier is sitting a different examination from the student beside them entered at Extended, and no amount of good general chemistry teaching changes that. The first useful thing a parent can do, before paying anybody for anything, is ask the school's examinations officer for the entry details in writing.

That request is reasonable and schools answer it. What comes back is short: subject, code, tier, the components the candidate is entered for, and the variant. From that single line you can read the grade ceiling, the number of papers, whether a practical test or a written alternative applies, and which past papers are the right ones to practise. Families who ask for it stop buying the wrong hours. Families who do not ask often discover in the final term that their child has been working through Extended material while entered at Core, or revising a practical test the school never entered them for.

One-to-one teaching is the format that can act on that information. A class of twenty-six moves at the pace of its scheme of work, and a good classroom teacher cannot stop for nine minutes to rebuild one student's understanding of why a titration answer lost two marks for an unrounded intermediate value. A single student in a single session can be taught from their own script: the questions they attempted, the marks they were awarded, the marks the scheme says were available, and the gap between the two. That is the whole argument for the format, and it only works if the person teaching reads mark schemes for a living.

Which brings the question back to the tutor. At IGCSE level the credential that predicts a result is not a degree in the subject, and it is not a general teaching qualification either, useful as both are. It is demonstrable familiarity with the specification the candidate is entered against: the assessment objectives the marks are grouped under, the command terms the questions are built from, and the published mark scheme's habit of paying for precise phrases a textbook never uses. Those things are checkable in one hour by a parent who does not know the subject, and the sections below set out exactly how.

Delivery for Saudi families is online. Lessons run over live video, one to one, scheduled against Arabia Standard Time and the Sunday-to-Thursday school week. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a Saudi address; in-home visiting is a service offered only in India. The practical consequence for a family in Riyadh, Jubail or Jazan is that the pool is no longer whoever lives within a thirty-minute drive. An Extended Physics 0625 specialist who marks for a board can teach a student in Najran on a Tuesday evening, which is not a thing the local market can arrange at any price.

The component numbers tell you which past papers are the right ones to practise

1-to-1-igcse-tutor.programmesIntro: Four stages sit around an IGCSE year in the Kingdom: the course the student is on, the alternative board a different school would have entered them for, the programme they came from, and the post-16 route the grades feed into. One-to-one support is bought at different points for very different reasons.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Single-subject courses, each with its own four-digit syllabus code and numbered component list. Many subjects run a Core and an Extended route with separate papers, separate content and separate grade ranges. The sciences add either a practical test or a written alternative to practical. A small number of subjects retain a coursework component that the school marks and Cambridge moderates.
programmes.countryNote: The most widely entered international route in the Kingdom, because it needs fewer specialist staff than a full Diploma and can be sat through an examination centre. That also makes it the route where tier and component decisions are most often taken quietly inside a department, which is why the written entry line matters so much here.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Graded on the 9 to 1 scale rather than A* to G, with Foundation and Higher tiers on the subjects that tier. Mathematics A 4MA1 is examined through two papers, both with a calculator, which changes preparation considerably against a board that includes a non-calculator component. Specification codes rather than syllabus codes identify the course.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools in the Kingdom enter candidates with Pearson while their neighbours enter with Cambridge, and some departments split by subject within one school. A family relocating between cities can find the board changes under them mid-course, which is one of the commonest reasons an outside specialist is brought in.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: A framework rather than a syllabus, assessed against published criteria strands rather than terminal written papers, and finishing with a Personal Project that the student designs and the school assesses. Students arriving from it into an IGCSE year are usually strong at structuring an extended response and unused to the compression a timed paper demands.
programmes.countryNote: Schools in the Kingdom that run the Diploma Programme frequently run the Middle Years Programme below it, so a student may move from criterion-based assessment straight into a numbered component list. The adjustment is almost entirely about examination technique rather than content, and it is short work in one-to-one sessions.

programmes.name: A Level and the IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The two routes an IGCSE record usually feeds into. A Level departments treat specific IGCSE grades as entry conditions for their own courses; Diploma Programme departments use them to argue Higher Level against Standard Level. Both treat Extended-tier mathematics and the separate sciences as assumed knowledge rather than something to revisit.
programmes.countryNote: Whichever route follows, the final secondary certificate is the document a Saudi university equivalency decision is taken on, not the individual IGCSE statement of results. Families planning towards a Saudi institution should read the receiving university's own published criteria rather than a third-party summary.

1-to-1-igcse-tutor.subjectsIntro: The subjects below are the ones Saudi families most often source from outside the school, with the code and the tier written out because those are what a match is actually made against. A request for help with maths is not specific enough to staff; a request for Extended 0580 Paper 2 technique is.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580)
subjects.description: The current structure pairs a non-calculator paper with a calculator paper at each tier, and Cambridge has revised that component list, so confirm it against the syllabus your child is entered for. Marks go on unshown method, on premature rounding inside multi-step work, and on algebraic rearrangement attempted mentally.

subjects.name: Mathematics A (Pearson Edexcel 4MA1)
subjects.description: Two papers, both with a calculator, graded 9 to 1. The absence of a non-calculator component shifts preparation towards efficient calculator use and away from arithmetic fluency, which catches out students transferring in from a board that examines both separately.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.description: Calculus, series, vectors and trigonometric identities at a level most IGCSE students have not met. Schools in the Kingdom offer it unevenly because it needs a teacher comfortable above the standard syllabus, so it is one of the subjects most often taught entirely from outside the school.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625)
subjects.description: Loses marks on the suggest and explain questions rather than on recall. A student who can state Newton's second law routinely drops the marks for applying it to an unfamiliar arrangement, because the mark scheme pays for a stated relationship and a direction, not for a correct number alone.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620)
subjects.description: Equation marks are the quietest loss in the whole subject: balanced symbols, state symbols where the question asks for them, and a formula written out rather than described. The alternative-to-practical paper examines experimental reasoning on paper, which is a separate skill from doing the experiment.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610)
subjects.description: The subject where definitions are examined most strictly. Transport, respiration and inheritance questions are marked against specific terms, and a paraphrase that a teacher would accept in class earns nothing. The longer questions reward sequencing a process rather than listing facts about it.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated and Combined Sciences (Cambridge 0654 and 0653)
subjects.description: Three sciences compressed into a double or single award. Content is thinner per discipline but the papers still move between biology, chemistry and physics inside one question paper, so a candidate carries three sets of conventions at once. Weak students often need one discipline rebuilt, not all three.

subjects.name: First Language English (Cambridge 0500)
subjects.description: Reading is assessed separately from directed writing and composition, and the two components fail for opposite reasons. Reading marks go on selecting and recasting evidence; writing marks go on register, control of sentence variety and finishing within the time rather than on vocabulary.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 and 0511)
subjects.description: A separate course from First Language English, with its own listening and speaking arrangements and a different idea of what good writing is. Students placed in it who should be in 0500, and the reverse, is a frequent and expensive misplacement that one diagnostic session usually identifies.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455) and Business Studies (Cambridge 0450)
subjects.description: Both fail on data response rather than on theory. A candidate who can define elasticity loses the marks for reading a figure off a table and explaining what it implies for the firm in the stem. Diagram labelling and the use of the case material carry more marks than most students assume.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478)
subjects.description: Theory papers reward precise terminology about data representation, networks and logic, while the programming element rewards legible pseudocode and documented design. Students who code well informally often write algorithms the mark scheme cannot credit because the structure is not visible.

subjects.name: Geography (0460) and History (0470)
subjects.description: Both examine source and case-study handling as a skill in its own right. History candidates lose marks by narrating rather than answering the question asked; geography candidates lose them on command terms inside the longer questions and on describing a pattern without quoting figures from the resource.

1-to-1-igcse-tutor.regionsTitle: Where one-to-one teaching changes the answer, city by city
1-to-1-igcse-tutor.regionsIntro: Distance is the real constraint across most of the Kingdom, and it bites differently in each city. Below is what the local staffing picture tends to look like and what a one-to-one online arrangement actually solves there, rather than a list of districts.

regions.name: Riyadh
regions.note: The widest choice of Cambridge and Pearson provision anywhere in the Kingdom, and roughly an hour of traffic from the north of the city to the south. Even here, Additional Mathematics 0606 and the separate sciences are the hardest classes to staff, so families source them from outside more often than any other subjects.

regions.name: Jeddah
regions.note: Provision runs along a long coastal spine from the historic centre north towards Obhur. The binding constraint is the school run rather than the tutor pool: a session that depends on a parent finishing a cross-city drive first is a session that gets moved twice a term. A fixed online slot removes that variable entirely.

regions.name: Dammam, Al Khobar and Dhahran
regions.note: One labour and school market behaving as three cities, with families routinely living in one and attending school in another. Board allegiance varies by campus, so siblings can sit Cambridge and Pearson versions of the same subject. Matching by specification code rather than subject name matters more here than almost anywhere.

regions.name: Jubail and Ras Tanura
regions.note: Industrial and camp communities where the school is small and the senior-school department smaller. A subject may be taught by a capable non-specialist because there is nobody else, and the family finds out when mock marks arrive. One-to-one teaching is usually bought to cover one named component, not a whole course.

regions.name: Al Ahsa and Qatif
regions.note: Roughly an hour and a half inland from the Eastern Province cluster, and the commute is what rules out a visiting arrangement for most families. Students here are commonly entered through examination centres rather than through a large international department, which makes the written entry line even more important.

regions.name: Madinah, Makkah and Taif
regions.note: Smaller international cohorts than the three big markets, with Cambridge entries more common than Diploma Programme ones. Specialist cover for Extended sciences is thin, and families often need a tutor who can teach the full Extended content rather than top up a taught course.

regions.name: Tabuk, NEOM and AlUla
regions.note: Fast-growing communities in the north-west where the schooling picture is still forming and mid-course arrivals are common. A student joining an IGCSE year part-way through needs the gap between two specifications mapped before teaching starts, which is diagnostic work rather than revision.

regions.name: Abha, Khamis Mushait and Jazan
regions.note: The southern cities, where Abha and Khamis Mushait sit about 25km apart and share a catchment. Distance makes a visiting specialist impractical for most subjects, so the honest comparison for a family here is between a local generalist and an online specialist, not between online and in-home.

regions.name: Buraidah, Ha'il and Najran
regions.note: Regional centres with small international cohorts and very few candidates per subject. A student may be the only one in their year taking Additional Mathematics or Computer Science, which means there is no class to join and no departmental past-paper practice to inherit. One-to-one is the only format available.

schoolClusters.note: The central region carries the widest mix of Cambridge, Pearson and IB provision in the Kingdom, with several long-established international schools alongside newer bilingual campuses. Students we support attend schools including those named here; they are listed as ecosystem context only.

schoolClusters.city: Jeddah, Thuwal and the western region
schoolClusters.note: Cambridge and IB provision both long established, with international schools serving expatriate communities along the coast and The KAUST School on the research campus at Thuwal, north of the city. Named here as context, with no affiliation implied.

The International Schools Group operates several campuses across the conurbation and at Jubail, with the Diploma Programme offered at some but not all of them. British and Cambridge provision sits alongside, which is why families here compare boards rather than schools.

1-to-1-igcse-tutor.modesIntro: One-to-one is a format, not a single product. The four arrangements below differ in what they are for, and buying the wrong one is the commonest way families waste money on IGCSE support. Each is delivered online, over live video, on Arabia Standard Time.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one on one named component
modes.description: A fixed slot aimed at a single component rather than a whole subject. The session is built from the student's last attempt at that paper type: what was attempted, what was awarded, what the scheme had available. Most families start here because it is the arrangement that produces evidence quickly and can be stopped without wasting a package.
bullets: One subject, one tier, one component number
Built from the student's own marked work, not a generic scheme
A written note after each session saying what moved and what did not
Stoppable at any point without an unused balance

modes.title: Diagnostic block for a mid-course arrival
modes.description: For a student joining an IGCSE year part-way through, or moving between boards. The first sessions map the gap between the specification already covered and the one they are now entered against, component by component, before any teaching is planned. Families relocating into Tabuk, NEOM or Riyadh mid-year use this most.
bullets: Specification-against-specification comparison, written down
Identifies topics taught on the old board and not the new one
Separates content gaps from technique gaps
Produces an hour estimate before a package is agreed

modes.title: Technique clinic before a series
modes.description: A short, dense block in the weeks before the papers, aimed entirely at how marks are collected rather than at content. Sessions work through timed questions under examination conditions, then read the mark scheme line by line against what the student wrote. It suits a candidate who knows the material and keeps scoring below their understanding.
bullets: Command terms, assessment objectives and mark-scheme phrasing
Timed attempts marked against the published scheme
Variant-correct past papers rather than whatever is online
A shortlist of repeat errors, tracked across attempts

modes.title: Coursework and practical-paper feedback
modes.description: For subjects that still carry a school-marked component, and for the alternative-to-practical papers. A tutor reads the student's own draft and gives feedback against the published criteria. The writing, the data and the decisions remain the student's throughout, and the school's own supervision arrangement stays in charge.
bullets: Feedback on the student's own draft, in writing
Criteria-referenced comment rather than correction
Nothing drafted, dictated or supplied by the tutor
Experimental reasoning practised for the written alternative

sections.heading: An IGCSE entry is a code, a tier, a component list and a variant digit
paragraphs: The examination entry your school submits does not say Chemistry. It says 0620, a tier, a set of component numbers and a variant. Those four facts decide the grade ceiling, the number of papers, whether a laboratory practical or a written alternative applies, and which past papers are the correct ones to practise. A parent who has that line in writing can buy teaching precisely. A parent who does not is buying a subject name and hoping the rest lines up, which it frequently does not.

The code identifies the syllabus and its version. Cambridge revises syllabuses and the component list moves when it does, which is why a past paper downloaded from a search result can belong to a structure your child is not sitting. The tier is the consequential part: on Cambridge-tiered subjects a Core entry is graded C to G and an Extended entry A* to E, so a Core candidate cannot be awarded above a C however well the papers go. Tier entry is a school decision and it is reversible, but only before the entry deadline.

The variant digit is the part almost nobody explains. Cambridge runs the same syllabus in several time zones and sets different papers for each, so a candidate in the Kingdom sits a different question paper from a candidate in the United Kingdom or in East Asia on the same syllabus. Practising the wrong variant is not fatal, but it misleads a student about question style and about how a topic tends to be examined. A tutor who asks for the variant before the first session has told you something useful about how they work.

table.caption: COMPONENT NUMBERING ON A CAMBRIDGE SCIENCE ENTRY
rows: Secure recall and elimination under time pressure
Recall plus application to unfamiliar stems
Short written answers using exact subject terms
Extended explanation, calculation and data handling
Practical test, sat in a laboratory
Candidates at schools entering the practical route

sections.heading: What one-to-one changes, question by question
paragraphs: The case for one-to-one teaching at IGCSE is narrow and strong: it is the only format that can be run from a single student's marked script. A classroom teacher with twenty-six candidates teaches the scheme of work and marks to it. That is the right job for a class. It cannot stop for nine minutes while one student is taken back through why a correct final answer earned two marks out of four because the intermediate working never reached the page.

In practice a good session looks like forensic work rather than teaching. The student brings a recent attempt, marked. The tutor has the published mark scheme open beside it. They go line by line: this answer earned the mark, this one did not, here is the phrase the scheme wanted and here is what you wrote. By the third or fourth question a pattern appears, and the pattern is almost never a content gap. It is a habit, and habits are fixable in a way that a year of missing content is not.

That approach also produces something a parent can read. After two or three sessions there should be a short written list: the repeat errors, in order of how many marks they cost, with evidence from the scripts. If a tutor cannot produce that list, they are teaching the subject rather than the student, and the premium a one-to-one arrangement carries over a group class is not being earned. A family is entitled to ask for it before agreeing a longer package.
bullets: Bring marked work to the first session, not a textbook
Expect the mark scheme open on screen beside the student's answer
Expect a written list of repeat errors ranked by marks lost
A content gap and a technique habit need different numbers of hours

sections.heading: Assessment objectives: the weighting inside the paper nobody reads
paragraphs: Every Cambridge and Pearson specification groups its marks under assessment objectives, and publishes a table showing how the marks divide between them. Most syllabuses use some version of the same split: one objective for recall and understanding, one for applying that understanding to material the candidate has not seen, and in the sciences a third for experimental skills. The exact weightings differ by subject and by syllabus version, so the only sensible instruction is to read the table in the specification your child is entered for.

The reason this matters is that revision almost always targets the first objective and almost never targets the second. A student rereads notes, which builds recall. The paper then hands them an unfamiliar context and asks them to apply what they know to it, and recall alone does not reach the mark. This is the mechanism behind the most frustrating conversation in IGCSE teaching, the one where a parent says their child clearly knows the subject and the marks say otherwise. Both statements are usually true.

A tutor who works from assessment objectives teaches differently. Instead of covering a topic, they take an unfamiliar stem on a familiar topic and make the student do the transfer out loud, repeatedly, until it stops feeling like a trick. Ask a prospective tutor which assessment objective your child is losing marks against. A specialist will answer with a distinction and an example. A generalist will answer about the topic, which tells you what you need to know.

table.caption: WHAT EACH KIND OF OBJECTIVE ASKS FOR
rows: Describes around the term without using it
The exact published term, nothing more
A context the student has never met, then explain or suggest
Recites the topic as taught in class
The named principle applied to this stem
A table, graph or source, then describe or calculate
Gives a trend with no figures quoted
Figures lifted from the resource, with units
Discuss, evaluate, justify, to what extent
A weighed judgement that answers the question asked
Plan, improve, identify a source of error
Says be more careful or use better equipment
A named variable, a named control, a measurable change

sections.heading: Command terms are the whole difference between knowing and scoring
paragraphs: The first word of an IGCSE question is an instruction, and it is costed. Describe and explain are not interchangeable; state and suggest want answers of different kinds; compare requires a stated point of comparison in the same sentence as both items. Candidates lose marks on questions they could answer because they answered a different instruction from the one printed. This is not carelessness, and telling a teenager to read the question more carefully does not fix it, because the problem is that they do not know what each term is asking for.

The repair is mechanical and quick. A student is given a set of questions on content they already know, with the command terms varied, and made to write the opening clause of each answer only. No full answers. Just the first eight words, which is where the command term is either obeyed or ignored. Done for twenty minutes a week over a term, this closes a gap worth several marks a paper in the sciences, in geography and in business studies, and does it without covering any new content at all.

It is also a reasonable thing to ask a prospective tutor to demonstrate. Hand them a past-paper question and ask what the command term rules out. A tutor who reads mark schemes will tell you what the examiner will not accept, which is the useful half of the answer. A tutor who has only taught the content will explain the topic instead. Both responses are honest; only one of them is worth a one-to-one premium.

table.caption: COMMAND TERM, MARK SCHEME, AND THE ANSWER CANDIDATES ACTUALLY WRITE

sections.heading: Ask for artefacts, not answers: checking a tutor in one hour
paragraphs: A parent who does not know chemistry can still tell a specialist from a competent generalist, because the test is not subject knowledge. It is whether the person can produce documentary evidence of how they work. Interview questions are easy to prepare for and tell you almost nothing. Artefacts are harder to fake and much more revealing, and a tutor who works the way this page describes will have them to hand without preparing anything.

Ask for three things before the trial lesson. First, a past-paper answer the tutor has marked themselves, showing where each mark was awarded and where one was withheld. Second, a page of the relevant specification with their own working annotations on it, which shows whether they read specifications at all. Third, a line from a published mark scheme they consider badly worded, with their reason. The third request is the sharpest, because only somebody who reads schemes closely has an opinion about one.

What a weak response looks like is also predictable. A list of universities attended. A number of years taught. An offer of testimonials. None of these is dishonest and none of them evidences specification knowledge. Nobody can verify an unverifiable results claim, so stop trying and ask for the artefacts instead. Then use the trial lesson for the only question a parent can answer directly: did the session work from my child's own marked script, and did it end with something written down?

sections.heading: The honesty line in a room nobody else can see
paragraphs: One-to-one teaching is the arrangement with the highest risk of crossing into malpractice, and saying so plainly is more useful than pretending otherwise. In a classroom there are witnesses. In a private session there is a tutor, a student and a piece of assessed work, and the pressure to be helpful is considerable. Several providers competing for these searches resolve that pressure by producing the work. That is academic misconduct under board rules, the penalty falls on the student and not on the provider, and it can remove a subject grade or a whole certificate.

The line itself is not complicated. A tutor may teach the content, explain the criteria, work through a comparable example that is not the assessed task, read a draft the student has written and give feedback on it in writing. A tutor may not supply sentences for the student to use, dictate structure paragraph by paragraph, provide data the student did not gather, or correct a draft to the point where the improvement belongs to the tutor. The work, the decisions and the mistakes stay with the candidate.

What a family should do is keep a record. Dated session notes, the feedback given in writing, the student's drafts in sequence. If a school ever asks how a piece of work developed, that record answers the question in a way that nobody's assurance can. Schools in the Kingdom run their own malpractice processes and the board has its own; a family that can show the trail is in a strong position, and a family that cannot is relying on being believed.
bullets: Feedback in writing on the student's own draft, kept and dated
No sentences, structures or data supplied by the tutor
Comparable practice tasks, never the assessed task itself
The school's own supervision arrangement stays in charge throughout

sections.heading: What one-to-one IGCSE teaching costs in this market, and what the hour contains
paragraphs: Rates in the Kingdom are advertised rather than published, which is a meaningful distinction. The figures below are what vendors and tutor marketplaces put on their own pages. They are not a market average, they are not audited, and they are not what IB Gram charges. Read them as the shape of the market a family is negotiating inside, and expect the number you are actually quoted to depend on things the advertisement does not mention.

What moves the figure, roughly in order of weight: subject scarcity first, because an Extended Physics or Additional Mathematics specialist is harder to find than a Core Mathematics one everywhere in the world; then marking or examining experience; then level, where Higher Level work sits above Standard Level, which sits above IGCSE; then whether the tutor travels, which loads the price with time that is not teaching; and finally package length. A rate at the top of a band is not evidence of quality. It is evidence of scarcity, examining experience, or confident marketing, and only the first two are worth paying for.

The more useful question is what the hour contains. An hour that includes marked work returned before the session, a mark scheme open on screen, and a written note afterwards is a different product from an hour of explanation, even at the same price. Ask what happens between sessions and ask who marks the written work. Those two answers separate the market more reliably than the rate does.

sections.heading: Sunday to Thursday, and where a weekly one-to-one hour actually fits
paragraphs: The school week in the Kingdom runs Sunday to Thursday, with Friday and Saturday as the weekend. Rival pages written for other markets inherit a Monday-to-Friday assumption and quietly get this wrong, which matters because it changes which evenings are usable. Sunday carries the weight of the week restarting and is the worst evening for demanding technique work. Wednesday and Thursday evenings sit against a weekend, which makes them the best slots for sessions that set written work.

Arabia Standard Time is UTC+3 and the Kingdom does not change its clocks. A tutor in a country that does will drift by an hour twice a year unless the slot is pinned to Saudi local time rather than to theirs. Pin it to Saudi local time in writing at the start and the problem never arises. The arithmetic also decides which tutors can realistically hold a slot: a six o'clock Saudi evening is a comfortable working hour in the United Kingdom and a late one in India, and that difference shows up in reliability over a full term rather than in the first fortnight.

During Ramadan school days shorten and household routines move later, so the sensible approach is to agree a different weekly slot for that period in advance rather than cancelling and losing it. Long summer and midyear breaks are worth treating the same way. A paused slot with an agreed restart date survives; an abandoned one gets filled. Families whose schools run three terms should also check their own school's published calendar, because international and British-curriculum schools in the same city often break on different weeks.

rows: Comfortable everywhere; usually taken by younger students
Workable for both; the most contested slot of the week
Easy from the United Kingdom, an evening shift in India

sections.heading: The series, counted backwards, and what a one-to-one plan looks like at each distance
paragraphs: Cambridge and Pearson both run a June series, which is the main one for schools in the Kingdom, and a November series used for resits and for November-entry candidates. Cambridge also operates a February and March series, but that series is an India-only entry and a Saudi candidate cannot sit it, so any advice built on it is advice for a different country. Entries close several months ahead of the June papers and the exact date belongs to your school's examinations officer, not to a web page.

Counted backwards, the year has four useful distances. More than two terms out is the window where content can still be built and a tier decision can still be argued with evidence. Two terms out is where the tier conversation has to be had, because after the entry deadline the ceiling is fixed. One term out is technique: command terms, assessment objectives, timed attempts, variant-correct papers. The last few weeks are for repeat errors only, and starting new content there does more harm than good.

The resit decision comes after results and it is a cost question as much as an academic one. A November entry needs enough notice to enter, and a student repeating a component with no change in how they prepare tends to repeat the mark as well. If the diagnosis from the summer papers was technique rather than content, a short, dense block aimed at the specific component is usually the better use of money than retaking the whole course. If it was content, be honest about how many hours that actually takes.
bullets: More than two terms out: content, and the tier argument while it is still open
Two terms out: the entry decision, in writing, with the examinations officer
One term out: command terms, timed papers, variant-correct practice
The last weeks: repeat errors only, no new content

sections.heading: After the certificate: equivalency, the Qiyas tests and the two routes out
paragraphs: An IGCSE statement of results is not the document a Saudi university makes an equivalency decision on. Equivalency, or mu'adalah, is a Ministry of Education decision taken on the final secondary certificate, and it applies in the same way to an IB Diploma, to A Levels and to an American high school diploma. IGCSE grades sit underneath that as the entry conditions a post-16 department uses, and as evidence a school reads when arguing Higher Level against Standard Level. Families should read the Ministry's own published requirements rather than a summary.

Alongside equivalency sit the Qiyas tests, run by the National Center for Assessment under the Education and Training Evaluation Commission. Qudurat, the General Aptitude Test, examines verbal and quantitative reasoning rather than syllabus content and can be sat in Arabic or in English. Tahsili, the Achievement Test, covers the science-stream subjects, and its content follows the Saudi national curriculum. That last point is the one worth telling an international-curriculum family, because the overlap with an IGCSE or Diploma course is partial and the framing is different, which is why strong students are sometimes surprised by it.

No page should publish a threshold or a weighting formula for either test, because universities set their own and they differ by institution and by programme. Competitive engineering, medicine and science programmes lean hardest on Tahsili. Some institutions also state a maximum age for the secondary certificate they will accept. The practical advice is narrow and reliable: read the receiving university's own published admission criteria, and start reading them a long time before the application, not during it.

process.title: Send the entry line
process.description: Subject, syllabus or specification code, tier, the component numbers and the variant, as the school has it written down. If you do not have it, the examinations officer will provide it on request. This one line removes most of the guesswork from matching and from planning the first month.

process.title: Send recent marked work
process.description: A mock paper, a class test or a returned assignment with the marks on it. Unmarked work is much less useful. The point of the first session is to read the gap between what was attempted and what was awarded, and that needs a marked script rather than a description of how things are going.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: One session, no commitment, with the specialist who would teach the course. Judge it on whether it worked from your child's own script, whether the mark scheme was open, and whether something was written down at the end. Those three things predict the next term better than any credential does.

process.title: Agree the plan and the slot in writing
process.description: What is being worked on, which component, how many sessions, what will be reported and when. Pin the weekly slot to Saudi local time rather than to the tutor's, so a clock change in their country does not move your Wednesday. Agree now what happens to lessons during long school breaks.

process.title: Read the written notes, not the vibe
process.description: A short note after each session saying what moved and what did not. After three sessions there should be a ranked list of repeat errors with evidence from the scripts. If that list does not exist by then, say so early rather than at the end of a package.

process.title: Review at the end of a block
process.description: Compare marked work from before and after on the same component, under the same conditions. Decide whether to continue, change tutor, change component or stop. A good arrangement makes that decision easy because the evidence is already written down.

whyPoints.title: Matched to a code, not a subject
whyPoints.description: A request for help with chemistry can be staffed by almost anybody. A request for Extended 0620 Papers 4 and 6, variant 2, can only be staffed by somebody who knows that structure. We match on the entry line, which is why we ask for it before anything else.

whyPoints.title: The pool is not the neighbourhood
whyPoints.description: Because lessons are online, a family in Jazan, Najran or Ha'il draws on the same specialists as a family in Riyadh. The alternative outside the three big markets is usually a capable local generalist, and for one difficult component that is not the same thing.

whyPoints.title: Evidence a parent can read
whyPoints.description: Written session notes and a ranked list of repeat errors with marks attached. Not a satisfaction score, not a testimonial, not a claim about results that nobody can check. The test of a one-to-one arrangement is whether it leaves a trail, and ours is designed to.

whyPoints.title: A clear line on assessed work
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach, explain criteria and give written feedback on drafts the student has written. They do not supply sentences, structures or data. We say this on the page because the alternative is sold openly in this market and the penalty for it falls on the student.

whyPoints.title: Scheduled around the real week
whyPoints.description: Sunday to Thursday, Arabia Standard Time, slots pinned to Saudi local time so a clock change elsewhere does not move them. Ramadan and the long breaks are planned for in advance rather than improvised, which is how a weekly slot survives a full year.

whyPoints.title: Start with one component
whyPoints.description: Most families do not need a whole course rebuilt. They need one paper type fixed. Starting narrow makes the result visible in weeks, keeps the cost proportionate and makes it straightforward to stop if the arrangement is not working.

faqs.question: Which Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 topics only show up as a problem once a paper is sat without a calculator?
faqs.answer: Surds and index laws, fraction arithmetic inside algebraic rearrangement, and standard form are the usual three. A student can handle all of them with a calculator and then stall when the device is taken away, because the underlying number fluency was never built. The symptom is a correct method with an arithmetic slip in the middle, which costs the accuracy mark and sometimes the following marks too. Confirm which components your child is entered for before planning this work, because Cambridge has revised the 0580 component structure and the non-calculator paper is not present in every version.

faqs.question: In a one-to-one session, how do you find which Biology 0610 command term a student keeps misreading?
faqs.answer: By taking three or four marked longer questions on content the student knows well, and comparing the command term in each stem against the first clause of what they wrote. The pattern shows up quickly: a student who describes when asked to explain will do it consistently, not occasionally. Once the term is identified the repair is short, because no new content is needed. Twenty minutes a week writing only the opening clause of answers, with the terms varied, closes it inside a term.

faqs.question: Why does a student who knows all of Physics 0625 still lose marks on the suggest questions?
faqs.answer: Suggest signals that the stem is unfamiliar on purpose. It is testing whether a known principle can be applied to a situation the candidate has not been taught, which is a different objective from recall. Students who revise by rereading notes build the recall and never practise the transfer, so they recite the taught version of the topic and the mark scheme cannot credit it. The fix is deliberate practice on unfamiliar stems about familiar content, out loud, until applying the principle stops feeling like a trick question.

faqs.question: What goes wrong in the Chemistry 0620 alternative-to-practical paper that teaching more content will not fix?
faqs.answer: That paper examines experimental reasoning in writing, which is a separate skill from doing the experiment. Candidates are asked to identify a variable, name a control, read a measurement to the right precision, or suggest an improvement. Answers that say be more careful or use better equipment earn nothing, because the scheme wants a named variable and a measurable change. Students who have done plenty of laboratory work still lose these marks, because nobody has taught them the written conventions the paper is marked against.

faqs.question: Which part of Cambridge IGCSE Economics 0455 most often needs outside teaching?
faqs.answer: Data response, by a wide margin. Candidates arrive able to define elasticity, draw a market diagram and explain a government intervention, then lose marks because they do not quote figures from the table in the stem or link their answer to the specific economy described. The theory is the part schools teach well. The habit of answering from the resource rather than from memory is the part that tends to be assumed, and it is worth several marks a paper once it is built.

faqs.question: What should a 1-to-1 IGCSE tutor be able to tell me about assessment objectives before I book a package?
faqs.answer: They should be able to say which objective your child is losing marks against, and show you the evidence from a marked script. A specialist will distinguish between recall marks and application marks and give you an example of each from your child's own work. A generalist will answer about the topic instead, which is a reasonable answer to a different question. The distinction matters because the two problems need different teaching and very different numbers of hours to repair.

faqs.question: Can I ask a tutor to send me a page of the specification with their own annotations on it?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is one of the more revealing things to ask for. A tutor who works from the specification will have marked-up pages already and will send one without preparing anything. A tutor who works from a textbook will send a contents page or a topic list, which is not the same document and does not evidence the same knowledge. Neither response is dishonest, but only the first tells you the person reads what the examination is actually built from.

faqs.question: Is a tutor who teaches one subject on both Cambridge and Pearson better than two single-board specialists?
faqs.answer: For one student entered on one board, no. Breadth across boards is useful to a tutor comparing specifications, which matters if your child is transferring mid-course, but it is not what a settled candidate needs. What a settled candidate needs is somebody who knows the component list, the variant and the mark-scheme habits of their own entry in detail. Ask which board the tutor has taught most recently and for how long, then match that to the entry line rather than to the subject.

faqs.question: How do I check a 1-to-1 tutor has read the mark scheme and not just the textbook?
faqs.answer: Ask them for a line from a published mark scheme they think is badly worded, and why. Only somebody who reads schemes closely and repeatedly has an opinion about one. A second test works too: hand them a past-paper question and ask what the command term rules out. A scheme reader will tell you what the examiner will not accept, which is the half of the answer that earns marks. A content teacher will explain the topic instead.

faqs.question: Our tutor is strong on content but weak on examination technique, so do we change tutor or add a second one?
faqs.answer: Usually neither at first. Say the problem out loud and ask for the next three sessions to be built from marked scripts with the mark scheme open, with a written list of repeat errors at the end. Plenty of strong content teachers can do that work and simply have not been asked to. If the list does not appear after three sessions, change tutor rather than adding one, because two people teaching the same component tends to confuse a student rather than help.

faqs.question: In a private one-to-one session, who is actually checking that the work my child submits is their own?
faqs.answer: Nobody is watching, which is exactly why a family should set the arrangement up to leave a record. Keep dated session notes, the written feedback given on each draft, and the drafts themselves in sequence. The school's own supervision arrangement stays in charge of the assessed component throughout. If a question is ever raised about how a piece of work developed, that trail answers it, and no assurance from anybody substitutes for having it.

faqs.question: May a 1-to-1 tutor annotate a draft of an IGCSE coursework piece, and in what form?
faqs.answer: A tutor may read a draft the student has written and give feedback on it, and written feedback is better than spoken because it can be kept and shown. What the feedback may do is point at a criterion the draft has not met, ask a question about an unsupported claim, or note that a section is undeveloped. What it may not do is supply replacement sentences, dictate a structure paragraph by paragraph, or correct the draft to the point where the improvement belongs to the tutor rather than the candidate.

faqs.question: What record should a family keep of a one-to-one session that touched assessed work?
faqs.answer: Four things, all of them small. The date and length of the session. What was discussed, in a line or two. The written feedback given, saved as it was sent. And the student's own draft as it stood before and after. Kept in order, that is a complete account of how a piece of work developed. It takes a few minutes a week and it is the only form of protection that does not depend on somebody taking a family's word for it.

faqs.question: What does a school's malpractice process look like if a tutor is suspected of over-helping?
faqs.answer: The school investigates first, because the component is marked and submitted by the school, and the board has its own process above that. Outcomes range from the work being resubmitted to a component mark being withheld, and in serious cases a subject grade or a certificate can be affected. The penalty falls on the candidate, not on the tutor or the provider, which is the asymmetry families should understand before accepting any offer that sounds like help with producing the work itself.

faqs.question: Does one-to-one teaching change what counts as acceptable help on a Middle Years Programme Personal Project?
faqs.answer: The rules do not change with the format, but the risk does, because a private session has no witnesses. The Personal Project is the student's own design, process and reflection, assessed by the school against published criteria. A tutor may discuss how criteria work, ask questions that make the student justify a choice, and give feedback on a draft the student wrote. Choosing the topic for them, planning the process or writing the reflection moves it out of the student's hands, and the assessment is about exactly that process.

faqs.question: How many one-to-one hours a week is too many for a single IGCSE subject?
faqs.answer: More than two hours a week on one subject is usually a sign the diagnosis is wrong rather than the dose. Technique problems need short, frequent, well-spaced work with written practice in between, and three hours of talking does less than one hour plus a marked attempt. Real content gaps are the exception and can justify more for a defined block. If a provider recommends a high weekly volume before seeing marked work, ask what evidence the recommendation is based on.

1-to-1-igcse-tutor.closingHeading: Start with one line from the school office
1-to-1-igcse-tutor.closingBody: Before paying anybody for anything, ask your school's examinations officer for the entry details in writing: subject, syllabus or specification code, tier, component numbers and variant. Send that line and a piece of recent marked work, and the first session can begin with a diagnosis rather than an introduction. The free trial lesson is with the specialist who would teach the course, and it should end with something written down. Lessons are delivered online, one to one, over live video, scheduled against Arabia Standard Time and the Sunday-to-Thursday week, which is what makes an Extended specialist available to a family anywhere in the Kingdom rather than only in its three largest cities.
