abha.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach 'Asir families across the Diploma, the Middle Years Programme and Cambridge or Edexcel IGCSE. Each is matched to a named syllabus and a named level rather than to a subject in general, because a Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches Higher Level candidate and a Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation Standard Level one need genuinely different teaching.

intro.heading: Why an Abha family ends up looking outside the city
paragraphs: Start with the money, because it is what most families want first and almost nobody in this market will put it in writing. Advertised rates for IB subject tuition in the Kingdom begin at about SAR 180 an hour on tutoring-company listings, with Higher Level and Advanced Placement tracks published nearer SAR 200 to 220. General senior-school private tuition in Riyadh is quoted at SAR 200 and above by tutor marketplaces, while budget online platforms advertise IGCSE support from as little as SAR 35. Those are advertised figures, published by the providers themselves. They are not a market average, and they are not our price.

The second thing to understand is that in Abha the hourly figure is only half the sum. 'Asir has far fewer international-curriculum campuses than Riyadh, Jeddah or the Dammam-Khobar-Dhahran cluster, so a family wanting a Higher Level Physics tutor in Abha or an Extended Essay supervisor is not choosing between several local candidates. They are usually choosing between one who happens to be free and none at all. An in-home arrangement adds the tutor's travel to the bill and narrows the pool to whoever lives within driving distance of your district. Teaching online removes the travel line from the invoice and widens the pool to anyone who teaches the syllabus.

IB Gram does not sell home visits in Saudi Arabia; home visits are a service we offer only in India. Every lesson for an Abha family runs one-to-one over live video, on Arabia Standard Time, with the tutor's screen shared so that past papers, mark schemes and working are visible to both sides at once. That is stated plainly here rather than buried four screens down, because the phrase a parent types is frequently 'home tutor' and the honest answer in 'Asir is that the thing worth paying for is the specialist, not the commute.

Quality is the next question and it is harder than price. There is no public register you can look up to confirm that somebody knows Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620 rather than chemistry in general. What a family can check is specific: which board and which syllabus code, whether the tutor has taught the current guide rather than the one before it, whether they have marked for a board and in what capacity, and what they say when asked where candidates lose marks in a particular paper. A tutor who answers with topic names and command terms has taught the course. A tutor who answers with adjectives has not.

Then the logistics, which in Abha are geographic rather than administrative. The school week runs Sunday to Thursday; Friday and Saturday are the weekend, so a weekday evening slot is the normal shape and a Friday morning block is the usual overflow. The drive decides the rest. A family in Al Manhal, a family in Khamis Mushait twenty-five kilometres east and a family up in the Soudah villages are not free at the same hour, and in the wet months cloud sits on the escarpment road. Slots are pinned to Saudi local time, so a tutor abroad changing their own clocks does not move your lesson.

The last part of this page is the part almost no competitor writes: what happens after the certificate. An IB Diploma, a set of A Levels or an American high school diploma all need an equivalency decision, the mu'adalah, from the Ministry of Education before a Saudi university treats the certificate as equivalent to the Saudi secondary certificate. Qudurat and Tahsili sit alongside that step, run by the Education and Training Evaluation Commission through its National Center for Assessment. Tahsili follows the Saudi national curriculum, which is precisely why international-curriculum students find its framing unfamiliar even where the content overlaps.

abha.programmesIntro: Four programmes account for nearly every enquiry that reaches us from 'Asir. Two are IB, one is the sixteen-plus examination stage that most private schools here reach for, and one is the primary stage that decides how hard the next two years feel. The notes under each are about Abha specifically, not about the programme in the abstract.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus the core: the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS. Higher Level courses are built on roughly 240 recommended teaching hours against about 150 at Standard Level, and that difference is where most outside support is spent. The core carries points of its own through the Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay matrix, so a strong set of subject grades can still be undone by a neglected essay.
programmes.countryNote: An Abha family taking on the Diploma is usually doing it at a distance from the nearest campus that runs it, or doing part of it by arrangement. That makes two things urgent: Higher Level subject choices need to be right early, because a late change is harder to absorb without a full subject department nearby, and Extended Essay supervision needs a named adult from the start. A Diploma Programme tutor in 'Asir is most often hired for exactly those two pressure points.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Five years of concept-led teaching assessed against published criteria rather than against a single terminal paper, finishing with the Personal Project. The criteria are the thing families misread: a student can know the content and still sit at the bottom of a criterion band because they have never been taught what the strand actually asks for. Command-term literacy starts here, not in the Diploma.
programmes.countryNote: In Abha the Middle Years Programme years are where a gap becomes expensive later. Mathematics and the sciences are the usual culprits: a student arriving in the Diploma or in IGCSE with shaky algebra loses marks in Physics two years later for reasons that have nothing to do with Physics. Families here often use these years for maintenance teaching rather than crisis teaching, which is cheaper per mark gained than anything bought in a final term.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Two-year courses examined by written paper, with coursework in some subjects and none in others. Cambridge grades most subjects A* to G in this region and tiers several, including Mathematics 0580, into Core and Extended entries. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE grades 9 to 1 and tiers Mathematics A into Foundation and Higher. The tier decision caps the grade available, so it has to be made on evidence rather than optimism.
programmes.countryNote: An IGCSE tutor in Abha is most often asked for Mathematics, the separate sciences and English, in that order. The local pattern is a private school that offers the board but cannot always staff every subject with a specialist, so one or two subjects end up taught by somebody teaching outside their degree. Families here are rarely shopping for a general tutor; they are filling a named hole in a timetable.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led primary teaching organised around transdisciplinary themes rather than separate subject periods, with no external examination at the end. The exit point is the exhibition. Outside support at this stage is almost never remedial in the exam sense; it is about reading fluency, number sense and written English, the three things everything after it is built on.
programmes.countryNote: Primary enquiries from Abha are usually about a transition rather than a problem. A family moving a child from a national-curriculum primary into an international-curriculum school, or planning for a relocation to Riyadh or Jeddah, wants the written-English gap closed before the move rather than after it. One or two sessions a week over an autumn term does more here than an intensive block ever will.

abha.subjectsIntro: These are the IB subjects 'Asir families ask for most, with a note on what each one is actually examined on and where candidates reliably drop marks. Where a subject is tiered or split into routes, the route matters more than the subject name: a request for 'a maths tutor' is not specific enough to act on.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The algebraic route, and the one most engineering and physics courses expect. Higher Level carries a third paper that Standard Level does not, alongside the internally assessed exploration. The common failure is not difficulty but fluency: candidates who meet proof, complex numbers and calculus without automatic algebra spend their working time on manipulation instead of method. A Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches tutor in Abha is the single most requested match we see from 'Asir.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The modelling and statistics route, with technology permitted throughout. It is not the easy option; it is a different set of skills, weighted towards interpreting output and justifying a model in words. Marks go missing in the writing rather than the arithmetic. Students who chose it to avoid algebra are often the ones who struggle, because the Higher Level content still demands it.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics, fields, waves and thermal physics, with Higher Level extensions that have no Standard Level counterpart. The marks lost are rarely conceptual. They go on unit errors, on graphs drawn without a line of best fit, and on extended-response answers that describe the right physics without using the command term the question asked for. A Higher Level Physics tutor in Abha is usually hired for the written answers, not the equations.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Stoichiometry, bonding, energetics, kinetics, equilibrium and organic chemistry, with the internally assessed investigation on top. Organic mechanisms and equilibrium are where outside teaching earns its fee. Definitions are marked strictly: a candidate who writes 'the energy change' where the mark scheme wants 'the enthalpy change under standard conditions' has lost the mark for vocabulary rather than for chemistry.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: A large content course where strong students still lose marks on the long-answer questions. The pattern is consistent: a correct recall answer that never addresses the verb in the question. 'Explain' needs a mechanism, 'outline' needs brevity, and 'suggest' expects an answer not taught in the syllabus. Data-handling questions on unfamiliar experiments reward technique over memory.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Microeconomics, macroeconomics and the global economy, assessed on written papers and an internally assessed portfolio of commentaries built from published news articles. Diagrams are not decoration: an unlabelled axis or a shift drawn the wrong way costs marks that the surrounding essay cannot recover. Evaluation is the Higher Level dividing line and the part most candidates practise least.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Organisational structure, human resources, finance, marketing and operations, with a case study released ahead of the examination. Candidates who learn the tools but never apply them to the named business in front of them score in the middle band and stay there. Application and evaluation are where the grade is decided, and both can be taught directly.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Guided textual analysis, a comparative essay and oral work, with an additional written task at Higher Level. The usual weakness is a candidate who can summarise a text but cannot write about how it works. Analysis of form, structure and audience is a trainable skill, and it is the one that separates a mid-band response from an upper-band one.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: System fundamentals, computational thinking, algorithms and the internally assessed solution, with abstract data structures added at Higher Level. Students who code well often write poorly about what they have coded, and the written paper is marked on the explanation. Pseudocode discipline and trace tables are the quickest wins available in this subject.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: The two written core components carry Diploma points through a matrix, and both are marked on a published set of criteria rather than on the quality of the idea alone. The Extended Essay lives or dies on its research question. A tutor's job here is to teach the criteria, question the argument and give feedback on the student's own drafts, never to produce the work.

abha.igcseSubjectsIntro: Where an Abha family is working at IGCSE rather than IB, these are the subjects and syllabus codes that come up. Codes are as the boards publish them; your school's examinations officer holds the entry codes that will actually be used, and those are the ones that matter.

igcseSubjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580, Edexcel 4MA1)
igcseSubjects.description: The tiering decision is the whole game. A Core or Foundation entry caps the grade available, and once the entry is made it cannot be improved by effort. Evidence from marked papers across a term, not a single mock, should decide it.

igcseSubjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625, Edexcel 4PH1)
igcseSubjects.description: Electricity and the practical-skills questions do most of the damage. Candidates sit a written paper about experiments they may never have run, so reading an unfamiliar method and spotting the controlled variable is an examinable skill in its own right.

igcseSubjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620, Edexcel 4CH1)
igcseSubjects.description: Moles, electrolysis and the qualitative-analysis tests account for most lost marks. The tests reward rote accuracy: the precipitate colour and the reagent have to be exact, and partial credit is rare.

igcseSubjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610, Edexcel 4BI1)
igcseSubjects.description: A memory-heavy syllabus examined with precision. Transport in plants, enzymes and inheritance are the recurring weak spots, and candidates lose marks for naming a process without describing the mechanism the question asked for.

igcseSubjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 and 0511)
igcseSubjects.description: Directed writing and the summary task carry a disproportionate weight for the time spent teaching them. The summary is marked on content points and on language separately, so a fluent answer that misses the points still scores badly.

igcseSubjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450, Edexcel 4BS1)
igcseSubjects.description: Case-study application decides the grade. Candidates who recite definitions score in the lower bands; candidates who apply the same definitions to the business described in the paper move up two bands with no extra content learned.

abha.regionsTitle: Abha, Khamis Mushait and the 'Asir districts we teach into
abha.regionsIntro: 'Asir is not one commute. The city centre, the northern expansion, the twin city to the east, the escarpment villages above and the Tihama descent below all produce different school runs, and the school run decides what time a lesson can start. These notes exist so a slot can be set once and left alone.

regions.name: Al Manhal
regions.note: Central Abha, close to the municipal core and the ring road. School runs here are short, so Al Manhal families are usually the earliest in the city to be free: a 16:30 start holds in term time without anyone eating in the car.

regions.name: Al Sadd
regions.note: Named for the Abha dam on the southern edge of the city. The dam lake and the surrounding park pull weekend traffic, which makes a Friday morning block easier to keep than a Friday afternoon one for families here.

regions.name: Abha Al Jadeed
regions.note: The newer residential expansion spreading north of the old centre, with wider roads and newer compounds. A 17:00 start is comfortable from here most of the year, and the drive is predictable enough to plan two subjects on separate evenings.

regions.name: Al Qabel
regions.note: On the northern approach towards the airport road. The straight-line distance to a central school flatters the actual run, because the route doubles back through the city. Families here tend to settle on a later slot and keep it.

regions.name: Khamis Mushait
regions.note: About 25 km east of Abha and effectively its twin. Families routinely live in one city and attend school in the other, so the two share a catchment. A Cambridge IGCSE tutor in Khamis Mushait is the same match as one in Abha; only the start time shifts.

regions.name: Ahad Rafidah
regions.note: South-east of Khamis Mushait on the open highway, and the longest regular commute in the cluster. This is where the argument for an online slot is strongest: the drive that would be spent reaching a tutor is the hour the lesson needs.

regions.name: Al Soudah
regions.note: The escarpment above the city, climbing towards 3,000 metres. Cloud and the wet-season rain make the road slow and occasionally closed, so a fixed online slot survives weather that a scheduled drive simply does not.

regions.name: Rijal Almaa
regions.note: Down the Aqabat on the Tihama side, a long descent from the plateau. Families here are furthest from any international-curriculum campus in the province, which changes the question from 'which tutor' to 'is this subject available at all'.

schoolClusters.city: Jeddah and the Red Sea coast
schoolClusters.note: When an 'Asir family needs Diploma provision the province cannot supply, Jeddah is the usual first look because the flight is short and relatives are often already there. Students we support attend schools in this cluster, and families use the same list when weighing boarding against a full relocation.

The deepest pool of IB provision in the Kingdom, and the cluster an 'Asir family moves into most often for work. The practical value of the list is in the transfer conversation: a school admitting a student mid-course will ask what has been covered, and a tutor can produce that record from marked work.

Dammam, Al Khobar, Dhahran and Jubail behave as one school market, and the Diploma is offered at some campuses there but not all of them. An 'Asir family with a parent rotating to the Eastern Province usually wants to know which campuses run the Diploma rather than only the Middle Years Programme.

abha.modesIntro: Four shapes cover almost everything an Abha family asks for. The right one depends less on the subject than on how much time is left before the series and how much of the problem is content rather than technique. All four run one-to-online-one over live video on Arabia Standard Time.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one, Sunday to Thursday
modes.description: The default and the cheapest per mark gained. One or two fixed evening slots a week through the term, with marked work going back and forth in between. The slot is pinned to Saudi local time so it does not drift when a tutor abroad changes their own clocks, and it is held through the autumn and spring terms rather than rebooked each week.
bullets: Fixed slot, same day and time each week
Written work marked between lessons, not during them
Pinned to Arabia Standard Time, never to the tutor's local time
Reviewed at the end of each block of hours

modes.title: Friday or Saturday blocks
modes.description: The Kingdom's weekend is Friday and Saturday, which gives 'Asir families a long uninterrupted window that a school evening never provides. A two-hour weekend block suits Internal Assessment work, Extended Essay drafting and full past papers under timed conditions, because none of those fit comfortably into sixty minutes after a school run.
bullets: Two-hour windows for full papers under timed conditions
Better for drafting work than a weekday evening
Useful where a parent wants to be present for the review
Often paired with one weekday slot in the same week

modes.title: Intensive run-up before a series
modes.description: A compressed block in the weeks before the June or November series, built around past papers and mark schemes rather than new content. By this point the syllabus is either known or it is not, and the available marks sit in technique: reading the command term, allocating time by mark tariff, and knowing when to abandon a question.
bullets: Past papers marked to the published scheme, then re-sat
Timing drills against the mark tariff
Topic triage: what is still worth learning and what is not
No new content introduced in the final fortnight

modes.title: Internal Assessment and coursework review
modes.description: Short, scheduled sessions focused on a student's own draft. The tutor reads what the student has written, explains which criterion strand the work is currently sitting in and why, and sets the next revision for the student to make. The tutor does not write, redraft or supply text for assessed work, and says so to the student directly.
bullets: Criterion-by-criterion feedback on the student's own draft
Research question stress-tested before the writing starts
A record of what was discussed, for the school's supervision trail

sections.heading: What outside tuition actually costs an Abha family
paragraphs: A parent in Abha asking what this costs is usually met with 'contact us'. The table below is the opposite of that. Every figure in it is an advertised rate, published by a provider or a marketplace, with the kind of source named beside it. None of it is what IB Gram charges, and none of it is a market average: an advertised rate is a shop window, not a transaction.

Read the spread rather than any single line. Non-specialist general tutoring is advertised from around SAR 55 an hour, and budget online platforms go lower still for IGCSE, from about SAR 35. At the other end, senior-school examination subjects in Riyadh are quoted at SAR 200 and above, IB subject tuition starts near SAR 180 on company listings, and Higher Level or Advanced Placement tracks are published at roughly SAR 200 to 220. Some international providers quote in dollars at around USD 60 an hour, which moves with the exchange rate and frequently arrives with a card fee attached.

The gap between SAR 35 and SAR 220 is not a quality ladder you can read off a price list. It is mostly a scarcity gap. A great many people can take a willing student through a Standard Level maths topic; very few can take a Higher Level Physics candidate through an extended-response question and explain, in mark-scheme language, why a physically correct answer scored two marks out of five. In 'Asir the second kind of person is not going to be your neighbour, and that is the entire argument for paying for a specialist rather than for a drive.

One practical note on using the table. Ask any provider which line their quote sits on, and ask what the quote excludes: marking between lessons, Internal Assessment feedback, written reports, and whether Higher Level is billed differently from Standard Level. A provider who cannot answer that is quoting you a number rather than a service, and the number will move later.

sections.heading: What moves the hourly figure, in order of weight
paragraphs: Scarcity of the subject and level does more to the price than anything else, and it does it everywhere, not only here. A Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation Standard Level tutor is available in quantity; a Higher Level Physics or Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches Higher Level specialist is not. The Higher Level course carries roughly 240 recommended teaching hours against about 150 at Standard Level, plus components the Standard Level course does not sit, so the teaching is harder and the pool of people who can do it is smaller. Price follows the pool.

Marking and examining experience is the second lever. A tutor who has marked for a board has read several hundred answers to the same question and knows what the scheme credits and what it quietly ignores. That is a genuinely different thing from knowing the content, and it is the one claim worth paying a premium for. It is also the claim most often asserted and least often evidenced, so ask which board, which component, and in what capacity. An answer that names the paper is worth something; an answer that says 'extensive examiner experience' is worth nothing.

Travel is the third and the most avoidable. An in-home arrangement in any Saudi city prices in the tutor's journey, and a cancelled visit still costs somebody the trip. In 'Asir the journey can be a climb up the escarpment in cloud. Removing travel from the equation is not a small saving; it is the difference between a tutor pool bounded by a twenty-minute drive and one bounded only by who teaches the syllabus.

Package length and timing make up the rest. Rates quoted close to a series reflect demand rather than quality, and a block agreed in the autumn term is usually priced more calmly than the same block agreed eight weeks out. What should not move the price is a promise about the outcome. No tutor, however experienced with a mark scheme, can guarantee a grade, and any quote that leans on an outcome rather than on the work is selling the wrong thing.
bullets: Subject scarcity and level do most of the work on price

sections.heading: Judging a tutor when nobody local can vouch for them
paragraphs: In a large city a family can usually find somebody who has used a tutor before. In Abha the international-curriculum community is small enough that the recommendation network thins out fast, and once you are hiring somebody who is not in 'Asir, word of mouth stops working altogether. What replaces it is a set of questions with checkable answers, asked in a trial lesson rather than over a chat thread.

Start with the syllabus, not the subject. Ask which board, which syllabus code and which version of the guide the tutor has taught. A Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620 candidate and a Pearson Edexcel 4CH1 candidate sit different papers with different question styles, and a tutor who treats them as the same course will cost your child marks. For IB, ask whether they have taught the current subject guide or the one before it, because the assessment model changed and the old past papers are not a like-for-like resource.

Then ask where marks are lost. This single question separates people quickly. A tutor who has taught the course will answer with topics and command terms: organic mechanisms, the qualitative-analysis tests, 'explain' answers that describe instead of explaining, graphs without a line of best fit. A tutor who has not will answer with generalities about confidence and exam stress. Both answers can be delivered pleasantly; only one of them is information.

Finally, ask what happens between lessons and what happens if it is not working. Marked written work returned with annotations is the only reliable evidence that teaching is landing, and a tutor who does not mark between sessions is selling an hour rather than a result. On fit, the honest position is that some matches do not work and the fix is a different tutor, early, not a longer run at the same one. We would rather re-match in week three than defend a pairing into a second term.

sections.heading: The Abha school run, and the hours it leaves
paragraphs: This is the part that decides whether tutoring happens at all, and it is the part rival pages skip because it requires knowing the city. Abha is not laid out like a Gulf coastal city. It sits on a plateau at around 2,200 metres with the escarpment on three sides, the built-up area climbs and drops, and the twin city of Khamis Mushait is roughly 25 km east with a shared school catchment. A family's address does not just change their distance to school; it changes the shape of their afternoon.

The constraint in 'Asir is rarely congestion of the Riyadh kind. It is gradient, weather and distance. A run from Ahad Rafidah or down from the Soudah villages is long before anything goes wrong, and in the wet months cloud sits on the escarpment road and the descent to the Tihama slows to a crawl. The sensible response is not to schedule optimistically and then cancel. It is to set the slot thirty minutes later than the best case and keep it for the whole term.

The table below is built from road distance and terrain rather than from traffic surveys, so treat the times as a starting point for your own household and not as a measurement. What it gets right is the ordering: central districts free up first, the twin city thirty minutes behind, the outlying towns and the escarpment later again. A family who sets the slot against their actual worst week rather than their best one almost never has to move it.

One further point specific to online delivery. Because nobody is travelling, a late slot costs nothing extra and a weather day does not cancel a lesson. The family in Rijal Almaa and the family in Al Manhal get the same tutor at the hour that suits each of them, which is not a thing an in-home arrangement in this province can offer at any price.

sections.heading: Arabia Standard Time against the tutor's own working week
paragraphs: The Kingdom runs on Arabia Standard Time, UTC+3, and does not change its clocks. That one fact causes more cancelled lessons than anything else on this page, because most countries a specialist tutor might live in do change theirs. A slot agreed in conversation as 'half past five your time' drifts by an hour twice a year unless it is written down in Saudi local time and left there.

The second half of the problem is the tutor's own week rather than their clock. A full-time tutor in India or the United Kingdom can take a Saudi evening slot indefinitely. A serving classroom teacher cannot reliably take one at 14:30 their time on a Tuesday, because they are teaching. This is why a tutor's availability is worth asking about in the same breath as their qualifications: a brilliant match who can only do Thursdays at 21:00 is not a match for a fifteen-year-old in Abha with school the next morning.

Weekends are the other asymmetry. Friday and Saturday are the Kingdom's weekend, and for most of the tutor world they are a working Friday and a Saturday. That actually helps: a Friday morning in Abha is a Friday working morning almost everywhere else, which makes it the easiest two-hour block in the week to fill with a specialist who is busy on weekday evenings.

The table below converts a 17:30 Abha slot into the tutor's own time in the places our 'Asir matches usually sit. Use it as a filter when a provider offers you somebody without naming their base. If a tutor's location would put your child's lesson at midnight their time, the arrangement will quietly degrade within a term, whatever anybody promises at the outset.

sections.heading: 'Asir weather, altitude and the term that gets interrupted
paragraphs: Abha has a climate no other part of the Kingdom has, and it shows up in the academic year in ways a page written for Riyadh will never mention. At around 2,200 metres the summer is wet rather than scorching, cloud sits on the escarpment, and the roads that matter to a school run are the ones that climb. Families in the Soudah villages and on the Tihama descent lose more school mornings to weather than families in any Gulf city do.

That interacts badly with in-home tutoring and barely at all with online lessons. A tutor who has to reach your district is one road closure away from a cancelled hour, and the hour is usually not refunded in anybody's model, only rebooked into a week that is already full. A lesson delivered over live video on a fixed slot survives a wet Tuesday. The only thing it needs is a connection and a quiet room.

The other 'Asir distinctive is the tourist season. The province is a domestic summer destination, which fills the city with visitors precisely when international-curriculum schools are between years and when a family might otherwise have used the long break for catch-up work. A household hosting relatives through that period and planning to start tutoring in the same weeks is planning to do two things badly. The fix is simple: agree the slot before the break, start light, and hold it.

Ramadan moves roughly eleven days earlier each year against the Gregorian calendar, so it drifts across the academic year rather than sitting in one term. School days shorten during it and evening patterns change in every Saudi household. Dates are confirmed by moon sighting and differ by a day between countries, so we do not print them. What we do is move the slot later for the period and agree the shift in advance rather than week by week.

sections.heading: From an 'Asir certificate to a Saudi university place
paragraphs: This is the biggest hole in the Saudi tutoring market and it is worth reading even if your child is years away from it. An IB Diploma, a set of A Levels and an American high school diploma are all foreign certificates as far as a Saudi university is concerned. Before one is treated as equivalent to the Saudi secondary certificate, it needs an equivalency decision, the mu'adalah, from the Ministry of Education. That is an administrative process with its own evidence requirements, and it is separate from anything the IB or Cambridge does.

Alongside it sit the Qiyas tests, run by the Education and Training Evaluation Commission through its National Center for Assessment. Qudurat, the General Aptitude Test, assesses verbal and quantitative reasoning rather than syllabus content, and is sat in Arabic or in English. Tahsili, the Achievement Test, covers the science-stream subjects: mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology and English. The critical fact for an 'Asir family in an international-curriculum school is that Tahsili content follows the Saudi national curriculum.

That is why international-curriculum students regularly find Tahsili harder than their own examinations. The material overlaps but the framing does not: topic order, terminology and the expected method differ from a Cambridge or IB treatment of the same physics. A student who can write a strong Higher Level Physics extended response can still be caught out by a question posed the way the national syllabus poses it. Preparation for it is a separate piece of work from subject tuition, and it is better started as a planned strand than as a panic in the final term.

Universities publish their own admission formulas combining school grades with the Qiyas results, and the weightings differ by university and by programme, with competitive engineering, medicine and science programmes leaning hardest on Tahsili. Some also state a maximum age for the certificate they will accept. We do not publish thresholds or formulas here, because they differ by institution and by intake and a wrong number is worse than none. Check the criteria on the university's own admissions pages, and start checking in the first Diploma year rather than the second.

sections.heading: Starting from Abha, including what happens if nobody is free
paragraphs: The useful first message is short and specific: the board, the syllabus code, the level, the year group, the subject, and two or three windows in the week that genuinely work after the school run. 'My son needs help with maths' starts a conversation. 'Year 11, Cambridge 0580 Extended, struggling with trigonometry and bearings, free Sunday and Tuesday after 17:00 in Khamis Mushait' gets a named tutor proposed.

Next comes a free trial lesson with the tutor actually proposed, not a sales call and not a different tutor. The point of the trial is diagnostic in both directions. The tutor finds out what the student can do under light pressure, and the family finds out whether this person can explain where the marks are. Ask them, during the trial, where candidates lose marks in the paper your child is weakest at. The quality of that answer predicts the next six months better than any credential.

After the trial there is a written baseline built from marked work rather than from impressions, a plan with the first block of hours in it, and a fixed weekly slot in Saudi local time. Then reviews at the end of each block. If a match is wrong, the honest fix is a different tutor early rather than a longer run at the same one, and we would rather do that in week three than argue about it in month three.

And the honest answer to the awkward question. Sometimes no specialist is free in the subject, level and window you need, particularly for scarce Higher Level sciences in the weeks before a series. When that happens we say so and give you the choice: wait for the slot that fits, take a different window, or start with a tutor who covers part of the need while the specialist is pencilled in. What we do not do is put a generalist in front of a Higher Level candidate and let the family find out in February. We also never write, redraft or supply text for an Internal Assessment, an Extended Essay, a Theory of Knowledge essay or a Personal Project: the work has to be the student's own, and a tutor's job is to teach the criteria and give feedback on what the student has written.

process.title: Send the syllabus, not the subject
process.description: Board, syllabus code, level, year group and the two or three windows that work after your district's school run. An IGCSE tutor in Abha can be proposed within a day from that; 'needs help with science' takes a week of questions first. If you do not know the code, your school's examinations officer does.

process.title: A free trial lesson with the proposed tutor
process.description: Sixty minutes with the person who would actually teach, not a sales call and not a stand-in. The student works on something real while the tutor diagnoses. You listen for one thing: can this person say where marks are lost in the paper your child is weakest at, in topic and command-term language.

process.title: A written baseline from marked work
process.description: Before any block is agreed, a short written baseline drawn from marked questions rather than from a chat. It names the topics that are secure, the topics that are not, and the technique gaps that are costing marks independently of content. This is the document you measure progress against later.

process.title: A fixed weekly slot in Saudi local time
process.description: The slot is written in Arabia Standard Time and held for the term, so a tutor abroad changing their own clocks does not move your lesson. Set it against your worst school-run week rather than your best one. Online IB tuition in Abha costs nothing extra for a later start, because nobody is driving.

process.title: Review at the end of each block
process.description: At the end of a block of hours, a review against the baseline using marked work: what moved, what did not, and whether the plan or the tutor should change. A review that reports effort rather than marks is not a review. If the match is wrong, we re-match rather than extend.

whyPoints.title: The specialist, not the nearest person
whyPoints.description: In 'Asir the pool of people who teach a given Higher Level syllabus within driving distance is very small, and sometimes empty. Teaching online replaces that pool with everyone who teaches the syllabus. A Diploma Programme tutor in 'Asir is matched on the course your child is sitting, not on a postcode.

whyPoints.title: Rates you can actually interrogate
whyPoints.description: Every SAR figure on this page is an advertised rate with its source type named, not a market average and not our price. You can take that table to any provider and ask which line their quote sits on. Vagueness about money in this market is usually evasion rather than discretion.

whyPoints.title: Slots set against the real school run
whyPoints.description: A family in Ahad Rafidah is not free when a family in Al Manhal is, and a wet week on the escarpment road changes both. Slots are set against your worst week and pinned to Arabia Standard Time, so the lesson survives weather, clock changes and a late pickup.

whyPoints.title: Marked work as the evidence
whyPoints.description: Progress is reported from annotated written work against a written baseline, not from a sense that things are going well. That is slower to produce and harder to fake. It is also the only thing that tells you in November whether the money spent since the autumn term has moved any marks.

whyPoints.title: Academic honesty stated plainly
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches the criteria, questions the argument and gives feedback on the student's own drafts. We do not write, redraft or supply text for an Internal Assessment, an Extended Essay, a Theory of Knowledge essay or a Personal Project. Several providers in this market are vague about that line; we are not.

whyPoints.title: No claims we cannot evidence
whyPoints.description: No grade guarantees, no success percentages, no star ratings, no counts of anything we cannot show you. Nothing on this page claims approval or partnership from the Ministry of Education, the Education and Training Evaluation Commission, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, because we hold none of those.

faqs.question: Does an 'Asir student holding an IB Diploma still need Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: Yes. A foreign or international school certificate needs an equivalency decision, the mu'adalah, from the Ministry of Education before a Saudi university treats it as equivalent to the Saudi secondary certificate. That applies to the IB Diploma, to A Levels and to an American high school diploma alike, and it is separate from anything the IB itself issues. It is an administrative process with its own evidence requirements, so the practical advice for an Abha family is to find out what documents are needed during the first Diploma year rather than discovering the list in the final term.

faqs.question: Why does Tahsili catch out an Abha student who has only studied Cambridge science?
faqs.answer: Because Tahsili content follows the Saudi national curriculum, not an international one. It covers mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology and English, and the material overlaps heavily with Cambridge or IB science. What does not overlap is the framing: topic order, terminology and the method a question expects. A student who writes strong extended responses for Cambridge 0625 can still be caught by the same physics asked the way the national syllabus asks it. Preparation for it is a separate strand of work from subject tuition, and it works far better planned than panicked.

faqs.question: Can a student in Abha sit Qudurat in English rather than in Arabic?
faqs.answer: Qudurat, the General Aptitude Test, is run by the Education and Training Evaluation Commission through its National Center for Assessment and is sat in Arabic or in English. It assesses verbal and quantitative reasoning rather than syllabus content, so there is no body of material to revise in the way there is for a subject paper. What improves a score is familiarity with the question types and with the pace. Confirm the language options and the registration windows on the Commission's own channels, since arrangements are set by them and not by a school.

faqs.question: Where should an Abha family check a Saudi university's actual admission criteria?
faqs.answer: On that university's own admissions pages, programme by programme. Universities publish their own formulas combining school grades with the Qudurat and Tahsili results, and the weightings differ by institution and by programme, with competitive engineering, medicine and science courses leaning hardest on Tahsili. Some also state a maximum age for the certificate they will accept. Third-party sites in this market contradict each other on the numbers, which is why no threshold or formula appears anywhere on this page. Read the primary source, and read it in the first Diploma year.

faqs.question: When should an Abha family start outside support for a Middle Years Programme student?
faqs.answer: At the point a criterion band stops moving, which is usually earlier than a parent expects. Middle Years Programme work is assessed against published criteria, and a student can know the content while sitting in a low band because nobody has taught them what the strand actually asks for. In Abha the subjects that justify early support are mathematics and the sciences, because a weak algebra foundation reappears as lost Physics marks two years later. Maintenance teaching across these years costs less per mark gained than anything bought in a final term.

faqs.question: Is it too late to add a tutor in the second Diploma year from Abha?
faqs.answer: No, but the work changes shape. In the second year there is rarely time to reteach a syllabus, so sessions move to past papers, mark schemes and triage: which topics are still worth learning, which are not, and where technique is losing marks that content already covers. Internal Assessment deadlines also sit in this year and usually need protecting first. The honest caveat is availability. Scarce Higher Level science specialists fill up in the months before a series, so a late start narrows the choice of tutor rather than the usefulness of the hours.

faqs.question: What should an Abha student do in the break before the first Diploma year starts?
faqs.answer: Three things, none of them a full course. Shore up algebra if a science or a mathematics Higher Level is coming, because that is the gap that costs most later. Read around two or three possible Extended Essay areas so the research question is not invented in a hurry. And get used to command terms: the difference between 'explain', 'outline', 'suggest' and 'evaluate' decides marks from the first assessment onwards. 'Asir summers are the domestic tourist season, so plan light, scheduled work rather than an intensive block nobody will keep.

faqs.question: How early do Higher Level choices need to be settled for a student in 'Asir?
faqs.answer: Earlier than for a family in Riyadh, because the fallback is thinner. A Higher Level course runs on roughly 240 recommended teaching hours against about 150 at Standard Level, and it carries components Standard Level does not sit, so a change made late is expensive to absorb. Where a local campus cannot staff a chosen Higher Level subject at all, the family needs to know that before the choice is locked rather than after. Ask the school directly which Higher Level subjects it will actually run next year, not which it lists.

faqs.question: What does a Year 10 IGCSE student in Abha need that a Year 11 student does not?
faqs.answer: Content security and a tier decision made on evidence. Year 10 is when a Cambridge 0580 or Edexcel 4MA1 entry tier should be argued from marked papers across a term rather than from one mock, because a Core or Foundation entry caps the grade available and effort afterwards cannot lift the cap. Year 11 work is mostly technique: timing against the mark tariff, reading command terms, and the qualitative-analysis or practical-skills questions that reward rote accuracy. The two years need different tutoring, and paying for the second kind in Year 10 is premature.

faqs.question: What does an hour of IB tuition cost an Abha family compared with the advertised Riyadh rate?
faqs.answer: The advertised Riyadh figures are the only published reference points, and they are the right starting point for 'Asir too, because online delivery means the tutor is not local to either city. IB subject tuition is advertised from about SAR 180 an hour on tutoring-company listings, with Higher Level and Advanced Placement tracks nearer SAR 200 to 220. Those are provider-published rates rather than a market average or our price. What Abha genuinely does change is the in-home comparison: travel loading and road conditions here make a visiting tutor costlier and less reliable than in Riyadh.

faqs.question: Is there a free trial lesson for an Abha family, and what happens in it?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it runs with the tutor actually proposed rather than with a salesperson or a stand-in. It is diagnostic in both directions. The student works on something real so the tutor can see what holds up under light pressure, and you watch how the tutor explains. The question worth asking inside the hour is where candidates lose marks in the paper your child is weakest at. An answer naming topics and command terms tells you this person has taught the course; an answer about confidence tells you they have not.

faqs.question: Does a scarce Higher Level subject cost more for an Abha student than a common Standard Level one?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the reason is supply rather than geography. The number of people who can take a Higher Level Physics or Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches Higher Level candidate through an extended-response question in mark-scheme language is small, and advertised rates reflect it: Higher Level tracks are published nearer SAR 200 to 220 against about SAR 180 for general IB subject tuition. Because lessons are online, an Abha family pays the same scarcity premium a Riyadh family does, without the travel loading a visiting specialist in 'Asir would have to charge.

faqs.question: Is a small group class ever better value than one-to-one for an 'Asir family?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it depends on what is broken. A group works where several students share one content gap and the teaching is exposition: a topic nobody was taught properly, or examination technique for a common paper. It does not work for Internal Assessment feedback, for a student whose problem is specific to their own written answers, or where the shared timetable cannot survive an 'Asir school run. In practice most Abha enquiries are individual gaps in individual papers, which is the case one-to-one exists for.

faqs.question: Do we pay per lesson or per block, and what happens to a lesson lost to weather on the Soudah road?
faqs.answer: Blocks of hours are the normal arrangement, with a review at the end of each, because a block lets the tutor plan beyond the next session and lets you measure progress against a baseline. On lost lessons, online delivery removes most of the risk: a wet week on the escarpment closes roads, not connections, so a fixed online slot usually runs when a drive would not. Where a session genuinely cannot happen, it is rescheduled rather than written off, and the notice arrangements are agreed before the block starts.

faqs.question: Does the hourly rate change in the weeks before the June series for an Abha student?
faqs.answer: Rates advertised close to a series tend to reflect demand rather than any change in teaching quality, and the scarce subjects move most: Higher Level sciences and mathematics fill first. The practical consequence for an 'Asir family is not mainly financial. It is choice. A block agreed in the autumn term is priced more calmly and gives you a real selection of tutors; the same block agreed eight weeks out usually means taking whoever is still free in your window. Book the calendar early even if the hours start light.

abha.closingHeading: What to send us from Abha
abha.closingBody: One message does it: the board, the syllabus code, the level, the year group and the two or three windows that genuinely work after your district's school run. We will propose a named tutor who teaches that syllabus, set up a free trial lesson with that person, and write a baseline from marked work before any block of hours is agreed. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Arabia Standard Time, Sunday to Thursday, with Friday and Saturday blocks where a longer window helps. If no specialist is free in your subject and window, we will tell you that instead of sending a generalist.

affordable-ib-tutor.heroEyebrow: CHOOSING BETWEEN CHEAP, LOCAL AND RIGHT
affordable-ib-tutor.heroSubtitle: An affordable IB tutor in Saudi Arabia is rarely the one with the lowest hourly figure. It is the one whose lessons are still happening in the eighth month. Budget platforms advertise IGCSE one-to-one from around SAR 35 an hour, while a Higher Level specialist is listed at four or five times that, and the gap between those two numbers hides a decision rather than a bargain. Below are the five ways a Saudi family can buy IB help, what each costs in lost sessions as well as in SAR, and which suits which situation. Teaching is one-to-one, live online, Sunday to Thursday.

affordable-ib-tutor.tutorsIntro: Every tutor below names the syllabus and level they teach rather than the subject in general, because that distinction is the whole difference between a cheap hour and a wasted one. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Saudi local time.

intro.heading: The decision is not cheap against expensive - it is five different products
paragraphs: Parents searching for affordable IB help in the Kingdom are usually weighing five quite different things against each other without anyone having laid them side by side. There is the budget online platform advertising from around SAR 35 an hour. There is the local generalist who will come to a Riyadh or Jeddah address and charge senior-school rates for a subject they have not taught at Higher Level. There is the school's own after-school support, which is free and often excellent but limited to the subjects the school can staff. There is a shared group class. And there is a subject specialist teaching one-to-one over live video, which is what this page is about.

These are not five price points on one product. They are five products, and the reason families feel misled afterwards is that they compared the hourly figures as though they were buying the same thing. A platform tutor at the bottom of the band may be excellent for a Year 9 student consolidating algebra and completely wrong for a DP2 student whose Chemistry Paper 2 extended responses are collapsing. The school's after-school club cannot help with the one subject the school could not recruit for, which is precisely the subject most families are looking for.

The second thing nobody prices is attrition. A lesson that does not happen has no hourly rate at all, and the main cause of lessons not happening in Saudi Arabia is a calendar mismatch rather than a lack of goodwill. The school week here runs Sunday to Thursday with Friday and Saturday as the weekend. Most of the countries where IB and IGCSE specialists live run Monday to Friday with a Saturday and Sunday weekend. A tutor's free day and a Saudi student's free evening are therefore often in different parts of the week, and an arrangement that ignores this loses sessions steadily from about the sixth week onward.

Work out what one lost lesson a month actually costs and the arithmetic stops being abstract. Over a thirty-week course that is roughly seven missing sessions out of thirty, which is close to a quarter of the teaching gone - and the sessions lost are rarely random. They go in the weeks when school pressure is highest, which is when teaching is most valuable. A slightly dearer tutor whose own working week overlaps a Saudi evening properly delivers all thirty. That is the real comparison, and almost nobody in this market writes it down.

So the recommendation at the end of this page is not 'buy the expensive one'. It is narrower than that: identify the single component that is costing marks, decide whether the problem is diagnostic or just needs volume, choose the cheapest option that can actually solve that specific problem, and fix the slot in Saudi local time before you fix the tutor. Four of the five options are sometimes correct. IB Gram delivers its part of that as one-to-one teaching over live video; we do not send a tutor to a Saudi address, because home visits in the Kingdom are not a service we run - that is something we offer only in India.

affordable-ib-tutor.programmesIntro: Which programme a student is in decides how much of the problem a cheaper tutor can solve. These are the IB programmes running in Saudi international schools, with what each one asks of a tutor and where the local pool thins out.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects with three normally at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. A large share of most subject grades is produced as internal assessment across two years rather than in an examination hall. This is the stage where a generalist stops being useful: the Higher Level extension topics in the sciences and in Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches are taught by a much smaller group of people than the Standard Level courses underneath them.
programmes.countryNote: Saudi Diploma candidates sit the May session, which concentrates demand into the autumn and spring terms and makes a cheap but unreliable arrangement most likely to fail exactly when it matters. The practical constraint in smaller cities is not price - it is that a Higher Level specialist in a scarce subject is often not resident anywhere nearby.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Each subject is marked against four criteria with published descriptors, and the Personal Project runs in the final year of the programme. Students lose marks by writing well without writing to the descriptor, which is a teachable skill and one of the few places where a cheaper, less specialised tutor genuinely does the job. The exception is mathematics, where a gap left here becomes expensive two years later.
programmes.countryNote: MYP support is the best-value money a Saudi family spends, because the tutor pool at this level is wide and the rates sit near general senior-school figures. Schools in the Kingdom run the MYP more widely than the Diploma, so some families discover only in Year 11 that their school cannot offer the Higher Level subject their child wants.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led and transdisciplinary, with no external examinations, so support here is about reading stamina, written sentence structure, number fluency and the habit of explaining reasoning out loud. Short and frequent beats long and occasional. A tutor at this stage does not need subject specialism, which makes the cheapest sensible option usually the right one.
programmes.countryNote: Primary slots are the easiest to fill in the Kingdom because the child is home by mid-afternoon, which opens hours a Diploma student does not have. That flexibility means a family can often take a tutor whose own working day ends early, and the weekend mismatch matters much less than it does at Diploma level.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: A career-related study combined with at least two Diploma courses, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. Only a small number of international schools offer it, so a family choosing the CP has usually chosen a particular school first. Paid help is normally for the Diploma courses inside it, plus deadline structure for the reflective project.
programmes.countryNote: Because CP cohorts in the Kingdom are small, almost nobody locally has taught the specific combination a given student is doing. Online delivery is not a preference here but the only practical route, and families comparing it against a local option are usually comparing it against nothing.

affordable-ib-tutor.subjectsIntro: Price follows scarcity, and scarcity follows which subjects are hardest to staff. These are the courses Saudi families most often need outside help with, named by the component where the marks actually go.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The Higher Level extension has no Standard Level counterpart, so a tutor who taught SL well can still be out of their depth. Marks vanish in extended responses where the student narrates an effect instead of deriving it, and in questions that assume comfortable algebraic rearrangement. The hardest subject in the Kingdom to staff locally outside Riyadh and the Eastern Province.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics are the recurring trouble spots, and the data booklet is a skill rather than a reference. Equilibrium is the topic most often rushed at the end of the course because it sits late in most schemes of work. The internal assessment ceiling is set by the research question long before any data exists.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof, complex numbers and vectors sit on top of an already full core at Higher Level, and Paper 3 asks for sustained investigative reasoning rather than recall. Students who arrive with weak MYP algebra lose marks on manipulation rather than on concepts, which is diagnosable in one lesson and slow to fix.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content-heavy, and examined with unusual strictness on command terms: outline, describe, explain and discuss each carry different expectations and students answer all four the same way. Statistical handling in the internal assessment is where a general science teacher runs out of ground and a specialist earns the difference.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy decides the grade more than prose quality does. A correctly labelled and correctly shifted diagram is worth more than a fluent paragraph without one, and the Higher Level quantitative paper punishes students who treated the subject as essay-based. Commentaries need a current article tied tightly to one syllabus concept.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Rarely staffed deeply in Saudi schools, which makes it one of the scarcest subjects in this market. Paper 1 rewards precision about abstract data structures that students have only met in code, and the internal assessment needs a client, a documented development cycle and evidence of testing rather than a working program.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: The source paper is a technique examination disguised as a content one: provenance, purpose and value have to be used rather than named. Higher Level adds depth-study essays where students who know the material still score mid-band for answering around the question rather than inside it.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Most needed by students arriving from a national-curriculum or American school. The guided analysis rewards close reading of an unseen passage under time pressure, and the individual oral needs a global issue that can be sustained for the full ten minutes. Responds quickly to a short block of focused lessons.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: Often chosen as a lighter science and then found to be a systems-thinking course with its own vocabulary. Marks go on questions asking students to evaluate a management strategy, where a list of advantages scores far below a weighed judgement. Few local tutors have taught it specifically.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Cheap points left on the table. Both the exhibition and the essay reward precision about knowledge claims rather than general cleverness, and the matrix with the Extended Essay shifts the Diploma total. Two or three sessions on the prescribed title is a small outlay against the points involved.

affordable-ib-tutor.regionsTitle: Where the cheap option exists and where it does not
affordable-ib-tutor.regionsIntro: The hourly bands advertised in the Kingdom are broadly national. What is not national is whether a family has any local alternative at all, and that is what decides whether price is even the right question.

regions.name: Riyadh
regions.note: The one Saudi market with genuine local choice at Diploma level, which is why the cheap-against-right decision is sharpest here. It is also the market where a low quoted rate most often means a generalist charging senior-school prices for a Higher Level course they have never taught.

regions.name: Jeddah and the western coast
regions.note: British, IB, German, American and Indian curricula operate in the same city, so a tutor who is cheap and available may be fluent in the wrong one. Families along the northern spine towards Obhur also lose an evening to the commute if they choose somebody who has to travel.

regions.name: Dhahran, Al Khobar and Dammam
regions.note: A single school and labour market where families live in one city and attend school in another. The local pool is real at Standard Level and thin at Higher Level, so the saving from going local usually disappears into a subject mismatch.

regions.name: Makkah and Taif
regions.note: Makkah sits roughly 80km east of Jeddah and its calendar bends around the Hajj and Umrah seasons, which affects when intensive blocks are workable. The international-school options are fewer than on the coast, so scarce Diploma subjects are rarely covered locally at any price.

regions.name: Madinah and Yanbu
regions.note: Industrial and regional centres where the school choice is small and a Higher Level science specialist is unlikely to be resident. For these families the comparison is not a cheap tutor against a dear one but a qualified tutor against none, which changes what affordable means.

regions.name: Buraidah and Ha'il
regions.note: Al-Qassim and the north, where distance from the central markets is the binding constraint. Families here who insist on a local face often end up funding travel time inside the hourly rate, which is the most expensive way to buy a cheap tutor.

regions.name: Najran and Jazan
regions.note: The far south, with the longest journeys to any deep tutor pool in the Kingdom. Group classes are sometimes the only locally available format, which works for drill and fails for anything criterion-referenced like an internal assessment draft.

regions.name: NEOM, Tabuk and AlUla
regions.note: The north-west, where families frequently arrive part-way through a course because of work. Catching up mid-Diploma is the most expensive scenario in this market, and the one where waiting for a local option to appear costs more than the lessons would have.

schoolClusters.note: More than one IB programme runs at several schools here, and families choose between schools rather than between cities. The subject a school cannot recruit for is the usual reason a paid tutor enters the picture, and it is worth asking about before enrolment rather than in Year 11.

The International Schools Group runs several campuses across the conurbation, and the Diploma is offered at some of them rather than all. A move within the cluster can therefore change a child's curriculum, which is the detail families most often miss when relocating inside the Kingdom.

Several curricula sit within a short drive of each other and term structures differ school by school, so advice about when to start support has to come from the family's own school calendar rather than from a city-wide assumption.

affordable-ib-tutor.modesIntro: The format is the cheapest lever a family has. Same tutor, same hour, very different totals depending on how the time is bought.

modes.title: Paired sessions for two students on the same course
modes.description: Two students sitting the same syllabus at the same level, within a grade of each other, can share an hour and halve the cost each with very little loss. Siblings in the same year group and two classmates in the same Higher Level subject are the usual pairs. It breaks down the moment the levels differ, because one of them is then being taught the wrong course for part of the hour.

modes.title: Single-component block
modes.description: Six to eight lessons aimed at one named thing: the Physics extended-response questions, the Economics diagrams, the History source paper. The target is agreed before the first lesson and tested with the same style of question at the end. For families who want to spend as little as possible while still finding out whether tutoring helps, this is the honest shape.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one on a protected evening
modes.description: The standing arrangement, pinned to a Sunday-to-Thursday evening in Saudi local time so it survives a tutor's own clock change elsewhere. Costs more per term than a block and less per unit of progress over a two-year course, because the tutor stops re-diagnosing the student every month and starts building on what came before.

modes.title: Draft review timed to school deadlines
modes.description: Sessions scheduled around the school's own internal assessment or Extended Essay draft dates rather than weekly. The tutor reads what the student has written, marks it against the published criteria, and the student makes every change. A tutor may not write, draft or produce any part of assessed work, and a provider offering that is selling a malpractice case rather than a grade.

sections.heading: Five ways to buy IB help in the Kingdom, laid side by side
paragraphs: Put the options in one table and the decision usually makes itself. The budget online platform is the cheapest hour available and the most variable; what you get at the bottom of its band is typically an early-career tutor, a short introductory block, or a session with more than one student on the screen. The local generalist is the most reassuring and the most frequently mismatched, because the subject a Saudi family needs at Higher Level is rarely the subject the available local tutor has taught at Higher Level.

The school's own after-school support is free, delivered by someone who knows the scheme of work, and limited in exactly the way that matters: it cannot cover a subject the school could not recruit for. That is worth saying plainly, because it is the commonest reason a family starts looking outside in the first place. A shared group class is good value for volume and poor value for diagnosis, since no tutor can find and fix one student's specific algebra gap while four others wait.

The online subject specialist is the dearest per hour and the only option whose availability is not limited by who happens to live within driving distance. For a family in Jazan, Yanbu or Tabuk that is not a marginal advantage; it is the difference between the right tutor and no tutor. The sensible way to read the table below is to find your situation in the last column first and then look left at what it costs, rather than starting from the price and working towards a justification.

sections.heading: What affordable means once cancelled lessons are counted
paragraphs: An hourly rate describes a lesson that happens. The useful figure is cost per unit of progress across a term, and that depends on attrition. Picture two arrangements over a thirty-week course: one at a low rate that loses a session a month, one slightly dearer that loses none. The low-rate arrangement delivers around twenty-three lessons instead of thirty. Even before the quality question, it has lost close to a quarter of its teaching, and it has lost it in the weeks when school pressure peaked - which is exactly when the sessions were worth most.

Attrition is predictable, which means it is avoidable. The causes repeat: a slot that sits outside the tutor's own working day, so cancellations arrive from their side; a slot on a Thursday evening, which is the start of the Saudi weekend and the most reliably abandoned hour in the week; a tutor whose country changes its clocks while the Kingdom does not, so an agreed time quietly shifts by an hour twice a year; and a subject mismatch, which produces the slowest kind of loss because the lessons continue while the marks do not move.

The fix costs nothing. Agree the hour in Saudi local time rather than the tutor's. Ask whether that hour is inside their normal working day and on a day they normally teach. Take a Sunday-to-Wednesday evening for the standing lesson and keep Thursday and the weekend for blocks and draft reviews. Then count delivered lessons at the end of the first eight weeks rather than counting the hourly rate at the start. A family that does those four things will usually find the cheaper option has become genuinely cheaper, because it is no longer leaking sessions.

sections.heading: Which day is free for whom: the weekend mismatch nobody prices
paragraphs: Saudi families rest on Friday and Saturday. Most of the world's IB and IGCSE specialists rest on Saturday and Sunday. That single difference decides which evenings a given tutor can hold reliably, and it is almost never discussed before money changes hands. A full-time teacher in the United Kingdom has a free Sunday, which is a school night in the Kingdom - excellent for a Saudi student's Sunday evening and awkward for Thursday, which is mid-week for them. A tutor who works a Monday-to-Saturday week, as much of the Indian sector does, has the opposite profile.

The clock matters too, but less than the calendar. Arabia Standard Time is UTC+3 and the Kingdom does not observe daylight saving, so a slot agreed in the tutor's own local time will move by an hour twice a year if their country changes its clocks. India sits two and a half hours ahead, so an early-evening Saudi lesson is comfortable for them and a late one is not. A tutor on the North American east coast is seven or eight hours behind, which makes a Saudi weekday evening their early morning - not a sustainable weekly commitment at any price.

Use the table as a shortlist filter before you discuss rates. If a tutor's weekend and working hours cannot cover the two or three evenings your family can genuinely protect, their hourly figure is irrelevant. If they can, the conversation about price starts from a position where the lessons will actually take place, which is the only basis on which cheap and dear can be compared at all.

sections.heading: The subjects Saudi schools most often cannot staff, and why that sets the floor
paragraphs: A low advertised rate is only a bargain if somebody at that rate can teach the course. The reason scarce subjects cost more everywhere is that the pool of people who have actually taught the Higher Level extension is small, and it does not expand when a school's timetable needs it to. Private and international schools in the Kingdom are licensed by the Ministry of Education, with school evaluation running through the Education and Training Evaluation Commission, and neither of those processes can conjure a Physics HL teacher into a city that has none.

What happens instead is familiar to any family that has been through it. A school offers the Diploma but runs only Standard Level in a subject; or offers the subject at Higher Level with a teacher covering it outside their specialism; or offers it online through a third party. None of those is a scandal, and schools are usually candid about it if asked directly. The problem is that families ask after enrolling rather than before, and then look for the cheapest tutor to patch a gap that needed a specialist from the start.

The table below is the question to put to a prospective school, and the reason the market prices some subjects well above others. Read it as a budgeting document: if your child's intended Higher Level combination includes two of the scarce rows, the realistic plan involves an outside specialist from DP1 rather than a rescue in DP2, and the cheapest version of that plan is the early one.

sections.heading: Where the marks actually go, subject by subject
paragraphs: Buying an hour of general subject help is the most common way to waste money in this market. Marks are lost in specific, diagnosable places, and naming the place turns a vague purchase into a short, cheap, targeted block. In Physics it is the extended response where a student describes rather than derives. In Biology it is the command terms: outline, describe, explain and discuss each have a different expectation and most students answer all four identically. In Economics it is the diagram - unlabelled, or labelled but not shifted.

In Chemistry the two recurring places are organic mechanisms and the use of the data booklet, with equilibrium a close third because it usually sits late in the scheme of work and gets rushed. In Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches the loss is rarely conceptual; it is algebraic manipulation carried forward from the MYP, which shows up as arithmetic slips in questions the student understood perfectly. In History it is provenance used as a label rather than as an argument. In English it is time management on the guided analysis.

Every one of those is a six-to-eight lesson problem rather than a two-year problem, which is why an affordable plan usually looks like two short blocks in different terms rather than a standing weekly commitment. The way to find your row in the table is to take the last three pieces of marked work and read the examiner's or teacher's comments rather than the grade. The comments name the component; the grade only names the symptom.

sections.heading: Academic honesty: the cheapest mistake a family can avoid
paragraphs: Some providers in this market will offer to produce assessed work. It is the one purchase in this whole decision that can cost a student their Diploma, so it belongs in a page about affordability. A tutor may not write, draft or produce an Internal Assessment, an Extended Essay, a Theory of Knowledge essay or a Personal Project - not a section, not a model version, not a rewritten paragraph that reappears in the submission. Schools are required to be satisfied the work is the student's own, and authentication procedures exist precisely to test that.

What a tutor may legitimately do covers almost everything a family actually wants. They can teach the skills the component assesses, explain what each criterion strand is asking for in plain language, suggest methods or sources worth investigating, read a draft the student has written and say where it falls short of the descriptor, and ask the questions that turn an unworkable research question into a workable one. The student then makes every change themselves. That boundary is the difference between feedback and production, and a tutor worth paying states it in the first session without being asked.

There is a practical defence as well as an ethical one. Keep the drafts. A dated sequence of the student's own versions, with the feedback they received and the changes they then made, is the clearest possible answer if authorship is ever questioned. It costs nothing, it takes a shared folder, and it protects a student against a suspicion that is far more expensive to rebut after the fact than to prevent.
