sections.heading: Four levers that cut the bill without cutting the value
paragraphs: The first lever is timing. Support bought in the autumn term of DP1 costs a fraction of the same gap addressed in the spring term of DP2, because the problem is smaller and the slots are available. The same logic applies a stage earlier: two terms of MYP mathematics is the cheapest intervention in the entire sequence, and skipping it is what produces Higher Level repair work later at the highest rates in the market.

The second is narrowing the target. One component, named in advance, measured with a past paper at the end. The third is pairing: two students on the same board, the same subject and the same level, within about a grade of each other, sharing one hour. That nearly halves the cost per student and loses very little, as long as nobody tries to pair a Standard Level student with a Higher Level one. The fourth is format discipline - using one-to-one for diagnosis and for draft feedback, and a shared session for drill and discussion, rather than paying individual rates for volume work.

What does not work as a saving: a cheaper tutor who has not taught the level, because the lessons continue while the marks do not move and you discover it a term later; a longer package bought up front for a discount, before anyone knows whether the match is right; and dropping to a group for internal assessment feedback, which is individual by nature. The honest version of affordable is a smaller, earlier, better-aimed purchase rather than a cheaper hour.

sections.heading: What to ask before you agree a lower rate
paragraphs: A low quote is information, not a conclusion. Four questions tell you whether it is a bargain or a mismatch. Which syllabus and which level have you taught, and for how long? Which component do you think is costing this student marks, and what in the trial lesson made you think so? Which day and hour are you offering in Saudi local time, and is that inside your own normal working day? And what will you not be able to fix this term?

The fourth question is the most diagnostic. Everybody can answer the first three plausibly. A tutor who says plainly that two years of missing algebra will not close in eight weeks, or that an internal assessment already submitted cannot be improved, is a tutor who will tell you the truth later when it is inconvenient. A tutor who says everything is fixable has told you what they think you want to hear, which is a poor foundation for a thirty-week arrangement at any rate.

On the commercial side, settle four things before the first invoice: what happens to a missed lesson, how much notice a reschedule needs, whether marking written work between sessions is inside the fee, and whether the slot is held during a long break. Then take the free trial lesson, which comes before any fee is agreed, and judge it on whether it produced a diagnosis you can read rather than a recommended package. If the match is wrong after two or three lessons, changing tutor should cost nothing beyond the lessons taken.
bullets: Which syllabus and level, taught for how long - not which subject
Which component is leaking marks, and what in the trial showed it
Which hour, in Saudi local time, and is it inside their working day
What will not close this term - the answer reveals the tutor

sections.heading: The recommendation, stated as plainly as the question deserves
paragraphs: For a primary or lower-MYP student, take the cheapest sensible option. Subject specialism is not the constraint at that stage; consistency and frequency are. A platform tutor or a local generalist on two short weekly sessions does the job, and the slot is easy to fill because the child is home in the afternoon. Spending Diploma-level money here is the most common unnecessary purchase in this market.

For an IGCSE student, start with the school. Ask which tier the child is entered for and confirm it in writing, because Cambridge IGCSE is tiered on many subjects - Core is graded C to G and Extended A* to E, and a Core entry caps the award at a C however well the paper goes. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE grades 9 to 1. Tier entry is a school decision and reversible only before the entry deadline. Once the tier is right, a single-component block aimed at the paper that is losing marks is usually enough, and it is cheap.

For a Diploma student, the recommendation is narrower and it is the reason this page exists. Buy a specialist for the Higher Level subject the school cannot staff deeply, buy them in DP1 rather than DP2, protect a Sunday-to-Wednesday evening in Saudi local time, and use short blocks for the other subjects as specific components fail. That combination is usually cheaper over two years than a rolling arrangement with a generalist, and far cheaper than a rescue in the final terms. Lessons from IB Gram are delivered one-to-one over live video anywhere in the Kingdom; we do not place tutors at Saudi addresses, and the free trial lesson comes first.

process.title: Read the last three pieces of marked work
process.description: Not the grades - the comments. Teachers and examiners name the component: the derivation, the command term, the diagram, the timing. That name is what turns an open-ended purchase into a six-lesson block with a measurable end, and it costs nothing to find. Bring it to the trial lesson.

process.title: Decide whether the problem needs diagnosis or volume
process.description: Diagnosis means nobody yet knows which topics are costing marks, and that needs one-to-one. Volume means the student knows what to do and has not done enough of it, and that can be shared or grouped. Getting this one judgement right is the single biggest saving available to a Saudi family.

process.title: Protect the evenings before you choose anybody
process.description: Work out which Sunday-to-Thursday evenings genuinely survive your family's week and treat them as fixed. Then look for a tutor whose own working week covers them. Choosing the tutor first and hunting for a slot afterwards is how arrangements quietly collapse around the sixth week.

process.title: Take the free trial and judge the diagnosis
process.description: No fee is agreed beforehand. The trial should end with a named component, a plan for the first block and a measure you can re-run later. A trial that ends with a package recommendation and no diagnosis has answered a different question than the one you asked.

process.title: Count delivered lessons at eight weeks
process.description: Re-run the measure and count how many of the scheduled sessions actually happened. Two numbers, five minutes. They tell you whether the arrangement is working and whether it is really as cheap as it looked. Continuing, switching tutor and stopping are all reasonable answers at that point.

whyPoints.title: The options are compared, not just ours
whyPoints.description: Four of the five ways to buy IB help in the Kingdom are sometimes the right answer, including the school's own free support and a shared group class. Saying so costs us some enquiries and saves families money, which is a better trade than the alternative of pretending one hour suits every situation.

whyPoints.title: Scarcity is named rather than implied
whyPoints.description: Physics HL, Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL, Computer Science and the specialist language courses are the subjects Saudi schools most often cannot staff deeply. That is why they cost more, everywhere, from everyone. Knowing which rows apply to your child's combination is the difference between a budget and a surprise.

whyPoints.title: The slot is treated as part of the price
whyPoints.description: An hour agreed in Saudi local time, on a day inside the tutor's own working week, delivers thirty sessions out of thirty. An hour agreed loosely leaks a session a month, which is close to a quarter of a course. The slot is negotiated before the rate, because it determines whether the rate means anything.

whyPoints.title: The honesty line is drawn in the first session
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches the skill, explains the criteria and comments on a draft the student has written. Writing, redrafting or supplying any part of an internal assessment, Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge essay or Personal Project is malpractice, and we decline it. Keeping dated drafts is recommended as a defence, not as a formality.

whyPoints.title: Stopping is easy on purpose
whyPoints.description: The arrangement is per lesson, the slot belongs to the family rather than the tutor, and changing tutor after two or three lessons costs nothing beyond those lessons. Nobody is asked to buy a long package before knowing whether the match works, because that is the purchase families most often regret in this market.

faqs.question: What may a tutor do with a Chemistry internal assessment draft, and what would cross into malpractice?
faqs.answer: They may teach the skills the task assesses, explain what each criterion strand rewards, discuss whether a research question is narrow enough to produce usable data, and read a draft the student has written and say where it falls short of the descriptor. They may not design the investigation, supply text, rewrite a discussion section, or process the data for the student. The practical test is simple: if any sentence or decision in the submitted work originated with the tutor rather than the student, it has crossed the line. Keeping dated drafts makes the distinction easy to demonstrate later.

faqs.question: How many drafts of an Extended Essay can a paid tutor legitimately read?
faqs.answer: There is no fixed number, because the limit is on what the tutor does rather than on how often they do it. The school's supervisor has a formal role with a defined number of reflection sessions, and that structure belongs to the school. An outside tutor reading additional drafts is acceptable as long as every comment is feedback on the student's own text and every change is made by the student. What makes the number feel high is usually the wrong kind of help: if each round involves the tutor reshaping prose, one round was already too many.

faqs.question: Is proofreading an internal assessment allowed if the tutor changes nothing themselves?
faqs.answer: Pointing out that a section is unclear, that a term is used inconsistently, or that a conclusion does not follow from the data is legitimate feedback and the student then fixes it. Working through the document correcting grammar and phrasing is not, even if the tutor types nothing into the file, because the resulting text reflects the tutor's judgement rather than the student's. The safe form is to name the problem and its location and let the student solve it. Schools and the IB's authentication requirements both treat the origin of the writing as the question that matters.

faqs.question: Who supervises the MYP Personal Project, and can a cheaper tutor take that role?
faqs.answer: Supervision belongs to the school and cannot be bought. A school-appointed supervisor meets the student, monitors the process journal and confirms the work is their own. An outside tutor cannot take that role and should not offer to. What a tutor can usefully do is teach planning technique, help the student set a goal that is actually achievable in the time available, and discuss how to keep a process journal that records decisions rather than activities. Contributing to the product itself, or writing journal entries, would be malpractice regardless of what it costs.

faqs.question: How do we keep a record showing the internal assessment is our child's own work?
faqs.answer: Use a dated folder and keep every version. A sequence of the student's own drafts, each one later than the last, with the feedback received between them and the changes that followed, is the clearest evidence there is. Keep raw data files, lab notes, search histories for sources and any photographs of apparatus. None of this takes extra work if it is done as you go, and it turns a potential dispute into a two-minute conversation. Families who assemble it afterwards find it far harder, because the natural traces of the work have already been overwritten.

faqs.question: Does a Theory of Knowledge essay follow the same honesty rules as a subject internal assessment?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the temptation is greater because the essay is argumentative rather than technical, so a supplied structure looks less like cheating than supplied data does. It is not less. The student selects the prescribed title and builds the argument; a tutor may clarify what a knowledge claim is, probe whether an example genuinely supports the claim, and point out where reasoning jumps. Handing over an argument outline the student then writes up would be producing the work. The practical safeguard is the same: keep the drafts, and make sure the thinking visible in them is the student's.

faqs.question: Which Physics HL topics have no Standard Level equivalent, and does that change who we should pay?
faqs.answer: The Higher Level extension material is additional rather than deeper versions of the same content, which is why a tutor who taught Standard Level competently can still be unable to help. It changes who you should pay more than how much: ask directly whether the tutor has taught the HL extension and marked HL scripts, not whether they have taught Physics. In the Kingdom this is the subject where that question matters most, because schools outside Riyadh and the Eastern Province frequently cannot staff HL Physics deeply and cover it with a general science teacher instead.

faqs.question: Why do strong Biology students still lose marks on the command terms?
faqs.answer: Because Biology rewards knowing the content and pays only for presenting it in the form the command demands. Outline, describe, explain and discuss each expect a different structure and a different depth, and a student who knows the topic will often write a full description where an explanation was asked for and score about half. The fix is unusually cheap: take past answers the student has already written, identify the command in each question, and rewrite to the command rather than to the topic. Six to eight sessions on this typically moves more marks than the same hours spent on new content.

faqs.question: Where does weak algebra from the MYP show up later in Diploma Economics?
faqs.answer: In the Higher Level quantitative paper and in anything involving elasticity, revenue, cost curves or market calculations under time pressure. Students who chose Economics expecting an essay subject meet arithmetic they last practised in Year 9, and the loss looks like carelessness rather than a gap. It shows up as correct method with a dropped sign, a misplaced decimal, or a percentage change calculated the wrong way round. Targeted manipulation practice rather than more Economics content is the efficient repair, which makes it a short block instead of a term.

faqs.question: What does an Economics examiner want in a diagram that a fluent paragraph cannot replace?
faqs.answer: Axes labelled with the correct variables, curves labelled, the initial and new positions both shown, the shift drawn in the right direction, and the areas or points the argument refers to actually marked on the figure. A paragraph can describe all of that and still not earn the diagram marks, because those marks are allocated to the figure. Students who write well are the most likely to lose them, since they trust the prose to carry the point. Drilling diagrams against a fixed checklist is one of the fastest mark gains available in the subject.

faqs.question: Which Chemistry topic is most often rushed at the end of the Diploma course?
faqs.answer: Equilibrium, with acids and bases close behind, because both sit late in most schemes of work and arrive when internal assessment deadlines are competing for the student's attention. The result is a topic covered at speed and never consolidated, which then appears in papers the student otherwise handles well. Families who know this in advance plan a short block for it rather than discovering the gap in a mock. The same pattern applies to the later organic chemistry material, where mechanism steps get memorised rather than understood.

faqs.question: Which Diploma subjects do Saudi international schools most often fail to staff deeply?
faqs.answer: Higher Level Physics, Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, Computer Science, the specialist language A courses, and anything with a small cohort such as Further Mathematics. Schools respond reasonably - offering the subject at Standard Level only, assigning a teacher from an adjacent specialism, or arranging a third-party online course. None of that is hidden, but it is rarely volunteered either. Ask the question before enrolment, subject by subject, for the combination your child intends to take, and ask who has taught the Higher Level extension rather than the subject.

faqs.question: What happens when an Eastern Province school cannot run a Higher Level subject a student needs?
faqs.answer: The common outcomes are a switch to Standard Level, a move to another school within the Dammam, Al Khobar and Dhahran cluster, or an outside arrangement alongside the school timetable. The cluster behaves as one school market and families routinely live in one city and attend in another, so a move is more practical here than almost anywhere else in the Kingdom. The International Schools Group runs several campuses and the Diploma is offered at some rather than all of them, so check programme availability campus by campus rather than assuming the group is uniform.

faqs.question: How do compound and campus schools in the Kingdom differ from city schools for subject choice?
faqs.answer: Campus and compound schools serve a defined community, so cohorts are small and stable and the timetable is built around what that community needs. The upside is strong pastoral knowledge of each student. The limit is breadth: a small cohort cannot sustain six Higher Level options, so subject choice is narrower and an unusual combination may not run at all. Families in these settings are the most frequent users of outside teaching, not because the schooling is weaker but because a small school cannot offer everything a particular student's plan requires.

faqs.question: What should a family ask a Saudi school about subject availability before enrolling?
faqs.answer: Five questions. Which IB programmes do you run, and to which year group? For the combination we intend, which subjects are available at Higher Level rather than Standard Level only? Who teaches each of those, and have they taught the Higher Level extension before? If a subject does not run this year because the cohort is too small, what happens? And how does your term calendar compare with the Ministry of Education school year? Ask in writing, keep the answers, and ask again before subject choices are locked in rather than after.

faqs.question: Does the Education and Training Evaluation Commission assess a private tutor as well as a school?
faqs.answer: No. Private and international schools in the Kingdom are licensed by the Ministry of Education, and school evaluation and accreditation runs through the Education and Training Evaluation Commission, which also operates e-services covering national school accreditation and the approval of international accreditation bodies. None of that extends to individual tutors, and no tutoring provider holds a regulator's endorsement. What a family can verify instead is concrete: which syllabus and level the tutor has taught, for how long, and whether they have marked for the board.

affordable-ib-tutor.closingHeading: Affordable means the smallest purchase that solves the actual problem
affordable-ib-tutor.closingBody: Name the component, decide whether it needs diagnosis or volume, choose the cheapest option that can genuinely handle that, and protect a Sunday-to-Wednesday evening in Saudi local time before you choose a person. For a primary student the cheap option is usually right. For an IGCSE student, the tier conversation with the school comes first and costs nothing. For a Diploma student in a subject the school cannot staff deeply, an early specialist is the cheaper plan even though the hour costs more. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, and the free trial comes before any fee.

al-ahsa.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB Diploma and Middle Years subjects and Cambridge or Edexcel IGCSE to students across the oasis. Each one works to a named syllabus and level rather than to a year group, so a Chemistry HL student and an IGCSE Co-ordinated Sciences student are not handed the same person.

intro.heading: Why Al Ahsa families end up looking outside the oasis for subject teaching
paragraphs: Al Ahsa is the oasis governorate around Hofuf and Al Mubarraz, in the Eastern Province, and it is a UNESCO World Heritage site. It is also a working region: the Ghawar field sits beneath it, King Faisal University sits inside it, and the Aramco communities on its northern and western edges bring in professional families on two- and three-year postings. Those families arrive carrying a curriculum. Some arrive with a half-finished IB Diploma.

What they discover quickly is that Al Ahsa and the Dhahran-Khobar-Dammam conurbation are not one school market. The coastal cluster behaves as a single catchment, with families living in one town and driving to a school in another. The oasis does not join that circuit. An hour and a half each way is a three-hour daily commitment before any homework is opened, which rules out a daily international-school run for most households and pushes the real decision somewhere else: stay local for schooling, and buy the specialist teaching separately.

That is the honest shape of the problem on this page. It is not that Al Ahsa lacks schools or lacks good teachers. It is that a Higher Level Physics specialist, an examiner who has marked Economics Paper 3, or a Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics teacher is a thin slice of any teaching workforce, and a governorate of this size will have a handful at most across all of its schools combined. Whether one of them is free at seven in the evening on the day your child is free is a question of arithmetic, not ambition.

One-to-one lessons over live video change that arithmetic. The pool a Hofuf family can reach stops being the drivable radius and becomes everyone who teaches that syllabus and is awake at a workable hour on Arabia Standard Time. A family in Al Omran and a family in Al Khobar then face the same question, which is whether the tutor genuinely knows the paper, not whether they can get across the oasis by half past four.

Everything below is organised the way the week actually runs. The school day and the drive come first, because they decide which slots exist at all. The time zone comes next, because it decides which tutors can hold those slots week after week. Only then is it worth talking about who the tutor is, what the market charges, and how to check a claim before paying for it.

Lessons are delivered online, one to one, over live video. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a Saudi address; in-home visits are a service we run only in India, and we would rather say so plainly on this page than let a parent find out after booking.

al-ahsa.programmesIntro: Al Ahsa students sit a narrower range of international qualifications than Riyadh or Jeddah students do, and a good share of them transfer in part-way through. These four are the ones that come up, with what each one demands of a family in this governorate specifically.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP is inquiry-led and has no external examinations. Progress is reported against learning outcomes rather than paper marks, which is why parents moving from a national-curriculum primary often cannot tell whether their child is ahead or behind. Support at this stage is diagnostic rather than remedial: reading fluency, number sense, written explanation in English, and the habit of showing reasoning rather than only an answer.
programmes.countryNote: For an Al Ahsa family the PYP question is usually about continuity. A child who starts in an inquiry-led primary and then has to move into a Cambridge Lower Secondary or MoE stream locally meets a sharp change in how work is set and marked. Early one-to-one teaching here is mostly about building the written-explanation habit that both systems reward, so the transition does not cost a year.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP assesses against four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight, with command terms doing much of the work. The Personal Project in the final year is the first substantial independent piece most students produce. Marks are lost on criterion coverage rather than on content: a strong answer that never addresses criterion C still caps at a low band, and students rarely see that pattern without someone showing them.
programmes.countryNote: MYP provision thins out fast outside the main cities, so Al Ahsa students more often reach the end of Year 11 from a Cambridge Lower Secondary or MoE route and then step into the Diploma. If your child is in an MYP stream, the useful work is criterion literacy and Personal Project supervision support; if they are not, the useful work is closing the gap in independent written research before DP1 starts.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Higher Level carries more content and in several subjects an extra paper. The core contributes points through the TOK and Extended Essay matrix. Internal Assessment is a fixed share of most subject grades and is marked at school against published criteria before external moderation, which makes it the most controllable component in the whole Diploma.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma students in Al Ahsa are often either boarding or commuting weekly to the coast, or studying at a school that runs the Diploma with one teacher per subject and no second specialist. Both situations produce the same request: a Higher Level specialist for one or two subjects, taught in the evening, with Internal Assessment feedback that does not depend on catching a teacher between lessons.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: Two boards, overlapping subject lists, different paper structures and different tiering rules. Cambridge offers Core and Extended tiers in several subjects; Edexcel uses a Foundation and Higher split in its own. Grading runs 9 to 1 on the reformed international scale in some subjects and A* to G in others, depending on board and syllabus. The syllabus code on the entry form, not the subject name, is what a tutor must teach to.
programmes.countryNote: Al Ahsa families sit IGCSE both at private bilingual schools locally and as private candidates through a registered centre on the coast. Entries close months ahead of the June series, and a private candidate has to arrange a centre themselves. Cambridge and Edexcel both run a June and a November series for candidates here; your school's examinations officer holds the exact entry dates.

al-ahsa.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma and Middle Years subjects Al Ahsa families most often ask for, with the part of each course that actually costs marks. A tutor is matched to the subject and level on your child's timetable, including the specific Higher Level options where those exist.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The Higher Level course adds proof, complex numbers and a much heavier calculus load, and Paper 3 asks for extended reasoning rather than isolated technique. Most lost marks trace back to algebraic fluency from two years earlier: a student who still manipulates surds and rational functions slowly runs out of time before the thinking starts.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology use carry the course, and the graphic display calculator is assumed rather than optional. Students lose marks by reporting an answer the calculator produced without the interpretation the question asked for, and by treating statistical tests as recipes rather than as arguments about data.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Higher Level extends into further mechanics, induction and quantum topics with no Standard Level equivalent. The recurring problem is not the physics but the mathematics inside it: logarithmic scales, gradients with units, and uncertainty propagation in the internal investigation. Extended-response marks hang on definitions stated precisely.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms, equilibrium and energetics produce most of the difficulty, and the data booklet is a skill in its own right. Students who learn reactions as lists rather than as mechanisms stall the moment a paper asks them to predict an unfamiliar product. The internal investigation needs a measurable, sensibly scoped variable, chosen early.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The content volume is the trap. Command terms separate a four-mark answer from a seven-mark one, and students who revise by rereading notes rather than by writing to the mark scheme plateau. Statistical treatment of data in the internal investigation is where Higher Level candidates most often give away marks they had earned in the laboratory.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams are marked, not decorative: axes, labels and a shifted curve carry credit on their own. Paper 3 at Higher Level is quantitative and rewards method shown step by step. Evaluation is the component students most often skip under time pressure, and it is usually where the remaining marks sit.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The course rewards application to the stimulus rather than recall of a framework. Students quote a tool correctly and then never anchor it to the case, which caps the answer. Higher Level extension topics and the research project both need writing discipline more than extra content.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is an unseen guided analysis, and students lose marks by summarising rather than analysing how meaning is made. The Higher Level essay demands a sustained line of argument across a complete work. For students whose school teaching is in English but whose home language is not, the gap is usually in precise critical vocabulary.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Paper 1 and Paper 2 reward precise pseudocode and a clear grasp of data structures; the Higher Level case study adds an annually set topic that has to be researched properly rather than skimmed. The internal solution needs a client, a documented design and testing evidence, not just working code.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: TOK contributes points through the matrix with the Extended Essay, and both the exhibition and the essay are marked against published criteria. Students who treat it as an opinion piece score badly; the marks come from using specific knowledge claims and real examples, and from answering the prescribed title as written.

al-ahsa.igcseSubjectsIntro: IGCSE is the other half of the picture in Al Ahsa, taught locally at private bilingual schools and sat by private candidates through registered centres on the coast. These are the subjects families ask for most, by board where the boards differ materially.

igcseSubjects.name: Mathematics
igcseSubjects.levels: Cambridge Core and Extended · Edexcel Foundation and Higher
igcseSubjects.description: The tier decision matters more than any revision plan: a Core entry caps the available grade, and a student entered on the wrong tier cannot recover it in the examination hall. Most lost marks are method marks on multi-step questions where working was never written down.

igcseSubjects.name: Additional Mathematics
igcseSubjects.description: Taken alongside Extended Mathematics by students heading for Mathematics AA HL or A Level. It introduces calculus and more formal algebra early, and it is the single best preparation for the first term of the Diploma. Almost no school in the oasis staffs it as a separate class.

igcseSubjects.name: Combined and Co-ordinated Sciences
igcseSubjects.description: One or two grades covering biology, chemistry and physics content. Students who then move to Diploma sciences arrive with real gaps, especially in physics mathematics and organic chemistry, because the award compresses three subjects into less teaching time than separate sciences get.

igcseSubjects.name: Physics
igcseSubjects.description: Separate-science physics is the usual route into Physics HL. Marks are lost on unit handling, on graph work, and on the practical paper or alternative-to-practical, where candidates describe an experiment without a controlled variable or a measurable outcome.

igcseSubjects.name: Chemistry
igcseSubjects.description: Moles and stoichiometry decide the grade. A candidate who is slow with mole calculations loses marks across every paper rather than in one topic, and the qualitative analysis section rewards learned observations that cannot be reasoned out on the day.

igcseSubjects.name: Biology
igcseSubjects.description: High content volume with a heavy emphasis on precise terminology. Extended-response questions are marked against specific points, so a fluent paragraph that misses three of them scores less than a plain list that hits them all.

igcseSubjects.name: English as a Second Language
igcseSubjects.description: Distinct from First Language English in both demand and grading, and the choice between them has consequences for sixth-form and Diploma entry. The reading paper rewards exact lifting and rewording; the writing paper rewards register control more than vocabulary range.

igcseSubjects.name: Economics and Business Studies
igcseSubjects.description: Both reward structured evaluation and accurate diagram or calculation work. Students treat the data-response section as a comprehension exercise and lose the analysis marks, which is the difference between a mid and a top grade in most series.

al-ahsa.regionsTitle: The oasis, town by town, and what it means for a lesson slot
al-ahsa.regionsIntro: Al Ahsa is not one settlement but a ring of towns and villages around two urban centres. Where a family lives changes the school run, the evening traffic and therefore the hour at which a lesson can realistically start. These are the parts of the governorate that come up most.

regions.name: Hofuf
regions.note: The administrative and commercial centre, and where most private schooling in the governorate sits. Families here have the shortest school runs and the widest local choice, which usually means an early-evening lesson slot is comfortable rather than tight.

regions.name: Al Mubarraz
regions.note: The second urban centre, effectively continuous with Hofuf for daily purposes. School and work journeys cross between the two constantly, so a parent's return home, not the school bell, is often what decides whether a six o'clock lesson works.

regions.name: Al Oyun
regions.note: A northern oasis town with its own schools but little senior international provision. Students here who want Cambridge or Diploma subjects commute into Hofuf or study locally and buy the specialist subject teaching separately in the evenings.

regions.name: Al Omran
regions.note: East of the main centres, agricultural and residential. The journey into Hofuf is short but the return in late afternoon is slow, which tends to push a workable weekday slot past six o'clock rather than into the school-run window.

regions.name: Al Battaliyah and Al Taraf
regions.note: Village settlements inside the palm belt north of Hofuf, with primary and intermediate provision locally and senior schooling further in. The practical effect is that older students lose travel time daily and need lessons that start after the journey, not during it.

regions.name: Al Qarah
regions.note: On the eastern edge of the oasis near the Jabal Al Qarah caves, residential and semi-rural. Families here plan around one car and one driver more often than families in Hofuf do, so a fixed weekly slot is worth more to them than a flexible one.

regions.name: Abqaiq
regions.note: A company town on the governorate's northern side with its own residential community and a transient professional population. Children arrive and leave part-way through courses, which makes mid-course catch-up the normal case here rather than the exception.

regions.name: Udhailiyah
regions.note: A smaller inland community west of the oasis, well away from any school cluster. Distance is the whole constraint: there is no version of this journey that produces a daily international-school run, so online subject teaching is not a convenience but the only option.

regions.name: Haradh and the southern governorate
regions.note: Towns strung out south-west towards the Empty Quarter margin, where provision is national-curriculum and distances are long. Families here sit IGCSE as private candidates more often than anywhere else in the governorate.

schoolClusters.city: The Dhahran, Al Khobar, Dammam and Jubail cluster
schoolClusters.note: The closest concentration of international and British-curriculum schooling to the oasis, roughly an hour and a half from Hofuf. Families who want Diploma or full IGCSE provision locally either relocate into this cluster, board a child inside it, or commute weekly rather than daily.

schoolClusters.city: Riyadh, for families who relocate or board
schoolClusters.note: When a posting changes or a subject combination is not available in the Eastern Province, Riyadh is the usual destination. Its schools between them cover the Primary Years, Middle Years and Diploma Programmes, which makes a full IB route through to Year 13 more realistic there than anywhere nearer.

schoolClusters.city: Jeddah and Thuwal, for a transfer west
schoolClusters.note: Families moving across the Kingdom mid-course usually land in one of these, and the curriculum question reopens on arrival. A student can often keep the same board but almost never the same scheme of work, which is where a term of catch-up comes from.

al-ahsa.modesIntro: Four ways families in the governorate use one-to-one teaching. All of them run over live video on Arabia Standard Time; the difference is the shape of the commitment, not the delivery.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one, one subject
modes.description: The standard arrangement: a fixed slot each week in a single subject, held by the same tutor through the year. It works because it is boring. The tutor sees the same student often enough to spot a pattern, and the slot survives a school trip or a travel week because it is pinned to the calendar rather than negotiated each time.
bullets: Same tutor, same hour, same day of the week
Work set between lessons and marked before the next one
A short written note to the parent after each session
Slot held through a school holiday if the family asks

modes.title: Two subjects in one evening
modes.description: Common for Diploma students with two weak Higher Levels and one free evening. Two sessions back to back with different specialists is harder work than one, so it suits a student who is behind rather than one who is stuck, and it is usually a term-long arrangement rather than a permanent one.
bullets: Different specialist for each subject, never one generalist
A short break between the two sessions
Homework load agreed across both so it does not double
Reviewed at the end of each term and usually dropped back to one

modes.title: Internal Assessment and coursework review
modes.description: Short, intensive blocks around a draft deadline. The tutor reads the student's own work, explains what the published criteria reward, and shows where the argument or the data handling falls short. The student then rewrites it. The tutor does not produce any part of the submitted work, and says so to the student in those words.
bullets: Feedback against the criteria the school will mark against
Method and data-handling review before writing starts
Clear line between teaching and producing the work
A record of what was discussed, for the school if asked

modes.title: Pre-series intensive
modes.description: A block of sessions in the weeks before a series, built around past papers under timed conditions. It is the least useful mode for content gaps and the most useful for examination technique: question choice, timing, command terms, and the habit of writing what the mark scheme rewards rather than everything the student knows.
bullets: Whole papers under time, then marked against the real scheme
Question-by-question timing plan agreed with the student
Targeted at technique, not at teaching a syllabus from scratch
Runs around the school's own revision timetable, not against it

sections.heading: Where a lesson actually fits in an Al Ahsa week
paragraphs: The school week here runs Sunday to Thursday. Friday and Saturday are the weekend. That single fact invalidates most tutoring copy written for a Monday-to-Friday market, and it changes which evenings are worth anything. Thursday evening in Al Ahsa behaves like a Friday evening in London: nobody wants a lesson, and a student who agrees to one turns up having already left the week behind.

Sunday is the mirror image. It is the first day back, the day homework is set rather than due, and the day a student is most able to absorb teaching that will be useful for the rest of the week. Families who schedule their one weekly session on a Sunday or Monday evening get noticeably more out of it than families who leave it until Wednesday, and much more than families who put it on a Thursday because that was the slot that happened to be free.

The second constraint is the school run and the drive home. Local schooling in Hofuf and Al Mubarraz finishes in the early afternoon, but a parent coming back from the coast or from a plant site is often not home before six. Where the family runs one car, that return decides the start time, not the school bell. A slot agreed at five and quietly starting at ten past, every week, becomes a fifty-minute lesson that was paid for as an hour.

The third is Ramadan, which drifts across the academic year because it moves roughly eleven days earlier each year against the Gregorian calendar. School days shorten, the rhythm of the household changes, and late-evening study becomes normal rather than exceptional. The practical answer is to agree the shifted slot a fortnight ahead and keep it in place for the whole month, rather than rescheduling week by week and losing two sessions to confusion.

sections.heading: The hour and a half to Dhahran, and what it does to school choice
paragraphs: The Eastern Province coastal strip works as one market. Dammam, Al Khobar and Dhahran run into each other, the King Fahd Causeway puts Bahrain inside a day trip, and families routinely live in one of the three and school their children in another. Al Ahsa sits outside that arrangement by about ninety minutes of road, which is enough to break a daily commute but not enough to make the coast irrelevant.

What that produces is a small set of recognisable family decisions, and each one creates a different tutoring need. Some families relocate into the coastal cluster for schooling and keep a house in the oasis. Some board a child with relatives in Khobar during the week. Some commute weekly, driving in on Sunday morning and back on Thursday afternoon. And a large number simply stay, enrol locally, and accept that two or three subjects will have to be taught by somebody who is not at the school.

The last group is the one this page is written for, and the arithmetic is straightforward. A governorate of this size will have a small number of senior specialists in any given subject across all of its schools combined, because that is what the subject mix of a teaching workforce looks like anywhere. The question is never whether good teachers exist here; it is whether one of the four people who have taught Physics HL to examination standard is free on the evening your child is free, and willing to take a private student.

Online teaching removes the geography from that question without pretending the geography does not exist. It does not make the drive shorter, and it does not replace a school. What it changes is the size of the pool a Hofuf or Al Oyun family is choosing from, and therefore the chance that the person teaching Paper 3 has actually marked Paper 3.

sections.heading: Arabia Standard Time against your tutor's own working week
paragraphs: The Kingdom runs on Arabia Standard Time, UTC+3, and does not change its clocks. That is an advantage that most families never think to use. A slot agreed in Saudi local time is stable all year here; it is the tutor's country that moves. A tutor in London is three hours behind in their winter and two hours behind once their clocks go forward, so a seven o'clock Al Ahsa lesson is a four o'clock lesson for part of the year and a five o'clock lesson for the rest. If the booking was ever written down in the tutor's time, it will drift twice a year and nobody will notice until a student sits in front of an empty screen.

The fix is mechanical. Pin every slot to Arabia Standard Time, write it that way in the confirmation, and let the tutor absorb the shift. The second half of the fix is to ask about the tutor's own working week, not only their time zone. A tutor whose school day runs Monday to Friday is at work on your Sunday and your Monday, which are precisely the two evenings worth having. A tutor who teaches in the Gulf, or who tutors full time, has those evenings free.

India is the case worth understanding properly, because a large share of the tutoring market for Gulf families sits there. India is two and a half hours ahead of Arabia Standard Time, so a seven o'clock lesson in Hofuf is half past nine at night in Delhi or Chennai. That is workable for one or two sessions and unsustainable as a daily pattern, which is why Indian tutors fill Gulf evening slots early and why a request made in the middle of a term often cannot be met at the hour a family wants.

None of this argues for one country over another. It argues for asking two questions before agreeing a slot: what the offset is, and whether the tutor's own week collides with yours. A good match on both holds for a year. A bad match on either produces a rescheduled lesson every third week, which is how support quietly stops working without anyone deciding to stop it.

sections.heading: Which subjects the oasis cannot staff, and why that is not a criticism
paragraphs: Every school in the world is short of the same teachers. Higher Level Physics, Mathematics AA at Higher Level, Chemistry with real organic depth, Computer Science, Economics at Higher Level and the second modern language are hard to recruit in Riyadh, hard to recruit in Dubai and hard to recruit in Manchester. A governorate the size of Al Ahsa is not failing when it cannot field two of each; it is simply too small a workforce for that to be likely.

The pattern is predictable enough to plan around. Sciences are usually covered to Standard Level and stretched at Higher Level, because the same teacher takes both and the Higher Level extension topics are the first thing to be rushed at the end of the course. Mathematics splits badly: a school that has to offer both Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation across two levels needs four distinct courses from a department that may have two senior teachers. Options and Higher Level extensions are where the thinning shows first.

Second languages are the other reliable gap. A Diploma student needs a language B, and a school with a small cohort cannot run five of them. Families find themselves told that French is available and Spanish is not, or that a language will run only if enough students choose it, which turns a subject choice into a timetable lottery. Students sitting a language as a school-supported self-taught option need outside teaching more than anyone else on this list.

What follows from all of this is a specific way of asking for help. Not "my child needs a tutor", but "my child is sitting Chemistry HL with option material on the schedule, the internal investigation is due in the spring term, and the school has one chemist". That request can be matched precisely. The vague one gets a generalist, and a generalist is exactly the thing that does not solve a Higher Level problem.
bullets: Higher Level extension topics are the first casualty of a one-specialist department
Mathematics AA and AI across two levels is four courses, not one subject
Language B choice is often decided by cohort size rather than by the student
Internal Assessment supervision is the hardest thing for a stretched teacher to do well
Computer Science and Economics HL are thin everywhere, not only here

sections.heading: What tutoring costs in this market, and who publishes the numbers
paragraphs: Rates in the Kingdom are published by the people selling the lessons, which means every number a parent finds online is marketing until proved otherwise. The bands below are advertised rates taken from tutoring platforms, tutor marketplaces and tutoring companies serving Saudi families. They are not a market average, they are not survey data, and none of them is what IB Gram charges. They are useful because they show the shape of the market and what moves a price inside it.

What drives the number, roughly in order of weight: subject scarcity first, then examiner or marking experience, then level, then whether the tutor travels, then the length of the commitment. Scarcity does more work than parents expect. A Mathematics AA Higher Level specialist and a Mathematics Standard Level tutor are different markets, and the gap between them is wider than the gap between a weak and a strong tutor inside either one. Level follows the same logic: Higher Level sits above Standard Level, which sits above Middle Years, which sits above IGCSE.

Travel loading is where the Al Ahsa comparison gets interesting. An in-home tutor charges for the hour and absorbs the journey, or charges for the journey and absorbs nothing. In a governorate where the specialist pool is small and distances inside the oasis are real, that loading is not a rounding error; it is the reason in-home senior-subject tuition is quoted at the top of the local range when it is available at all. Online teaching deletes that line from the invoice, which is a straightforward cost argument rather than a claim about quality.

Two practical notes. Ask what a rate includes before comparing two of them: past papers, marked written work, a written report, and contact between lessons are sometimes inside the hour and sometimes extra. And treat a provider quoting in dollars as quoting a different product; currency alone adds a conversion and often a premium, and a parent budgeting in riyals should convert before comparing.

sections.heading: How to check that a tutor knows your child's syllabus, not just the subject
paragraphs: A tutor who knows chemistry and a tutor who knows your child's chemistry course are different purchases. The gap shows up in the first lesson and costs a term to discover if you are not looking for it. Three questions separate them, and all three can be asked in a trial lesson by a parent who does not know the subject.

First, ask which syllabus and which code. A Diploma student is on a specific subject guide at a specific level, with specific option or extension material. An IGCSE student is entered against a numbered syllabus with a tier. A tutor who answers "IGCSE Chemistry" has told you nothing; a tutor who asks which board, which code and whether the entry is Core or Extended has told you a great deal. Get the code from the school's examinations officer and use it in the conversation.

Second, ask about the mark scheme rather than the content. A good answer sounds like method: what a six-mark extended-response question rewards, which command terms change the required answer, where candidates in this paper routinely give away marks they had earned. Examiner or marking experience is worth paying for precisely because it produces that kind of answer, and it is checkable — ask which board, which paper, which component, and over how many series. A tutor who has marked will answer immediately and specifically.

Third, ask what they will not do. The honest answer includes the Internal Assessment: a tutor teaches the skill, reads the student's own draft, explains the criteria and gives feedback. They do not produce the work, and a tutor who offers to is a risk to the student's Diploma, not a shortcut through it. A tutor who volunteers that boundary before being asked has usually worked inside a school.

What none of this gives you is a number. No tutor can promise a grade, and any claim of a guaranteed improvement should be read as marketing rather than as information. What a parent can verify is the syllabus, the marking experience, the plan for the first month, and whether the student came out of the trial lesson able to do something they could not do at the start of it.

sections.heading: What an online lesson looks like from an Al Ahsa sitting room
paragraphs: A lesson is a live video call with a shared whiteboard, one tutor and one student. Nothing is recorded in advance and nothing is pre-packaged; the student talks, the tutor listens and writes, and the hour follows what the student actually cannot do. The setup that works is unglamorous: a laptop rather than a phone, a wired or strong connection, headphones, a notebook and a pen, and a table in a room where a door can be closed. A tablet with a stylus is a genuine advantage in mathematics and the sciences, because the student can write rather than type.

The shared whiteboard is where most of the teaching happens. A tutor works a mathematics problem line by line in the same way they would on a classroom board, except that the student can write on it too, which matters more than it sounds. The most useful thing a tutor can see is a student's own working as it goes wrong. Past papers are shared on screen or sent ahead, questions are attempted under time where that is the point of the exercise, and mark schemes are opened afterwards rather than before.

Written work moves between lessons rather than during them. A student photographs or uploads their attempt, the tutor annotates it and returns it, and the next session starts from the annotations. That rhythm is what makes a single weekly hour productive: the hour is for teaching, and the marking happens in between. Parents get a short written note after each session saying what was covered, what was set and what the tutor is watching.

Two practical matters families ask about. Connections drop; when they do, the tutor reconnects and the time is made up, and a session interrupted beyond repair is rescheduled rather than charged. And a parent is welcome in the room for a first lesson and welcome to ask for a summary at any point, though most teenagers work better once the audience leaves. Lessons are not published or shared with anyone outside the family and the tutor.

sections.heading: Arriving in Al Ahsa part-way through a course
paragraphs: Mid-course arrivals are routine in this governorate. A posting starts in the autumn, a family moves from Dubai, Cairo, Chennai or Houston in the middle of a term, and a student who was halfway through a Diploma or an IGCSE course lands in a new school with a different scheme of work. Nothing about this is unusual, and it is survivable — but it is survivable on purpose, not by hoping.

The first thing to establish is what has actually changed. The board may be the same and the order of teaching different, which is the most common and most deceptive case: a student who has covered organic chemistry and not yet covered energetics arrives in a class that did it the other way round, and they look lost in lessons while being perfectly competent in half the course. Mapping covered against not-yet-covered, topic by topic, takes one diagnostic session and saves a term of guessing.

The second is the assessed work. Internal Assessment timelines differ between schools even inside one board, and a transfer student can arrive with a draft the new school will not accept, or with nothing started where the cohort is already on a second draft. This is a question for the Diploma Programme coordinator in the first week, not the fourth, because the realistic options narrow quickly. The same applies to entries: a student moving late may need a centre arrangement for a June or November series, and the examinations officer holds those deadlines.

The third is the pace of catch-up. A term of genuine gap in one subject is recoverable with a weekly hour and honest homework. Two Higher Level subjects at once needs more than that, and it needs the family to accept a heavier few months rather than a permanent arrangement. What does not work is treating a transfer as a reason to start everything again; the useful plan is narrow, written down, and reviewed at the end of the first month against what the student can now do.

process.title: Tell us the syllabus, not the year group
process.description: The useful first message names the board, the subject, the level and where your child is in the course: Chemistry HL with the internal investigation due in the spring term, or Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics entered at Extended tier. That is enough to search the right pool. A year group alone is not, and it is the reason generic requests get generic tutors.

process.title: A free trial lesson with the specialist
process.description: One hour, no payment, with the tutor we think fits. It is a diagnostic rather than a sales call: the tutor finds out what the student can and cannot do, and the student finds out whether this person can explain things. You will know by the end of the hour, and so will your child, whose opinion on this matters more than most parents expect.

process.title: Pin the slot to Arabia Standard Time
process.description: The slot is written down in Saudi local time and the tutor absorbs any clock change in their own country. We check that their working week does not collide with your Sunday and Monday evenings, because those are the two most useful evenings in an Al Ahsa week and the ones a Monday-to-Friday teacher cannot cover.

process.title: Agree a one-month plan in writing
process.description: Three or four specific things the first month is for, with how each will be checked. Not "improve in physics" but "write uncertainty correctly in the investigation, and stop losing graph-gradient marks". A plan a parent cannot check is a plan nobody can be held to, and it is how a term disappears without anyone noticing.

process.title: Review at the end of the first month
process.description: We ask what has changed in school work, not in confidence. If the match is wrong, we change the tutor rather than asking the student to adapt to it; two or three lessons is usually enough to tell. If the plan was wrong, we rewrite the plan. Either way the review happens on a date agreed in advance.

process.title: Reset before each series
process.description: In the weeks before a June or November series the work changes shape: whole papers under time, marked against the real scheme, with a question-order and timing plan agreed with the student. This runs alongside the school's own revision timetable rather than competing with it, and it is the point at which technique matters more than content.

whyPoints.title: The pool is national and the match is by syllabus
whyPoints.description: A family in Udhailiyah and a family in Al Khobar choose from the same tutors, because the search is over everyone who teaches that syllabus at that level and can hold a Saudi evening slot. Distance from Hofuf stops being a selection criterion, which is the whole practical argument for teaching this way.

whyPoints.title: One to one, live, and never a recording
whyPoints.description: Every lesson is a live video session with one tutor and one student, following what that student cannot yet do. Recorded courses have their place, but they cannot hear a student explain a method wrongly and stop them mid-sentence, which is most of what useful teaching consists of.

whyPoints.title: The week and the clock are planned, not assumed
whyPoints.description: Slots are set against a Sunday-to-Thursday week and pinned to Arabia Standard Time, and we check the tutor's own working week before confirming. That is why a slot agreed in the autumn term is still the same slot after the tutor's country changes its clocks.

whyPoints.title: A clear line on assessed work
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach, review and give feedback on the student's own Internal Assessment, Extended Essay, TOK essay or Personal Project. They do not produce any part of it. That boundary is stated to the student in the first session, because a Diploma lost to a malpractice finding cannot be repaired by a good grade elsewhere.

whyPoints.title: No numbers we cannot stand behind
whyPoints.description: There is no success rate on this page, no star rating and no count of tutors, because any figure without a sample, a date and a method is decoration. What we will put in writing is the tutor's syllabus and marking experience, and a plan for the first month that a parent can check.

whyPoints.title: Independent, and plain about what we do not sell
whyPoints.description: IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform with no affiliation to any board, regulator or school. Lessons for Saudi families are delivered online; we do not send a tutor to an address in the Kingdom, and in-home visits are a service we run only in India.

faqs.question: What should an Al Ahsa parent ask a tutor before the first paid lesson?
faqs.answer: Four things. Which syllabus and code your child is entered against, and whether the tutor has taught that exact one. What a high-mark extended-response answer in that paper actually needs, which tests method rather than content knowledge. What they will not do with assessed work, where the right answer includes reading and giving feedback on a draft but never producing it. And what the first month is for, stated as things that can be checked in school work. A tutor who answers all four specifically has taught the course; one who answers in generalities about confidence and motivation may not have.

faqs.question: How do I check that a tutor knows the exact Cambridge IGCSE syllabus my child is entered for?
faqs.answer: Get the syllabus code and the tier from your school's examinations officer before you ask anybody anything. Cambridge subjects carry numbered codes and several run Core and Extended tiers with different papers, so "IGCSE Chemistry" is not a specification. Then ask the tutor which paper carries the practical or alternative-to-practical component, what the tiering means for the top grade available, and where candidates in that paper lose marks most often. A tutor who has taught it answers without hesitating. One who has taught the subject but not the syllabus will talk about chemistry instead of about the examination.

faqs.question: Does a tutor need experience of Eastern Province schools to teach a Hofuf student well?
faqs.answer: Not for the subject teaching, which follows the board's syllabus and is the same in Hofuf as in Manchester. It helps for two narrower things. A tutor who has worked with Gulf families understands a Sunday-to-Thursday week without being reminded, and will not set a heavy task on a Thursday night. And they are used to a school calendar that differs from the one they grew up with, including a Ramadan period that moves across the year. Useful, then, but a long way behind knowing the syllabus and having marked the paper.

faqs.question: What does examiner experience mean on a Diploma tutor's profile, and how can a parent verify it?
faqs.answer: It means the tutor has marked that board's scripts for a live series, applying a published mark scheme to real candidates' work. That matters because it teaches what the scheme rewards rather than what a textbook says, which is where most available marks sit. Verify it by asking four specifics: which board, which subject, which component or paper, and across how many series. Someone who has done it answers immediately and in that form. Treat an unspecific claim of examiner status as unverified, and never pay a premium for one, because the premium is for the specificity.

faqs.question: If the first tutor is not right for my child, how quickly can an Al Ahsa family change?
faqs.answer: Two or three lessons is usually enough to tell, and that is the point to act rather than hoping it improves. Tell us what is wrong in practical terms, since "they do not explain things the way she thinks" is more useful than "it is not working", and we match again from the same pool. The slot stays where it is, which matters more than it sounds, because a family that has solved a Sunday evening around a school run does not want to solve it twice. Nothing is owed for lessons that have not been taught.

faqs.question: Can an Al Ahsa family choose the gender of the tutor for a one-to-one Diploma subject?
faqs.answer: Yes. One-to-one online teaching makes this a straightforward filter rather than a negotiation: say so in the first message and the search is run that way from the start. It is one of the practical advantages of a national pool over a local one, because a family choosing from four available specialists in the governorate may have no choice at all, while a family choosing from everyone who teaches that syllabus almost always does. The same applies to a request for a tutor who speaks Arabic as well as the subject.

faqs.question: How many students does one tutor usually carry, and why should a parent care?
faqs.answer: Ask, because the answer tells you what you are buying. A full-time tutor with a heavy weekly load has less capacity to mark written work carefully between sessions, and marking between sessions is where a single weekly hour becomes productive. A serving teacher has term-time constraints and may be unavailable in the weeks that matter most before a series. Neither is wrong. What matters is that the tutor can state how much written work they will mark each week and when they will return it, and then does it.

faqs.question: What does my child need at home in Al Ahsa for an online lesson to run properly?
faqs.answer: A laptop rather than a phone, a stable connection, headphones with a microphone, and a room where a door closes. Paper and a pen stay essential: students who type their mathematics lose the handwriting speed they will need in the examination hall. A tablet with a stylus is a real advantage in the sciences and mathematics because the student can write onto the shared whiteboard. No software needs buying, and nothing beyond a browser normally needs installing. A phone works in an emergency and should never be the plan.

faqs.question: How does a tutor show working on a Mathematics AA problem over video?
faqs.answer: On a shared whiteboard that both people can write on, line by line, exactly as it would be done on a classroom board. The difference is that the student writes too, and that is the point: the most useful thing a tutor can watch is a student's own working as it goes wrong, because the error is almost never in the last line. Graphs, diagrams and calculator screens are shared the same way. Past papers are opened on screen, attempted under time where timing is the lesson, and marked against the real scheme afterwards.

faqs.question: Are lessons recorded, and who in the family is able to watch them back?
faqs.answer: Only if the family asks for it, and then the recording belongs to the family and the tutor and goes nowhere else. Plenty of students revise well from a recording of a difficult explanation, particularly in mathematics and physics. Plenty of others speak much less freely when they know the session is being kept, which costs more than the recording is worth. The decision is the family's, it is made before the lesson rather than during it, and it can be changed at any point. Lessons are never published or used as marketing.

faqs.question: What happens if the connection drops in the middle of a Physics lesson?
faqs.answer: The tutor waits and reconnects, and the lost minutes are added back to the session. If the connection will not hold, the lesson is rescheduled rather than charged, and the tutor sends through what was planned so the student can work on something in the meantime. Connections in the oasis are generally good, but a shared household link under evening load is the usual culprit rather than the service itself. Where drops recur, a wired connection for the laptop fixes it more often than any other single change.

faqs.question: How does a tutor mark written Economics work between two Al Ahsa lessons?
faqs.answer: The student photographs or uploads the attempt, the tutor annotates it against the mark scheme and returns it before the next session, and the session starts from those annotations rather than from a new topic. In Economics the annotations are mostly about two things: whether the diagram carries the marks it should, with axes, labels and the shift drawn correctly, and whether evaluation was actually attempted rather than assumed. Students lose the evaluation marks far more often than the analysis ones, and seeing that written on their own script is what changes it.

faqs.question: Which Diploma topics do Al Ahsa students most often arrive needing outside teaching for?
faqs.answer: Higher Level extension material, almost every time, because it is the part of the course a single-specialist department reaches last and fastest. In practice that means further mechanics and induction in Physics, the Higher Level organic and equilibrium content in Chemistry, proof and the heavier calculus in Mathematics AA, and Paper 3 in Economics. Internal Assessment supervision is the other recurring request: it is the hardest thing for a stretched teacher to do properly, and it is a fixed share of the grade that the student has months of control over.

faqs.question: Why does organic chemistry cause more trouble than the physical chemistry topics?
faqs.answer: Because it cannot be answered by substitution into an equation. Physical chemistry rewards a reliable method: identify the quantity, pick the relationship, calculate carefully. Organic chemistry rewards pattern recognition across mechanisms, and a student who has learned reactions as a list stops the moment a paper asks them to predict a product they have not seen. The route through it is mechanism-first teaching with a lot of unfamiliar-substrate practice, plus drawing discipline, because curly arrows drawn from the wrong place lose marks that the reasoning had already earned.

faqs.question: Where do IGCSE Mathematics candidates in the oasis lose the most marks?
faqs.answer: On method marks they never wrote down. Multi-step questions carry credit for the working, and a candidate who does the algebra mentally and writes one wrong final answer scores nothing where a candidate with visible working would have scored most of it. After that: the wrong tier, which caps a grade before the paper even starts, and calculator habits that round too early and carry an error through three steps. All three are fixable in a term, and none of them is about mathematical ability.

faqs.question: What should a family in Udhailiyah or Haradh do if there is no international school within reach?
faqs.answer: Two routes, and they are often combined. Enrol locally for schooling and buy the senior subject teaching separately in the evenings, which is what most families in the far parts of the governorate do. Or sit IGCSE as a private candidate through a registered centre, which means arranging the centre yourselves and watching the entry deadlines months ahead of the June series rather than weeks. Either way the subject teaching happens online, because at that distance the pool of reachable specialists is not small, it is empty.

al-ahsa.closingHeading: Start with one subject, one slot and a free trial lesson
al-ahsa.closingBody: The useful first step is narrow. Pick the subject where the next assessment is already worrying your child, get the syllabus code and level from the school, and tell us where in the course they are. We will put a specialist in a free trial lesson with them, pinned to an evening that survives a Sunday-to-Thursday week and a drive home from the coast. If the match is right you will know inside the hour, and so will your child. If it is not, we match again and you have lost nothing but an evening. Everything is taught one to one, live online, on Arabia Standard Time.

al-khobar.tutorsIntro: The tutors below are the ones Al Khobar families ask for most: Diploma specialists in the sciences and mathematics, Cambridge IGCSE teachers across both mathematics tiers, and Middle Years Programme subject teachers. Each profile names the syllabus taught and the papers covered, so you can check the match before a trial lesson.

intro.heading: Start with where your child is in the year, not with the subject
paragraphs: The most useful thing a family in Al Khobar can tell a tutor is not the subject. It is the point in the year the student has reached. A Year 10 student three weeks into a Cambridge IGCSE course needs content taught properly the first time. A DP2 student eight weeks from the June series needs papers marked against a published mark scheme and the two topics that keep costing marks closed off. Both of those students are doing mathematics. They are not the same job, and a tutor who treats them as one wastes a term. Everything on this page is organised that way: where the student stands, then what actually helps.

The second thing is geography, because in this city geography sets the hours. Al Khobar is where a large share of the Eastern Province's international-school families live, while a large share of the schools sit in Dhahran, in Dammam or behind a campus gate. A family in Al Aqrabiyah or Al Bandariyah can be twenty minutes from the school gate at eleven in the morning and fifty minutes from it at half past two. By the time the car is home, the usable study window is narrower than the school day suggests, and it is bounded at the other end by the hour at which a fifteen-year-old stops absorbing anything.

The third is staffing. The Dammam, Khobar and Dhahran conurbation behaves as one labour and school market, and by Saudi standards it is a deep one. Depth is not the same as coverage. A school can run the full Diploma and still have one Physics teacher, no Economics specialist at Higher Level, and a mathematics department stretched across Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation at two levels each. Families do not usually look for an IB tutor in Al Khobar because the school is weak. They look because one subject, at one level, has no second pair of hands in the building.

Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to Saudi addresses; home visits are a service we offer only in India. Saying that plainly makes the stronger argument, not the weaker one. Online IB tuition in Al Khobar means the Chemistry Higher Level specialist your child works with was chosen from everyone available on Arabia Standard Time, rather than from the few people willing to drive to Al Thuqbah at seven in the evening. The travel loading leaves the invoice at the same moment it leaves the diary.

What follows is the year counted forward from wherever the student is standing now: the school-run arithmetic that decides the slot, what the local cluster struggles to staff, where marks go missing between a good classroom and a good grade, what a tutor may and may not touch on assessed work, and the route from an international certificate to a university place in the Kingdom or abroad. Money is discussed in SAR, with the source of every band named.
