al-khobar.programmesIntro: Four programmes account for almost every enquiry from Al Khobar. Which one a student sits in changes the whole shape of support: the Primary Years Programme is about habits, the Middle Years Programme about criteria, Cambridge IGCSE about papers and tiers, and the Diploma about six subjects, three of them at Higher Level, plus a core that carries points of its own.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The Primary Years Programme is enquiry-led and transdisciplinary. There are no external papers, so nothing is at stake in a grade sense, and that is exactly why families misread it. What is at stake is the habit set: reading stamina, written explanation, number fluency and the willingness to show working. A child who leaves the programme fluent in ideas but unwilling to write them down arrives in the Middle Years Programme with a problem that takes two years to undo.
programmes.countryNote: In Al Khobar most primary support is requested for English writing and for number work, usually because a family has moved from a system with heavier drilling and the parent cannot tell whether the child is behind or simply taught differently. A diagnostic session that reads a week of the child's own written work is worth more here than any syllabus comparison, and it is quick.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The Middle Years Programme assesses against four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight, with descriptors rather than marks per question. A student can know the content and still land in the middle band because the answer never addressed the criterion. The Personal Project in the final year is the first genuinely independent piece of assessed work most students meet, and it is where organisation, not ability, decides the outcome.
programmes.countryNote: Requests for an MYP tutor in Al Khobar cluster around two moments: the move into Years 9 and 10 when criteria start to bite, and the Personal Project. Families whose children will transfer into a Cambridge IGCSE class rather than continue into the Diploma also ask for a bridging term, because criterion-based marking and paper-based marking reward different writing.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: IGCSE is examined on papers, and the paper you are entered for matters as much as the revision you do. Cambridge mathematics runs Core and Extended tiers with different grade ceilings. The sciences run separate papers for multiple choice, structured questions and either a practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper. English as a Second Language and First Language English are different qualifications with different reading demands, and students are sometimes in the wrong one for a year before anybody notices.
programmes.countryNote: An IGCSE tutor in Al Khobar is most often wanted for mathematics tiering decisions and for the sciences, where the practical component unsettles students who have done little laboratory work. Because candidates in the Kingdom enter the June series or the November series, a Year 11 student who starts in the autumn term has two realistic windows rather than one, which changes what is worth attempting.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The Diploma is six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, each graded one to seven, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. The core adds up to three further points through a matrix that combines the Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay grades, giving a maximum total of forty-five. Each subject carries an internally assessed component marked by the school and moderated by the board.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma enquiries from Al Khobar divide neatly. In DP1 the ask is content and Internal Assessment planning. In DP2 it is paper technique, predicted grades and whichever Higher Level subject has pulled away. Students at Dhahran campuses often sit the Diploma alongside a cohort large enough to run most subjects, which makes the one unavailable Higher Level option the whole reason a family looks outside the school at all.

al-khobar.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma subjects Al Khobar families ask for most often, with the levels usually available. Each description says what the subject actually assesses and where marks tend to go missing, because a parent choosing a tutor needs to know which part of the course is the problem before paying anybody to fix it.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The algebra-heavy route, expected by most engineering, physics and economics degrees. Marks are lost less often on the hard topics than on unstructured working: a correct answer with no visible method earns a fraction of the available marks. At Higher Level the proof and calculus extensions have no Standard Level equivalent, so a student who switches down late carries topics they will never be examined on.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology-led problem solving. Students who find Analysis and Approaches punishing often read this as the easy option and are surprised by the written interpretation: a correct regression with no comment on what it means scores poorly. Graphical calculator fluency is assumed rather than taught, and that gap shows up in timed conditions rather than in homework.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Conceptually the subject that separates students fastest. The common failure is not mechanics but the written explanation of a mechanism, where a mark scheme wants a chain of causes and gets a restatement of the formula. Higher Level adds depth rather than breadth in several topics, so a student who is fine at Standard Level content can still be two levels short on the extension questions.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms, energetics and equilibrium cause most of the trouble, and the internally assessed investigation causes the rest. The investigation needs a measurable, controllable variable chosen early; students who choose late end up with data that cannot support an analysis, and no amount of writing rescues it. The data booklet is allowed and is routinely underused.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content-heavy and deceptively approachable. Students revise by reading, then lose marks on command terms: distinguish, outline, explain and discuss each want a different structure, and the mark scheme pays for the structure. The statistics within the course surprise students who chose Biology to avoid mathematics, and the internally assessed investigation needs a design that produces enough data to test.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams carry marks, and incomplete diagrams are the single most common loss: axes unlabelled, no title, no shift arrow. The Higher Level extension questions reward quantitative work that Standard Level students never meet. Evaluation is a separate skill from explanation, and most students who plateau at a middle grade are explaining competently and evaluating not at all.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study driven, with a prescribed stimulus for one paper. Students lose marks by writing general theory where the question wanted the named firm in the material. The internally assessed project differs by level and needs primary or secondary research chosen to fit the question rather than the other way round, which is where a tutor earns their fee early rather than late.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Unseen textual analysis plus studied works, with an individual oral in which the student must connect a global issue to two texts. Students who read widely still underperform when they analyse content and ignore form. Higher Level adds a written essay on a studied work, which is a research task with a deadline rather than an examination skill.

subjects.name: Arabic A and Arabic B
subjects.description: Arabic A is a literature or language-and-literature course for fluent speakers; Arabic B is a language-acquisition course, with ab initio for beginners. Families in Al Khobar often need to settle which is correct for a child who speaks Arabic at home but has been schooled in English, because the wrong choice costs grade points for two years and is awkward to reverse.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Algorithmic thinking, systems fundamentals and a solution-development project. The project fails most often on scope: a student builds something impressive that does not map onto the assessment criteria, and the criteria are what is marked. Higher Level adds abstract data structures and a case study released for the series, which rewards reading it early rather than in the final month.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: The core is assessed through a Theory of Knowledge exhibition and essay plus a four-thousand-word Extended Essay, and the two grades combine in a matrix worth up to three points on the Diploma total. Students who treat the core as administration leave those points on the table. A supervisor at school owns the process; a tutor can only ever work on the student's own drafting and thinking.

al-khobar.igcseSubjectsIntro: Al Khobar also has a large Cambridge and Edexcel population, including students at British-curriculum schools who will never enter the Diploma. These are the IGCSE subjects most often requested, with the syllabus codes families see on entry forms, because a tutor who does not know the code does not know the paper structure either.

igcseSubjects.name: Mathematics (0580)
igcseSubjects.description: Two tiers with different grade ceilings and overlapping but not identical content. The tiering decision is usually made by the school in Year 10 and is the single highest-leverage conversation a family can have, because a capable student entered for Core cannot reach the top grades however well they perform.

igcseSubjects.name: Additional Mathematics (0606)
igcseSubjects.description: Taken alongside Extended mathematics by students heading for Higher Level mathematics or a mathematics-heavy A Level. It introduces calculus and more formal algebra early, and it is the best available bridge into the Diploma for a student arriving from a British-curriculum school.

igcseSubjects.name: Physics (0625)
igcseSubjects.description: Multiple choice, theory and either a practical test or the alternative-to-practical paper, depending on the school's entry. Students lose most marks on graph work and on explanations that describe rather than account for an observation. Knowing which practical route the school has entered changes how a tutor prepares a candidate.

igcseSubjects.name: Chemistry (0620)
igcseSubjects.description: Moles and stoichiometry defeat more candidates than organic chemistry does, because the arithmetic is unforgiving under time pressure. Qualitative analysis tables are examinable and memorisable, and students routinely arrive at the paper without having learned them, which is free marks given away.

igcseSubjects.name: Biology (0610)
igcseSubjects.description: Definitions are examined strictly and partial credit is thin, so a loosely remembered definition scores nothing. Transport in plants, respiration and inheritance account for a disproportionate share of lost marks. The alternative-to-practical paper tests experimental reasoning rather than recall and needs its own preparation.

igcseSubjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510 and 0511)
igcseSubjects.description: Reading and writing dominate, and the summary question is a technique rather than a comprehension exercise. Students at English-medium schools in the Eastern Province are sometimes entered here when First Language English would suit them better, or the reverse, and a single diagnostic reading task settles it.

igcseSubjects.name: Economics (0455)
igcseSubjects.description: Diagram accuracy and definitional precision carry the marks, and the structured data-response question is where most candidates lose them. It is a common first encounter with evaluation as a marked skill, which is why students who go on to Diploma Economics find the transition easier than their classmates.

igcseSubjects.name: Business Studies (0450)
igcseSubjects.description: Applied rather than theoretical: answers must use the business described in the case material. The recurring loss is generic advantage-and-disadvantage writing where the question asked for a recommendation with justification, which is a different paragraph shape and takes a few weeks to install.

al-khobar.regionsTitle: Al Khobar districts and what the school run does to a lesson slot
al-khobar.regionsIntro: These notes are about timing rather than prestige. The question that matters for a weekly lesson is which direction the afternoon run goes and how long it takes on a bad day, because that decides the earliest hour a slot can hold for a whole term rather than for a quiet week.

regions.name: Al Khobar Al Shamalia
regions.note: The northern residential grid, well placed for the Dhahran school corridor on King Saud Road. The run is short in distance and unreliable in time, because the final approach bunches at the same hour every afternoon. Families here can usually hold an early-evening slot through the term.

regions.name: Al Aqrabiyah
regions.note: Dense apartment living between the Corniche and the Prince Faisal bin Fahd road, close to Khobar's retail strip. Children at city schools are often home earliest of anyone in this list, which makes it one of the few districts where a late-afternoon slot genuinely survives a whole term.

regions.name: Al Bandariyah
regions.note: Older villa streets inland of the Corniche, within reach of both Khobar city schools and the Dhahran approach. The mixed direction of travel is the complication: siblings at different schools can return forty minutes apart, so one shared study hour rarely works for both.

regions.name: Al Thuqbah
regions.note: West of the centre and oriented towards the Dammam expressway. The commute is longer and more exposed to the highway, so families here tend to settle on a later slot and keep it rather than chase an earlier one that fails on the days traffic is heavy.

regions.name: Al Rakah
regions.note: Straddling the boundary towards Dammam, with children split between Dammam and Dhahran schools. Two directions of travel out of one household is the defining feature, and it is the strongest practical argument in this city for a tutor whose availability is not tied to a route.

regions.name: Doha and the Dhahran approach
regions.note: Closest to the Dhahran campuses, with the shortest distance of any district and a gate queue that can erase the advantage. Pick-up timing varies more here from one day to the next than anywhere else in Al Khobar, which argues for a slot with a margin built into it.

regions.name: Half Moon Bay and the southern coast
regions.note: Compound and coastal housing south of the city, with a long northbound run to the Dhahran and Khobar schools. The commute is predictable but slow, so the realistic weekly pattern is two later sessions rather than three early ones, and that is worth planning around.

regions.name: The causeway side of the city
regions.note: Streets near the King Fahd Causeway approach, where some families hold ties on both sides of the water and a weekend can start on Thursday afternoon. A Thursday evening lesson is a poor bet here; a Sunday-to-Wednesday pattern holds far better across a term.

schoolClusters.note: The schools most Al Khobar families drive to. The International Schools Group operates several campuses across the Eastern Province, and the Diploma is offered at the American School of Dhahran and at ISG Jubail rather than at every campus, which is a distinction worth confirming before enrolment.

City schools serving the Khobar and Dammam population directly, running a mix of Cambridge, Edexcel and national-curriculum pathways. Subject availability at Higher Level and at Extended tier varies year to year with cohort size, which is the usual trigger for an outside specialist.

schoolClusters.note: A small number of Al Khobar families look at Bahrain, because the causeway puts a second school market inside an hour's drive. It is a real option and a demanding daily commute, and it is the one school decision in this city that is made on road time rather than on curriculum.

sections.heading: What a search for IB and IGCSE tutors in Al Khobar is usually about
paragraphs: A parent typing this phrase into a search box rarely wants a list of names. They want to know whether anybody genuinely teaches their child's syllabus, at their child's level, in a slot that survives contact with the school run. Those are three separate questions, and the third is the one that quietly kills most arrangements. A tutor who is excellent on paper but only free at four in the afternoon is no use to a household whose car gets back from Dhahran at ten past five.

The second thing behind the search is usually one component rather than a whole subject. An IB tutor in Al Khobar is most often wanted for one of four things: a Higher Level science the school teaches thinly, a mathematics course that has drifted away from the student since the previous year, an Internal Assessment with a deadline and no plan, or paper technique in the term before a series. Naming which of the four it is shortens the matching process from a week to an afternoon, and it also tells you how many lessons are realistic.

The third is cost, and families here discuss it directly rather than by hint. Advertised rates across the Kingdom span a wide band. Tutoring platforms list general online tutoring from around SAR 55 an hour. Tutor marketplaces put general senior-school private tuition in Saudi cities at SAR 200 and above. Tutoring companies advertise IB subject tutoring from around SAR 180, with Higher Level and premium tracks quoted nearer SAR 200 to 220, and some international providers quote in dollars instead. Those are published advertised figures, not a market average, and none of them is IB Gram's price.

sections.heading: The Al Khobar school run, and the hours it actually leaves
paragraphs: Al Khobar is where a great many Eastern Province families live; a great many of the schools are somewhere else. The Dammam, Khobar and Dhahran conurbation functions as a single labour and school market, so a child can sleep in Al Aqrabiyah, sit in a classroom in Dhahran and have a parent working in Dammam. That arrangement is convenient for everything except timetabling a weekly lesson, because the afternoon return leg is the least predictable part of the day and nobody controls it.

The figures in the table are indicative rather than measured, and your own week is the only reliable source. The structural point stands regardless of the exact minutes: the earliest slot that holds all term is not the earliest slot that works on a quiet Sunday. A session pencilled in for five o'clock because the car got home at half past four once will be missed four times before the half-term break, and a missed slot does more damage than a later one. Choose the hour that survives a bad day and keep it.

Two further constraints sit on top of the traffic. The school week runs Sunday to Thursday, so Thursday evening behaves like a Friday and the week's written work has a different rhythm from the Monday-to-Friday one most imported tutoring copy assumes. During Ramadan the school day shortens and the useful study hours move later, which suits online delivery and plays badly with a fixed driving route. A slot agreed in Arabia Standard Time absorbs both of those changes without renegotiating anything.

sections.heading: The year counted forward from where your child stands now
paragraphs: Support that starts from a point in the year beats support that starts from a subject. The two-year courses, the Diploma and most IGCSE programmes, have a shape, and the same tutor does four quite different jobs inside it. In the first autumn term the job is teaching. By the following spring it is the Internal Assessment. In the final autumn it is predicted grades and university applications. In the last eight weeks it is papers, and only papers. A family that buys the wrong one of those four gets a polite tutor and no movement.

Entries are the one deadline a family cannot move. Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel candidates in the Kingdom enter the June series or the November series; the February and March sitting that appears on tutoring pages copied from India is not open to Saudi candidates. Final entry windows close several months before the papers sit, and the exact date belongs to your school's examinations officer rather than to any tutoring website, this one included. For the Diploma, the May session is the one almost every Saudi IB school enters, and the school's Diploma coordinator holds the calendar.

Two calendars in the same city complicate the start date. Ministry of Education schools run a two-semester year that opens in late August and closes in late June, with an autumn break, a midyear break and an Eid Al Fitr break. International and British-curriculum schools set their own calendars and most of them run three terms, so two children in neighbouring villas can be on different timetables and on different holiday weeks. Work backwards from your own school's published calendar rather than from a general one, and confirm the mock weeks early, because mocks are what a predicted grade is built from.

sections.heading: What the Dammam, Khobar and Dhahran cluster cannot always staff
paragraphs: The Eastern Province cluster is one of the better-served school markets in the Kingdom, and that is precisely why the gaps in it are so specific. A school with a healthy Diploma cohort will still carry single-teacher departments. One Physics teacher covers both levels and the internally assessed work. One Economics teacher covers Higher and Standard Level with a free period between them. A mathematics department of three covers two courses at two levels each, which is four distinct syllabuses before anybody is ill.

The subjects that go thin are predictable. Higher Level Physics and Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches top the list, because the extension content is genuinely harder to teach and the pool of people who can teach it is small everywhere. Then come Economics and Business Management at Higher Level, Computer Science, Psychology, Music, and any second language beyond the two or three a school can timetable. Arabic A for a child schooled in English is its own problem, since the course assumes a literary register that conversational fluency does not supply.

This is why a search for a Cambridge IGCSE tutor in the Eastern Province or an IB Diploma tutor in Dhahran is usually a question about availability rather than distance. A family does not need somebody nearby. They need somebody who teaches that paper at that level and is free at half past five on a Monday. Online delivery is the honest answer to that, not a compromise version of a better arrangement, because the pool it draws from is the only pool large enough to contain the specialist in question.

sections.heading: Where marks go missing between a good classroom and a good grade
paragraphs: Most students who underperform at IGCSE or in the Diploma are not short of content. They are short of the thing that converts content into marks, and it has three parts: command terms, mark-scheme structure and timing. A command term is an instruction with a technical meaning. Explain wants a mechanism. Outline wants brevity. Discuss wants both sides and a judgement. Evaluate wants weighted criteria. A student who writes a strong explanation in answer to evaluate has written a good answer to a different question.

Mark schemes are published documents, and reading them changes behaviour faster than any amount of revision. A six-mark question is usually six separable marking points, not one flowing paragraph, and a student who writes in bullet-shaped sentences collects them. Diagrams in Economics carry marks for axes, labels and the shift itself. In the sciences, a question asking why something happens is paying for the chain of causes and not for the final statement. None of this is advanced; it is simply invisible until somebody marks a paper in front of the student.

Grade boundaries and predicted grades are the two mechanisms parents most often misread. Boundaries are set after the papers are marked, so a slightly harder paper moves the boundary down and nobody loses out, which also means last year's boundary is a guide and not a target. A predicted grade is the school's professional judgement, built from mocks and classwork, submitted for university applications; it is not a promise, and it is not something a tutor can award. What a tutor can do is produce the marked evidence a school reasonably takes into account.
bullets: Learn the command terms as a vocabulary list, with an example answer for each
Read the published mark scheme for one paper before revising for it
Count the marks and write that many separable points
Treat last year's grade boundary as context, never as the target

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do with an Internal Assessment or Extended Essay
paragraphs: Every Diploma subject carries an internally assessed component, and the Extended Essay, the Theory of Knowledge essay and the Middle Years Programme Personal Project sit alongside it. All of that work must be the student's own, and the school declares it as such. A tutor may not write, draft or produce any of it, and nobody at IB Gram will. That boundary is not a disclaimer bolted to the end of a sales page; it is the difference between support that helps and support that ends a Diploma.

What a tutor can legitimately do is substantial. They can teach the skills the task needs before the task starts: how to frame a research question, how to choose a variable that can actually be measured, how to structure an argument, how to reference. They can read the student's own draft and say where the criteria are not being met, in criterion language, leaving every change to the student. They can catch a method problem in week two rather than week ten, which is the single most valuable intervention available on assessed work.

The practical test for a family is simple. Ask any prospective tutor what they do with a first draft. A good answer describes reading it against the criteria and handing back questions. A bad answer offers to tidy it up, strengthen the wording or fill the gaps. Internal Assessment feedback that leaves the student with more work to do is the version that is allowed, and it is also the version that teaches something. The school supervisor remains the owner of the process throughout, and their deadlines outrank everybody else's.

sections.heading: From an international certificate to a university place
paragraphs: This is the part of the picture almost no tutoring page in the Kingdom covers, and it is the part that decides what the previous two years were for. A foreign or international school certificate is not automatically treated as equivalent to the Saudi secondary certificate. Ministry of Education equivalency, the mu'adalah decision, is the step that makes it usable, and it applies to the IB Diploma, to A Levels and to an American high school diploma alike. Families find out about it late far more often than they find out about it early.

Alongside equivalency sit the Qiyas tests. Qudurat, the General Aptitude Test, is run by the National Center for Assessment within the Education and Training Evaluation Commission, and it tests verbal and quantitative reasoning rather than syllabus content, in Arabic or in English. Tahsili, the achievement test, covers the science-stream subjects: mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology and English. The important fact about Tahsili is that its content follows the Saudi national curriculum, which is why Tahsili preparation is a genuine piece of work for an international-curriculum student rather than a formality.

An IB or IGCSE student has usually met most of the Tahsili material and almost none of its framing. The topics overlap; the sequence, the emphasis and the question style do not. That is a learnable gap, and it is learnable much more comfortably in the year before it matters than in the term of the test. Saudi universities publish their own admission criteria combining school grades with the Qiyas results, and the weightings differ by university and by programme, so the only trustworthy source is the university's own published criteria. No tutor can promise a university place, and anyone who does is telling you something about themselves.
bullets: Ask your school's counsellor about equivalency in the first year, not the last term
Check whether target universities state a maximum age for the certificate
Treat Tahsili as a separate syllabus with overlapping content, and plan for it
Read the admission criteria on the university's own site, not on a third-party summary

sections.heading: One-to-one online against the in-home market in Al Khobar
paragraphs: The fair comparison is not online against a classroom; it is online against the alternative a family is actually weighing, which in this city is a private tutor who drives to the district. That option exists, families use it, and it has real advantages: a teenager who will not engage on a screen sometimes engages across a table, and a younger child may need the physical presence. Those are good reasons, and they are the only good reasons, because on every other axis the comparison runs the other way.

Cost is the clearest axis. A tutor who drives is paid for the driving, whether or not it appears as a line item, and in a conurbation where a cross-city run can take forty-five minutes each way that loading is substantial. Tutor marketplaces put general senior-school private tuition in Saudi cities at SAR 200 an hour and above, while tutoring companies advertise IB subject tutoring from around SAR 180 with premium Higher Level tracks quoted nearer SAR 220. Travel is one of the five things that move those numbers, alongside level, scarcity, examiner experience and package length.

The deeper axis is the pool. A family in Al Rakah choosing an in-home tutor is choosing from the people prepared to drive to Al Rakah on a weekday evening. A family choosing online is choosing from everyone who can teach that syllabus in a slot that works on Arabia Standard Time. For Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, or Chemistry Higher Level, or Economics Higher Level, those two pools are not comparable in size. IB Gram does not sell in-home visits anywhere in the Kingdom; home visits are a service we offer only in India.

sections.heading: Arriving in the Eastern Province part-way through a course
paragraphs: Al Khobar takes in families mid-year more than most Saudi cities, because the industrial and energy employers of the Eastern Province move people on their own schedule rather than on the school calendar. A child arriving in February into a Diploma that started in August is in a specific and solvable position, but it needs to be diagnosed rather than assumed. The question is never how far behind they are in general. It is which topics the new school has already examined and what the Internal Assessment timetable looks like.

Three things decide how hard the transfer is. First, whether the two schools run the same course: a move from A Levels into the Diploma, or from an American high school programme into Higher Level sciences, is a change of structure and not just of content. Second, how much assessed work has already been completed and whether any of it travels. Third, the language of instruction in the previous school, which matters more for the written subjects than families expect and shows up in the first marked essay.

In practice the first fortnight is diagnosis, not teaching. A tutor should sit with the new school's scheme of work, the topics already tested and the student's own last marked papers, then produce a written list ordered by what is examined soonest. Catching up on everything at once is not possible and is not the goal; being secure on what the next assessment covers is. Families who move into the cluster in the final year should also ask about predicted grades early, because the new school has little evidence on which to build one.

process.title: Tell us the syllabus, not just the subject
process.description: Chemistry is four different jobs depending on whether it is Cambridge 0620 Extended, Edexcel International GCSE, Diploma Standard Level or Diploma Higher Level. Send the subject, the level, the board and the school. If you have an entry form or a scheme of work, that answers the question faster than any conversation, and it shortens matching to hours.

process.title: A free trial lesson, then a written starting point
process.description: The first session is diagnostic. The tutor works through recent material, marks something the student has already written and ends with a short written assessment of what is actually wrong. You keep that document whether or not you continue with us. A diagnosis that says only that the student needs more practice is not a diagnosis.

process.title: Fix the slot against a bad traffic day
process.description: We agree the hour in Arabia Standard Time, around the Sunday-to-Thursday week, chosen so it survives a heavy afternoon rather than an easy one. If the tutor sits in a country that changes its clocks, the slot stays pinned to your local time and theirs moves, because the Kingdom does not change its clocks at all.

process.title: Weekly work, marked before the next lesson
process.description: Each session sets written work, and the tutor marks it against the published mark scheme before you meet again. The student sees where marks were available and not taken. You get a short note saying what moved and what did not, which is the only reliable way to tell a productive term from a comfortable one.

process.title: Review at the end of the term, and say so if it is not working
process.description: At the end of a term we look at marked evidence rather than impressions and decide whether to continue, change tutor or stop. If the match is wrong after two or three lessons, say so and we change it. If no specialist is free for the subject and slot you need, we will tell you that instead of offering a generalist.

whyPoints.title: Matched on the paper, not the postcode
whyPoints.description: The constraint in Al Khobar is not the number of good teachers in the Eastern Province. It is whether one of them teaches that exact paper at that exact level and is free when your child is home. Matching on syllabus first and availability second is the only ordering that reliably produces a tutor who can help.

whyPoints.title: Built around the Sunday-to-Thursday week
whyPoints.description: Most tutoring copy a Saudi family reads was written for a Monday-to-Friday week and quietly assumes it. Thursday evening here is the start of a weekend, Sunday carries the week's first homework load, and Ramadan moves the usable hours later. Scheduling that starts from those facts holds together across a term.

whyPoints.title: Money discussed in SAR, with the source named
whyPoints.description: Advertised rates in this market range from around SAR 35 an hour on budget IGCSE platforms to SAR 220 for premium Higher Level tracks, and every one of those numbers is published by a provider rather than measured across the market. We quote our own figure directly and explain what moves it, instead of asking you to request a callback.

whyPoints.title: A hard line on assessed work
whyPoints.description: A tutor here reads a student's own Internal Assessment, Extended Essay or Personal Project draft and gives feedback against the criteria. They will not write it, redraft it or fill its gaps. That line costs us some enquiries from families who wanted the other thing, and it is the reason the support is safe to accept.

whyPoints.title: The university endgame treated as part of the work
whyPoints.description: Ministry of Education equivalency, the Qiyas tests and overseas entry requirements are not a separate topic from tutoring; they decide which subjects and levels matter. We will tell you what the mechanism is and send you to the university's own published criteria for the numbers, because the numbers differ by institution and by programme.

whyPoints.title: Plain answers about what we cannot do
whyPoints.description: We hold no accreditation from the Ministry of Education, from the Education and Training Evaluation Commission, from the IB or from Cambridge, and we say so. We have no office in the Kingdom. We do not guarantee grades, scores or admissions. What is left is a tutor, a syllabus and a weekly hour that is kept.

faqs.question: Our child starts DP1 at a Dhahran campus after the summer break - when should outside support begin?
faqs.answer: The useful window is the first six weeks of the autumn term, not the end of it. Two things happen early in DP1 that are expensive to fix later: Higher Level choices settle in practice even where they are nominally reversible, and the first topics of each course become the foundation everything else is stacked on. A tutor working in those six weeks is teaching slightly ahead of the class and closing gaps left over from IGCSE. Starting in the spring term instead means the same tutor spends the first month on repair work rather than on progress, which costs you lessons.

faqs.question: What should a Year 10 Cambridge IGCSE student in Al Khobar have secured before the spring term?
faqs.answer: Three things. The tier they are entered for in mathematics and the sciences, confirmed in writing rather than assumed, because Core and Extended have different grade ceilings. Fluency in the arithmetic the subject assumes, particularly moles in Chemistry and rearranging equations in Physics, since neither is taught again. And the habit of reading a mark allocation and writing that many separable points. A Year 10 student who holds those three arrives in Year 11 able to spend the year on papers rather than on catching up, which is the whole difference between the two years.

faqs.question: Is it too late to add Diploma support once DP2 has already started in the Eastern Province?
faqs.answer: No, but what you are buying changes. In DP2 the realistic gains come from paper technique, question selection, timing and closing two or three specific weak topics, not from reteaching a year of content. A tutor who claims otherwise is selling you comfort. The one genuine deadline risk is the internally assessed work, so the first conversation should establish what has been submitted internally and what has not. Families who start in the final autumn term usually see movement; families who start six weeks before the papers see less, and should expect that to be said plainly.

faqs.question: How does an MYP student in Al Khobar prepare for the move into Year 10 IGCSE?
faqs.answer: The content transfer is usually fine; the assessment transfer is not. Middle Years Programme marking rewards an answer that addresses a criterion descriptor, while IGCSE marking rewards an answer that collects discrete marking points under time pressure. Students who have never written to a mark allocation lose grades for a term while they learn to. A short bridging block over the summer, built on past paper questions with the mark scheme visible, closes most of that gap. Mathematics is the subject where the change in style bites hardest and earliest.

faqs.question: How many points does the Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay matrix add to a Diploma total?
faqs.answer: Up to three, on top of the maximum forty-two available from six subjects graded one to seven, giving the forty-five-point ceiling. The two core grades are combined in a published matrix, so a strong Extended Essay can pull a weaker Theory of Knowledge grade upward and the reverse is also true. Those three points decide more university offers than families expect, because they sit exactly where competitive thresholds tend to fall. Treating the core as paperwork rather than as assessment is the most common avoidable loss in the whole Diploma.

faqs.question: What is a predicted grade on the Diploma, and can an Al Khobar school be asked to revise one?
faqs.answer: A predicted grade is the school's professional judgement of the grade a student is likely to achieve, built from mocks, classwork and internally assessed marks, and submitted to universities during applications. It is not a promise, and no tutor can award or raise one. Schools will normally reconsider a prediction when new marked evidence appears, which is why a tutor's marked papers matter more than a tutor's opinion. Ask the school what evidence it uses and when the prediction is finalised, then make sure the best available evidence exists before that date.

faqs.question: Why do grade boundaries move between one examination series and the next?
faqs.answer: Because boundaries are set after the papers are marked, not before they are written. If a paper turns out harder than intended, the boundary for each grade moves down so that candidates are not penalised for the paper they happened to sit. That makes last year's boundary useful context and a poor target. The practical consequence for revision is that chasing a specific raw mark is less useful than removing the recurring mark-scheme misses, because the mark needed is not knowable in advance and the misses are.

faqs.question: What does Cambridge tiering mean for a Khobar student choosing Core or Extended Mathematics?
faqs.answer: Cambridge mathematics is examined at two tiers with overlapping content and different grade ceilings. A student entered for Core cannot reach the top grades no matter how well they perform, so the entry decision caps the outcome before any revision happens. Schools usually decide in Year 10 on the basis of classwork. If a family believes the decision is wrong, the time to raise it is then, with marked evidence, not in Year 11. The same logic applies to the Core and Extended papers in the separate sciences.

faqs.question: How is internally assessed coursework moderated once a Khobar school submits it?
faqs.answer: The school marks the work against the published criteria, then the board samples and reviews that marking and may adjust the school's marks up or down across the cohort. An individual student is not remarked in isolation. Two things follow. First, the quality of the school's own marking affects the whole group, so a well-run department is worth a great deal. Second, a tutor cannot influence moderation, only the standard of the work the student submits, which is the only lever anybody outside the school actually holds.

faqs.question: What is Ministry of Education equivalency, and when should a Khobar family start it?
faqs.answer: Equivalency, the mu'adalah decision, is the Ministry of Education's determination that a foreign or international school certificate is equivalent to the Saudi secondary certificate. Without it, a Saudi university does not treat an IB Diploma, A Levels or an American high school diploma as a qualifying certificate. Start asking in the first year of the final two, not in the last term, because the documents required take time to assemble and some universities state a maximum age for the certificate they will accept. Your school's counsellor deals with this regularly and is the right first call.

faqs.question: Why do Eastern Province students on an international curriculum find Tahsili harder than their own papers?
faqs.answer: Because Tahsili follows the Saudi national curriculum. Its subjects, mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology and English, overlap heavily with what an IB or IGCSE student has studied, but the sequence, emphasis and question style come from a different syllabus. Students arrive knowing the material and not recognising the questions, which reads as a content gap and is actually a framing gap. It is learnable, and it is much easier to learn in the year before the test than in the month before it. Treat it as a separate syllabus with familiar content.

faqs.question: Does Qudurat test syllabus content a Diploma student has already covered?
faqs.answer: Largely not. Qudurat, the General Aptitude Test, is run by the National Center for Assessment within the Education and Training Evaluation Commission and tests verbal and quantitative reasoning rather than taught syllabus material. It can be sat in Arabic or in English. That makes it a test of practised technique more than of revision: familiarity with the question types, the pacing and the answer format accounts for most of the improvement available. Diploma students often approach it as a content examination and spend their preparation time in the wrong place entirely.

faqs.question: Can a student in Al Khobar apply to a Saudi university and an overseas one in the same cycle?
faqs.answer: Yes, and many families in the Eastern Province do, but the two routes want different things at different times. Saudi applications turn on the equivalency decision and the Qiyas results. Overseas applications turn on predicted grades, subject prerequisites at Higher Level and, for some systems, additional tests or essays. The calendars do not align, so the practical risk is a collision between a Qiyas sitting and an overseas deadline. Map both timelines on one page in the first term of the final year and the clashes become visible while they are still movable.

faqs.question: Does Mathematics AA or Mathematics AI matter more for an engineering application from the Eastern Province?
faqs.answer: For engineering, physics and most quantitative degrees, Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is the course that is normally expected, and some departments state it outright. Applications and Interpretation is a respected course with a different purpose, weighted towards modelling and statistics, and it suits different degrees. The decision needs to be made against the published entry requirements of the actual universities a student is considering, before the subject choice is locked in, because changing course a year in is painful and sometimes impossible.

faqs.question: What does an overseas university ask for from a school leaver in the Dammam, Khobar and Dhahran cluster?
faqs.answer: Usually a predicted or final Diploma total, specified grades in named Higher Level subjects, and evidence of English language competence, with the details varying widely by country and course. Some systems want an additional admissions test or a written statement, and the deadlines sit earlier than families expect, often in the first term of the final school year. The documents themselves are rarely the difficulty; the timing is. Build the list of requirements from each university's own admissions pages and work backwards from the earliest deadline on it.

al-khobar.closingHeading: A sensible next step for an Al Khobar family
al-khobar.closingBody: Send three things: the subject with its level and board, the point in the year the student has reached, and the earliest hour that works on a bad traffic day rather than a good one. We will say whether a specialist in that exact syllabus is free in that window, and if nobody is, we will tell you so rather than offering a generalist. The first lesson is free, diagnostic, and ends with a written account of what is actually wrong, which is yours to keep whatever you decide next. Everything runs live online, one-to-one, on Arabia Standard Time.

alula.tutorsIntro: Each tutor below teaches one named subject at a named level over live video: Economics HL, Biology SL, Geography 0460. In a county where the local pool for any given Higher Level subject may be empty, the question stops being who is nearby and becomes who knows the paper your child will sit.

intro.heading: Four alternatives, and why families here usually end up with the fourth
paragraphs: A parent searching for IB and IGCSE tutors in AlUla is almost never comparing one local tutor against another. The county's resident school-age population is small, its international-curriculum provision is newer than in Riyadh, Jeddah or the Eastern Province, and the professional community has grown quickly around heritage, hospitality and the development work of the Royal Commission for AlUla. The result is a market with real demand and almost no local supply of subject specialists at examination level. So the real question is structural, and it has four answers.

The first is boarding or weekly accommodation near a school in a larger city, which solves subject availability and costs the family the child's presence at home. The second is splitting the household so one parent lives where the school is, which solves the schooling and strains everything else. The third is waiting: accepting the subjects the school can actually run this year and choosing around them, which is a legitimate decision and is sometimes the right one. The fourth is keeping the child at their school and bringing a subject specialist in over live video for the components that need one.

We obviously have an interest in the fourth. That is exactly why this page states the other three plainly, with what each costs and what each buys, and why the comparison table below is the first thing on it. A family that chooses boarding after reading this page has made a good decision; a family that chooses online tuition without ever weighing boarding has not made a decision at all. The honest case for video lessons here is narrow and strong: it is the only one of the four that changes which specialist teaches your child without changing where your child lives.

Everything we arrange is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the Kingdom; in-home visits are a service we run only in India. In a county several hours' drive north of Madinah, with domestic air connections and a small professional population, no in-home service could offer a Geography examiner or an Economics HL specialist anyway. What video does offer is a tutor matched to the syllabus rather than to the map.

The rest of this page is about how AlUla's school market is actually shaped — who teaches what, which subjects have no local specialist and what that does to a student's options — and then about mechanics: what the first month produces, how a grade is actually constructed from papers and criteria, what a predicted grade is and is not, and how the Sunday-to-Thursday week and the seasonal rhythm here shape a weekly slot. No calendar year appears anywhere on it, because a page that names one is wrong within twelve months.
bullets: All lessons are online and one-to-one; there is no in-home option in the Kingdom.
The comparison table weighs boarding, relocation, waiting and online support side by side.
Matching is by subject, level and component — not by year group or by proximity.
Cambridge and Pearson candidates here sit the June and November series; February/March is India-only.
A four-week review on marked work decides whether support continues, changes or stops.

alula.programmesIntro: Four frameworks reach families in this part of Madinah Province, through the local school, through a school in a larger city, or through a transfer. They differ most in what they hand a parent at the end of a term, which is the thing worth understanding before you buy any support at all.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: No external examinations and no subject grades in the familiar sense. Reporting is against conceptual understanding, approaches to learning and the learner profile, which is informative for a teacher and frequently opaque to a parent reading it for the first time. What a family can usefully track at this stage is reading age, written structure, number fluency and whether the child can explain a method out loud. The culminating exhibition is the first long independent task a child owns from start to finish.
programmes.countryNote: In AlUla the early-years cohort is small and mixed, with children arriving from national-curriculum schools, from abroad and from other international schools in the Kingdom. The practical risk is not falling behind but being taught a method twice in two different ways. Support at this age is a reconciliation job, and it is short: a term is usually enough to settle which approach the child will use and make it secure.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Each subject is assessed against four published criteria, marked out of eight each, and the descriptors are public. A parent can read exactly what Criterion D rewards and compare it against the feedback their child received, which makes the MYP unusually auditable if you know where to look. The Personal Project in the final year is assessed on the process journal as much as the product, and the standard and extended mathematics routes diverge enough to decide Diploma options later.
programmes.countryNote: MYP students in AlUla often carry strong general knowledge of the region's history and archaeology from living here, which helps in individuals and societies and does nothing for criterion discipline. The gap we see most is between what a student knows and what the descriptor is asking them to produce. Reading the four criteria aloud with a student and marking one of their own pieces against them is usually a revelation, and it takes one session.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Externally examined subject by subject against a published syllabus code — 0580 Mathematics, 0460 Geography, 0450 Business Studies, 0470 History, 0610 Biology. Core and Extended routes carry different papers and different grade ceilings. Grading is A*-G or 9-1 depending on the variant entered. Because the papers are short and the mark schemes are literal, IGCSE is the level at which technique is most visibly separable from knowledge, and the level at which a term of focused work shows up most clearly in a result.
programmes.countryNote: For AlUla families the IGCSE years are where the consequences of a small school become concrete, because option blocks are built around the staff available rather than around demand. A student who wants Geography and History and Business Studies may find two of the three in the same block. That is worth discovering in Year 9, when a conversation with the school can still change something, rather than in Year 10 when it cannot.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, graded 1-7 for 42 points, plus up to three points from the Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay matrix for a maximum of 45. Each subject combines externally examined papers with internally assessed work the school marks and the IB moderates. Papers for schools on a northern-hemisphere year are sat in the May session. Higher Level is not Standard Level with extra chapters; it changes how shared content is examined.
programmes.countryNote: The Diploma is the point at which AlUla's staffing arithmetic bites hardest, because a school needs a qualified specialist per subject per level and a small cohort cannot justify six Higher Level groups. Families here typically need outside support for one or two Higher Levels rather than across the board, which makes the spend narrow and the matching requirement precise. A generalist cannot cover Higher Level Economics or Biology credibly.

alula.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma subjects AlUla families ask for most, described by what the assessment actually rewards. The pattern across them is the same: students lose marks to command terms and mark-scheme wording far more often than to gaps in knowledge.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Definition, diagram, application, evaluation — a four-move structure the mark scheme expects every time. Higher Level adds a quantitative paper and a heavier evaluation load. The internally assessed portfolio of commentaries on real news articles is where most of the recoverable marks sit, because students choose articles with no clear policy question in them and then cannot evaluate anything.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study driven, with a pre-released case for the examined paper and an internally assessed research project. Students who know the tools still lose marks by applying them generically instead of to the organisation in front of them. 'Evaluate' here means a judgement supported by the case's own evidence, and a general answer about any business scores poorly however well written.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Short-answer and extended-response work plus fieldwork at Higher Level. Named case studies carry the marks, and students who revise themes without examples cap themselves around the middle bands. Command terms matter unusually much here: 'examine', 'evaluate' and 'to what extent' demand three different structures, and the region supplies strong real material on water, heritage management and tourism pressure.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Source work, essays and a historical investigation that the student designs. Paper 1's source questions are a technique, not a knowledge test: students who treat them as comprehension lose the marks for provenance and for cross-referencing. The investigation fails at the question stage more often than at the writing stage, exactly as coursework does in every other subject.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Precise terminology, process sequencing and an internally assessed scientific investigation worth a fifth of the grade. The commonest avoidable loss is answering 'explain' with a description. Higher Level extends shared topics in ways that change the questions asked about them rather than simply adding content to memorise.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Two written papers plus the investigation. The data booklet is permitted and underused, calculations are marked for method as well as answer, and organic mechanisms reward drilled practice over re-reading. Students arriving from a different board often have the content and not the question style, which is a fast fix and an easy one to miss.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: At Higher Level, two long papers plus Paper 3, an extended problem-solving paper worth a fifth of the grade, and the exploration. Paper 3 rewards building an argument through an unfamiliar context, which routine practice does not prepare a student for. Proof, series and calculus technique are where the Higher Level term time goes.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics with the graphic display calculator treated as a working tool. Interpretation carries the marks: a correct regression with no sentence saying what it means is worth little. Many engineering courses expect Analysis and Approaches instead, so the route decision needs the university destination in view from the MYP years.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Unseen analysis, a comparative essay, an internally assessed oral built around a global issue, and an extra essay at Higher Level. The oral rewards preparation that happens weeks earlier — extract choice and the link to the global issue — and punishes improvisation in a way that is obvious to an examiner on a recording.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: An interdisciplinary course that can satisfy either a science or an individuals-and-societies requirement, which is genuinely useful for a student in a school with constrained option blocks. It rewards systems reasoning and named examples; water management, land use and heritage protection in this part of the Kingdom provide unusually concrete ones.

alula.igcseSubjectsIntro: Cambridge IGCSE requests from AlUla concentrate in the humanities and business subjects the local option blocks most often collide, plus the sciences and mathematics that gate Higher Level entry later.

igcseSubjects.name: Geography (0460)
igcseSubjects.description: Case studies decide the grade. Students revise themes, examiners reward named places with figures attached. Map and graph skills are a separate discipline from the content and are examined as such, which makes them quick to improve.

igcseSubjects.name: History (0470)
igcseSubjects.description: Source-based papers plus depth study. Provenance, reliability and cross-referencing are techniques with mark-scheme wording behind them, and most students have never been shown the wording.

igcseSubjects.name: Business Studies (0450)
igcseSubjects.description: Short answers, data response and extended evaluation. Marks go missing in the evaluation questions, where students list advantages instead of reaching a supported judgement about the business in the stimulus.

igcseSubjects.name: Mathematics (0580)
igcseSubjects.description: Extended is what Diploma schools expect for Higher Level mathematics, and it caps differently from Core. The current Extended route includes a non-calculator paper, which exposes weak arithmetic fluency immediately.

igcseSubjects.name: Biology (0610)
igcseSubjects.description: Definitions must be exact, processes must be in order, and experimental design questions reward naming the control variables. Diagram labelling is the fastest set of marks to recover in a short run-up.

igcseSubjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510)
igcseSubjects.description: Reading, writing in a specified text type, and listening. Text type conventions — a report is not an article, an email is not an essay — are learnable in two sessions and are where able students quietly lose marks.

alula.regionsTitle: AlUla county and the places families here actually travel between
alula.regionsIntro: AlUla is a county, not a compact town, and the distances inside it shape a study week. These are the places families we support live in or move between, with what each one means for a weekly online slot.

regions.name: AlUla Old Town (AlDeera)
regions.note: The historic mudbrick settlement and the oldest part of the county, now restored and heavily visited. Families living near it work around visitor-season traffic and evening events, which makes a slot before 6pm steadier than one after it.

regions.name: Al Jadidah
regions.note: The arts district and one of the main residential concentrations, with cafés, studios and a walkable centre. Short journeys here mean the after-school window is genuinely usable, and an early-evening slot is easier to hold than in most of the county.

regions.name: The AlUla oasis and palm farms
regions.note: The cultivated valley floor running through the county, with scattered farm residences and agricultural work that follows its own daily rhythm. Connectivity varies by property, so a bandwidth check before the first session matters more here than it does in the town centre.

regions.name: Hegra (Al-Hijr)
regions.note: The Nabataean site that made the county internationally known and the Kingdom's first UNESCO World Heritage listing. Families working in site management and conservation often have fieldwork hours that run early, which pushes lessons towards the evening rather than straight after school.

regions.name: Ashar Valley
regions.note: Resort and hospitality development in the sandstone canyons east of the oasis. Hospitality rosters are the scheduling problem here, not distance: the parent who wants to sit in on a first session is frequently on shift when it would naturally run.

regions.name: AlUla International Airport area
regions.note: North-east of the oasis, with domestic connections that make a trip to Riyadh or Jeddah a day rather than a drive. This is why boarding at a school in a larger city is a real option here in a way it is not in more remote parts of the Kingdom.

regions.name: Tayma
regions.note: An ancient settlement north of the county on the historic trade route, with its own small resident population. Families here face the same subject-availability arithmetic as AlUla and fewer local alternatives again, which makes a fixed online slot the only practical form of specialist support.

regions.name: Madinah
regions.note: The provincial capital, several hours south, with a wider set of schools and a different term structure. Families comparing a move there are comparing subject availability at Higher Level, not facilities, and the comparison is worth making in writing before Year 10.

schoolClusters.note: The deepest pool of IB World Schools in the Kingdom and the most common destination for an AlUla family considering boarding or relocation. Diploma option blocks here are wider simply because cohorts are larger, which is the whole of the argument for moving and should be weighed against everything a move costs. Students we support attend schools of this kind; we have no relationship with any of them.

schoolClusters.city: Jeddah and the Red Sea coast
schoolClusters.note: Reachable from the county by a short domestic flight, and the alternative cluster for families who want a coastal city rather than the capital. Boards differ school by school here — some run the Diploma, some Cambridge courses, some both — and term dates differ from each other and from the Ministry of Education school year, so compare published calendars rather than assuming.

Dammam, Al Khobar, Dhahran and Jubail behave as a single school market, and families routinely live in one and attend school in another. It matters to AlUla families mainly as a transfer destination, because a parent's next posting inside the Kingdom often lands here and the receiving school's subject list decides whether a Diploma continues unbroken.

alula.schoolDisclaimer: Schools are named as ecosystem context for families weighing their options in and around AlUla. No affiliation, endorsement or relationship with any named school or group is implied.
alula.modesIntro: Four ways families here use one-to-one support, in rough order of how often an AlUla family actually needs them. Each is delivered over live video and each is reviewed on marked work after four weeks.

modes.title: One Higher Level subject, weekly
modes.description: The commonest arrangement in this county by some distance: a single Higher Level subject the school cannot staff with a specialist, taught weekly in a fixed slot alongside the school's own teaching. The tutor works to the school's scheme of work where one exists and to the subject guide where it does not, and reports against components rather than topics.
bullets: A named specialist in that subject and level, not a tutor covering two sciences
Written note after each session naming the component worked on
Past papers marked against the published scheme between sessions
Reviewed on marked work at four weeks and again at the end of term

modes.title: Coursework clinics against the criteria
modes.description: Scheduled sessions around a draft the student has already written: the tutor reads it against the published criteria, asks the questions the supervisor and examiner will ask, and names the criterion gaps. The student then rewrites it themselves. No tutor writes, drafts or completes any part of an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge essay or Personal Project.
bullets: Research question and method tested for feasibility before any data is collected
Feedback mapped to criterion letters and their mark allocations
A record of the exchange, so the school can see the work is the student's own
Timed to the school's internal deadlines rather than to ours

modes.title: Technique work in the run-up to a series
modes.description: A short block of sessions built on timed papers and real mark schemes rather than content, for a student whose knowledge is adequate and whose answers are not. The pattern is simple: sit the paper under time, mark it honestly, teach from the errors, repeat. Starting around eight weeks out gives this room to work; starting two weeks out does not.
bullets: Command-term drills before full papers, because that is where most marks leak
Marking against the published scheme, with the student marking one themselves
Mornings during study leave, evenings during term
Explicitly unsuitable for a student who is behind on content, and we will say so

modes.title: A bridging term after a transfer
modes.description: For a student arriving from a different board or a different country part-way through a course. The first fortnight produces a map: topics taught and not met, coursework started and under what deadline, and which board's conventions the student has internalised. The term then works down that list in priority order rather than following whatever came up in class that week.
bullets: A written topic and deadline map before teaching starts in earnest
Board conventions taught explicitly, not absorbed by accident
Progress measured against the map, so the gap is visibly closing
An honest read in week two on what one term can and cannot recover

sections.heading: The four options an AlUla family is actually weighing
paragraphs: Before any discussion of tutoring, a family here should put the real alternatives on one page. There are four, and three of them have nothing to do with us. Boarding or weekly accommodation near a school in a larger city buys the full option block and the peer group, and it costs fees, travel and the child being elsewhere. Splitting the household so one parent lives near the school buys the same academic result and transfers the cost onto the family rather than onto a school bill. Accepting what the local school can run this year costs nothing and may close a university route two years later. Bringing in a subject specialist over live video keeps the child at home and buys teaching in one or two components rather than a whole school.

The variable that decides between them is not money. It is how many subjects are a problem. If one Higher Level subject has no specialist, option four is obviously proportionate and the other three are not. If three subjects are compromised, if the peer group has effectively disappeared, or if the student needs laboratory access the school cannot provide, then boarding or relocation deserves serious weight and no amount of video tuition substitutes for it. We have told families that. It is a better conversation to have in Year 9 than in DP1.

The second variable is the student. A fourteen-year-old who works independently and wants to stay with their friends is well served by a weekly specialist slot. A sixteen-year-old who is drifting, in a cohort too small to produce academic competition, may need the environment more than the teaching. No tutor fixes an absent peer group over video, and anyone who tells you otherwise is selling.

The table below sets the four side by side on the axes that actually move a decision: what each fixes, what it costs in something other than money, how reversible it is, and what it cannot do. Read the last column first.

sections.heading: How AlUla's school market is actually shaped
paragraphs: The shape of this market follows from three facts. The resident school-age population is small. International-curriculum provision arrived recently and is still growing alongside the county's development. And a large part of the adult professional community is here on contracts tied to heritage, conservation, hospitality and infrastructure work, which means both the parent body and the teaching body turn over faster than in an established city. Each of those facts has an academic consequence a family can plan around once it is named.

A small cohort means option blocks are built around available staff, not around demand. One qualified specialist per subject is normal; two is a luxury. If that one teacher leaves between terms, the subject does not pause politely — the school covers it, usually competently and usually with someone whose own specialism is adjacent. Adjacent is fine for a Standard Level course in the first year. It is not fine for Higher Level Paper 3 or for supervising a scientific investigation in a subject the teacher did not study.

Newer provision also means fewer back-years of institutional memory. A school running its first or second Diploma cohort has not yet accumulated the folder of past investigations, graded exemplars, internally moderated samples and known-good research questions that a school in its fifteenth cohort hands to every new student without thinking about it. That absence is invisible to a parent and expensive to a student, because exemplars are how most teenagers work out what the standard actually looks like.

Finally, turnover in both directions produces a steady stream of mid-course arrivals and departures. Students come in from national-curriculum schools, from British schools abroad, from American-curriculum schools, each with a different idea of what an exam question wants. In a large school that mix is absorbed by setting and by sheer numbers. In a small one it sits inside a single class of twelve, and the teacher cannot run four conventions at once.
bullets: Option blocks follow staffing, so ask which subjects actually ran last cohort
One specialist per subject is normal here; cover teaching is adjacent, not expert
A young Diploma programme has few graded exemplars, which students need to calibrate
Mid-course arrivals bring four different exam conventions into one small class

sections.heading: Which subjects have no local specialist, and what that costs a student
paragraphs: The subjects that go unstaffed in a small school are predictable, because they are the ones with the smallest natural uptake and the scarcest teaching pool anywhere: Higher Level physics, Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, Higher Level chemistry where the teacher's own degree was in biology, Computer Science at Higher Level, Economics and Business Management where one teacher covers both, and second languages beyond the obvious ones. None of this is unique to AlUla. What is specific to AlUla is that there is no second school down the road to absorb the gap.

The cost lands in three places. First, Paper 3 and the Higher Level extension topics, where a non-specialist teaches the content correctly and cannot model the examiner's expectations because they have never marked them. Second, the internally assessed work, where supervision quality is the single largest controllable factor in the grade, and where a supervisor outside their own subject cannot tell a feasible research question from an unfeasible one. Third, predicted grades, which a teacher less familiar with the standard tends to set conservatively, and a conservative prediction closes university doors before any paper is sat.

That third consequence is the one families under-rate and the one worth acting on earliest. A predicted grade is a professional judgement by the school, used by universities to make conditional offers, and it is informed by the evidence in front of the teacher. If the only evidence is classwork marked by someone outside their specialism, the prediction carries that uncertainty. Marked past-paper work, assessed against real schemes by a specialist, is evidence a school can take into account, and gathering it early in DP2 is more useful than arguing about a prediction after it has been submitted.

What this means practically is that support here should be bought narrowly and early rather than broadly and late. One Higher Level subject, from the start of DP1, focused on the components a non-specialist cannot cover, usually does more than three subjects bought in panic in the final term.
bullets: Higher Level physics, Mathematics AA HL and Higher Level computer science go unstaffed most often
A non-specialist can teach content and cannot model examiner expectations
Coursework supervision quality is the largest controllable factor in that grade
Marked specialist work early in DP2 is evidence a school can weigh for a prediction

sections.heading: What a first month produces, and the decision at the end of it
paragraphs: A month is long enough to know whether support is working and short enough that nobody has lost much if it is not. We structure it the same way every time, so a parent can hold us to it rather than relying on a feeling about whether lessons are going well. The first session is a diagnostic on real work: a past paper, a current coursework draft, a returned school assessment. It ends with a component-level read in writing — what is secure, what is weak, what order to address it in, and roughly how long each item should take.

The second and third sessions teach the first item on that list and set work between them. The fourth sits a timed piece and marks it against the published scheme. At the end of the fourth week you have three things: the initial read, two sets of marked homework, and a timed piece marked to the real standard. That is evidence, not atmosphere, and it supports a genuine decision. Continue, change tutor, change the component being targeted, or stop.

We ask families to make that decision out loud, because the failure mode in tutoring is not a bad tutor. It is a plausible arrangement that nobody ever evaluates, running for three terms because cancelling feels awkward. If the marked work has not moved and the tutor cannot explain why in specific terms, that is a change-tutor conversation and we would rather have it in week four than in month six.

One caution about expectations in that window. Four weeks reliably moves technique — command terms, structure, mark-scheme literacy, working shown — and reliably does not close a two-year content gap. If the diagnostic says content, expect the first visible movement in marked work later, and judge the month on whether the gap list is shrinking rather than on whether a grade has jumped.

table.caption: THE FIRST FOUR WEEKS
rows: Diagnostic on real work: a paper, a draft or a returned assessment
