sections.heading: Equivalency, Qudurat and Tahsili: the endgame nobody writes about
paragraphs: For a family planning on university inside the Kingdom, the IB Diploma is one of three things that have to be in place, and the other two are frequently discovered late. The first is equivalency: a Ministry of Education decision that treats the foreign certificate as equivalent to the Saudi secondary certificate. The second and third are the national tests run by ETEC through its assessment centre — Qudurat, the general aptitude test, and Tahsili, the achievement test.

Qudurat tests verbal and quantitative reasoning rather than syllabus content, and is sat in Arabic or in English. Because it is a reasoning test, an international-curriculum student is usually no worse placed than anybody else, and preparation is mostly about format and timing. Tahsili is the harder problem. It covers science-stream subjects — mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology and English — and its content follows the Saudi national curriculum. An IB or IGCSE student has studied overlapping material in a different order, with different emphases and different terminology, which is precisely why they often find it harder than their own examinations. That single fact is worth more to a Saudi parent than most of what this market publishes, and almost nobody writes it down.

Universities publish their own admission criteria combining school results with the two tests, and the weightings differ by university and by programme, with competitive engineering, medicine and science programmes leaning hardest on the achievement test. This page does not publish any threshold or formula, because they differ by institution and programme and third-party sources disagree with each other. The only reliable source is the university's own published criteria, and a family should read them directly rather than take a tutoring site's word for it. Some universities also state a maximum age for the secondary certificate they will accept, which affects students who take a gap.

Where tutoring fits is narrow and worth stating honestly. A tutor can teach the subject content a test covers and can teach test format and timing. A tutor cannot promise a score, cannot promise admission, and cannot tell you what a given programme will require this cycle. Nor can anybody shorten an equivalency decision. What a family can do is start the process in the right order and early, which is the whole purpose of the table above.

sections.heading: Switching curriculum, and when in the year it is realistic
paragraphs: The Kingdom's international population moves, and curriculum switches are therefore routine rather than exceptional. The question families ask is whether a switch is possible; the more useful question is when, because the same move is straightforward at one point in the year and damaging at another.

Moving from a national-curriculum school into IGCSE transfers more than families expect in mathematics and the sciences, where content is often ahead, and less than they expect in written style: answers are compressed, method is implicit, and the extended-response marks that reward explanation go unclaimed. Moving from a British route into the Diploma transfers content well and assessment habits poorly — command terms, Theory of Knowledge and an independent investigation at internal assessment scope are all new. Moving from an American route is the reverse again: breadth for depth, continuous assessment for examination weighting, and Higher Level sciences and mathematics as the pressure points.

Timing decides the cost. A switch at the start of a course is a change of plan. A switch after the first of the two final years has begun is a change of plan plus an assessed-work problem, because internal assessment timelines differ between schools even inside one board, and a student can arrive with a draft the new school will not accept or with nothing started while the cohort is on a second draft. A switch in the final year is rarely advisable and is sometimes unavoidable, in which case the first conversation belongs with the receiving school's coordinator in the first week, with the actual drafts in hand.

What a receiving school asks for is predictable: reports, transcripts, any completed coursework, and evidence of what has been covered. What a family should ask in return is just as predictable and more often forgotten. Which subjects run at the level the student needs, this year rather than in the prospectus. Who supervises Extended Essays and how many each supervisor carries. What happens if a chosen Higher Level subject does not attract enough students. And how the school's own calendar compares with the one the family is leaving, since two schools in one city can be on different years.

sections.heading: Making a weekly slot survive the year
paragraphs: A good tutor in an unstable slot produces less than an average tutor in a stable one, and this is the part of the arrangement a family controls completely. The school week runs Sunday to Thursday. Sunday and Monday evenings are the two most useful slots, because teaching lands before the week's work is written rather than after it has been handed in. Thursday evening is the least useful: the weekend starts that night and a student will attend politely and absorb very little.

Arabia Standard Time is UTC+3 and the Kingdom does not change its clocks, which makes a Saudi-pinned slot the stable one by definition. Write the hour in Saudi local time in the confirmation and let the tutor absorb any seasonal change in their own country. The second question, which parents ask far less often, is what the tutor's own working week looks like: somebody teaching in a school on a Monday-to-Friday timetable is at work during your two best evenings, and no amount of goodwill fixes that.

Then there are the predictable interruptions, and the fix for each is to decide in advance rather than week by week. During Ramadan, school days shorten and household routines change, so the sensible approach is to agree one shifted hour a fortnight ahead and hold it for the whole month. Because Ramadan drifts earlier each year against the Gregorian calendar, it lands at a different point of the course for each cohort, so last year's arrangement is not a guide. Long school holidays are the other case: keeping the slot at reduced frequency usually beats releasing it, because reclaiming a good evening in a busy autumn is harder than holding it.

The last piece is what happens around a series. In the weeks before a June or November entry, outside sessions should complement the school's revision timetable rather than compete with it, which means the tutor needs to know what the school is running. Entries themselves are administrative and dated: Cambridge and Pearson both run June and November series for candidates in the Kingdom, and the February and March series is available only to candidates in India, which families here are wrongly told often enough to be worth repeating. Your school's examinations officer holds every real date.

process.title: Say where in the year your child is
process.description: The first message that can be matched well names the subject, the level, the board, and where the student sits in the course — first year, final year, eight weeks from a series, newly arrived from another system. The same subject request needs a different tutor at each of those points, and the stage is the detail families most often leave out.

process.title: We shortlist on checkable evidence only
process.description: Tutors are shortlisted on the subject guide and level they have taught, and on marking experience recorded as board, subject, component and number of series. Nothing is ranked, because a ranking would be a number we invented. Where a tutor cannot state their experience in checkable terms, it is not published as a credential.

process.title: Use the free trial hour to test the claims
process.description: One hour at no charge with the matched specialist, used as a diagnostic rather than a sales call. Ask which board and component they have marked and across how many series, and ask what they will not do with assessed work. A tutor who answers precisely has taught the course. You will also learn whether your child can work with them.

process.title: Pin the slot and check the tutor's week
process.description: The hour is written in Arabia Standard Time, and the tutor absorbs any clock change in their own country. We check that their working week leaves your Sunday and Monday evenings free, because those are the two most useful slots in a Saudi school week and a Monday-to-Friday teacher elsewhere cannot hold either of them.

process.title: Agree a first month a parent can audit
process.description: Three or four specific changes, written down, each verifiable without knowing the subject: writes uncertainty correctly, finishes the paper with time to check, stops losing method marks to mental arithmetic. A plan nobody can check is a plan nobody can be held to, and that is how a term disappears without a decision being taken.

process.title: Review against marked work
process.description: At the end of the first month we look at school assessment marks and at marked written work with the tutor's annotations beside the school's. If the match is wrong we change the tutor; if the plan was wrong we rewrite it; if the work is not being done between sessions we say so. The review date is set before the first lesson.

whyPoints.title: No ranking, because none can be verified
whyPoints.description: We do not claim to be the top provider in the Kingdom and we publish no satisfaction rate, star rating or tutor count. No authority ranks tutors here, so any such figure would be ours and unverifiable. What is published is the tutor's subject guide, level and marking experience, in a form a parent can test in an hour.

whyPoints.title: Clear about what nobody licenses
whyPoints.description: The Ministry of Education licenses schools and decides certificate equivalency; ETEC evaluates schools and runs the national tests. Neither licenses a tutor, and IB Gram holds no accreditation, approval or partnership from either, nor from the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. Saying so is more useful to a parent than implying the opposite.

whyPoints.title: A national pool rather than a drivable radius
whyPoints.description: Matching runs over everyone who teaches that subject guide at that level and can hold a Saudi evening slot. That is why a family in Jubail, Hofuf or Khamis Mushait chooses from the same tutors as a family in north Riyadh, and why the difference is largest in scarce subjects at Higher Level.

whyPoints.title: Honest about the in-home trade-off
whyPoints.description: A tutor in the room is harder for a teenager to ignore and reads the student more easily. Those are real advantages and a family whose problem is motivation should weigh them. Our case for online teaching is narrower and more specific: depth of specialism, no travel in the price, and a slot that survives a relocation.

whyPoints.title: The assessed-work boundary, stated first
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach method, explain published criteria and give feedback on the student's own Internal Assessment, Extended Essay, TOK essay or Personal Project. They produce no part of it, and the student is told so in the first session. A record of each session is available if a school ever asks for one.

whyPoints.title: Online delivery, said plainly
whyPoints.description: Lessons are one to one over live video on Arabia Standard Time. We do not send a tutor to an address in the Kingdom and home visits in Saudi Arabia are not something we sell; in-home teaching is a service we run only in India. The search phrase is what parents type, and this is what we actually do.

faqs.question: Is any tutor in Saudi Arabia officially licensed or ranked by an authority?
faqs.answer: No. Private and international schools are licensed by the Ministry of Education and evaluated through ETEC, and the IB authorises schools to offer its programmes, but none of those processes extends to private tutors. There is no register, no licence requirement and no public ranking of tutoring providers in the Kingdom. That is why a claim to be the top choice means nothing on its own, and why a parent's only reliable route is to check the specific things a tutor can evidence: the subject guide taught, the level, the component marked and the number of series.

faqs.question: Our school says it is accredited — does that tell me anything about a tutor working with its students?
faqs.answer: Nothing at all, and the two are easy to conflate. A school's licence and accreditation concern the institution: premises, governance, curriculum provision and staffing, handled by the Ministry of Education and ETEC, with some schools also using international accreditation bodies. A private tutor sits entirely outside that framework, whether or not their student attends an accredited school, and nobody audits their subject knowledge or teaching. So the useful follow-up to the word accredited is always what exactly is accredited, and then a separate set of questions about the person actually teaching.

faqs.question: Does an IB Diploma earned in the Kingdom need anything extra before a Saudi university will accept it?
faqs.answer: Yes. A foreign or international school certificate requires an equivalency decision from the Ministry of Education before a Saudi university treats it as equivalent to the Saudi secondary certificate, and this applies to an IB Diploma, A Levels and an American high school diploma alike. It is a separate administrative process with its own requirements, applied for after results are published. Families who learn about it late lose time between certificate and offer. Universities also publish their own admission criteria, which may include the national aptitude and achievement tests, and those criteria should be read directly.

faqs.question: Why do international-curriculum students find the national achievement test harder than their own examinations?
faqs.answer: Because its content follows the Saudi national curriculum rather than theirs. The achievement test covers mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology and English, and an IB or IGCSE student has usually studied overlapping material in a different order, with different emphases and different terminology. The knowledge is largely there; the framing is not. The aptitude test is a different matter, since it assesses reasoning rather than syllabus content and preparation is mostly about format and timing. No page should publish a required score, because requirements differ by university and by programme.

faqs.question: How does the Ministry of Education license private and international schools here?
faqs.answer: Schools operate under a licence issued by the Ministry, and school evaluation and accreditation runs through ETEC, which provides services for national school accreditation and for approving the international accreditation bodies many international schools also use. What this covers is the institution rather than the individual lesson: whether the school may operate, what it may offer, and how it is evaluated. For a parent, the useful follow-up is not whether a school is licensed but which subjects it can actually staff at the level their child needs this year.

faqs.question: What does ETEC do, and what does it not do?
faqs.answer: The Education and Training Evaluation Commission handles education evaluation in the Kingdom, including school accreditation services and the approval of international accreditation bodies, and it runs the national aptitude and achievement tests through its assessment centre. What it does not do is license, inspect or rank private tutors or tutoring companies, publish a required test score that applies everywhere, or make admission decisions — those belong to individual universities, which set and publish their own criteria. No tutoring provider holds any approval or accreditation from it.

faqs.question: What happens when a school cannot run a Higher Level subject a student has chosen?
faqs.answer: Several things, none of them announced in a prospectus. The subject may run only if enough students choose it, and a small cohort can mean it does not run at all. It may run with one teacher covering both levels, which usually compresses the Higher Level extension at the end of the year. Or the school may arrange remote provision, leaving the student without a teacher in the building. Ask before enrolling which subjects run at Higher Level this year, how many teachers the department has, and what the minimum cohort is.

faqs.question: Why do families in one Saudi city school their children in another?
faqs.answer: Because provision is uneven and catchments are not administrative. The Dammam, Al Khobar and Dhahran conurbation behaves as one market, so a family living in one town and schooling in another is ordinary there. Makkah's families commonly use the Jeddah cluster roughly 80km west. Al Ahsa is an hour and a half from the coastal schools, which pushes families towards boarding, weekly commuting or relocating. In each case the daily journey, not the school's quality, is what ends up setting what time a weekday lesson can start.

faqs.question: How does a school's own calendar differ from the Ministry of Education school calendar?
faqs.answer: Substantially, and it catches relocating families. MoE public schools run a two-semester year starting in late August and ending in late June, with an autumn break, a midyear break and an Eid Al Fitr break. International and British-curriculum schools set their own calendars and most run three terms, with dates that differ school by school inside the same city. Two schools a few streets apart can therefore be on different years, so always work from the published calendar of the school your child actually attends rather than from any general one.

faqs.question: Moving from an MoE school into IGCSE, what carries over and what has to be rebuilt?
faqs.answer: Usually more content than expected and less written technique. Mathematics and the sciences are often ahead or level, and the obstacle is the style of answer: compressed working, implicit method, and the extended-response marks that reward explanation left unclaimed. English-medium technical vocabulary is the other common gap, particularly in the sciences. The practical plan is a diagnostic first, then writing practice against real mark schemes rather than more content teaching. Tier decisions also matter immediately, because a Core entry caps the available grade before any teaching starts.

faqs.question: When in the school year is a curriculum switch actually realistic?
faqs.answer: At the start of a course it is a change of plan. After the first of the two final years has begun it becomes a change of plan plus an assessed-work problem, because internal assessment timelines differ between schools even inside one board and a student can arrive with a draft the new school will not accept. In the final year it is rarely advisable and sometimes unavoidable, in which case the first conversation belongs with the receiving school's coordinator in the first week, with the actual drafts and transcripts in hand rather than described from memory.

faqs.question: Is it better to finish IGCSE at the previous school or restart in the Kingdom?
faqs.answer: If the student is in the final IGCSE year and the entries are already made, finishing where they are is almost always better, even at some inconvenience, because entries, coursework and centre arrangements are all tied to that school. If the move happens earlier, restarting locally is usually cleaner than trying to run a remote arrangement. The deciding questions are whether the same board and syllabus are offered, whether any coursework can carry across, and whether the receiving school can enter the student for the series they are aiming at.

faqs.question: Which subjects are hardest to pick up after a mid-course switch into the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Mathematics at Higher Level, the sciences at Higher Level where extension topics have already been taught, and any second language. Mathematics is hardest because it is cumulative: a gap in the first term reappears in every later topic rather than staying where it was. Sciences are hard because the internal investigation may already be under way. A language is hard because fluency is built over years, not terms. Subjects built on essays and sources are generally the most recoverable, because the skill transfers even when the content does not.

faqs.question: How late can a lesson start if the school run in our city finishes late?
faqs.answer: Later than most families assume, and that is one of the practical advantages of the online format. Where a parent is driving back across Riyadh or along the Jeddah spine, the realistic start is often after six, and in some households after seven. The important thing is to set the slot against the real return time rather than the hopeful one: a lesson agreed for five that starts at ten past, every week, is a fifty-minute lesson paid for as an hour. Better to book the later slot and keep it intact.

faqs.question: What happens to a weekly slot during the long holiday between school years?
faqs.answer: The useful options are to hold it at reduced frequency or to release it formally, and those are different things. Holding it means the same hour is still yours in the autumn, which matters because reclaiming a good evening in a busy term is harder than keeping it. Reduced frequency also lets the break do the work it is uniquely good for: collecting data for assessed work, repairing one weak subject, reading for an extended piece. Trying to repair three subjects over a holiday repairs none and starts the year tired.

faqs.question: If weekday evenings are full, do Saturday morning lessons work for an IB student?
faqs.answer: They work well for intensive blocks and poorly as a substitute for a weekday slot. Friday and Saturday are the weekend here, and a longer Saturday morning session suits timed paper practice before a series, where a student needs an uninterrupted stretch rather than an hour. For ordinary weekly teaching, a weekday evening is better, because what is taught can be used in school the next day. If the week is genuinely full, the honest conversation is about dropping something rather than adding a weekend commitment.

faqs.question: How many hours a week of outside teaching does an IB student actually need?
faqs.answer: For one subject, one hour a week plus the work set between sessions is the normal and sufficient answer, and more than that usually indicates the wrong plan rather than a harder subject. Two subjects can justify two hours, ideally not stacked in one evening and never with the same tutor covering both. More than three hours a week across subjects is a sign that something structural needs addressing — a level that is wrong, a gap from an earlier year, or work not being done between lessons, which no amount of extra tutoring fixes.

best-ib-home-tutor.closingHeading: Check four things, then test them in a free hour
best-ib-home-tutor.closingBody: Nobody can tell you who the best IB home tutor in Saudi Arabia is, because no authority ranks or licenses tutors here. What you can do is check four things — the subject guide and level taught, the component marked and over how many series, the stated boundary on assessed work, and a first month written so you can audit it. Send us the subject, the level and where your child is in the year, and we will put a specialist in a free trial hour so you can test all four yourself. Lessons are taught one to one over live video on Arabia Standard Time, timed to a Sunday-to-Thursday week.

intro.heading: A better question than who is best
paragraphs: Families searching for the best IB IGCSE tutor in Saudi Arabia are asking something reasonable in a form nobody can answer. There is no register of tutors in the Kingdom, no published comparison, and no inspection body that rates private tutors the way the system rates schools. Every ranking you will read on a vendor page was written by the vendor. So the honest version of the question is narrower and much more useful: which tutor is right for this student, in this subject, at this point in the year?

That last clause does most of the work, and it is why this page opens on the calendar rather than on credentials. A Year 10 student in the autumn term needs content taught properly and a tier decision argued early. The same student two terms later needs timed papers and mark-scheme discipline, and the teacher who was ideal in the autumn may be the wrong choice in the spring. A student in the first Diploma year needs an internal assessment timeline more than they need revision. These are different jobs.

Around all of that sits a system most newly arrived families have not met before. Private and international schools in the Kingdom hold a licence from the Ministry of Education. School evaluation and accreditation runs through the Education and Training Evaluation Commission, which operates e-services for national school accreditation and for the approval of international accreditation bodies. None of that applies to a private tutor, and a provider implying otherwise is misrepresenting what those bodies do.

At the far end of the school years sits the equivalency decision — mu'adalah — which a foreign or international certificate needs from the Ministry of Education before a Saudi university treats it as equivalent to the national secondary certificate, plus the Qudurat and Tahsili tests run through Qiyas. Those two things reach backwards into subject choices made years earlier, which is exactly why a page about choosing a tutor has to mention them at all.

One point of plain fact before any of it: teaching for Saudi families is delivered online, one to one, over live video. Nobody is sent to a Saudi address; in-home visits are something we run only in India. For a family in Al Ahsa, Tabuk or Abha that is not a compromise but the whole point, because the pool of people who have actually taught a given Higher Level component is national and international rather than local.

The rest of this page follows that order. It starts with the course calendar and what each stage of it actually requires, moves through the regulatory picture a family has to read correctly, sets out the equivalency and testing route to a Saudi university, then deals with assessed coursework, the subject topics that generate outside requests, and the staffing limits of a school cluster. It ends with the three questions that let you judge a tutor yourself, since nobody else is going to do it for you.

programmes.countryNote: Settle the tier first: a Core entry caps the grade at C and the decision closes with the entry deadline. Ask which tier each subject is entered at, and keep the answer.

programmes.description: Criterion-referenced subject assessment ending in the Personal Project. A grade from 1 to 7 is assembled from strand descriptors rather than a single paper, so knowing the content is necessary and not sufficient.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The Higher Level Paper 3 extension is a different kind of question: a long, structured problem on unfamiliar ground. Few local teachers have taught it often.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The extended-response marks are where strong students still lose. A correct calculation with no stated assumption or defined symbol is not a full answer.

subjects.name: Chemistry

sections.heading: Where your child sits in the year decides what good looks like
paragraphs: A tutor who is right in one term can be the wrong choice two terms later, and that is the most useful idea on this page. Early in a course the job is content and habit. The student has gaps from the previous stage, a tier or level decision is still open, and nobody has looked at a mark scheme yet. What a family wants then is a patient subject teacher who will go back and fix foundations without making the student feel remedial.

Mid-course, the job changes. The syllabus is mostly taught and the marks are being lost somewhere specific. Now the right tutor is the one who can look at a marked paper and name the component, who marks against the published scheme rather than a model answer, and who makes the student do the marking themselves. Patience matters less here than precision. A teacher who re-explains topics kindly will keep the student comfortable and the grade still.

In the final weeks the job narrows again, to technique and triage. Which questions to attempt first, how many marks a command term is worth, what to do with the last twenty minutes of a paper. Nothing new is learned usefully at this point, and a tutor who proposes starting a fresh topic three weeks out is selling hours rather than teaching. The table below sets out what to ask for at each stage, because the request a family makes is what decides the match it gets.

sections.heading: How schools here are licensed and evaluated, and what that cannot tell you
paragraphs: Private and international schools in the Kingdom operate under a licence from the Ministry of Education. Separately, school evaluation and accreditation runs through the Education and Training Evaluation Commission, usually shortened to ETEC, which operates e-services covering national school accreditation and the approval of international accreditation bodies. A school may additionally be authorised to run IB programmes, or be a registered Cambridge examination centre, which are decisions made by those organisations rather than by a Saudi regulator.

All of that is genuinely worth understanding, and all of it is about schools. No part of it extends to a private tutor. There is no licence, no register and no evaluation framework for tutoring in the Kingdom, which means anybody can describe themselves however they like. A provider that implies a regulator has approved it is either confused or hoping you are, and that is a reason for caution rather than reassurance.

So what can a parent actually check? Whether the tutor names your child's syllabus code and components correctly. Whether they can explain what the Higher Level extension adds. Whether they will look at a piece of marked work and tell you what they would do first. Whether they say plainly what they cannot fix in the time available. These are all verifiable in a single conversation, and they are worth more than any claim about standing that nobody publishes. It is also worth separating two things families often merge: a school's accreditation describes an institution and its processes, while a tutor's usefulness is a question about one person and one component. Neither tells you anything reliable about the other.

sections.heading: Equivalency and the Qiyas tests reach back into subject choices
paragraphs: A foreign or international school certificate needs an equivalency decision from the Ministry of Education before a Saudi university will treat it as equivalent to the national secondary certificate. That applies to an IB Diploma, to A Levels and to an American high school diploma alike. Some universities also state a maximum age for the certificate they will accept, so a long gap between leaving school and applying is worth checking rather than assuming.

Alongside it sit two tests delivered by the National Center for Assessment, Qiyas, under ETEC. Qudurat, the General Aptitude Test, measures verbal and quantitative reasoning rather than taught content, and can be sat in Arabic or in English. Tahsili, the Achievement Test, covers the science-stream subjects: mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology and English. Universities publish their own admission criteria combining school results with these tests, and the weighting differs by university and by programme.

The reason this belongs on a page about choosing a tutor is that it reaches backwards. Tahsili follows the Saudi national curriculum, so an international-curriculum student has usually met the material in a different order and a different vocabulary — a mapping problem before a revision one. And a student who drops a science at Standard Level in the first Diploma year has quietly narrowed their options. No tutor can promise an admission outcome, and no cut-off figures appear here: check them with the university itself. The practical move is to read the published criteria for two or three target programmes while the student is still choosing subjects, rather than after the final results arrive and nothing can be changed.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do with an internal assessment or Extended Essay
paragraphs: Assessed coursework is where this market is least honest, so it is worth being exact. The school owns the process. An Extended Essay has a supervisor at school who holds the formal reflection sessions and signs off the work; an internal assessment is supervised by the subject teacher; a Personal Project has a school supervisor too. A tutor sits outside all of that, which means a tutor can add real value and can also, if careless or dishonest, put a qualification at risk.

Legitimate help is substantial. Teaching the criteria strand by strand, so the student knows what each one pays for. Testing a research question for feasibility — is the data obtainable at this school, in this time, within the word limit. Teaching the statistics or the referencing the student needs to handle their own results. Reading a draft the student wrote and saying where an argument is unsupported, a method is not reproducible, or a conclusion goes further than the evidence.

What falls outside it is simple to state. No tutor here will write, draft or complete any part of an internal assessment, an Extended Essay, a Theory of Knowledge essay or a Personal Project, and a tutor asked to do so will decline and explain why. Keep your own dated record of drafts as the work progresses. Nobody needs it until a question is asked, and then it is the only thing that answers it properly. Tell the school's supervisor that outside support exists, too: transparency costs nothing and removes the question before it is raised.

sections.heading: The trouble spots that most often need teaching from outside
paragraphs: Certain topics generate outside requests year after year, and they are not random. In Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level it is Paper 3 and the proof work: a long structured problem on unfamiliar ground, which rewards sustained reasoning rather than a remembered method. Students who have been taught procedurally stall at the second part of the question, and schools often have one teacher who has taught it more than twice.

In Physics the recoverable marks sit in the extended responses rather than the calculations. A student produces the right number, states no assumption, defines no symbol, and loses half the available credit while believing the answer was correct. In Biology the equivalent is the six-mark question: six separate true facts score about four, because the scheme pays for linked reasoning. Both are technique problems masquerading as knowledge problems, which is why they respond quickly to teaching.

At IGCSE the pattern is different. Moles and stoichiometry in Chemistry, and algebraic fluency in Mathematics, are the two gaps that surface a full year later in the first Diploma term. A student can pass the IGCSE comfortably with weak quantitative work and then struggle badly within weeks of starting Higher Level. If a family is choosing where to spend on tutoring at Year 11, those two areas repay it more than anything else. English as a Second Language is the third candidate, for a different reason: marks there move on summary technique and register rather than vocabulary, so a confident speaker can sit well below their spoken level on paper and nobody notices until a mock.

sections.heading: What the local school picture cannot staff, and how families work around it
paragraphs: School size decides subject availability more than curriculum does. A school running one Diploma cohort cannot offer every Higher Level option, because an option with four students in it does not pay for a teacher. So a family can enrol at a school authorised to run the Diploma and still find that the subject their child wants is not on the timetable, or is taught by somebody covering it rather than specialising in it. That is not a failing; it is arithmetic.

The workarounds families actually use are worth naming. Some commute across a city, or between the three Eastern Province cities, to reach a school that runs the subject. Some take the subject online through a provider the school accepts. Some keep the school subject and add outside teaching for the component the school cannot cover well. Compound and camp schools, serving a single employer community, have their own version of this problem in a smaller catchment.

Before enrolling, ask the school three specific questions in writing: which Higher Level subjects actually ran last cohort rather than which are listed, how many teachers cover each science, and what happens if a chosen option does not attract enough students. The answers tell you more about the next two years than any prospectus will, and they also tell you where outside teaching is likely to be needed. Ask the same questions again a year later if a teacher leaves, because a cluster with one specialist per subject has no bench, and the loss of a single teacher reshapes a cohort's options within a term.

sections.heading: Judging a tutor when nobody publishes a ranking
paragraphs: Since no table of tutors exists, the family has to run its own comparison, and three questions do most of the work. Which syllabus code and components does my child sit? What does the Higher Level extension add that Standard Level does not have? Here is a marked answer — why did it score what it scored? Somebody teaching the course answers all three in specifics. A subject graduate revising alongside the student stalls on the second or the third.

Then use the trial lesson as evidence rather than as a sales call. Send a question the student got wrong, with the student's own working, before the session. Watch whether the tutor diagnoses the error or re-teaches the topic, whether the student is doing most of the talking by the halfway point, and whether there is a concrete next step at the end. Reassurance is pleasant and tells you nothing about the next six months.

Be sceptical of every unverifiable number. Advertised rates in this market are published by the providers themselves — a tutoring-company listing puts IB subject tutoring in Riyadh from about SAR 180, rising to roughly SAR 200 to 220 for Higher Level tracks — and those are advertised figures, not an average and not our price. Success percentages, star ratings and headcounts are worth even less. No tutor can promise a grade, and the ones who try have told you what you needed to know about them before you paid anything.

faqs.question: What may a tutor do with a Chemistry internal assessment draft, and what must they never touch?
faqs.answer: A tutor may teach the criteria, test whether the research question is measurable with school equipment, check that the uncertainty and error treatment is sound, and comment on a draft the student has written. What they must not touch is the text itself: no rewriting, no supplying paragraphs, no producing the analysis. The school's subject teacher supervises the work formally, and the student's own hands stay on the keyboard throughout.

faqs.question: How many drafts of an Extended Essay can a tutor read before it stops being the student's work?
faqs.answer: The number matters less than what happens to each one. Reading several drafts and returning comments is legitimate, because the student is the one acting on them. The line is crossed when the comments become the text: suggested sentences, rewritten paragraphs, supplied structure the student did not devise. Your school sets its own expectations on formal drafts and reflection sessions, so ask the supervisor what they permit and work inside that.

faqs.question: Who supervises the Extended Essay at a Saudi school, and where does a tutor fit around them?
faqs.answer: A school-appointed supervisor holds the formal role, including the reflection sessions, and that cannot be delegated to anybody outside. A tutor works alongside it: helping test a research question for feasibility, teaching the subject content the essay needs, and giving feedback on the student's own drafts. Keep the supervisor informed that outside support exists. Transparency costs nothing and removes any question later about whose work it is.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help choose a Personal Project topic in the Middle Years Programme?
faqs.answer: They can help the student interrogate their own idea, which is different from supplying one. Useful questions are whether the goal is specific enough to assess, whether the evidence of process can realistically be collected, and whether the criteria can all be met by that project. The topic should come from the student. A tutor who arrives with a list of projects has misunderstood what the component is for.

faqs.question: What record should a family keep to show an internal assessment is the student's own work?
faqs.answer: Dated drafts, in order, saved as separate files rather than overwritten. Notes from the student's own planning. The raw data or working, not only the finished write-up. Keep any feedback received, from the school and from a tutor, so the trail shows comment and response rather than text appearing from nowhere. None of this is needed until a question is asked, and then nothing else answers it as well.

faqs.question: Is proofreading an assessed piece allowed, and where exactly is the line drawn?
faqs.answer: Pointing out that spelling, punctuation or referencing need attention is normally acceptable; silently correcting the text is not, because the corrected words are then not the student's. The practical test is whether the student has to do something after the feedback. Flagging a pattern of errors leaves work to do. Returning a clean document leaves none. Check your school's own written policy, since schools draw this line in slightly different places.

faqs.question: Which topics in Mathematics AA at Higher Level most often need teaching from outside?
faqs.answer: Paper 3 work and formal proof, consistently. The paper sets a long structured problem on unfamiliar ground, and it rewards sustained reasoning rather than a remembered method, so students taught procedurally stall partway through. Complex numbers and the harder calculus also generate requests. Schools frequently have a single teacher who has taught Paper 3 more than once, which is why the subject appears in outside requests more than any other.

faqs.question: Why do strong students still lose marks on the Physics extended-response questions?
faqs.answer: Because the mark scheme pays for reasoning that strong students perform silently. The calculation is right, but no assumption is stated, symbols go undefined, and the final answer carries no unit or no comment on whether it is reasonable. Half the credit on those questions sits in exactly those moves. It is a technique problem rather than a knowledge problem, which is why it responds to a few weeks of targeted work.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE Chemistry topics cause the most trouble in the first Diploma term?
faqs.answer: Moles and stoichiometry, every time. A student can pass IGCSE Chemistry comfortably with shaky quantitative work, because other topics carry the grade, and then meet Higher Level calculations within weeks of starting the Diploma. Energetics and the mechanism-level treatment of organic reactions follow close behind. Spending Year 11 time on quantitative chemistry is the cheapest insurance a family can buy against a difficult first Diploma term.

faqs.question: What makes a Biology six-mark answer score full marks rather than four?
faqs.answer: Linked reasoning. Six separate true statements usually score about four, because the scheme credits a chain of cause and effect rather than a list of facts. The answer needs the right command term read correctly, points connected with because or therefore, and the specific terminology the scheme names. Students practise this fastest by marking their own answers against the published scheme and writing down which mark they missed.

faqs.question: Does a private school's Ministry of Education licence tell a parent anything about a tutor?
faqs.answer: Nothing at all, and the distinction is worth holding onto. Private and international schools in the Kingdom operate under a licence from the Ministry of Education, and school evaluation runs through ETEC. Neither process covers private tutoring, which is unregulated. So a school licence says something real about the school and nothing about the person teaching your child in the evening. Judge the tutor on component knowledge instead.

faqs.question: What does ETEC evaluation of a school tell a parent, and what does it leave out?
faqs.answer: The Education and Training Evaluation Commission runs school evaluation and accreditation services, including the approval of international accreditation bodies, so its work speaks to institutional quality and process. What it does not tell you is whether a particular Higher Level option will run next year, how many specialists teach each science, or who will cover a subject if a teacher leaves. Those are the questions that decide a student's two years.

faqs.question: What happens when a Saudi international school cannot run a Higher Level subject at all?
faqs.answer: Usually the option simply does not appear on the timetable, because a class of four does not pay for a teacher. Families respond in one of three ways: commuting to a school that runs it, taking the subject online through a provider the school accepts, or keeping a different subject and adding outside teaching for the gap. Ask which options actually ran with the last cohort rather than which are listed.

faqs.question: Why do families in one Saudi city commute to a school in another, and does it change the tutoring?
faqs.answer: In the Dammam, Al Khobar and Dhahran conurbation it is routine, because the three cities work as one school market and the right programme may sit in a neighbouring one. It changes tutoring in one way: the earliest workable lesson time moves later, since the student is home much later than the bell suggests. Book the slot against arrival time and keep a margin for a bad run.

best-ib-online-tutor.tutorsIntro: The profiles below are IB subject teachers rather than general tutors. Each one names the group, the subject and the level they teach, because a Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL specialist and a Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation SL specialist are doing two different jobs for two different students.

intro.heading: A tutor you can actually keep every week, then a tutor who is right
paragraphs: Parents in the Kingdom usually arrive at this search in the same order. Something in the school report moved the wrong way, the subject teacher has thirty other students, and the family decides to buy an hour a week of undivided attention. Then the practical questions start. Which evening? Before or after dinner? Does the tutor work on a Sunday, which is a working day here and a weekend day almost everywhere else? And can a Chemistry Higher Level specialist, who may be in Chennai, Manchester or Toronto, hold seven in the evening Riyadh time for the next two terms without it quietly collapsing?

Those are not administrative details. They decide whether the tuition happens at all. The most common way private tuition fails in Saudi Arabia is not a bad teacher: it is a slot that was agreed in one term, rescheduled twice in the next, moved to a Thursday because of a school trip, and then abandoned. An online lesson removes travel from both sides of the arrangement, which is the single biggest reason an online slot survives where an in-home one does not. Nobody is sitting in traffic on the Northern Ring Road at a quarter to seven hoping to make a seven o'clock start.

So this page is built logistics first. It sets out what a Saudi weekday evening actually looks like, where a lesson fits inside it, and what Arabia Standard Time does to a tutor whose own country puts its clocks forward and back. Only then does it turn to the part most providers lead with: who the teacher is, what the level demands, what the market charges, and what a lower hourly rate usually removes from the hour. The order matters because the constraints run in that order in real life.

The honest framing of the word best is this. No organisation ranks IB tutors in Saudi Arabia, no regulator licenses them, and any provider telling you they employ the finest teachers in the country is describing their marketing rather than their staff. What a family can genuinely compare is narrower and more useful: whether the tutor teaches this subject at this level, whether they can describe the papers and the mark scheme without looking them up, whether the hour sits where your household can protect it, and what you are charged for it. Four checkable things beat one unverifiable claim.

IB Gram is an independent matching platform, not a school and not a Saudi centre. Teaching for families in the Kingdom is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video; we do not send a tutor to a Saudi address, and in-home visiting is something we offer only in India. The argument for that is not cost-cutting. It is supply: a family in Al Malqa searching within driving distance is choosing from whoever lives nearby and is free, while the same family searching online is choosing from the people who actually teach Physics Higher Level for a living.

best-ib-online-tutor.programmesIntro: Four IB programmes reach Saudi families, and each one asks a different question of an online tutor. The age range decides the session length, the attention span and how much of the hour a parent should expect to sit near.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led primary teaching with no external examination and no numerical grade to point at. Support here is about the things the programme assumes a child already has: number fluency, reading stamina, handwriting speed and the habit of explaining an answer out loud. A primary online session is shorter than a secondary one, usually forty minutes, and it runs earlier in the evening because a nine-year-old is not teachable at eight o'clock.
programmes.countryNote: Primary slots are the hardest to staff for Saudi families, because the window that works for a young child here is late afternoon, and a late Saudi afternoon is the middle of the working day for a tutor in the United Kingdom. It is the one case where a tutor further east, in India or South East Asia, usually fits the household better than one further west.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Five years assessed against four published criteria per subject, each marked out of eight and converted to a grade out of seven. Students who have only ever been given percentages find the criteria opaque, and so do their parents. The useful work in an online MYP hour is reading the criterion descriptors against the student's own marked task and naming which band the writing actually sits in.
programmes.countryNote: Saudi schools split sharply at this age. Some run the MYP to Year 11, some hand students to Cambridge IGCSE at Year 10, and a family relocating between cities inside the Kingdom can meet both in eighteen months. The MYP years are also where Higher Level viability is quietly decided, because the mathematics set a student sits in MYP 4 and 5 constrains the Diploma route available later.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Grades run one to seven per subject, with up to three further points from the core, and the written papers are only part of the total: every subject carries an internally assessed component marked by the school and moderated externally. Most of the demand for an online IB tutor in the Kingdom sits here.
programmes.countryNote: Almost every Saudi IB school enters its candidates for the May session, which means the Diploma runs as one continuous twenty-four month block with a single real deadline at the end of it. Families who relocate into the Kingdom part-way through the first Diploma year arrive inside that block rather than at the start of it, and the catching-up work is specific and countable.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: A smaller route combining at least two Diploma courses with a career-related study, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. Where a school offers it, the Diploma subjects inside it are examined exactly as they are on the full Diploma, so subject tutoring is identical; the difference is the surrounding structure and the reflective project.
programmes.countryNote: The Career-related Programme is uncommon in Saudi Arabia and a family should confirm with the school in writing which Diploma courses sit inside it and at what level. That list, not the programme name, is what an online tutor needs before the first lesson, because it decides whether the student is sitting a Higher Level paper or a Standard Level one.

best-ib-online-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects Saudi families most often ask for by name. The description for each one says what it actually assesses and where the marks tend to leak, because that is what a tutor has to be able to talk about before the first lesson is worth paying for.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic fluency carries this course. Higher Level adds proof, complex numbers and a much heavier calculus load, and Paper 3 asks for extended problem solving across topics rather than within one. Marks leak where working is skipped: method marks exist on the mark scheme and an unsupported correct answer collects fewer of them than students expect.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology-heavy work, with graphical calculator technique assessed rather than assumed. The common failure is treating it as the easier route and then meeting the statistical inference at Higher Level unprepared. Some engineering and mathematics degrees name Analysis and Approaches specifically, so the route choice has consequences beyond the grade.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Definitions are marked strictly and the extended-response questions reward a stated principle before any arithmetic. Higher Level adds depth across fields, induction and quantum topics. The internally assessed investigation is where most of the recoverable marks sit, because experimental design and uncertainty treatment can be taught in a way that content recall cannot be rushed.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms, energetics and equilibrium are the reliable trouble spots, and the data booklet is a skill rather than a safety net. Students lose marks writing equations that are not balanced and reaching for a calculator before a mole ratio. Higher Level extends almost every topic rather than adding separate ones, which makes a weak foundation expensive.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume of content tempts students into memorising and away from command terms. A question asking to explain and a question asking to outline want different amounts of writing, and the mark scheme pays for the one asked. Statistical treatment of data and the internally assessed investigation are both taught skills and both recover marks quickly.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy decides more marks than essay style. Axes labelled properly, a shift drawn in the right direction and the new equilibrium identified will outscore a longer answer without a diagram. Higher Level adds quantitative work and the paper three calculations, and the internally assessed commentaries need real published articles and disciplined word counts.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Unseen textual analysis is the component that separates grades. Students arrive able to summarise and leave needing to analyse how meaning is constructed. The individual oral and the Higher Level essay both reward a narrow, defensible line of argument over broad coverage, and both are internally assessed on published criteria the student should have read.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: A language acquisition course that trips students who speak English fluently at home but have never been assessed on register, audience and text type. Writing tasks are marked against a specified text type, so a blog written as an essay loses marks that have nothing to do with vocabulary. Listening and reading comprehension both reward timed practice.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study response under time pressure, with tools applied rather than described. The reliable gap is evaluation: students explain a concept and stop, where the command term asked them to weigh it. Higher Level extension topics and the research project both ask for application to a real organisation with real figures.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pseudocode under examination conditions behaves differently from code in an editor, and students who build well on screen often cannot trace an algorithm on paper. Higher Level adds abstract data structures and resource management. The internally assessed solution needs a genuine client and documented testing, both of which a tutor may advise on but never produce.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Case-study recall plus command-term discipline, with marks available for naming a real place and a real figure rather than describing a general pattern. The Higher Level extension on global interactions is a different kind of writing from the optional themes, and students often prepare for one and are examined on both.

subjects.name: Arabic A: Literature
subjects.description: For students taking Arabic as their first language, the assessment is literary analysis in Arabic rather than language practice. Guided textual analysis and the comparative essay both reward close reading of a short extract. Families should confirm with the school which works are on the studied list before matching a tutor to the course.

best-ib-online-tutor.regionsTitle: Where families using this page are reading from
best-ib-online-tutor.regionsIntro: Distance is the honest reason online teaching works in the Kingdom. These notes are about the evening, not the postcode: what time school ends, how long the drive home takes, and therefore which hour a lesson can realistically own.

regions.name: Riyadh
regions.note: Roughly an hour across in traffic from north to south, so two families at the same school can have school runs that differ by forty minutes. A seven o'clock start is the safe default here; a six o'clock one works for families who live close to school and fails for everyone else.

regions.name: Jeddah
regions.note: A long coastal spine from the historic centre north to Obhur, which means the commute home is a straight line but a long one. Families at the northern end routinely protect a later slot, and siblings at different schools rarely get back at the same time.

regions.name: Dammam, Al Khobar and Dhahran
regions.note: One labour and school market behaving as three cities. Families live in one and attend school in another, so the school run can cross the conurbation twice a day. Compound families often finish earlier and can hold a late-afternoon slot that city families cannot.

regions.name: Al Ahsa
regions.note: About an hour and a half inland from the Eastern Province cluster. Where a subject is not taught locally at Higher Level, the realistic alternatives are a long commute to Al Khobar or an online specialist, and most families reading this page have already priced the commute.

regions.name: Jubail
regions.note: An industrial city with an international school community and a working week built around plant shifts. Parents on rotation want a slot that survives the weeks they are away, which argues for a fixed evening the student can attend without an adult in the room.

regions.name: Makkah and Taif
regions.note: Makkah sits roughly eighty kilometres east of Jeddah, with Taif further inland and higher. International-curriculum provision is thinner here than on the coast, so Higher Level sciences and the two mathematics routes are the requests that come up most often.

regions.name: Madinah and Yanbu
regions.note: Two separate school markets a long drive apart. Yanbu's industrial community and Madinah's city schools keep different calendars, and a family moving between them inside a school year can meet two different term structures in one Diploma course.

regions.name: Abha and Khamis Mushait
regions.note: About twenty-five kilometres apart at altitude in 'Asir, sharing one catchment. The pool of local specialists in Diploma sciences is small, and the honest answer for a Higher Level subject here is usually a teacher somewhere else, taught live over video.

regions.name: Tabuk, NEOM and AlUla
regions.note: Fast-changing communities in the north west where families often arrive mid-course and part-way through a Diploma year. The scheduling question here is less about traffic and more about settling a new household into a fixed weekly hour before the term gets away.

schoolClusters.note: The widest IB provision in the Kingdom and the deepest competition for evening slots, because families here are the most likely to already be running two or three activities a week alongside school. Students we support attend schools including those below.

A mix of IB and Cambridge provision spread along the coastal spine, plus the campus community at Thuwal. Several schools run both an international and a national section, and the term dates for the two are not always the same.

Diploma provision sits at particular campuses rather than everywhere, and British-curriculum schools sit alongside them in the same conurbation. Families comparing across Dammam, Al Khobar and Dhahran are often comparing two different boards as well as two different schools.

best-ib-online-tutor.schoolDisclaimer: Schools are named here as context for the education system Saudi families work inside; IB Gram has no affiliation, partnership or agreement with any of them.
best-ib-online-tutor.modesIntro: Three ways families buy online IB teaching, and they are not interchangeable. The weekly slot builds something; the intensive block fixes something; the component clinic protects marks that are about to close.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one, same hour every week
modes.description: The default and the one that compounds. A fixed evening, the same teacher, work set between sessions and marked before the next one. It is the only pattern that can follow a syllabus in order, which matters most in the first Diploma year when the content is still being laid down rather than revised.
bullets: One hour or ninety minutes, pinned to Arabia Standard Time
Written feedback to the parent after each session
Work set and marked between lessons, not just during them
The slot is held through school holidays unless you release it

modes.title: Intensive block before a series
modes.description: Two or three sessions a week for a defined number of weeks, aimed at a specific paper rather than a whole course. The content teaching is largely over by this point, so the hours go on timed questions, mark scheme reading and the particular topics the student's own past-paper record says are weak.
bullets: Built backwards from the school's own mock and entry deadlines
Past papers marked against the published mark scheme, not impressions
A timing plan per paper, practised rather than described
Finishes when the series starts, with no open-ended commitment

modes.title: Component clinic for internally assessed work
modes.description: Short, focused sessions around the internally assessed component of one subject, timed to the school's own draft deadlines. The tutor reads the criteria with the student, asks the questions a moderator would ask, and gives feedback on what the student has written. The tutor never writes or redrafts any part of it.
bullets: Criterion-by-criterion reading of the student's own draft
Research question and method interrogated before data collection
Word and page limits checked against the school's guidance
A written record of what was advised, for the school's honesty file

sections.heading: What best can mean for an online IB tutor, once availability is counted
paragraphs: Strip the marketing out of this search and three constraints are left. The first is subject and level: whether anyone genuinely teaches Physics Higher Level or Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL rather than teaching mathematics and sciences in general. The second is the hour: whether that person is awake, working and free at the time your household can protect. The third is price, sustained across a course rather than for one month. Each constraint cuts the shortlist, and they cut it in a particular order, which is why a family that starts with price usually ends up with a generalist.

The order matters because the constraints are not equally flexible. Price can be negotiated by buying fewer hours or shorter sessions. The hour can sometimes be moved by half an hour either way. Subject specialism cannot be negotiated at all: a Biology teacher cannot cover Chemistry Higher Level energetics because the family would prefer not to pay twice. So the sensible sequence is to fix the specialism, then find the hour inside the pool that remains, then decide what shape of commitment the budget supports. Done in that order, the shortlist is small and real. Done in reverse, it is large and useless.

This is also where an honest provider and an evasive one separate. Ask a provider which teacher would take the lesson, what level they teach it at, and which evenings they hold. A specific answer names a person, a subject, a level and two or three candidate slots. An evasive answer talks about a network of experienced educators and offers to confirm later. The second answer usually means the match will be made from whoever is free when you pay, which is the common way a family ends up with a capable teacher who is wrong for the paper.

None of this is a ranking, and no organisation in the Kingdom publishes one. The Ministry of Education licenses schools and the Education and Training Evaluation Commission runs school evaluation and accreditation services; neither rates private tutors, and IB Gram holds no approval from either. What you can do instead is run the four checks below in order and compare the answers you get.

sections.heading: The Saudi weekday evening, hour by hour, and where a lesson fits
paragraphs: The school week runs Sunday to Thursday, with Friday and Saturday as the weekend. That single fact reshapes everything, because almost every tutoring page written for an international audience quietly assumes Monday to Friday. A Saudi student's hardest school day is Sunday, when the week restarts, and their Thursday is a Friday in every other sense: homework gets postponed, and a lesson scheduled late on a Thursday is the one most often cancelled. The two evenings that reliably work in practice are Monday and Tuesday, with Wednesday close behind.

Inside the day, the usable window is narrower than parents expect. School finishes early by European standards, often between half past two and half past three, and then the drive home absorbs anything from fifteen minutes to the better part of an hour depending on the city and the district. What follows is food, prayer, younger siblings and some decompression. A lesson that starts before five is fighting the commute; a lesson that starts after half past eight is fighting fatigue, and a tired student in the second half of a Higher Level session is not learning, they are attending.

The practical answer is a start between five and half past seven, with seven as the most protected hour in most Saudi households. Ninety minutes works for a Diploma student if the material is problem-based and the session has a break in it. Sixty minutes is right for most Middle Years Programme work. Forty minutes is the honest ceiling at primary. None of this is a rule a provider should impose: it is a conversation a provider should have before fixing the slot, and the absence of that conversation is itself informative.

One more scheduling fact is specific to the Kingdom and worth planning for. During Ramadan the school day shortens and household routines shift to later in the evening, so many families move the lesson rather than pause it. Autumn and midyear breaks differ between schools in the same city, because international schools set their own calendars while Ministry of Education schools run a two-semester year. Confirm your own school's published dates and tell the tutor at the start of the term, not the week before.

sections.heading: Arabia Standard Time, and a slot that has to survive a whole course
paragraphs: Saudi Arabia runs on Arabia Standard Time, UTC+3, and does not change its clocks. That makes the Kingdom the stable side of any arrangement and the tutor's country the moving one. A family that agrees seven in the evening with a teacher in the United Kingdom has agreed four in the afternoon their time during one half of the year and five in the afternoon during the other, and if the slot was ever written down as a British time rather than a Saudi one, it will drift by an hour twice a year without anyone deciding to move it.

The fix is clerical and it takes one sentence. Agree the lesson in Arabia Standard Time, write it down that way, and make it the tutor's job to absorb their own clock change. A tutor in India sits two and a half hours ahead, which makes a Saudi evening a late Indian evening and is the reason Indian-based teachers can hold Saudi slots comfortably. A tutor in continental Europe or the United Kingdom is taking a Saudi evening in their own afternoon, which is the most sustainable arrangement of all. A tutor in North America is taking it before dawn, which is why those slots fail first.

The second thing that drifts is the school's own timetable. Schools change finishing times between terms, add a late activity, or move an examination week, and a slot that was comfortable in the autumn term becomes a rush in the spring. Build one review into the arrangement at the start of each term: confirm the slot, confirm the length, confirm what happens in the weeks around mock examinations. Families who do this keep the same hour for two years. Families who do not end up renegotiating mid-term, which is when a tutor's other commitments have already filled the gap.

Finally, pin the holiday policy at the start rather than when the holiday arrives. The long summer break runs for weeks, and a slot released in June without agreement is a slot somebody else has in September. The usual arrangement is either to hold the hour at a reduced frequency or to agree in writing that the same hour is reserved for the return. Both are reasonable; what fails is leaving it undiscussed.

sections.heading: Once the hour exists, the level decides which teacher is right
paragraphs: Higher Level and Standard Level in the same named subject are not the same course taught at two speeds. Higher Level carries extra content, a different paper structure and, in most subjects, a third written paper that asks for synthesis across topics rather than recall within one. A teacher who is fluent in Standard Level Chemistry can deliver most of a Higher Level syllabus and still be the wrong choice, because what the Higher Level student needs is somebody who has marked the extension questions and knows how they are rewarded.

The check is specific and it takes two minutes. Ask the tutor to describe the paper structure of the exact course, including the weighting of each paper and the internally assessed component. Ask which topics the Higher Level extension adds and which it merely deepens. Ask where in the student's own marked work the lost marks are, and listen for whether they talk about the mark scheme or about effort. A teacher who knows the specification answers in the vocabulary of the specification: components, criteria, command terms, weightings. A generalist answers in adjectives.

Examiner experience is worth paying for, and it is worth understanding before you pay. A teacher who has marked for a board has read hundreds of answers against one mark scheme and knows exactly which phrases collect marks and which look impressive and earn nothing. That is a genuine edge on the written papers. It says less about internally assessed work, which is marked by the school and moderated afterwards, and nothing at all about whether the person can hold the attention of a fifteen-year-old at seven in the evening. Ask which board, which component and which years of experience, and treat an unwillingness to specify as an answer.

The last part of the level question is the mathematics route, because it reaches beyond the grade. Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation are separate courses with separate papers, and some university programmes in engineering, mathematics and physical sciences name the first one specifically. A student in the Middle Years Programme whose set work closes off the Analysis and Approaches route has had a university decision made for them two years early. That is worth checking with the school while it is still reversible.
bullets: Ask for the paper structure and weightings of the exact course, not the subject
Ask what the Higher Level extension adds, topic by topic
Ask which board and which component any examiner claim refers to
Ask what the tutor would do in the first three sessions, and why in that order
Ask who teaches the lesson if that person is unavailable for a fortnight

sections.heading: What the market advertises, and what a cheaper hour quietly removes
paragraphs: Published rates in the Kingdom are easy to find and easy to misread. Tutoring platforms advertise general online tutoring from around SAR 55 an hour and budget IGCSE one-to-one from around SAR 35. Tutor marketplace guides describe general private tuition in Riyadh at roughly SAR 50 for primary and SAR 200 and above for senior-school examination subjects. Tutoring company listings put IB subject tutoring in Riyadh from around SAR 180 an hour, with Higher Level and advanced tracks advertised at roughly SAR 200 to 220. International providers quoting in dollars sit near sixty dollars an hour. Every one of those figures is a vendor's advertised rate rather than a market average, and none of them is IB Gram's price.

What moves the number is predictable, and scarcity moves it most. A Higher Level Physics or Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL specialist is scarce everywhere in the world, so their hour costs more in Riyadh for the same reason it costs more in Dubai or Singapore. After scarcity comes marking or examining experience, then level, then whether the tutor travels, then the length of the package. The one item on that list a family can remove entirely is travel, which is a real part of an in-home rate in Riyadh and Jeddah and which an online lesson deletes rather than discounts.

The more useful question is what a lower rate takes away, because the hour on screen often looks identical. At the bottom of the market the hour is the whole product: nothing is marked between lessons, nothing is written to the parent, no past paper is prepared in advance and the teacher meets the student's work for the first time during the session. Moving up the bands buys preparation, marked work returned before the next lesson, written feedback a parent can read, and a teacher who knows the mark scheme well enough to predict the loss before it happens. Ask what happens between the lessons, and the band becomes legible.

Price a term rather than a lesson. One subject, one hour a week across a thirteen-week term is thirteen hours, and that multiplied by any band above gives a number a family can actually decide about. Two subjects double it. An intensive block in the weeks before the series adds to it rather than replacing it. Families who do this arithmetic early tend to buy one subject properly instead of three subjects thinly, which is almost always the better decision.
