sections.heading: Where a Diploma subject grade is actually decided
paragraphs: A Diploma subject grade is not one examination. Every subject carries written papers plus an internally assessed component that the school marks against published criteria and the board moderates afterwards. The written papers differ in what they reward: one paper may be short-answer and data-based, another extended response, and at Higher Level a third asking for synthesis across the course. Weightings differ by subject and by level, which is why a family should ask the school's Diploma Programme coordinator for the component list and the percentages rather than assuming the sciences and the humanities are built the same way.

Command terms are where the gap between knowing and being paid opens up. Describe, explain, evaluate, justify and discuss are not stylistic preferences; each one maps to a mark allocation and a required shape of answer. A student who explains when the paper asked them to evaluate has written something true and collected part of the marks. This is the cheapest thing to fix in any subject and the most consistently neglected, because it feels like technique rather than content. In practice it is both, and it is the first thing a good tutor audits in a marked script.

Grade boundaries move between sessions because papers vary in difficulty, and the boundary is set after the marking to keep the standard level across sessions. This is why a mark out of eighty means nothing on its own and why a school's internal grade is a judgement rather than a measurement. Predicted grades are a related but separate thing: they are the school's professional forecast, submitted for university applications, and they are set by the teacher using mock performance, internally assessed work and classroom evidence. A tutor can change the evidence the forecast is built from. Nobody can change the forecast itself by asking.

What follows from all this is a simple instruction for the first month of tuition. Get the marked scripts, not the grades. A percentage tells a tutor almost nothing; an annotated script tells them which command terms the student misreads, which topics collapse under time pressure, and whether the marks are being lost in the first question or the last. Families who bring three marked pieces of work to a first lesson buy a diagnosis. Families who bring a report card buy a conversation.

sections.heading: When to start, counted by year group
paragraphs: The value of an hour of tuition is not constant across the course. It is highest where the work it changes is still open, and it falls as components close. In the Middle Years Programme almost everything is open, including which mathematics route and which Higher Level subjects will later be viable, so the hour spent there buys options rather than marks. In the final term before the May session almost everything is closed except examination technique, so the same hour buys execution. Both are worth buying. They are not the same purchase, and a family should know which one they are making.

The first Diploma year is the most under-bought and the most consequential. The content laid down in that year is examined at the end of the second, internally assessed work usually begins in it, and the mock performance that generates a predicted grade draws on it. A student who leaves the first year with a shaky foundation in Chemistry energetics or in algebraic manipulation will spend the second year paying interest on it. An hour a week across the first year is the cheapest version of this decision; three hours a week in the final term is the expensive version of the same decision, made late.

At the other end, it is genuinely not too late to start in the final year, provided the aim changes. With one or two terms left the realistic targets are command-term discipline, paper timing, the internally assessed component if it is still open, and the two or three topics the student's own past-paper record shows are costing the most. That is a defined job with a visible result. What cannot be done in a term is rebuild two years of missing foundations, and a provider who promises otherwise is selling something that does not exist.

For families relocating into the Kingdom mid-course, the year group matters less than the point in the course. Arriving in the first Diploma year is awkward but recoverable. Arriving in the second is a specific piece of work: establish which components are already submitted, which are still open, what the new school's deadlines are, and whether the subject combination transfers at the same levels. That audit is the first lesson, and it should produce a written list rather than reassurance.

sections.heading: Equivalency, Qudurat and Tahsili: the part nobody budgets for
paragraphs: A family whose child will apply to a Saudi university has a second project running alongside the Diploma, and most tutoring pages never mention it. A foreign or international school certificate needs an equivalency decision from the Ministry of Education before a Saudi university treats it as equivalent to the Saudi secondary certificate. That applies to an IB Diploma, to A Levels and to an American high school diploma alike. It is an administrative process with its own evidence requirements, and it is the kind of thing families discover late because the school's own focus is the Diploma.

Alongside it sit the two Qiyas tests, run by the National Center for Assessment under the Education and Training Evaluation Commission. Qudurat, the General Aptitude Test, assesses verbal and quantitative reasoning rather than syllabus content, and is available in Arabic and in English. Tahsili, the achievement test, covers the science-stream subjects: mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology and English. Universities publish their own admission criteria combining school results with these tests, and the weightings differ by university and by programme. Those criteria are published by the universities themselves and that is where a family should read them.

The part worth saying plainly is why Tahsili is harder for an international-curriculum student than for a national-curriculum one. Its content follows the Saudi national curriculum. An IB or IGCSE student has studied physics and chemistry properly, but in a different order, with different emphases and different terminology, and often in a different language of instruction. The material overlaps; the framing does not. That gap is bridgeable with preparation, and it is a different piece of work from Diploma subject tutoring, which is why it should be planned as a separate block rather than squeezed into an existing hour.

Two practical cautions. No tutor and no provider can promise a university place, and anybody publishing a required Qudurat or Tahsili score is reporting something that varies by university, by programme and by intake. Treat such figures as unverified. The university's own admissions pages and the Ministry's equivalency guidance are the only sources worth planning against, and some universities also state a maximum age for the secondary certificate they will accept, which is worth checking before a gap year is decided.

sections.heading: Academic honesty, and what an online tutor may do with assessed work
paragraphs: The IB treats academic honesty as a condition of the award rather than a school rule, which makes this the sharpest line in private tuition. The internally assessed components are the student's own work, supervised by a teacher at the school who signs for their authenticity. An outside tutor sits beside that process and has a legitimate and useful role in it, but a narrow one. The distinction is between teaching and producing, and it is not a grey area in practice even though it is often described as one.

What a tutor may do: teach the underlying content, read the published criteria with the student, interrogate a research question before any data is collected, explain what a criterion descriptor actually asks for, point at a paragraph that does not answer the question, discuss whether a method will produce usable results, and teach the student to proofread. What a tutor may never do: write any part of the assessment, redraft the student's sentences into their own, supply a method or a conclusion for copying, or produce coursework of any kind. We do not offer that service and would not take the work.

This matters commercially as well as ethically, because several providers visible in this market sit on the wrong side of it. A service that advertises completed assessments is selling a risk the family carries, not the provider: malpractice findings fall on the candidate and can cost the award. If a tutor's feedback arrives as a rewritten paragraph rather than a question, that is the signal to stop. Feedback that improves a student leaves the student's own voice in the document and a trail of their own decisions behind it.

A practical habit protects everybody. Keep the drafts. A student who can show successive versions of their own work, with dated notes on what changed and why after each round of feedback, has a record that answers any question a school or a moderator might ask. Ask the tutor to summarise in writing what was advised in each session on an assessed component. It takes a minute, it makes the feedback more useful, and it means the honesty question never becomes a conversation about memory.

sections.heading: Getting started, and what happens when the specialist is not free
paragraphs: The sequence is short. Tell us the subject, the level, the board and the school, and send two or three pieces of marked work. Name two evenings that your household can genuinely protect and give them in Arabia Standard Time. We come back with a teacher who actually teaches that course at that level, with the evenings they can hold, and a free trial lesson is scheduled before any payment. The trial is a diagnosis: the teacher works through the student's own marked script, identifies where the marks are going, and says what the first three sessions would do.

After the trial you get a short written plan: what the sessions will cover in what order, what will be set between them, and what evidence will show whether it is working. Then the weekly work begins, with feedback after each session written to the parent rather than reported verbally to the student. At the end of the first month the plan is reviewed against the marked work, not against impressions. If the student has not moved, that is a conversation about approach or about match, and it is better had at four weeks than at four months.

The honest part is what happens when the person you need is not available at the hour you need. Scarce specialisms at Higher Level are genuinely scarce, and sometimes the best available option at seven in the evening is not the best teacher of that subject in the pool. When that happens we say so and lay out the real choices: wait for the slot to open, take a different evening, shorten the session to fit a narrower window, or start with a strong teacher of the adjacent level while the specialist's timetable clears. What we will not do is put a generalist in front of a Higher Level student and let the family find out in the third week.

If the match is wrong, say so early. Two or three sessions is enough to tell whether a teenager will work with a particular teacher, and a change at that point costs nothing but a fortnight. A change in the final term costs much more. Families who treat the first month as a trial of the arrangement rather than the start of a commitment end up with better arrangements, and the providers who resist that framing are telling you something about how they fill their own timetable.

process.title: Send the subject, the level and the marked work
process.description: The brief that produces a good match is specific: the board, the subject, the level, the school and two or three pieces of recently marked work. The scripts matter more than the grades, because an annotated paper shows which command terms are misread and which topics collapse under time pressure. A report card shows neither.

process.title: Name two evenings in Arabia Standard Time
process.description: Give two candidate slots your household can genuinely protect, written in Saudi local time, and say what the school finishing time and the drive home actually are. Two options rather than one roughly doubles the pool of specialists who can take the lesson, which is the difference between a match this week and a wait.

process.title: Meet the teacher in a free trial lesson
process.description: The trial is a diagnostic session, not a sales call. The teacher works through the student's own marked script, names where the marks are going, and sets out what the first three sessions would cover and in what order. A family should finish it knowing whether this person knows the specification, and whether their child will work with them.

process.title: Agree a short written plan
process.description: Before the weekly work starts, agree what the sessions cover in sequence, what is set between them, how feedback arrives, and what evidence will show whether it is working. Agree the holiday and cancellation policy at the same time, including what happens to the slot across the long summer break.

process.title: Weekly lessons, with marked work between them
process.description: A fixed hour, the same teacher, work set after each session and marked before the next one. Feedback is written to the parent after every lesson, naming what was covered, what was set and what the next session will do. The hour on screen is the visible part; the marking between the hours is where much of the value sits.

process.title: Review at four weeks against the evidence
process.description: At the end of the first month, compare marked work from before and after rather than impressions. If the student has moved, the plan continues and the targets are reset. If nothing has moved, the honest options are a different approach, a different teacher or stopping, and we will say which one we think it is.

whyPoints.title: The hour is treated as the first constraint, not the last
whyPoints.description: Most providers match a tutor and then negotiate a time, which is how families end up with a capable teacher at an hour nobody can protect. We ask for the school finishing time, the drive home and two candidate evenings first, then search the pool that can actually hold one of them. It is a less impressive sentence and a more durable arrangement.

whyPoints.title: Matched by level, not just by subject
whyPoints.description: Higher Level and Standard Level are different courses with different papers and different mark schemes. A teacher is put in front of a Higher Level student only if they teach that extension and can describe how it is examined. Where the specialist is genuinely unavailable at your hour, we say that rather than substituting quietly.

whyPoints.title: Slots written in Arabia Standard Time
whyPoints.description: Every agreed lesson time is recorded in Saudi local time, and the tutor absorbs their own country's clock changes. That single piece of clerical discipline is why a slot agreed in the autumn term is still the same slot in the spring, instead of drifting by an hour twice a year while everyone assumes somebody else noticed.

whyPoints.title: Rates quoted as what they are
whyPoints.description: The SAR figures on this page are advertised rates published by tutoring platforms, marketplaces and companies in the Kingdom, given so a family can judge a quote in context. They are not a market average and they are not our price. What a particular match costs depends on the subject's scarcity, the level and the teacher's examining background.

whyPoints.title: A firm line on assessed work
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach content, read criteria with the student and give feedback on what the student has written. No part of an internally assessed task, an Extended Essay, a Theory of Knowledge essay or a Personal Project is ever written or redrafted by a tutor. We say this plainly because several services in this market do not, and the risk of that choice falls on the candidate.

whyPoints.title: Online, stated plainly, with the reason
whyPoints.description: Teaching for Saudi families is delivered one-to-one over live video. We do not send tutors to Saudi addresses; in-home visiting is a service we run only in India. The reason is supply rather than cost: an online match draws on the people who actually teach a scarce Higher Level subject, instead of whoever lives within a drivable radius and happens to be free.

faqs.question: Which year group gets the most out of starting with an online IB tutor, and which gets the least?
faqs.answer: The first Diploma year returns the most, because the content is still being laid down, internally assessed work is still open and the mock performance that produces a predicted grade has not happened yet. An hour a week there changes what is examined eighteen months later. The lowest return is a late start in the final term with the expectation of rebuilding foundations, because only technique, timing and one or two topics can realistically move by then. That is still worth buying; it is simply a smaller job. Decide which purchase you are making before you compare prices, because the two are often quoted as though they were the same thing.

faqs.question: My child is in the final year of the MYP - is an online IB tutor premature?
faqs.answer: Not if the aim is the right one. At MYP 4 and 5 the useful work is twofold: writing to the four published criteria rather than writing generally, and keeping Diploma options open. The second matters more than families realise. The mathematics set a student sits at this stage can decide whether Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches is available later, and some engineering and mathematics degrees name that course specifically. A term of work that supports a set-change case while the school can still act on it is worth more than the same term spent on Diploma content a year early. Ask the school which route each set leads to, in writing.

faqs.question: What should the first Diploma year buy from an online tutor that the second year cannot?
faqs.answer: Foundation and sequence. In the first year a tutor can teach topics in syllabus order, repair gaps from IGCSE or the MYP, and start the internally assessed component early enough for the research question to be interrogated before data is collected. None of that is available in the second year at the same price, because the course has moved on and the school's deadlines are closer. The second year buys different things: mark scheme technique, paper timing, mock preparation and the specific topics past papers expose. Both are real. The first year is cheaper for the same effect, which is why it is the most under-bought stretch of the Diploma.

faqs.question: Is it worth hiring an online IB tutor in the final two terms before the May session?
faqs.answer: Yes, with the targets set honestly. In two terms a student can fix command-term discipline, build a timing plan per paper and practise it, finish an internally assessed component properly if it is still open, and work through the two or three topics their own marked past papers show are costing the most. That is a defined job with visible results. What two terms cannot do is replace two years of missing foundations across three Higher Level subjects. A provider who accepts that brief without flagging it is selling reassurance. Bring the marked scripts to the first lesson and the realistic target becomes obvious to everyone.

faqs.question: How does paper weighting differ between Higher Level and Standard Level in the same subject?
faqs.answer: It differs by subject, which is exactly why it has to be checked rather than assumed. Higher Level courses generally carry more content, longer papers and, in many subjects, an additional written paper that asks for synthesis across topics instead of recall within one. The internally assessed component usually carries a similar proportion at both levels but is marked against the same criteria with higher expectations at Higher Level. Ask your school's Diploma Programme coordinator for the component list and the percentage weighting of each part for your child's exact course. A tutor who cannot state those numbers for the subject they teach has not read the specification recently enough.

faqs.question: What is a command term, and how does an online tutor teach one over video?
faqs.answer: A command term is the instruction verb that tells a student what kind of answer earns the marks: describe, explain, compare, evaluate, justify, discuss. Each maps to a mark allocation and a shape of answer, so a student who explains where the paper asked them to evaluate has written something true and collected part of the marks. Teaching it over video is straightforward and works well on screen: the tutor and student read the question, read the mark scheme, write an answer together on a shared document, then mark it against the scheme line by line. Most students need this done a dozen times before it becomes automatic.

faqs.question: Why do grade boundaries move between sessions, and should a family worry about it?
faqs.answer: Boundaries move because papers vary in difficulty and the boundary is set after marking so that the same grade means the same thing across sessions. A harder paper produces lower boundaries. This is why a raw mark out of eighty tells a family nothing on its own, and why a school's internal grade is a judgement rather than a measurement. There is nothing to worry about and nothing to game. The practical consequence is simply that a student should be prepared to a standard rather than to a mark, and that comparing this term's percentage with last term's is only meaningful if the papers were comparable.

faqs.question: Who decides a predicted grade, and can an online tutor influence it?
faqs.answer: The school decides it. A predicted grade is the teacher's professional forecast of the final result, submitted for university applications, and it is built from mock performance, internally assessed work and classroom evidence. A tutor cannot change the forecast by asking, and no reputable provider should offer to. What a tutor can change is the evidence the forecast rests on: better mock scripts, an internally assessed component finished on time and marked well, and visible improvement in the classroom. Work on the evidence early, because once the forecast has been submitted the window has closed for that application cycle.

faqs.question: How much of a Diploma subject grade is decided before the written papers?
faqs.answer: A meaningful share, and the exact figure depends on the subject. Every Diploma subject carries an internally assessed component marked by the school against published criteria and moderated externally, and in some subjects that component plus any oral or practical element accounts for a substantial part of the total. Those marks close on the school's own deadlines, well before the examinations. That makes them the most protectable part of the grade and the most commonly neglected, because they do not feel like an examination. Ask the coordinator for the component weightings in writing, then work out which deadlines are the real ones.

faqs.question: What does Ministry of Education equivalency do for an IB Diploma in the Kingdom?
faqs.answer: It is the step that turns an international certificate into something a Saudi university will treat as equivalent to the Saudi secondary certificate. Without that decision the Diploma is a qualification the university cannot place. The same applies to A Levels and to an American high school diploma. It is an administrative process with its own evidence requirements rather than an academic hurdle, and it runs on its own timetable alongside the Diploma. Families discover it late because the school's attention is on the Diploma itself. Start reading the Ministry's own guidance in the first year rather than the final term, and keep original documents together.

faqs.question: Does an IB Diploma student in Saudi Arabia need to sit Qudurat as well?
faqs.answer: If the plan includes a Saudi university, in most cases yes. Qudurat, the General Aptitude Test, is run by the National Center for Assessment under the Education and Training Evaluation Commission, and universities use it alongside school results in their own published admission criteria. It assesses verbal and quantitative reasoning rather than syllabus content, and it is available in Arabic and in English. Science-stream applicants are usually looking at Tahsili too. Because weightings differ by university and by programme, the only reliable source is the admissions page of each university the student is applying to. Nobody should be quoting you a required score.

faqs.question: Why is Tahsili harder for an IB student than for a national-curriculum one?
faqs.answer: Because its content follows the Saudi national curriculum. An IB student has studied mathematics, physics, chemistry and biology seriously, but in a different order, with different emphases, different terminology and often a different language of instruction. The material overlaps; the framing does not. A question can be entirely familiar in substance and unfamiliar in the way it is posed, which costs time under test conditions. The gap is bridgeable with preparation aimed at the test's own framing rather than at Diploma content, and it should be planned as a separate block of work rather than absorbed into an existing subject hour.

faqs.question: Which mathematics route do Saudi engineering programmes expect from an IB applicant?
faqs.answer: Competitive engineering and physical science programmes generally expect the more analytical route, and some name Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches specifically, usually at Higher Level. Applications and Interpretation is a full mathematics course and the right choice for many students, but it is not interchangeable for those applications. The decision is made earlier than families expect, because set placement in the Middle Years Programme or at IGCSE constrains what the Diploma school will allow. Check each programme's own published prerequisites rather than relying on general advice, and if the route is wrong, raise it with the school while a change is still administratively possible.

faqs.question: Does an online tutor help with Qudurat and Tahsili preparation, or only school subjects?
faqs.answer: Both are available, and they are different pieces of work. Diploma subject tutoring follows the IB specification. Qiyas test preparation follows the test's own framing: reasoning technique and timing for Qudurat, and for Tahsili the Saudi national curriculum's treatment of mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology and English, which is where an international-curriculum student has the most to adjust to. Trying to cover both inside one weekly subject hour usually means neither is done properly. Plan a separate block, start it well before the test date the student is entered for, and check the official criteria for the universities being applied to.

faqs.question: What should a Diploma student have ready before applying to universities overseas?
faqs.answer: Predicted grades from the school, a transcript, the subject and level combination documented, an English language position if the destination requires one, and a personal statement or equivalent written by the student. For some destinations, specific Higher Level subjects are prerequisites rather than preferences, so the list of offers a student can realistically receive is largely fixed by the subject choices made two years earlier. Build the shortlist around the actual subjects and levels rather than around ambition, check each university's own published requirements, and treat predicted grades as the school's forecast rather than as a result already achieved.

faqs.question: How early should a family start thinking about equivalency paperwork?
faqs.answer: Earlier than feels necessary. The equivalency decision from the Ministry of Education is document-driven, and documents from a previous country are harder to obtain once a family has moved again. Starting in the first Diploma year means gathering certificates, transcripts and any attestations while they are still easy to request. Some universities also state a maximum age for the secondary certificate they will accept, which matters if a gap year is being considered. Read the Ministry's own guidance and each university's admissions pages directly, because third-party summaries of this process disagree with each other and with themselves.

best-ib-online-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the hour, then with the teacher
best-ib-online-tutor.closingBody: If you take one thing from this page, make it the sequence. Decide which evening your household can genuinely protect, write it down in Arabia Standard Time, and treat that as the first filter rather than the last negotiation. Then find somebody who teaches your child's exact subject at your child's exact level, and ask them to describe the papers and the mark scheme before you ask them anything about themselves. Send us the subject, the level, two candidate evenings and two or three pieces of marked work, and we will come back with a teacher who fits all of it and a free trial lesson to test it. Lessons are one-to-one, live over video, and the slot is yours.

intro.heading: Four options, one decision
paragraphs: A family typing best IB tuition in Saudi Arabia into Google is rarely shopping for a brand. They are weighing four concrete options against each other: the support the school already gives, a group revision centre, a private tutor who drives to the villa, and one-to-one teaching delivered online. Each costs something different, each suits a different problem, and each runs out somewhere. The useful question is not which provider calls itself the best, but which of the four fits the subject, the level and the term the student is actually in.

The comparison is harder here than it looks, because the signals a parent would normally trust do not apply to tutoring. Schools in the Kingdom hold a licence from the Ministry of Education and are evaluated through the Education and Training Evaluation Commission. Those processes are real, documented and worth understanding. Neither covers private tutors, and no Saudi body issues a tutoring licence at all. So the word best, on this kind of query, cannot mean officially approved. It has to mean something a family can check for itself in an afternoon.

That is what this page supplies. It prices the four options side by side using rates the providers themselves advertise, separates what a school licence certifies from what a tutor's record shows, and sets out five checks that reliably distinguish a subject specialist from a generalist with a website. None of it asks you to trust a claim, and all of it can be tested in a single trial lesson with recently marked work on the screen in front of both of you. The order matters too, so the page runs cost first, credentials second, and the university endgame third.

There is a second half to the decision that almost nobody in this market writes about. An IB Diploma earned in Riyadh or Jeddah is a foreign certificate, and a Saudi university treats it as equivalent to the national secondary certificate only after an equivalency decision from the Ministry of Education. Alongside that sit the Qiyas tests, Qudurat and Tahsili, whose content is built on the national curriculum. A family choosing tuition for the Diploma years is also, quietly, choosing how ready the student will be for a test written around a syllabus they never studied.

Lessons for Saudi families are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a Saudi address; home visits are a service we offer only in India. That constraint is also the argument for this format. A family in Najran, Tabuk or Al Ahsa is matched on exactly the same basis as a family in Al Olaya, because the pool of available teachers is not limited to whoever can reach the door by seven in the evening.

subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology use. Marks go in interpretation, not calculation: a correct regression with no comment on meaning scores less than parents expect.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Definitions are examined strictly, and extended responses want linked reasoning rather than a list of facts. Higher Level adds topics with no Standard Level equivalent.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics generate most requests. The internally assessed investigation rewards a focused research question far more than an ambitious one, and students choose too broadly.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume is the problem, not difficulty. Candidates who revise by rereading score badly on command terms such as evaluate and distinguish, where the scheme wants a comparison.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and precise definitions decide the lower band; the top band needs evaluation that weighs assumptions. Higher Level adds quantitative work students did not expect.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Unseen analysis and the individual oral both reward a defensible line of argument. Students writing in a second language need technique more than vocabulary.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study papers punish generic answers. Tools have to be applied to the stimulus in front of the candidate, and the internally assessed commentary needs a real organisational issue.

sections.heading: The four options, priced and compared
paragraphs: Start with what each option costs and what it is for. Advertised rates span a wide band: general online tutoring listed from around SAR 55 an hour on platform pages, senior-school private tuition in Riyadh quoted at SAR 200 and above in tutor-marketplace guides, IB subject tutoring from around SAR 180 on tutoring-company listings, and Higher Level tracks at roughly SAR 200 to 220. International providers often quote near $60 an hour. Those are figures the providers advertise themselves, not a market average, and not what IB Gram charges.

Price is the least interesting column in the table below. A school clinic costs nothing extra but is usually run by the same teacher whose lesson the student already did not follow. A group centre spreads a revision syllabus across several students, which works for a content gap and fails for one consistently misread paper. A tutor who drives to the villa buys presence in the room and pays for it twice: in travel loading on the advertised rate, and in a pool narrowed to whoever lives a reasonable drive away.

Online one-to-one changes one variable, and it is the one that decides Diploma outcomes: the tutor is chosen by subject and level rather than by proximity. A family in Najran and a family in Al Olaya can both book the same Chemistry Higher Level specialist. The trade is honest and worth stating plainly. A quiet room and a stable connection are required, and nobody arrives at the door, in exchange for a pool that is not capped by the local commute.

sections.heading: School licences, ETEC evaluation, and what neither says about a tutor
paragraphs: Private and international schools in the Kingdom hold a licence issued by the Ministry of Education. Separately, school evaluation and accreditation run through the Education and Training Evaluation Commission, which operates e-services both for national school accreditation and for approving the international accreditation bodies schools choose to work with. A school offering the Diploma also carries authorisation from the IB organisation to deliver that programme. Three bodies, three distinct jobs, and not one says anything about the person teaching your child on a Tuesday evening.

That gap is the point. There is no national register of private tutors in Saudi Arabia, and no regulator issues a tutoring licence. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or partnership from the Ministry, from the Commission, or from the IB organisation, and any provider implying otherwise should be asked to produce the document. What exists instead is checkable evidence about one named teacher: which syllabus they have taught, at which level, across how many cohorts, and whether they have marked written papers for a board.

For a parent the consequence is a reordering of questions. A school's licence and its evaluation report describe the institution, including class sizes and which Higher Level options it can genuinely staff. They do not say whether anyone in the building has taught Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level for more than a single cohort. Ask the school that second question in writing, ask a prospective tutor the same one, and the place where the two answers diverge is where outside teaching earns its fee.

sections.heading: Five checks that separate one provider from the next
paragraphs: The first check is specificity. A provider that answers a Physics Higher Level enquiry with a tutor described as a science specialist has told you nothing, and the same sentence would have come back for Biology Standard Level. Ask for the subject, the level and the component. The second check is marking exposure: a tutor who has marked written papers for a board has read several hundred answers to one question and knows which phrasing earns the mark. Ask how recently, and for which papers.

The third check is mark-scheme literacy, and a trial lesson exposes it fastest. Hand the tutor a question the student lost marks on and ask what the scheme actually wanted. A good answer names the command term, says what a comparison or an evaluation has to contain, and explains why a correct fact in the wrong form scored nothing. A weak answer re-teaches the topic. The fourth check is the academic-honesty boundary, where the right answer is a stated limit rather than an offer of help.

The fifth check is reporting. Ask what the family receives after each session and after the first month, and ask to see the format before paying. A note saying the session went well is decoration. A note naming the paper, the question, the error type and the work set is a record you can hold a provider to, and it is the only thing that makes a later conversation about value possible. Providers who will not show the template usually do not have one.

sections.heading: Equivalency and the Qiyas tests: the part nobody prices in
paragraphs: An IB Diploma, an A Level certificate and an American high school diploma are all foreign qualifications in the Kingdom. Before a Saudi university treats one as equivalent to the national secondary certificate, the Ministry of Education issues an equivalency decision, known as mu'adalah. The process runs on documents rather than on grades, and some universities also state a maximum age for the certificate they will accept. Families who leave this to the final school term find that paperwork, not marks, has become the constraint on an application.

Alongside equivalency sit the two Qiyas tests, run by the Education and Training Evaluation Commission through its National Center for Assessment. Qudurat, the General Aptitude Test, measures verbal and quantitative reasoning rather than syllabus content, and can be sat in Arabic or English. Tahsili, the Achievement Test, covers mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology and English, and its content follows the Saudi national curriculum. That single fact is why international-curriculum students often find Tahsili harder than their own examinations: the material overlaps, but the framing does not.

Universities publish their own admission criteria combining school grades with these results, and the weighting differs by institution and by programme. No threshold or formula is reproduced here, because they move and they differ; read the university's own published criteria. What a tutor can usefully do is treat preparation as a mapping exercise, setting the national-curriculum topic list against what the student has actually studied and teaching the gaps. No tutor can promise an admission outcome, and a provider who does is describing something nobody controls.

sections.heading: The first month: diagnostic, plan and the first honest report
paragraphs: A free trial lesson exists to produce information, not a sale. It should open with work the student has already had marked, because a tutor reading real marked answers learns more in twenty minutes than any assessment written for the purpose would show. By the end a family should hold a short written starting point: which topics are secure, which are not, which paper is costing most, and whether the loss is content, technique or time management. Those four findings are the plan's foundation.

The month that follows should narrow rather than broaden. Two or three topics, one paper type, and a weekly piece of written work marked against the published scheme beat a tour of the syllabus. Where several subjects are weak at once, the honest move is to sequence them, starting with the one whose technique transfers furthest, instead of booking four tutors and filling every evening. A student with no free evenings stops doing the school's own work, which costs more than it buys.

At the end of the first month a report should be specific enough to argue with. It should name what was taught, what the marked work showed, where the student still loses marks, and what the next four weeks target. If it shows no movement, something in the plan changes: the tutor, the focus, the frequency, or the diagnosis itself. A provider whose answer to a flat month is to recommend more hours has not read its own report.

sections.heading: Papers, weightings and command terms, where quality becomes measurable
paragraphs: Every Diploma subject publishes its assessment structure in the subject guide: how many written papers, what each contains, the weighting each carries towards the final grade, and the share held by the internally assessed component. Those figures are the most useful page a parent never reads. They show which paper is worth fixing first, and they often reveal that the component a student has quietly ignored carries more weight than the one they revise hardest. Ask the school's Diploma coordinator for the current guide.

Command terms are where knowledge and marks come apart. Describe, explain, evaluate, justify and distinguish each demand a different structure, and a mark scheme pays for the structure. A candidate who answers an evaluate question with two accurate descriptions has written nothing false and still scores in the lower band. This is teachable in weeks rather than years, which is why it is the first thing a good tutor works on when the diagnostic shows strong content and weak paper marks.

Grade boundaries complete the picture. They are set after each series against the demand of that particular paper, so the mark needed for a given grade moves. A mock mark is therefore a position, not a prediction, and a boundary that shifted between two series says more about those papers than about the cohort. Families who understand this stop treating one mock as a verdict and start reading the trend across several marked pieces, which is what a tutor's reporting should make visible.

sections.heading: Building a weekly slot into a Sunday to Thursday week
paragraphs: The school week in the Kingdom runs Sunday to Thursday, with Friday and Saturday as the weekend. Every scheduling decision follows from that, and most tutoring copy written for other markets gets it wrong. A Sunday session lands on the first school day, when the week's homework has not yet arrived and the student is least tired. A Thursday session sits on the last school day, with a two-day break after it, which suits setting work and suits reviewing it poorly.

Arabia Standard Time is UTC+3 and the Kingdom does not change its clocks. A tutor based in India is two and a half hours ahead; one in the United Kingdom is three hours behind in their winter and two in their summer, so an agreed slot drifts twice a year unless it is pinned to Kingdom local time rather than the tutor's. Writing the slot down in local time, on both sides, prevents the single most common scheduling failure in this market.

The rest is local. A school run finishing late in an outer Riyadh district pushes a workable start past seven. Shortened school days during Ramadan move the whole evening, and lessons shift with them rather than pausing. Three-term international calendars and the two-semester Ministry year do not align, so a family with children in both systems manages two sets of holidays. Agreeing the slot against the student's own school calendar, not a generic one, is what stops it being lost.

process.title: Name the subject, level and board
process.description: Give the exact subject, whether it is Higher or Standard Level, the programme and the year group. Naming the component that is losing marks narrows the match further.

process.title: Free trial lesson and diagnostic
process.description: A one-to-one session over live video, with no payment. Bring recently marked work. It ends with a written starting point: secure topics, weak topics, and the paper losing most marks.

process.title: Agree the plan and pin the slot
process.description: A four-week focus is set from the diagnostic, with a fixed weekly time written down in Arabia Standard Time. Work between lessons is set, marked and returned before the next session.

process.title: Review at the month and change what fails
process.description: A written report names what was taught, what the marked work showed and what the next four weeks target. If nothing moved, the focus, the frequency or the tutor changes.

whyPoints.title: Matched by subject and level, not location
whyPoints.description: A Chemistry Higher Level request goes to a Chemistry Higher Level teacher wherever they are. Because lessons run online, the pool is not limited to who can reach a district.

whyPoints.title: Rates quoted plainly, in SAR
whyPoints.description: Fees are given in riyals before a trial lesson, with what moves them stated: level, subject scarcity, marking experience, block length. Other providers' advertised figures are reported here as theirs.

whyPoints.title: Built around the Kingdom's week and clock
whyPoints.description: Slots are agreed Sunday to Thursday in Arabia Standard Time and written down in local terms, so a tutor's own clock change does not quietly move the lesson by an hour.

whyPoints.title: A stated limit on assessed work
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback against published criteria. No tutor writes, completes or rewrites an internal assessment, an Extended Essay or a Personal Project.

whyPoints.title: Reporting you can hold us to
whyPoints.description: A note after each session and a written report at the month, naming papers, question types and error patterns rather than effort. It makes the decision to continue or stop an informed one.

faqs.question: What should the written starting point from a first diagnostic lesson contain?
faqs.answer: Four things, in writing and short enough to read: which topics the student holds securely, which they do not, which paper is costing the most marks, and whether that loss is content, technique or time management. It should name the specific questions the tutor looked at, so you can check the conclusion against the evidence. A starting point saying the student needs confidence is a sentiment rather than a diagnosis.

faqs.question: How soon after a first month is it fair to expect a change in paper marks?
faqs.answer: Technique moves faster than content. Where the diagnostic showed strong knowledge and weak command-term handling, a difference in marked written work often appears within three or four sessions, because the student is finally being paid for what they already knew. Where the gap is genuine content across several topics, a month buys the first two topics properly rather than a visible jump in grade.

faqs.question: Who owns the study plan once a diagnostic is finished, the tutor, the school, or us?
faqs.answer: The family owns it, which is why it should exist on paper. The school sets the scheme of work and the internal deadlines, and a tutor's plan sits inside those rather than competing with them. The tutor drafts it from the diagnostic, you reorder the priorities, and the school's calendar fixes the dates it must respect. Where the two clash, the school deadline wins.

faqs.question: What happens if a diagnostic shows three weak subjects rather than one?
faqs.answer: Sequencing beats simultaneity. Booking three tutors fills every evening, removes the time the student needs for the school's own work, and usually produces three stalled starts. The better order begins with the subject whose technique transfers furthest, often the one where command-term handling is the problem, then adds a second once a weekly routine holds and the student is not exhausted.

faqs.question: If a first month produces no movement at all, what should change before the second?
faqs.answer: Something specific, named in advance. The usual candidates are the diagnosis, the focus, the frequency and the tutor, in roughly that order of likelihood. A flat month most often means the plan targeted the wrong cause: technique work where the gap was content, or content coverage where the student already knew it. More hours without a changed diagnosis repeats the month at twice the price.

faqs.question: How does a late school finish in an outer Riyadh district square with a tutor whose own working week runs Monday to Friday?
faqs.answer: It usually works, because the overlap is in the evening rather than the school day. A student finishing the run at six can start at seven, which is late afternoon for a tutor in Europe and late evening for one in India. The constraint bites on Sunday, a full school day here and the start of nothing on a Monday-to-Friday week. Agree Sunday availability explicitly.

faqs.question: Can a Sunday evening lesson survive the first weeks of a new term?
faqs.answer: Often better than a midweek one. Sunday is the first school day, so no homework has accumulated and the student is least tired, which suits teaching new technique rather than reviewing it. The risk is the opposite: there is nothing recent to mark. The fix is to set written work on Thursday for return on Sunday, so the weekend carries the practice.

faqs.question: Is a Thursday evening session a bad idea in the Kingdom?
faqs.answer: Not bad, but different. Thursday is the last school day, with Friday and Saturday after it, so anything taught has two days before the next lesson can check it. That makes Thursday strong for setting substantial written work and weak for correcting an error that needs following up quickly. For a resit candidate working to a fixed series, Thursday plus weekend practice pairs well.

faqs.question: Does a slot pinned to Arabia Standard Time move when the tutor's country changes its clocks?
faqs.answer: No, and that is exactly why it should be pinned that way. The Kingdom stays on UTC+3 and does not change its clocks. A tutor in the United Kingdom shifts an hour twice a year, so a slot recorded in their local time silently moves against your school run. Record it as a Kingdom-local time on both sides, in writing, and the tutor absorbs the change.

faqs.question: What happens to a weekly lesson when shortened school days during Ramadan push the evening later?
faqs.answer: The slot moves rather than pausing. School hours shorten, the day ends earlier, and family evening patterns change, so a fixed seven o'clock session may work better later, or may suit an afternoon that was impossible in ordinary term time. Agree the arrangement a few weeks ahead, keep the same frequency, and shorten sessions rather than skipping weeks if energy is the issue.

faqs.question: Why does a command term such as evaluate earn marks that describe does not?
faqs.answer: Because the mark scheme pays for a structure, not for information. Describe asks for features; evaluate asks for a judgement supported by weighed evidence, usually with limitations acknowledged. A candidate who answers an evaluate question with two accurate descriptions has written nothing false and still scores in the lower band, because the required comparison never appears anywhere in the answer.

faqs.question: How should a family read a grade boundary that moved between two series?
faqs.answer: As information about those papers, not about the cohort or the student. Boundaries are set after each series against how demanding that paper turned out to be, so the mark needed for a grade rises when a paper was easier and falls when it was harder. The practical consequence is that a mock mark is a position in a range, and the trend across several marked pieces matters more.

faqs.question: Is a predicted grade a forecast, a target, or something a school negotiates?
faqs.answer: It is the school's professional judgement of what the student is likely to achieve, based on marked work, mocks and the teacher's reading of the trajectory. It is not a promise, and no tutor can change it directly. What tutoring can change is the evidence the school is looking at, which is why timing matters: work produced before predictions are finalised counts, and work produced afterwards does not.

faqs.question: What does internally assessed work change about how a paid lesson is spent?
faqs.answer: It narrows what a tutor is allowed to do, and the limit is worth insisting on. A tutor can explain what a criterion strand asks, question a research design, point at a section that does not yet answer the criterion, and teach the writing technique the component rewards. No tutor writes, completes or rewrites the work, which stays the student's own from first draft to submission.

best-ib-tuition.closingHeading: Start with a trial lesson, not a brochure
best-ib-tuition.closingBody: The way to test any claim on this page is a free trial lesson with recently marked work on the screen. Bring a question the student lost marks on and ask the tutor what the mark scheme wanted. You will learn more from that twenty minutes than from any provider's description of itself, and you will leave with a written starting point whether or not you book anything.

best-ib-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below are matched to a named IB subject and level. What follows the match is the part that matters for this search: a trial lesson that is taught rather than sold, a written diagnosis you keep, and a term review that says what has not improved as well as what has.

intro.heading: Nobody awards 'best', so the family has to do the checking
paragraphs: The phrase in the search box is doing a job. A parent typing it is not expecting a league table; they are asking how to avoid wasting a term and a few thousand riyals on somebody who does not actually know the course. That is a reasonable question with a real answer, and the answer is not a provider's self-assessment. It is a short list of things a family can establish for itself in one conversation, plus an honest account of the claims that cannot be checked by anyone at all.

Start with what the system does and does not cover, because families coming from other countries often assume more oversight than exists. Private and international schools in the Kingdom are licensed by the Ministry of Education, and school evaluation and accreditation run through the Education and Training Evaluation Commission, which operates e-services for national school accreditation and for the approval of international accreditation bodies. Those arrangements govern schools. They do not vet the person who teaches your child privately for an hour on a Tuesday evening. There is no public register of individual tutors to consult, no licence number to ask for, and no complaints body that rules on teaching quality.

That gap is where the marketing lives. Browse this market for an afternoon and you will collect success percentages with no sample size, star ratings with no source, claimed tutor headcounts, and the word best attached to everything. None of it is checkable, which makes all of it equally worthless as evidence. IB Gram is not going to tell you it is the best IB tutor in Saudi Arabia, because no such title is awarded and a provider claiming it is describing how it sells rather than how it teaches. What we can do is hand you the checks and accept being measured by them.

The checks themselves are unglamorous and they work. Does the tutor name the component rather than the subject? Have they taught the specific course, at the specific level, to a mark scheme? Can they look at your child's marked work and tell you in one sentence which paper the marks are going missing on? Will they teach in the trial lesson instead of pitching? What do they say they will do if a coursework draft arrives in poor shape two days before a school deadline? A specialist answers all five quickly and concretely. A generalist talks about confidence and rapport.

The rest of the page runs through the system surrounding the decision, because the good tutor is only half the problem. There is the school's own evaluation and what it does and does not tell you. There is the difference between an institution's accreditation and an individual's qualification, which families routinely conflate. And there is the end of the road for a Saudi-based student: the Ministry of Education equivalency decision that makes an international certificate usable here, and the Qiyas tests that sit beside it. That last part is the biggest gap in this market and the part where the wrong advice costs the most.
bullets: No public register of private tutors exists in the Kingdom to check against
School licensing and school evaluation are not tutor qualifications
Any success rate without a sample size, date and method is marketing
A specialist names the component; a generalist names the subject
Equivalency and the Qiyas tests belong in the first Diploma year, not the last

best-ib-tutor.programmesIntro: The IB does not issue one qualification, it issues several, and they are treated differently once a student applies to a university. Because this page is about verification, each programme below is described alongside what the resulting certificate actually is, which is the thing that matters when a Saudi university or a foreign one assesses it.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme, full Diploma
programmes.description: Six subjects with three normally at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and the creativity, activity and service requirement. The total runs to 45 points: up to 7 in each subject and up to 3 from the Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay matrix. A failing grade in a core component can prevent the award of the Diploma whatever the subject points add up to, which is why the core deserves attention from the first term.
programmes.countryNote: The full Diploma is the version equivalency processes and university admission pages are written around, so a student who ends up with course results instead of a Diploma is in a different conversation. Any Saudi-based family planning a local university application should read the specific university's published admission criteria in the first Diploma year, because it may change which subjects should be taken at Higher Level.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme courses
programmes.description: A student may take individual Diploma Programme courses and receive results for those courses rather than the full Diploma. Schools use this for students carrying a heavy load elsewhere, for mid-course arrivals, and for students who need particular subjects without the core. The teaching and the examinations are the same; what differs is what is awarded at the end and how an admissions office reads it.
programmes.countryNote: This is the arrangement most often misunderstood by families, and the one worth asking the school about directly before accepting it. Course results and a Diploma are not interchangeable on a university application, and the equivalency process treats a certificate on its own terms. Ask the coordinator, in writing, exactly what your child will hold at the end and check it against the universities you are considering.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Assessed against four published criteria in each subject, each marked out of eight, rather than as a percentage. Years 4 and 5 carry the Personal Project, which is marked on the process as much as on the product. Some schools enter students for the optional on-screen examinations and some do not, so what a student leaves the programme holding varies between schools in the same city.
programmes.countryNote: Because entry for the optional assessments is a school decision, a family moving between schools in the Kingdom can find the picture changes underneath them. The check to run here is simple: ask the school what, if anything, your child will be formally awarded at the end of the programme, and what the receiving Diploma or IGCSE school will want to see.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Diploma Programme courses combined with a career-related study, a reflective project, and a core covering personal and professional skills, service learning and language development. It is offered at far fewer schools than the Diploma, in the Kingdom and everywhere else, so students on it rarely have a local cohort or a locally available tutor who has seen the structure before.
programmes.countryNote: The verification question here is sharper than usual. Ask whether a prospective tutor has taught the specific Diploma courses inside the programme rather than whether they have taught the Diploma, because those are different claims. For university planning, check how each target institution treats the programme, since the answer varies far more than it does for the full Diploma.

best-ib-tutor.subjectsIntro: A tutor who has genuinely taught a subject answers a specific question about it without pausing. Each subject below is paired with the question that exposes the difference, taken from the part of the course that cannot be bluffed. Use them in the trial lesson; the answers take about thirty seconds each and tell you more than any profile.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Ask what the third Higher Level paper asks for that the first two do not. A specialist describes extended multi-stage problems and the method marks lost when students write answers without working; they will also say that the Standard Level course has no equivalent paper. Anyone who treats Higher Level as the Standard Level course with more topics has not taught it.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Ask which calculator skills the papers assume. The honest answer is specific about graphical display calculator technique, regression and statistical testing, and about students who reach a correct value and then write a conclusion not tied back to the data. A tutor who answers by comparing this course to the analysis course in general terms has probably only taught the other one.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Ask where candidates lose marks on the long-answer paper. A specialist talks about explanation chains compressed into one sentence, unit and significant-figure discipline, and the way Higher Level content layers onto the shared core so a weak core topic is examined twice. They should also ask what apparatus the school has before discussing the investigation.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Ask what the data booklet is for and how students under-use it. The answer should be concrete: which constants and relationships are supplied, and why that changes what is worth memorising. Follow with mechanisms. A tutor who has taught the course will mention charges and curly arrows unprompted, because that is where the marks go.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Ask how an extended response is credited. A specialist says it is marked against a list of specific points, so a fluent essay that misses several of them scores poorly, and that definitions are marked strictly. Anyone who describes biology as a memory subject and leaves it there is describing how they revised it, not how it is examined.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Ask what wrecks a guided textual analysis. The answer is context-dumping and writing about content instead of technique and structure. A Higher Level specialist will also name the separate formal essay on a studied work and explain how its assessment differs from the papers. Vague answers about critical thinking mean no marked scripts have passed through their hands.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Ask whether an answer without a diagram can reach the top band. The correct answer is no, and a specialist explains that the diagram must be correctly labelled and correctly shifted, not merely present. They should also name the Higher Level quantitative paper and the three commentaries in the internal assessment, each built on a recent article and marked on the application of a named key concept.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Ask when preparation for the third Higher Level paper should start. A specialist says as soon as the pre-released case study is available, because that paper rewards months of work on one organisation. They will also warn that students pick organisations that cannot supply the information the internal assessment needs, which is the single most common avoidable problem in the subject.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Ask which component Standard Level candidates do not sit. The answer is the regional-option third paper, which carries more than a third of the Higher Level grade on its own. A specialist will also name the source-work paper and say which question type is most often mishandled. This is the subject where the Higher Level and Standard Level courses diverge most sharply.

subjects.name: Chemistry and Physics internal assessment
subjects.description: Ask what they will and will not do with a draft investigation. The only acceptable answer involves reading the student's own work, mapping it against the published criteria, asking the questions an examiner would ask, and sending the student away to redraft. Any hint of tidying it up, drafting a section or supplying analysis is a reason to end the conversation.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Ask how the essay differs from a normal essay. A specialist explains that it answers a prescribed title and is assessed on the quality of the argument about knowledge rather than on examples collected, and that the exhibition works from objects and a prompt. A tutor who offers to find good examples for your child has misunderstood the component and the rules.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: Ask what makes a research question answerable. A specialist talks about narrowing until the question can be answered inside the word limit with sources the student can actually reach, and about the reflection requirement and what it is for. They should also say, without being asked, that the school's supervisor leads and that a tutor works alongside that rather than around it.

best-ib-tutor.regionsTitle: The provision picture, city by city
best-ib-tutor.regionsIntro: What you can verify locally depends on where you are, because provision is uneven across the Kingdom. In two cities a family compares schools; in most of the rest it takes what exists. These notes describe what a family can realistically check about local provision before concluding that an outside specialist is needed.

regions.name: Riyadh
regions.note: The deepest provision in the Kingdom and the only market with a genuine choice between schools running the same Higher Level combination. It is also the one city where a family can compare a local private tutor against an online specialist on quality rather than on availability, which makes the checks on this page immediately useful.

regions.name: Jeddah
regions.note: A long coastal city with IB World Schools, Cambridge schools and long-established international schools serving particular communities. Term dates and calendars differ school by school here, so a claim about what is normal in Jeddah should always be checked against your own school's published calendar rather than against a general description.

regions.name: Dammam, Al Khobar and Dhahran
regions.note: A single school market spread across three cities, with Diploma provision at some campuses and not others. Families here can verify something most cannot: whether a subject combination exists anywhere within reach. That answer often decides whether outside teaching is a preference or the only route.

regions.name: Makkah and Madinah
regions.note: Provision is thinner than in the two largest cities, and the local pool of people who have taught a specific Higher Level course is correspondingly smaller. The honest check here is arithmetic rather than judgement: ask how many candidates sat the subject locally last series, because a tutor cannot have taught a course nobody ran.

regions.name: Jubail and the industrial cities
regions.note: Campus and company schooling shapes what is available, and the parent population includes a high proportion of professionals who read a specification carefully. Families here tend to run the checks on this page properly, and they are also the quickest to notice when a provider's claims cannot be substantiated.

regions.name: Thuwal, Tabuk, AlUla and NEOM
regions.note: Newer and campus-based communities where mid-course arrivals are common and the local tutoring market is young. There is very little local reputation to draw on, which means the verification burden sits almost entirely with the family and the checks matter more here than anywhere else.

regions.name: Abha, Khamis Mushait and the south
regions.note: Small international-curriculum cohorts sharing a catchment at altitude, where subject specialists are scarce for structural reasons rather than temporary ones. A family here is usually not choosing between a local tutor and an online one; the question is whether the online tutor is the right one.

schoolClusters.note: The largest set of Diploma and Cambridge provision in the Kingdom. Schools are licensed by the Ministry of Education and evaluated through ETEC, and several also hold accreditation from international bodies. None of that describes a private tutor's competence. Students we support attend schools including these.

A mixed cluster of IB World Schools, Cambridge schools and community international schools. Ask a school directly which programmes it is authorised to offer and which subjects it will actually run at Higher Level next year, because the second answer is the one that affects your child.

Several campuses across the Dammam, Al Khobar, Dhahran and Jubail market, with the Diploma offered at some and not at others. This is the cluster where checking subject availability before enrolling, rather than after, saves families the most trouble.

modes.description: Free, and deliberately not a sales call. The tutor teaches something real, usually a question your child has already got wrong, while you watch what they do with a wrong answer. The questions in the subjects list on this page are the ones to ask afterwards; a specialist answers each in a sentence and names a component.

modes.title: A written diagnosis you keep
modes.description: The first working session produces a short document rather than an impression: the component and the topics where marks are being lost, and the order in which they will be addressed. It is the thing you hold the tuition to at the end of term, and it is also the handover document if the tutor ever has to change.

A priority order with reasons attached

modes.title: A term, then an honest review
modes.description: A term is long enough to judge and short enough to stop. The review states what has measurably changed with reference to marked work, what has not changed, and what should happen next, including the option of stopping or moving the hours to a different subject. A review containing only good news is not a review.

Explicit about what has not improved

modes.title: Coursework review with a feedback trail
modes.description: For an internal assessment, Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge essay or reflective project. The tutor reads the student's own draft, maps it against the published criteria, asks the questions an examiner would ask, and the student redrafts. Feedback is given in writing, which is deliberate: it evidences that the work is the student's.

sections.heading: What 'best' can mean, given that nobody awards it
paragraphs: The word has no referent in this market, and pretending otherwise is the first dishonesty. There is no examination for tutors, no ranking body, no published outcome data, and no mechanism by which one provider could be shown to outperform another. So any page that answers the question by asserting itself is answering a different question than the one you asked. The useful move is to replace an unanswerable claim with a set of answerable ones, which is what a parent was reaching for in the first place.

Three kinds of claim circulate here. The first is checkable in a conversation: what the tutor has taught, at what level, to which board, and whether they can read your child's marked work and locate the problem. The second is checkable with a document: a degree, a teaching qualification, a record of marking or moderating for a board. The third is not checkable at all, and this is the category that fills most provider websites. Satisfaction percentages, star ratings, grade-improvement figures and tutor headcounts are presented as evidence and are not evidence, because none of them carries a sample size, a date or a method.

The practical rule is to pay attention only to the first two categories and treat the third as noise. If a provider cannot tell you how a number was produced, the number is decoration. Our own position on this page is the same one we would want applied to a competitor: judge the specificity of the answers, the quality of the trial lesson, and whether the written diagnosis after the first session names a component or hedges. Those three things are visible to a family before any money changes hands, which is exactly why they are the ones worth using.

sections.heading: What is regulated in Saudi education, and what is not
paragraphs: Families arriving from elsewhere often assume a tutor sits inside the same oversight as a school. They do not, and understanding the shape of the system makes it obvious why the checks have to be yours. Private and international schools in the Kingdom are licensed by the Ministry of Education. School evaluation and accreditation run through the Education and Training Evaluation Commission, which operates e-services for national school accreditation and for the approval of international accreditation bodies. Alongside those sits the National Center for Assessment, Qiyas, which runs the admission tests.

Each of those bodies does a specific job and none of them does yours. A school licence says a school may operate. An evaluation outcome says something about a school's provision at a point in time. Programme authorisation from the IB says a school may deliver a programme. Not one of them is a statement about an individual who teaches your child privately for an hour a week, and none of them can be cited by a tutoring provider as a qualification. If a provider implies otherwise, that is itself a useful signal about everything else on their site.

The thing families most often conflate is an institution's accreditation with an individual's qualification. A school holding accreditation tells you about processes, governance and provision. A tutor's competence is a separate question answered by their own subject background and their record of teaching the actual course. Both matter and they are not substitutes. The table below separates the jobs so you can stop looking for the wrong assurance from the wrong body, which is where a surprising amount of a family's energy goes.

sections.heading: What a school evaluation report tells a parent, and what it leaves out
paragraphs: Evaluation outcomes are a genuine source of information and a poor source of the information families actually want. They describe a school as an institution: leadership, provision, safeguarding, curriculum delivery, the quality of teaching across a cohort. Read as a description of an organisation they are useful. Read as a prediction of what your particular child's Higher Level physics year will be like, they are close to silent, because the thing that will decide that is one teacher and one small group.

The questions that actually predict a Diploma student's experience are narrower than anything an evaluation covers. How many students are entered for each Higher Level option. Who teaches that option, and whether they taught it last year. Whether the school has ever run the option before. Whether a subject is taught by a specialist or by someone covering it alongside another subject. What happens to the group if that teacher leaves mid-course. Schools answer these questions when asked directly and almost never publish them, so a family has to ask.

This is also where the honest case for outside teaching sits, and it is a case about risk rather than about quality. A Higher Level option running with one teacher and a handful of students is a single point of failure on a component that will decide a university offer and cannot be repeated. Buying outside subject teaching in that situation is redundancy, not criticism of the school. Equally, a well-staffed subject with a specialist teacher and a decent-sized group may need nothing at all, and a tutor who cannot tell you which of those two situations you are in should not be billing you.
bullets: Ask how many candidates are entered for each Higher Level option
