sections.heading: The autumn term, and why early hours are the cheapest you will buy
paragraphs: Nothing about an autumn-term rate is lower. Those hours are cheap because of what they prevent. A student who learns to set out working so that method marks are earned, and who can read a command term accurately, never has to be taught either skill again. Both take a handful of lessons in a quiet term and are close to untrainable in the weeks when four subjects are demanding revision at the same time.

The content case runs the same way. In the sciences the autumn term covers the foundations everything later rests on: moles and equations in Chemistry, forces and energy in Physics, cells and transport in Biology. A student who ends that term secure in them finds the spring work hard but comprehensible. A student who does not spends the spring reciting rather than reasoning, and recitation runs out of marks somewhere around the four-mark questions.

This is also the term to deal with the practical component. Cambridge sciences carry either a practical examination or an alternative-to-practical paper, and the alternative paper is a written test of method, precision and sources of error rather than of content. It can be taught, but it is taught by working through other people's experiments and criticising them, which is slow. A student who has criticised a long run of experimental methods by the end of Year 10 reads that paper as a familiar exercise rather than as an unpleasant surprise in the middle of a difficult fortnight.

sections.heading: Mocks, the spring term, and the one report worth reacting to
paragraphs: School mock examinations produce the first evidence worth spending money on. Earlier marks mostly measure how a class has settled; a mock marked to the published scheme measures what a candidate can do alone against a clock. Ask for the script itself, not only the percentage. The useful information is in which questions lost marks and why, and a percentage hides every bit of it.

Read the breakdown with three questions. Were marks lost on content the student has not learned, on method they could not set out, or on command terms they misread? Each carries a different price. Unlearned content takes lessons. Method takes practice with feedback. Misread command terms take one session and then discipline. A tutor who cannot tell you which of the three is costing your child most has not marked enough scripts to be worth a premium.

The spring term is also when predicted grades are produced for post-16 applications, and a prediction is a professional estimate rather than a promise. If a number looks wrong, the productive question is which components it rests on. Coursework deadlines land in the same weeks, and the line there is firm: a tutor teaches the skills a component assesses and gives feedback on a draft the student has written. No tutor should write any part of assessed work. Keep the drafts and the feedback together as you go, because a dated trail answers a school's questions in a way assurances cannot.

sections.heading: The last stretch before the June series, and what an hour buys then
paragraphs: Entries close months ahead of the June series and the deadline sits with the school's examinations officer, so the tier and the component list are usually fixed well before the final term starts. That changes what tutoring can do. Nothing in the last eight weeks lifts a Core entry above a C, and nothing reteaches two years of a course. What the hours can do is recover marks the candidate is already close to earning.

The work in that window is deliberately narrow. Timed questions every week, marked against the scheme. The two or three weakest topics taught properly rather than revised. Command terms drilled until the student underlines them without thinking. The practical or alternative-to-practical paper, which is the most neglected component in most candidates' revision. Then full papers to time in the final fortnight, so that the clock stops being a surprise on the day.

Expect a good tutor to refuse things in this period. Starting a new topic from nothing with three weeks left is usually a worse use of the hour than making half-known topics reliable. A tutor who agrees to every request a worried parent makes in the final term is being agreeable rather than useful. The same discipline applies to how many subjects are under support at once: two is about the most a candidate can absorb in a final term, and a family funding four is paying for hours nobody has time to use.

sections.heading: What actually drives an IGCSE online tutor's rate
paragraphs: The table below lists what moves an advertised figure, with the kind of listing each piece of evidence comes from. None of these numbers is IB Gram's price and none is a market average. They are the advertised starting points of businesses competing for enquiries, which makes them useful as a floor and misleading as a benchmark for what a family should expect to pay.

Scarcity does most of the work. An Additional Mathematics or Extended Physics specialist is rare in every Saudi city, and the rate reflects how many families are chasing the same small group of people rather than how good any one of them is. Marking experience is the second driver, and the one most worth paying for at this level, because a tutor who has marked a paper knows what a scheme credits and what it silently ignores.

Level runs the other way. IGCSE rates sit below Diploma Higher Level rates for the same tutor, so a family moving a child into a post-16 course should expect the hourly figure to rise rather than hold. Travel is the only driver that disappears completely online. An in-home arrangement in Riyadh prices the drive and the traffic risk into the hour; a video lesson does not. Package length is the last driver and the easiest to misread: a lower hourly figure inside a long block is only cheaper if the whole block gets used, and a school term holds fewer teachable weeks than a calendar suggests.

sections.heading: The November series, resits, and starting late without wasting money
paragraphs: Candidates in the Kingdom sit the June and November series. Cambridge also runs a February and March series, but that sitting is open to candidates in India only, and a family told otherwise has been handed a wrong fact they may act on. November is the resit route, and also the route for students whose school year does not centre on a June finish.

A November entry changes the shape of a year rather than its content. The work runs through the summer and the autumn term with the papers at the end of it, which means a student revises one course while classmates begin the next. That is harder than it sounds, and it is the main reason resit candidates need fewer hours of content and more hours of structure: a written weekly plan, a fixed slot, and marked work coming back when it was promised.

Starting late is not the same as starting too late. A student arriving in the Kingdom part-way through Year 11, or a family deciding in the spring that one subject needs help, can still make a material difference to the result. The difference comes from triage. Name the two components where marks are most recoverable and work only on those. One practical point for late starters: confirm with the school that the entry has been made, and for which tier, before a single lesson is paid for. More than one family has found out the answer far too late to change it.

faqs.question: What should an online IGCSE tutor ask for before the first lesson is booked?
faqs.answer: The board, the syllabus code, the tier and the most recent piece of timed work, ideally the marked script rather than the percentage. A tutor who asks for all four is planning a diagnostic. A tutor who asks only for the subject and the year group is planning to start at the front of the textbook, which is the most expensive way to teach a student who is already most of the way through a course.

faqs.question: How is a starting point measured when a student has no recent timed marks?
faqs.answer: By creating one. A first session can set two or three past questions under time, marked live against the published scheme, which produces more usable information than an hour of conversation about how the subject feels. The output should be a short list: which components are weak, whether the cause is content, method or command terms, and what gets worked on first.

faqs.question: Who owns the teaching plan once lessons start, the tutor or the school?
faqs.answer: The school owns the course and the entry; the tutor owns the plan for the hours you are paying for. Those should agree, which means the tutor needs to know the school's scheme of work and the order topics are being taught in. Where they diverge, the school's sequence wins during term time and the tutor's priorities take over in a revision block.

faqs.question: How do we decide whether to keep paying after one full term?
faqs.answer: Compare marked work from the start of the term against marked work from the end of it on the same question type. If lost method marks have fallen and the student can now explain what a command term wants, the money is working even if the grade has not moved yet. If neither has changed in a term, the problem is the match or the plan rather than the number of hours.

faqs.question: What does a plateau look like in an IGCSE subject, and what breaks it?
faqs.answer: Marks that stall two or three off the grade above, on papers the student finishes comfortably. It usually means the easy marks are secure and the extended-response questions are not. Breaking it needs a change of activity rather than more hours: writing answers to a scheme, comparing them with a full-mark version, and rewriting until the structure is automatic. That loop usually takes three or four sessions to bite.

faqs.question: How many evenings a week can an IGCSE student give up before lessons stop helping?
faqs.answer: Two is comfortable, three is the practical limit, and four usually produces worse results than two because there is no time left to do the work set. A Sunday-to-Thursday school week with homework already in it does not have five teachable evenings. Where several subjects are weak at once, rotating subjects across a fortnight beats stacking them into one week.

faqs.question: What happens to a weekly online lesson in the week of school mock examinations?
faqs.answer: It is usually worth keeping and worth repurposing. The most useful mock-week session is a short run through the paper type being sat the next morning, focused on timing and command terms rather than new content. Some families prefer to move the slot to the week afterwards so the hour can be spent on the marked script, which is the better long-term use of it.

faqs.question: Is a Saturday morning session better than a school-night one for an IGCSE candidate?
faqs.answer: Often, yes. Friday and Saturday are the weekend in the Kingdom, so a Saturday morning student arrives rested and with time to finish the work set afterwards. The trade is that momentum through the school week is weaker, and a tutor on a Monday-to-Friday calendar elsewhere may not offer Saturdays at all. Ask before the slot is agreed rather than afterwards.

faqs.question: Do lessons stop over the long summer break, and what does that cost later?
faqs.answer: Most families pause and that is usually reasonable. The exception is a student going into the final year with a weak subject, or a November candidate, where a reduced schedule through the break is the difference between arriving ready and arriving behind. If you pause, agree in writing whether the slot is held, because a popular evening hour rarely survives six idle weeks.

faqs.question: How do shortened school days during Ramadan change what an evening lesson can cover?
faqs.answer: School days are shorter and evening routines shift, so the hour that worked in the autumn may not work at all. Some families move the session later, others move it earlier in the afternoon while the school day ends sooner. Plan for less homework capacity rather than more, and treat the period as a time to consolidate taught material instead of introducing a difficult new topic.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE components can still be improved in the last eight weeks, and which are fixed?
faqs.answer: The tier and the component list are fixed once entries close. Anything that depends on technique is still open: command terms, timing, the structure of extended answers, and the practical or alternative-to-practical paper, which rewards taught method rather than long revision. Content gaps across whole topics are the hardest thing to close in that window, which is why triage beats coverage.

faqs.question: How do three papers in one IGCSE subject combine into a single grade?
faqs.answer: Each component carries a published weighting, the marks are scaled accordingly and the total is compared against grade boundaries set after that series. A candidate can therefore lose a grade on a weak component even with strong papers elsewhere. Ask the school which components your child is entered for and what each is worth, because that decides where revision time is best spent.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a raw mark and the grade printed on an IGCSE result?
faqs.answer: A raw mark is what the examiner awarded on that script. It is scaled to the component's weighting, combined with the other components, and then read against boundaries set for that series once the papers have been marked. This is why a percentage from a mock, marked against an older boundary set, is an indication rather than a forecast of a grade.

faqs.question: Why does a mock percentage not translate into an IGCSE grade?
faqs.answer: Because boundaries are set after each series against the difficulty of those papers and the performance of that cohort, and because a school mock may use a different paper mix or a harsher internal mark scheme. Treat the percentage as a ranking of the student against their own earlier work, and treat the marked script as the document that tells you what to do next.

best-igcse-tutor.tutorsIntro: Below are tutors who teach Cambridge and Edexcel IGCSE courses to students in the Kingdom. Read them the way you would read a shortlist: look for the syllabus codes and the components, and then ask the questions set out further down this page before you commit to anything.

intro.heading: What a parent is really choosing between
paragraphs: The search term is a superlative but the decision underneath it is a comparison. A family typing this query has usually already tried the school's own support, or a group class, or a platform that charged very little and sent a different person each week, and is now trying to work out which of five quite different things to buy next. Ranking them against each other is impossible in the abstract, because they do different jobs. A group class at a local centre is good value for structure and pace and cannot diagnose why one student keeps losing four marks on the same type of question. A matched specialist can do the second and is a waste of money if the first is what the student needs.

So the honest version of this question is not which provider is best. It is: what is the specific thing going wrong, and who is equipped to fix that? A student who understands the material and will not sit down and work needs supervision and someone they respect. A student losing marks on alternative-to-practical technique needs someone who has prepared candidates for that paper. A student about to be entered at the wrong tier needs twenty minutes of advice and no lessons at all. The three answers cost very different amounts, and a provider who sells the same package to all three is not diagnosing anything.

There is a second reason the superlative does not survive contact with reality. Fit is a real variable and it is not a quality ranking. A tutor who is precise, patient and methodical will get a quiet, anxious student further than a brilliant, fast-talking one, and the reverse is true for a student who learns by arguing. Neither tutor is better. One of them is better for your child, which is why a trial lesson tells you more than a biography, and why changing tutor after two sessions is a normal administrative act rather than a complaint about anybody.

This page is therefore built as a set of tests rather than as a pitch. What the five options actually are and what each is for. What the credentials mean, one by one, and which of them predicts anything about an IGCSE result. What examiner experience is and how to check it in a sentence. The questions to ask in a trial lesson and what a real answer sounds like. Which claims to discount on sight. Then the practical constraints in the Kingdom: the Sunday-to-Thursday week a weekly slot has to survive, what the local school market can and cannot staff, and what changes when a family has just moved curriculum.

Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the Kingdom; home visits are a service we offer only in India. That is relevant to this particular query, because the question of who is genuinely good at teaching a specific IGCSE component and the question of who lives within a twenty-minute drive have nothing to do with each other. Removing distance from the search is the only way the first question gets a real answer, especially outside Riyadh, Jeddah and the Eastern Province cluster.
bullets: Ask which board, which paper and when they last marked it; vagueness is the answer
Ask for the syllabus codes they have taught and how many cohorts they saw through
Use the trial lesson as an interview, and ask for a past paper marked with reasons
Discount any figure offered without a number of candidates, a date and a method
Expect to change tutor occasionally; fit is not a judgement on anyone's ability

best-igcse-tutor.programmesIntro: A tutor is only as useful as their grip on the specific qualification in front of them. These are the four courses Saudi families most often need taught at this stage, described from the tutor's side: what a person has to know to teach each one well, and what the gap looks like when they do not.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: A tutor teaching Cambridge needs the tier structure in their head, not looked up: which subjects split into Core and Extended, what each ceiling is, and which papers belong to which tier. In the sciences they need to have prepared candidates for either the practical test or the alternative-to-practical paper, because that component examines apparatus, method, error and tabulation as a skill in its own right. Ask which of the two your child sits and watch whether the answer is instant.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge is the more common board in Saudi international schools, so most tutors in this market will claim it. The claim is cheap and the check is easy: ask for the four-digit code and the paper numbers. A tutor who has genuinely taught 0620 Extended will say the paper numbers before you finish the question. One who has taught chemistry in general will ask you which papers those are.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Reported 9 to 1 rather than A* to G, tiered only in mathematics, and with the sciences examining experimental skill inside the written papers rather than in a separate component. A tutor who moves from Cambridge to Edexcel without noticing will teach good subject content against the wrong question architecture. The coursework options differ too, and whether a school has taken one changes what the year contains.
programmes.countryNote: Edexcel entries in the Kingdom cluster in schools that also run Edexcel A Levels. Families who move between a Cambridge school and an Edexcel school mid-course need a tutor who can name the differences rather than one who treats the two as the same examination. That is a fair question to ask directly in a trial lesson, and the answer is diagnostic either way.

programmes.name: Cambridge O Level
programmes.description: Still entered by some schools, particularly those serving South Asian communities, and routinely confused with IGCSE by tutors and parents alike. The syllabuses are related but the components are not identical, and a candidate entered for O Level who is taught from IGCSE past papers will meet question styles in the examination that nobody rehearsed with them.
programmes.countryNote: This is the single most common silent mismatch in the Kingdom's tutoring market. If your child's entry says O Level, say so when you ask for a tutor, and ask the tutor to confirm they have taught that specification rather than the IGCSE equivalent. A good tutor will volunteer the difference before you raise it.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Assessed against four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight, with no external written papers in most schools. A tutor used only to examined courses will teach content well and miss what the criteria reward, which is where MYP grades are actually won and lost. The Personal Project needs a documented process rather than a polished product.
programmes.countryNote: Plenty of Saudi students sit in the Middle Years Programme and then move into IGCSE or straight into the Diploma, and the two assessment cultures are genuinely different. A tutor who can explain criterion-referenced marking to a parent in plain words is a tutor who understands it. One who converts everything to percentages is guessing.

best-igcse-tutor.subjectsIntro: A tutor's subject claim is testable, and the test is different in each subject. For each of these, here is the thing a genuine specialist knows and a capable generalist usually does not. Use them as interview questions; you do not need to know the answers yourself to hear which kind of answer you are getting.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Ask whether they teach 0580, 0607 or Edexcel 4MA1, and what the difference means for a student heading to IB mathematics. A specialist will mention the investigation paper on 0607 and the non-calculator component without prompting, and will talk about method marks rather than right answers.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: Ask how 0606 prepares a student for the first term of A Level or IB Higher Level mathematics. A specialist talks about calculus and trigonometry arriving a year early and about how much easier the sixth-form start becomes. A generalist describes it as harder mathematics.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.levels: Tiered on Cambridge, single tier on Edexcel
subjects.description: Ask which practical component the candidate sits and what it rewards. A specialist distinguishes the practical test from the alternative-to-practical paper and talks about error, apparatus and tabulation. They will also mention graph marks, which are the cheapest marks on the paper and the most often dropped.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.levels: Tiered on Cambridge, single tier on Edexcel
subjects.description: Ask where Extended candidates separate from Core ones. The answer should be moles, electrolysis and organic chemistry, and a specialist will say which of the three your child's school usually rushes. Vague answers about revision technique indicate someone teaching from a textbook rather than from the papers.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.levels: Tiered on Cambridge, single tier on Edexcel
subjects.description: Ask how strictly definitions are marked. A specialist will say the syllabus wording earns the mark and a near-enough answer earns nothing, and will be able to give an example. They will also raise the data-interpretation questions, which are where students who revised only their notes lose ground.

subjects.name: Combined and co-ordinated sciences
subjects.description: Ask what a student from this route is missing if they go on to a higher-level science. A specialist answers with topics, not with reassurance. That list is the most valuable thing a tutor can give a family at the end of Year 11, and it takes one session to produce.

subjects.name: First language English
subjects.description: Ask whether the school has taken a coursework route in place of a written paper. A specialist will ask you that question first, because it changes the whole year. They will also talk about writing to a stated form and audience rather than about creative writing in general.

subjects.name: English as a second language
subjects.description: Ask whether the entry is the code where speaking is reported separately or the one where it counts towards the grade. A specialist knows there are two and knows which one matters for a student applying abroad. They will also mention that the listening paper is the least practised component.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies
subjects.description: Ask what the difference is between a definition and an answer. In economics a specialist talks about labelled diagrams and an explicit written link to the question; in business about recommendations justified against the case material. These two subjects are the most commonly taught by a non-specialist anywhere in the Kingdom.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Ask how they teach pseudocode and trace tables. A specialist will say immediately that strong programmers lose marks by writing working code where pseudocode was asked for. A tutor whose background is software rather than teaching often does not know this until a student's mock comes back.

subjects.name: History and Geography
subjects.description: Ask what a source question is really testing. The answer should be using the source rather than describing it, with provenance doing work. In geography, ask about the skills paper and whichever coursework or alternative paper the school has chosen, because the skills are learnable in a way the case studies are not.

best-igcse-tutor.regionsTitle: What the weekly slot looks like, city by city
best-igcse-tutor.regionsIntro: A tutor who is right on paper is useless at an hour your child cannot sustain. The constraint varies across the Kingdom in ways that have nothing to do with teaching: commute length, when the school day ends, what the family's working week looks like, and how far the nearest alternative is if this does not work out.

regions.name: Riyadh
regions.note: The city is roughly an hour across in traffic, so the gap between the end of school and the start of a lesson is a real negotiation. Families in the north of the city often cannot start before six, which pushes a second subject to a different evening rather than the same one.

regions.name: Jeddah
regions.note: A long coastal spine from the historic centre north to Obhur, and the commute decides the slot more than the school day does. Families further north routinely settle on a later start and a shorter session rather than a longer one that ends too late.

regions.name: Al Khobar, Dammam and Dhahran
regions.note: Three cities that behave as one: a family may live in one, work in a second and send children to school in a third. The practical effect is an unpredictable arrival time, so a slot with ten minutes of slack built into it survives where an exact one does not.

regions.name: Jubail
regions.note: Industrial shift patterns mean a parent is often unavailable at precisely the hour a child is free, which matters because someone has to be in the house for a younger student. Earlier sessions tend to work better here than in the big cities.

regions.name: Makkah and Madinah
regions.note: The year bends around the Hajj and Umrah seasons, which affects travel, traffic and family availability rather than the syllabus. Evening slots carry most of the year, and it is worth agreeing in advance which weeks will be skipped rather than cancelling them one at a time.

regions.name: Al Ahsa
regions.note: An hour and a half inland from the Eastern Province cluster, so any option involving a drive to a larger city is a serious undertaking. That removes in-home tutoring from the realistic list for most scarce subjects and makes the slot easier to protect.

regions.name: Tabuk, AlUla and the north-west
regions.note: Long distances and a thin local market, with project housing bringing in families mid-course. The scheduling question here is usually the connection rather than the clock: test a live video lesson properly before committing to a weekly arrangement.

regions.name: Abha and Khamis Mushait
regions.note: A shared catchment at high altitude, about 25km apart, with a small international-school market between them. Families often have no local fallback at all, which makes the reliability of a weekly slot matter more than its exact time.

schoolClusters.note: Ask any of these schools the same question you would ask a tutor: who teaches the higher-tier set, and how many candidates are in it. A school with a specialist in every subject is rare anywhere, and the honest ones will tell you which subjects are covered rather than specialised.

Riyadh has the widest range of programmes in the Kingdom, and families here are more likely to be choosing between schools than compensating for one. The questions worth asking before enrolling are about timetabling and set sizes, not about facilities.

Company and campus schooling dominates here, which means cohorts turn over as contracts rotate and a subject set can change size between one year and the next. Ask about the specific campus rather than the group, because programmes differ between them.

Ask for a past-paper question to be worked and marked. What comes back tells you whether this person reads a mark scheme for a living or has looked at one occasionally.

modes.description: The arrangement most families want: a fixed slot, the same person, running alongside the school's scheme of work. Continuity is most of the value here, because a tutor who has seen four weeks of a student's working knows things that cannot be handed over in a note. Agree the slot in Arabia Standard Time so it survives a clock change elsewhere.

Families use this when a grade has dropped and nobody can say why, or when a predicted grade looks out of line with the work. It is cheap and it often prevents a term of the wrong teaching.

modes.description: When the match is wrong, the second tutor should not start from nothing. Diagnostic notes, the topics covered, the work set and what the student responded to all carry across. sections.heading: The five things a family is actually choosing between
paragraphs: Before any judgement about quality, it helps to see the options as different products rather than as better and worse versions of one. There are five in this market, and each is genuinely the right answer for some students. The mistake families make is not picking the wrong one on purpose; it is picking by price or by availability without ever naming what the hour is supposed to achieve.

The school's own support comes first because it is free and aligned with the teaching. Its limit is that the explanation a student did not understand is likely to be delivered again by the person who gave it the first time. A group class at a centre buys structure, pace and company at a low cost per hour, and cannot do individual diagnosis. A large platform at a headline rate buys availability and a low entry price, and typically cannot promise the same person next week or that they have taught your board and tier. A local in-home tutor buys presence in the room, which genuinely helps some students, and carries a travel loading in the rate while narrowing the search to whoever lives nearby.

A matched online specialist is the fifth, and its honest description is narrow: it reaches scarce specialisms and it teaches technique against the actual mark scheme. It cannot put an adult physically in the room, and it cannot do the student's work for them. Read the table the way a buyer should, by starting from the last column. Whatever is going wrong, rule out the options that structurally cannot fix it, and then compare only what is left.

sections.heading: What good actually means for an IGCSE tutor
paragraphs: Strip away the marketing and a good IGCSE tutor does four separable things. They know the specific assessment: the board, the code, the tier, the components, and what each paper rewards. They can diagnose, which means reading a student's own work and saying where the marks went and why, rather than inferring a weakness from a grade. They can teach, which is a different skill again and includes being liked enough to be listened to by a fifteen-year-old. And they are reliable, which sounds trivial until a tutor starts missing sessions in the final term.

Those four are not equally distributed and they are not equally scarce. Assessment knowledge is the one most often claimed and least often held. Teaching skill is common among school teachers and variable among people whose background is entirely one-to-one. Diagnosis is the rarest of the four and the easiest to test, because you can simply hand over a marked paper and see what comes back. Reliability cannot be tested in advance at all, which is why continuity of the same named person matters more than any credential.

A fifth factor sits outside the tutor altogether, and it is fit. Pace, manner, how much silence a tutor tolerates, whether they explain or interrogate: these determine whether a competent tutor is effective with your particular child. Fit is not a ranking and it is not predictable from a profile. That is the whole argument for treating a trial lesson as the decision point and for treating a change of tutor as routine. A family that has changed tutor once and found the right one has done this process correctly, not badly.
bullets: Assessment knowledge: the board, the code, the tier, the components
Diagnosis: reading the student's own work rather than inferring from a grade
Teaching: explaining it again differently, and being listened to
Reliability: the same person, the same slot, through the final term

sections.heading: Credentials, one by one, and what each one predicts
paragraphs: Qualifications are not interchangeable signals of quality; each predicts something specific and is silent about the rest. A subject degree predicts content security far above IGCSE level and tells you nothing about whether the holder has read a mark scheme. A teaching qualification predicts training in how learning is structured and assessed, which matters most with a disengaged or anxious student, and says nothing about this board's papers. Marking experience predicts knowledge of how answers are actually credited, and says nothing about whether the person can explain anything to a teenager.

The most reliable single credential for an IGCSE candidate is years spent teaching this specific syllabus to this tier in a school, because it bundles several of the others and it is the easiest to verify. A tutor who has taught 0625 Extended for six cohorts will know which topics the textbook handles badly, which questions recur, where their own students historically lost marks, and what the alternative-to-practical paper does to a student who has never tabulated results properly. None of that can be bluffed for more than two questions.

Treat company certificates as what they are: evidence that a company runs a training programme. Treat a tutoring-only background as neither good nor bad but as something to test, since it predicts strong one-to-one diagnosis and gives no evidence about seeing a cohort through to a result. And treat any credential that is described rather than named as absent. 'Highly qualified' is not a qualification. 'Examiner experience' without a board, a paper and a recent series is a phrase, not a fact.

sections.heading: Examiner experience: what it is, and the sentence that checks it
paragraphs: Boards recruit practising teachers to mark their papers, train them on the mark scheme for that series, and monitor their marking against it. A person who has done that has seen several hundred real answers to the same question and watched which ones were credited. That is genuinely valuable, especially in the final terms, because it converts vague advice about exam technique into specific knowledge: which of two plausible phrasings earns the mark, how much a diagram has to show, whether a missing unit costs anything.

The phrase is also one of the most elastic in this market. It can mean current marking for your board on your paper. It can mean one series a decade ago on a different specification. It can mean marking at a different level entirely, or team leadership, or a colleague's experience described loosely in a company biography. All of those get written the same way on a website, so the phrase itself carries almost no information.

One sentence resolves it: which board, which paper, and when did you last mark it? A real answer comes back immediately and specifically, naming a component and a recent series, and is often accompanied by an unprompted detail about what that marking taught them. A weak answer becomes general, moves to a different qualification, or shifts to how long the company has been operating. Neither answer should end the conversation on its own, because a superb teacher without marking experience will beat an indifferent examiner. But a provider who will not answer that question plainly has told you something important about everything else on their page.
bullets: Which board, which paper, and when did you last mark it?
What did the marking change about how you teach this component?
Was it this specification, or an earlier version of it?
A plain 'no, but I have taught it for six cohorts' is a good answer

sections.heading: The claims to discount, and the questions that test them
paragraphs: This market runs on unverifiable assertion, and the reason is simple: a parent cannot check a teaching claim before buying, so a provider who invents one is rarely caught. The defence is not cynicism but a short list of standard questions. Each row of the table below pairs a common claim with what it might really mean, the question that tests it, and what a genuine answer sounds like.

The general principle applies beyond this table. Any figure offered without a number of candidates, a date and a method is decoration. A ranking claim that no independent body awarded means nothing, and in a market with no official ranking, every provider claiming to be the leading one is making the same empty statement. A star average on a platform aggregates self-selected reviews, and those reviews usually describe responsiveness and politeness rather than whether a grade moved. None of this means the provider is bad; it means the claim is not evidence, and you should ask for something that is.

What a reputable provider can actually offer is narrow and verifiable: a named tutor, a stated syllabus and component, a free trial lesson you can judge, a past paper marked with reasons written down, and a clear statement of what happens when the match is wrong. Ask for those five. A provider who supplies them has given you more than a page of adjectives ever could, and a provider who deflects has answered the question anyway.

sections.heading: The week a weekly slot has to survive
paragraphs: A tutor who is ideal on paper and available at an impossible hour is not available. The school week in the Kingdom runs Sunday to Thursday, with Friday and Saturday as the weekend, and most tutoring copy aimed at this market is recycled from elsewhere and quietly assumes otherwise. That is how families end up offered a Saturday afternoon that collides with the only free family day, or a Thursday evening that is the eve of the weekend and the first thing to be skipped once term gets heavy.

Arabia Standard Time is UTC+3 and the Kingdom does not change its clocks. Most countries tutors live in do, twice a year, so a slot agreed as the tutor's local time will quietly move by an hour and land on dinner or on homework. Agree it in Saudi local time and let the tutor's own clock move around it. Ask a prospective tutor what time the lesson is in their time zone, too, because a tutor teaching at eleven at night their time will be a different tutor by the middle of a term.

The third constraint is the student, not the diary. Most families settle somewhere between five and eight in the evening on Sunday to Wednesday. Earlier collides with the end of the school day and the commute, which in Riyadh and Jeddah is substantial. Later costs more in concentration than it buys in content. Two shorter sessions in a week generally outperform one long one, because the work set in between is where consolidation happens. Long sessions, full papers and coursework feedback belong on a Friday or Saturday morning.

sections.heading: Why the local school cannot usually be the answer
paragraphs: Families rarely look outside the school first. They look outside it after something has not worked, and it is worth understanding why, because it changes what you should ask a tutor to do. Private and international schools in the Kingdom are licensed by the Ministry of Education, and school evaluation runs through the Education and Training Evaluation Commission, which operates e-services for national school accreditation and for the approval of international accreditation bodies. That governs the institution, not who stands in front of the higher-tier set.

The binding constraint is cohort size. A subject needs enough candidates to justify a specialist and a timetable slot, so in smaller schools one teacher covers a department and the hardest courses get the least specialist attention. There is also a quieter version: the subject that exists on the option block but is taught in a combined set, where higher-tier candidates sit in a room mostly working at the lower tier and receive extension sheets instead of teaching. Both are visible if you ask, and neither is a criticism of a school doing its best with the numbers it has.

What this means practically is that your tutor's job is defined partly by the school's gap. If the school teaches the content well and cannot spare time for technique, buy technique. If the subject is covered by a willing non-specialist, buy the subject properly. If the set is combined and your child is on the higher tier, buy the higher-tier material explicitly and say so when asking for a tutor. Families who describe the school situation accurately get matched better than families who describe only a grade.
bullets: Ask which subjects are taught by a specialist in that specific subject
Ask whether higher-tier and lower-tier candidates are taught in the same room
Ask how many candidates are in the set your child sits in
Tell a prospective tutor what the school does well, not only what is wrong

sections.heading: After a move: the tutor you need is not the one you had
paragraphs: A family that has just relocated into the Kingdom, or between schools inside it, has a specific and different problem. The student is not simply behind. They are carrying a background that overlaps the new syllabus awkwardly: ahead in places, missing specific topics, and above all trained on a different style of question. A tutor who treats this as a general weakness will teach content the student already has, and the student will continue writing answers the mark scheme cannot pay for.

The right tutor for a mid-course arrival does two things in the first fortnight. They audit, topic by topic, against the new school's scheme of work rather than against the syllabus in the abstract, and they look specifically at assessment style: command words, answer length, what counts as evidence, whether practical write-ups have ever been required. The output is a list in three parts, which is never taught, taught differently, and taught but not secure. The middle group is the one families do not anticipate and the one that explains most of the confusion.

Board changes deserve naming separately. Moving from an Edexcel school to a Cambridge school, or in the other direction, changes the components even where the content is similar, and a Cambridge science candidate suddenly needs practical-paper technique nobody has mentioned. Ask a prospective tutor directly whether they have taught both boards and what the differences are. If they treat the two as the same examination, they will not see the gap your child has just acquired.
bullets: Audit against the new school's scheme of work, not the syllabus in general
Check assessment style before content; it is usually the larger gap
A board change moves the components even when the content matches
Expect specific missing topics, not a general weakness

sections.heading: What this costs, and what the price is actually signalling
paragraphs: Rates in this market run from advertised figures of about SAR 35 an hour on budget platforms to around SAR 180 to 220 for specialist and examiner-experienced tracks, with general private tuition for senior-school examination subjects advertised at 200 and above by tutor-marketplace guides, and some international providers quoting around USD 60 an hour. Those are other people's advertised rates, published on their own pages, and not a market average or a price list of ours. What is useful about them is the shape rather than the numbers.

Price in this market signals scarcity more than quality. A rate rises because fewer people can do the job: higher tier, scarcer subject, marking experience, a component with a practical element. It also rises for reasons that buy nothing, chiefly travel time in an in-home arrangement, which is paid for and taught during by nobody. So a high rate is weak evidence of a good tutor and reasonable evidence of a scarce one, and a low rate is good evidence that many people could have taken the booking.

The practical test is to match the rate to the job. Supervision and company while working: the low end is appropriate and the saving is real. Content teaching on topics the class rushed: a competent subject teacher in the middle of the range. Technique, mark-scheme judgement, a practical or coursework component, or anything in the final terms: pay for the specialism, because the entire value is in knowing what the examiner does with the answer. Families who get this wrong usually get it wrong in both directions at once, buying expensive supervision and cheap technique.

sections.heading: Starting, and how to leave if it is not working
paragraphs: The sequence is short and the first step is free. Tell us the board, the syllabus code, the tier and the components your child is entered for, plus where the student is in the course. We arrange a trial lesson with a specialist in that exact syllabus, and you should use it as an interview: ask the component questions from this page, ask for a past-paper question to be worked and marked with reasons, and watch whether the answers are specific. You keep the written summary either way, including if you decide to go elsewhere.

Two things worth saying plainly. The scarcer the specialism, the harder the slot is to fill, so a request for higher-tier physics with marking experience at six in the evening may take longer than a request for lower-tier mathematics. When nobody suitable is free at the hour you want, the honest answer is to say so and offer the nearest workable alternative, rather than putting a generalist in the room and letting you find out in week five.

Leaving should be as easy as starting. If the match is wrong after two or three sessions, say so; the diagnosis and notes carry across to a new tutor so a change costs one session of overlap rather than a month. If a term of work has not moved anything, that is worth a straight conversation about whether the subject, the format or the timing is the problem, and sometimes the right answer is to stop. A provider whose review never arrives at stopping is reviewing its own revenue rather than your child's progress.

process.title: Describe the situation, not just the subject
process.description: The board, the code, the tier and the components, plus what the school does well and what it does not cover. A family who says the school teaches the content and never practises long answers gets matched better than one who says their child is struggling in chemistry. A recent marked paper is the single most useful attachment.

process.title: Use the trial lesson as an interview
process.description: Ask the component questions on this page. Ask which paper the tutor last marked and when. Ask for a past-paper question worked and marked with reasons written down. The lesson is free, and what you are assessing is whether this person thinks in mark schemes or in topics.

process.title: Confirm the match on the code, not the subject name
process.description: Cambridge 0620 and Edexcel 4CH1 are different examinations, and Cambridge O Level is not IGCSE. Before anything recurring starts, have it confirmed in writing that the tutor has taught the specification your child is entered for, including the practical or coursework component.

process.title: Fix the slot in Saudi local time
process.description: Agree the hour in Arabia Standard Time so a clock change in the tutor's country moves their evening and not your child's. Ask what time the lesson falls in the tutor's own time zone, because a slot that is late at night for them will not survive a full term.

process.title: Check the first month against something concrete
process.description: Not a feeling, but marked work: are the method and presentation marks coming back, is answer length tracking the mark allocation, is the work set being done? Those move within a few sessions. A whole grade takes longer and depends on where the course is.

process.title: Review honestly, including the option of stopping
process.description: At the end of a block or a term: what moved, what did not, and whether to continue, change tutor, change subject or stop altogether. Sometimes fewer hours in a different subject is the better purchase, and a provider who says so is worth more than one who never does.

whyPoints.title: Every claim here is one you can test
whyPoints.description: There are no rankings, pass rates or star averages on this page, because none of them could be verified by the person reading it. What is offered instead is a named tutor, a stated syllabus and component, a free trial lesson, and a past paper marked with reasons. Those four are checkable before any money changes hands.

whyPoints.title: Matched on the component, not the subject
whyPoints.description: A chemistry tutor is not automatically a tutor for your child's chemistry paper. Matching runs on the board, the code, the tier and the components, which also happens to be the easiest thing for a parent to verify: ask which papers the candidate sits and listen for whether the answer arrives immediately.

whyPoints.title: A named tutor, kept
whyPoints.description: Continuity carries information that cannot be written down. A tutor four weeks into a student's working knows which mistakes are habits and which were accidents. Platforms that send whoever is free cannot build that, which is why the same named person each week matters more than any credential on a profile.

whyPoints.title: Changing tutor is routine, not a complaint
whyPoints.description: Fit is a real variable and it is not predictable from a biography. If the match is wrong after two or three sessions, the notes and diagnosis hand over and a new tutor starts from what is already known. Knowing that in advance is part of what makes a trial lesson a real decision rather than a formality.

whyPoints.title: Clear limits on assessed work
whyPoints.description: Where a subject carries coursework, a tutor teaches the skills, questions the plan and gives feedback on the student's own draft. No part of it is written, redrafted or edited for the student, and the school's own supervision process stays in charge. That boundary exists to protect the candidate, so it is stated rather than implied.

whyPoints.title: The slot is built for a Saudi week
whyPoints.description: Sunday to Thursday is the school week, Arabia Standard Time does not shift, and most tutors live somewhere that changes its clocks twice a year. Agreeing the hour in Saudi local time is a small administrative decision that quietly decides whether the arrangement still exists in the final term.

faqs.question: Does a tutor need to have taught the curriculum my child is leaving, or only the one they are joining?
faqs.answer: Only the one they are joining, with one caveat. The teaching job is to get the student to the new examination, so knowledge of the new board, tier and components is what matters. The caveat is diagnosis: a tutor who recognises what a CBSE, American or national-curriculum background typically produces will find the real gaps faster, because they know to check for data-response technique rather than for content. Ask whether they have taught students who arrived from that system before. A no is not disqualifying, but it means the first fortnight should be a careful audit rather than general teaching.

faqs.question: We are moving from an Edexcel school to a Cambridge school mid-course, so does the tutor need to change too?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily, but they need to acknowledge the change and name what it alters. The content overlaps heavily; the components do not. Your child will now sit a tiered entry where there was none, and in the sciences a practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper that Edexcel examines inside its written papers instead. A tutor who has taught both boards can work through that in a session. A tutor who treats the two as the same examination will teach good content against the wrong architecture, which is the most expensive kind of competent teaching.

faqs.question: My child is finishing the Middle Years Programme and moving into IGCSE, so what should the tutor already know?
faqs.answer: That the two assess different things. The Middle Years Programme marks against four criteria per subject with no external written papers in most schools, so a student can be genuinely strong and completely unpractised at timed recall under pressure. A tutor who understands this starts with timed papers early, not because the student lacks knowledge but because the skill has never been trained. Ask them to explain criterion-referenced marking in plain words. A tutor who immediately converts everything into percentages has not taught the programme and is guessing at the gap.

faqs.question: Is it better to finish IGCSE with the old board remotely or restart with the new school's board?
faqs.answer: It depends on how far through the course the student is and whether the old school will still enter them. Late in Year 11, finishing the specification already studied is usually less damaging, provided an entry route exists, because the alternative is re-learning a syllabus with months to go. Earlier in the course, aligning with the new school is almost always right: the student sits in the lessons, meets the deadlines and is entered with the cohort. Ask both schools what they can actually administer before deciding, because entry logistics, not teaching, usually settles it.

faqs.question: What happens to coursework already completed at a previous school?
faqs.answer: That is a question for the new school's examinations officer rather than for a tutor, and the answer varies by board, by subject and by how far the work had progressed. Sometimes it can be carried and submitted; sometimes the new school has taken a different route for that subject and the work has nowhere to go. Ask early, because the answer changes what the first term has to achieve. If the work cannot carry, a tutor's job becomes rebuilding it to the new criteria with the student doing all the writing, which needs time the family may not have budgeted.

faqs.question: How do we decide between a British-curriculum school and an IB school when relocating to the Kingdom at fourteen?
faqs.answer: At fourteen the practical questions beat the philosophical ones. Which school can actually timetable the subjects your child needs after sixteen, how large the sets are, who teaches the higher tier, and what the student has already covered. A student two years into a British curriculum usually loses least by continuing it. A student arriving from a system closer to the Middle Years Programme may settle faster in an IB school. Both routes lead to good universities; the deciding factors are subject availability and continuity, and those are school-specific rather than curriculum-specific.

faqs.question: Why is a specialist in IGCSE Physics hard to find locally even in the big Saudi cities?
faqs.answer: Because the pool is small at every stage. A school needs enough higher-tier candidates to justify a physics specialist, and the people qualified to teach that tier are in demand everywhere in the world, not only here. Those who do come are usually employed full-time by a school, which limits how many evening students they can take and when. Add the requirement for practical-paper experience and the number shrinks again. That scarcity is the reason the rate is higher and the reason a geographic search produces a generalist while a syllabus-based search produces a specialist.

faqs.question: What does it mean when a school says a subject is offered online through a partner provider?
faqs.answer: It usually means the school cannot staff the subject and has bought it in, which is a sensible solution and worth understanding in detail. Ask who teaches it, whether the sessions are live or recorded, how many students are in the group, who marks the work and who the student asks when they are stuck between sessions. A live small group with a specialist is a real course. A recorded library with a tutor on call is self-study with support, which suits a motivated student and not an uncertain one.

faqs.question: How does class size at a Saudi international school change what a tutor needs to do?
faqs.answer: In a large set the teaching is good and the individual attention is thin, so the tutor's job is usually diagnosis and technique: finding the specific pattern of lost marks nobody has time to notice. In a very small set, the attention is high but the set may be combined across tiers, so the tutor's job becomes delivering higher-tier material the room is not covering. Both are legitimate and they need different briefs. Tell a prospective tutor the set size and whether tiers are taught together; it changes the plan immediately.

faqs.question: Why do families in the Dammam, Al Khobar and Dhahran cluster commute to a school in another city?
faqs.answer: Because the three function as a single labour and school market. Housing, employment and schooling are decided separately, so a family may live in one city, work in a second and send children to a third, and the school chosen is the one with the right programme rather than the nearest one. The practical consequence for tutoring is unpredictable arrival times after school, which makes a slot with a little slack in it far more durable than an exact one, and makes earlier evening starts harder than families expect.

faqs.question: What options exist for a family in a Saudi town with no international school at all?
faqs.answer: Three in practice. Enrol locally and supplement the subjects that matter with outside teaching, which is what most families in the smaller towns do. Board or relocate one parent to a city with a suitable school, which is expensive and disruptive but sometimes right for a final two years. Or follow a distance programme with a registered examination centre, which demands an organised student and real parental involvement. Whichever route, the examination entry has to be arranged through a centre, so confirm that logistics exist before committing to a syllabus.

faqs.question: What does a school's own evaluation report tell a parent about the teaching?
faqs.answer: Less than families hope, and still something. Evaluation reports describe the institution: governance, safeguarding, facilities, curriculum breadth, and overall judgements about teaching quality across the school. They do not tell you who teaches the higher-tier chemistry set this year, how large it is, or whether the mock marking is moderated by anyone. Staff turnover means a report can describe a department that has since changed entirely. Read it for the institutional picture and then ask the subject-level questions directly, because those are the ones with a grade attached.

faqs.question: Which evenings of the Sunday-to-Thursday week actually work for a weekly lesson?
faqs.answer: Sunday through Wednesday, with most families settling between five and eight in the evening. Thursday looks free and is the first slot abandoned once term gets heavy, because it is the eve of the weekend. Earlier than five collides with the end of the school day and the commute, which in Riyadh and Jeddah is substantial. Later than eight costs more in concentration than it gains in time. If two subjects are needed, put them on different evenings rather than back to back, and keep Friday or Saturday mornings for long sessions.

faqs.question: How much notice is needed to move a regular weekly slot?
faqs.answer: For a permanent change, a week or two is reasonable, because the tutor's other students occupy the surrounding hours and a swap often has to be arranged between several families. For a single session, a day or two is usually workable and the same day rarely is. The practical advice is to look ahead at the term calendar once, early, and move the slot deliberately around known fixtures and examination weeks rather than cancelling repeatedly. Repeated last-minute changes are the most reliable way to lose a good tutor's best hour.

faqs.question: Can a student take two IGCSE subjects in the same evening?
faqs.answer: It can be done and it usually should not be. Two consecutive hours of one-to-one teaching after a full school day produces a second hour that is substantially less useful than the first, and the work set in both subjects then lands on the same days. Spreading them across the week gives the student time to attempt and absorb what each tutor set. The exception is the intensive period before a series, when sessions get longer and less frequent anyway and the schedule is built around full papers rather than weekly teaching.

faqs.question: What happens to a weekly slot during the midyear break?
faqs.answer: Most families either pause and keep the slot reserved, or reduce to one session a week to hold the habit without filling a holiday with schoolwork. Both are normal. What is worth avoiding is an unplanned gap: a break of several weeks with no contact means the first session back is spent re-establishing where the student was. If the student is heading into a heavy term or towards a series, the break is also the best available window for the untaught topics nobody has time for in term.

faqs.question: Does a tutor outside the Gulf understand why a slot has to move during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: A tutor who has taught students in this region will raise it before you do. School days shorten, the family rhythm shifts and an afternoon slot that worked all term stops working, so lessons typically move later in the evening or into the earlier part of the day, sometimes at a reduced frequency. Because the month moves earlier against the Gregorian calendar each year, it falls at a different point in the academic year each time. Ask a prospective tutor how they have handled it before; the answer tells you whether they have actually taught here.

faqs.question: How does a tutor's own holiday calendar collide with a Saudi school year?
faqs.answer: More often than families expect. A tutor based in the United Kingdom or Europe takes holidays in August and over the Christmas period; a tutor in India works around a different set of festivals; and none of those align neatly with a Saudi international school's three terms or with a Ministry of Education two-semester year. The fix is a single conversation at the start: ask which weeks they will not be available across the year and whether cover is offered. Discovering it in the term before a series is considerably worse than knowing in advance.

best-igcse-tutor.closingHeading: A short checklist before you choose anyone
best-igcse-tutor.closingBody: Get the board, the syllabus code, the tier and the component list from your school. Decide what the hour is actually for: supervision, content, or technique. Then put four questions to any provider, including this one. Which papers does my child sit? Which of them have you taught, and for how many cohorts? Which board and paper did you last mark, and when? And what happens if the match is wrong after two sessions? Specific answers to those four tell you more than any ranking claim, because nobody independently ranks tutors in this market. Lessons here are one-to-one over live video on Arabia Standard Time, around the Sunday-to-Thursday week, and no tutor travels to a Saudi address.

For Al-Qassim families that detail matters more than usual: a tutor may be carrying a whole course rather than supporting a class, so the match has to be exact before a trial lesson rather than after one.

intro.heading: The qualification first, then everything that follows from it
paragraphs: This page is built in the order the qualification itself imposes. Not the city, not the tutor, not the price: the assessment structure, because that is what the next two years are measured against and almost everything a family has to decide follows from it. A Cambridge IGCSE grade is produced by a small number of written papers and, in the sciences, a practical component, with a ceiling set by the tier the candidate was entered for. A Diploma grade is produced by papers plus an internally assessed piece marked at school and moderated by the board. Those are different machines, and feeding the wrong input into either wastes a year.

Why that ordering matters more in Buraidah than in Riyadh or Jeddah is a matter of local supply. Al-Qassim is an agricultural province in the centre of the Kingdom, and its private-school sector is almost entirely national curriculum. That is a description of what is available rather than a judgement about quality; the national curriculum serves the overwhelming majority of students here perfectly well. But it means a student working towards IGCSE or the Diploma in this province is usually studying a syllabus their own school does not teach, and the ordinary scaffolding of a subject teacher, a department, a mock paper and an internal deadline is not automatically there.

The practical consequence is that someone has to hold the syllabus. In a Dhahran or Riyadh international school that is the head of department. In Buraidah it is often the family, assisted by whoever they appoint. A tutor in that position is not topping up a taught course; they are teaching it, sequencing it, setting the mock papers and watching the entry window. The work is bigger, which is worth knowing before comparing hourly rates with a family whose school does the heavy lifting for them.

Everything is delivered live online, one-to-one, over video. No tutor is sent to a Saudi address; in-home teaching is a service we offer only in India. In a province where the nearest Diploma cohort may be several hours away by road, that is not a second-best arrangement. It is the only arrangement under which a student in Al Mithnab or Ar Rass can work weekly with somebody who has actually taught Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, and it costs nothing in travel at either end.

From there the page works forward to the thing Al-Qassim families ask about most and almost no tutoring site covers: the route from an international certificate into a university place, in the Kingdom or abroad. Ministry of Education equivalency, Qudurat and Tahsili each have a mechanism, a timing and an owner. Knowing them in the first of the final two school years changes subject choices; discovering them in the last term does not.
bullets: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel candidates in the Kingdom enter the June series or the November series
The tier a candidate is entered for sets the highest grade available, whatever the revision
Each Diploma subject carries an internally assessed component marked at school and moderated by the board

Tahsili follows the Saudi national curriculum, so its framing is unfamiliar even when its content is not
