sections.heading: The Sunday-to-Thursday week and the clock a tutor works to
paragraphs: The school week in the Kingdom runs Sunday to Thursday, with Friday and Saturday as the weekend. Most tutoring copy on the internet was written for a Monday-to-Friday country and quietly assumes it, which is why families end up offered a Saturday slot that collides with the only free day of the week and a Sunday slot the tutor treats as part of their own weekend. A workable arrangement starts from the Saudi week and finds a tutor whose working week overlaps it, not the other way round.

The second fact is the clock. Arabia Standard Time is UTC+3 and the Kingdom does not change it, in either direction, at any point in the year. A tutor in a country that does observe daylight saving will drift by an hour against your slot twice a year unless the agreement is written in Saudi local time rather than theirs. That single sentence in the arrangement prevents the most common scheduling failure in cross-border online tuition, which is a family discovering in the autumn that their fixed Sunday slot is now an hour into dinner.

For a Stage 9 student the practical window is narrow. School finishes in the early afternoon, the commute in Riyadh or along the Jeddah spine can take most of an hour, and homework still has to happen. One hour between five and eight on two school evenings is the shape that survives a term; three evenings is usually the point at which something else gives way. During Ramadan school days shorten and household routines move later, so slots shift rather than stop, and the sensible plan is agreed before the month begins rather than during it.

sections.heading: Checkpoint now, Ministry of Education equivalency later
paragraphs: A Checkpoint report has no standing in a university application and never will. It is worth saying plainly, because the search that brings families here often carries an unspoken worry that a low scale score at fourteen has already closed something. It has not. What the report does is feed the IGCSE sets and tiers a student is placed in, and those do eventually matter, because they shape which Diploma or A Level subjects are available two years later and those are the ones universities read.

The step families in the Kingdom most often have not heard of sits at the end. A foreign or international school certificate needs an equivalency decision from the Ministry of Education, known as mu'adalah, before a Saudi university treats it as equivalent to the Saudi secondary certificate. This applies to the IB Diploma, to A Levels and to an American high school diploma alike. It is an administrative process with its own evidence requirements, and it is worth a parent reading the Ministry's own published requirements in the year before the application rather than discovering them during it.

Alongside it sit the Qiyas tests. Qudurat, the General Aptitude Test, is run by the Education and Training Evaluation Commission through its National Center for Assessment and tests verbal and quantitative reasoning rather than syllabus content, in Arabic or in English. Tahsili, the Achievement Test, covers science-stream subjects and follows the Saudi national curriculum. That last point is the one that catches international-curriculum students: the material overlaps with what an IGCSE and Diploma student has studied, but the framing does not, so a strong IB candidate can meet an unfamiliar paper. Weightings differ by university and by programme, and the only reliable source for them is the university's own published admission criteria.

sections.heading: What a Checkpoint tutor should and should not touch
paragraphs: Checkpoint carries no coursework, which removes most of the academic honesty questions that surround an Internal Assessment or an Extended Essay later on. What it does not remove is the habit. A Stage 9 student who gets used to a tutor producing the answer is being set up to fail at IGCSE, where coursework and controlled assessment exist, and at Diploma level, where a school can refer suspected malpractice and the consequences reach the certificate itself.

The line is simple to state and worth stating. A tutor teaches, questions, models a method, marks the student's own work and explains what a mark scheme is paying for. A tutor must never write the coursework, complete an assignment or draft a paragraph the student then submits as their own, and no honest tutor will offer to. Where a school sets a piece of assessed work, the tutor's job is to teach the skill it tests before it is written and to discuss the feedback after it is returned, not to sit alongside the student while it is produced.

This has a practical edge for Checkpoint families. Past papers and published mark schemes are the right material for a tutor to work through, and they are the material that makes the technique visible. A school's own internal assessments are not: they are the school's evidence about the student, and a tutor who has worked through one in advance has destroyed its value as evidence for exactly the set and tier decision the family is trying to influence. Ask a prospective tutor what they use. The answer tells you what you are buying.

process.title: Send the report, or say there isn't one
process.description: Share the Checkpoint feedback report if it has arrived, or the school's internal data and the last set of marked work if it has not. Either is enough to start from. What we want is evidence, not a description of the problem, because a parent's account of a weak subject and the strand data behind it usually point in different directions.

process.title: A free trial lesson spent on diagnosis
process.description: The first lesson is free and is not a sales call. A specialist reads the strand data, tests the suspected gap directly with questions pitched at the level above and below it, and separates missing content from technique and from timing. Parents are welcome to sit in, and most find the second half more useful than the first.

process.title: A written plan naming two or three strands
process.description: You get the plan in writing before the second paid lesson: which strands will be taught, in what order, why that order, and what will be used to check each one. If the honest answer is that the school's own intervention group covers it, the plan says so and nothing further is sold.

process.title: A fixed slot on Arabia Standard Time
process.description: Lessons are booked at a stated Saudi local time, held in Saudi local time, and unaffected by any clock change in the tutor's own country. One hour a week on a school evening is the usual shape at Checkpoint level; two evenings is for a student carrying weaknesses in two subjects before IGCSE placement.

process.title: Reassess against a Checkpoint-style paper
process.description: Every six to eight weeks the flagged strand is retested under timed conditions, and the result decides what happens next. A strand that holds comes off the list. A strand that does not gets a different approach or a different tutor. A list that is empty ends the arrangement, and that is a successful outcome rather than a lost customer.

process.title: Hand over at the IGCSE transition
process.description: When a student moves into Stage 10 the brief changes, and so should the teaching. Some students keep the same tutor; others need one who has marked for the board and knows where the IGCSE mark scheme differs from a Stage 9 one. We say which, before the course starts rather than after the first mock.

whyPoints.title: The report sets the plan, not the sales call
whyPoints.description: Every match starts from the Checkpoint strand data or the school's own marked work. That is why the plan arrives in writing and names specific strands rather than a subject, and why it sometimes says the school's free intervention group is enough and no tutoring is needed.

whyPoints.title: Specialists at the right level, not above it
whyPoints.description: A Diploma physics examiner can teach Stage 9 science, and will usually be priced as a Diploma physics examiner. We match on the stage and the strand, which is why Checkpoint work is not quoted at senior-subject rates and why nobody is paying for scarcity that this teaching does not require.

whyPoints.title: No travel loading inside the rate
whyPoints.description: In-home tuition in the Kingdom prices the tutor's drive into the hour and restricts the pool to whoever lives nearby. Lessons here are delivered one-to-one over live video, so a family in Jubail or Khamis Mushait picks from the same specialists as a family in north Riyadh.

whyPoints.title: Rates explained before anything is agreed
whyPoints.description: Advertised Saudi rates run from around SAR 35 to SAR 220 an hour depending on tier and scarcity, and we will tell you where a quote sits in that range and why. What is inside the hour, including marking between lessons, is stated before you commit rather than discovered afterwards.

whyPoints.title: Honest about assessed work
whyPoints.description: A tutor here teaches, questions, models and marks the student's own work. Nobody will produce a piece of coursework, and anybody who offers to at any stage of the pathway is selling the student a problem that surfaces at IGCSE and gets worse at Diploma level.

whyPoints.title: Built for the Saudi week
whyPoints.description: Slots are agreed against the Sunday-to-Thursday school week and pinned to Arabia Standard Time, so a tutor's own daylight saving change does not move your lesson. Ramadan timing is planned before the month starts, not negotiated in its first week.

faqs.question: Does a Cambridge Checkpoint result ever appear in a Saudi university application?
faqs.answer: No. Checkpoint is diagnostic, not a qualification, and nothing from it reaches a university file. What it influences is the IGCSE set and tier a student is placed in, and those shape which Diploma or A Level subjects are open two years later. Those final qualifications are what a university reads, after a Ministry of Education equivalency decision recognises them against the Saudi secondary certificate. So a weak scale score at Stage 9 closes nothing by itself, but ignoring what it says about algebra or scientific method can narrow the subject choices that do matter.

faqs.question: If my child sits Checkpoint now, what still has to happen before a Saudi university accepts the certificate?
faqs.answer: Several steps, none of them involving Checkpoint. The student sits IGCSE or International GCSE, then a final qualification such as the IB Diploma or A Levels. That certificate then needs an equivalency decision, mu'adalah, from the Ministry of Education before a Saudi university treats it as equivalent to the Saudi secondary certificate. Alongside it most applicants sit Qudurat, and science-stream applicants sit Tahsili, both run by the Education and Training Evaluation Commission through Qiyas. Requirements and weightings differ by university and programme, so check the university's own published admission criteria rather than a third-party summary.

faqs.question: Does a weak Checkpoint science score say anything about how Tahsili will go years later?
faqs.answer: Less than families assume, because the two tests are measuring different things. Checkpoint science reports performance against the Cambridge curriculum framework. Tahsili covers science-stream subjects following the Saudi national curriculum, so the content overlaps but the framing and the expected approach do not. A student can score well at Checkpoint and still find Tahsili unfamiliar. What does transfer is the underlying mathematics and the habit of reading a question precisely, which is one reason the algebra and scientific-method strands are worth fixing at Stage 9 rather than later.

faqs.question: Which part of Checkpoint mathematics matters most for the Qudurat quantitative section later on?
faqs.answer: Number and the non-calculator skills inside it. Qudurat tests verbal and quantitative reasoning rather than syllabus content, and the quantitative half rewards fluency with fractions, ratio, percentages and estimation done quickly in the head or on paper. A Stage 9 student who leans on a calculator for arithmetic will meet that gap years later under time pressure. Geometry and statistics matter less for this purpose. None of this means starting Qudurat preparation at fourteen; it means that of two equally weak strands, number is the one with the longer tail.

faqs.question: Do overseas universities ask to see a Cambridge Lower Secondary Checkpoint statement of achievement?
faqs.answer: No. Overseas applications are built on IGCSE or International GCSE grades, the final qualification such as the IB Diploma or A Levels, predicted grades, a reference and in some systems a standardised test. A Checkpoint statement of achievement has no place in that file. It is worth keeping anyway, because schools often ask for it when a student transfers mid-pathway and it is the fastest way for a new school to place a student sensibly in sets without waiting a term to form its own view.

faqs.question: When should support start for a student entering Cambridge Lower Secondary at Stage 7?
faqs.answer: For most students, it should not. Stage 7 is a settling year and the sensible default is to let the school teach and watch what the first full set of reports says. The exception is a student arriving from a different system, where the gap is structural rather than a weakness: a transfer from a national-curriculum or American-curriculum school often has content coverage in a different order and has never met Cambridge command vocabulary. A short block in the first term, aimed at the framework rather than at topics, saves a much longer repair at Stage 9.

faqs.question: Is Stage 9 too late to fix a mathematics gap before Checkpoint?
faqs.answer: No, and Stage 9 is when most families start. The constraint is scope rather than time. Eight to twelve weeks of weekly one-to-one is enough to repair one named strand properly and to make visible progress on a second. It is not enough to rebuild number, algebra, geometry and statistics at once, and a tutor who promises that is describing coverage rather than learning. Pick the strand that blocks the most later work, which is almost always algebra or number, and accept that the others move partly as a consequence.

faqs.question: What should a Cambridge Primary Stage 6 student have secured before Checkpoint?
faqs.answer: Three things, and none of them is advanced content. Arithmetic fluency without a calculator, including fractions and the times tables that sit underneath them. Reading stamina, meaning the ability to hold a longer text in mind while answering questions about it. And the habit of answering the question asked rather than the question the student expected, which at this age is the single largest source of lost marks. A Stage 6 student with those three in place rarely needs tutoring; one missing the first usually does.

faqs.question: How does Checkpoint preparation differ from IGCSE preparation in the same subject?
faqs.answer: The purpose differs, so the teaching should. Checkpoint is diagnostic and the marks are not banked towards a certificate, so the work is content and foundation: filling gaps, building fluency, teaching the student to show reasoning. IGCSE is terminal and tiered, so technique against a published mark scheme becomes half the job, and command terms, timing and the structure of an extended answer start to carry real marks. A tutor who teaches Stage 9 like an IGCSE course wastes time on examination craft the student cannot yet use.

faqs.question: My child is moving into Stage 9 part-way through the year. What does catching up to Checkpoint involve?
faqs.answer: An audit against the Cambridge curriculum framework rather than against the new school's scheme of work. A mid-stage arrival usually has an uneven map: some Stage 8 content covered in depth, some never met, and some met under different terminology. The first job is to find the holes, which takes a lesson or two of targeted questioning rather than a term of observation. The second is to teach Cambridge command vocabulary, because a student who knows the science and does not know what explain is asking for will underperform on every paper.

faqs.question: What does a Cambridge Checkpoint tutor charge per hour in the Kingdom?
faqs.answer: Advertised rates published by Saudi platforms and tutor marketplaces run from around SAR 35 an hour at the budget online end to SAR 200 and above for senior examination subjects in Riyadh, with primary private tuition in the capital advertised around SAR 50. Checkpoint teaching sits in the lower half of that spread because the supply of competent lower-secondary teachers is wide. Those are figures providers publish about themselves rather than a market average, and none of them is IB Gram's price; we quote per match and tell you what is inside the hour.

faqs.question: Why does a Checkpoint science tutor cost less than an IGCSE Physics specialist?
faqs.answer: Scarcity, almost entirely. Checkpoint science is broad and foundational, and a large number of qualified teachers can teach it well. IGCSE and Diploma physics is narrower, more mathematical, and the pool of people who have taught and marked it is much smaller. Level also matters: an examiner's feel for a mark scheme is worth paying for where marks are being banked towards a certificate and worth less where the test is diagnostic. Paying a Diploma rate for Stage 9 science buys scarcity the teaching does not need.

faqs.question: Is a Checkpoint group revision class ever better value than one-to-one?
faqs.answer: Yes, in one specific case: the student is missing content across a whole topic, is otherwise functioning, and will ask a question in front of other people. Content delivery scales reasonably well, so a group is a sensible purchase there. It fails for technique, for timing, and for a student who has gone quiet, because all three need somebody watching one student work and intervening at the moment the error happens. Start with the school's own Stage 9 intervention group, which is usually free and run by the teacher who writes the set recommendation.

faqs.question: What happens in the free trial lesson for a Checkpoint subject?
faqs.answer: A specialist reads the strand report with you, then tests the suspected weakness directly rather than taking it on trust. That usually means questions pitched one level above and one below the flagged strand, which separates missing content from shaky technique from simple slowness under time pressure. The lesson ends with a verbal diagnosis and a short written note. It is not a sales call, and if the conclusion is that the school's own group covers the gap, the note says so and nothing is sold.

faqs.question: How many weeks of Checkpoint support does a Stage 9 student actually need?
faqs.answer: For one named strand, eight to twelve weekly hours is the honest range, with the strand retested under timed conditions at the end. Two strands take longer than twice as long if they are unrelated and less than twice as long if one sits underneath the other, which is why algebra is taught before statistics rather than alongside it. Open-ended weekly tutoring with no retest date is the arrangement to avoid: without a checkpoint of its own, nobody can tell whether the hours are working or simply continuing.

faqs.question: Can a Checkpoint feedback report be used to argue for Extended rather than Core at IGCSE?
faqs.answer: It is the best evidence a parent has, though the decision remains the school's. Bring the strand breakdown rather than the headline score, because a case built on one number is easy to dismiss and a case built on strong algebra and number strands against one weak statistics strand is not. Ask what else the school is weighing, ask when the entry deadline falls, and ask in writing. Tier entry is reversible only before that deadline, after which the Core ceiling of a grade C is fixed whatever happens in the papers.

cambridge-checkpoint-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the report, not with a package
cambridge-checkpoint-tutor.closingBody: If a Checkpoint feedback report has arrived and nobody has explained it, send it over and have a specialist read it with you in a free trial lesson. You will leave that lesson knowing which two strands are worth paying for, roughly what the market charges for teaching at that level, and whether the school's own intervention group already covers it. Lessons for families in the Kingdom run one-to-one over live video, on a fixed slot in Arabia Standard Time, inside the Sunday-to-Thursday week. If the honest answer is that no tutoring is needed yet, we would rather say so now than sell a term of it.

intro.heading: What you are buying when you hire Cambridge IGCSE help in the Kingdom
paragraphs: A parent typing cambridge IGCSE home tutor into Google in Riyadh, Jeddah or Al Khobar is usually not shopping for a teaching philosophy. They are trying to price a single decision: pay someone to travel to the family's residence for a fixed hour each week, or buy that hour some other way. The honest answer is that the travelling version is the most expensive form of the same hour, and the extra money does not go into teaching. It goes into a car, a commute and a tutor pool that stops at the edge of one city.

That matters more in the Kingdom than it does in most markets, because the thing a Cambridge candidate usually needs is narrow. A child entered for Chemistry 0620 Extended does not need a science teacher. They need somebody who knows that the qualitative analysis questions reward a stated observation and a stated conclusion as separate marks, and who can look at a Paper 4 script and say which of the two is missing. In a city of a few international schools, the number of adults who can do that for 0620 and happen to live twenty minutes away is small. The in-home model asks you to choose from that small set and then pay a premium for the driving.

The cost picture is also wider than most pages admit. Published Saudi tutoring rates run from about SAR 35 an hour on budget online platforms to SAR 200 and above for senior-school examination subjects, with IB and premium tracks advertised higher again. Those are advertised rates from vendor listings and marketplace guides, not a market average, and nothing on this page is IB Gram's own price. What the range tells you is that the number on a quote is mostly reporting scarcity and travel, not quality, and that a family can read it if they know which lever is being pulled.

IB Gram sells the narrow thing. Lessons for families in Saudi Arabia are delivered one-to-one over live video, on a fixed slot in Arabia Standard Time, and no tutor travels to a Saudi address; home visits are a service offered only in India. That is stated plainly because it changes the economics in your favour. Removing the drive removes the only reason the tutor pool had to be local, so a family in Khamis Mushait can be matched to the same 0606 specialist as a family in north Riyadh, and nobody is paying for a car.

The rest of this page is built to be used in order. It sets out the four arrangements a Saudi family actually chooses between and what each costs, breaks an in-home visit down into paid teaching minutes, explains which Cambridge syllabuses carry a scarcity premium and why, shows four shapes the same budget can take across a term, and then deals with the parts nobody advertises: how to tell a high rate for skill from a high rate for rarity, what you get to see each week, and what no fee can buy.

cambridge-igcse-home-tutor.programmesIntro: Cambridge runs a continuous route from lower secondary to post-16, and the stage your child is at changes what tutoring is for. Below is what each stage assesses and what it means for a family in the Kingdom, where a school's stage coverage and its staffing rarely match exactly.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary
programmes.description: The three years before an IGCSE entry, assessed internally and often with Cambridge Checkpoint tests at the end. There is no public grade at stake, which is exactly why weak algebra and weak written English survive this stage unnoticed. The work that decides a 0580 Extended grade is mostly done here: directed number, fractions, rearranging formulae and writing a method a reader can follow.
programmes.countryNote: In the Kingdom this is the cheapest stage to buy help in and the one families most often skip. A child who arrives in Year 10 unable to handle algebraic fractions will spend paid Cambridge hours on Year 8 content at a senior-subject rate. One hour a fortnight at this stage costs far less than the catching up it prevents.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE, Core tier
programmes.description: On tiered subjects, Core sits the shorter paper set and is graded C to G. A Core candidate who answers everything correctly is still awarded no higher than a C. It is the right entry for a student who would otherwise be swamped, and the wrong one for a student whose problem is technique rather than content, because it closes a route rather than fixing it.
programmes.countryNote: Tier entry is a school decision in Saudi schools as everywhere else, taken by the department and reversible only before the entry deadline. Families are frequently told late. Ask your child's school in writing which tier each subject is entered at and when the deadline falls, because that single answer changes what an hour of tutoring should be spent on.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE, Extended tier
programmes.description: Extended sits the longer paper set and is graded A* to E. The content overlaps Core heavily, but the question style does not: Extended asks for multi-step reasoning, unfamiliar contexts and answers where the method carries most of the marks. Most of the price difference between tutors is really a difference in how well they teach that step, not in how well they know the subject.
programmes.countryNote: This is the tier most international schools in Riyadh, Jeddah and the Eastern Province enter their stronger sets for, and the tier most outside tutoring in the Kingdom is bought for. It is also where a specialist earns their rate, because the Extended papers are the ones that punish unstated working and misread command words.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS and A Level
programmes.description: The post-16 Cambridge route, taken in two halves, with subject choices that narrow sharply after IGCSE. Mathematics, the sciences and economics all assume specific IGCSE groundwork, and a gap that was survivable at Extended becomes structural here. Many families buy their first tutoring in the term after IGCSE results, when the step up is suddenly visible.
programmes.countryNote: Some schools in the Kingdom run this route and some switch to the IB Diploma after IGCSE, and a family relocating between cities can find their child moving between the two. Knowing which post-16 route a school runs before Year 11 subject choices are locked is worth more than any amount of last-term tutoring.

cambridge-igcse-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: Cambridge codes matter more than subject names. The notes below say what each syllabus actually assesses and where the marks tend to go missing, because that is what decides whether an hour of paid teaching is worth buying and what the tutor has to be able to do in it.

subjects.name: Mathematics 0580
subjects.description: Paper 2 or 4 carries the Extended weight, and both reward written method. Marks are lost less for wrong answers than for answers that arrive with no visible route. The non-calculator discipline, index laws and rearranging formulae are the recurring weaknesses behind a grade that sits a band below the student's classwork.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics 0606
subjects.description: Taken alongside 0580 Extended by students heading for a mathematical post-16 route. It introduces calculus, logarithms, binomial expansion and trigonometric identities, and it assumes 0580 algebra is automatic. Students who met it late describe the jump as a different subject rather than a harder one, which is usually a fair description.

subjects.name: International Mathematics 0607
subjects.description: A separate syllabus, not a variant of 0580, with a graphics calculator assumed throughout and an investigation paper on the Extended route. Treating it as 0580 with a calculator is the standard error. It is most often entered where a school runs the IB Diploma afterwards, because the method habits transfer.

subjects.name: Chemistry 0620
subjects.description: Mole reasoning, the qualitative analysis tables and equation writing carry a large share of the Extended marks. Candidates lose marks for omitting state symbols, conditions and units rather than for not knowing the chemistry, and for giving an observation where the question asked for a conclusion as well.

subjects.name: Physics 0625
subjects.description: The extended-response items reward a chain of reasoning with the physics named at each step. The alternative-to-practical route tests experimental thinking without a laboratory: reading a scale, spotting a systematic error, suggesting an improvement that is actually testable. Both are teachable and neither is in most revision guides.

subjects.name: Biology 0610
subjects.description: Definitions are marked strictly and partial definitions earn nothing. The highest-value technique is learning which word the mark scheme requires, then writing it, and separating a description of data from an explanation of it. Students who revise by rereading notes tend to plateau here.

subjects.name: Economics 0455
subjects.description: Diagrams are marked for labelling, axes and the shift being explained in words, not for being drawn neatly. Candidates who can draw a correct diagram still lose marks by leaving the reader to infer what moved and why. The data-response and extended-writing questions ask for different things in the same paper.

subjects.name: Business Studies 0450
subjects.description: Calculation items are small but reliable marks, and they are routinely dropped. The longer evaluation questions need a judgement supported by the case material, not a list of advantages and disadvantages. Context from the stimulus has to be used by name, which is the single most common gap.

subjects.name: Geography 0460
subjects.description: Map and photograph skills, data-handling and the fieldwork-style questions are where marks move. Case-study detail has to be specific, with places and figures from the student's own learning. Generic answers about flooding or urbanisation score at the bottom of the band however well written they are.

subjects.name: History 0470
subjects.description: The source paper and the essay paper reward opposite habits. Source questions ask for inference, provenance and cross-reference; essay questions ask for argument and weighting. Students taught only one of the two drop a grade on the other, and schools short of specialists usually drill the essay.

subjects.name: First Language English 0500
subjects.description: The directed-writing task is assessed on reading as well as writing: the response has to use the passage, adopt the right form and register, and select rather than summarise. Fluent writers who ignore the brief score in the middle band. The composition task rewards control, not length.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language 0510
subjects.levels: Single tier, with a speaking endorsement
subjects.description: A different qualification from 0500 with a different mark scheme, and a tutor has to know which one the student is entered for. Reading tasks reward precise retrieval and paraphrase; writing tasks reward hitting the task type exactly. The speaking component is prepared for separately.

cambridge-igcse-home-tutor.regionsTitle: Where Cambridge families are, and what local in-home supply looks like
cambridge-igcse-home-tutor.regionsIntro: The case for buying an hour online rather than at the door is strongest where the drive is long or the pool is thin. These notes describe what the in-home market looks like city by city, which is the honest basis for the comparison and the reason the price of travel differs so much across the Kingdom.

regions.name: Riyadh
regions.note: Roughly an hour across in traffic from north to south, so an in-home tutor is realistically serving one part of the city. A family in Al Narjis and a family in Al Olaya draw on different pools for the same syllabus, and an evening visit across that distance is paid for twice: once in the rate and once in the slot it blocks.

regions.name: Jeddah
regions.note: A long coastal spine from the historic centre north to Obhur. Supply concentrates around the schools in the north, so families at either end of the spine pay most for the travel element. Senior-subject in-home rates advertised for Jeddah sit in the same band marketplace guides publish for Riyadh.

regions.name: Dhahran, Al Khobar and Dammam
regions.note: One labour and school market: families routinely live in one city and attend school in another. That helps in-home supply more than anywhere else in the Kingdom, but it still concentrates on British and Cambridge-curriculum schools, so the scarce syllabuses stay scarce.

regions.name: Jubail
regions.note: An industrial city with a school population tied to the plants, and a commute that makes an in-home visit from the Dammam cluster expensive in time. Cambridge subject coverage exists; a specialist in a single code often does not, which is where an outside match earns its place.

regions.name: Al Ahsa and Qatif
regions.note: Al Ahsa sits about an hour and a half inland from the Eastern Province cluster, and Qatif sits inside it. For Al Ahsa in particular, an in-home arrangement means either a local generalist or a long drive priced into the hour, which is the clearest case on this page for buying the hour online.

regions.name: Makkah and Taif
regions.note: Makkah is roughly 80km east of Jeddah and Taif sits inland at altitude. Families here are commonly choosing between a school in the city and a longer run towards Jeddah, and the in-home tutor pool for a specific Cambridge code is correspondingly thin in both.

regions.name: Madinah and Yanbu
regions.note: Two separate markets rather than one. Yanbu's school population is tied to the industrial city and Madinah's to a larger urban catchment, and neither supports a deep bench in subjects such as 0606 or 0478. Distance is the binding constraint, not willingness to pay.

regions.name: Abha and Khamis Mushait
regions.note: About 25km apart in 'Asir at high altitude, sharing a catchment. The two towns together form one small market, so a family looking for a 0620 Extended specialist at the door is usually choosing from nobody. Online removes the question entirely.

regions.name: Tabuk, NEOM and AlUla
regions.note: The newest and most dispersed part of the picture, with families arriving mid-course and schooling arrangements still settling. In-home tutoring is barely a market here. What families ask for instead is a stable weekly slot that survives a relocation, which a video lesson does and a car cannot.

regions.name: Thuwal, Buraidah, Ha'il, Najran and Jazan
regions.note: Thuwal serves a single campus community north of Jeddah; the others are regional centres with limited international provision. Across all of them the pattern is the same: general tutoring is available, syllabus-specific Cambridge teaching is not, and the drive is the expensive part of any local arrangement.

schoolClusters.note: The capital holds the widest mix of curricula in the Kingdom, with British, Cambridge, IB and American routes all running, sometimes inside one group. Private and international schools here are licensed by the Ministry of Education, and school evaluation runs through the Education and Training Evaluation Commission. Students we support attend schools including those below.

Jeddah's international provision is long established and spread along the coastal spine, and it mixes Cambridge, IB and national-system international schools. Thuwal, north of the city, serves the campus community at the King Abdullah University of Science and Technology. Families here often choose a school for its post-16 route rather than its IGCSE offer.

schoolClusters.city: Dhahran, Al Khobar, Dammam and Jubail
schoolClusters.note: The Eastern Province cluster behaves as one market, and the British and Cambridge-curriculum schools in it are the reason Cambridge codes are so familiar to families here. The International Schools Group operates several campuses across the area; not all of them run the same programmes, and subject availability differs campus by campus.

modes.description: One hour a week on the same day and time through the term, which is what most Cambridge candidates actually need. The slot is agreed in Arabia Standard Time so it does not move when a tutor's own country changes its clocks. The hour is spent on the paper the student is weakest on, not on a march through the syllabus the school is already covering.

sections.heading: The decision behind a Cambridge IGCSE home tutor search
paragraphs: A Cambridge IGCSE home tutor, in the sense a Saudi parent means it, is an adult who arrives at the family's residence at a set time each week and teaches one child one subject. That is a real market in Riyadh, Jeddah and the Eastern Province, it has a published price, and for some families it is the right answer. It is worth saying what it is good at before saying what it costs: a younger child who will not settle to work without an adult physically present, a household where screen time is already a battle, or a short run of sessions where the logistics of getting a laptop, a quiet room and a stable connection together every week is the actual obstacle.

What it is not good at is matching. The moment a tutor has to drive, the pool shrinks to the people who live within driving distance of your district and are free at the hour your child is free. For a widely taught syllabus that is a large enough pool. For Additional Mathematics 0606, International Mathematics 0607, Computer Science 0478 or a specific Chemistry 0620 paper problem, it frequently is not, and families end up hiring a capable generalist at a specialist's rate because that was who was available.

There are four arrangements a family in the Kingdom genuinely chooses between, and they are rarely laid out side by side. An in-home tutor, a centre or group revision course, whatever the school offers after hours, and one-to-one teaching over live video. The table below gives the advertised band for each, what it costs beyond the fee, and the case in which it is the right call. Every figure in it is an advertised rate drawn from vendor listings and tutor-marketplace guides in this market, not a market average and not IB Gram's price. Read it as a description of what each option is buying your money, then read the next section, which takes the in-home hour apart.

sections.heading: What an in-home hour costs once the travel is inside the number
paragraphs: An hourly rate is a unit of time, and the question nobody asks is which hour. A tutor who drives forty minutes each way for a sixty-minute lesson has given up well over two hours to deliver one, and no working adult does that for the same money they would take for an hour at a desk. The cost shows up in one of three ways: a higher headline rate, an explicit travel charge, or a minimum booking of ninety minutes or two hours so the drive is amortised. All three are reasonable from the tutor's side. All three mean the paid hour is not pure teaching.

There is a second cost that never appears on a quote, which is the slot. A visit has to land after the school run and before the evening collapses, in a window that is already narrow on a Sunday-to-Thursday week. A tutor who can only reach your district by half past six has effectively chosen your child's lesson time, and if that clashes with a sibling's commitment or a parent's commute, the family moves around the tutor. Removing the drive gives the slot back, which is worth something even when the rate is identical.

The table below sets the arrangements against each other on the measure that matters, which is how many minutes of teaching a family actually pays for per visit. The bands are advertised rates published by tutoring platforms, tutoring companies and marketplace guides in this market, quoted so the comparison has real numbers in it rather than adjectives. They are not IB Gram's price and not a market average. The pattern they show is consistent: the travelling hour is the most expensive and the least flexible form of the same teaching, and the gap widens the further a family lives from the schools.

sections.heading: The scarcity premium, Cambridge syllabus by Cambridge syllabus
paragraphs: Research on this market points at one driver of price above all others, and it is not teaching quality. It is scarcity. A Mathematics 0580 teacher is available in every secondary school in the Kingdom. A teacher who has taught 0606 to a full cohort and marked it is not, and a school that enters six students for 0478 Computer Science is often staffing it with a willing physicist. Those two facts set the rate long before anyone asks how good the teaching is.

This is useful to a parent because it is checkable. If a quote is high, you can ask which of the levers is behind it: the level, the specific code, marking experience for the board, or the travel. A tutor who says the rate reflects 0606 being a small-entry subject they have taught repeatedly is telling you something verifiable. A tutor who cannot name the lever is quoting what the market will bear. Both may teach well, but only one of them has told you what you are buying.

The table maps the Cambridge codes families in the Kingdom most often buy outside help for against how thin local supply tends to be, what the premium is actually paying for, and what a capable non-specialist usually misses in that subject. The last column is the real argument for a specialist: not that the generalist is weak, but that the thing they miss is specific and expensive. A physicist teaching 0478 will teach logic well and may never mention that the practical evidence has to be presented in a form an examiner can mark.

sections.heading: Four ways to spend the same Cambridge tuition budget
paragraphs: Once a family has a number in mind, the shape of the spend matters as much as the size of it. The same money buys a year of fortnightly contact, two terms of weekly contact, six intense weeks before a series, or a marking service across three subjects. Those are genuinely different purchases, and the right one depends on whether the problem is content, technique or confidence, which is exactly what a diagnostic session is for.

The commonest expensive mistake is buying intensity instead of time. A family that waits until the last stretch before the papers and then books four sessions a week is paying the highest weekly cost for the lowest-leverage work, because content gaps cannot be closed at that distance and all the hours go into damage control. The opposite mistake is cheaper but still real: a year of comfortable weekly lessons that never move to timed papers, so the student knows the subject and still underperforms on the day.

The table sets out four shapes and what each one is good and bad at. It is written as a planning tool rather than a price list, and it deliberately includes the option most providers do not sell, which is spending less on live hours and more on having work marked properly. For a disciplined student in a decent school, that is often where the marks are. Whatever shape a family chooses, it should be reviewed at the end of a term against evidence, not renewed by default.

sections.heading: Telling a high rate for skill apart from a high rate for rarity
paragraphs: Rates in this market are advertised without explanation, so a parent is left comparing two numbers with nothing attached. The way through it is to ask questions whose answers cannot be improvised. Which papers does my child sit for this code, and what is each worth? Which two topics in this syllabus do most candidates lose marks on, and what does the mark scheme want instead? If you have marked for the board, which component and what did it teach you about how students answer it? A specialist answers all three in ordinary language without reaching for a prospectus.

Marking experience is worth paying for, but it has to be specific to be worth anything. Somebody who has marked Chemistry 0620 Paper 4 has read several hundred attempts at the same question and knows which wording the scheme accepts. That is a different kind of knowledge from having taught the subject for years, and it is the thing most reliably reflected in a higher rate. It is also easy to check in conversation: ask what the commonest avoidable loss on that component is, and listen for a specific answer rather than a general one about revision.

The other half of the judgement is about fit rather than credentials. A tutor who has taught inside the Kingdom knows the Sunday-to-Thursday week, the shortened school day in Ramadan and the way international school calendars differ from each other in the same city. That is convenience rather than teaching quality, and it should be priced as convenience. Where it genuinely matters is continuity: a tutor who understands the local school year is less likely to schedule an intensive run across a break, and more likely to work backwards from the series the school has actually entered.
bullets: Ask for the paper structure and weightings of your child's code, unprompted
Ask which component the tutor has marked, and what it taught them
Ask for the two commonest avoidable losses in that syllabus
Ask what the first four weeks would cover, and why in that order
Treat any promise about a grade as a reason to stop the conversation

sections.heading: What a parent gets to see, and why that is part of the price
paragraphs: An in-home lesson is visible by default: you can hear it from the next room. A video lesson has to be made visible deliberately, and whether a provider does that is a fair thing to judge them on. The things worth insisting on are a shared whiteboard the student writes on rather than watches, work that exists as a file afterwards, a short written note after each session, and marked scripts that come back annotated rather than graded. None of that is exotic, and all of it is checkable in a trial lesson.

The mechanics are ordinary. Lessons run in a browser on a laptop with a headset, and the tutor and student share a whiteboard where both can write, which matters for maths and chemistry because the working is the lesson. Past papers and mark schemes are shared on screen and annotated live, so a student watches a question being read before it is answered. A tablet with a stylus works well as a second device for handwriting, but a laptop is the better primary one because two panels have to be visible at once.

Connection trouble is the predictable failure and it should be planned for rather than apologised for. A dropped connection in the middle of a timed paper means the student keeps working and the session resumes, with the paper finished on paper and photographed if necessary. Recording policy should be explicit, with any recording made for the family's use and nobody else's, and a parent should be able to sit in on a session without arranging it in advance. These are not features; they are the minimum conditions for buying teaching you cannot see.

sections.heading: Where outside teaching pays for itself in the Cambridge subjects
paragraphs: Some Cambridge losses are cheap to fix and some are not, and a family deciding where to spend should know the difference. Business Studies 0450 is the clearest example of a cheap fix. The calculation items are small, predictable and frequently dropped, and the evaluation questions need a judgement anchored in the case material by name. A student who learns to quote the stimulus and commit to a conclusion can move a grade without learning any new content, which is a few hours of work rather than a term.

Economics 0455 behaves similarly but for a different reason. Candidates draw correct diagrams and lose marks because nothing in the written answer explains what moved, in which direction and why. Geography 0460 has its own version: case-study answers that are perfectly reasonable in general terms and score at the bottom of the band because they name no place and no figure. In both subjects the gap is between knowing the material and presenting it in the form the scheme rewards, and that is the most efficient thing a specialist hour can address.

The expensive problems are structural. History 0470 asks for inference, provenance and cross-reference on the source paper and sustained argument on the essay paper, and a school short of specialists tends to drill whichever the department is confident in, leaving the other underprepared. International Mathematics 0607 taught as though it were 0580 produces students who can do the algebra and cannot handle the investigation paper or the calculator method it assumes. Additional Mathematics 0606 started in the final term is the hardest of all, because it is new content under time pressure rather than old content presented better.
bullets: 0450: calculation marks and case-anchored evaluation are quick, high-yield fixes
0455: diagram marks depend on the written explanation, not the drawing
0460: a named place and a real figure separate the top band from the bottom
0470: the source paper and the essay paper reward opposite habits
0606 and 0607: structural gaps that need a term, not a revision course

sections.heading: What no rate buys, at any price
paragraphs: A page about value has to be clear about what is not for sale. No tutor can guarantee a grade, a point improvement or a particular outcome in a series, and any provider who offers one is either misunderstanding the assessment or hoping you do. Grade boundaries are set after the papers are marked and move with the cohort and the paper, so a promise made in advance is a promise about something nobody controls. A tutor can tell you where the marks are currently going and what closing that gap would take. That is a forecast, not a commitment, and it should be worded as one.

The second thing not for sale is the student's own work. A tutor teaches, explains, questions and gives feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor does not write the coursework, does not produce a portfolio component, and does not supply text for a submitted piece, because that is malpractice under the board's rules and the consequence lands on the candidate rather than on the tutor. This is worth saying plainly in a market where some providers advertise close to the line. Good feedback sounds like a question about why a paragraph is where it is, not a better paragraph arriving by email.

The third is standing we do not have. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform with no approval, licence, accreditation or partnership from the Ministry of Education, the Education and Training Evaluation Commission, Cambridge or any school named on this page, and no office in the Kingdom. Schools here are licensed by the Ministry of Education, and school evaluation runs through the Education and Training Evaluation Commission; neither body endorses tutors. Any figure quoted here is an advertised rate from a vendor listing, and no statistic about our own results appears on this page because none of it would come with a sample size, a date and a method.

sections.heading: Starting without committing money, and what happens if nobody is free
paragraphs: The first step costs nothing and should produce something you can read. Tell us the Cambridge code, the tier your child is entered at and which paper is the problem, and the trial lesson is spent on a short diagnostic rather than a pitch: a few questions from the relevant paper, worked and watched, so the tutor can separate a content gap from a technique gap from a confidence gap. You keep the written summary whether you book anything or not, and it is useful on its own, because it tells you which of the four spending shapes in this page actually fits.

Then the calendar. Candidates in the Kingdom sit the Cambridge June and November series; in India, Cambridge also runs a February and March series, which is not available here, and copy that says otherwise has been lifted from an Indian page. Entries close months ahead of the papers and your school's examinations officer holds the exact dates, including the deadline after which a tier cannot be changed. Working backwards from the series rather than forwards from today is what decides whether weekly teaching or an intensive block is the sensible purchase.

Sometimes the honest answer is that nobody suitable is free. A single specialist in a small-entry code may have no slot in the window your child needs, and the choice is then a different time, a waiting list, or a well-matched generalist for the content with marked-script support for the technique. We will say which of those we think is right for your child, and we will say when none of them is worth the money, because a family that pays for the wrong thing does not come back. If you want to compare city by city, the Cambridge pages for Riyadh, Jeddah, Dammam, Dhahran and Al Khobar set out the local picture in each.

process.title: Send the code, the tier and the paper
process.description: Not the subject name. Chemistry 0620 Extended with a Paper 4 problem is a different brief from Co-ordinated Sciences, and 0580 is a different brief from 0607. If you do not know the tier, ask the school in writing; the answer also tells you when the entry deadline falls.

process.title: Free trial lesson and a written diagnostic
process.description: Sixty minutes with a specialist in that code, spent on questions from the relevant paper rather than on introductions. It ends with a written note separating content gaps from technique gaps, and naming what the first four weeks would cover and in what order. You keep it either way.

process.title: Fix the slot in Arabia Standard Time
process.description: The weekly time is pinned to local time, not to the tutor's, so a clock change in their country does not move your child's lesson. Slots are chosen against the Sunday-to-Thursday week and the school run, with Friday and Saturday available when the week is already full.

process.title: Teach, set work, mark it, report it
process.description: Each session has work attached, and that work is marked against the published scheme before the next one. Losses are labelled as content, method or command word, so the pattern becomes visible across a term. A short written note after each lesson says what was covered and what comes next.

process.title: Review at the end of a term against evidence
process.description: Compare marked work from the start of the term against marked work from the end, on the same paper type. That is the only honest basis for continuing, changing the shape of the support or stopping. We will tell you when the evidence says stopping is the right call.

whyPoints.title: The pool is national, not within a twenty-minute drive
whyPoints.description: Removing the car removes the only reason the tutor pool had to be local. A family in Al Ahsa, Khamis Mushait or Tabuk can be matched to the same 0606 or 0607 specialist as a family in north Riyadh, which is the whole argument for buying the hour online rather than at the door.

whyPoints.title: You pay for teaching time, not travelling time
whyPoints.description: No part of the fee covers a commute, a minimum booking length designed to amortise a drive, or a travel loading. Sixty booked minutes are sixty taught minutes. That is the clearest difference between this and the in-home market whose advertised rates are quoted on this page.

whyPoints.title: Matched on the syllabus code, not the subject label
whyPoints.description: 0580 and 0607 are different courses; 0500 and 0510 are different qualifications; Core and Extended are different ceilings. Matching starts from the code and the tier your child is entered at, because a tutor who knows the subject but not the specification will teach the wrong thing well.

whyPoints.title: Every rate on this page is attributed
whyPoints.description: The SAR figures here are advertised rates published by tutoring platforms, tutoring companies and tutor-marketplace guides in this market. They are not a market average and not our price. Quoting them with their source type is how a parent can tell a scarcity premium from a quality premium.

whyPoints.title: A stated line on assessed work
whyPoints.description: A tutor reviews, questions and gives feedback on a draft the student has written themselves. No tutor here produces coursework or supplies text for a submitted component, and we say so rather than leaving it vague, because in this market the vagueness is usually deliberate.

whyPoints.title: One written record per session
whyPoints.description: A short note after each lesson and marked work in between, so the teaching you are paying for leaves evidence you can read. It also makes the term review possible, because improvement is judged on comparable marked papers rather than on how the lessons felt.

faqs.question: Which questions about Core and Extended should a Cambridge tutor answer before I pay for a first hour?
faqs.answer: Three, and the answers should come without hesitation. Which tier is my child entered at, and which papers does that tier sit? What is the highest grade available on that tier, and is the entry still changeable? And what would the first four weeks cover differently at Core than at Extended? A tutor who knows the specification will tell you Core is graded C to G and Extended A* to E, that the entry is a school decision reversible only before the deadline, and that the teaching differs in question style more than in content. Vague answers here usually mean subject knowledge without specification knowledge.

faqs.question: How do I check that a tutor teaches 0607 International Mathematics and not just 0580?
faqs.answer: Ask what the graphics calculator is assumed to do in 0607 that it is not assumed to do in 0580, and ask about the investigation paper on the Extended route. A tutor who has taught 0607 will talk about calculator-led method, about sketching and reading graphs as a technique rather than a check, and about how the investigation rewards a structured exploration. A tutor who has only taught 0580 will describe 0607 as the same syllabus with different numbering. That one question separates them, and it takes a minute of a trial lesson.

faqs.question: Is a tutor who has taught Cambridge inside the Kingdom worth more than one who has not?
faqs.answer: Worth something, but less than families assume, and it should be priced as convenience rather than teaching quality. What local experience buys is calendar sense: they know the week runs Sunday to Thursday, that the school day shortens during Ramadan, that international school terms in the same city differ from each other, and that entries are made for the June and November series. A tutor from elsewhere can learn all of that in one conversation. What cannot be learned in a conversation is the specification knowledge, so weight that first and treat local familiarity as a tie-breaker.

faqs.question: How many Cambridge subjects should one tutor be teaching my child at once?
faqs.answer: Usually one, occasionally two inside a closely related pair. A tutor who is genuinely strong on Chemistry 0620 Extended and Biology 0610 can carry both, because the mark-scheme habits overlap. A tutor offering Mathematics 0580, Physics 0625, Business Studies 0450 and First Language English 0500 is offering availability rather than specialism, and the hour will be spent on general study skills. If your child needs two subjects, it is usually better value to book two specialists in one evening than one person for both, even though the logistics are slightly worse.

faqs.question: What does a written first report from a Cambridge IGCSE tutor need to contain?
faqs.answer: Four things. The code and tier the student is entered at, in writing, so a mismatch surfaces immediately. Specific evidence: the questions attempted in the session and what happened on each. A separation of content gaps from technique gaps, because they cost different amounts to fix. And a plan for the first four weeks with an order and a reason for that order. What it should not contain is a predicted grade, a promise, or a target expressed as a number without any basis. If the report could have been written about any student, it was.

faqs.question: What does my child actually need at home for a Cambridge IGCSE lesson over video?
faqs.answer: A laptop rather than a phone, a headset with a microphone, a quiet room with a door, and a printed copy of the paper being worked on where possible. The laptop matters because two things have to be visible at once: the question and the shared whiteboard. A tablet with a stylus is excellent as a second device for handwriting working, and poor as the only device. Connection speed matters less than stability; a dropped frame is harmless, a dropped connection mid-question is not. Nothing needs installing beyond a browser.

faqs.question: Can a Cambridge lesson handle the Geography 0460 map and photograph questions on screen?
faqs.answer: Yes, and arguably better than on paper, because the extract can be magnified and annotated live while the student explains what they are reading. The technique being taught is sequencing: locate, describe what the evidence shows, then explain using the correct terms. On a shared whiteboard the tutor can mark up the extract as the student talks, so the gap between seeing a feature and writing a mark-worthy sentence about it becomes visible. The one thing to insist on is that the annotated extract is saved and sent afterwards, so the student can redo it unaided.

faqs.question: How is a Cambridge ICT 0417 practical task supervised when the tutor is not in the room?
faqs.answer: A tutor does not supervise an assessed practical task at all; the school does, under its own conditions, and the work must be the student's own. What a tutor can do beforehand is teach the skills the task will need and then teach how evidence is presented so an examiner can award marks for it. Students regularly produce a working solution and then lose marks because the screenshots, filenames and annotations do not show what they did. Practising that evidence trail on non-assessed exercises over a shared screen is legitimate, useful and entirely separate from the assessed work itself.

faqs.question: Can two siblings entered for different Cambridge tiers share one weekly session?
faqs.answer: It is possible and it is usually poor value. The tier difference is the problem: a Core candidate and an Extended candidate in the same subject sit different papers with different question styles, so an hour split between them gives each roughly half a lesson aimed at the wrong target. Where sharing does work is two siblings on the same code and tier revising the same topic, and even then one of them tends to take the hour. If the budget is fixed, a fortnightly individual hour each is generally better than a shared weekly one.

faqs.question: How much of an online Cambridge hour is teaching, and how much is set-up?
faqs.answer: Set-up should be two or three minutes: open the browser, join the room, open the shared whiteboard and the paper. If more than that disappears each week, something is wrong with the arrangement rather than with the format. A well-run hour starts with the marked work from last time, spends most of its length on live problem-solving with the student writing, and ends by setting what comes next. The written note afterwards is produced by the tutor on their own time. Compare that with a travelling arrangement, where settling in alone can take a similar few minutes.

faqs.question: Which Cambridge Business Studies 0450 questions cost strong students the most marks?
faqs.answer: The small calculation items and the longest evaluation question, for opposite reasons. The calculations are predictable and students skip them under time pressure or lose the marks to unshown working and missing units. The evaluation question asks for a judgement supported by the specific case material, and strong students write a balanced list of advantages and disadvantages instead, then stop. A list without a decision sits in the middle band however well expressed. Fixing both is a small number of hours of work, which makes 0450 one of the cheapest grades to move.

faqs.question: Why do Economics 0455 candidates lose marks on diagrams they can draw correctly?
faqs.answer: Because the diagram is not the answer. Marks are available for a correctly labelled diagram with properly named axes, and then separately for the written explanation of what shifted, in which direction and why, with the consequence followed through. Students who have practised drawing produce an accurate figure and a sentence saying the price has changed, leaving the reasoning for the reader to supply. The fix is a habit rather than content: draw it, label it, then narrate it in three sentences. It is the single most reliable mark gain in the subject.

faqs.question: What makes the Cambridge History 0470 source paper different from the essay paper?
faqs.answer: They reward opposite habits. The source paper wants inference from the evidence, attention to who produced it and why, and cross-reference between sources that disagree. The essay paper wants a sustained argument with weighted factors and a conclusion that commits. A student drilled only on essays writes everything they know about the period in response to a source and scores poorly; a student drilled only on sources writes a cautious essay that never argues. Schools short of specialists tend to teach whichever the department is confident in, which is why this is a common reason to buy outside teaching.

faqs.question: Where does 0607 International Mathematics diverge from 0580, and who should sit which?
faqs.answer: 0607 assumes a graphics calculator throughout and treats it as a method tool rather than a checking device, and the Extended route carries an investigation paper with no equivalent in 0580. 0580 rewards written algebraic method and includes a paper without a calculator. Neither is harder in general; they suit different students and different next steps. Schools running the IB Diploma afterwards often prefer 0607 because the habits transfer. The decision belongs to the school and the family together, and it should be made before the entry rather than discovered after it.

faqs.question: Why is Additional Mathematics 0606 the Cambridge subject most often started too late?
faqs.answer: Because it looks like an extension of 0580 and is not. It introduces calculus, logarithms, binomial expansion and trigonometric identities, and it assumes the 0580 algebra underneath is automatic rather than achievable. A student who meets it in the final term is learning new content under time pressure while also revising everything else, which is the most expensive position to buy help from. Started early, it is a manageable extra subject for a student heading towards a mathematical post-16 route. Started late, no amount of paid intensity makes it comfortable.

cambridge-igcse-online-tutor.tutorsIntro: Every tutor below is matched to a Cambridge syllabus code rather than a subject label. Ask them which paper your child sits, what the mark scheme rewards on it, and where their own students lose marks.

intro.heading: Four ways to fix a Cambridge grade, and who you are actually hiring
paragraphs: A family in the Kingdom with a weak Cambridge IGCSE subject has four realistic options, and only one of them is this page. The school can offer extra sessions, which cost nothing and are run by the teacher whose lessons produced the problem. A local tutor can be hired to travel, which works in Riyadh, Jeddah and the Dammam cluster and barely works anywhere else. A group revision course can be bought, which is cheap per head and paced for the middle of the room. Or a specialist can be matched one-to-one over live video, which is what a Cambridge IGCSE online tutor means here. Each option solves a different problem, and the cheapest is not always the wrong one. Most families end up using two.

The comparison is easy. The harder question is who the specialist actually is. Cambridge publishes a syllabus for every subject, and the gap between a graduate who knows the subject and somebody who has taught that syllabus to candidates is wider than most parents expect. A chemistry graduate can explain electrolysis. A teacher who has marked the paper knows that the three-mark version of the question wants the electrode, the half-equation and the observation, in that order, and that a candidate who writes a paragraph gets one mark. Qualification and syllabus experience are different claims, and only one of them is checkable in an hour.

Tiering makes this urgent rather than academic. Cambridge tiers many of its IGCSE subjects: Core is graded C to G and Extended is graded A* to E, so a Core entry caps the grade at a C whatever the candidate does on the day. Tier entry is the school's decision and it closes at the entry deadline. A tutor who cannot say, from a marked paper, whether Extended is realistic is not yet useful to a family in Year 10. That single judgement is worth more than a term of general revision, and it is the first thing worth testing. Ask for it in writing, and ask what in the marked work produced it.

Delivery here is online, one-to-one, over live video, timed to the Sunday-to-Thursday week and pinned to Arabia Standard Time. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a Saudi address; home visits are a service offered only in India. For a Cambridge family that is usually an advantage rather than a compromise, because the constraint on quality in this market is not distance but supply: a school in Tabuk or Abha may have one teacher covering three sciences, and no amount of driving produces a second one. The rest of this page is the comparison, the verification script, the year-group timing and the university endgame nobody writes about.

cambridge-igcse-online-tutor.programmesIntro: Cambridge runs a continuous route from lower secondary into the IGCSE years, and most Saudi international schools place students on it before Year 10. These are the three stages a tutor is asked for.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary
programmes.description: The stages that feed the IGCSE years, ending in Checkpoint tests in English, mathematics and science. Results here are diagnostic rather than certificated, which makes them cheap evidence about a tier decision two years ahead.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Two years to a certificated grade, tiered on many subjects. Sciences add either a practical test or the alternative-to-practical paper, and a few subjects keep a school-marked component that the board moderates by sample.
programmes.countryNote: Saudi candidates sit the June series as the main one and the November series for resits and November-entry candidates. Entries close several months ahead of the June series and your school's examinations officer holds the exact date.

programmes.name: The route out of IGCSE
programmes.description: Most Cambridge candidates in the Kingdom move into A Levels or the IB Diploma. Which Extended grades a student holds decides which subjects a school will let them take, so the IGCSE year is a selection event.
programmes.countryNote: A foreign school certificate needs an equivalency decision from the Ministry of Education before a Saudi university treats it as equivalent. The IGCSE years sit below that step but feed the transcript it rests on.

cambridge-igcse-online-tutor.subjectsIntro: Cambridge subject names hide the thing that matters, which is the syllabus code. These are the codes Saudi families ask for most, and what a tutor has to know about each.

subjects.name: Cambridge Mathematics 0580
subjects.description: The default entry. Extended adds functions, vectors and harder algebra, and the calculator paper punishes candidates who never learned to show method. The tier decision matters more here than anywhere.

subjects.name: Cambridge Biology 0610
subjects.description: Definitions are marked strictly and the extended-response questions want linked reasoning rather than lists. A tutor should be able to recite the wording the mark scheme accepts for osmosis.

subjects.name: Cambridge Chemistry 0620
subjects.description: Half-equations, moles and the qualitative analysis tables carry most of the lost marks. Students who can calculate correctly still lose marks on state symbols and observation wording.

subjects.name: Cambridge Physics 0625
subjects.description: Rearranging formulae under time pressure is the real skill, and the practical component is examined either by a laboratory test or the alternative paper. Ask which one the school enters.

subjects.name: Cambridge ICT 0417
subjects.description: Theory plus practical assessment at a computer, where marks go on following a specification precisely. A tutor who is good with software but has never seen the practical mark scheme is the wrong hire.

subjects.name: Cambridge Business Studies 0450
subjects.description: Case-study material carries the higher-mark questions, and candidates lose marks by answering generally instead of from the text in front of them. Application is a separate skill from knowledge here.

subjects.name: Cambridge History 0470
subjects.description: Source handling and essay writing are assessed separately and taught separately. Most candidates are stronger on one than the other, and a diagnosis takes one marked paper.

subjects.name: Cambridge First Language English 0500
subjects.description: Reading questions reward precise selection; the writing tasks reward control of register and structure. Fluent speakers routinely underperform here because fluency is not what is being marked.

cambridge-igcse-online-tutor.regionsTitle: Where Cambridge candidates in the Kingdom sit
cambridge-igcse-online-tutor.regionsIntro: Cambridge entries are spread across the Kingdom unevenly, and the staffing picture differs sharply between a city with several international schools and a city with one.

regions.name: Riyadh
regions.note: The widest choice of boards in one city, and the deepest local tutor pool. Also the city where a Cambridge family is most likely to be offered a generalist at a specialist price.

regions.name: Jeddah
regions.note: British-curriculum and IB schools along the coastal spine, with Cambridge entries common. Distance within the city is the scheduling problem, not availability.

regions.name: Dhahran and Al Khobar
regions.note: British and Cambridge curricula are well established here. Families often live in one city of the cluster and attend school in another.

regions.name: Makkah and Madinah
regions.note: Fewer international schools, so Cambridge candidates are concentrated in a small number of cohorts and subject choice at senior level is narrower.

regions.name: Tabuk and NEOM

sections.heading: The four options, set side by side
paragraphs: School support is the first thing to exhaust, because it is free and because the teacher setting the mock papers knows what is on them. Its limit is structural: a department that cannot staff a subject properly during the day cannot staff it better at four in the afternoon. Where a Saudi school has one teacher covering several sciences, extra sessions reproduce the original problem with a tired teacher. Ask the head of department who will run the sessions and how many students will be in the room before you decline anything else.

A local in-home tutor buys presence. For a fourteen-year-old who will not work unless somebody is sitting beside them, that is worth paying for, and in Riyadh, Jeddah or the Dammam cluster it is available. The cost is travel, loaded into the rate whether or not it appears on the invoice, and the pool is whoever lives within a reasonable drive. For an Accounting candidate in Al Ahsa the pool is nobody, and that is not a failure of effort.

A group revision course is paced for the median student in the room, which is efficient and often enough for a candidate who has understood the content and needs timed practice. It is the wrong purchase for a diagnosed, specific weakness. One-to-one over live video is the opposite trade: it costs more per hour and buys a specialist in the exact syllabus, chosen from anywhere rather than from a twenty-minute radius. The table sets the four options against each other.
