sections.heading: What a Cambridge subject qualification actually proves
paragraphs: Four different claims get bundled into the word qualified, and they are worth separating. A degree in the subject proves content knowledge at a level well above IGCSE. A teaching qualification proves training in how adolescents learn. Having taught the syllabus proves familiarity with the sequence, the set topics and the school-marked components. Having examined for the board proves something narrower and more valuable: knowing what the mark scheme accepts and what it quietly refuses.

Only the last two change what happens in an IGCSE lesson, and both are checkable. Ask which syllabus code they have taught and in which series. Ask what changed in the subject the last time Cambridge revised it. Ask them to describe how a specific question type is marked, and listen for whether they talk in marks or in adjectives. Examiner experience checked this way is worth paying for; examiner experience claimed in a profile line is worth nothing.

A good answer is concrete and slightly boring. It sounds like a teacher saying that candidates lose two marks on the same part of the same question every series, naming the part, and describing the fix in terms of what the student writes rather than what the student knows. A weak answer talks about passion, rapport and building confidence. Those things matter, and they are not the thing being bought at this price. Ask which of the four claims is actually being made, and write the answer down before you call the next provider.

sections.heading: Core and Extended, and the hour that decides the ceiling
paragraphs: On a tiered Cambridge subject, the tier sets the ceiling before any teaching happens. Core is graded C to G; Extended is graded A* to E. A candidate entered for Core who answers every question correctly is still awarded a C, and no later effort moves it. That is published board information rather than an opinion, and it is the single most consequential thing a Saudi family can get wrong about a Cambridge year. Ask the school to confirm the tier and the full component list in writing, because a corridor answer is not a record.

The decision belongs to the school. Departments weigh classwork, mock performance and their own appetite for risk, and a school that enters a borderline student for Core is often protecting them from an unclassified result rather than limiting them. The decision is reversible only before the entry deadline, which falls months ahead of the June series. After that point the conversation is over, which is why the useful purchase is early and small.

What an outside specialist adds is an independent reading of the marked work. A tutor who has taught both tiers can say whether the gap to a reliable Extended performance is a term of teaching or a year of it, and can put that in writing with the questions that produced the view. No tutor can promise the school will agree. What the family gains is an argument made in mark-scheme terms rather than in parental conviction, which is a different conversation in a head of department's office.

sections.heading: How a Cambridge paper is actually marked
paragraphs: Marks are awarded against a scheme, not against a general impression of understanding. The command term at the front of a question tells the candidate which kind of answer earns marks: state wants a fact, describe wants observable detail, explain wants a causal chain, suggest wants applied reasoning about something unfamiliar. Students treat these as stylistic variants of one another and lose marks they already know the content for. Read one past question with your child and name the command term out loud; it takes two minutes and it is usually the cheapest lesson of the week.

Grade thresholds move between series because papers differ in difficulty, and they are set after marking rather than before. This is why a raw mark that produced one grade in one series can produce a neighbouring grade in another, and why a school report expressed as a percentage is not a grade prediction. A tutor who talks about thresholds honestly will say that a target is a range, and will aim a candidate several marks clear of a boundary rather than at it.

A predicted grade is a professional judgement made by the school from the evidence it holds. An outside tutor does not set one and cannot change one, but marked work produced in tutoring is legitimate evidence a school may consider. The practical move is to make that work exist: full papers, done to time, marked against the published scheme, with the script kept. Evidence of that kind is harder to argue with than a parent's report of progress.

sections.heading: When to start, from Lower Secondary to the first Diploma year
paragraphs: The cheapest intervention in a Cambridge career happens before the IGCSE course begins. A Stage 9 student with a hole in algebra or in scientific writing carries it into Year 10, where the syllabus moves too fast to repair foundations. Checkpoint results are useful precisely because they are low-stakes: they diagnose without consequence, and a term of work on what they expose is worth more than the same term spent a year later.

In Year 10 the question changes from foundations to tier. The useful work is establishing where the student actually sits on Extended-level questions, not just on classwork, because classwork is often set at the level the teacher expects rather than the level the paper demands. By the spring term of Year 10 a family should know which subjects are safe, which are borderline and which are at risk, and should have that in writing from somebody who reads mark schemes.

In Year 11 the work is technique and timing, and the honest answer about starting late is that it depends on the diagnosis. A candidate losing marks on command terms and timing can move a grade in a term. A candidate missing a year of content cannot, and a tutor who says otherwise is selling. Insist on the diagnosis before the block of sessions, and treat a refusal to give one as the answer. After the IGCSE years, the first Diploma year punishes students whose Extended grade came from memorising rather than from understanding, which is where a quiet follow-on term pays for itself.

sections.heading: Equivalency, Qudurat and Tahsili: the part nobody writes about
paragraphs: A foreign or international school certificate is not automatically equivalent to the Saudi secondary certificate. An equivalency decision from the Ministry of Education is the step that makes it usable in a Saudi university application, and it applies to the IB Diploma, to A Levels and to an American high school diploma alike. An IGCSE statement of results sits below that step: it is evidence inside the file rather than the thing being recognised. Families who discover this in the final school year discover it late.

Qudurat, the General Aptitude Test, is run by the Education and Training Evaluation Commission through its National Center for Assessment, known as Qiyas. It tests verbal and quantitative reasoning rather than syllabus content, and is sat in Arabic or English. Tahsili, the Achievement Test, covers mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology and English, and its content follows the Saudi national curriculum. That last fact is why strong Cambridge candidates often find it unfamiliar: the material overlaps but the framing does not.

Universities publish their own admission criteria combining school grades with the Qiyas tests, and weightings differ by institution and by programme. No page should publish a cut-off and this one does not; the only reliable source is the university's own published criteria for the programme in question. What the IGCSE years contribute is the groundwork: a student who kept mathematics, physics and chemistry at Extended has studied the content Tahsili draws on, even where the question style is new to them.

sections.heading: Five questions for a first call with a Cambridge tutor
paragraphs: First, which syllabus code have you taught, and in which series? A tutor who answers with a subject name rather than a number has told you something. Second, which component does my child's school enter for the practical element, and what difference does it make? The answer should name both options and explain which demands laboratory experience the candidate may not have. Third, what do your students most often lose marks on in this paper, and what do you do about it?

Fourth, from this marked paper, is Extended realistic? The answer should point at specific questions and specific marks, and should come with a caveat about who actually decides. Fifth, what will you send me, and how often? A written plan, a record of marked work and a short note after each session are reasonable; a monthly paragraph of encouragement is not. These five questions take fifteen minutes and they filter harder than any profile page.

Use the free trial lesson as the test rather than the sales call it often becomes. A specialist will spend it on a marked paper and a diagnosis, and will tell you at the end which component is costing marks and roughly how many sessions the repair needs. A generalist will spend it teaching something, pleasantly, and will offer a package. The difference is visible inside the first twenty minutes, and it costs nothing to find out. Write the five questions down and ask them in the same order of every provider you speak to, because comparing the answers is the whole point.

faqs.question: What should a Year 9 student finishing Cambridge Lower Secondary have secured before the IGCSE course begins?
faqs.answer: Algebraic fluency, the habit of showing method, and the ability to write a causal explanation in sentences rather than bullet points. Those three carry every Cambridge IGCSE subject, and all three are cheap to build at Stage 9 and expensive to build in Year 11. Checkpoint results expose the gaps without consequence. A term of targeted work on what they reveal is worth more than the same term spent after the IGCSE syllabus has started moving.

faqs.question: At what point in Year 10 does a Cambridge mark become worth acting on?
faqs.answer: Once the class has sat something written to the paper's standard rather than to the teacher's expectation, which is usually the first proper assessment of the spring term. Before that, classwork is set at a level chosen for teaching, not for examining, and strong classwork can hide a weak examination performance. The first assessment written in paper format is the first honest data point, and it arrives early enough to change a tier entry if it needs to.

faqs.question: Does a Cambridge IGCSE candidate entering DP1 need a different tutor from the one who taught them Extended?
faqs.answer: Often yes. Extended rewards accurate recall and clean method; the first Diploma year rewards handling unfamiliar material and sustaining an argument. A tutor who was excellent at drilling 0580 technique may not be the right person for Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches, where the demand changes rather than merely increases. Keep the tutor if they have taught both courses; change if they have only ever taught to the IGCSE ceiling.

faqs.question: Is there any point starting Cambridge IGCSE support in the final weeks before the papers?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on the diagnosis. A candidate who understands the content and is losing marks on command terms, timing and question selection can move meaningfully in a few weeks, because the fix is in how answers are written. A candidate missing substantial content cannot, and should be told so rather than sold a block of sessions. Ask for the diagnosis before the package, and expect an honest tutor to decline work they cannot do.

faqs.question: What changes for a Cambridge candidate who moves school between Year 10 and Year 11 inside the Kingdom?
faqs.answer: The syllabus is national to the board, so the content is portable, but almost nothing else is. Set texts, practical component choices, tier entries and the sequence topics were taught in all differ by school. The new school's entry decisions govern. Get the new department's component list in writing in the first week, and compare it against what was actually covered.

faqs.question: How do Cambridge grade thresholds differ from the grades printed on a school report?
faqs.answer: A school report usually converts a raw percentage into a grade using last series' thresholds or a departmental rule of thumb. Real thresholds are set after the board has marked the papers, so they move between series as papers vary in difficulty. A report grade is therefore an estimate built on an estimate. Treat it as a direction of travel, and aim a candidate several marks clear of a boundary rather than at the boundary itself.

faqs.question: What does a Cambridge mark scheme pay for in a four-mark explain question?
faqs.answer: Usually four separate creditable points linked into a chain, not one point explained at length. The scheme lists acceptable alternatives for each mark and often requires a specific term rather than a synonym. Candidates lose marks by writing fluently around the answer, and gain them by writing four short linked statements. This is why a tutor who has read the scheme teaches differently from one who has only read the textbook.

faqs.question: How is a Cambridge IGCSE predicted grade produced, and who signs it off?
faqs.answer: The school produces it from the evidence it holds, usually mock performance, classwork and the department's judgement, and the head of department or examinations officer signs it. An outside tutor neither sets nor changes it. What a tutor can do is add evidence: full papers done to time and marked against the published scheme, with the scripts kept. A prediction is a professional estimate rather than a promise.

faqs.question: What happens if a Cambridge candidate misses one paper of a multi-paper subject?
faqs.answer: The school reports the absence to the board and the outcome depends on which component was missed and why, with medical evidence treated differently from a missed flight. In some cases a grade can still be awarded from the remaining components; in others the subject is incomplete for that series and the candidate enters the next one. Your school's examinations officer is the only reliable source here.

faqs.question: Is a Cambridge IGCSE remark ever worth requesting, and what does the process involve?
faqs.answer: It is worth considering when a grade sits just below a boundary and is out of line with everything else the candidate produced. The request goes through the school rather than the family, there is a fee, and a mark can go down as well as up. Ask the department to look at the component breakdown first: a single weak component usually explains the grade.

faqs.question: Is Qudurat sat in Arabic or English, and does that change how a Cambridge student prepares?
faqs.answer: It is available in Arabic and in English, and the choice matters for a student schooled entirely in English. Qudurat tests verbal and quantitative reasoning rather than syllabus content, so preparation is about question format and pacing rather than revision of topics. A Cambridge candidate's mathematical fluency transfers well; the verbal reasoning section rewards practice with the test's own question styles.

faqs.question: What should a Cambridge IGCSE student in Year 11 already know about the Qiyas tests?
faqs.answer: Enough to plan, which is less than families fear. They should know that Qudurat tests reasoning rather than content, that Tahsili follows the Saudi national curriculum in the sciences and mathematics, and that both sit after the IGCSE years rather than during them. The useful action in Year 11 is subject retention: keeping mathematics and the sciences at Extended keeps the later options open. Detailed preparation belongs to the post-16 years.

faqs.question: Does a Cambridge candidate who leaves the Kingdom mid-course still need the equivalency step?
faqs.answer: Only if the family intends to use the final certificate for a Saudi university application. Equivalency is a recognition step applied to the school-leaving qualification, so a student who finishes abroad and applies abroad never meets it. A student who finishes abroad and later applies to a Saudi university does. Keep every statement of results and school transcript from the Cambridge years, because reconstructing them years later from another country is the part families find hardest.

faqs.question: How does a university outside the Kingdom use Cambridge IGCSE grades when the post-16 qualification is unfinished?
faqs.answer: As corroborating evidence rather than as the offer condition. Overseas admissions tutors read IGCSE grades to sanity-check a predicted A Level or Diploma result, and to see whether a subject prerequisite has been studied at all. A strong Extended profile makes an ambitious prediction credible; a thin one makes it look optimistic. Some courses also set a specific IGCSE grade as a minimum for English or mathematics.

intro.heading: Five ways to fix a weak Cambridge subject, and what each one really costs
paragraphs: Nobody hires a tutor in a vacuum. By the time a family in the Kingdom searches for a Cambridge IGCSE tutor, they have usually already weighed four other things: whether the school's own after-school intervention will be enough, whether a group revision course would be better value, whether a private tutor who drives to the house is worth the premium, and whether a disciplined candidate could get there on past papers alone. All four are reasonable, and at least two of them are sometimes the right answer. This page compares them properly rather than pretending the comparison does not exist.

The school's intervention has an advantage nothing else can match: the teacher knows the cohort, the scheme of work and what has actually been taught. Its weakness is that it is a group, usually built for the middle of the class, and the student who needs a specific gap closed is rarely the reason the session was timetabled. A group revision course has a different strength, which is calibration: sitting alongside other candidates on the same syllabus is the cheapest way to discover whether your answers are strong, and a solitary learner never gets that.

A private tutor who travels buys physical presence, and for some students that is decisive. A fourteen-year-old who will not engage with a screen, or a younger child who needs somebody at the table, is not being served well by anything delivered remotely, and it is dishonest to pretend otherwise. The costs are the pool and the loading. The pool shrinks to whoever will drive to your district on a weekday evening, and driving time is paid for whether or not it appears as a line on the invoice. Tutor-marketplace guides put general senior-school private tuition in Saudi cities at SAR 200 an hour and above.

A specialist online buys the opposite trade. The pool becomes everyone who teaches that exact Cambridge syllabus and is free in a workable Saudi slot, which for Additional Mathematics or Extended Physics is the difference between a choice and no choice at all. Tutoring companies advertise subject tutoring on international curricula from around SAR 180, and budget platforms list IGCSE one-to-one from around SAR 35, both of which are provider marketing figures rather than market averages. What it needs in return is a reliable connection and a student who will work on screen. A tutor never attends a Saudi address through IB Gram; India is the only country where in-home teaching is on offer.

The fifth option, past papers and self-study, is free and genuinely sufficient for a small number of candidates: disciplined, already working near the top grades, and losing marks only on technique. It fails for everyone else at the same point, which is marking. A student cannot mark their own script to a scheme they do not yet understand, and nobody can explain a mark scheme to themselves. That is the narrow thing a good Cambridge tutor supplies, and the honest way to judge any of these five options is to ask which of them puts marked work in front of your child every week.
bullets: The school's own intervention knows the cohort; it does not know your child's specific gap
A group course buys calibration against other candidates, which a solitary learner never gets
An in-home tutor buys presence, and pays for travel in the rate whether or not it is itemised
An online specialist buys the exact syllabus code and tier, from a far larger pool
Self-study with past papers fails at marking, which is the one thing it cannot supply

cambridge-igcse-tutor.programmesIntro: These are the qualifications a Saudi family is usually choosing between, or moving between, around this age. Each is described by what it gives and what it costs you in flexibility, because that is the comparison families are actually making when they ask about Cambridge.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Subject-by-subject, examined on written papers, one grade each, with Core and Extended tiers on many syllabuses and a practical test or alternative-to-practical paper in the sciences. Its strength is modularity: a candidate can take six subjects or nine, add one later, or sit a subject in a different series from the rest. Its weakness is that every structural decision, tier and paper route among them, is made on an entry form months before anyone revises.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge is the most widely sat international qualification at this level in the Kingdom, and candidates here enter the June series or the November series. Having two windows is a genuine advantage over systems with one, and it is routinely wasted because families only discover the November option after a disappointing June result.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The direct alternative at the same level. Subject content overlaps heavily with Cambridge, while paper structures, assessment objectives and the treatment of practical work differ. Edexcel assesses practical skills inside the written papers rather than through a separate component, which some families prefer and which changes the preparation substantially. Mathematics runs as more than one specification, one tiered and one not.
programmes.countryNote: Some schools in the Kingdom run Cambridge in most subjects and Edexcel in one or two, which is where families get caught: the board is a property of the subject rather than of the school. Confirm it per subject before engaging any tutor, because a specialist prepared on the other board is a poorer match than their experience suggests.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The non-examined alternative across the same years, assessed against four criteria per subject marked out of eight using published descriptors, with the Personal Project at the end and external eAssessment where a school offers it. It develops extended writing and independent enquiry well, and timed answering to a mark allocation hardly at all, which is exactly the skill a Cambridge paper pays for.
programmes.countryNote: Families comparing a Cambridge school with a Middle Years Programme school in the same Saudi city are usually told the choice is about philosophy. The practical difference is narrower: one produces a certificate of subject grades at sixteen and the other does not, and that certificate is what some sixth forms and employers ask to see.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS and A Level
programmes.description: The most common destination for a Cambridge IGCSE candidate. Entry requirements are written in IGCSE grades, usually naming the subject itself and often mathematics alongside it, and the step up in abstraction is real in mathematics and the sciences. Three or four subjects studied in depth, with no core, which suits a student who already knows their direction.
programmes.countryNote: Against the Diploma, this route trades breadth for depth and drops the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge entirely. For a Saudi family the relevant question is usually which route the local schools actually run to completion, since a two-year programme with a thin cohort is a risk whichever qualification it carries.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The other destination: six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service, with up to three core points and a ceiling of forty-five. Broader than A Levels and more administratively demanding, with an internally assessed component in every subject that is marked at school and moderated by the board.
programmes.countryNote: A Cambridge IGCSE certificate is accepted into Diploma entry everywhere, and the transition that catches students is not content but the internal assessment load across six subjects at once. Extended tier mathematics at IGCSE, and ideally Additional Mathematics, is what makes Higher Level mathematics survivable.

cambridge-igcse-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the Cambridge syllabuses support is most often asked for in the Kingdom. Each note says what the subject is most often confused with, or compared against, because that confusion is usually what has gone wrong by the time a family starts looking for help.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580)
subjects.description: Most often confused with its own tiers. Core and Extended share much of their content and differ in grade ceiling, so a candidate in Core cannot reach the top grades however the teaching goes. Against Edexcel, the chief practical differences are formula provision and question phrasing rather than topic coverage, which is why a tutor should be asked which board they have prepared candidates for.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (0606)
subjects.description: Routinely mistaken for a harder version of 0580, which it is not: it is an additional qualification sat alongside Extended mathematics, introducing calculus and formal algebra a year early. The nearest Edexcel equivalent is a separate Further Pure specification. It is the scarcest mainstream Cambridge specialism in this market, and that scarcity, not difficulty, is what sets the rate.

subjects.name: Physics (0625)
subjects.description: Compared against Edexcel, the decisive difference is the practical component: Cambridge entries carry either a practical test or the alternative-to-practical paper, while Edexcel assesses practical skills within its written papers. Families frequently do not know which route their centre entered, and it changes several months of preparation, so it is the first thing to establish.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620)
subjects.description: Often compared unfavourably with Biology on difficulty, which misreads where the marks go. Moles and stoichiometry defeat more candidates than organic chemistry, because the arithmetic cannot be bluffed under time pressure. Qualitative analysis tables are examinable and learnable, and a short block of work on those two things moves a grade more reliably than general revision.

subjects.name: Biology (0610)
subjects.description: Mistaken for the easy science because the content reads easily. Definitions are marked strictly with thin partial credit, so approximate recall scores nothing, and the command terms distinguish, outline, explain and discuss each demand a different structure the scheme pays for. Candidates here usually know more than their scripts show, which makes marked practice better value than more teaching.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated Sciences (0654)
subjects.description: Compared against the three separate sciences, this Double Award carries fewer papers and less total content for two grades. It is the sensible entry for many candidates and a trap for those aiming at sixth-form sciences, since some providers expect the separate subjects. Check the next stage's published requirements before choosing it on workload grounds.

subjects.name: First Language English (0500)
subjects.description: Compared against 0510 as a second language, and the comparison is frequently got wrong in both directions. First Language English demands analysis of a writer's method rather than of content, which is where confident readers lose marks. A single diagnostic reading task settles which entry is right, and it is worth doing before the entry rather than after the result.

subjects.name: Literature in English (0475)
subjects.description: Often assumed to be included in the English entry, and it is a separate qualification with its own papers and set texts. Sixth forms and universities sometimes name it specifically. Marks come from close reading of language rather than from plot knowledge, and a candidate who writes confident summaries of the story is usually scoring in the middle band.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478)
subjects.description: Compared against practical programming experience, which turns out to help less than families expect. Algorithms and programming are assessed on paper, where pseudocode is marked to a scheme rather than run, and the theory papers cover data representation, networks and systems. Specialists are scarce in this market, and the scarcity is in the examined form rather than in the coding.

subjects.name: Geography (0460)
subjects.description: Compared against History as the lighter humanity, and the fieldwork and skills paper make that comparison unsafe. Case studies have to be supplied by the candidate, so a student without a class and a shared example file is at a real disadvantage. Building that file from the first month is the whole difference between a middle grade and a strong one.

subjects.name: Accounting (0452)
subjects.description: Compared against Business Studies and chosen for the wrong reason: it is not a discursive subject at all, but structured double-entry work, financial statements and interpretation with no essay writing. It suits a methodical candidate extremely well, because practice is self-checking: a trial balance either balances or it does not.

cambridge-igcse-tutor.regionsTitle: Cambridge candidates by region, and what each one is choosing between
cambridge-igcse-tutor.regionsIntro: The comparison at the top of this page resolves differently depending on where a family lives, because local supply is not evenly spread. In two or three places a named local tutor is a real alternative. In most of the Kingdom the honest choice is between an online specialist and nothing in particular.

regions.name: Riyadh and the capital region
regions.note: Deep local supply and a genuine choice: families here are comparing a named local tutor against an online specialist, and cross-city travel time is the variable that usually settles it. This is also where the Cambridge against IB sixth-form decision is most often live, because both routes exist within reach.

regions.name: The Dammam, Khobar and Dhahran conurbation
regions.note: The largest Cambridge population outside the capital, behaving as one school market across three cities. Local supply covers most subjects, so the enquiries that travel outward are narrow: Additional Mathematics, Extended Physics, and Computer Science examined on paper rather than on a machine.

regions.name: Jeddah and Obhur
regions.note: A long coastal strip with the widest mix of boards in one city, which means more families here hold subjects on different specifications than anywhere else. The comparison that matters locally is not online against in-home but Cambridge against Edexcel, because both are genuinely available.

regions.name: Makkah and Taif
regions.note: Large populations with comparatively few international-curriculum candidates, and calendars that accommodate the Hajj and Umrah seasons. With little local specialist supply, the practical comparison narrows to an online specialist against the school's own capacity, and the answer usually depends on the subject rather than the student.

regions.name: Madinah
regions.note: A small international-curriculum cohort relative to the city's size, so a scarce Cambridge subject frequently has no local answer at all. Families here compare an online specialist against a group course run elsewhere, and the arithmetic of travel decides it before anything educational does.

regions.name: Jubail and Yanbu
regions.note: Industrial cities with schooling attached to the workforce, and a Cambridge population large enough to run most subjects and too small to staff every tier. The specific gap is the Extended entry in the sciences, which is also the entry most sixth-form science routes expect.

regions.name: Abha and Khamis Mushait
regions.note: Two cities roughly twenty-five kilometres apart at altitude in 'Asir, sharing a catchment and a small combined cohort. There is very little to compare locally, which makes the connection quality and the agreed slot the only two variables worth negotiating hard on.

regions.name: Tabuk, AlUla and NEOM
regions.note: Where households are arriving faster than provision is settling, so mid-course transfers are common and entries are sometimes already made before a family understands them. The first comparison here is rarely between tutors; it is between what the new centre has entered the candidate for and what the family assumed.

schoolClusters.city: Schools in the Kingdom named in directories as running a British or Cambridge pathway
schoolClusters.note: Provision changes year to year and by subject, so a school listed as Cambridge may run Edexcel in a subject or two, and a school listed as an IB school may also be a Cambridge centre. Confirm the board per subject with the school rather than inferring it from the name.

schoolClusters.city: Schools where an IGCSE certificate feeds an IB sixth form
schoolClusters.note: For families weighing Cambridge IGCSE against the Middle Years Programme, the practical question is what the local sixth form actually runs to completion. These schools appear in IB listings, and several of the Eastern Province campuses offer the Diploma at some sites rather than all of them.

cambridge-igcse-tutor.schoolDisclaimer: Named schools appear only as context for families comparing local provision; IB Gram has no relationship with any of them and does not act for any school or school group.
cambridge-igcse-tutor.modesIntro: Four arrangements, deliberately different from one another rather than three sizes of the same thing. Two of them are short pieces of work with a defined end, which is usually what a family comparing options actually wants first. All are one-to-one over live video on Arabia Standard Time.

modes.title: A single diagnostic review, before committing to anything
modes.description: One session and a written report, with no ongoing arrangement implied. A specialist works through recent material, marks a script the student has already produced, and writes down what is wrong, in what order to fix it, and roughly how long each part takes. Families comparing five options can use that document to decide between them rather than guessing.

modes.title: A tier-decision review in Year 10
modes.description: Narrow and consequential. Core and Extended carry different grade ceilings, and the entry is usually settled by the school on the basis of classwork. This is a short piece of work that produces marked evidence on both tiers' papers, so a family going back to the school is carrying something more useful than a conviction.

modes.title: Weekly teaching on one syllabus code
modes.description: The standard arrangement: one subject, one specialist, one fixed hour, with content running slightly ahead of the class and written work marked between sessions. The shared whiteboard is saved and sent afterwards, and the weekly note reports marks rather than impressions so a term produces a trend line instead of reassurance.

modes.title: Whole papers under timed conditions, marked cold
modes.description: No teaching. The candidate sits a complete paper to the real time allowance, submits it, and gets it back marked to the published scheme with the recurring misses named. Three papers normally reveal the entire pattern. It is the cheapest useful product here and it suits a candidate who holds the content and is losing marks on form.

sections.heading: The five options, set against each other
paragraphs: A comparison is only useful if it is willing to lose. Here is where each of the five options genuinely wins. The school's own intervention wins on knowledge of the cohort and costs nothing extra. A group revision course wins on calibration and on volume of past-paper exposure for the money. An in-home tutor wins where physical presence is the deciding factor for that particular child. Self-study wins for a disciplined candidate already near the top grades. An online specialist wins on exactness of match and on the size of the pool it draws from.

The losses are equally specific. The school's intervention is paced for a group. A revision course addresses nobody's particular gap. An in-home arrangement restricts the pool to whoever will drive to your district and prices the driving into the rate. Self-study cannot mark itself. And online delivery needs a working connection and a student who will engage on screen, which is a real condition rather than a formality; a parent who knows their child will not, should take that seriously rather than hoping.

The sixth row in the table is there because it keeps appearing in this market and should be named. Services offering to write, complete or improve coursework are not a cheaper option on the same scale as the others. Where a Cambridge syllabus carries coursework, the school declares the work as the student's own, and using such a service is malpractice with consequences that outlast any grade. Any provider offering it has told a family everything they need to know about the rest of their service.

sections.heading: Cambridge against Edexcel, subject by subject
paragraphs: Families treat the board as a property of the school, and it is a property of the subject. A school in the Kingdom can run Cambridge in mathematics and the sciences and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE in English, or the reverse, and the entry form is the only place that tells you. This matters because a tutor who has prepared candidates on one board is a weaker match on the other than their experience makes them look: the content overlaps, the question styles and mark-scheme habits do not.

The sharpest practical difference sits in the sciences. A Cambridge science entry carries either a practical test or the alternative-to-practical paper, and which one the centre chose changes what the lessons should contain for several months. Edexcel assesses practical skills inside its written papers rather than through a separate component. Neither approach is better; they demand different preparation, and a candidate prepared for the wrong one arrives at a paper they have not practised.

Mathematics is the second place families get caught. Cambridge 0580 is entered at Core or Extended tier, with the tier setting the grade ceiling before any revision happens. Edexcel runs more than one mathematics specification, one with tiered papers and one without. Beyond that sit the additional qualifications, Cambridge 0606 Additional Mathematics on one side and a separate Further Pure specification on the other, and whether the next stage expects one of them is a question for the sixth form rather than for a tutor.

sections.heading: Core against Extended, and why the entry decides the ceiling
paragraphs: This is the one comparison inside Cambridge that outranks every choice of tutor. Many syllabuses are entered at Core or Extended tier. The two share a great deal of content, they sit different papers, and they carry different grade ceilings. A candidate entered for Core cannot reach the top grades however good the teaching is and however hard they work. No amount of paid support changes that, which is why a family paying for help should establish the entry in writing before the first lesson.

Schools typically form the tiering view in Year 10, on classwork, and they are usually right. Where they are wrong, it is normally in one direction: a student who was weak early and has since improved stays in the view formed about them in the first term. The way to reopen that conversation is not conviction but evidence, which means marked questions from both tiers' papers, scored against the published scheme, carried to the school in a form a head of department can read in two minutes.

There is a mirrored error worth naming. Buying Extended-level teaching against a Core entry is waste: the student spends the year on material they will not be examined on, and the ceiling does not move. Buying Core-level teaching when the school intends an Extended entry is worse, because the gap appears in the examination rather than in the lessons. Confirm the tier, teach to the tier, and treat the tier itself as a separate decision made at the right moment with evidence rather than as a detail on a form.
bullets: Get the tier for every subject in writing before the first paid lesson
Reopen a tiering decision in Year 10, with marked evidence, not in Year 11
Teach to the entry, not to the ambition; the ceiling is set by the entry

sections.heading: A Cambridge specialist against a good general teacher
paragraphs: The most common quiet substitution in this market is a competent subject teacher standing in for a syllabus specialist. It is not fraud and it is often good value at the lower rates, because a strong physics teacher will teach physics well. What they will not reliably do is teach the examined form of this particular syllabus: how many papers there are, how long each is, which formulae are provided, which practical route the entry covers, and where the scheme releases marks that a textbook answer never collects.

The difference is measurable in a single question. Ask what the commonest avoidable mark loss is on the specific paper your child will sit. A specialist answers with a diagnosis: working not shown, so method marks die with a wrong final figure; graph axes unlabelled; a six-mark answer written as one paragraph instead of six separable points; qualitative analysis results half-remembered. A generalist answers with a sentiment about exam technique. Both answers are given confidently, and only one of them is information.

Where the generalist is the right purchase is content repair. A student with genuine gaps from the previous year needs teaching more than they need mark-scheme literacy, and paying a scarcity premium for that is poor value. The sensible pattern for a family comparing rates is to diagnose first, buy content repair at the ordinary rate where that is the problem, and reserve the specialist premium for the examined form in the final year. That sequence costs less across two years than either choice made exclusively.

sections.heading: One-to-one against a group, for a Cambridge candidate
paragraphs: Group teaching has one advantage that one-to-one structurally cannot supply, and it is worth more than families assume. A candidate working alone has no idea whether their answer is strong. They feel they have written plenty, and nothing tells them the scheme wanted four separable points. Sitting with two or three other candidates on the same syllabus supplies that comparison immediately and cheaply, and for a confident student who is quietly under-answering it can be the single most useful intervention available.

Where a group fails is pace and specificity. Three candidates with different gaps cannot be taught the same hour efficiently, and the session drifts towards the middle of the group, which is precisely where nobody's problem lives. The weaker candidate falls behind quietly and the stronger one is unchallenged, and both families pay for the hour. Group revision courses advertised per course rather than per hour look cheap for that reason, and the per-hour arithmetic is not the comparison that matters.

The arrangement that tends to work best is neither purely, and it is rarely offered because it is harder to sell. One-to-one teaching on the content and the syllabus, with occasional group paper sessions for calibration, gives a candidate both the specificity and the comparison. For a family weighing a group course against a Cambridge IGCSE tutor in Saudi Arabia, the honest answer is that the two are solving different problems, and that the diagnosis should come before the choice rather than after it.

sections.heading: Online against in-home, once the Saudi week is counted
paragraphs: This comparison usually gets made on cost, and cost is the least interesting part of it. The decisive variable is the week. The school week in the Kingdom runs Sunday to Thursday, and Friday and Saturday are the weekend. An in-home arrangement has to be built around one tutor's driving route on fixed afternoons, which means Thursday evenings get booked because they are free, and Thursday evenings are the first slot surrendered every time anything else happens. Saturday, the single most valuable study block in the Saudi week, is rarely offered at all.

Arabia Standard Time is the second structural fact. The Kingdom holds UTC+3 and does not observe daylight saving, so an arrangement agreed in a tutor's local time drifts twice a year, always mid-term. Written in Saudi local time, the drift lands on the tutor's side where it belongs. A tutor's own working week matters as much as their clock: somebody keeping a Sunday-to-Thursday week has the same weekend as your family, while somebody on a Saturday-and-Sunday weekend has your school night inside their time off and their Friday evening inside your weekend.

Those two facts favour online delivery for reasons that have nothing to do with price. A slot can move two hours later for the month of Ramadan and move back afterwards without renegotiating a driving route. A second session can be added in the final term as a diary question rather than a logistics problem. And a Saturday morning block, which is the best hour in the week to sit a whole paper, is available because nobody has to cross a city to reach it. Against that, presence remains the in-home option's real advantage, and for some students it still decides the matter.
bullets: Thursday evening is the worst weekly slot in the Kingdom; it will be given up first
Saturday is the best block in the week for a whole paper plus review
Record the slot in Arabia Standard Time so a tutor's clock change lands on their side
Ask about a tutor's own working week, not only their time zone

sections.heading: What a parent actually sees in an online Cambridge lesson
paragraphs: Families comparing options online are comparing something they cannot watch, which is a fair objection and an answerable one. A lesson is live one-to-one video with a shared whiteboard: the tutor and the student both write on it, working is typed and drawn rather than described, and the board is saved at the end and sent to you. A past paper is opened on screen and worked through question by question, with the published mark scheme beside it, so the student sees where the marks were released rather than being told about it.

Between lessons the student submits written work, a specialist marks it to the published scheme, and it comes back annotated with the scheme attached. That package, the saved whiteboard, the marked script and the mark scheme, is what a parent should insist on receiving, because it is checkable in a way that a report is not. A tutor who sends a cheerful summary and no marks is reporting a mood. Over a term the marks make a line, and a line is the only honest answer to whether the money is working.

Two practical matters are worth settling before the first session rather than after the first failure. Connectivity: agree what happens if the connection drops, whether the session pauses and resumes or is rescheduled, and who decides. Recording: ask plainly whether sessions are recorded, who can see a recording and for how long it is kept, and expect a clear answer. A parent may sit in on any lesson here, and a tutor who objects to a parent listening has raised a question that outweighs anything on their profile.

sections.heading: The June series against the November series, as a decision
paragraphs: Candidates in the Kingdom enter the June series or the November series. Cambridge also runs a February and March sitting which is open to candidates in India only, and because a great deal of tutoring material aimed at Gulf families is adapted from Indian pages, that calendar gets imported and acted upon. Confirm the series with your own school's examinations officer, who also holds the final entry windows, the paper combinations and the practical routes for every subject on the entry.

Having two windows is a real choice rather than a safety net, and most families only discover it after a result they did not want. A candidate who is genuinely behind in one subject can enter that subject in the November series and use the intervening months properly, while sitting the rest in June. That splits the load, and it costs a term of feeling out of step with classmates. Made deliberately on marked evidence, it is often the better decision; made as a reaction, it is a scramble.

The inverse comparison matters too. A November entry moves the intensive weeks into the start of a school year, when new teaching is also beginning, and it makes the preceding summer the main preparation window rather than a break. Entry deadlines sit correspondingly earlier. Nothing in the school's own calendar is built around a November candidate, so the planning has to be explicit. Final entries close months before papers, so the decision has to be made while it is still available rather than when it becomes urgent.

sections.heading: What the certificate gets compared against later
paragraphs: A Cambridge certificate is a currency rather than a destination, and judging a tutor's cost against a single grade understates the purchase. Sixth forms express their entry requirements in IGCSE grades, usually naming the subject itself and frequently mathematics alongside it, and an IB Diploma school looks at the same grades when deciding whether to support a student at Higher Level. The subjects and tiers settled at this stage decide which of those routes remains open two years later.

For families intending to stay in the Kingdom for university, the chain runs further. A Saudi university requires Ministry of Education equivalency, the mu'adalah decision, before treating a foreign or international certificate as equivalent to the Saudi secondary certificate, and that applies to whatever qualification the student finishes with rather than to the IGCSE itself. Alongside it sit the Qiyas tests run by the National Center for Assessment within the Education and Training Evaluation Commission: Qudurat, which examines reasoning rather than taught content, and Tahsili, whose content follows the Saudi national curriculum.

The IGCSE years are where the mathematics and science foundations that Tahsili later draws on are either laid or left. A candidate who drops a science at this stage, or who is entered at Core tier in mathematics, has narrowed a set of options that nobody mentioned at the time. Each university publishes its own admission criteria and those are the only figures worth trusting; no tutor should be quoting a required score, and no one should be promising a place anywhere. The useful work is simply knowing what gets compared against what, early enough to act on it.

Ministry of Education equivalency applies to the final certificate, not to the IGCSE

process.title: Send the entry form, or the four facts on it
process.description: The board, the syllabus code, the tier and the practical route. With those we can say within an hour whether a specialist in that exact paper is free in your slot. A tutor who quotes without asking for them has told you how closely they intend to work to your child's actual assessment, which is useful information at no cost.

process.title: Take the free diagnostic before comparing anything
process.description: One session, no commitment, ending in a written note of what is wrong and in what order to fix it. Use that document to choose between the five options on this page, including the ones that are not us. Families who decide the school's own intervention is sufficient have still got something from the hour.

process.title: Settle the tier question separately
process.description: If there is any doubt about Core against Extended, deal with it as its own piece of work in Year 10 rather than folding it into weekly lessons. Marked questions from both tiers' papers give a family something to take back to the school, and sometimes they confirm that the school was right, which is also worth knowing.

process.title: Fix the hour in Saudi time, and write down the exceptions
process.description: The slot is agreed in Arabia Standard Time against a Sunday-to-Thursday week, recorded in your local time so a tutor's clock change moves their hour rather than yours. We also agree in advance what happens during Ramadan, across the long summer break, and in the week of a school examination.

process.title: Expect the board, the script and the scheme after every session
process.description: The saved whiteboard, the marked written work and the published mark scheme it was marked against. Those three things make the arrangement checkable rather than reassuring. If any of them stops arriving, say so, because the first sign of a lesson drifting is a report that has marks in it one week and adjectives the next.

process.title: Review on the marks at the end of the term
process.description: We look at the mark trend rather than the impression and decide whether to continue, change tutor, change frequency, or stop. A wrong match in the first two or three lessons is changed at no cost. If no specialist is free for the code and slot you need, we say so instead of putting a generalist in front of your child.

whyPoints.title: The comparison is on the page, including where we lose
whyPoints.description: The school's own intervention, a group course, an in-home tutor, self-study and an online specialist each win somewhere specific, and this page says where. A family that reads it and chooses the group course has still been served. A provider unwilling to describe its competitors' advantages is describing a sales process rather than a service.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the code, the tier and the practical route
whyPoints.description: Cambridge is examined on defined papers, and two tutors who both teach Chemistry may be prepared for different assessments. We ask for the board, the syllabus code, the tier and the practical route before quoting, and we say plainly when nobody suitable is free rather than offering the nearest available person.

whyPoints.title: The lesson leaves evidence behind
whyPoints.description: The shared whiteboard is saved and sent, written work is marked against the published scheme and returned with it, and progress is reported as marks. A parent can check all three without watching a lesson, and may watch any lesson they like. A report with no marks in it tells you about a mood rather than a grade.

whyPoints.title: Built for a Sunday-to-Thursday week on a clock that never changes
whyPoints.description: Thursday evening here is the start of a weekend and the first slot to be lost; Saturday is the best block in the week for a whole paper. The Kingdom holds UTC+3 all year, so slots are recorded in Saudi local time and a tutor's seasonal clock change moves their hour, not yours.

whyPoints.title: A firm line on coursework
whyPoints.description: Where a Cambridge syllabus carries coursework, a tutor reads the student's own draft against the published criteria and returns questions. Nothing is written, redrafted or filled in on a student's behalf. Some of the cheapest offers in this market are cheap precisely because they do the other thing, which is malpractice rather than a discount.

whyPoints.title: Clear about what we are not
whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or partnership from Cambridge, Pearson, the Ministry of Education or the Education and Training Evaluation Commission, and is not connected to any school named here. There is no office in the Kingdom. No grade, score or university place is promised. What remains is a specialist, a syllabus and an hour that is kept.

faqs.question: How does a Cambridge tutor work through a past paper on screen without losing the student?
faqs.answer: The paper is opened on a shared whiteboard with the published mark scheme beside it, and the student writes rather than watches. The tutor works a question, then hands the next one over and stays quiet while it is attempted, which is the part that makes the hour useful. Annotations build up on the board as marks are identified, and the board is saved and sent afterwards. A session in which the tutor does all the writing has become a lecture, and the test for a parent is simply whose handwriting fills the saved file.

faqs.question: Are online Cambridge lessons recorded, and who is able to see the recording?
faqs.answer: Only where the family and the tutor have both agreed to it, and the answer should be given plainly before the first session rather than discovered later. Where a recording is made, the family receives it, and it is worth asking how long it is kept and who else can access it. Recordings are genuinely useful for a dense mathematics method a student will want to revisit, and less useful than families expect for discussion-based subjects. If a provider cannot answer this question clearly, that is itself the answer.

faqs.question: What happens if the connection drops in the middle of a Cambridge paper session?
faqs.answer: Agree the policy before the first lesson rather than after the first failure. The two reasonable arrangements are that the session pauses and resumes within the hour, or that the remaining time is rescheduled; what matters is that one of them is written down and that somebody tells you which happened. Intermittent connectivity is worth testing in the trial lesson, and a wired connection or a phone tethered as a backup resolves most of it. A tutor who treats a dropped lesson as the family's loss has told you about their terms.

faqs.question: Can a parent sit in on an online Cambridge IGCSE lesson?
faqs.answer: Yes, at any time and without arranging it in advance, and a tutor who objects has raised something that outweighs their profile. In practice most parents sit in once or twice early on and then stop, because the saved whiteboard and the marked script tell them more than listening does. Where a parent's presence changes a teenager's behaviour for the worse, the better compromise is to watch the first ten minutes and read the evidence afterwards rather than to withdraw oversight altogether.

faqs.question: How are chemistry mechanisms and graph work shared in an online lesson?
faqs.answer: On a shared whiteboard that both sides draw on with a mouse, a stylus or a finger. Mechanisms are drawn step by step rather than pasted in finished, which is the point: a student who watches a complete mechanism appear has learned nothing about constructing one. Graph work is done on an imported grid so axes, labels and a line of best fit are drawn by the student and marked as a paper would mark them. The board is saved, so the term produces a file of worked examples in the student's own hand.

faqs.question: Is a tablet enough for a Cambridge maths lesson, or is a laptop needed?
faqs.answer: A tablet with a stylus is genuinely good for mathematics and the sciences, often better than a laptop, because handwriting on a shared board is closer to writing on paper. What a tablet handles poorly is anything with two windows open at once, which includes working from a past paper while writing an answer. The practical arrangement many families settle on is a laptop for the call and the paper, with a tablet or paper beside it for the working, photographed and submitted afterwards.

faqs.question: How does a tutor mark a Cambridge script between lessons and return it?
faqs.answer: The student photographs or scans the script and submits it, the tutor marks it against the published mark scheme, and it comes back annotated with the scheme attached so the family can see what was being applied. The useful part is not the total but the pattern: the same two or three losses repeat across papers, and a running list of them is more actionable than a grade. Ask for the mark scheme every time. A marked script without the scheme beside it cannot be checked by anyone.

faqs.question: Is a Cambridge syllabus specialist worth paying more for than a good general science teacher?
faqs.answer: It depends on what is actually wrong. For content gaps, a strong general teacher at the ordinary rate is good value and the scarcity premium buys little. For a candidate who knows the material and keeps losing marks, the specialist premium is the whole point, because the losses are in the examined form: method not shown, axes unlabelled, a six-mark answer written as one paragraph. Diagnose first, buy content repair at the ordinary rate, and reserve the premium for the final year when form decides the grade.

faqs.question: What should a free trial lesson with a Cambridge tutor produce before we pay for anything?
faqs.answer: A document. A trial that is a pleasant conversation about goals has shown you the tutor is personable, which was never in doubt. A trial worth having works through material the student covered recently, marks something they have already written, and ends with a written note of what is wrong, in what order to fix it, and roughly how long each part takes. Ask for that note and keep it. If it says the student needs more practice, nothing was diagnosed and nothing should be bought.

faqs.question: Does a group Cambridge revision course ever beat one-to-one on value?
faqs.answer: For one specific student, yes: a candidate who is quietly under-answering and has no idea their answers are thin. A group supplies calibration against other candidates, which one-to-one structurally cannot, and courses advertised per course rather than per hour can be good value for past-paper volume. It fails on specificity, because three candidates with different gaps drift towards the middle of the group. The arrangement that works best is one-to-one teaching with occasional group paper sessions, and the diagnosis should come before the choice.

faqs.question: Why do Additional Mathematics tutors cost more than Extended Mathematics ones?
faqs.answer: Supply, not difficulty. Additional Mathematics introduces calculus and formal algebra a year early, and the people who teach it well are mostly teaching A Level or Diploma Higher Level mathematics instead, where the hours are steadier. That makes it the scarcest mainstream Cambridge specialism in this market. Negotiating rarely moves the figure; booking early in the year often secures a better tutor at the ordinary rate. If the subject matters for a sixth-form route, treat availability rather than price as the binding constraint.

faqs.question: Do we pay the same hourly rate for a tier-decision review as for a teaching lesson?
faqs.answer: A tier review is a short, defined piece of work rather than an open arrangement, and it is priced as such: typically a small number of sessions producing marked questions from both tiers' papers and a written view on which entry the evidence supports. It is worth buying on its own even if no weekly tuition follows, because a grade ceiling set by an entry form outweighs almost anything a year of lessons can achieve. Ask for the output in a form a head of department can read quickly.

faqs.question: Which documents from the Cambridge years are worth keeping for a Saudi university application?
faqs.answer: The statement of results and the certificate for every series sat, school transcripts and reports covering the same years, and confirmation of enrolment at each school attended. Equivalency, the mu'adalah decision, concerns the certificate a student finishes with, but the schooling record supporting it is assembled from all of these, and reconstructing them years later is slow. Keep digital copies as they arrive and ask your school's counsellor what their process has needed previously, since requirements are administered by the Ministry of Education rather than by schools.

faqs.question: Which Cambridge grades does a Saudi sixth form actually look at?
faqs.answer: Almost always the subject itself and mathematics, and often English as well, with the exact grades published by the school rather than set centrally. A school running Cambridge International AS and A Level will name a minimum grade in each subject a student wants to continue. A school running the IB Diploma uses the same grades to judge whether a student can be supported at Higher Level. Ask for the published requirements in Year 10, because they determine which subjects and tiers need protecting while that is still possible.

faqs.question: Does Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics at Extended tier satisfy an engineering route's requirements later?
faqs.answer: It is the entry that keeps the route open, and it is rarely sufficient on its own. Engineering routes ask for mathematics at the next level, A Level Mathematics or Diploma Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, and those courses assume Extended rather than Core. Additional Mathematics at IGCSE is the standard bridge and makes the first year of either noticeably less painful. Core tier closes the route quietly, which is why the tier decision in Year 10 deserves evidence rather than acceptance.

faqs.question: Do universities abroad treat Cambridge IGCSE differently from Edexcel International GCSE?
faqs.answer: Broadly no; both are recognised as qualifications at the same level, and admissions offices read the grades rather than the board. Where a difference appears it is usually in subject naming, since the two boards split English and the sciences differently, and an admissions system looking for a specific qualification occasionally cannot find its equivalent. The practical step is to check how a target university names the requirement and confirm that the student's certificate will show it, rather than assuming a board preference that generally does not exist.

cambridge-igcse-tutor.closingHeading: How to settle the comparison in one message
cambridge-igcse-tutor.closingBody: Send the board, the syllabus code, the tier and the practical route from the entry, plus the hour that works on a school night. We will tell you whether a specialist in that exact paper is free in that window, what it costs, and what the figure includes. If the honest answer is that the school's own intervention or a group course would serve you better, we will say so. The first lesson is free and diagnostic, and it ends with a written account of what is wrong and the order to fix it in. Everything is taught one-to-one over live video on Arabia Standard Time.

intro.heading: What counts as evidence, and who is awake to produce it
paragraphs: Start from the end. A family paying for teaching should be able to say, in writing, what changed. Four kinds of evidence do that job honestly. The first is an error-type list: not topics, but the specific recurring mistakes, such as an evaluate question answered as a description. The second is a question-by-question breakdown of a marked paper, which exposes pacing in a way a total never does. The third is movement on a criterion strand. The fourth is the student diagnosing their own errors unprompted.

Everything else sold in this market is a proxy for those four, and certification is the weakest proxy of all. No Saudi body licenses or certifies private tutors. The Ministry of Education licenses schools; school evaluation and accreditation run through the Education and Training Evaluation Commission. Examination boards appoint examiners to mark papers, which is a job rather than a credential about teaching. IB Gram claims no approval, accreditation or partnership from any of them, and a provider who does should be asked for the document.

That leaves one practical obstacle between a family and the evidence, and it is a clock. Teaching produces evidence only if the lessons actually happen, week after week, at a time a tired teenager can use. In the Kingdom that window is narrow: school runs Sunday to Thursday, Friday and Saturday are the weekend, and the usable hours sit between the end of the school run and the point where nothing more goes in. A slot that fights the week quietly stops happening. That is not a scheduling detail. It is the difference between four honest reviews of real evidence across a term and two cancelled lessons with an apology attached, which is why this page treats availability as a qualification rather than an administrative afterthought to be sorted out later.

This is where a tutor's own working week decides everything. Arabia Standard Time is UTC+3 and the Kingdom does not change its clocks. A tutor in India works a Monday to Saturday week two and a half hours ahead; a tutor in the United Kingdom is three hours behind in their winter and two in their summer, so an unpinned slot moves twice a year without anyone deciding to move it. Sunday, a full school day here, is a weekend or a quiet day in much of the world.

Lessons for Saudi families are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. No tutor is sent to a Saudi address, and in-home visits are something we provide only in India. The advantage for the evidence argument is specific: a tutor can be matched for genuine Sunday-to-Thursday availability in a scarce Higher Level subject, rather than for living close enough to drive to the house on a Tuesday.

sections.heading: The four kinds of evidence worth paying for
paragraphs: An error-type list is the first and the most useful. It names recurring mistakes rather than weak topics: a definition paraphrased instead of stated, an evaluate question answered descriptively, units dropped in the final line, working compressed so that method marks cannot be awarded. A list of four or five such errors, dated, is a far better record than a topic checklist, because errors are what a mark scheme actually penalises and they are countable from one piece of work to the next.

The second is a question-by-question breakdown of a timed paper. A total tells a family almost nothing; the breakdown tells them whether marks were lost evenly, lost at the end, or lost in one question type. That distinction decides the whole plan. Evenly spread losses point at content. Losses concentrated at the end point at pacing. Losses in one question type point at a command term. Any tutor can produce this, and a tutor who will not is declining to be measured.

The third and fourth are slower. Movement on a named criterion strand between two pieces of internally assessed work is the evidence that matters in the middle years and in any investigation-based component. And the last is the one families underrate: the student beginning to diagnose their own errors without being asked. When a teenager says the question wanted a comparison and they gave two descriptions, the teaching has transferred, and the support can start reducing.

sections.heading: Why a tutor's own working week decides whether this works
paragraphs: The usable teaching window in the Kingdom is small. School runs Sunday to Thursday, the run home finishes somewhere between four and six depending on the district, and after about half past eight a tired student stops absorbing anything. That is a window of roughly three hours, five evenings a week, and school homework has first claim on it. A tutor has to fit inside that window every week, not occasionally, or the evidence never accumulates.

A tutor's own country decides whether they can. Arabia Standard Time is UTC+3 with no seasonal change, so the Kingdom's clock is fixed while others move around it. The table below sets common tutor locations against the Saudi week. The pattern it shows is that the time difference is rarely the real problem; the working week is. Sunday is a full school day here and a weekend day in much of Europe and the Americas, which is exactly when many families most want a lesson.

There are two fixes and both are mechanical. Record the slot as a Kingdom local time, confirmed in writing by tutor and family, so that whoever's clocks change absorbs the change themselves. And ask directly, before matching, whether the tutor teaches on Sundays and how late they will work in their own evening. A tutor who says yes in principle and then cannot hold the slot in the second month has cost a family a term, which is the one thing a term cannot afford.
