sections.heading: Sunday and Thursday are not interchangeable
paragraphs: Within the Sunday to Thursday week, the choice of evening changes what a lesson can do. Sunday is the first school day. Nothing has been set yet, the student is rested, and new technique goes in well; the drawback is that there may be no recent marked work to read. Thursday is the last school day with a two-day break after it, which makes it excellent for setting substantial written work and poor for correcting an error that needs checking quickly.

Midweek evenings are the workhorses, because by Monday or Tuesday there is marked school work to look at and the week has not yet collapsed under homework. Wednesday often turns out to be the worst evening in practice, since assessments cluster late in the week and a student arrives already spent. None of this is universal, which is why the honest version is to try two evenings in the first month and keep the one the evidence prefers.

Two Kingdom-specific adjustments matter. Shortened school days during Ramadan move the whole evening, and the right response is to shift the slot rather than pause for a month, because a paused month in a Diploma year is expensive to recover. And school calendars differ: Ministry of Education schools run a two-semester year while most international schools run three terms, so holiday weeks have to be taken from the student's own school calendar rather than a general one. Download it once at the start of the year and agree the pauses from it.

sections.heading: What certification exists in tutoring, and what none of it proves
paragraphs: Four things get described as certification in this market, and it is worth separating them. A subject degree says somebody studied the discipline. A teaching qualification says they were trained to teach, usually in one national system. School-based professional development says their employer invested in them. An appointment to mark papers for an examination board says the board judged them reliable at applying one mark scheme. All four are real. None is a licence to tutor, and none is issued by anyone who inspects tutoring.

What does not exist is a certificate saying somebody is an approved IB tutor. Schools, not tutors, are authorised to run the Diploma, and that authorisation belongs to the school. Private tutors in Saudi Arabia are not registered, licensed or ranked by any public body, and the two regulators a family will encounter deal with schools: the Ministry of Education issues school licences, and the Education and Training Evaluation Commission handles evaluation and accreditation, including the approval of international accreditation bodies.

So the useful question is narrower than certified or not. It is which syllabus, at which level, for how many cohorts, and with what marking exposure. A teacher who has taught Higher Level Chemistry for six cohorts and marked for a board knows which phrasing is paid for; a certificate cannot convey that, and a confident claim about it can be checked in one conversation. The next section is how to run that conversation without needing to take anything on trust.

sections.heading: Verifying a claim about a tutor in one conversation
paragraphs: Start with the syllabus rather than the subject. Ask which syllabus and level the tutor teaches, how many cohorts they have taken through it, and what changed in the course most recently. A teacher who has lived with a syllabus answers the third question immediately and often with mild irritation. Somebody who has read the specification recently will answer it in general terms, which is the tell. This takes about a minute and is the single most efficient check available.

Then test mark-scheme knowledge with the student's own work. Hand over a question that lost marks and ask what the scheme wanted. The useful answer names the command term, describes the structure the examiner is paid to reward, and usually points at a phrase in the student's answer that was nearly right. Re-teaching the topic instead is a weak answer, because the school already taught the topic. This is not a trick question; it is the job.

Finally, ask about marking and about limits. For marking: which papers, and how recently, since mark schemes evolve. For limits: what the tutor will and will not do with a draft of assessed work. A clear boundary offered before being asked is the strongest signal in this market, and it is the opposite of what the essay mills in the same search results provide. Ask also what happens if the match is wrong after three sessions, and which of the written records would transfer to a different tutor.

sections.heading: Academic honesty: the limit, stated plainly
paragraphs: Internally assessed components, the Extended Essay, the Theory of Knowledge essay and the Personal Project all have to be the student's own work, and schools require declarations to that effect. A tutor working on any of them operates inside a narrow boundary. Explaining what a criterion strand is asking for is teaching. Questioning a research design before data collection is teaching. Saying that a section does not yet answer the strand it is aimed at is feedback. Producing any part of the text is not.

Phrased as a rule: a tutor may comment on, question and teach around a student's own draft, and may never supply words that end up in the submitted work. That holds for a sentence as much as for a chapter. It also rules out proofreading that silently fixes argument rather than flagging it, because the line a school cares about is whether the thinking is the student's. Any provider offering to produce a component is offering malpractice, and the consequence lands on the student.

The practical protection for a family is a record. Keep dated notes of what each session covered, keep the student's own successive drafts, and let the school's supervisor stay the person who signs off the process. Where a school asks questions, that trail answers them. Online sessions make this easier rather than harder, because the work is shared on screen from the student's own file and the session notes exist in writing by default.

sections.heading: Changing tutor without losing the evidence
paragraphs: Matches fail sometimes, and the honest version of this market admits it. The two common reasons are availability and fit. Availability failure shows up in the second month, when a tutor who agreed to Sunday evenings starts asking to move them, usually because their own working week does not really contain that slot. Fit failure shows up sooner: a student who understands everything in the session and cannot start the homework is being taught at rather than taught.

What makes a change cheap is the evidence trail. If an error-type list and a dated set of marked work exist, a new tutor starts from the diagnosis instead of rebuilding it, and the family can tell within two sessions whether the second match is better. Without that record, changing tutor means paying for the same diagnostic twice. This is the strongest practical argument for insisting on written evidence from the first session, before anyone needs it.

A change should also be a decision rather than a drift. Agree in advance what would trigger one: no movement on the error-type list after two reviews, repeated requests to move the slot, or a student who stops wanting to attend. Those three are observable and do not require anyone to judge a tutor's competence. Keeping the subject, the level and the syllabus fixed while changing the person means the brief stays the same and only the match moves, which is the cheapest version of this problem a family can arrange.

faqs.question: Which topics in Mathematics Analysis and Approaches most often need outside teaching rather than more practice?
faqs.answer: Proof, the Higher Level option topics, and anything where algebraic manipulation is the hidden step. More practice helps where a method is known and slow; it does nothing where the student cannot start. The tell is a blank page rather than a wrong answer. Evidence of repair is the student attempting a question they would previously have skipped, which shows up in a question-by-question breakdown before it shows in a total.

faqs.question: Why do strong Chemistry students lose marks on the energetics calculations?
faqs.answer: Usually presentation rather than chemistry. Energetics questions award method marks for stated steps, and a student who works it mentally and writes one line loses those marks even when the final figure is right. Sign conventions are the second culprit. Setting the working out so each step is visible protects most of the marks against an arithmetic slip, which is a habit worth building early rather than in the weeks before a series.

faqs.question: Which Physics definitions are examined most strictly, and how is that taught over video?
faqs.answer: The ones with a precise published form, where a paraphrase scores nothing: quantities defined as a rate, per unit something, or relative to a stated reference. Over video it is taught by comparison on a shared screen, with the student's own written definition beside the examiner's wording so the missing clause becomes obvious. Doing that four or five times usually fixes the habit, because the pattern of what gets omitted repeats.

faqs.question: What makes a six-mark Biology answer score full marks rather than four?
faqs.answer: Answering the verb. Most six-mark losses come from describing twice where the question asked for a comparison, or listing features where it asked for a mechanism. The second cause is breadth without development: six short points where three developed ones were wanted. Reading the mark scheme beside the student's own answer makes this visible faster than any explanation, and it is the kind of error that belongs on an error-type list.

faqs.question: Where does an Economics candidate lose the evaluation marks in a Paper 1 essay?
faqs.answer: In the last paragraph, usually by asserting a conclusion instead of weighing one. Evaluation marks are awarded for considering assumptions, short against long run, or the limits of the model used. A technically accurate essay with a confident ending frequently sits in the middle band. Diagram accuracy decides the lower band, so a student losing marks in both places is dealing with two separate problems, not one.

faqs.question: If no body certifies IB tutors, what document is actually worth asking to see?
faqs.answer: Nothing on its own, which is the honest answer. A subject degree, a teaching qualification and a letter of appointment to mark for a board are all real documents, and none of them says whether this tutor can teach your child's syllabus. What is worth asking for instead is specific: the syllabus and level taught, the number of cohorts, and the most recent papers marked. Those claims can be tested in conversation.

faqs.question: Does it matter whether a tutor has taught inside the Kingdom rather than elsewhere?
faqs.answer: Less than families expect for the subject, more than they expect for the logistics. The syllabus is identical wherever it is taught, so subject knowledge does not depend on location. What local experience brings is an understanding of the Sunday to Thursday week, how school calendars differ here, and how shortened days during Ramadan move an evening. A tutor without that can be told; a tutor who resists being told is the real problem.

faqs.question: Should a tutor be a serving school teacher or a full-time tutor, given the Sunday to Thursday week?
faqs.answer: Both work, and the week decides which. A serving teacher inside the Kingdom has the same Sunday to Thursday pattern as your child, which means their free hours are the same evenings everybody else wants. A full-time tutor abroad has more flexibility but may not treat Sunday as a working day. Ask the availability question before the credential question, because an excellent tutor who cannot hold the slot delivers nothing.

faqs.question: How do we check a claim of marking experience without a verifiable statistic?
faqs.answer: By asking what marking taught them. Somebody who has marked a paper will say which question candidates answered badly, which phrasing earned the mark and which near-miss did not, usually with a specific example. Somebody who has not will speak in generalities about standards. Ask which papers and roughly how recently, since mark schemes change. A claim nobody can audit is still testable by whether the detail behind it exists.

faqs.question: What happens to the evidence trail when a family changes tutor after six weeks?
faqs.answer: It transfers, if it exists in writing. The opening diagnostic, the error-type list and the marked work give a second tutor the diagnosis without repeating it, and a family can judge the new match within two sessions. Where none of that was recorded, the change costs another month of diagnostics. Agreeing in advance what would trigger a change, such as no movement after two reviews, keeps the decision from becoming personal.

faqs.question: How many drafts of an internal assessment can a tutor formally comment on?
faqs.answer: The school sets the limit on formal supervisory feedback, and the Diploma coordinator is the person to ask, because it differs by component. A tutor is not the supervisor and does not replace one. What a tutor can do at any stage is explain what a criterion strand asks for and say whether a section answers it, which is teaching rather than supervision. Keep the school informed that outside support is in place.

faqs.question: Which drafts and notes protect a student if a school asks how much help an internal assessment had?
faqs.answer: Successive drafts kept with their dates, and dated notes of what each tutoring session covered. That pair answers almost any question a school asks, because it shows the thinking developing in one person's hands over time. Online sessions help here, since the work is shared from the student's own file and session notes are written by default. The school's supervisor remains the person who signs off the process.

faqs.question: How does an Extended Essay supervisor at school differ from a tutor working on the same essay?
faqs.answer: The supervisor is appointed by the school, holds the formal meetings, signs the reflections and is accountable for the process. A tutor has no role in any of that. A tutor can teach research question design, explain what the criteria reward, and ask the questions that expose a weak argument, all on the student's own draft. Where the two give different advice, the supervisor's view governs, because the supervisor signs.

faqs.question: What does a school do if it suspects malpractice, and how does online tutoring stay clear of it?
faqs.answer: Schools investigate internally and report to the board, and outcomes can reach the whole Diploma rather than one component. Staying clear of it is procedural rather than a matter of good intentions: the student writes every word, the tutor comments and questions, drafts are kept with their dates, and the school is told that outside support exists. A provider offering to produce the work is offering a risk the student carries alone.

certified-ib-tutor.closingHeading: Ask for the evidence, then check the clock
certified-ib-tutor.closingBody: Book a free trial lesson with recently marked work, and leave with an opening error-type list rather than a promise. Then settle the unglamorous question: which Sunday to Thursday evenings are genuinely free after the school run, and does the tutor's own working week contain them. Those two steps answer the certification question better than any document could. Lessons run online, one-to-one, over live video on Arabia Standard Time.

intro.heading: An IGCSE grade comes from a specification, not from a certificate on a wall
paragraphs: An IGCSE grade is produced by a specification, a set of components and a tier, and everything else is commentary. The specification names the content and the assessment objectives. The components are the papers and, in the sciences, the practical or alternative-to-practical element. The tier, where a subject is tiered, sets the ceiling before any paper is marked. A tutor who cannot describe those three things for your child's subject is not in a position to plan anything, whatever qualifications they hold.

That is why the word certified does less work here than it appears to. No organisation certifies IGCSE tutors. Private and international schools in the Kingdom are licensed by the Ministry of Education; school evaluation and accreditation run through the Education and Training Evaluation Commission (ETEC), which also approves the international accreditation bodies schools use. Boards run their own centre approval for the schools that enter candidates. None of those processes reaches an individual tutor, and IB Gram claims no status from any of them.

What a family can verify is concrete. The syllabus code. The tier. The component list. Whether the tutor has taught or marked that specification rather than the subject in general. Whether they can say, without checking, which paper carries the practical marks and what a four-mark explain question needs. Those questions take ten minutes and they discriminate better than any badge, because they test the thing the grade actually depends on rather than the thing a provider finds easy to print. None of this requires expertise on the family's part. The statement of entry is a one-page document, and a tutor either recognises what is printed on it or does not, which is the whole of the test. A provider that steers the conversation back to credentials instead is answering a different question.

There is one certificate in this system that does get certified, and it is the student's rather than the teacher's. A foreign or international school certificate needs an equivalency decision from the Ministry of Education before a Saudi university treats it as equivalent to the Saudi secondary certificate, and that applies to an IB Diploma, to A Levels and to an American high school diploma alike. Alongside it sit Qudurat and Tahsili, run by the Education and Training Evaluation Commission through its National Center for Assessment.

Lessons at IB Gram are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, on Arabia Standard Time and around the Sunday-to-Thursday school week. We do not send a tutor to a Saudi address; home visits are a service we offer only in India. The sections below work outwards from the assessment structure: what the components are, who certifies what, how to test a claim in one conversation, where the marks sit, the university end of the system, and what changes when a student switches board.

sections.heading: The IGCSE assessment structure, which is what any claim gets checked against
paragraphs: Start with the document the grade comes from. A specification lists the content, the assessment objectives and the components, and it is public. Cambridge subjects carry a syllabus code: Mathematics 0580, International Mathematics 0607, Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620, Biology 0610. Pearson Edexcel uses its own codes for the same subject names. The code matters because two subjects with identical titles can have different papers, different tiering and different coursework rules, and a tutor who has taught one has not automatically taught the other.

Grading differs between the boards, and the difference is not cosmetic. Cambridge IGCSE runs A* to G, with many subjects tiered: Core caps at C whatever the candidate scores on the day, and Extended reaches A*. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE uses the 9 to 1 scale instead. A parent comparing one child's results with a sibling's at a different school in the same Saudi city may be comparing two scales that do not map neatly onto each other at any point.

Components are the other half of the structure. In the Cambridge sciences a candidate sits either a practical examination or an alternative-to-practical paper, and which of the two is entered is a school decision rather than a student one. Coursework survives in some subjects on one board and not on the other. The table sets the main checkpoints side by side. Take your own answers from the statement of entry rather than from this page, because the entry is what the board marks against.

sections.heading: Who certifies what in the Kingdom, and who certifies nobody
paragraphs: Four different things get approved in this system and none of them is a tutor. A school is licensed by the Ministry of Education to operate. School evaluation and accreditation run through the Education and Training Evaluation Commission, which also handles the approval of the international accreditation bodies that schools use. A school entering candidates goes through a board's own centre approval. And a student's certificate goes through equivalency before a Saudi university treats it as equivalent to the national one.

Nothing in that chain certifies the person teaching your child in a weekly online lesson. There is no national tutor register, no board-issued tutor licence and no evaluation body that inspects private tuition. A provider describing itself as approved, accredited or licensed by a ministry, a commission or an examination board is describing something that does not exist. IB Gram holds none of those statuses and claims none, which is a dull sentence to publish and a useful one for a family to be able to read.

What that means in practice is that the verification work falls to the family, and it is easier than it sounds. School-level licensing is a matter of record and the school will confirm it. Centre status shows up on the statement of entry. Equivalency is a published process at the Ministry with its own steps. And a tutor's competence is tested in a trial lesson against the specification, which is the only one of those four checks that reaches the thing you are actually paying for.

sections.heading: What a tutor's qualifications tell you, and the three questions that test them
paragraphs: A degree in the subject tells you the tutor studied it beyond school level. A teaching qualification tells you they were trained to manage a class and plan a course. Marking or examining experience tells you they have seen how a scheme credits an answer. All three are worth having and none of them is specific to the specification your child sits. That last gap is where most mismatches in this market come from, and it is the one a family can close in a single conversation before paying anything.

Three questions do most of the work. First: which syllabus code and tier is my child entered for, and what does that entry include? A tutor who teaches the specification will answer and then ask to see the statement of entry. Second: which component does this student lose most marks on, and how would you find out? A convincing answer involves timed past questions rather than a discussion. Third: what would you do in the first hour, and what would I receive afterwards?

Two answers should slow a family down. One is a claim of accreditation, approval or partnership involving a board or a ministry, because no such status exists for tutors and the claim itself tells you something about the provider. The other is an offer to take on an assessed component. A tutor teaches the skills a coursework or portfolio task assesses and gives feedback on a draft the student has written; nobody should be writing any part of it. The second offer is more common here than it should be.

sections.heading: Component by component: where the marks sit and what a specialist notices
paragraphs: Marks are lost in predictable places, and a specialist can name them before meeting the student. In Mathematics the losses sit in method shown badly and in algebra used inside other topics rather than in arithmetic itself. In Chemistry they sit in unbalanced equations, missing state symbols and mole arithmetic done at speed. In Biology the strictly marked definitions reject a near-miss paraphrase. In Physics the alternative paper tests experimental method, measurement precision and the sources of error, none of which more content revision touches.

Command terms sit underneath all of it. The scheme pays for the operation the paper named, so a description written where an explanation was asked for collects the content marks and loses the reasoning ones. Students rarely know this is happening, because the answer felt right and the handwriting filled the space. It is teachable in a few sessions, and for a student who already knows the content it is the highest-yield work a tutor can do with the hour.

The extended-response questions are where a strong candidate still loses a grade. A six-mark answer needs a structure: the point, the mechanism, and the link back to the context the question gave. A student who has never been shown that structure writes a paragraph of accurate material and collects half the marks available. A tutor who marks written work between lessons will see this in the second week. One who only talks for an hour each week will not see it at all.

sections.heading: Equivalency, Qudurat and Tahsili: the certificate that does get certified
paragraphs: This is the part of the system almost no competing page explains, and it matters more than any claim about a tutor. A foreign or international school certificate needs an equivalency decision from the Ministry of Education before a Saudi university will treat it as equivalent to the Saudi secondary certificate. The requirement applies to an IB Diploma, to A Levels and to an American high school diploma. IGCSE sits below that level, so the decision usually attaches to the qualification above it rather than to the IGCSE certificate itself.

Alongside equivalency sit two tests. Qudurat, the General Aptitude Test, is run by the Education and Training Evaluation Commission through its National Center for Assessment, and it examines verbal and quantitative reasoning rather than syllabus content. Tahsili, the Achievement Test, covers science-stream subjects and its content follows the Saudi national curriculum. That last detail is the one international-curriculum families need to hear: the material overlaps with what an IGCSE or Diploma student has studied, and the framing does not.

Universities publish their own admission criteria combining school grades with those tests, and the weightings differ by university and by programme. We publish no threshold and no formula, because third-party sites disagree with each other and the only reliable source is the university's own published criteria. Some universities also state a maximum age for the certificate they will accept. The practical advice is to read the criteria in the year before applying, and to treat an IGCSE subject list as the first decision that shapes the options.

sections.heading: Switching board or system part-way through, and what has to be re-checked
paragraphs: Families move between schools inside the Kingdom and arrive into it from elsewhere, and a change of school can mean a change of board. The content usually survives the move; the component list often does not. A student switching between Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel part-way through Year 10 keeps most of what they have been taught and inherits a different paper structure, a different grade scale and possibly a different coursework requirement. That is an administrative problem before it becomes a teaching one.

Three things need re-checking straight away. Which board and syllabus code the new school will enter, because the old code stops mattering from that point. Whether any coursework or portfolio work already completed transfers, which is a question for the new school's examinations officer rather than for a tutor. And whether a tier has been assumed rather than decided: a student placed in a Core set on arrival may well be an Extended candidate, and the entry deadline decides how long that stays open.

Students arriving from a Saudi national-curriculum school, or from a CBSE or ICSE school, face a different version of the same work. The mathematics usually transfers well. The written answers do not, because the new scheme rewards a structure the old one never asked for. Expect calculations to look fine and extended answers to lag for a term. That gap closes with marked written work rather than with more content teaching, and it closes faster when somebody names it in the first month.

sections.heading: Starting out: the diagnostic, the first month, and what a report should prove
paragraphs: The first session should produce evidence rather than reassurance. Two or three past questions on taught content, sat to time and marked live against the published scheme, tell a tutor whether the problem is content, method or command terms. The output is a short ordered list of components with the recoverable ones first. A family that receives that list has something to measure against later, which is the entire point of doing it before any teaching starts rather than after a month of it.

A first month is long enough to see three things. The student can name the command terms in their subject and say what each one demands. Marked work shows fewer lost method marks on the same question type. And the written note after each lesson refers to components and papers rather than to effort and attitude. A grade usually moves a term behind those three signals, so judging the first month by a grade is judging it far too early to be useful.

A report should prove something. The useful version names the component covered, what the student could not do at the start of the hour, what they can do now, and what has been set before the next session. A report saying the lesson went well proves nothing and could be written without any teaching having happened. If the match is wrong after two or three sessions, say so early: changing tutor in the first month costs a fortnight, and changing in the final term costs a great deal more.

faqs.question: Is one hour a week enough for a tiered IGCSE subject, or does it need two?
faqs.answer: One hour plus marked work is usually enough through Year 10, because the limiting factor is how much independent practice a student can complete and have corrected. Two hours start to earn their place when a tier change is being attempted, when a component has never been taught, or in the weeks before a series. Four hours a week on one subject almost always produces less than two, because nothing gets finished between sessions.

faqs.question: What time do online IGCSE lessons usually start for a family in the Eastern Province?
faqs.answer: Most settle between five and eight in the evening, Arabia Standard Time. Families commuting between Dammam, Al Khobar and Dhahran often need the later end of that window, because the school run across the cluster can run long. Agree the time in Saudi local terms and confirm it against the tutor's own working week, since a tutor outside the Gulf may count a Sunday evening as part of their weekend.

faqs.question: Can a student keep the same IGCSE tutor if the family moves to another Gulf country?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, because the lesson is delivered over live video rather than tied to an address. What changes is the clock. Most Gulf states sit within an hour of Arabia Standard Time, so the slot may shift slightly, and a move further afield needs the time re-agreed. The more important check is whether the new school uses the same board and component list, because that decides whether the teaching plan still applies.

faqs.question: How many weeks' notice does a permanent change of IGCSE slot need?
faqs.answer: Two to three weeks is reasonable for a permanent move, and more than that for a scarce subject. A tutor holding several fixed hours can rearrange two students quite easily; releasing a popular evening hour and asking for it back later rarely works, because the hour is taken quickly. Temporary swaps for an examination week or a school trip are usually straightforward with a few days' notice.

faqs.question: Do IGCSE lessons continue through the midyear break?
faqs.answer: That is a family decision, and the answer depends on the year group. A Year 10 student can pause with little cost. A Year 11 student with a weak component, or a November candidate, generally should not, because the break sits at the point where technique work pays most. If you pause, agree in writing whether the slot is held, since a mid-year gap is long enough for an evening hour to be reallocated.

faqs.question: What has to be re-checked when a student changes school inside the Kingdom mid-course?
faqs.answer: The board, the syllabus code, the tier and the component list, in that order. A move between two licensed international schools in the same city can still mean a different board and a different paper structure. Ask the new school's examinations officer what it will enter and whether any completed coursework transfers. Until those answers arrive, a tutor is planning against a specification the student may not actually be sitting.

faqs.question: Does a student moving from an MoE school need to repeat a year to enter IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Not usually, though the admitting school decides. The common outcome is entry into the same year group with support in subject English rather than a repeated year. The work that follows is mostly linguistic and structural: reading a question written in technical English, and writing an answer in the shape a mark scheme rewards. The underlying mathematics is often stronger than the new school expects.

faqs.question: If a new school uses a different board, does the old board's coursework still count?
faqs.answer: Rarely, and never automatically. Coursework is submitted by the centre that enters the candidate, so work completed for another board under another specification normally cannot be carried across. The examinations officer at the new school is the person who can say what is accepted and what has to be produced again. Ask before the first tutoring session, because the answer changes what the hours should be spent on.

faqs.question: How long does it take a student to stop writing answers in the old system's style?
faqs.answer: About a term of marked written work, in most cases. Recognition comes quickly and habit comes slowly: a student can explain what an explain question wants within two sessions and still default to describing under time pressure for weeks. The fix is volume with correction, which means written answers going back and forth rather than more teaching. Progress shows up first on four-mark questions and last on six-mark ones.

faqs.question: Is it better to self-study one IGCSE subject the new school does not offer?
faqs.answer: It can work, but the entry is the obstacle rather than the teaching. A candidate has to be entered by a centre, so the first question is whether any school will enter them for that subject and on what terms. Where that is settled, a weekly tutor plus a strict written plan can cover a specification. Where it is not, the hours are being spent on a qualification nobody has agreed to award.

faqs.question: What should the first written report from a tutor prove rather than describe?
faqs.answer: That something changed in the hour. The useful report names the component, says what the student could not do at the start, what they could do by the end, and what has been set before the next session. Anything that describes attitude, effort or enthusiasm without naming a paper or a question type is a description rather than evidence, and it cannot be checked against the diagnostic list.

faqs.question: How is a target grade set honestly at the start of IGCSE support?
faqs.answer: From evidence rather than ambition. A diagnostic produces a current working level, and the honest target is the next grade up with the components that would deliver it named explicitly. No tutor can promise a grade, and a provider who offers one is selling something they cannot deliver. A target set that way is useful because it can be checked against marked work every few weeks instead of only at the end.

faqs.question: What should a parent see in the first four sessions that shows the match is right?
faqs.answer: Four things. A diagnostic list that names components rather than topics in general. Written work going back marked, with the mark scheme visible. Notes that use the language of the specification. And a student who can explain what they got wrong rather than only that they got it wrong. If three of the four are missing after a month, raise it rather than waiting for a report.

faqs.question: How is homework set and checked between online IGCSE sessions?
faqs.answer: Normally as a timed set of past questions, sent after the lesson and returned before the next one, marked against the published scheme with the lost marks annotated. The volume matters less than the correction: unmarked practice teaches a student to repeat whatever they already do. Where a student writes on paper, a photograph of the script is enough for a tutor to mark and return it before the next hour.

dammam.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach the Eastern Province timetable: Diploma Programme subjects at Higher and Standard Level, Middle Years Programme courses, and Cambridge and Edexcel International GCSE papers. Each is matched to a Dammam student by syllabus and level rather than by location, because the specialist a family needs is rarely the one living nearest.

intro.heading: Start from where your child is in the year, not from a price list
paragraphs: The useful first question is not what tutoring costs in Dammam. It is where your child sits in the school year right now, because that decides what is still recoverable and what has already been banked. A student three weeks into the first Diploma year has two full years of assessment ahead and almost nothing locked in. A student in the second Diploma year has Internal Assessment deadlines either met or missed, predicted grades forming, and a university application that will be built on whatever the next two terms produce. Those are different problems, and they need different weekly commitments and different tutors.

Dammam adds a second variable. The Eastern Province capital is a wide, administratively busy city, and international enrolment is spread across it rather than concentrated in one or two compounds. Plenty of families living in Al Faisaliyah, Al Rakah or Al Shatea drive their children to school in Dhahran or Al Khobar and are not home until late afternoon. The hours left for a lesson are narrow, and they narrow further in the second Diploma year when Internal Assessment drafts start competing with homework. Knowing that in advance is the difference between a schedule that holds for a term and one that collapses in the third week.

Work forward from the year group and the endgame appears quickly. A Diploma, or an International GCSE and A Level route taken in the Eastern Province, is a foreign certificate. A Saudi university will want an equivalency decision — mu'adalah — from the Ministry of Education before it treats that certificate as equal to the Saudi secondary certificate. Most families meet that requirement late, in the term when applications are due, and discover at the same time that Qudurat and Tahsili are sat through Qiyas under the Education and Training Evaluation Commission, and that Tahsili content follows the Saudi national curriculum rather than theirs. None of it is difficult. It is simply earlier than it looks.

IB Gram teaches Dammam students one-to-one over live video. We do not run home visits in Dammam or anywhere else in the Kingdom; in-home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. That is a deliberate choice rather than a limitation. The pool of people in the Dammam, Al Khobar and Dhahran conurbation who have actually taught Mathematics AA HL or Edexcel International GCSE Chemistry to examination standard is small, and a family restricted to that pool often ends up with a willing generalist. Over video the geographic constraint disappears, and the constraint that replaces it — a workable hour on Arabia Standard Time — is one a family can solve.

The rest of this page is ordered the way the school year is ordered: what the term you are in has to achieve, what the examination series and entry windows demand, what the equivalency and Qiyas steps need from you, what the Eastern Province school belt can and cannot staff, and what this market charges to fill the gap. The money section is specific and it names who publishes each figure. It is just not first, because an hourly rate only means something once you know how many weeks you are buying and what those weeks have to deliver.

dammam.programmesIntro: Four routes account for almost every Dammam student who needs outside teaching: the two IB programmes that run before the Diploma, the Diploma itself, and the two International GCSE boards the Eastern Province's British-curriculum schools use. Each has a different assessment shape, so each needs a different kind of help.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The Primary Years Programme is organised around transdisciplinary units of inquiry rather than separate subject syllabuses, and it closes with the Exhibition in the final primary year. There are no external examinations, which is why families often read a flat report as nothing to act on. The three signals worth watching are written fluency in English, security with number facts, and whether a child can hold an extended line of reasoning across a page.
programmes.countryNote: In Dammam the primary question is usually about the move ahead rather than the present. A child who will cross into a Dhahran or Al Khobar school for Middle Years work is also crossing into a longer commute and a much heavier written load. Building writing stamina and arithmetic fluency during the primary years costs far less time than repairing them in Year 9.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The Middle Years Programme runs through Years 7 to 11 and assesses against four criteria per subject, each marked out of 8 and reported on a 1-7 scale. Mathematics, the sciences and Individuals and Societies all carry a criterion for investigating and one for communicating, so a student who knows the content but cannot structure a conclusion loses marks that look like subject weakness. The Personal Project in the final year is the first genuinely independent piece of work most students attempt.
programmes.countryNote: Eastern Province families often meet the Middle Years Programme at a school that runs it well to Year 9 and then expects students to choose a Diploma or an International GCSE route. Dammam students heading for Cambridge or Edexcel papers need the examination technique the MYP criteria do not drill: timed recall, mark allocations read as instructions, and command terms taken literally.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The Diploma Programme is six subjects — three at Higher Level, three at Standard — plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Subject grades run 1-7, so 42 points come from subjects and up to three more from the Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay matrix, giving 45. Higher Level courses carry more teaching hours, an additional paper in several subjects, and topics with no Standard Level equivalent. Internal Assessment is marked in school and moderated by the IB.
programmes.countryNote: Dammam students sitting the Diploma almost always do so at a school in Dhahran, Al Khobar or Jubail, which means an outside tutor has to work with that school's scheme of work and its Internal Assessment deadlines rather than a generic plan. It also means the Diploma Programme coordinator in another city holds the real dates, and a family should treat that office as the single source of truth.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Cambridge International GCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE are separate qualifications with separate syllabus codes, separate papers and separate grading practice, even where the subject name is identical. Cambridge tiers several subjects into Core and Extended and caps the Core grade; Edexcel runs most International GCSEs untiered at a single level. A two-year course usually ends in the June series, with the November series available for resits and for November-entry candidates.
programmes.countryNote: The Eastern Province's British-curriculum schools are concentrated in Dhahran and Al Khobar, so a Dammam family's board is often decided by the school they can get a place at rather than by preference. That matters for tutoring: a tutor has to know the board and the code, because practising Cambridge 0620 papers for an Edexcel 4CH1 entry wastes half the practice.

dammam.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma Programme subjects Dammam families ask for most, with the part of each course that actually decides the grade. A tutor who knows the subject but not the assessment is the commonest and most expensive mistake in this market.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The proof-heavy route, and the one most engineering and mathematics degrees expect at Higher Level. Higher Level adds proof by induction, complex numbers in polar form, vectors and a far longer calculus strand. Marks go on method presented as a legible argument, so a correct final answer with no visible working is a part-mark answer.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics-led and calculator-active, with modelling at its centre. Higher Level carries a substantial statistics and probability component plus graph theory. Students who switch here from Analysis and Approaches usually under-rate the writing: a modelling answer has to interpret the number in context, and an uninterpreted result loses the final marks.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Paper 1 is multiple choice, Paper 2 is structured and extended response, and Higher Level carries additional topics with no Standard Level equivalent. The reliable loss points are unit and significant-figure discipline, graph gradients read without checking axes, and definitions given loosely where the mark scheme wants exact wording.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms carry most of the difficulty, and the data booklet is only useful to a student who has practised with it. Higher Level extends into entropy, Gibbs free energy and more demanding organic pathways. Most lost marks are state symbols, incomplete equations and explanations that describe rather than explain.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The content volume is the trap. Command terms decide the mark here more sharply than in any other science: outline, describe, explain and evaluate each want a different shape of answer, and a student who writes everything they know about a topic is paid for very little of it.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams are the grammar of this subject. A correctly labelled and correctly shifted diagram carries marks that no amount of prose recovers, and the Higher Level paper adds quantitative work. The Internal Assessment commentaries need real published articles with enough substance to apply a named concept to.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tool-driven: Ansoff, BCG, break-even, investment appraisal. Marks come from applying a tool to the stimulus case rather than defining it, and the Higher Level extension questions expect evaluation with a stated judgement. Vague recommendations score poorly however well the theory is known.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is unseen textual analysis, including non-literary texts, which rewards technique over revision. The individual oral asks a student to link a global issue to one literary and one non-literary extract. Higher Level adds the essay on a studied work. Students who read widely but never practise timed analysis plateau early here.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: Assessed across reading, writing, listening and speaking, with a text-type requirement that catches students out: a blog, a formal letter and a speech are marked partly on register and convention. Higher Level reading passages are longer and the writing task expects a sustained argument rather than description.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Paper 1 covers system fundamentals and computational thinking; Higher Level adds abstract data structures, resource management and a case study released ahead of the examination. The Internal Assessment is a working solution with full documentation, and students usually over-build the program and under-write the design record.

dammam.igcseSubjectsIntro: Below are the International GCSE subjects Dammam students most often need outside teaching for, with the Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel codes side by side. The code matters more than the subject name, because the papers are not interchangeable between boards.

igcseSubjects.name: Mathematics
igcseSubjects.description: Cambridge tiers this subject into Core and Extended, which caps the achievable grade on the Core tier; Edexcel Mathematics A runs at Foundation and Higher. A student entered on the wrong tier is the single most common unforced error we see in the Eastern Province.

igcseSubjects.name: Physics
igcseSubjects.description: Both boards test practical reasoning through written questions rather than a practical examination for most candidates. Formula recall differs: the Edexcel paper expects more equations from memory, so a student switching boards mid-course has a specific, fixable gap.

igcseSubjects.name: Chemistry
igcseSubjects.description: The qualitative analysis and practical-technique questions reward students who have been shown the standard tests properly. Organic chemistry is lighter than at Diploma level, but ionic equations, moles and titration calculation steps generate most of the lost marks.

igcseSubjects.name: Biology
igcseSubjects.description: Content-heavy and definition-strict. Both boards penalise loose terminology — diffusion described as movement rather than net movement down a gradient loses the mark. Diagram labelling and experimental control questions are reliably worth practising.

igcseSubjects.name: English Language
igcseSubjects.description: Cambridge First Language English and Edexcel English Language A are marked against different assessment objectives, and the directed-writing tasks differ in form. A student moving between them needs to relearn the structure expected, not the language.

igcseSubjects.name: Economics
igcseSubjects.description: Diagram accuracy and definition precision carry the lower-mark questions; the extended-response questions want a weighed judgement rather than a list. Many students arrive strong on definitions and weak on the eight-mark evaluation that decides the grade.

igcseSubjects.name: Business Studies
igcseSubjects.description: The case-study material is the examination, not background reading. Marks come from using the figures and the context given, and generic answers about motivation or marketing score low even when the theory is accurate.

igcseSubjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
igcseSubjects.description: Cambridge Computer Science assesses algorithms, pseudocode and data representation; ICT is a different qualification with a practical component. Families frequently ask for one and need the other, so it is worth confirming the code on the school's entry list first.

dammam.regionsTitle: Dammam districts students join lessons from
dammam.regionsIntro: District matters in Dammam less for distance to a tutor than for distance to a school. The city is wide, the international school belt sits to the south in Dhahran and Al Khobar, and the length of that drive decides what hour an evening lesson can realistically start.

regions.name: Al Faisaliyah
regions.note: A large western residential district with good access to the King Fahd and Dhahran road corridors. Families here commonly school in Dhahran, which makes a late-afternoon return normal and pushes lessons towards the later end of the evening.

regions.name: Al Rakah
regions.note: Sits on the Dammam and Al Khobar boundary, so families here have the shortest run to the southern school belt of any Dammam district. That buys back the better part of an hour, and it is usually the one district where a 5pm start works on a school night.

regions.name: Al Shatea
regions.note: The north-eastern corniche district. Short trips inside Dammam, long ones to Dhahran or Al Khobar. Students here often prefer two shorter sessions in the week to one long one, because the evening is already fragmented by the drive home.

regions.name: Al Mazruiyah
regions.note: An established central-north district close to the older civic core. Mixed schooling: some families stay with strong private schools inside Dammam and use outside teaching specifically for the Higher Level subject their school does not offer.

regions.name: Al Adamah
regions.note: Near the historic centre and the port approaches. Traffic through the centre is the variable rather than raw distance, and a lesson slot here benefits from being set after the school run rather than inside a predicted gap.

regions.name: An Nakheel
regions.note: North of the centre along the coastal corridor, with newer housing. A common pattern here is siblings at different schools in different cities, which is why staggered rather than simultaneous sessions tend to survive the term.

regions.name: Uhud
regions.note: Inland and west of the centre, with a residential rhythm set by working hours rather than by school proximity. Families here are often the ones who weigh an online specialist against a long drive for an in-home option and choose on time, not price.

regions.name: Al Muraikabat
regions.note: Central, close to the railway station and the commercial district. Short internal journeys, heavy through-traffic at the end of the working day, and a strong preference among parents here for a fixed weekly slot rather than a floating one.

schoolClusters.city: Dhahran and Al Khobar — the belt most Dammam families drive to
schoolClusters.note: The Diploma Programme and British-curriculum provision for the conurbation is concentrated here rather than inside Dammam itself. A Dammam student is therefore usually working to a scheme of work set in another city, and an outside tutor has to ask which campus and which curriculum before anything else.

schoolClusters.city: Riyadh and Jeddah — where Eastern Province families look when a subject is not staffed
schoolClusters.note: When a Higher Level subject cannot be run locally, families either travel, change school, or take the subject from outside. Naming these schools is useful context for how thin Diploma provision is outside the three big centres; students we support attend schools of this kind across the Kingdom.

dammam.modesIntro: Four shapes of support cover almost every Dammam request. All of them are delivered one-to-one over live video on Arabia Standard Time, and all of them are built around the week the school sets rather than a standard timetable.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one teaching
modes.description: One or two fixed sessions a week in a single subject, tracking the school's scheme of work rather than running ahead of it. This is what most Dammam families start with and what works best across a full term, because it lets a tutor fix a gap in the week it appears instead of in a holiday catch-up block.

modes.description: A compressed run of sessions in the weeks before the June series or the May session, aimed at paper technique rather than new content. sections.heading: The term you are in decides what is still on the table
paragraphs: Every honest tutoring plan starts with a calendar position, not an hourly rate. In the autumn term of the first Diploma year almost nothing is fixed: Higher Level choices may still move, Internal Assessment has not started, and a weak IGCSE foundation can still be rebuilt from the bottom rather than patched. One session a week is often enough, and the work is foundational — algebraic fluency, graph interpretation, written structure, the habit of reading a question twice.

By the autumn term of the second Diploma year the shape of the grade is already visible. Internal Assessment drafts are moving, mock results are informing predicted grades, and university applications are being drafted against those predictions. The work changes character here. Content teaching still happens, but the higher-value activity is converting what the student knows into what a mark scheme pays for: command terms, mark allocations, and the discipline of answering the question asked rather than the one revised for.

The spring term of the final year is almost entirely technique. New content at that point is expensive and rarely recovers its cost, whereas a student who learns to budget time across a paper and to recognise which of four similar questions is being asked can move a grade boundary's worth of marks in weeks. After the May session the decisions change again: whether to accept a grade, whether a remark is worth requesting, and whether a November-series entry makes sense for a short International GCSE result.

It assumes a school in Dhahran, Al Khobar or Jubail, because that is where most Eastern Province Diploma students sit, and it deliberately names no dates. Your school's Diploma Programme coordinator or examinations officer holds the exact deadlines, and they differ between campuses in the same city.

sections.heading: The university endgame starts two terms earlier than families expect
paragraphs: A Diploma earned at a Dhahran or Al Khobar school is an international certificate, and that is the whole of the complication. A Saudi university does not treat it as the Saudi secondary certificate until the Ministry of Education issues an equivalency decision, the step families usually hear called mu'adalah. The same applies to A Levels and to an American high school diploma. It is a documentary process rather than an examination, but it needs attested paperwork and it sits in a queue, which is why starting it in the term applications are due is the commonest avoidable delay in this market.

Alongside equivalency sit the two Qiyas tests. Qudurat, the General Aptitude Test, is run by the National Center for Assessment under the Education and Training Evaluation Commission, and it measures verbal and quantitative reasoning rather than a syllabus. Tahsili, the Achievement Test, covers the science-stream subjects — mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology and English — and its content follows the Saudi national curriculum. Both are sat in Arabic or in English. Universities then combine school grades with these results using their own published formula, and those formulas differ by university and by programme.

We do not publish a threshold for either test, and you should be careful with any page that does. The weightings and the entry points move between institutions and between intakes, and a number copied from a third-party site is exactly the sort of fact a family acts on and regrets. The reliable source is the university's own admission page for the specific programme, read in the term before the application goes in.

For families applying overseas instead, the mechanics are different but the lead time is the same. Predicted grades become the currency, subject prerequisites at Higher Level decide which courses are even open, and references are written by teachers in a school that may be in a different city from your home. None of that is improvised well in the final term.

sections.heading: Why Tahsili reads as unfamiliar to a student taught in English
paragraphs: This is the part of the Saudi university route that catches strong students, and it is almost absent from the rest of this market's content. Tahsili is not a harder version of the Diploma sciences. It is a different examination culture applied to overlapping material. The content a Diploma or International GCSE student has studied largely covers what Tahsili asks about, but the framing is taken from the Saudi national curriculum: the ordering of topics, the technical vocabulary, the emphasis between recall and application, and the question format itself.

The format difference does most of the damage. A Diploma science student spends two years being rewarded for extended reasoning, method shown in full, and evaluation of a result. Tahsili pays for fast, accurate recognition instead. A student who has been trained to show working is being trained out of the habit that Tahsili rewards, and that reversal takes a few weeks of deliberate practice rather than more teaching. Nothing about it is beyond a student who has earned good Diploma predictions; it simply has to be practised as its own thing.

The language question matters too. The test is available in Arabic and in English, and a student schooled in English in Dhahran often assumes the English version removes the problem. It removes some of it. What remains is the technical vocabulary of a syllabus they have not studied, and the standard phrasings the national curriculum uses for definitions and derivations. A tutor who has taught both systems is genuinely useful here, and a tutor who has only taught one will teach the content again rather than the gap.

The sensible plan is to treat Tahsili as a separate, short, intense project rather than an extension of Diploma revision, and to start it in a term where it is not competing with Internal Assessment deadlines. The table sets out where the overlap sits and where it does not.

sections.heading: What the Eastern Province school belt cannot staff
paragraphs: The reason a Dammam family ends up searching for a tutor is usually structural rather than personal. Diploma provision in the conurbation is concentrated in a small number of campuses in Dhahran, Al Khobar and Jubail, and each of those campuses has to field a teacher for every Higher Level subject it offers. A school with one chemistry specialist can run Chemistry HL. A school that loses that specialist mid-course cannot, and the subject becomes a timetabled class taught by a willing non-specialist or a combined HL and SL group where the Higher Level extension gets the last twenty minutes.

The subjects this happens to are predictable. Mathematics AA HL, Physics HL and Chemistry HL are the hardest to staff anywhere, because the pool of people qualified to teach them to examination standard is small and competes with industry employment that pays better. Computer Science and the less common group two languages come next. Economics and Business Management are easier to staff but harder to staff well, because the gap between knowing the theory and knowing the mark scheme is wide and invisible on a CV.

Expatriate staffing cycles add a second layer. International school contracts in the Kingdom turn over, and a department that was strong one year can be thin the next without anything appearing in a report. Parents often read this as a drop in standards. It is usually one person leaving. The practical consequence is the same either way: the student in front of the gap needs outside teaching for that subject, for that year, and the school is rarely in a position to say so plainly.

This is also where distance stops being the real constraint. A Dammam family hunting for an in-home Mathematics AA HL specialist is drawing from the small set of such people who live within driving range and have a free evening. Teaching over live video replaces that set with the set of people who know the syllabus, which is the only criterion that was ever going to matter.

sections.heading: What this market charges, and what the number is actually tracking
paragraphs: Rates for one-to-one tuition in the Kingdom are published by platforms, agencies and individual tutors, and they vary by a factor of six. That spread is not noise. It tracks scarcity, level and whether anybody is driving. The table below collects advertised figures by tier and names the kind of source each comes from. They are advertised rates, not a market average, and none of them is IB Gram's price — we quote per student after a trial lesson, because an hour of Standard Level Business Management support and an hour of Higher Level Physics taught by an examiner are not the same product.

Four things move the number more than anything else. Subject scarcity comes first: a Mathematics AA HL or Physics HL specialist costs more everywhere, in every market, because there are fewer of them. Marking or examining experience comes second, and it is worth paying for in the final year specifically, because the value of it is knowing what a script is paid for. Level comes third — Higher Level above Standard Level, Diploma above Middle Years and International GCSE. Travel comes fourth: an in-home tutor in Dhahran prices the drive into the hour, which is one reason advertised in-home rates in the Eastern Province sit above the online bands for the same subject.

Package length and timing move it too, in both directions. A longer commitment usually reduces the hourly figure. Booking in the weeks before a series usually raises it, because demand concentrates and the specialists fill first. The honest advice is unglamorous: the cheapest version of this is to start early enough that weekly support at a normal rate replaces an intensive block at a premium one.

One thing worth being blunt about. A low advertised rate for an International GCSE subject frequently buys a generalist graduate working from a textbook rather than a board's papers and mark schemes. For a student two grades below target in Year 11 that can still be the right call. For a Higher Level student in the final Diploma year it almost never is, and families who try it usually pay twice.

sections.heading: An hour that survives the Sunday-to-Thursday week
paragraphs: The Saudi school week runs Sunday to Thursday, and Friday and Saturday are the weekend. Most tutoring content written for this market is quietly copied from British or Indian pages and assumes a Monday-to-Friday rhythm, which is why so much of it offers a Saturday morning slot as though that were the obvious choice. For a Dammam student, Saturday is the second day of the weekend and Sunday morning is a school morning. The usable windows are weekday evenings and, for intensive work, Friday and Saturday during the day.

The Kingdom sits on Arabia Standard Time, UTC+3, and does not change its clocks. That single fact causes more quiet disruption than anything else in a tutoring arrangement, because a tutor in a country that does change its clocks will see the agreed time move twice a year unless the slot is pinned to Saudi local time rather than to theirs. We pin it to Saudi local time. It sounds trivial until a Higher Level session silently relocates into the middle of a school night.

A tutor's own working week matters as much as the offset. A tutor based in a Monday-to-Friday country is working on Sunday morning when your child is at school and is free on Friday when your child is not. That mismatch is manageable but it narrows the realistic slots, and it is worth knowing before a family commits to a tutor they liked in a trial. The table sets out what a seven o'clock Dammam evening looks like from several common tutor locations.

Ramadan changes the pattern again. School days shorten, the structure of the evening moves, and most families prefer a later session or a short pause rather than holding a fixed late-afternoon slot through it. The long summer break and the autumn break raise the same question, and the honest answer is that a slot held with no teaching is a slot wasted — but a slot given up in a scarce subject can be hard to recover.
