sections.heading: Academic honesty on the Internal Assessment, the Extended Essay and the Personal Project
paragraphs: Several providers competing for these searches will, in practice, hand a student finished coursework. It is worth saying plainly what the boundary is, because a family paying for help on assessed work deserves to know which side of it they are on. The assessed work in the Diploma, the Middle Years Programme and International GCSE coursework has to be the student's own. A tutor may teach the skills it needs, question the method, point at the criterion the draft is not yet meeting, and send the student back to do the work again. A tutor does not write it, redraft it, or supply the sentences.

In practice a good Internal Assessment session looks like an interrogation rather than an edit. What is your research question actually asking? Which variable did you control and how do you know? Where does this graph show what you say it shows? Which criterion descriptor does this paragraph satisfy, and can you point to the words that satisfy it? A student who can answer those questions writes a better Internal Assessment than one who has been handed better paragraphs, and more to the point, it is theirs.

The school's supervisor remains the authority. The Extended Essay has a formal supervision structure with reflection sessions, and the number of drafts a supervisor may formally comment on is set by the school and the programme, not by us. An outside tutor works inside that structure. We keep a record of what was discussed in each session, which is useful to a student if they are ever asked how the work developed, and we tell families directly when a request crosses the line.

The Personal Project in the final Middle Years year is the same principle applied earlier. It is assessed on the process as much as the product, and the process journal is the evidence. A tutor who helps a student plan, question their own goal and record their decisions is doing the job. A tutor who produces the artefact has removed the entire point of the exercise and created a malpractice problem the student will carry.

sections.heading: Arriving in Dammam part-way through a course
paragraphs: Relocation into the Eastern Province mid-course is common enough to be treated as a normal case rather than an exception. A family arriving in the spring term with a student half-way through the first Diploma year faces a specific, bounded set of problems: a different school's scheme of work, a possible board change at International GCSE level, Internal Assessment work that may have started under a different brief, and subject options that may not match what the new school can run.

What transfers depends on the direction of travel. A student moving from a British school into the Diploma usually carries strong subject content and has to learn an unfamiliar assessment language — command terms, criterion-referenced marking, and the core of Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. A student moving from an American curriculum typically has broader coverage and less depth, and the gap shows at Higher Level in the sciences and in Mathematics AA. A student moving from the Saudi national curriculum into International GCSE has often met the content but not the examination format, and the first fixable gap is almost always technical English and question interpretation rather than subject knowledge.

A mid-Diploma move is the hardest case, and honesty serves a family better than optimism here. Internal Assessment work does not always travel cleanly between schools, subject combinations differ, and a student may lose a term of continuity in a two-year course. It is recoverable, but it needs a diagnostic before anybody promises a plan, and it usually needs two subjects supported rather than one.

The practical sequence we use is the same every time. Establish which board and which code the new school enters, get the current scheme of work, test the student against a past paper rather than against a report, and name the two or three gaps that will cost the most marks. Everything else follows from that, and it takes one session rather than a term to find out.

process.title: Tell us the board, the code and the deadline
process.description: The three facts that decide everything else. Cambridge 0580 and Edexcel 4MA1 are different papers; Higher Level and Standard Level are different courses; and a January Internal Assessment deadline and a final-term paper are different jobs. A school name and a year group alone is not enough to match a tutor properly.

process.title: A free trial lesson that works as a diagnostic
process.description: An hour with the tutor we think fits, built around a real past-paper question rather than a chat. The point is to find out where marks are actually being lost, and to let the student decide whether they can work with this person. There is no charge and no commitment attached to it.

process.title: A written starting point and a weekly plan
process.description: After the trial you get a short written note: what the student can already do, the two or three gaps that cost the most marks, and what the first month will cover. It names the slot in Saudi local time and says plainly what is realistic in the time available before the next assessment.

process.title: Weekly teaching against the school's scheme of work
process.description: Sessions run in the fixed slot, tracking what the school is teaching rather than a parallel syllabus. Work is set between sessions and marked before the next one. A short note after each session tells you what was covered and what was weak, so you are not asking a teenager for a summary.

process.title: A review at the end of the term, with an honest stop option
process.description: At the end of a term we look at whether the movement justifies the cost, using the student's own marked work rather than a feeling. Sometimes the answer is to continue, sometimes to change subject focus, and sometimes to stop. We will say so when stopping is the right answer.

whyPoints.title: Matched on the syllabus code, not on the map
whyPoints.description: The constraint that makes tutoring hard in Dammam is the size of the local specialist pool, not distance. Matching by board, code and level first means a family gets someone who has taught that paper, instead of the best available person who happens to have a free evening and a short drive.

whyPoints.title: The Eastern Province commute is a scheduling input
whyPoints.description: A student who gets home from a Dhahran school at half past four cannot start a demanding Higher Level session at five. We set the slot after the school run that actually happens, in Saudi local time, and we would rather agree a later hour that holds for a term than an early one that collapses.

whyPoints.title: The university route is planned alongside the teaching
whyPoints.description: Equivalency through the Ministry of Education, Qudurat and Tahsili through Qiyas, and overseas applications all have lead times that start earlier than families expect. We raise them in the first term of the second Diploma year rather than in the term the forms are due.

whyPoints.title: Assessed work is reviewed, never produced
whyPoints.description: A tutor reads a student's Internal Assessment or Extended Essay draft, questions the method, and names the criterion it is missing. The student does the writing. We say this before a family asks, because the alternative on offer elsewhere in this market creates a malpractice risk the student carries, not the provider.

whyPoints.title: Figures are attributed, and claims are not made
whyPoints.description: Every rate on this page is an advertised figure with its source type named, not a market average and not our price. We publish no success percentages, no ratings and no thresholds for Qudurat or Tahsili, because the honest version of those numbers is that they move and belong to whoever publishes them.

faqs.question: What transfers when a student moves from a Saudi national-curriculum school in Dammam into Cambridge IGCSE?
faqs.answer: More content than families expect, and less technique. The mathematics and science material largely overlaps, so a student is rarely starting from nothing. What does not transfer is the examination format: command terms read as instructions, mark allocations that tell you how much to write, and extended-response questions that want a weighed judgement rather than recall. Technical English is the other gap, and it is specific rather than general — a student may speak fluently and still not know that describe and explain earn marks differently. A term of focused work on question interpretation usually closes more of the distance than a term of content revision.

faqs.question: What does a Dammam student lose by joining the Diploma Programme after the first term has started?
faqs.answer: Continuity, mostly, and some Internal Assessment lead time. The taught content can be caught up, because the first term of a two-year course is foundational. Harder to recover is the embedded practice in how the Diploma assesses — criterion-referenced marking, command terms and the rhythm of drafting — which the rest of the cohort has been absorbing without noticing. Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay also start earlier than new arrivals assume. The realistic plan is a diagnostic first, two subjects supported rather than one for the first term, and a conversation with the Diploma Programme coordinator about which Internal Assessment deadlines have already passed.

faqs.question: How does an American-curriculum student in the Eastern Province catch up for Higher Level Chemistry?
faqs.answer: Depth is the issue rather than coverage. An American high school course typically introduces most of the topics but assesses them less deeply than Higher Level Chemistry does, so students arrive able to recognise material they cannot yet manipulate. The specific gaps are usually energetics and entropy, equilibrium calculations, and organic reaction mechanisms where a pathway has to be reasoned rather than recalled. Mathematical confidence with logarithms and rearrangement matters more than students expect. A sensible plan runs eight to ten weeks of targeted work on those topics alongside the school course, with past-paper questions used as the measure rather than textbook exercises.

faqs.question: We are relocating into Dammam from a CBSE school in India — does International GCSE assessment work differently?
faqs.answer: Yes, and in a way that is easy to underestimate. CBSE rewards accurate, complete recall against a defined syllabus. International GCSE papers give marks for applying content to unfamiliar material: a case study, a data set, an experiment described rather than performed. Students who have done well under CBSE often write everything they know and score poorly on questions that wanted one applied point. The fix is structural rather than academic — practise with past papers and mark schemes early, and learn what each command term pays for. Content gaps, where they exist, are usually smaller than the format gap.

faqs.question: Is it better to finish International GCSE at a Dammam school or to restart the course at a Dhahran one?
faqs.answer: It depends on one thing: whether the board and the syllabus codes match. If the Dammam school enters Cambridge and the Dhahran school enters Edexcel, a mid-course move means different papers, sometimes different content weighting, and coursework that may not transfer. If the codes match, moving is largely administrative. Ask both schools for their entry code list before deciding anything else. Where a move is unavoidable and the boards differ, the gap is bounded and teachable, but it should be identified deliberately rather than discovered in a mock.

faqs.question: Which Higher Level subjects do Eastern Province schools most often fail to staff?
faqs.answer: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, Physics HL and Chemistry HL are the hardest everywhere, and the Eastern Province competes with industry employment for exactly those people. Computer Science and less common group two languages follow. Economics and Business Management are easier to staff but harder to staff well, because knowing the theory and knowing the mark scheme are different things. The practical sign is a combined Higher and Standard Level class where the Higher Level extension gets the final part of the lesson, or a subject that has changed teacher mid-course.

faqs.question: Why do so many Dammam families send their children to school in Dhahran or Al Khobar?
faqs.answer: Because that is where the international and Diploma Programme provision sits. Dammam is the Eastern Province's administrative capital, but the campuses offering the IB Diploma and British-curriculum routes are concentrated to the south, and the Dammam, Al Khobar and Dhahran conurbation functions as one school market. Families routinely live in one city and attend school in another. The consequence for tutoring is a late school return, a shorter usable evening, and a scheme of work set by a school in a different city from the one on the home address.

faqs.question: How does Ministry of Education licensing of a private school in Dammam differ from what ETEC does?
faqs.answer: They answer different questions. The Ministry of Education licenses private and international schools to operate in the Kingdom — the permission to exist and to enrol students. The Education and Training Evaluation Commission handles evaluation and accreditation, including e-services for national school accreditation and the approval of international accreditation bodies. So a licence tells a parent a school is lawfully operating; an evaluation or accreditation outcome tells them something about quality. Neither says anything about an individual tutor, and no tutoring provider is licensed or accredited by either body.

faqs.question: What should a Dammam family ask a Dhahran school about subject availability before enrolling?
faqs.answer: Four questions, in writing. Which Higher Level subjects will actually run next year, as opposed to appearing in the brochure. Are any Higher and Standard Level groups taught together. Who teaches the Higher Level science and mathematics courses, and how long have they been in post. And which board and syllabus codes are entered for International GCSE. The answers predict more about your tutoring bill than anything else you can ask, and a school that answers them openly is telling you something useful in itself.

faqs.question: What happens when a Dammam school offers a Diploma subject only as an online option?
faqs.answer: It can work, but it is a different arrangement from a taught class and should be planned as one. A school-arranged online course typically supplies the teaching and the assessment route while leaving day-to-day monitoring to the student. That suits a self-managing student in the first Diploma year and tends to strain in the second, when Internal Assessment deadlines compete with five other subjects. Families in this position usually need outside support not for content but for pacing, deadline management and Internal Assessment feedback, which is a cheaper and narrower requirement than full subject teaching.

faqs.question: What time can a lesson start for a Dammam student whose school run comes back from Dhahran?
faqs.answer: Most families in that position settle on something between six and eight in the evening on a school night. A student arriving home at half past four needs food and a break before a demanding Higher Level session, and a slot set at five tends to be the first thing to slip. Al Rakah families, closest to the southern school belt, can often hold an earlier start. Lessons run on Arabia Standard Time and the slot is agreed in Saudi local time, so it does not move when a tutor's own country changes its clocks.

faqs.question: Does Arabia Standard Time cause a problem when the tutor is based in the United Kingdom?
faqs.answer: Only if the slot is agreed in their time rather than yours. The Kingdom is on UTC+3 and does not change its clocks; the United Kingdom does, twice a year. A seven o'clock Dammam lesson is four in the afternoon for a tutor in their winter and five in their summer, so if the arrangement is written down in British time it silently shifts by an hour twice a year. We fix the slot in Saudi local time, which means the tutor's clock moves and your child's school night does not.

faqs.question: How do lessons work during Ramadan for a student in the Eastern Province?
faqs.answer: School days shorten and the shape of the evening changes, so a fixed late-afternoon slot usually stops working. Most families either move the session later or pause for the month and resume afterwards. Both are fine, with one caveat worth knowing: in a scarce subject such as Physics HL, a released slot can be hard to recover, so it is better to move the hour than to give it up. Where a student is close to a series, a shorter and more frequent pattern often holds better than one long session.

faqs.question: What happens to a Dammam student's weekly slot across the long summer break?
faqs.answer: Three patterns work. Hold the slot and keep teaching at a reduced frequency, which suits a student entering the second Diploma year with Internal Assessment work to position. Pause and reserve the slot, which keeps the tutor but stops the cost. Or use the break for a focused block on a single weak topic and stop afterwards. The one choice that regularly causes trouble is releasing a slot in a scarce subject and assuming it will be there in the autumn term; in Higher Level mathematics and physics it often is not.

faqs.question: Does a Dammam student with an IB Diploma need Ministry of Education equivalency before applying to a Saudi university?
faqs.answer: A foreign or international school certificate needs an equivalency decision — mu'adalah — from the Ministry of Education before a Saudi university treats it as equal to the Saudi secondary certificate. That applies to the IB Diploma, to A Levels and to an American high school diploma alike. It is a documentary process rather than an examination: attested transcripts and certificates submitted through the ministry's own channel. The practical advice is to start it in the autumn term of the final school year rather than in the term applications are due, and to check the current requirements with the ministry directly.

faqs.question: Why does Tahsili feel harder than the Diploma papers for a student taught in English in Dhahran?
faqs.answer: Because the content overlaps but the framing does not. Tahsili follows the Saudi national curriculum, so the topic ordering, the technical vocabulary and the balance between recall and application are not the ones a Diploma student has practised for two years. The format reverses the habit too: Diploma science rewards extended method shown in full, while Tahsili pays for fast, accurate recognition. Sitting the English version removes the language barrier but not the syllabus framing. Treat it as a short separate project with its own practice, not as an extension of Diploma revision.

dammam.closingHeading: Start from the term you are in
dammam.closingBody: If your child is in the first Diploma year, there is time and the cheapest thing you can do is fix the foundation now. If they are in the second, the work is turning knowledge into marks and getting the equivalency and Qiyas steps moving before the term the applications are due. Either way the first move is the same: a free trial lesson with a subject specialist, built around a real past-paper question, followed by a short written note on where the marks are going. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Arabia Standard Time, timed to a Dammam school night rather than to a tutor's convenience.

dhahran.tutorsIntro: The tutors below are the kind of match a Dhahran enquiry usually resolves to: subject specialists who teach one syllabus properly rather than six badly, several with marking experience, all teaching live over video. Availability shifts week to week, so treat the list as a sample of the pool rather than a roster.

intro.heading: Start with what the evidence says, then decide what support to buy
paragraphs: Most tutoring decisions in Dhahran start from a feeling: the student seems to be working hard, the grades are not moving, and a parent wants someone to intervene. That is a reasonable instinct and a poor brief. A tutor who begins without evidence spends the first month teaching whatever the student happens to mention, which is usually the topic covered in school last week rather than the one that is costing marks. The faster route is to decide, before the first paid hour, what measurable thing you expect to be different in eight weeks, and what document will show it.

There are only four pieces of evidence that reliably answer the question. The first is a marked past paper with the mark scheme beside it, because that shows whether marks are being lost on content, on method or on the command term. The second is the school's own internal assessment grid for the Internal Assessment, which allocates marks criterion by criterion and tells you exactly which criterion is weak. The third is the predicted grade and the reasoning the teacher gave for it. The fourth is the student's own account of which questions they skip, which is often the most useful of the four.

That evidence base matters more in Dhahran than in a city with a deeper teaching market, because the subjects families here need most are the subjects hardest to cover locally. A school running one Diploma Programme physics teacher across two year groups and two levels has no spare capacity for a student who needs the Higher Level extension topics taught again slowly. The gap is structural, not a failure of the school, and it shows up in the same subjects every term: Higher Level Physics, Higher Level Chemistry, Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, and Computer Science.

Delivery is the part families ask about first, so it is worth being plain. IB Gram arranges one-to-one lessons delivered live over video, on Arabia Standard Time, to students in Dhahran and across the Eastern Province. We do not arrange in-home visits anywhere in the Kingdom; home visiting is a service we run only in India. The practical consequence is the useful part: a family in the Aramco residential camp is choosing from a pool of subject specialists rather than from the handful of people willing to drive onto the camp at six in the evening.

What follows is written to be used rather than admired. It sets out what the Dhahran school market can and cannot staff, what Eastern Province families are quoted in SAR and what moves the number, how a Sunday-to-Thursday week fits around a tutor in another time zone, what to ask to verify a claim about examining experience, and what a tutor may and may not touch on an Internal Assessment. If you only read one part, read the section on checking a claim.

dhahran.programmesIntro: Dhahran families move between the IB continuum and the Cambridge pathway more often than most, because the schools within reach of the camp and the university offer both and a transfer across town can mean a change of board. These are the four programmes that come up in Eastern Province enquiries, with what each one actually demands of a student here.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP is organised around transdisciplinary units of inquiry rather than discrete subject syllabuses, so there is no past paper to work through and no mark scheme to decode. Support at this age is about the mechanics underneath the inquiry: number fluency, reading stamina, handwriting speed, and the ability to explain a method out loud. A PYP student who can talk through how they got an answer is doing the thing the programme is measuring, and that is coachable in short sessions.
programmes.countryNote: In Dhahran the PYP question is usually about English reading level rather than mathematics, because many families arrive mid-primary from a system with a different reading scheme. A short diagnostic against the school's own benchmark, followed by two short sessions a week rather than one long one, suits this age group better than a weekly hour that eats into an already long compound school day.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP assesses eight subject groups against four criteria each, marked out of 8, with no final written examination unless the school enters students for eAssessment. The criteria are what the marks hang on, so a student who writes a good essay and ignores Criterion D is capped. The Personal Project in the final MYP year is the first piece of genuinely independent work most students ever produce, and it is where organisation rather than ability decides the grade.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP matters in Dhahran as the feeder into Higher Level science. A student who reaches the Diploma Programme without secure algebraic manipulation will meet it again in the first fortnight of Physics HL, and the Eastern Province schools cannot easily run a catch-up group for one or two students. Fixing it in the MYP years costs a fraction of fixing it in the first Diploma year.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject carries its own Internal Assessment worth a fifth to a quarter of the grade, and the core contributes up to three points through the Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay matrix. The Diploma is less a set of courses than a two-year project-management exercise with examinations attached, and the students who struggle are rarely the weakest ones.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma students in Dhahran skew heavily towards the engineering and medicine combinations, which means Physics HL, Chemistry HL and Mathematics AA HL in the same timetable. That is three Higher Level subjects with a practical or exploration component each, all due in the same window. Sequencing those three Internal Assessments is the single most useful thing an outside tutor does for a Dhahran Diploma student in the first year.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Two-year courses examined by written paper, with a syllabus code on every past paper and a specimen set published for each. Cambridge tiers some subjects into Core and Extended, and the tier decision caps the available grade, so it is a decision worth getting right rather than accepting by default. Saudi candidates sit the June series as the main sitting and the November series for resits and November-entry candidates.
programmes.countryNote: British-curriculum schools in Dhahran and Al Khobar run the Cambridge pathway, and families transferring between them and the ISG campuses sometimes change board mid-course. What transfers is the content; what does not transfer is the question style and the mark scheme. A term of targeted work on the new board's past papers usually closes that gap faster than retaking content the student already knows.

dhahran.subjectsIntro: Enquiries from Dhahran cluster tightly around the sciences and mathematics, which reflects what the families here do for a living and where the schools are thinnest. These are the Diploma Programme subjects that come up most, with what each one actually assesses and where the marks tend to go.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Three papers plus the internal investigation. Paper 1 is multiple choice and the data booklet is allowed; Paper 2 carries the extended-response questions where method marks are won and lost; Paper 3 is experimental and data analysis. Higher Level adds whole topics with no Standard Level equivalent. Most lost marks at Higher Level come from unit errors, from quoting a law instead of applying it, and from graph answers that omit the gradient's meaning.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Assessed by written papers and the internal investigation. Organic mechanisms and energetics are where Higher Level students lose ground, usually because the curly arrow convention is learned loosely and then penalised repeatedly. Calculation questions reward setting out the working so each stage earns its mark; a correct final answer with no working scores less than a wrong answer with sound method. The data booklet is a skill in itself.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The proof-heavy mathematics route, and the one most engineering-bound Dhahran students take. Higher Level adds complex numbers, proof by induction, vectors and far harder calculus. Paper 1 is sat without a calculator, which exposes any weakness in algebraic manipulation immediately. The mathematical exploration is twenty-ish pages of the student's own investigation, marked against criteria that reward personal engagement and reflection as much as mathematics.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The modelling and statistics route, assessed with the graphic display calculator in use throughout. Standard Level suits students heading for economics, business or life sciences; Higher Level is a serious course in its own right with statistics and modelling well beyond the Standard Level syllabus. Students lose marks by treating calculator output as the answer rather than as evidence that still needs interpreting in context.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content-heavy, with command terms doing more work than in any other science. The difference between outline, explain, describe and evaluate decides the mark on a six-mark question, and a student who writes everything they know about a topic will score below one who answers the verb. The internal investigation needs a variable that can genuinely be controlled, which is where most proposals fail first.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Written papers on systems, data structures and algorithms, plus a solution the student develops for a real client. Higher Level adds resource management, abstract data structures and object-oriented programming. It is one of the hardest subjects to staff locally because the people who can teach it well are usually employed doing it, which is why it appears disproportionately in Eastern Province tutoring enquiries.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Three papers at Higher Level, including a quantitative paper, plus three commentaries on published news articles. The diagram is the answer in this subject: a correctly labelled, correctly shifted diagram earns marks that no amount of prose recovers. Higher Level adds calculation across micro and macro. Commentaries fail on the extract choice more often than on the analysis.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is unseen textual analysis, Paper 2 a comparative essay on studied texts, with the individual oral and, at Higher Level, the essay on a studied text. Students arriving from a different system usually have the reading ability and not the analytical vocabulary. The fix is mechanical and quick: a repeatable structure for reading an unseen non-literary text under time pressure.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study driven, with a pre-released case for one paper and a research project drawing on real organisational data. The marks sit in application rather than recall, so a student who can define every tool and apply none will plateau in the low middle. Higher Level adds extension topics and a longer, more demanding paper structure.

subjects.name: Design Technology
subjects.description: Written papers plus a substantial design project, and a subject that rewards documentation discipline more than flair. Students lose marks by producing a good product with thin evidence of the iterative process behind it. Higher Level adds commercial production and user-centred design content. Few schools in the Eastern Province run it, so the student is often one of a very small cohort.

dhahran.igcseSubjectsIntro: The British-curriculum schools in and around Dhahran run Cambridge and Edexcel courses at this level, and families transferring between campuses sometimes change board without changing year group. Syllabus codes are the quickest way to confirm which course a child is actually sitting.

igcseSubjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Edexcel equivalent)
igcseSubjects.description: Two written papers, with the tier capping the grade available. Extended is the tier any student heading for Diploma Programme mathematics needs. The common failure is arithmetic under time pressure rather than unfamiliar content, and it is fixed by timed sets of past-paper questions rather than by re-teaching topics.

igcseSubjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625)
igcseSubjects.description: Multiple choice, theory and a practical-skills paper. The practical paper is the one that surprises students, because it tests the handling of apparatus and data rather than recall. Formula recall is assumed; the formula sheet does less work than students expect, so a fortnightly recall drill pays off.

igcseSubjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620)
igcseSubjects.description: Three papers, with the alternative-to-practical option in some centres. Students lose marks on ionic equations, on state symbols and on mole calculations where the working is skipped. Learning the qualitative analysis tables properly is a few hours of work that reliably converts into marks.

igcseSubjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610)
igcseSubjects.description: Heavy on precise definitions, which are examined strictly. A paraphrased definition of osmosis or active transport scores nothing. The practical paper rewards students who have drawn and labelled their own diagrams rather than only read them, which is straightforward to practise in an online session with a shared whiteboard.

igcseSubjects.name: Combined and Co-ordinated Sciences (Cambridge 0653 / 0654)
igcseSubjects.description: One or two award options covering biology, chemistry and physics in a single qualification. Suited to students who need science breadth without three separate courses, but it covers less depth, so a student planning Higher Level science should know what they are giving up before the option is locked in.

igcseSubjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 / 0511)
igcseSubjects.description: Reading, writing, listening and, in the 0511 variant, an assessed speaking component. Marks are won on register and task fulfilment rather than vocabulary breadth: a well-judged email that answers every bullet in the prompt beats an ambitious essay that answers two of them.

igcseSubjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478)
igcseSubjects.description: Two written papers covering computer systems, algorithms and programming. Pseudocode conventions carry marks of their own, and trace tables are the highest-yield topic for the time invested. Most students who find this course hard are strong programmers who have never written an algorithm out by hand.

igcseSubjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455)
igcseSubjects.description: Two papers, one multiple choice and one structured data response. The data-response question rewards reading the extract closely and quoting from it; students who answer from general knowledge lose the application marks. Diagram accuracy matters here as much as it does at Diploma Programme level.

dhahran.regionsTitle: Dhahran and the cities that share its school market
dhahran.regionsIntro: Dhahran does not function as a standalone school market. Dammam, Al Khobar and Dhahran behave as one labour and school catchment, families routinely live in one and attend school in another, and the practical question for a lesson slot is what the school run does to the hours either side of it.

regions.name: Saudi Aramco Residential Camp
regions.note: The main camp concentrates a large school-age population inside a controlled perimeter. Access arrangements for anyone coming in from outside are a real scheduling constraint, which is part of why online sessions suit camp families: the lesson starts when the student sits down, not when a visitor clears the gate.

regions.name: Dhahran Hills
regions.note: The newer residential area on the camp's southern side. School runs are short, which leaves the late afternoon genuinely usable for lessons rather than consumed by traffic. Families here often pair two subjects across one evening, with a gap for dinner between them.

regions.name: KFUPM campus
regions.note: The King Fahd University of Petroleum and Minerals community brings an academic household culture with it: parents who can follow the mathematics and want to see the working. Sessions for these families tend to be shorter and more technical, with the parent reading the lesson note rather than needing it explained.

regions.name: Ad Doha
regions.note: An older Dhahran neighbourhood between the camp and the airport road. Commutes to the international campuses are short but the roads load up at the same times every day, so a 4pm start is a different proposition here from a 5pm one.

regions.name: Al Rakah
regions.note: On the corridor between Dhahran and Al Khobar, and a common compromise address for a family with children at two different schools. Two school runs in opposite directions is the usual pattern, which makes a fixed weekly lesson slot more valuable than a flexible one.

regions.name: Al Khobar
regions.note: The retail and residential heart of the cluster, with British-curriculum and bilingual private schools alongside the international campuses. Evening traffic along the corniche road is the deciding factor for anything scheduled before five, and Thursday evenings behave like a Friday night elsewhere.

regions.name: Dammam
regions.note: The provincial capital, with the widest range of private schools in the cluster and a longer commute to the Dhahran campuses. Families here are the most likely to be running a child at a Dammam school and another at a Dhahran one, which is a scheduling problem before it is an academic one.

regions.name: Ras Tanura and Jubail
regions.note: Industrial communities north of the cluster with their own school provision, including an ISG campus at Jubail. Distance from the Dhahran campuses is the constraint: a specialist who is a twenty-minute drive from the camp is an hour and a half from here, which removes the visiting option altogether.

regions.name: Qatif and Al Ahsa
regions.note: Qatif sits on the coast north of Dammam; Al Ahsa is roughly an hour and a half inland. Both have families whose children attend school in the cluster, and both are far enough out that an evening lesson has to start after the drive home rather than before it.

schoolClusters.note: The Diploma Programme is offered at the American School of Dhahran, part of the International Schools Group, while the British-curriculum schools in the city run Cambridge courses through to IGCSE. Not every campus in the group runs the IB, which is the first thing to confirm before a transfer, because a move across the city can mean a move across boards.

The International Schools Group operates campuses across the Eastern Province, with the Diploma Programme offered at ISG Jubail as well as in Dhahran. Dammam and Al Khobar add a wide range of private and bilingual schools, several of which run Cambridge pathways. Subject availability at Higher Level differs campus by campus and year by year.

dhahran.modesIntro: Three formats cover almost every Dhahran enquiry. All of them are delivered live, one to one, over video on Arabia Standard Time. Which one fits depends on how far out the series is and whether the problem is content, technique or coursework.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one through the term
modes.description: A fixed slot in the same place every week, with work set between sessions and marked before the next one. This is the format that moves a grade, because it gives the tutor a diagnostic at the start and a measurable comparison eight weeks later. For a Higher Level science the useful length is ninety minutes rather than sixty, since a past-paper question plus the mark-scheme walkthrough does not fit into an hour.
bullets: Same day and time each week, pinned to Dhahran local time
Work set and marked between sessions, not just taught during them
A written note after each lesson naming what was covered and what is next
Reviewed against the original eight-week target rather than by feel

modes.title: Intensive block before a series
modes.description: A compressed run of sessions in the weeks before examinations, built around past papers under timed conditions rather than content delivery. The agenda is set by what the student actually drops marks on, which means the first session of a block is diagnostic even when the student has been taught weekly for a year. Friday mornings work well for these, since nothing else competes for the time.
bullets: Timed papers marked against the published mark scheme
A running list of recurring errors, revisited rather than mentioned once
Two or three sessions a week for a fixed number of weeks, then it stops
Friday and Saturday slots available while the school week is suspended

modes.title: Internal Assessment and coursework review
modes.description: Scheduled sessions around a student's own Internal Assessment, exploration, project or Extended Essay draft. The tutor reads what the student has written, maps it against the published criteria, and asks the questions the examiner will ask. They do not write, rewrite or redraft any part of it, and they do not supply the content. Keeping the work the student's own is the point, not a disclaimer attached to it.
bullets: Criterion-by-criterion feedback against the published descriptors
Questions and challenges on the student's own argument and method

sections.heading: What measurable progress looks like eight weeks in
paragraphs: A tutoring arrangement that cannot be audited is an expense, not an intervention. The audit needs to be set up before the first paid hour, and it needs to name a document rather than a feeling. For a written-paper subject that document is a timed past paper marked against the published mark scheme, sat at the start and again at the end of the eight weeks. For a coursework-heavy component it is the criterion grid, with a note of which criterion the student was weak on at the start.

The reason to insist on a timed paper rather than a topic test is that the two measure different things. A topic test tells you whether the student has learned the topic. A timed paper tells you whether they can produce marks under the conditions the grade is actually awarded in, which is a separate skill and frequently the one that is broken. A student who scores well on homework and poorly in examinations usually has a technique problem dressed up as a knowledge problem, and eight weeks of content revision will not touch it.

The honest version of the eight-week promise is modest. A specific, diagnosable gap closed in eight weeks looks like this: fewer dropped method marks in a calculation paper, a command term answered as asked rather than as remembered, a graph question that now carries the interpretation sentence the mark scheme wants. Whole-grade movement in a Higher Level subject is a longer project and depends on how much of the course remains. Any tutor who offers a grade outcome at this stage is selling something that cannot be delivered, and should be treated with real scepticism.

Set the review date in the diary at the start. If the agreed document has not moved after eight weeks of weekly sessions, the right decision is a different tutor or a different diagnosis, not more of the same hours. That is a harder conversation to have after six months of invoices than after two, which is the practical reason to fix the date in advance.
bullets: Name the document before you buy the hours: a timed paper or a criterion grid
Sit the baseline paper under examination conditions, not as homework
Expect specific, diagnosable gains in eight weeks; not a grade promise
Put the review date in the diary on day one

sections.heading: What the Dhahran school market can and cannot staff
paragraphs: The international schools within reach of Dhahran are small by the standards of a large city system, and small cohorts create a staffing arithmetic that no amount of goodwill solves. A Diploma Programme physics group might hold a dozen students split across Higher and Standard Level in two year groups, taught by one specialist. That teacher can deliver the course. What they cannot do is run a second parallel pass through the Higher Level extension topics for the three students who need it, because there is no second teacher and no spare timetable slot.

This is why the subjects that recur in Eastern Province tutoring enquiries are so predictable. They are the ones where a school needs a scarce specialist and can only justify one: Higher Level Physics, Higher Level Chemistry, Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, Computer Science, and Design Technology. Add the subjects a school may not be able to run at all in a given year because too few students opted for them, and the pattern is complete. None of this reflects badly on the schools; it is what a small cohort looks like from the inside.

The engineering-led household culture around the Aramco camp and the university compounds sharpens the effect. Subject choices skew hard towards the physics, chemistry and mathematics combination that opens engineering and medicine applications, so demand concentrates on exactly the subjects where local cover is thinnest. A family in a city with twenty international schools has options; a family here has the school's one specialist and whoever they can reach beyond the city.

The practical conclusion is that the question to ask a school is not whether it teaches a subject but what happens when a student falls behind in it. The answer tells you whether an outside tutor is a luxury or the only available route, and it is a question with a concrete answer: a named teacher with named clinic hours, or nothing.

sections.heading: The four documents that tell you where a student actually stands
paragraphs: Parents in Dhahran are, as a group, unusually comfortable with evidence. The same instinct that reads a well-plotted graph at work applies here, and it changes the first conversation for the better. There are four documents worth putting in front of a prospective tutor, and a tutor's reaction to them is itself a useful signal.

The marked past paper with the mark scheme beside it is the most informative of the four. It separates three different failures that look identical on a report card: the student did not know the content, the student knew it and could not produce it under time pressure, or the student answered a different question from the one asked. Each needs a different intervention, and a tutor who cannot tell you which one they are seeing after twenty minutes with the paper is guessing.

The criterion grid for an Internal Assessment is the second. Internal Assessment marks are awarded criterion by criterion against published descriptors, so a weak mark is always a weak criterion, and that is specific enough to act on. The third is the predicted grade together with the teacher's reasoning, which tells you what the school thinks and on what basis. A predicted grade is a professional judgement made from the evidence available at the time; it is not a promise, and it is not a ceiling either.

The fourth document does not exist until you make it: the student's own list of the questions they skip. Ask a student to go through a paper and mark every question they would leave until last, and the pattern that emerges is usually sharper than anything on the report card. It also hands the student part-ownership of the diagnosis, which matters more at sixteen than at eleven.

sections.heading: What tuition costs in the Eastern Province, and what moves the number
paragraphs: Rates in this market are published inconsistently, so the only honest way to discuss them is to say who advertises what. The figures below are advertised rates taken from tutoring platforms, marketplace guides and tutoring companies serving the Kingdom. They are not a market average, they are not what IB Gram charges, and a single advertised number tells you nothing on its own: the same hour at the same price can be a subject specialist or a generalist with a textbook.

What actually moves an hourly rate, in rough order of weight, is subject scarcity first. A Higher Level Physics or Mathematics AA HL specialist costs more than a Standard Level mathematics tutor in every market on earth, because the pool is smaller. After that comes marking or examining experience, then level — Higher Level above Standard Level, above the MYP, above IGCSE — then whether the tutor travels, and then package length. A visiting tutor in this cluster is paid for the driving as well as the teaching, and in a conurbation an hour across, the driving is not a rounding error.

The useful question is not what the rate is but what the hour contains. An hour that includes marked work returned before the next session, a written note to the parent, and a diagnostic the tutor can show you is a different product from an hour of talking through the topic the student mentioned at the start. Ask what happens between sessions, and whether the first session is diagnostic. The answer is more predictive of value than the number.

Treat advertised rates as a floor rather than a quotation, and treat a quoted figure far below the band as information about what is being bought. There is a legitimate place for a cheaper non-specialist: if the problem is IGCSE arithmetic fluency, a capable generalist who sets and marks practice is better value than an examiner. If the problem is Paper 2 mechanism marks in Chemistry HL, it is not.

sections.heading: A Sunday-to-Thursday week, a UTC+3 clock, and a tutor somewhere else
paragraphs: The school week in the Kingdom runs Sunday to Thursday, and Friday and Saturday are the weekend. Most tutoring copy written for this market is inherited from British or Indian pages and quietly assumes the opposite, which is how a family ends up offered a Saturday morning slot as though it were a weekday. The working week is the organising fact of any schedule here, and the usable weekday window for a Dhahran student is roughly between the end of the school run and the point where a teenager stops absorbing anything, which in practice means late afternoon to mid-evening.

Arabia Standard Time is UTC+3 and the Kingdom does not change its clocks. That makes a slot agreed with a tutor in a country that does observe daylight saving drift by an hour twice a year unless the slot is pinned to Dhahran local time rather than to the tutor's. It is a small administrative point that causes a disproportionate amount of disruption, because the drift lands in the middle of a term and collides with whatever else occupies that hour.

The table below sets the common tutor locations against a five o'clock Dhahran slot. The pattern worth noticing is that a tutor in India or Pakistan is teaching in their own evening, which is sustainable; a tutor in the United Kingdom is teaching in their afternoon, which collides with a school day if they are also a serving teacher; and a tutor further east is teaching very late at night, which is not a durable weekly arrangement whatever they say at the outset.

Study patterns also shift during Ramadan, when school days shorten and evening routines change. The sensible approach is to agree a different slot for that period in advance rather than improvising week to week, and to accept that the shape of the week will be different rather than pretending it is not. Ramadan moves roughly eleven days earlier against the Gregorian calendar each year, so it drifts across the academic year and lands in a different part of the course each time.

sections.heading: Online one-to-one against a visiting tutor in the Dhahran cluster
paragraphs: This is the comparison most Dhahran families are actually making, and it deserves a straight answer rather than a sales pitch. IB Gram delivers lessons online, one to one, over live video; we do not arrange visits to a Saudi address, and home visiting is something we run only in India. The argument for the online format in this particular cluster is not a general claim about technology. It is about what the geography does to the tutor pool.

Dammam, Al Khobar and Dhahran work as a single catchment that takes close to an hour to cross in traffic, with controlled access at the camp and the university compounds on top. A visiting tutor therefore has a realistic radius of a few neighbourhoods, and within that radius the number of people who can teach Physics HL at examination standard is small. Pay for the travel and you are paying a premium for proximity, which is the one variable that has no effect on whether the mark scheme gets explained properly.

An online session removes distance from the matching problem entirely. The pool becomes everyone who can teach that syllabus at that level and is awake at five in the afternoon Dhahran time, which for Higher Level Physics is the difference between a shortlist of one and a shortlist worth choosing from. It also removes the quiet cost of a visiting arrangement: the session that is cancelled because the tutor is stuck on the Dammam road, and the twenty minutes of settling either side of the hour you paid for.

There are genuine trade-offs and it is worth naming them. A young child works better with someone in the room. A practical subject needs the school's laboratory whatever happens in a tutorial. A student who will not engage on screen is not going to be fixed by a better platform. For a Diploma Programme student working through past papers, though, a shared screen with the paper and the mark scheme side by side is the same experience as sitting next to someone, and it starts on time.

sections.heading: How to verify what a tutor tells you about themselves
paragraphs: Every tutoring market contains claims that are easy to make and hard to check, and this one is no exception. The claims worth testing are specific: that the tutor has examined the subject, that they know this syllabus rather than the subject in general, that they have taught at this level, and that they have worked with students in a Saudi school context. Each has a question that produces a verifiable answer, and each has a vague answer that tells you to keep looking.

Examining experience is the claim most often stretched. The question that settles it is not whether they have examined but what they marked, for which board, and which component. Someone who has marked a specific paper will tell you what the mark scheme does with a borderline answer, what the commonest error in that component is, and what moderation felt like. Someone who has not will talk about examinations in general terms. You do not need to verify a certificate to hear the difference.

Syllabus knowledge is testable in about ninety seconds. Ask what changed in the current subject guide, which topic students find hardest in the first term, and what the Internal Assessment criteria are called in that subject. A specialist answers without hesitating because they have taught it this term. A generalist describes the subject rather than the course. For an IGCSE subject, ask for the syllabus code and check it against your child's paper: a tutor who does not know whether they teach 0620 or 0654 does not teach either regularly.

Then there is the claim nobody can support. Results claims without a sample size, a date and a method are not evidence of anything, and a figure like a satisfaction percentage or a star rating without a verifiable source is marketing. The honest answer to "how much will my child improve" is a description of what gets measured and when, not a number. Treat a confident number as a reason to ask one more question.

sections.heading: Academic honesty on the Internal Assessment, the Extended Essay and the Personal Project
paragraphs: This part of the market has a problem, and a Dhahran family browsing search results will meet it quickly. Several providers advertise help with the Internal Assessment and the Extended Essay in language that is deliberately ambiguous about who produces the work. The line is not ambiguous at all under the rules the student is assessed by: assessed work must be the student's own, and a school that suspects otherwise has a malpractice process to follow that can cost the student the qualification.

What a tutor may legitimately do is substantial. They may help a student choose a research question that is actually investigable, explain what each assessment criterion rewards, read a draft and say which criterion is underserved, ask hard questions about method and evidence, point out that a conclusion does not follow from the data, and teach the referencing convention. They may also teach the content the student needs in order to do the work. None of that produces a single sentence of the submitted document.

What a tutor may never do is write, rewrite, redraft, edit in, or supply text, data or analysis for an assessed piece. The test is simple and worth applying yourself: if the finished work contains a sentence, a calculation or an idea the student cannot explain and defend in their own words, something has gone wrong. Schools are also required to keep a record of supervision, and students are asked to reflect on their own process, which makes substituted work easier to detect than families often assume.

For the Personal Project in the final MYP year and for the Extended Essay, the supervisor at school owns the formal process, including the number of formally recorded meetings. An outside tutor works alongside that, not instead of it, and the supervisor should know an outside tutor is involved. If a provider offers to handle a draft rather than discuss it, that is the point to stop the conversation.

sections.heading: Equivalency, Qudurat and Tahsili for an Eastern Province school leaver
paragraphs: Families in Dhahran split roughly into those applying overseas and those applying to Saudi universities, and a large number keep both routes open. The Saudi route involves three mechanisms that almost nothing in the tutoring market explains, and getting them wrong late is expensive in a way that a weak unit test never is.

The first is equivalency, the mu'adalah decision issued by the Ministry of Education. A foreign or international school certificate — an IB Diploma, A Levels, an American high school diploma — is not automatically treated as equivalent to the Saudi secondary certificate. It has to go through an equivalency process before a Saudi university will accept it. The process has documentary requirements, and some universities state a maximum age for the certificate they will accept, so it is worth establishing the steps in the first year of the Diploma rather than after results.

The second and third are the Qiyas tests run by the National Center for Assessment under the Education and Training Evaluation Commission. Qudurat, the General Aptitude Test, assesses verbal and quantitative reasoning rather than syllabus content, and is sat in Arabic or English. Tahsili, the Achievement Test, covers the science-stream subjects — mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology and English — and its content follows the Saudi national curriculum. That last detail is the one international-curriculum families most need to hear: an IB or IGCSE student has studied material that overlaps with Tahsili without being framed the way Tahsili frames it.

The practical consequence is that Tahsili preparation is a mapping exercise, not a revision exercise. A Higher Level chemistry student is not short of chemistry; they are unfamiliar with how the national curriculum sequences and words it. Universities publish their own admission formulas combining school grades with the Qiyas results, weighted differently by university and by programme, with competitive engineering, medicine and science programmes leaning hardest on Tahsili. The weightings and any thresholds change, so the only reliable source is the university's own published admission criteria for the intake you are applying to.

sections.heading: Getting started from Dhahran, including what happens when nobody is free
paragraphs: The first conversation is a diagnosis, not a sale, and it goes faster if you arrive with the evidence described earlier: a marked paper, a criterion grid if coursework is involved, the predicted grade, and the subject and level written down exactly as the school writes it. "Maths" is four different courses at Diploma Programme level; "Maths AA HL" is one. Half the mismatches in this market start with a vague subject line.

After that comes a trial session with the proposed tutor, which should be diagnostic rather than a lesson. A useful trial produces three things: a short written account of where the student stands, a named first target, and the tutor's own view of how long it will take. If a trial produces only enthusiasm, you have learned nothing you can act on, and that is a reason to try a different tutor rather than to buy a package.

Sometimes the honest answer is that nobody suitable is free at the hour you need. Higher Level Physics at five in the afternoon Dhahran time is a narrow intersection, and in that case the options are a different slot, a waiting period, or starting with a related subject while the right person becomes available. We would rather say that than put a Standard Level biology tutor in front of a Physics HL student and let you discover the difference in the third week. A family that is told no once tends to trust the yes.

Then the arrangement should be reviewed on the date you set at the beginning, against the document you named. Weekly lessons that have become a habit nobody evaluates are the commonest way tutoring money is wasted, in Dhahran and everywhere else. Either the evidence moved or it did not; both answers are useful, and only one of them means carrying on unchanged.
bullets: Bring the subject and level exactly as the school writes it, plus a marked paper
Expect the trial to produce a written diagnosis and a named first target
Accept a waiting period over a mismatched specialist, especially at Higher Level
Review on the agreed date against the agreed document, not on impressions

process.title: Tell us the subject, the level and the series
process.description: The exact course title as the school writes it, the level, the board, and which series the student is working towards. For an IGCSE subject the syllabus code removes any remaining ambiguity. This is a two-minute step that prevents the commonest matching error in this market: the right subject at the wrong level.

process.title: Send the evidence you already have
process.description: A marked past paper with the mark scheme, the latest report, an Internal Assessment criterion grid, or the predicted grade and the reasoning behind it. Anything that shows marks rather than impressions. This is what a tutor reads before the trial, and it is what the first target gets set against.

process.title: Meet the proposed tutor in a trial session
process.description: A free diagnostic session with the specialist we think fits, run live over video at a Dhahran-friendly hour. The output is a written account of where the student stands and one named target, not a sales conversation. If the fit is wrong, say so and meet someone else.

process.title: Fix the slot to the Sunday-to-Thursday week
process.description: Agree a weekly time pinned to Dhahran local time rather than to the tutor's clock, so nothing drifts when another country changes its clocks. Late afternoon and early evening suit most Eastern Province school runs; Friday mornings are kept for intensive blocks before a series.

process.title: Review on the date you set at the start
process.description: Sit the comparison paper, or revisit the criterion grid, and decide on evidence. Carry on, change the plan, change the tutor, or stop. All four are legitimate outcomes, and deciding on the agreed date is what keeps the arrangement honest.

whyPoints.title: Matched by syllabus, not by distance
whyPoints.description: The constraint in the Dhahran cluster is the size of the local specialist pool, not the willingness of anyone to drive. Teaching online removes distance from the matching decision, so a Physics HL student is matched to a Physics HL teacher rather than to the nearest available adult with a science degree.

whyPoints.title: Built around the Saudi week and the Saudi clock
whyPoints.description: Slots are set Sunday to Thursday and pinned to Arabia Standard Time, so a tutor in a country that observes daylight saving does not drag your slot an hour sideways mid-term. Friday and Saturday are available for intensive blocks, when the school week is not competing for the time.

whyPoints.title: Diagnosis first, and in writing
whyPoints.description: Every arrangement starts with a baseline you can see: a timed paper marked against the published scheme, or a criterion-by-criterion read of a draft. A named target and a review date come out of the first session, which is what makes it possible to tell later whether the hours did anything.

whyPoints.title: Coursework reviewed, never written
whyPoints.description: A tutor reads the student's own Internal Assessment, exploration, project or essay, maps it against the published criteria and asks the questions an examiner would ask. They do not draft, rewrite or supply text or data. That line is the whole of our position on assessed work, and it is not negotiable.

whyPoints.title: No claims we cannot support
whyPoints.description: No grade guarantees, no satisfaction percentages, no star ratings, no regulator or board endorsement. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or partnership from the Ministry of Education, the Education and Training Evaluation Commission, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and has no affiliation with any school named on this page.

whyPoints.title: An honest no when there is no match
whyPoints.description: Scarce Higher Level subjects at a narrow hour sometimes have no specialist free. We say so, and offer a different slot, a waiting period or a different starting subject, rather than filling the hour with someone who teaches the subject at a lower level and hoping the gap is not noticed.

faqs.question: What does a Physics HL lesson look like on screen when the student is in Dhahran and the tutor is not?
faqs.answer: The paper and the mark scheme sit side by side on a shared screen, and the tutor annotates as the student works. A graphics tablet lets the tutor draw free-body diagrams and circuits by hand, which matters in physics because the diagram carries marks of its own. The student works problems live rather than watching, because a session where the tutor does the physics teaches very little. Most sessions end with a timed question set as work before the next lesson, marked and returned with the mark scheme attached so the student sees where the marks sat.

faqs.question: How are circuit diagrams, graphs and working shared during an online science session?
faqs.answer: Through a shared whiteboard that both sides can draw on, usually with the tutor on a graphics tablet and the student either drawing on screen or working on paper and holding it to the camera. For graph work, plotting on paper and photographing it is often better practice than drawing on screen, because the examination is sat with a pencil and a ruler. Scanned or photographed written work sent before the session lets the tutor mark it in advance and spend the lesson on the errors rather than on reading.

faqs.question: Is a lesson recorded, and who in a Dhahran family can watch it back?
faqs.answer: Recording is arranged with the family rather than assumed. Where a family wants it, the recording goes to that family and is used for revision; it is not shared further or used for anything else. Many students find the recording most useful for a dense Higher Level topic they want to replay at their own pace, and least useful for a past-paper session they have already annotated. If you would rather no recording existed, say so at the start and none is made.

faqs.question: What happens if the connection drops in the middle of a session on the Aramco camp?
faqs.answer: The tutor waits and reconnects, and if the connection does not come back within a few minutes the remaining time is rescheduled rather than lost. A dropped connection is a logistics problem, not a reason to pay for silence. In practice the fix is usually mundane: a wired connection or a phone hotspot as a fallback, the camera off if the line is poor so the audio and the shared screen hold, and the working typed or photographed rather than relying on video quality.

faqs.question: Does a Dhahran student need a laptop, or is a tablet enough for a Mathematics AA HL session?
faqs.answer: A laptop with a separate sheet of paper is the better setup for mathematics, because the student needs to write by hand at speed while reading the screen. A tablet works if it is paired with a stylus and the student is already comfortable writing on it, but a tablet used as a screen with paper beside it is cramped for a ninety-minute session. Headphones matter more than most families expect, and a second device propped as a document camera turns a phone into a way of showing handwritten working instantly.

faqs.question: What does a parent in Dhahran receive after each session?
faqs.answer: A short written note naming what was covered, what the student got right, what is still wrong and what has been set before the next lesson. It is deliberately brief and specific rather than encouraging in general terms, because a note that says the session went well is not information. Over a term those notes become the record you review against the original target, which is why they name topics and components rather than describing effort. Ask for them if they do not arrive.

faqs.question: What do Eastern Province families pay for one-to-one IB tuition, and what moves the figure?
faqs.answer: Advertised rates in this market run from around SAR 35 an hour on budget online platforms to SAR 200 and above for senior-school examination subjects, with IB subject tutoring advertised from about SAR 180 and premium Higher Level tracks around SAR 200 to 220. Those are advertised figures published by platforms, marketplace guides and tutoring companies, not a market average and not our price. What moves the number is subject scarcity first, then marking experience, then level, then whether the tutor travels, then how long the package is.

faqs.question: Why does a Physics HL specialist cost more per hour than a Biology SL tutor?
faqs.answer: Because the pool is smaller, not because the hour is longer. Many graduates can teach Standard Level biology competently; far fewer can teach the Higher Level physics extension topics and explain what the mark scheme does with a borderline extended response. Scarcity sets the rate in every tutoring market. Level compounds it: Higher Level sits above Standard Level, which sits above the MYP and IGCSE. If a quoted Physics HL rate looks like a Standard Level biology rate, the useful question is what the tutor has actually taught at Higher Level.

faqs.question: What happens in the free trial lesson before a Dhahran family commits to anything?
faqs.answer: It is a diagnostic session rather than a sample lesson. The tutor works through a piece of the student's own marked work or a short timed question set, establishes where the marks are being lost, and writes a short account of what they found with one named first target. You should finish it knowing something you did not know before. If the trial produces only reassurance, that is a reason to meet a different tutor rather than to buy hours, and saying so costs nothing at that stage.

faqs.question: Is a small group ever better value than one-to-one for Mathematics AI SL?
faqs.answer: Occasionally, and it depends on what is broken. If three students share the same gap in interpreting calculator output, a group can work, because the discussion is part of the teaching and the rate per student falls. If the problem is that one student cannot manipulate algebra at speed, a group hour gives them a share of the attention and a full share of the pace. For Standard Level content revision a group can be reasonable value; for technique faults specific to one student it rarely is.

faqs.question: Does the hourly rate change in the weeks before the May session?
faqs.answer: Demand concentrates sharply in the run-up to examinations, and what changes most is availability rather than price. The specialists with examining experience fill up first, so a family that starts looking a month before the papers is choosing from whoever is left at the hour they need. If an intensive block is part of the plan, book the slot early even if it starts later. Treat a provider who raises a rate because the series is close as information about how they operate.

faqs.question: What should a family expect to pay for Internal Assessment feedback compared with a teaching hour?
faqs.answer: It is usually charged as ordinary session time, because that is what it is: a tutor reads the draft against the published criteria beforehand and spends the session asking the questions an examiner would ask. The reading happens outside the hour. What should concern you is any provider charging a separate fixed fee per draft, because that tends to describe a product where the document comes back improved rather than the student coming back better informed. Ask exactly what will be returned before agreeing to anything.

faqs.question: How do I check that a tutor has genuinely examined Chemistry HL rather than only taught it?
faqs.answer: Ask which board, which component and which paper they marked, then ask what the mark scheme does with a borderline answer on that component. Someone who has marked it describes moderation, the commonest error and how method marks are allocated when the final answer is wrong. Someone who has not talks about examinations in general. You are not verifying a certificate; you are listening for the specificity that only comes from having sat with a batch of scripts and a scheme.

faqs.question: Does it matter whether a tutor has taught in the Kingdom before, for a KFUPM-bound student?
faqs.answer: Less than families expect for the teaching, more than they expect for the logistics. Subject expertise does not change with geography: the Higher Level physics syllabus is identical in Dhahran and anywhere else. What local experience buys is an understanding of the Sunday-to-Thursday week, of how a compound school day is shaped, and of what equivalency and the Qiyas tests mean for a student applying to a Saudi university. A tutor who asks about the school's calendar and the series before the first lesson has it; one who assumes a Monday-to-Friday week does not.

faqs.question: What happens if the match is wrong after the second lesson?
faqs.answer: Say so, and we change the tutor rather than persuade you to persevere. A mismatch after two sessions is usually about teaching style, pace or rapport rather than competence, and none of those improve by being endured. The useful thing to send is specific: the student switched off at this point, the explanations assume knowledge they do not have, the pace is too slow for them. That makes the second match better rather than merely different, and it is the same information the next tutor needs anyway.

faqs.question: What should a Dhahran parent ask a prospective Mathematics AA HL tutor in the first ten minutes?
faqs.answer: Four questions. Which topics in the Higher Level course do students find hardest in the first term, and why? What does Paper 1 without a calculator expose that Paper 2 does not? What are the assessment criteria for the mathematical exploration called, and which one is most often underserved? And what will you not do with my child's exploration? The answers are either specific and immediate, or general and reassuring. The first means they taught it this term; the second means they read about it.

dhahran.closingHeading: What to do next if your child is in a Dhahran school
dhahran.closingBody: Write down the subject and level exactly as the school writes it, find the most recent marked paper with its mark scheme, and note one thing you want measurably different in eight weeks. Send those three things and we will put a subject specialist in front of your child for a free diagnostic session, live over video at an hour that fits the Sunday-to-Thursday week. You will get a written account of where the student stands and one named target out of it. If the fit is wrong, we change the tutor; if no specialist is free at your hour, we say so rather than substituting someone who teaches the subject at a lower level.
