intro.heading: One decision, four answers, and only one of them is a person you choose
paragraphs: The search for an Edexcel IGCSE home tutor is usually the end of a short and frustrating process. A report has come home, a department has said the student is capable of more, and the family has decided to buy help. From there the real decision has four answers: take whatever extra sessions the school offers, hire somebody local who will travel, book a group revision course, or match a specialist one-to-one. Each is right in different circumstances, and the fourth is the only one where you genuinely choose the individual teacher. That is the whole argument of this page. The temptation is to skip the decision and book the first available tutor, which is how families end up paying for a term of general revision before anybody has worked out what is actually wrong.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE is a different animal from Cambridge in ways that matter when hiring. It grades on the 9 to 1 scale rather than in letters. Mathematics A 4MA1 is tiered Foundation and Higher while most other subjects are untiered. The sciences examine practical skills inside the written papers rather than in a separate practical session. A tutor who has spent a career on Cambridge syllabuses can teach the content perfectly and still misread what the Pearson papers ask for, which is a specification problem rather than a knowledge problem.

Fewer Saudi schools enter Edexcel than Cambridge, and that changes the market. The local pool of tutors who have actually taught 4PM1 Further Pure Mathematics or 4ET1 English Literature to Pearson candidates is small in Riyadh and Jeddah and effectively empty elsewhere. An in-home arrangement is limited to whoever lives within a reasonable drive, and the rate carries that travel whether or not anyone itemises it. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a Saudi address; home visits are a service offered only in India. What we match is one-to-one teaching over live video.

So the recommendation, stated before the detail rather than after it: exhaust the school's own support first because it is free and informed, then buy one diagnosed hour from somebody who has taught your child's exact specification, and only then decide how many hours to commit. The sections below give you the four options side by side, the questions that separate a Pearson specialist from a general science or English teacher, what the Saudi market advertises, what a parent actually sees in an online session, and the university step that sits at the end of the road. None of this needs a long commitment to begin. One hour, one marked paper and one honest written answer is enough to tell you whether the problem is content, technique or motivation, and those three need different purchases.

edexcel-igcse-home-tutor.programmesIntro: Pearson runs a route from lower secondary into the International GCSE years, and most Saudi families meet it in Year 10. These are the three stages a tutor gets asked for.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International Lower Secondary
programmes.description: The curriculum many British-curriculum schools in the Kingdom run before the International GCSE years. It is not certificated in the way the later years are.
programmes.countryNote: Schools here set their own internal assessments at this stage, so a Year 9 grade means whatever that department means by it. Ask what it was measured against.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Two years to a grade on the 9 to 1 scale. Mathematics A is tiered Foundation and Higher; most other subjects are single-tier. Practical and investigative skills in the sciences are examined inside the written papers.
programmes.countryNote: Saudi candidates sit the June series as the main one and the November series for resits and November entries. Entry decisions and the component list belong to your school, and the examinations officer holds the deadlines.

programmes.name: What the Edexcel years feed into
programmes.description: Most candidates continue to A Levels or into the IB Diploma. Which grades a student holds decides which post-16 subjects a school will allow.
programmes.countryNote: A Saudi university needs an equivalency decision from the Ministry of Education on the final school certificate. The International GCSE results sit inside that file as supporting evidence rather than as the qualification being recognised.

edexcel-igcse-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: Pearson identifies every course by a specification code, and the code is what a tutor should be able to talk about. These are the eight Saudi families ask for most on this route.

subjects.name: Edexcel Physics 4PH1
subjects.description: Two written papers with practical and investigative skills examined inside them. Rearranging equations under time pressure and describing a method precisely are the two skills that separate grades here.

subjects.name: Edexcel Chemistry 4CH1
subjects.description: Moles, electrolysis and organic reactions carry most of the lost marks. Candidates who can do the arithmetic still lose marks on state symbols and observation wording.

subjects.name: Edexcel Biology 4BI1
subjects.description: Definitions are marked tightly and the longer questions reward linked reasoning over lists. Experimental design questions are the part most often untaught, because they sit awkwardly in a crowded scheme of work.

subjects.name: Edexcel Science Double Award 4SD0
subjects.description: Two grades from combined biology, chemistry and physics content. One tutor rarely covers all three credibly, so families often buy the weakest science separately and leave the rest with the school.

subjects.name: Edexcel English Language A 4EA1
subjects.description: Non-fiction reading and transactional writing, with a prescribed anthology. Marks go on precise selection and control of register, so fluent speakers underperform.

subjects.name: Edexcel English Literature 4ET1
subjects.description: Set texts, unseen poetry and extract-based questions. The hardest component is the unseen, where there is no revision to fall back on.

subjects.name: Edexcel History 4HI1
subjects.description: Source handling and extended writing are assessed as separate skills. Most candidates are markedly better at one than the other, and a single marked paper shows which.

subjects.name: Edexcel Geography 4GE1
subjects.description: Physical and human topics plus fieldwork-style data questions. The data response is what a tutor repairs quickest, because it rewards method over more case studies.

edexcel-igcse-home-tutor.regionsTitle: Where Edexcel families are, and what that does to the choice
edexcel-igcse-home-tutor.regionsIntro: Edexcel entries sit mostly in British-curriculum schools. Where you live decides how real the in-home option is.

regions.name: Riyadh

regions.name: Jeddah
regions.note: British-curriculum schools along the coastal spine make Edexcel common, but the city's length means an in-home tutor charges for the drive twice over.

regions.name: Al Khobar and Dhahran
regions.note: British and Cambridge curricula are both well established. Edexcel candidates here are often in smaller cohorts, so a subject may be taught by one teacher with no second opinion available.

regions.name: Jubail and Yanbu
regions.note: Industrial cities where camp and company schooling shapes the week. Parents on rotation often need a slot that moves with the shift pattern.

regions.name: Tabuk, AlUla and NEOM
regions.note: A changing picture with families arriving part-way through a course. Mid-year joiners who need a specification they have never seen are the typical request from here.

regions.name: Buraidah, Hail and Najran
regions.note: Few or no international schools, so a local in-home Pearson tutor is not a realistic option at all. Distance is the constraint.

schoolClusters.note: British-curriculum and IB schools share the capital, and some hold more than one route. Confirm with the school whether the senior sets are entered with Pearson or Cambridge before hiring anyone.
The Jeddah spine and the Dammam cluster both hold long-established British-curriculum schools. Subject availability at senior level varies by campus rather than by city.

sections.heading: The four answers, and the one we would recommend
paragraphs: Start with the school, because it is free and because the people running it set the mock papers. The limit is structural rather than one of goodwill: a department that cannot staff a subject properly in the timetable will not staff it better at four in the afternoon, and in a small Edexcel cohort the teacher running the extra session is the same teacher whose lessons produced the gap. Ask who will run it, how many students will be there, and what the sessions will actually cover.

A local in-home tutor buys presence, which is the right purchase for a student who will not work unless an adult is in the room. It is available in Riyadh, Jeddah and the Dammam cluster and not much elsewhere, the rate carries travel, and the choice is restricted to whoever lives nearby and happens to know the Pearson specification. A group revision course buys timed practice cheaply and is paced for the middle of the room, which suits a candidate who understands the content and needs mileage.

Our recommendation is sequential rather than exclusive. Take the school's sessions. Buy one diagnosed hour from somebody who has taught the exact specification code. Read the diagnosis, then decide how many hours to commit and in which component. Families who buy a term of general revision before they know what is wrong usually pay twice, once for the wrong tutoring and once for the right. sections.heading: How to tell a Pearson specialist from a good teacher
paragraphs: Four separate claims hide inside the word qualified, and they are worth pulling apart before any money moves. A degree proves subject knowledge well above International GCSE level. A teaching qualification proves training in how teenagers learn. Having taught the specification proves familiarity with the component structure, the prescribed anthology or set texts, and the sequence a school uses. Having marked for the board proves the narrowest and most useful thing of all, which is knowing what the scheme credits and what it silently refuses.

Only the last two change what happens in an Edexcel lesson, and both can be verified in fifteen minutes. Ask which specification codes they have taught and in which series. Ask what the practical and investigative skills questions look like in the Pearson science papers, since a Cambridge-trained tutor will reach for a separate practical paper that does not exist here. Ask them to describe how a six-mark extended answer is marked, and listen for whether the answer is counted in marks or described in adjectives.

A good answer is specific and faintly dull. It sounds like a teacher saying that their candidates lose the same two marks on the same part of the same question every series, naming the part, and describing the fix in terms of what the student writes rather than what the student understands. A weak answer talks about rapport, confidence and passion for the subject. Those matter, and they are not what is being bought at a specialist rate. Write the answers down and compare them across providers.

sections.heading: What the in-home market charges, and what travel does to it
paragraphs: Every published Saudi figure is vendor marketing, so treat all of them as advertised rates rather than as a market average. Tutoring-platform listings begin near SAR 55 an hour for general, non-specialist support, and budget platforms advertise one-to-one IGCSE help from around SAR 35. A tutor-marketplace guide puts general private tuition in Riyadh near SAR 50 an hour at primary level and above SAR 200 for senior-school examination subjects. Some international providers quote in dollars, around $60 an hour. None of these is what IB Gram charges.

An in-home rate carries travel loading whether or not it appears on the invoice. A tutor crossing Riyadh in the early evening sells two hours of their day for one hour of teaching, and the number reflects that. The same arithmetic explains why the in-home pool collapses outside the three big urban clusters: there is no rate at which a 4PM1 specialist drives to Buraidah twice a week. Scarcity of the specification, not distance alone, is what moves the figure.

What the published bands are genuinely useful for is calibration. A quote at the bottom of the range for a scarce Pearson specialism should prompt a question about what is missing: marking between lessons, a written plan, familiarity with the component, or simply hours. A quote at the top should prompt a question about what the extra buys in terms a parent can check. Ask both questions out loud. A provider who cannot answer either is pricing on confidence rather than on content.

sections.heading: What a parent actually sees in an online Edexcel lesson
paragraphs: The mechanics are less exotic than the phrase online tutoring suggests. The tutor and the student share a video call and a shared whiteboard, and the paper being worked through is on the screen for both of them. For a 4PH1 physics question that needs a circuit drawn and a calculation written out, the tutor annotates the diagram while the student writes the working, and both halves stay visible. A graphics tablet at the tutor's end does most of the work, and the student needs nothing more exotic than a laptop and a pen.

Written work still happens on paper, which surprises families. A candidate should sit a full past paper by hand, under time, because that is what the examination is, and then photograph it for the tutor to mark against the published scheme. The marked script comes back annotated. That cycle is the single most valuable thing in the arrangement, and it is also the first thing a cheap hourly rate quietly removes, so ask whether marking is included before you compare two numbers.

What the parent sees is a short note after each session saying what was covered, what was set, and what the next session will do, plus the marked papers as they accumulate. Recordings are sometimes available and worth asking about, particularly for a candidate revisiting a difficult topic. A parent is welcome to sit in, though for most teenagers it changes the session for the worse. Judge the arrangement on the marked scripts, not on the atmosphere of the hour.

sections.heading: Foundation, Higher, and what no fee can change
paragraphs: Pearson grades International GCSE on the 9 to 1 scale, with 9 at the top. Mathematics A 4MA1 is tiered into Foundation and Higher, and the tier a candidate is entered for constrains the grade available to them, which makes it the most consequential administrative decision of the year. Most other Edexcel subjects are single-tier, so the ceiling question only bites in mathematics for most families. Confirm both the tier and the full component list with the school in writing.

The entry decision belongs to the department. It is made from classwork, mock performance and a judgement about risk, and it is reversible only before the entry deadline the examinations officer works to. A family that learns in the spring term that their child sits Foundation has learned it too late to change. The useful purchase is early and small: a specialist reading marked work and saying whether Higher is realistic, with the questions that produced the view.

What that buys is an argument in the right language. No tutor can promise a school will change an entry, and anyone who does is overselling. What a written view does is replace a parent's impression with somebody's reading of the mark scheme, which carries differently in a head of department's office. The same logic applies after results: a grade sitting just below a boundary and out of line with everything else the candidate produced is worth asking the school to look at component by component.

sections.heading: Equivalency, Qudurat and Tahsili at the end of the road
paragraphs: An international school certificate is not automatically equivalent to the Saudi secondary certificate. The step that makes it usable is an equivalency decision from the Ministry of Education, and it applies to A Levels, the IB Diploma and an American high school diploma alike. The International GCSE results sit inside that file as supporting evidence rather than as the qualification being recognised, which is why the grading scale sometimes needs explaining: a 9 to 1 statement of results is less familiar to some readers than letter grades.

Qudurat, the General Aptitude Test, is run by the Education and Training Evaluation Commission through its National Center for Assessment, known as Qiyas. It tests verbal and quantitative reasoning rather than taught content, and is sat in Arabic or English. Tahsili, the Achievement Test, covers mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology and English, and its content follows the Saudi national curriculum. That is precisely why a strong Edexcel candidate can find it unfamiliar: the material overlaps but the framing and the expected approach do not.

Universities publish their own criteria combining school grades with the Qiyas tests, and the weightings differ by institution and by programme. This page publishes no threshold and no formula, because those change and because the only reliable source is the university's own published criteria for the specific programme. What the Edexcel years contribute is groundwork: keeping the sciences and mathematics through to the final grade covers most of the content Tahsili draws on, even where the question style is new.

sections.heading: The first month, and what to do if it is not working
paragraphs: A reasonable first month produces three things: a written plan naming the component and the question types, at least one full paper done to time and marked against the published scheme, and a visible change in how the student writes an answer. Content knowledge moves slowly and technique moves fast, so the early evidence is usually in the shape of answers rather than in a grade. Ask to see the marked script rather than a progress report, because one of those is evidence and the other is prose.

If nothing has moved after four sessions, the cause is one of three things and they need different fixes. The diagnosis was wrong, in which case ask for it again from the marked work. The student is not doing the work set between sessions, in which case fewer hours and firmer homework beats more hours. Or the match is wrong, which happens and is nobody's fault. A tutor who is competent but not landing with this particular teenager is still the wrong tutor.

Changing tutor should cost a conversation rather than a term. Ask for the plan and the marked papers to be handed over, keep the slot, and expect the new tutor to re-diagnose rather than to inherit somebody's conclusions. The one thing worth protecting through a change is the evening itself: a mid-week slot already carved out of a Sunday-to-Thursday household is harder to replace than a tutor, which is the reverse of what most families assume.

faqs.question: What does an Edexcel International GCSE home tutor advertise per hour in Riyadh, and what is folded into that number?
faqs.answer: Published figures in the Kingdom are vendor marketing, so read them as advertised rates. A tutor-marketplace guide puts senior-school examination subjects above SAR 200 an hour in Riyadh, while budget platforms advertise one-to-one from around SAR 35. The spread reflects travel loading, how scarce the specification is, whether marking between lessons is included, and how much examining the tutor has actually done. Ask which of those four a quote includes.

faqs.question: Does a 4CH1 Chemistry tutor cost more than a 4BI1 Biology one at the same level?
faqs.answer: Usually a little, and the reason is supply rather than difficulty. More teachers are comfortable delivering biology to International GCSE standard than are comfortable with the quantitative side of chemistry, so the chemistry pool is smaller and the rate sits higher. The gap is modest compared with the jump to Further Pure Mathematics. If a provider quotes identical rates across every science, ask how they are matching tutors to specifications at all.

faqs.question: If we book an Edexcel tutor and the first month produces nothing measurable, what should happen to the fee?
faqs.answer: You should not be arguing about the fee; you should be re-diagnosing. Ask for the marked scripts and the original written plan, and check whether the work set between sessions was actually done. If the diagnosis was wrong, a reasonable tutor redoes it without charging for a second diagnosis. If the match is wrong, change tutor and keep the slot. Agree at the outset how notice and part-used packages are handled, in writing.

faqs.question: Is marking a full 4EA1 English paper between lessons charged as a lesson?
faqs.answer: It depends on the provider, and the answer tells you a lot. Marking a full English Language A paper against the published scheme takes close to an hour of skilled work, so a tutor who includes it at no extra charge is either absorbing it or not really doing it. Ask directly whether marking is inside the hourly rate, charged separately, or excluded. A slightly higher rate with marking included is usually cheaper per mark gained.

faqs.question: How many hours of Edexcel science support does one weak written paper usually need?
faqs.answer: Nobody can answer that honestly before seeing a marked paper, which is the point of a diagnosis. As a rough shape: a technique problem, where the candidate knows the content and loses marks on detail and command words, often moves within six to eight sessions. A genuine content gap across a year of teaching takes a term or more. Treat any number quoted before a paper has been seen as a guess.

faqs.question: Does Tahsili cover anything a 4PH1 Physics candidate has not met in the Edexcel specification?
faqs.answer: The physics content overlaps substantially, but the framing does not. Tahsili follows the Saudi national curriculum, so topic emphasis, notation and the expected solution style can all differ from what a Pearson candidate has practised, and the test is taken under a different kind of time pressure. Treat it as a separate preparation task rather than as revision of 4PH1. The overlap means the groundwork is done; it does not mean the test is familiar.

faqs.question: Is the 9 to 1 grading scale understood by Saudi universities, or does it need explaining in the file?
faqs.answer: Admissions offices that regularly read international transcripts handle it routinely, but it is sensible to assume it needs explaining rather than to assume it does not. Keep the Pearson statement of results with its own grade descriptions, and keep the school's explanation of the grading scale if one is issued. The equivalency decision on the final school certificate is the step that matters most; the International GCSE grades support it rather than carry it.

faqs.question: Does an Edexcel candidate aiming at an overseas engineering course need Further Pure Mathematics?
faqs.answer: It is rarely required and often useful. Overseas engineering offers are made on the post-16 qualification, so Further Pure Mathematics is not usually a stated condition. What it does is make the first year of A Level Mathematics or Diploma Higher Level mathematics noticeably less brutal, because calculus and series have already been met. Decide it alongside the post-16 plan rather than on its own.

faqs.question: How does the English requirement work for a student whose Edexcel English was 4ES1 rather than 4EA1?
faqs.answer: English as a Second Language and English Language A are different qualifications with different demands, and universities treat them differently. Some accept either as evidence of English; others specify a first-language qualification or a separate language test. This varies by institution and by programme, so the only safe route is to read the published entry requirements for the specific course. Where there is doubt, a separate recognised English test removes the question entirely.

faqs.question: At what age or stage does the equivalency step actually happen for a family on the Edexcel route?
faqs.answer: It happens around the final school certificate rather than during the International GCSE years, so for most families it arrives in the last year of school or just after it. The practical consequence is administrative: keep every statement of results, transcript and school letter from Year 10 onward, because assembling them retrospectively is the part families find hardest, particularly after a move between countries.

faqs.question: How does an online tutor handle an Edexcel physics question that needs a drawn circuit and a calculation in the same answer?
faqs.answer: On a shared whiteboard with both halves visible at once. The tutor draws and annotates the circuit using a graphics tablet while the student writes the working, and each can see the other's marks appear. For a question of this kind that is closer to sitting beside someone than a video call sounds, because the diagram and the algebra stay on screen together rather than competing for one sheet of paper.

faqs.question: What does a parent actually receive after each Edexcel session, and what should be in it?
faqs.answer: A short note is enough, and it should contain four things: what was covered, what was set for the week, what the student found hard, and what the next session will do. Adjectives are not information. Alongside the notes, the marked scripts should accumulate somewhere you can find them, because those are the evidence the arrangement is working. The marked papers are the record; the notes are only the commentary on them.

faqs.question: Does a student need a printer for Edexcel past papers, or does everything happen on screen?
faqs.answer: A printer helps and is not essential. Full papers should be written by hand under timed conditions because that is what the examination requires, so either print them or write the answers on paper beside the screen. The script is then photographed for marking. Doing everything on screen is fine for teaching and poor for rehearsal, because the handwriting load is part of what the paper tests.

faqs.question: How is an Edexcel English Literature extract annotated live when both sides are looking at the same page?
faqs.answer: The extract goes on the shared whiteboard and both people mark it up. The tutor underlines and questions while the student adds notes, and the annotation builds visibly rather than being handed over finished. For unseen poetry this is the whole method: the student has to see somebody else's reading being constructed in real time before they can construct their own, and the annotated page is saved for revision.

intro.heading: The hourly rate is the least informative number in the quote
paragraphs: A family comparing an Edexcel IGCSE online tutor against the alternatives is usually comparing hourly rates, which is the wrong comparison. The published figures in the Kingdom run from around SAR 35 an hour on budget platforms to above SAR 200 for senior-school examination subjects in a Riyadh marketplace guide, and both numbers are vendor marketing rather than a market average. The same hour can include a marked past paper, a written plan and a tutor who has examined the component, or it can include none of those. Two providers quoting the same figure are often selling different products, and the only comparison that means anything is cost per mark gained rather than cost per hour.

Set the four options against each other properly. The school's own extra sessions cost nothing in money and something in realism, because the department that could not staff the subject in the timetable is the department running them. A local in-home tutor costs the rate plus the travel folded into it, and the choice is limited to whoever lives within a drive. A group revision course costs least per head and is paced for the middle of the room, which is good value for a candidate who needs mileage and poor value for one with a specific weakness. One-to-one online costs most per hour and buys a specialist in the exact Pearson specification, chosen from anywhere.

Five things move an Edexcel rate, in roughly this order of weight. Scarcity of the specification comes first: a 4PM1 Further Pure Mathematics specialist is rarer in this market than a 4BS1 Business one, and the rate follows supply. Examining or marking experience comes second, because knowing what the scheme credits is a narrow and valuable skill. Level and tier come third, with Higher tier work priced above Foundation. Whether the tutor travels comes fourth, which is why an online hour strips out a cost the in-home hour carries. Package length comes last and moves the number least, whatever the sales conversation suggests. A provider who leads with package length is pricing the conversation rather than the teaching.

Delivery here is online, one-to-one, over live video, on Arabia Standard Time and inside the Sunday-to-Thursday week. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a Saudi address; home visits are a service offered only in India. For a family in Qatif, Jazan or Taif that removes the only real obstacle, which is that the specialist does not live nearby and never will. The rest of this page is the anatomy of the price: what each payment structure actually commits you to, when a group class is genuinely better value, what the money buys technically, the four ways families pay for the wrong thing, and when to start spending on the university step rather than on the subject.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE

programmes.name: The November resit route

programmes.countryNote: Resit decisions in the Kingdom are often made late, which is what makes them costly. The entry has to be made through a school or a centre.

programmes.name: A Levels and the IB Diploma
programmes.description: The qualification a Saudi or overseas university actually reads. Rates at this level sit above International GCSE rates everywhere, which is worth knowing before a family commits its whole tutoring budget two years early.

edexcel-igcse-online-tutor.subjectsIntro: Pearson prices follow the specification code rather than the subject name. These eight show the spread.

subjects.name: Edexcel Mathematics A 4MA1
subjects.description: The most widely taught Edexcel code, so the deepest pool of tutors and the lowest rates. Higher tier work is priced above Foundation because the multi-step problems take longer to teach.

subjects.name: Edexcel Mathematics B 4MB1
subjects.description: An untiered route with more algebraic demand and no Foundation safety net. Fewer tutors have taught it, so quotes sit above 4MA1 for the same number of hours.

subjects.name: Edexcel Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1
subjects.description: Calculus, series and coordinate geometry well beyond 4MA1. The scarcest Edexcel specialism in this market and the one with the widest spread between advertised rates.

subjects.name: Edexcel Business 4BS1
subjects.description: Case-study questions carry the higher marks and candidates lose them by answering generally. A plentiful tutor pool keeps the rate moderate, which makes verification matter more, not less.

subjects.name: Edexcel Economics 4EC1
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and data response decide the grade more than definitions do. Candidates who can draw a diagram correctly still lose marks by failing to label and then use it.

subjects.name: Edexcel Computer Science 4CP0
subjects.description: Theory plus programming, where marks go on decomposition and documented logic rather than working code. Tutors who program are common; tutors who know this scheme are not.

subjects.name: Edexcel Accounting 4AC1
subjects.description: Double-entry, adjustments and final statements, with marks on presentation convention. Rates sit high for the same reason as Further Pure Mathematics: almost nobody locally has taught it.

subjects.name: Edexcel English as a Second Language 4ES1
subjects.description: A different qualification from English Language A, with different demands and a different standing in university applications. The rate is moderate; the choice of entry matters more than the rate.

sections.heading: What an Edexcel hour is actually priced on
paragraphs: Scarcity of the specification does most of the work. A 4MA1 Mathematics A tutor is drawing on the deepest pool in the market, so the rate sits near the bottom of the published range. A 4PM1 Further Pure Mathematics or 4AC1 Accounting specialist is drawing on almost nobody, and the quotes spread accordingly. This is supply rather than difficulty: Accounting is not harder than physics, it is simply taught by fewer people in this part of the world, and the number reflects that honestly.

Examining experience is the second driver and the one most often claimed without evidence. Somebody who has marked for the board knows what the scheme credits and what it quietly refuses, which is worth paying for when it is real and worth nothing when it is a profile line. It is checkable in fifteen minutes: ask which component, in which series, and ask them to describe how a six-mark answer is credited. Listen for whether the answer is counted in marks or described in adjectives.

The remaining three drivers are smaller and more predictable. Higher tier work costs more than Foundation because the teaching takes longer. An in-home arrangement carries travel, which is the cost an online hour removes rather than discounts. Package length moves the number least of all, and a provider who opens with a discount for a year of hours is selling the commitment rather than the teaching. The table below gives each driver with the question that tests it.

table.caption: WHAT MOVES AN EDEXCEL RATE, AND HOW TO TEST IT
rows: Which codes have you taught, and in which series?
How is a six-mark answer credited on this paper?
Which tier is my child entered for, and why?
Is any part of this quote for getting here?
What happens to hours we do not use?

sections.heading: Cost per mark, not cost per hour
paragraphs: The useful unit is the mark, not the hour. An hour that ends with a candidate understanding why they lost four marks on the same question type in three consecutive papers is worth several hours of general revision, and it may cost twice as much. Families who optimise on the hourly figure alone reliably end up buying more hours, because the cheap hour tends to be the one without marking, without a diagnosis and without anybody who has read the scheme.

Marking is where this shows up most sharply. Marking a full Edexcel paper against the published scheme takes close to an hour of skilled work. A provider charging at the bottom of the published range and promising marking is either absorbing that cost, which is unlikely to last, or not really doing it. A slightly higher rate with marking genuinely included usually produces more movement per riyal, because the marked script is the only honest evidence of what is actually going wrong.

The same logic decides between the four options. School sessions are free and therefore unbeatable on cost per mark when the department can really teach the gap. A group course is excellent value for timed practice after content is secure. An in-home tutor is worth the travel loading for a student who will not work without an adult present. One-to-one online wins when the problem is specific, the specification is scarce, or the family does not live where the specialists do, which covers most of the Kingdom.

sections.heading: Per lesson, per block, or a term at a held rate
paragraphs: Paying per lesson costs most per hour and commits least. It is the right structure at the start, before anyone knows whether the diagnosis was correct and whether the tutor lands with this particular teenager. It is also the right structure for a family whose school calendar is unpredictable, since nothing is tied up when a mock timetable moves or an examination week swallows two evenings.

A term block buys a small discount and something more valuable, which is a held evening. In a Sunday-to-Thursday household the mid-week evening slot is scarcer than the tutor, and a block is partly a way of reserving it. Before signing one, get three things in writing: what happens to hours left unused at the end of the term, how much notice is needed to move a session, and whether the agreed rate survives a change of tutor. Providers who will not put those in writing are telling you something.

A compressed pre-series block is priced per week rather than per hour, and it is the easiest purchase to get wrong. It works for a candidate whose content is secure and whose marks are being lost on technique, timing and question selection. It does not work for a candidate missing a year of teaching, and an honest tutor will say so and decline. Ask for the diagnosis first, and treat a refusal to give one before taking payment as the answer to the question you were asking.

sections.heading: When a group class genuinely beats one-to-one
paragraphs: A group class is better value than one-to-one more often than one-to-one providers admit, and the deciding factor is what the candidate needs rather than what they can afford. Where the content is understood and the problem is mileage under time pressure, a group of five working through papers with a specialist is good teaching at a fraction of the rate. Everybody in the room benefits from hearing somebody else's wrong answer taken apart, which is a real pedagogical advantage rather than a cost compromise.

It stops working the moment the weakness is specific. A candidate losing marks on a particular question type in 4EC1 Economics needs that question type taken apart against their own script, and no group can spend twenty minutes on one student's diagram. The same applies to any subject where the local teaching has been thin rather than merely fast: a group class assumes a shared baseline, and a student below it spends the hour watching.

Some Edexcel subjects do not work in groups in this market for a simpler reason. There are not enough 4AC1 Accounting or 4PM1 Further Pure Mathematics candidates in any one Saudi city to form a group at the same stage, so the choice there is one-to-one or nothing. For the widely taught codes, the honest advice is to use a group for timed practice and buy one-to-one hours for the specific thing a marked paper has identified. Ask any provider how many candidates they actually have at your child's exact stage before believing in a group.

sections.heading: What the money buys technically
paragraphs: The mechanics are unglamorous and they are most of what distinguishes a good online hour from a bad one. The tutor and student share a video call and a whiteboard, with the paper visible to both. A graphics tablet at the tutor's end lets a diagram be annotated while the student writes the working, so an Edexcel physics or economics question with a drawing and a calculation stays in one place. A student needs a laptop, a pen, paper, and a connection that holds a video call.

The marking cycle is the part worth paying for. A candidate sits a full paper by hand, under time, because that is what the examination is, photographs it, and gets it back annotated against the published scheme. That loop produces the only evidence anybody has about whether the hours are working, and it is the first thing a very low rate removes. Ask explicitly whether full-paper marking is inside the hourly figure, charged separately, or simply not offered.

Recordings, session notes and shared files are worth asking about rather than assuming. A recording helps a candidate revisiting a hard derivation and is of limited use otherwise, so it is rarely worth a premium. A short written note after each session saying what was covered, what was set and what comes next costs the tutor five minutes and tells a parent more than a monthly report. Judge the arrangement on the accumulating marked scripts, not on the atmosphere of the hour.

sections.heading: Four ways Saudi families pay for the wrong thing
paragraphs: The first is buying content when the loss is technique. A candidate who understands the material and writes answers that miss what the scheme credits does not need the topic taught again, and paying for that is the most common waste in this market. The second is buying hours before a diagnosis. A term agreed on the strength of a school report, without anybody reading a marked script, is a term bought on guesswork, and the correction costs another term.

The third is buying the wrong subject. Families reliably fund the subject the student complains about rather than the one that is actually at risk, and those are often different. A student loudly miserable about 4EC1 Economics may be sitting on a quiet problem in 4MA1 that will matter more for every post-16 route. A marked paper in each candidate subject, read by somebody who knows the specification, sorts this out in an evening.

The fourth is spending the whole budget two years early. Tutoring at post-16 level costs more than at International GCSE level everywhere, and a family that has spent heavily on an already secure Edexcel grade has less available when the qualification that universities actually read comes round. Fix what is broken, protect what is at risk, and keep something back. That is not a sales position; it is the arithmetic of a four-year run at school. Ask which of these four a payment is about to do, because the answer is usually obvious once the question is asked out loud.

sections.heading: When to start spending on the university step
paragraphs: The university endgame is where Saudi families are least well served by the pages they find, so it is worth stating the mechanism plainly. A foreign or international school certificate needs an equivalency decision from the Ministry of Education before a Saudi university treats it as equivalent to the national secondary certificate. That applies to A Levels, the IB Diploma and an American high school diploma alike. International GCSE results sit inside that file as supporting evidence rather than as the qualification being recognised.

Qudurat, the General Aptitude Test, is run by the Education and Training Evaluation Commission through its National Center for Assessment, known as Qiyas. It tests verbal and quantitative reasoning rather than taught content, and is sat in Arabic or English. Tahsili, the Achievement Test, covers mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology and English, and its content follows the Saudi national curriculum. That is why a strong Edexcel candidate can find Tahsili unfamiliar: the material overlaps, but the framing and the expected approach do not.

On timing, the honest answer is that paying for Qudurat or Tahsili preparation during the International GCSE years is almost always premature. What those years contribute is subject retention: keeping mathematics and the sciences through to a solid grade covers the content the later tests draw on. Universities publish their own criteria combining school grades with the Qiyas tests, weightings differ by institution and programme, and no page should print a threshold. Read the university's own published criteria for the specific programme.

process.title: Send the code, not the subject
process.description: Name the Pearson specification code and the tier where there is one. A quote against a subject name is a quote against the wrong thing, and the code is what the rate is priced on.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson first
process.description: Spent on a paper your child has already sat, it should end with a written diagnosis naming the component, the question types and an estimate of hours. No payment until that exists.

process.title: Choose the payment shape deliberately
process.description: Per lesson while you are still testing the match, a term block once the evening matters more than the flexibility. Get unused hours and notice periods in writing.

process.title: Measure in marks, not in hours
process.description: A full paper done to time and marked against the scheme every few weeks. If the component that was weak is no longer the weak one, the money is working.

whyPoints.title: Rates explained, never hidden
whyPoints.description: We will tell you what moves a quote and which part of it is the teaching. Every SAR figure on this page is another provider's advertised rate.

whyPoints.title: Marking stated, not implied
whyPoints.description: Full papers marked against the published scheme between sessions, with the annotated script returned. If a rate excludes marking, we say so rather than leaving you to discover it.

whyPoints.title: Matched on the Pearson code
whyPoints.description: A 4PM1 family gets somebody who has taught 4PM1. We would rather say nobody is free this term than put a general mathematician in front of a Further Pure candidate.

whyPoints.title: The same rate everywhere
whyPoints.description: A family in Jazan reaches the same specialist as a family in Riyadh at the same figure, because nobody is driving. We do not send anyone to a Saudi address.

whyPoints.title: No promises attached to money
whyPoints.description: No grade guarantee, no refund tied to an outcome, no score threshold published for Qudurat or Tahsili. A diagnosis and an estimate of hours, in writing.

faqs.question: Why does a 4PM1 Further Pure Mathematics tutor cost more per hour than a 4BS1 Business one?
faqs.answer: Supply, almost entirely. A great many teachers can deliver Business to International GCSE standard, so that pool is deep and the rate sits low in the published range. Very few people in or reachable from this market have taught Further Pure Mathematics to Pearson candidates, so the rate climbs. It is not a statement about which subject is harder. If a provider quotes the same figure for both, ask how they are matching tutors to specification codes at all.

faqs.question: Does the hourly rate for an Edexcel online tutor fall if we book a whole term up front?
faqs.answer: Usually a little, and the discount is the least valuable part of the arrangement. What a term block really buys is a held mid-week evening, which in a Sunday-to-Thursday household is scarcer than the tutor. Treat any large discount for a long commitment with caution, because it prices the commitment rather than the teaching. Before signing, get unused hours, notice periods and what happens on a tutor change in writing.

faqs.question: What happens to prepaid Edexcel hours if our child's school changes the mock timetable?
faqs.answer: That depends entirely on what was agreed, which is why it should be agreed at the start. A reasonable arrangement lets sessions be moved within the term with a few days' notice and carries a small number of unused hours forward. An unreasonable one expires them at a fixed date. Saudi school calendars differ school by school and mock weeks move, so this is not a hypothetical question; ask it before the first invoice.

faqs.question: Is an Edexcel resit block cheaper than a term of weekly lessons, and when is it the right buy?
faqs.answer: It is usually cheaper in total and more expensive per week, because the hours are compressed into the autumn term before the November series. It is the right buy when the candidate missed a grade narrowly and the diagnosis points at technique, timing or one weak component. It is the wrong buy when the original grade reflected a year of missing content, which a few intensive weeks cannot replace however they are priced.

faqs.question: What should an Edexcel online tutor charge for reading a mock script we already have?
faqs.answer: Expect their normal hourly rate for roughly an hour of work, because marking a full paper against the published scheme and writing a useful diagnosis takes about that long. What you should receive is not a grade but a list: which questions lost marks, which question types recur, and what the fix is in terms of what the student writes. Many providers fold this into a free trial lesson, which is the cheapest way to get it.

faqs.question: Are two 4EC1 Economics siblings in one session half price, and should they be?
faqs.answer: Rarely half price, and often not a good idea. A tutor teaching two students does not halve their preparation or their marking, so the rate falls less than parents expect. More importantly, two siblings are rarely at the same point in the specification, and the hour drifts towards whichever of them is more confident. Separate hours on the same evening preserve the household's time without the teaching compromise, which is usually the better trade.

faqs.question: For Edexcel 4AC1 Accounting, does a group class work at all, or is one-to-one the only option?
faqs.answer: In this market it is effectively one-to-one or nothing. There are too few Accounting candidates at the same stage in any single Saudi city to assemble a group that is genuinely working on the same thing, and a group drawn from several schools will be at several points in the specification. The subject also rewards working through complete final statements slowly, which does not survive being shared five ways in an hour.

faqs.question: Does a Saudi university see the Edexcel specification codes, or only the subject names and grades?
faqs.answer: The statement of results shows the subject titles and grades, and the codes appear as administrative detail rather than as something an admissions reader weighs. What matters is which subjects were taken and what grade each earned on the 9 to 1 scale. Keep the original statement with its grade descriptions, because a reader less familiar with that scale may need the explanation that comes with it.

faqs.question: When should a family start paying for Qudurat preparation rather than Edexcel subject teaching?
faqs.answer: Not during the International GCSE years. Qudurat tests verbal and quantitative reasoning rather than taught content, so preparation is about question format and pacing, and it belongs to the post-16 years when the test is actually in view. Money spent on it at fifteen displaces money that would fix a subject grade which is about to decide post-16 options. Retain mathematics and the sciences and leave the test preparation until later.

faqs.question: Does a student who sat 4MA1 Foundation have a realistic route into a Saudi science programme?
faqs.answer: It makes the route harder rather than closing it. A Foundation entry constrains the grade available, and post-16 mathematics courses usually expect the Higher content, so a student in that position typically needs to cover the gap before or during the first post-16 year. That is a real and well-trodden piece of work. The decision worth making early is whether a Higher entry is realistic while the entry can still be changed.

faqs.question: What does the Ministry of Education equivalency step actually cost a family in time?
faqs.answer: Mostly document gathering rather than tutoring time, which is why nobody budgets for it and everybody feels it. The file is assembled around the final school certificate and rests on transcripts and statements of results going back through the Edexcel years. Families who have moved countries during school find this the hardest part. The practical action from Year 10 is to keep every original document in one place, which costs nothing now and saves weeks later.

faqs.question: How is an Edexcel 4CP0 Computer Science programming task taught when the tutor cannot see the keyboard?
faqs.answer: By looking at the problem rather than the typing. The marks go on decomposition, data choices and documented logic, so most of a good session is spent on paper or a shared whiteboard before any code is written. Where code matters, the student shares their screen and talks through what they wrote, which is a better exercise than being watched typing. Candidates who can program and cannot explain their design are exactly the ones losing marks.

faqs.question: Is a recorded Edexcel lesson worth paying extra for, and who should be allowed to watch it?
faqs.answer: Rarely worth a premium. A recording genuinely helps a candidate revisiting a difficult derivation or a long worked solution, and is of little use for a discussion-led hour. If recordings are offered, ask who can access them, how long they are kept and whether the student can be recorded at all without consent. Most families find they never rewatch one.

faqs.question: What internet connection does an Edexcel online lesson actually need in a Saudi compound?
faqs.answer: Less than families fear. A stable connection that holds a video call with a shared whiteboard is enough, and that is a lower bar than streaming video. The common problems are a shared household connection at peak evening hours and a device on the far edge of the wireless range rather than raw bandwidth. A wired connection or a position closer to the router fixes most of it.

edexcel-igcse-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Pearson Edexcel International GCSE specifications rather than a generic version of the subject. Matching starts from the four-character code on the centre's entry list, because the paper a student sits is set by that code and not by the subject title printed on a school report.

intro.heading: Edexcel, Cambridge, or the board your school already entered
paragraphs: Most families searching for an Edexcel IGCSE tutor are at one of three decision points. Either the school has entered Edexcel and they want someone who genuinely knows those papers; or the student is moving between boards and nobody has told them what changes; or they are choosing a route for Year 10 and comparing Edexcel against Cambridge and against the IB Middle Years Programme. The three need different answers, and the common failure in this market is a page that treats International GCSE as one thing. It is not. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE and Cambridge International GCSE are separate qualifications from separate awarding organisations, with separate specifications, separate codes, separate component structures and different conventions about what is given on the paper.

The practical consequence is blunt. A tutor who has spent five years teaching Cambridge 0620 Chemistry and has never opened the Edexcel 4CH1 specification will teach the chemistry correctly and prepare a student for the wrong assessment. The content overlap is large, so nothing looks wrong for weeks. What differs is the component structure, the balance between paper and practical assessment, how much the student has to recall rather than read off a sheet, and the wording the mark schemes credit. Those differences are small individually and decisive in aggregate, and they are exactly what a parent cannot evaluate from a profile page.

So the larger part of this page is about the tutor rather than the subject. What qualification actually matters for an Edexcel specification, and in what order. What a degree evidences and what it does not. Why marking experience is worth a premium in the final two terms and close to nothing in the first. Why a serving teacher is sometimes the ideal tutor and sometimes the least available person in the Kingdom. And, concretely, six questions you can ask in a trial lesson, with what a strong answer and a weak answer each sound like, so the judgement does not depend on taking anybody's word for it.

On delivery: IB Gram teaches one-to-one over live video. There are no home visits in Saudi Arabia and a tutor does not travel to a Saudi address — in-home teaching is something we offer only in India. For this particular query that is not a compromise. The number of people in any Saudi city who have taught a specific Edexcel specification to examination standard is small, and the number who have marked for it is smaller. Restricting the search to people within driving range of your district selects on who is free on a Tuesday rather than on who knows 4PH1, and it is the wrong variable to optimise.

The rest of the page runs: Edexcel set against the alternatives, with a subject-by-subject comparison table; what a tutor needs to know that is specific to this board; how to check a tutor against the specification; what each credential really evidences; the grading scale and what a number on a statement of results means; where Edexcel students lose marks; the entry calendar counted backwards from a series; what changes on a board switch; and what Saudi schools enter and why an outside specialist is often needed at all.

edexcel-igcse-tutor.programmesIntro: Four qualifications sit in the comparison a family makes at this age. Setting them side by side is more useful than describing any one of them alone, because the choice between them determines which tutor a student needs and which papers they will eventually sit.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: A two-year course per subject, assessed entirely by externally marked papers in most subjects, reported on the 9 to 1 scale with 9 highest. Several subjects are tiered — Mathematics A runs Foundation and Higher — and tier entry limits the top grade available. Specifications are identified by a four-character code such as 4MA1, 4PH1 or 4CH1, and that code determines the papers, the content list and what appears on any formula sheet.
programmes.countryNote: In the Kingdom this is a common route in British-curriculum schools and the practical route for a student whose own school does not offer an international qualification, because Pearson accepts external candidates through centres that take them. The family's job is to confirm the codes on the entry list and, for an external entry, to find a centre and meet its window, which closes months before the June series.

programmes.name: Cambridge International GCSE
programmes.description: The other widely entered International GCSE, with four-digit codes such as 0580, 0620 and 0625. Several subjects split into Core and Extended tiers, with the Core tier capping the grade. Component structures differ from Edexcel: the sciences typically spread assessment across a multiple-choice paper, a theory paper and a practical-skills component rather than concentrating it in two written papers.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge and Edexcel both appear in Saudi schools, sometimes within the same school for different subjects, which is why a family should never assume one board across a timetable. Cambridge's February and March series is available in India only; a candidate in the Kingdom sits the June series or the November series for either board.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International A Level
programmes.description: What an Edexcel International GCSE most naturally feeds into: modular units, graded A* to E, with subject prerequisites that destination universities state explicitly. Depth replaces breadth — three or four subjects instead of eight or nine — and the mathematical demand in the sciences rises sharply from the International GCSE baseline.
programmes.countryNote: For a Saudi family aiming at a British or Commonwealth university this is often the most efficient route, and the subject choices have to be made against a shortlist of courses rather than against preference. A student carrying an Edexcel International GCSE in Mathematics A at Higher tier is in a reasonable position to continue; one carrying a Foundation tier grade usually needs a bridging term first.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The alternative at the same age, assessed against four criteria per subject, each out of 8 and converted to a grade from 1 to 7. There are no external papers in most subjects, and the criteria reward investigating, communicating and reflecting as well as knowing. The Personal Project in the final year is assessed largely on process.
programmes.countryNote: Families in the Kingdom choosing between this and Edexcel are really choosing between two things: an externally examined, portable, subject-by-subject qualification, and a programme that feeds naturally into the IB Diploma. Students who move from the Middle Years Programme into Edexcel for Year 10 usually arrive articulate and completely unpractised at sitting a long timed paper, which is a specific and fixable gap.

edexcel-igcse-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the Edexcel International GCSE specifications families in the Kingdom most often need outside teaching for, each with its code and the thing a tutor has to know about it that a general subject teacher may not. Confirm the code against the centre's entry list before booking anything.

subjects.name: Mathematics A
subjects.description: Two written papers per tier, and the tier decision is the most consequential one in the whole qualification: a Foundation entry caps the achievable grade however well the student performs. A tutor needs to know which topics appear only on the Higher papers, and whether a move between tiers is still possible before the entry window closes.

subjects.name: Further Pure Mathematics
subjects.description: A separate qualification rather than an extension, covering calculus, series and coordinate geometry a year ahead of the main course. Sensible alongside a secure Higher tier grade in Mathematics A and never as a substitute for fixing one. A tutor who has only taught 4MA1 will not know this content list.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Two written papers covering the whole specification, with practical skills assessed through written questions rather than a practical examination. Formula recall is the difference families notice most against Cambridge: a tutor has to know precisely which equations are provided and which the student must hold, because that changes what revision looks like.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Two written papers, with the content concentrated rather than spread across components. Ionic equations, moles and titration calculations generate most of the lost marks, and the qualitative analysis questions reward a student who has been shown the standard tests in order rather than asked to memorise a table of results.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content-heavy and definition-strict across two papers. Terminology is marked tightly — diffusion described as movement rather than net movement down a gradient loses the mark — and experimental design questions on controls and variables are reliably worth practising because they recur in a predictable form.

subjects.name: English Language A
subjects.description: Assessed against different objectives from Cambridge First Language English, with a differently framed directed-writing task. A student moving from Cambridge needs to relearn the expected structure rather than the language, and a tutor who cannot describe that difference has not read this specification.

subjects.name: English Literature
subjects.description: A separate entry from English Language, which families regularly discover late. Set texts are chosen by the centre, so the first question any tutor should ask is which texts the school is teaching. Essay structure and quotation discipline carry more marks here than breadth of reading.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and precise definitions carry the shorter questions; the extended-response questions want a weighed judgement with the judgement actually stated. Students commonly arrive strong on definitions and weak on evaluation, which is where the grade is decided and which responds quickly to structured practice.

subjects.name: Business
subjects.description: The case material is the examination rather than background reading. Marks come from using the figures and the context supplied, so generic answers about motivation or marketing score poorly even when the theory is accurate. Ask a prospective tutor what they would do with a specific past case before booking.

subjects.name: Human Biology
subjects.description: A distinct specification from Biology, with a different content list and a different emphasis on physiology and health. Entered less often, so specialists are scarcer, and a tutor teaching from 4BI1 materials will leave gaps. Worth confirming which of the two the centre has entered before any teaching is planned.

edexcel-igcse-tutor.regionsTitle: Where in the Kingdom Edexcel is taught and entered
edexcel-igcse-tutor.regionsIntro: Board entry varies by school and sometimes by subject within a school, so the useful geography here is where British-curriculum provision sits and where a family is likely to be looking at an external entry instead. These notes describe the entry picture rather than any school's quality.

regions.name: Riyadh
regions.note: The widest mix of provision in the Kingdom, with British-curriculum, IB and American schools in the same city and no single dominant board. Families here most often need help confirming which board a subject is entered on, because a timetable can carry both.

regions.name: Jeddah
regions.note: Strong British and Cambridge presence along the coastal spine, with Edexcel entries appearing subject by subject rather than school-wide. A family moving between Jeddah schools should expect to check codes again rather than assume continuity.

regions.name: Al Khobar and Dhahran
regions.note: The densest British-curriculum provision in the Kingdom relative to population, concentrated in a small geographic area. Students here are the most likely to be entered through their own school's centre rather than externally.

regions.name: Dammam
regions.note: Families commonly school in the Khobar and Dhahran belt rather than locally, so the entry centre is often in a different city from the home address. That matters for a private candidate, because the centre sets the window and the logistics.

regions.name: Jubail and Yanbu
regions.note: Industrial cities with international provision tied to employer communities. Subject availability is narrower than in the big three centres, and an external entry for a less common specification such as Further Pure Mathematics may need a centre elsewhere.

regions.name: Makkah and Madinah
regions.note: International-curriculum provision is limited relative to population, and most Edexcel enquiries here concern a student studying privately for an external entry rather than following a school course. Centre availability is the first question to settle.

regions.name: Tabuk and the north-west
regions.note: Including AlUla and NEOM, where communities are new and growing and families frequently arrive part-way through a two-year course. Board continuity across a move is rarely guaranteed, so a codes check is the first thing we do.

regions.name: Abha and Khamis Mushait
regions.note: Two 'Asir cities roughly twenty-five kilometres apart sharing a catchment at high altitude. Distance to any specialist is the binding constraint, and teaching over video is usually the only way a scarce specification is covered at all.

schoolClusters.note: British-curriculum provision is dense here by Saudi standards and concentrated in a small area, so a family can realistically compare schools. Board entry still differs by subject, and the International Schools Group runs several campuses of which not all offer the same curricula. Students we support attend schools of this kind.

The capital carries British, IB and American provision simultaneously, which is why board confusion is commonest here. A student can be entered on Edexcel for one subject and Cambridge for another in the same school year, and the only reliable record of that is the centre's entry list.

schoolClusters.city: Jeddah, Thuwal and the western coast
schoolClusters.note: Long-established international schools follow several different systems along this coastline, and two students at neighbouring schools can be sitting entirely different qualifications in the same subject. For a family budgeting for support, that difference matters more than the school's reputation.

sections.heading: Edexcel set against the alternatives a family is weighing
paragraphs: The comparison most families need is not between Edexcel and nothing; it is between Edexcel and Cambridge for the same subject, and occasionally between an International GCSE route and the IB Middle Years Programme. Start with the board comparison, because it is the one that changes what a tutor must know. Both boards are long-established, both are recognised by universities, and neither is harder than the other in any general sense. They differ in structure, and a student prepared for one structure and entered for the other loses marks that have nothing to do with how well they understand the subject.

Three structural differences matter most. The first is component count. Cambridge sciences typically spread assessment across a multiple-choice paper, a theory paper and a practical-skills component, while the Edexcel sciences concentrate it in two written papers with practical skills assessed in writing. That changes how revision has to be distributed: more content per sitting on Edexcel, and no separate practical component to prepare for. The second is formula provision. How much a student must recall rather than read from a sheet differs between the boards, and it is a direct, checkable question a tutor should be able to answer immediately. The third is tiering, which exists on both boards under different names and caps the top grade available on the lower tier.

Against the Middle Years Programme the comparison is different in kind. An Edexcel International GCSE is externally examined, subject by subject, portable, and reported on a scale an admissions office anywhere recognises. The Middle Years Programme is internally assessed against criteria, is not a set of examination grades, and feeds naturally into the IB Diploma. A family choosing between them is choosing between an examined qualification at sixteen and a continuous programme to eighteen, and the honest answer depends on where the student is going rather than on which is academically superior.

The table sets out the subject-level comparison a tutor should know cold. If a prospective tutor cannot describe the difference for the specific subject your child sits, they are teaching the subject rather than the specification, and that is the distinction this whole page turns on.

sections.heading: What a tutor has to know that is specific to this board
paragraphs: A good Edexcel tutor knows four things a good subject teacher may not. The first is the code. Every specification is identified by four characters — 4MA1, 4PH1, 4CH1, 4BI1, 4EA1 — and the code, not the subject name, determines the papers, the content list and the assessment weightings. A tutor who asks for the code in the first message is a better sign than one who asks for the school's name. Human Biology and Biology are different specifications with different content; Mathematics A and Further Pure Mathematics are different qualifications. Getting this wrong is not a nuance, it is teaching the wrong course.

The second is the content list, read as statements rather than as topics. Edexcel specifications state what a candidate must be able to do, statement by statement, and a paper tests those statements. A tutor who teaches from the specification can tell a student which statements are secure and which have never been tested; one who teaches from a textbook covers chapters and hopes the mapping holds. In a board switch this matters enormously, because the differences between two boards' content are specific statements rather than whole topics, and they are findable in an afternoon by anyone who bothers.

The third is formula and data provision. What a student is given on the paper and what they must recall is a defined fact for each specification, and it directly determines what revision should contain. A tutor who has taught the other board will often assume the provision they are used to, and the student discovers the gap in the examination hall. Asking the question is enough to find out: a tutor who knows the answer gives it immediately, and one who does not will offer to check, which is an honest answer and also a signal.

The fourth is the mark scheme. Edexcel publishes mark schemes with its past papers, and they reward particular wordings. The gap between a correct answer and a credited answer is where most of the recoverable marks on any script sit, and a tutor who talks about the mark scheme before talking about the science is telling you they have read one. That single tell is more predictive than any credential on this page.

sections.heading: How to check a tutor against the specification in one hour
paragraphs: A trial lesson is a test, and most families waste it on introductions. An hour is enough to establish whether a tutor knows this board, and it does not require the parent to know the subject. The method is to ask questions whose answers are specific and checkable, then listen for whether the reply is concrete or general. Generality is the tell. A tutor who knows the specification answers with codes, component names, formula provision and mark-scheme wording. One who does not answers with reassurance.

Ask what they would do with a specific six-mark question from a past paper, and listen to the order of their reasoning. A tutor who begins with the command term and the mark allocation, then works to the content, has taught to this assessment. A tutor who explains the science again — correctly, fluently, at length — has not. Both answers sound competent to a non-specialist. Only one of them predicts a grade, and the difference is audible as soon as you know to listen for it.

Ask about marking. If a tutor has marked for a board, they will name the board, the specification and the component without inflating it, and they will usually volunteer a limitation — that they marked one paper and not another, or that it was several series ago. Vague phrasing like examiner-trained or exam-board experienced, with nothing specific behind it, is worth probing rather than accepting. The claim is cheap to make and easy to check with one follow-up question.

Finally, ask about failure. What is the commonest reason a student loses marks on Paper 2 of this specification? A strong answer is specific and diagnosable: a named topic, a named question type, a described error. A weak answer is exam technique or time management, which is true of every paper ever set and tells you nothing. The table below gives the six questions and the two kinds of answer, so you can use it in the session rather than remembering it afterwards.

sections.heading: What each credential actually evidences
paragraphs: Credentials are shorthand, and the shorthand is misleading in both directions. A doctorate in physics evidences content knowledge far beyond International GCSE level and evidences nothing at all about whether the holder has read 4PH1 or knows what its mark schemes credit. A teaching qualification evidences trained classroom practice and planning, which matters most with younger or disengaged students, and says nothing about board familiarity. Both are useful signals. Neither is the signal a family searching for an Edexcel specialist actually needs.

Current school teaching on the specification is the strongest single indicator, because it combines content, assessment and the practical knowledge of how a centre runs entries. It carries one real cost: serving teachers have the least availability in exactly the term when demand peaks, and a teacher carrying five classes and a coursework load has limited capacity for marking a tutee's work between sessions. That trade is worth making explicit rather than discovering it in the second term.

Marking or examining experience is the credential most worth paying a premium for, and only at the right point in the course. What it buys is knowledge of what a script is paid for: which of two correct answers earns the mark, how a scheme treats a near-miss, where a marker stops reading. In the final two terms and through the mock cycle that is worth a great deal. In the first year of a two-year course, when the job is building content, it is worth very little, and paying for it early is a common overspend.

A platform rating or review count deserves the most caution. It evidences that previous customers were satisfied enough to respond, which is not nothing, and it evidences no grade outcome and carries no sample size, date or method. We publish no ratings or success percentages for exactly that reason. Treat a high rating as weak corroboration and ask the six questions anyway; they take ten minutes and they test the thing that actually matters.
