sections.heading: The 9 to 1 scale, and what a number on a statement of results means
paragraphs: Pearson reports Edexcel International GCSE on the 9 to 1 scale, with 9 the highest grade. Cambridge reports most International GCSEs on A* to G, with the numerical scale used for some subjects, so a family holding results from both boards may be reading two different scales on the same page. The practical advice is to ask the centre which scale appears on the statement of results for each subject rather than assuming, particularly where a school enters different boards for different subjects.

Grade boundaries move between series, and that is the fact families find hardest to accept. A boundary is set after the papers are marked, based on how the cohort performed and on statistical and expert judgement about the demand of that particular paper. It is not a fixed percentage announced in advance. So a student scoring the same raw mark in two different series can receive two different grades, and a tutor who promises a grade is promising something nobody controls. What a tutor can honestly offer is a range, revised against each timed paper, with the assumptions stated.

Tiering interacts with the scale in a way that catches families late. On a tiered subject such as Mathematics A, a Foundation entry limits the grade available regardless of performance. That decision belongs to the centre and is made by an entry deadline, which means it is an administrative question with an academic consequence, and it is not reversible after the window closes. A family who believes their child should be on the Higher papers has to raise it with the school early and in writing, with evidence from marked work rather than from a feeling.

Remarks and resits are the other two levers after results. A review of marking is worth considering where a mark sits very close to a boundary or where a component result is wildly out of line with the others; it is not a general second chance, and the centre handles the request within a published window. A November-series resit is the other route, and it needs to be decided quickly because entries for it close soon after results. Both are decisions better made with a marked script in front of you than with an impression.

sections.heading: Where Edexcel students lose marks, specification by specification
paragraphs: Across Edexcel scripts the losses cluster, and they cluster differently by subject. In Mathematics A at Higher tier the pattern is method that is correct and unwritten: a student who computes a multi-step problem mentally earns the answer mark and loses the method marks, which on a long question is most of the marks available. The fix is layout rather than mathematics, and it is quick. The second Mathematics pattern is the final question left blank, which is a time-budget problem and responds to whole papers sat against a clock rather than to more topic practice.

In Physics 4PH1 the losses are precision losses. Definitions given in approximate words where the scheme expects exact ones. Units omitted or wrong by a factor of a thousand. Graph gradients read without checking what each axis plots. Equations that had to be recalled and were recalled nearly correctly. Each of those is worth one or two marks and together they routinely account for a grade. In Chemistry 4CH1 the equivalent cluster is ionic equations, state symbols, and mole calculations where the student knows the method and loses the arithmetic, plus explanations that describe a process rather than explain why it happens.

In Biology 4BI1 the single largest fault is loose terminology, because the scheme marks definitions tightly and a near-synonym does not score. The second is answering at the wrong length: a two-mark question receiving a paragraph while a six-mark question receives two lines. In English Language A the losses are structural — a directed-writing task answered in the wrong form or register, and an analysis that identifies a technique without explaining its effect. In Economics and Business the pattern is identical to each other: strong definitions, weak evaluation, and generic answers that ignore the figures supplied in the case.

None of these is a content problem, which is why re-teaching the syllabus produces so little movement. They are diagnosable in a single marked paper, they are teachable in weeks rather than terms, and they transfer across subjects: a student who learns to read mark allocations as instructions improves in every paper they sit. That is why the first fortnight of any plan here is a timed component and a ranked fault list rather than a revision schedule.

sections.heading: The entry calendar, counted backwards from a series
paragraphs: Edexcel candidates in the Kingdom sit the June series and the November series. The June series is the main one for a two-year course; November carries resits and November-entry candidates. Final entries are made by the centre and close several months ahead of the June series, and your school's examinations officer holds the exact date — it differs by centre and by whether the entry is late. For a private candidate the window is the same shape but the responsibility for meeting it sits with the family, which is why we settle the entry route before planning any teaching.

The school week in the Kingdom runs Sunday to Thursday, with Friday and Saturday as the weekend, and that reorders a revision timetable copied from a British or Indian source. Sunday morning is a school morning here. Weekday evenings carry routine weekly teaching, and the long unbroken blocks for whole timed papers fall on Friday and Saturday during the day. Arabia Standard Time is UTC+3 with no seasonal change, so a slot agreed with a tutor in a country that does change its clocks must be written down in Saudi local time or it will drift by an hour twice a year.

School calendars then differ from each other within the same city. Public schools run two semesters from late August to late June with an autumn break, a midyear break and an Eid Al Fitr break; international and British-curriculum schools set their own three-term calendars. Ramadan shortens the school day and reshapes the evening, and most families either move the session later or pause for the month and resume afterwards. In a scarce specification, moving the hour is better than releasing it.

Counting backwards is the useful discipline, and almost nobody in this market does it. Two years out, the course begins and the only job is the foundation it assumes. One year out, tier decisions firm up. Several months out, entries close. Eight weeks out, the work becomes technique. The table lays that out, and it names no dates on purpose: the centre's deadlines are the ones that bind, and they are not the same everywhere.

sections.heading: Switching to Edexcel mid-course, and what actually transfers
paragraphs: Board switches happen more often than anybody plans for, usually because a family relocates within the Kingdom or into it, and the receiving school enters a different board. The good news is that most of the content transfers: at this level the overlap between Cambridge and Edexcel in the sciences and mathematics is large, and a student is never starting again. The work is finding the specific differences and closing them, which is a short, defined job if somebody actually reads both specifications side by side.

Three things reliably need attention. Content statements that exist on one specification and not the other — rarely whole topics, usually particular statements inside a topic. Formula and data provision, which changes what has to be recalled and therefore what revision contains. And component structure: a student who has prepared for a separate practical-skills component and is now sitting two written papers has to redistribute their revision, and one moving the other way has a new component to learn to sit. None of that is difficult. All of it is invisible unless somebody looks.

A move from the IB Middle Years Programme into Edexcel for Year 10 is a different diagnosis. The student usually arrives able to investigate, communicate and reflect, and completely unpractised at sitting a long timed paper, because the Middle Years criteria do not require it. That is an examination-stamina gap rather than a content gap, and it responds to timed practice from the first term. A move from a national-curriculum school needs the opposite emphasis: the content is largely there, and what is missing is the habit of applying it to unfamiliar material and the technical English the mark schemes credit.

Timing matters more than direction. The clean boundary is the start of Year 10, where the two-year course begins and nothing has to be recovered. A move part-way through Year 11 is survivable when the board is the same and the entry can still be made, and difficult when neither is true. Where a family has any choice about when to move, aligning it to a boundary costs far less in support than moving mid-course and buying the recovery afterwards.

sections.heading: What Saudi schools enter, and why an outside specialist is often needed
paragraphs: Private and international schools in the Kingdom are licensed by the Ministry of Education, with school evaluation and accreditation running through the Education and Training Evaluation Commission, which operates e-services for national school accreditation and for the approval of international accreditation bodies. None of that determines which awarding organisation a school enters, or whether it can field a specialist for a particular specification next year. Those are staffing and commercial decisions made school by school, and they are the decisions a family's tutoring need actually rests on.

In practice, board entry in the Kingdom is mixed and sometimes mixed within a single school. A school may enter Edexcel for mathematics and Cambridge for the sciences, or change board between cohorts when a head of department changes. Families routinely assume one board across a timetable and discover otherwise in Year 11. The fix is administrative and takes one email: ask the examinations officer for the entry list with codes, per subject, for your child's cohort, and keep it.

Specialist availability is the second structural issue. Less commonly entered specifications — Further Pure Mathematics, Human Biology, English Literature as a separate entry — are taught by fewer people, and a school that offers them may be doing so with a teacher whose main subject is adjacent. That is not negligence; it is what a small cohort allows. It does mean that the student in front of that gap needs outside teaching for that specification, for that year, and the school is rarely positioned to say so plainly.

Class size finishes the argument. A group of twenty-five in a subject with substantial written assessment gives each student a small share of a teacher's marking attention, and the students who most need their written answers interrogated are the least likely to volunteer. Buying one-to-one time buys exactly that: somebody watching one student work through one question and interrupting at the right moment. No staffing level in any school makes that available to everyone, which is the honest reason this market exists.

process.title: Send the entry list, with codes
process.description: Ask your school's examinations officer for the subject-by-subject entry list for your child's cohort, including the four-character Edexcel codes. That single document removes every assumption a tutor would otherwise make, and families are frequently surprised by what is on it. If the student is an external candidate, the centre's confirmation serves the same purpose.

process.title: Use the trial lesson as a test
process.description: An hour with the tutor we think fits, built around one real Edexcel past-paper question. Ask the six questions from the table on this page. You are testing whether this person talks about mark schemes and components or only about the subject, and the difference is audible within ten minutes. No charge and nothing to commit to.

process.title: A timed component and a ranked fault list
process.description: In the first fortnight the student sits a whole Edexcel component under real time pressure, marked against the published scheme. The output is a list of where the marks went, ordered by how many, and that list is what the teaching plan is built on rather than a general sense of weakness.

process.title: Teaching mapped to specification statements
process.description: Weekly sessions against the specification itself, with statements marked off as they are secured and past-paper questions used as the test of each. You receive a short note after every session naming what was covered, what was set and what was weak, so progress is visible without interrogating a teenager.

process.title: A term review against marked scripts
process.description: At the end of a term we compare the week-one component with a comparable later one and make a recommendation: continue, change the subject being supported, or stop. We state a range rather than a grade, because grade boundaries are set after marking and nobody can promise one honestly.

whyPoints.title: Matched on the code, not the subject name
whyPoints.description: Matching starts from the four-character Edexcel code on the entry list. Human Biology is not Biology, Further Pure Mathematics is not Mathematics A, and a tutor fluent in a Cambridge specification is not automatically fluent in the Edexcel one. Getting the code right before the first lesson prevents the most expensive mistake available in this market.

whyPoints.title: You are given the questions to test us with
whyPoints.description: The six questions in this page's table are the ones we would want a family to ask, including of our own tutors. A provider confident in its matching has no reason to keep them private, and a family able to test a tutor directly does not have to rely on anybody's description of their own quality.

whyPoints.title: Marking experience priced where it earns its keep
whyPoints.description: Examining experience buys knowledge of what a script is actually paid for, which is worth a premium in the final two terms and very little in the first year of a two-year course. We say which point of the course a tutor's background suits, rather than selling the strongest-sounding credential regardless of when it helps.

whyPoints.title: The entry route is treated as part of the job
whyPoints.description: For an external candidate the centre, the window and the component list matter as much as the teaching, and we map them backwards from the series before planning hours. A well-taught student with no valid entry has nothing to show for a year, and that failure is entirely preventable with one early conversation.

whyPoints.title: No ratings, no percentages, no promised grades
whyPoints.description: Grade boundaries are set after papers are marked, so a promised grade is a promise about something nobody controls. We publish no success percentages, no star ratings and no tutor headcounts, because none of them could carry a sample size, a date and a method. We give you a marked script instead.

faqs.question: What transfers if a student moves from Cambridge IGCSE to Edexcel International GCSE part-way through Year 10?
faqs.answer: Most of the content, and almost none of the assessment preparation. At this level the overlap in mathematics and the sciences is large, so a student is not starting again. What has to be found and closed is specific: content statements present on one specification and absent from the other, differences in which formulae are provided rather than recalled, and a changed component structure. Reading both specifications side by side identifies all three in an afternoon. Budget six to ten sessions for the switch rather than a full term of re-teaching, and confirm the new codes with the centre before any of it starts.

faqs.question: Can a student in the Kingdom move from the IB Middle Years Programme into Edexcel International GCSE for Year 10?
faqs.answer: Yes, and Year 10 is the clean boundary for it, because the two-year Edexcel course begins there. The content gap is usually modest. The real gap is examination stamina: the Middle Years criteria do not require a student to sit a long timed paper, so a student can arrive articulate, reflective and unpractised at answering a full component against a clock. Start timed practice in the first term rather than the last, keep the specification open in lessons so coverage is visible, and expect the first few timed papers to understate what the student actually knows.

faqs.question: Does an Edexcel International GCSE in Mathematics prepare a student for Mathematics AA HL in the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: A secure Higher tier grade in 4MA1 is a reasonable foundation, and a Foundation tier grade generally is not. Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level assumes fluent algebraic manipulation, confident work with functions and graphs, and comfort with formal notation, and it adds proof, complex numbers and a long calculus strand on top. A student coming from the Higher tier with gaps in algebra should close them in the summer before the Diploma rather than during the first term, because in this subject every later topic assumes an earlier one and unclosed gaps compound rather than sit still.

faqs.question: What does a student coming from a national-curriculum school need before starting Edexcel International GCSE Physics?
faqs.answer: Less physics than families expect and more technique. The mechanics, waves and electricity content overlaps substantially, so the knowledge base is usually sound. Three things need building. First, the habit of applying content to unfamiliar situations rather than reproducing a taught example. Second, the technical English the mark schemes credit, which is a bounded list of standard explanatory sentences rather than general language work. Third, precision discipline: units, significant figures and exact definitions, which are marks rather than presentation. A term of focused work on those three usually outperforms a term of content revision.

faqs.question: Is it worth switching a student from Edexcel Mathematics A to Further Pure Mathematics?
faqs.answer: They are not alternatives. Further Pure Mathematics, 4PM1, is a separate qualification taken alongside Mathematics A rather than instead of it, and it introduces calculus, series and coordinate geometry a year early. It is worth adding for a student with a secure Higher tier performance who is heading towards A Level Mathematics or Mathematics AA HL, because it removes much of the step up. It is a poor decision for a student still shaky on the main course, where the same hours spent securing 4MA1 will do more for both the grade and the next qualification.

faqs.question: How do I find out whether my child's school in the Kingdom enters Cambridge or Edexcel?
faqs.answer: Ask the examinations officer for the entry list, by subject, with codes, for your child's cohort, and ask for it in writing. Do not infer it from the school's curriculum description, because schools in the Kingdom frequently enter different boards for different subjects and sometimes change board between cohorts when a head of department changes. A four-digit code beginning with a zero indicates Cambridge; a four-character code beginning with a four indicates Edexcel. Keep that document, because every tutoring decision and every past paper you buy depends on it.

faqs.question: Why would a Saudi school choose Edexcel International GCSE over Cambridge?
faqs.answer: Usually for structural and practical reasons rather than academic ones. The Edexcel sciences concentrate assessment in two written papers with practical skills assessed in writing, which removes the logistics of a separate practical component — a real consideration for a school with constrained laboratory capacity or a small cohort. Specification familiarity among staff matters too: a department recruited largely from one system tends to enter that system's board. Subject availability and the fit with the school's sixth-form offer also play a part. None of this makes either board better, and both are widely recognised.

faqs.question: What happens if a school in the Kingdom enters a student on the Foundation tier against the family's wishes?
faqs.answer: The entry belongs to the centre, and after the window closes it is not reversible, so this has to be raised early and in writing. A Foundation entry caps the grade available regardless of performance, which makes it an administrative decision with a lasting academic consequence. Bring evidence rather than an opinion: marked work, a timed Higher tier paper the student has sat, and a comparison against the boundary marks published with past papers. Schools generally respond to evidence on this point, and a tutor can supply a timed Higher paper and a mark for exactly this purpose.

faqs.question: Can a student sit Edexcel International GCSE as a private candidate in Saudi Arabia?
faqs.answer: Pearson accepts external candidates through centres that take them, so the qualification itself is available this way. The practical constraint is finding a centre: not every school that enters its own students will accept outside ones, availability is concentrated in the larger cities, and some subjects with practical or coursework components are harder to place than fully written ones. Approach centres early and get the answer in writing, because entry windows close months before the June series. Teaching can be arranged online; the entry cannot be improvised late and is the family's responsibility to secure.

faqs.question: Which Edexcel subjects are least likely to be taught by a specialist in a Saudi school?
faqs.answer: The less commonly entered specifications. Further Pure Mathematics and Human Biology are taught by fewer people anywhere, and a school with a small cohort may cover them with a teacher whose main subject is adjacent. English Literature entered separately from English Language is another, because a single English department often prioritises the language entry. Physics at the top of the ability range competes with industry employment for the same graduates across the Kingdom. In each case the school is doing what a small cohort allows, and the student in front of the gap is the one who needs outside teaching.

faqs.question: When do Edexcel International GCSE entries close relative to the June series?
faqs.answer: Final entries are made by the centre and close several months ahead of the June series, with a later window available at additional cost. The exact dates differ by centre and by entry type, and your school's examinations officer holds them — so does the centre an external candidate is using. The practical rule is to treat the autumn term of the final year as the deadline season rather than the spring, and to confirm in writing that the subject, the code and the tier on the entry are the ones you expect. Discovering an error after the window is the expensive outcome.

faqs.question: How does a Sunday-to-Thursday school week change the best time for an Edexcel lesson?
faqs.answer: It moves the week rather than shortening it. Friday and Saturday are the weekend in the Kingdom and Sunday morning is a school morning, so revision timetables copied from British or Indian sources put sessions in the wrong places. Weekday evenings carry routine weekly teaching. Friday and Saturday daytime are the only long, unbroken windows, which makes them the right place for a whole timed paper that has to be sat and then marked and discussed in one sitting. Most families end up with one weekday evening hour and a weekend block closer to a series.

faqs.question: Our Edexcel tutor is in the United Kingdom — how is the lesson slot kept stable through their clock changes?
faqs.answer: By writing the slot down in Saudi local time rather than theirs. The Kingdom is on UTC+3 all year with no seasonal change; the United Kingdom moves its clocks twice a year. If an arrangement is recorded in British time, it silently shifts by an hour in each direction annually, and an hour is enough to push a session into a school night or into the middle of dinner. Fixing the hour in Saudi local time means the tutor's clock moves and the student's school evening does not. It is a small administrative point that prevents a recurring one.

faqs.question: How should an Edexcel student's weekly schedule change in the final eight weeks before the June series?
faqs.answer: Content work should mostly stop and extraction should start. Whole papers sat against the clock, marked against the published scheme, with the student's own script read beside it. Two or three shorter sessions a week beat one long one at this stage, because the work is diagnostic and repetitive rather than expository. Reserve the long weekend block for full components. The single most useful addition is a per-paper plan for the final twenty minutes, since the last question left blank is one of the most common and most recoverable losses on any Edexcel script.

faqs.question: What happens to Edexcel lessons during Ramadan and the midyear break?
faqs.answer: School days shorten during Ramadan and the shape of the evening changes, so a fixed late-afternoon slot generally stops working. Most families move the session later in the evening or pause for the month and resume afterwards, and both are reasonable. In a scarce specification, moving the hour is better than releasing it, because a released slot can be hard to recover. The midyear break is a good place for a focused block on one weak topic rather than routine weekly lessons, and the long summer break suits reduced-frequency teaching if the student is entering their final year.

faqs.question: How much notice is needed to change a regular Edexcel lesson slot?
faqs.answer: For a one-off move, as much as you can give, and a day is usually workable. For a permanent change to the weekly slot, expect to need a couple of weeks, because the tutor's other students hold the adjacent hours and the new time has to be free in both calendars. Scarce specifications are the least flexible: a Further Pure Mathematics or Physics specialist with a full week may have only one alternative hour available. Agreeing a slot that genuinely survives the school term at the outset avoids most of this.

edexcel-igcse-tutor.closingHeading: Get the code, then test the tutor
edexcel-igcse-tutor.closingBody: Two actions settle most of what this page covers. Ask your school's examinations officer for the entry list with codes, per subject, in writing — it is one email and it removes every assumption anybody would otherwise make. Then use a trial lesson as a test rather than an introduction, with the six questions from the table on this page in front of you. Listen for whether the answers are specific: codes, components, formula provision, mark-scheme wording. The trial lesson is free, it is built around one real Edexcel past-paper question, and it ends with a written note on where the marks are going. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Arabia Standard Time.

intro.heading: Where the student sits in the year decides what an evening is for
paragraphs: The same weekday evening buys three different things depending on when in the year it is booked. In the autumn term it buys diagnosis and foundation repair, which is the cheapest and most useful work available all year. By the spring it buys content coverage against a syllabus that is running out of teaching weeks. In the eight weeks before the May session it buys technique, timing and an error log, and nothing else, because there is no longer room to learn anything new well enough to be examined on it.

Families rarely arrive at the start of that sequence. Most call after a mock, which is usually mid-year, and the honest first conversation is about what is still reachable rather than about the tutor's qualifications. A Diploma student with a weak Paper 1 technique and four months left is in a strong position. The same student with four weeks is in a different one, and a provider who describes both the same way is selling rather than teaching.

That is why this page runs forward through the year rather than listing services. It starts with the calendar, moves to the shape of the Sunday-to-Thursday week and the hours inside it that are actually usable, then to the time zone problem that decides who can teach at six in the evening in Riyadh, then to cost, then to the two Diploma years, and finally to what happens after results when a Saudi university enters the picture.

The scheduling facts underneath all of it are simple and widely ignored by pages copied from British or Indian sites. The school week runs Sunday to Thursday; Friday and Saturday are the weekend. The Kingdom sits on Arabia Standard Time, UTC+3, and does not observe daylight saving, so a slot agreed with a tutor in a country that does will drift twice a year unless it is pinned to Saudi local time in writing. India is two and a half hours ahead of Saudi local time, which makes a Saudi evening a late Indian one. The same arithmetic runs the other way for a tutor in the UK, for whom a late Saudi evening is a comfortable afternoon, so the hour a family can offer quietly decides which half of the world they are hiring from.

One thing is fixed. Lessons for Saudi families are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not send a tutor to an address in Riyadh, Jeddah or anywhere else in the Kingdom; home visits are a service offered only in India. For an evening slot that matters more than it first appears: the hour after a school run is exactly the hour a travelling tutor spends in traffic, and removing the journey is what makes a six o'clock start possible at all.

evening-ib-tutor.programmesIntro: An evening slot does different work in each year of the programme. These are the three stages Saudi families book for most often, in the order a student meets them.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme, first year
programmes.description: The year where evening work is cheapest and most effective, because the gaps are still foundational and there is time to close them. Higher and Standard Level choices settle early, Internal Assessment work begins, and a weak start in Mathematics or a science compounds through everything that follows.
programmes.countryNote: Saudi cohorts are small, so a student who picks a Higher Level the school can barely staff is often studying it in an unusually thin class from the first term.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme, final year
programmes.description: Evenings here compete with Internal Assessment deadlines, the Extended Essay, mock examinations and university applications in the same months. The sequencing matters more than the hours: content repair early in the year, then technique, then whole papers to time.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Shorter evening sessions suit this stage, since criterion-assessed tasks are redone properly rather than revised. The useful target is the habit of reading a criterion before starting, which transfers directly into the Diploma two years later.

sections.heading: The year forward: autumn diagnosis, spring coverage, then technique
paragraphs: Start by locating the student rather than the subject. In the autumn term of either Diploma year, an evening hour is diagnostic money: there is time to find a foundation gap, close it, and let the school's own teaching do the rest. Rearranging equations, reading a criterion, writing a paragraph that answers the question asked. This is the cheapest work in the year because it compounds, and it is the work families buy least often because nothing has gone visibly wrong yet.

By the spring the calculation changes. The syllabus is being delivered against a finite number of teaching weeks, mock results have arrived, and the student now has evidence about which components they lose marks on. Evening slots here are best spent on the two or three topics that recur in that evidence rather than on a general sweep. International and British-curriculum schools in the Kingdom set their own calendars and most run three terms, so send the tutor your school's published calendar rather than assuming a shared one.

In the last stretch before the May session, an evening can only do technique. Command terms, question types, timing, the error log, and the discipline of writing what the mark scheme credits rather than everything known about the topic. Content teaching at this point is usually a comfort purchase. Ask your Diploma Programme coordinator for the component deadlines and the mock timetable, build the evenings backwards from those, and accept that the final fortnight should be lighter rather than heavier.

sections.heading: The Sunday-to-Thursday week, hour by hour
paragraphs: The school week in the Kingdom runs Sunday to Thursday, with Friday and Saturday as the weekend. That has two consequences most families work out the hard way. Sunday evening is the hardest slot to sell to a teenager, because it is the first night of the week and the weekend has just ended. Thursday evening is the easiest to fill and the least productive, because the weekend starts in a few hours and attention has already left the building.

Inside a weekday the usable window is narrower than it looks. School finishes, the run home takes what it takes, and there is a stretch of food, prayer and decompression that no tutoring schedule should fight. In most Saudi cities that puts the first realistic start between five and six in the evening, with the slot after it the most contested hour of the week. By eight the student has usually done school homework as well, and an hour booked at nine costs more in sleep than it returns in learning.

The practical advice is unfashionable: book earlier than feels convenient, and book Monday, Tuesday or Wednesday where there is a choice. A student who has a fixed Tuesday at half past five for a whole year builds a habit that survives a bad week. One who has a floating slot somewhere between seven and nine renegotiates it every time something comes up, and the renegotiation itself costs more than the half hour saved.

sections.heading: Arabia Standard Time against a tutor's own clock
paragraphs: The Kingdom is on Arabia Standard Time, UTC+3, and does not observe daylight saving. Several of the countries where specialist IB teachers live do. The consequence is that a slot agreed in the tutor's local time will move twice a year relative to the student's evening, and the family will discover it on a school night. Agree every slot in Saudi local time, in writing, and let the tutor's clock be the one that shifts.

The size of the gap decides who can realistically teach a given hour. India is two and a half hours ahead of Saudi local time, so a six o'clock start in Riyadh is half past eight in the evening for a tutor in Delhi or Chennai, which is workable, and a nine o'clock start is nearly midnight, which is not. A tutor in the UK is three hours behind in their winter and two in their summer, so a late Saudi evening is a comfortable late afternoon for them. Continental Europe sits between the two.

That asymmetry is worth using rather than fighting. If a family needs an early evening slot, the widest pool sits in India and the Gulf. If the only possible hour is after eight, the pool shifts west to the UK and Europe. The table below sets out how each weekday evening hour actually lands, and a family that knows this can ask for availability in the right direction instead of being told repeatedly that nothing is free.

sections.heading: The term Ramadan falls in, and the evening that changes shape
paragraphs: Ramadan moves roughly eleven days earlier each year against the Gregorian calendar, so it drifts steadily across the academic year and lands in a different term from one cycle to the next. That means a family cannot plan a permanent evening pattern around it. What can be planned is the response, because the effect on a study week is consistent even though the timing is not.

School days shorten during the month, which frees afternoon time that did not exist before. Evening patterns change in the other direction: the hours immediately after sunset are family hours, and the productive study window often moves later into the night or earlier into the afternoon. Many families switch their weekly slot to an afternoon for the month and switch back afterwards, which works provided the tutor is told early enough to hold the alternative hour. A tutor based abroad will not have a shortened working day themselves, so the afternoon slot a Saudi family wants for the month is often easier to arrange than the evening one it replaces.

Two practical points follow. First, ask the school for its published timings for the month rather than assuming last cycle's apply, since schools differ and the dates are confirmed by moon sighting and vary by a day between countries. Second, if the month overlaps the final run to the May session, move whole-paper practice to the weekend and keep evenings short and technical. A tired hour spent well is worth more than a long one spent for the sake of the schedule.

sections.heading: What an evening IB tutor is quoted at, and what moves the number
paragraphs: Every figure here is an advertised rate published by a tutoring company or a marketplace, not a market average and not a quote from IB Gram. Tutoring-platform listings for general, non-specialist online tutoring in the Kingdom start around SAR 55 an hour. A tutor-marketplace guide puts general private tuition in Riyadh at about SAR 50 an hour for primary work and above SAR 200 for senior-school examination subjects. Tutoring-company listings advertise IB subject tutoring in Riyadh from roughly SAR 180, with Higher Level and premium tracks quoted near SAR 200 to 220. Providers quoting in dollars sit around sixty an hour.

The hour of the evening affects supply more than price. A five o'clock slot is available from a wide pool and is rarely surcharged. A late slot is scarce, and scarcity of availability sometimes shows up as a premium even though the teaching is identical. What genuinely moves the rate is subject scarcity, examiner or marking experience, level, whether the tutor travels, and package length. In-home tuition carries a travel loading, which is a cost with no academic return attached to it.

Two questions change the real hourly cost more than the headline figure. Ask whether marking written work between sessions is billed as time, because a Diploma student handing in a paper each week generates real marking hours. And ask what a written report costs, if one exists at all. A provider who cannot answer either in one message is not running the arrangement you think you are buying, and no provider should be quoting a success rate without saying how it was measured.

sections.heading: Two Diploma years, two different evenings
paragraphs: In the first Diploma year the enemy is drift. Nothing is due, the examinations are far away, and a student can fall a long way behind while reporting that everything is fine. An evening slot in this year should therefore be partly diagnostic by design: a short piece of timed work every few weeks, so a gap is caught by evidence rather than by a mock. This is also the year to start Internal Assessment thinking, because a research question chosen carelessly early costs months later.

In the final year the enemy is collision. Internal Assessment deadlines, the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge, mock examinations and university applications arrive in overlapping months, and the evening is the only flexible resource a family has. The sequencing question is therefore sharper than the quantity question. Content repair belongs early in the year, technique in the middle, whole papers at the end, and nothing should be scheduled in the week a major component is due.

Both years reward the same unglamorous practice: a written record after each session naming what was covered, what was diagnosed and one task before the next. Without it, a weekly evening becomes a conversation. With it, a parent who does not teach the subject can still see whether the same error is in its fourth week. No tutor can promise a grade or a points total, and a provider who offers one is making a claim nobody can keep.

sections.heading: After results: equivalency, Qudurat and Tahsili
paragraphs: For families applying inside the Kingdom there is a stage after the Diploma that most international-school advice skips. A foreign or international school certificate needs an equivalency decision, mu'adalah, from the Ministry of Education before a Saudi university treats it as equivalent to the Saudi secondary certificate. That applies to the IB Diploma, A Levels and an American high school diploma alike, and some universities state a maximum age for the certificate they will accept.

Alongside it sit the Qiyas tests, run by the National Center for Assessment under the Education and Training Evaluation Commission. Qudurat, the General Aptitude Test, measures verbal and quantitative reasoning rather than syllabus content and can be sat in Arabic or in English. Tahsili, the Achievement Test, covers the science-stream subjects: mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology and English. Universities publish their own admission formulas combining school results with these tests, and the weightings differ by university and by programme.

Tahsili is the one that costs Diploma students evenings they did not plan for, and the reason is structural. Its content follows the Saudi national curriculum, so an IB student meets material that overlaps their own syllabus without being framed or sequenced the same way. Preparation is therefore a separate piece of work from Diploma revision, not a by-product of it. No thresholds or weighting formulas appear here because they differ by institution; check the university's own published admission criteria, and start that reading before the final year, not during it.

faqs.question: Does a later evening slot cost more than an early one in the Kingdom?
faqs.answer: The teaching is identical, so a difference in price reflects scarcity of availability rather than quality. A five o'clock start can be filled from a wide pool of tutors in India and the Gulf; a nine o'clock start can only be filled from further west, and a smaller pool occasionally carries a premium. Ask directly whether the quoted rate varies by hour, and get it in writing. The more useful saving is to book earlier in the evening and earlier in the term.

faqs.question: Is the marking done between two evening sessions in the same week charged as time?
faqs.answer: It depends on the provider, and it is the question that moves the real hourly cost most. A Diploma student handing in a paper each week generates genuine marking hours, and some providers include that inside the rate while others bill it separately or decline it altogether. Ask which applies before the first session, and ask what the marked work comes back as: a per-question record is worth paying for, a tick and a grade is not.

faqs.question: How many weekday evenings a week can a Diploma student absorb before sleep suffers?
faqs.answer: Two is comfortable for most students, three is the practical ceiling, and four is usually counterproductive during term. The limiting factor is not willingness but the school homework that still has to be done after the session. A student carrying three Higher Levels and real gaps in two of them is better served by two weekday evenings and one longer weekend block than by four school nights, because the weekend block can hold a whole paper.

faqs.question: Is sharing an evening slot with a classmate ever better value than one-to-one?
faqs.answer: Occasionally, and only when the two students have the same gap in the same subject at the same level. Listening comprehension and discussion-based work survive a pair. Technique work does not, because the whole value is in the tutor watching one student's working and interrupting at the right moment. Where a pair does work, insist on the same written record for each student, since the common failure is one child getting the teaching and the other getting the hour.

faqs.question: Does an evening rate change in the weeks before the May session?
faqs.answer: Advertised rates in this market are published per hour and do not usually carry a seasonal increase, but availability tightens sharply as the session approaches and the best slots go first. The practical effect on a family's bill is not a higher rate but a worse hour, or a less specialised tutor than they would have had in the autumn. If a specific subject at Higher Level matters, book the slot early in the year and keep it rather than waiting for a mock to justify it.

faqs.question: Why does Tahsili sit awkwardly beside a Diploma student's own evening revision?
faqs.answer: Because it tests the same subjects from a different starting point. Tahsili covers mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology and English, and its content follows the Saudi national curriculum, so the material overlaps a Diploma syllabus without matching its framing, sequence or emphasis. Revising one does not revise the other, and treating Tahsili preparation as a by-product of Diploma work is the commonest planning error. It needs its own evenings, scheduled separately and ideally before the final-year deadline crush.

faqs.question: What does Ministry of Education equivalency involve once Diploma results arrive?
faqs.answer: It is a decision the Ministry makes about whether an international certificate is treated as equivalent to the Saudi secondary certificate, and a Saudi university needs it before the certificate counts for admission. It applies to the IB Diploma, A Levels and an American high school diploma alike. The documents, the route and the processing time are published by the Ministry itself, and some universities also state a maximum age for the certificate they accept, so read both sources rather than a forum.

faqs.question: Should Qudurat practice take an evening slot away from a Higher Level subject?
faqs.answer: Not during the final run to the May session, and ideally not from the subject that is weakest. Qudurat tests verbal and quantitative reasoning rather than syllabus content, so it rewards familiarity with the question formats more than fresh teaching, and that familiarity can be built in shorter and less frequent sessions. The sensible pattern is to start it in the first Diploma year or the summer before the final one, when evenings are not already contested by component deadlines.

faqs.question: Which parts of Tahsili does a Diploma science student have to learn from scratch?
faqs.answer: Rarely whole topics, more often framing. A student who has studied Chemistry at Higher Level will recognise the chemistry but may not recognise the expected method, the level of detail rewarded, or the order in which ideas are introduced. English sections test a different register from a Diploma language course. The efficient approach is to work through the test's own published material first to find the mismatches, then teach only those, rather than re-covering science a Diploma student already knows.

faqs.question: When in the final school year should equivalency paperwork be started?
faqs.answer: Read the requirements early in the year and assemble documents before results arrive, because the paperwork is administrative rather than academic and competes for exactly the weeks when examinations do not. What cannot be done early is anything that needs the final certificate itself. Universities publish their own admission criteria and deadlines, and those vary by institution and programme, so the family's first task is to identify which universities are in scope and read their criteria directly.

faqs.question: How does an evening lesson handle a physics diagram when the student is already tired?
faqs.answer: By having the student draw rather than watch. The shared whiteboard takes handwriting and the student can also draw on paper and show the page to camera, which is quicker at the end of a school day than fighting a stylus. A tired student copying a tutor's neat diagram learns almost nothing, so the usual pattern is a rough sketch from the student, then one correction, then a second attempt. Sessions late in the evening are kept shorter for this reason.

faqs.question: Can a parent look in on a weekday evening session without derailing it?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the first two sessions are the moment to do it. Sit where the screen is visible rather than beside the microphone, and say at the start that you are listening. What to watch for is simple: is the student working while the tutor watches, or is the tutor talking while the student watches? The first is teaching. Dropping in unannounced halfway through a session is the version that costs attention, so arrange it in advance.

faqs.question: What happens when the bandwidth drops at the evening peak in a Riyadh compound?
faqs.answer: The session continues on audio with the shared whiteboard, which needs a fraction of the data that video does, and the tutor narrates what they are writing. If the drop costs more than a few minutes the time is made up by extending the next session rather than squeezing the current one. Families with a known evening dip usually move the slot half an hour earlier, which solves it outright more often than any technical fix does.

faqs.question: How is homework set on a Sunday evening checked before the next session?
faqs.answer: The task is set as one specific piece of work rather than a page range, and it is sent to the student in writing at the end of the session. It is submitted as a photograph or a file a day before the next slot so the tutor can read it beforehand, which means the session starts with the correction rather than the reading. A task that is only looked at live wastes the first fifteen minutes of every lesson.

evening-ib-tutor.closingHeading: Say where you are in the year, then pick the hour
evening-ib-tutor.closingBody: Send the subject, the level and where the student sits in the year: autumn, post-mock, or the final stretch before the May session. Then take the free trial lesson, which is one past-paper question worked live online so the gap can be seen rather than described. You will get a recommendation on how many evenings are warranted and which hour between Sunday and Thursday is realistic given who teaches the subject. Every slot is agreed in Arabia Standard Time and written down, so it does not move when another country changes its clocks.

experienced-ib-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB Diploma Programme and Middle Years Programme subjects to families across the Kingdom. Each profile names the subjects and levels that person actually teaches, the boards they have taught for, and the hours they hold open on Arabia Standard Time. Ask about complete cohorts taught before you ask about anything else.

intro.heading: Experience you cannot book is experience you do not have
paragraphs: Most families searching for an experienced IB tutor in Saudi Arabia start from the wrong end. They begin with the subject, then the level, then a degree or a teaching qualification, and they arrive at the question of availability last, after they have already decided who they want. Then the schedule collapses. The tutor they chose teaches in a school until four in the afternoon in their own time zone, which is seven in the evening here, by which point a Diploma student in Riyadh has been working since half past two and has nothing left to give.

So this page runs the other way round. It starts with the Saudi school week, which runs Sunday to Thursday. It then counts the hours that week leaves after the school run, and sets those hours against what an experienced tutor in India, the United Kingdom, South Africa or South East Asia is actually doing at that moment on their own clock. Only after that does it get to credentials, cost and the university endgame, because a tutor who cannot reach your window every week for a whole term is not a candidate, whatever their record.

That ordering is not a stylistic choice. Lessons for Saudi families are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a Saudi address; in-home visits are a service we run only in India. What online delivery buys a family here is exactly the thing the four-hour evening window takes away: access to a national and international pool of subject specialists instead of whoever happens to live within a twenty-minute drive of the compound gate. A student taking Chemistry at Higher Level gets a Chemistry Higher Level teacher, not a general science graduate who is nearby.

The word experienced also needs taking apart, because it is doing a lot of unexamined work in this market. Years in a classroom is the weakest measure of the lot. The measures that predict whether a tutor can move a Diploma grade are narrower and all of them are checkable: complete cohorts taken through to the final papers in that subject at that level, series marked for a board, internal assessments supervised to submission, and whether the person can tell you what changed in the current subject guide. A tutor with fifteen years of A Level teaching and one year of Diploma teaching is experienced, but not at the thing you are buying.

What follows is the version we would give a family over the phone. The week and the clock first, because they decide who is reachable. Then the units of experience that matter, and the ones that do not transfer. Then the advertised rates in this market, with who publishes each figure, so you can see what the premium on experience actually looks like in riyals. Then what an online lesson involves from your side of the screen, and finally the Ministry of Education equivalency and Qiyas testing route that most subject tutoring never touches.

experienced-ib-tutor.programmesIntro: Saudi schools run several IB programmes side by side, and a family moving between them loses a term to the transition unless somebody plans for it. These are the four programmes an experienced tutor is asked to work across here, with what each one actually demands of a student in the Kingdom.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: An inquiry-led primary framework with no external examinations and no published grades. Progress is recorded against learning outcomes, portfolios and teacher judgement, which makes it the hardest programme for a parent to assess from the outside. Reading fluency, number facts and written stamina are the three things that either get built here or get paid for later with interest.
programmes.countryNote: Primary tutoring is the scarcest format in the Kingdom, because a seven-year-old can only work in a short window straight after school and that window is the one every family wants. Experienced primary teachers who will take a 16:30 Arabia Standard Time slot are rarer than Diploma specialists, so these slots are agreed a term ahead.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups marked against four published criteria per subject, each scored out of eight and converted to a grade out of seven by a published boundary table. The Personal Project sits in the final year. Students arriving from a marks-out-of-100 system usually misread the criteria entirely, writing more when the criterion wanted a different kind of response.
programmes.countryNote: A good number of international schools in Riyadh and Jeddah run the MYP and then move students into the Diploma Programme, while others switch to Cambridge IGCSE at Year 10. A family that changes school mid-Kingdom can cross that line without noticing, which is the single most common reason a Year 10 student here suddenly needs outside teaching.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three normally at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Subject grades run one to seven, giving 42 points, with up to three more from the Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay matrix. Internally assessed work is set and marked inside the school and then moderated externally, so it closes long before the final papers.
programmes.countryNote: The Diploma is the programme Saudi families buy the most tutoring for, and almost all of it is bought too late. The internal assessment in a science subject is drafted in the first year and finished early in the second; by the time a parent sees a disappointing mock in the spring term, that component is already fixed and only the written papers are still moveable.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: A smaller IB route combining at least two Diploma courses with a career-related study, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. It is assessed partly through Diploma subject examinations and partly through the career-related qualification, so the tutoring need is usually concentrated in the two or three Diploma courses the student carries.
programmes.countryNote: Fewer schools in the Kingdom offer the Career-related Programme than offer the Diploma, so a family considering it should confirm directly with the school which Diploma courses are available inside it. Where it is offered, the tutoring brief is narrow and short: shore up the examined Diploma subjects and leave the reflective project to the school's own supervisor.

experienced-ib-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma subjects families in the Kingdom ask for most often. Each note says what the subject actually assesses and where an experienced teacher expects to find the marks, because that is the test of whether a tutor has taken a cohort through it or only read the guide.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof, calculus and algebraic fluency, with a non-calculator paper at both levels. Higher Level adds proof by induction, complex numbers, Maclaurin series and a far longer calculus reach. Marks go missing in method lines rather than in answers: a student who writes only the final value loses the working marks a marker is contractually required to look for.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology-heavy work, with graphical calculator use assumed throughout. Higher Level carries substantial statistics, matrices and graph theory. Students who chose it to avoid algebra find the Higher Level statistics harder than the calculus they were avoiding, and lose marks on interpreting output rather than on producing it.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Three written papers plus an internally assessed investigation. Paper 1 is multiple choice and the data analysis section; Paper 2 is structured and extended response; Paper 3 covers the option and experimental technique. The recurring loss is unit and uncertainty treatment in the investigation, which costs criterion marks no amount of content revision recovers.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium, organic mechanisms and the Higher Level extensions that have no Standard Level equivalent at all. The internally assessed investigation is where most Diploma Chemistry grades are quietly decided. An experienced teacher will ask to see the research question before anything else, because a question that cannot generate enough data cannot reach the top bands.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Heavy on precise definition and on statistical handling of biological data, which catches strong students who write fluently but imprecisely. Command terms decide the mark here more than in any other science: an answer that describes when the question said explain is complete prose and an incomplete answer.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy, real-world application and the internally assessed commentaries built on published news articles. Higher Level adds quantitative questions and a longer policy paper. Marks are lost on diagrams drawn without labels or without a shown shift, and on commentaries that summarise an article instead of applying a specific theory to it.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study analysis against named tools, with a pre-released case for one paper and an internally assessed research project. Students arriving from an essay-based system write general business commentary and score in the lower bands; the mark scheme rewards a named tool applied to the specific organisation in front of them.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Guided textual analysis, a comparative essay, the individual oral and, at Higher Level, the essay on a studied text. The oral is where an unprepared student loses most, because it needs a global issue and two extracts chosen and defended well before the recording date the school sets.

subjects.name: Arabic A and Arabic B
subjects.description: Arabic A is studied as a first language with literary analysis in Arabic; Arabic B is the acquisition route for students who read and speak it to varying levels at home. Families in the Kingdom often misplace a child between the two, and the wrong placement shows up as a ceiling on the grade rather than as weak work.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Paper 1 and 2 on systems, algorithms and the case study, plus the internally assessed solution. Higher Level adds the abstract data structures and recursion that defeat students who can code but have never been examined on tracing a structure by hand on paper under timed conditions.

experienced-ib-tutor.regionsTitle: Where the families we teach actually live, and what the evening looks like there
experienced-ib-tutor.regionsIntro: Distance is the honest argument for online teaching in the Kingdom, and it works differently in each city. In Riyadh the constraint is traffic; in the Eastern Province it is that a family lives in one city and attends school in another; in Tabuk, Yanbu or NEOM it is that the local specialist pool for a Higher Level subject may not exist at all.

regions.name: Riyadh
regions.note: Roughly an hour across in traffic north to south. A family in Al Olaya and a family in Al Narjis do the same school run at very different cost, which is why two households at the same school ask for slots ninety minutes apart.

regions.name: Jeddah
regions.note: A long coastal spine from the historic centre north to Obhur. Schools sit along it unevenly, so a northern household can spend as long on the Corniche as a Riyadh family spends crossing the city, and the 17:00 slot is often unusable.

regions.name: Dhahran
regions.note: Camp and compound life sets the rhythm here: a short, predictable school run, then structured activities that fill the early evening. Lessons from 18:30 tend to survive the term better than earlier ones, because they sit after the activity block rather than inside it.

regions.name: Al Khobar
regions.note: Part of a single school and labour market with Dammam and Dhahran, with the King Fahd Causeway to Bahrain at one end. Families commute between all three cities for school, so the slot has to be set from the household's own door-to-door time, not from the school's bell.

regions.name: Jubail
regions.note: An industrial city with a compact international school provision and long working hours for one or both parents. Diploma students here often study late and independently, which makes a single ninety-minute lesson early in the week more effective than two shorter ones.

regions.name: Yanbu
regions.note: A Red Sea industrial city where the local pool for a Higher Level science or Mathematics Analysis and Approaches specialist is thin. Families here were already using video lessons before most of the Kingdom, and the scheduling conversation is usually about the tutor's base, not about travel.

regions.name: Tabuk
regions.note: A regional centre in the north-west with limited international-curriculum provision. A student carrying three Higher Levels here will usually be the only one in their year doing so, which makes an outside specialist less of a top-up and more of the main teaching for that subject.

regions.name: NEOM
regions.note: A new and fast-changing community, with families arriving mid-course from several different school systems. The common brief here is a mid-year arrival into the first Diploma year, where the student has covered the content in a different order and needs mapping onto the school's scheme of work.

schoolClusters.note: Riyadh holds the Kingdom's densest cluster of international-curriculum schools, and provision inside it varies: some run the full PYP, MYP and Diploma route, others run only part of it, and several run Cambridge alongside. Students we support attend schools including the following.

The Eastern Province cluster behaves as one market: International Schools Group runs several campuses, the Diploma is offered on some of them and not others, and the British-curriculum schools sit alongside. Students we support attend schools including the following.

experienced-ib-tutor.modesIntro: There are only a few lesson patterns that survive a Saudi term intact. These are the ones that work, and the reasoning behind each, so a family can pick on logistics rather than on a sales conversation.

modes.title: One weekly ninety-minute slot, early in the week
modes.description: The default, and the pattern with the best survival rate across a term. Placed on a Sunday or Monday evening it gives the student four school days to act on what came out of the lesson, and it gives the tutor a full week of the student's written work to mark before the next one. For a single weak subject this is usually all that is needed.
bullets: Best for one subject at one level, taught over a whole term
Fixed day and time in Arabia Standard Time, booked for the term
Written work photographed and sent between lessons for marking
A short note to the parent after each session

modes.title: A paired slot early and mid-week for two Higher Levels
modes.description: A student carrying two demanding Higher Levels cannot usefully cover both in one evening; attention is gone after the first ninety minutes. Splitting them across a Sunday or Monday and a Wednesday keeps each subject fresh and spreads the written work across the week rather than piling it onto one weekend.
bullets: Two separate specialists, one per subject, rather than one generalist
Each lesson on a fixed weekday, never both on the same evening
Shared written record so neither tutor duplicates the other's work
Reviewed together at four weeks against the school's own assessments

modes.title: A Friday morning block
modes.description: Friday morning is the one genuinely free daytime block in the Saudi week, and it suits work that does not fit a tired weekday evening: a full past paper under timed conditions, a long piece of internal assessment analysis, or catch-up teaching for a student who arrived mid-course. Families who take a Friday slot tend to keep it, because nothing competes for it.
bullets: Two to three hours, long enough for a complete paper and its review
Suits mid-course arrivals and students rebuilding a weak foundation
Also the easiest slot for a tutor based further east to reach
Can run fortnightly alongside a weekday evening slot

modes.title: An intensive run before a series
modes.description: A short, dense block of lessons in the weeks before the May session or a Cambridge June series, aimed at examination technique rather than content. It is the most expensive way to buy support per week and the least effective way to fix a content gap, so we say plainly when a family is too late for it to do what they hope.
bullets: Two or three sessions a week for a fixed number of weeks
Past papers marked to the published mark scheme, not to a feeling
Timing, question choice and command terms, not new teaching
Agreed with an end date, so it does not drift into the series itself

sections.heading: The hours a Saudi school week actually leaves
paragraphs: Start with the week, because the week decides everything else. The school week in the Kingdom runs Sunday to Thursday, and Friday and Saturday are the weekend. A family that has moved from the United Kingdom, Ireland, South Africa or India spends a whole term re-learning that Sunday is a working day and that Thursday evening is the start of the weekend rather than the middle of the week. Any tutor who proposes a Monday and Wednesday pattern without asking about this has not worked with a Saudi family before, and that single question tells you more than a profile does.

Now count the hours the week leaves. Most international schools in Riyadh, Jeddah and the Eastern Province finish their secondary day somewhere between half past two and half past three. A school run across Riyadh at that hour can take forty minutes in each direction. In the Dammam, Al Khobar and Dhahran cluster, families routinely live in one city and attend school in another, so the door-to-door figure is longer than the map suggests. By the time a Diploma student is home, fed and has started the evening's own work, the usable window for a lesson is roughly five in the afternoon to nine at night, five evenings out of seven.

That window is four hours wide, and it is the same four hours for every family in the country. A tutor who teaches Chemistry at Higher Level superbly at eleven in the morning Saudi time is no use to a student who is sitting in a Chemistry lesson at school at eleven. This is why availability, not credentials, is the first filter we apply to a match. An experienced tutor who cannot reach that window every week for a whole term is not a candidate for a weekly slot, however strong the subject knowledge, because a slot that has to move every third week stops being a routine and starts being a negotiation.

Two patterns survive the window well. One lesson of ninety minutes on a Sunday or Monday, early in the week, while the student still has school days left to act on what came out of it. Or two sixty-minute lessons, one early and one on a Wednesday, for a student carrying two Higher Levels. Thursday evening works for almost nobody; the weekend begins at the school gate and attention goes with it. Friday morning is the one free daytime block in the week, and it is the slot families guard most once they have it.

sections.heading: Arabia Standard Time against your tutor's own working day
paragraphs: Arabia Standard Time is UTC+3 and the Kingdom does not change its clocks. That one fact causes more cancelled lessons than any other. A slot agreed with a tutor in a country that does observe daylight saving will move twice a year unless it is pinned to Saudi local time, and the way it usually breaks is silent: the tutor logs on at the right time on their clock and finds nobody there. So the slot is set in Arabia Standard Time, written down in Arabia Standard Time, and the tutor's own clock is allowed to move underneath it.

The raw offsets are easy. India is two and a half hours ahead of the Kingdom, so six in the evening here is half past eight there. Pakistan is two hours ahead. Singapore and Malaysia are five ahead, which puts a Saudi evening lesson at eleven at night on their side and rules out a weekly commitment. The United Kingdom is three hours behind in their winter and two behind in their summer. South Africa is one hour behind all year, and Turkey shares the Kingdom's clock exactly. Eastern North America sits seven or eight hours behind depending on the season, which turns a Saudi evening into their mid-morning.

What actually decides availability is not the offset but the tutor's employment. A serving school teacher in India finishes the classroom day in the early afternoon on their clock, which is late morning here, and is genuinely free for a Saudi evening lesson. A serving teacher in the United Kingdom is still at work when the Saudi window opens, so only the late end of it is reachable, and only on days with no after-school duty. A retired examiner in the United Kingdom, by contrast, is free in their own afternoon, which maps exactly onto the strongest Saudi slots. This is why we name the tutor's base and working pattern before a family agrees to anything.

The practical test is one question, asked before the trial lesson: what else sits in that hour on your side, every week, for the next fourteen weeks? A tutor who answers precisely has thought about it. A tutor who answers that they are flexible has not, and flexible is the word that precedes the first reschedule request in week three. A good match here is boring: the same hour, the same two faces, the same marked work arriving between sessions, through the autumn term and the spring term alike.

sections.heading: What experienced actually consists of, once you count it
paragraphs: Every tutoring profile in this market says experienced. The word is free, so it carries no information, and a parent cannot sift a shortlist with it. What can be sifted is a set of countable units, each of which maps onto something a student will feel in a lesson. The most useful single unit is the complete cohort: a group taken from the start of a course through to the final papers, in that subject, at that level. A teacher who has done that three or four times knows which topic the cohort always meets too late, and plans the year to arrive there early.

The second unit is series marked for a board. A marker applies a mark scheme rather than explains one, and that is a different mental habit from teaching. Someone who has marked a Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel component knows which wordings score and which near-misses do not, and can tell a student exactly why a fluent paragraph earned two of four marks. The claim is checkable in conversation: the board, the component code, the role, and what the standardisation process actually required of them. Vague answers here are the most common bluff in the market.

The third and fourth units are narrower but decide real grades. Internal assessments supervised to submission, because the criterion wording and the band descriptors are learned by doing them, not by reading them. And syllabus revisions lived through, because subject guides change: topics are dropped, assessment outlines are restructured, command term lists are rewritten. An experienced tutor should be able to say what is different in the current guide for your child's subject without looking it up, and a tutor who cannot is teaching the course they themselves were taught.

None of this needs a reference or a certificate to verify. It needs four questions and ten minutes of attention, and the answers are either specific or they are not. That is also why we will not publish a figure for how good our matching is: any number would be a claim a family cannot check, and the whole point of the units below is that each one can be checked by the person paying.

Series marked for a named board, with the component and the role stated
Internal assessments supervised through to the school's submission deadline
A clear answer on what changed in the current subject guide
Mock papers the tutor wrote and marked themselves
Time in a Gulf or Saudi school, which shows in how they talk about the week
