expert-ib-tutor.programmesIntro: Three IB programmes run in Saudi schools, and a family rarely needs the same kind of help in each. These notes say what outside teaching is usually bought for at each stage.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Taught through transdisciplinary units rather than subject syllabuses, so there is no paper to prepare for and no mark scheme to learn. Outside support here is reading fluency, number confidence, or settling a child who arrived mid-unit.
programmes.countryNote: In the Kingdom the PYP usually feeds a school that also runs the Middle Years Programme, so the real question is readiness for subject-split teaching in two years.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Assessed against published criteria rather than examination papers, and finished with the Personal Project. Students never taught what criterion A rewards produce good work that scores mid-band. Expert help here is criterion literacy plus the content the Diploma assumes.
programmes.countryNote: Several Saudi schools run the Middle Years Programme without the Diploma above it, so families plan a move at the end of Year 11 - into a Diploma school, Cambridge IGCSE, or another city.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects at Higher or Standard Level plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Every subject carries written papers and an internal assessment, and that is where a term of drift is hardest to recover.
programmes.countryNote: A Saudi Diploma student also carries the university endgame: Ministry of Education equivalency, and for most Saudi universities the Qudurat and Tahsili tests sat through Qiyas. Neither is taught inside the Diploma.

expert-ib-tutor.subjectsIntro: Expertise is subject-shaped. A tutor strong on Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation is not automatically right for Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level. These are the components families ask for most.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof, calculus and the Paper 3 problem-solving paper only Higher Level sits. Marks go missing on unjustified steps rather than wrong answers.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and heavy technology use. Students who moved across from Analysis and Approaches carry algebraic habits that cost modelling marks.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The Higher Level extensions and the uncertainties work inside the internal assessment. Strong students still lose marks on explain questions wanting a mechanism.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics. The data booklet is allowed and routinely underused; knowing which page holds what is worth marks in a timed paper.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: A large terminology load against a small set of recurring command terms. The internal assessment stands or falls on a variable that can be measured.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and the evaluation sentence. A correct diagram with no labelled shift pays less than half of what the same thinking should earn.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The individual oral and the Paper 1 unseen analysis. Students write about what a text says and forget the question asks how it is built.

subjects.name: Arabic A and Arabic B
subjects.description: Two courses often confused at enrolment. Arabic A is literature for first-language students; Arabic B is acquisition, and the paper demands differ.

expert-ib-tutor.regionsTitle: Where the families searching for this actually are
expert-ib-tutor.regionsIntro: Distance is the honest reason online teaching wins outside the three big clusters. Where a family lives decides how many in-home specialists exist within reach, and the answer is rarely a national average.

regions.name: Riyadh
regions.note: Roughly an hour across in traffic. Al Olaya and Al Malqa families attend the same schools with different school runs, which decides whether a 4pm slot works.

regions.name: Jeddah
regions.note: A long coastal spine from the historic centre north to Obhur. Families live at one end and school at the other, so evening slots are safer.

regions.name: Dammam, Al Khobar and Dhahran
regions.note: One labour and school market. Families live in one of the three and attend school in another, and the Diploma runs at only some campuses.

regions.name: Al Ahsa
regions.note: An hour and a half inland from that cluster. The local pool of Diploma subject specialists is small, and driving to Al Khobar costs an evening.

regions.name: Thuwal
regions.note: The KAUST campus community north of Jeddah, served by The KAUST School. A compound study week is quiet and predictable, which suits a fixed slot.

regions.name: Abha and Khamis Mushait
regions.note: About 25km apart in 'Asir at altitude, sharing one catchment. Higher Level science and Mathematics AA specialists are hardest to find here.

schoolClusters.note: Riyadh holds the widest spread of IB provision in the Kingdom, and schools here set their own calendars - three terms in most international schools against two semesters in nearby Ministry of Education schools.
Jeddah mixes IB and Cambridge provision, sometimes inside one school, so a family weighing the Diploma against A Levels is choosing between two corridors of one building.

expert-ib-tutor.modesIntro: Three shapes of support cover almost every family arriving through this page. The shape matters more than the hours: two well-placed sessions a week beat four badly placed ones.

modes.title: One weekly slot on one named component
modes.description: A single ninety-minute session each week, fixed to the same evening, aimed at one subject and usually one paper inside it. That gives a tutor continuity enough to see a mark pattern.

sections.heading: Four kinds of help, and what each one actually fixes
paragraphs: The search that brings a family here is usually typed at a specific moment. A report has come home with a 4 in a Higher Level subject, or a Diploma student has met an internal assessment they cannot start. The decision is not whether to buy help. It is which of four kinds to buy, and the four are not interchangeable - each fixes a different problem, and three of them will be wrong for any given family at any given moment.

Start with the school, because a subject teacher's diagnosis is free and better informed than anybody else's. Ask which component the marks are being lost on, and ask to see the mark scheme the teacher is working from. A group revision centre is cheap per hour and genuinely useful for a popular subject with a predictable paper, but it cannot follow one student's pattern of errors. An in-home tutor solves supervision and narrows the pool to drivable distance.

A one-to-one online specialist inverts that last trade. The pool becomes everyone who teaches the component well rather than everyone within a twenty-minute drive of your district, and the travel loading comes back out of the rate. The figures below are advertised rates published by tutoring platforms and tutor-marketplace guides in this market - not a market average, and not a price here. What an arrangement costs depends on the subject, the level, how scarce that specialist is, and how long the arrangement runs.

sections.heading: What a school licence covers, and what it leaves to you
paragraphs: Private and international schools in the Kingdom are licensed by the Ministry of Education. School evaluation and accreditation runs through the Education and Training Evaluation Commission, ETEC, which operates e-services for national school accreditation and for the approval of the international accreditation bodies many international schools also hold. A school running the Diploma has additionally been authorised to do so by the IB itself, which is a programme-level decision about the school rather than about any individual teacher inside it.

What that system governs is the institution: governance, premises, safeguarding, and whether the programme is delivered as the programme requires. It is a real safeguard and worth reading - a school's evaluation report is one of the few documents a parent can obtain that was not written by the school's own marketing department. What it does not do is tell you whether the person teaching Higher Level Chemistry this year has taught Higher Level Chemistry before, or has ever opened the current subject guide.

That is not a criticism of Saudi schools. It is how school regulation works everywhere. Staffing a Diploma is hard in any country: a school needs a specialist for every Higher Level it offers, and a single resignation in a small department can leave a cohort taught by a willing generalist for a term. Ask the school directly, in writing, which subjects at which levels it is running this year and who teaches each of them. A straight answer is a good sign.

sections.heading: One question that tests any claim of expertise
paragraphs: Every profile in this market claims subject expertise and examiner experience. Both claims are checkable with a single question each, and the question takes under a minute of a trial lesson. For subject expertise: which syllabus points in this subject does my child's school usually run short of time on, and what do you do differently there? A specialist answers with topic names. A generalist answers with adjectives about the programme and then changes the subject.

For examiner experience, the question is which component. Marking Paper 1 of one subject for one board teaches a very specific thing: what the published scheme pays for, and which near-miss answers earn nothing at all. It does not confer general authority over the Diploma. A tutor who names the component, the board and what marking changed about their teaching is telling you something real. A tutor who offers the word examiner with no component attached is not.

The third question is the honesty one, and it matters most on assessed work. Ask where their help stops on an internal assessment draft. The answer you want is specific and limited: they will read the student's own writing, point at a criterion not yet met, ask questions, and hand it back. A tutor who offers more than that is offering something a school is required to report, and it is the family that carries the consequence afterwards. Ask all three questions in the trial lesson, before money changes hands, and write the answers down.

sections.heading: Expertise read off the assessment, not off a CV
paragraphs: The gap between knowing a subject and being paid for knowing it is almost entirely command terms. State, outline, describe, explain, analyse, evaluate and justify each buy a different amount of writing, and a student who answers an explain question with a description has written something true that earns nothing. This is the single most transferable thing an expert tutor teaches, and it is invisible in a textbook, because textbooks are not written to a mark scheme.

Paper structure decides where a term of work should go. In the Diploma sciences the internal assessment carries a fifth of the final grade and is the one component a student controls completely, which makes it the first place to look when a predicted grade is lower than a family expected. In Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level there is also Paper 3, a shorter problem-solving paper that Standard Level does not sit and that rewards a kind of thinking the other papers do not reach.

Grade boundaries move, and understanding why stops a family reading too much into a single mark. Boundaries are set after papers are marked, against how the cohort performed on that version of the paper, so a raw mark does not map to a grade until the session has been graded. A predicted grade is a teacher's professional judgement built from work already seen. It is not a promise, it can be revised, and arguing with it is less useful than improving the evidence behind it.

sections.heading: What changes year group by year group
paragraphs: In the Middle Years Programme the useful work is criterion literacy. A student who can read criterion C and say what it actually rewards writes differently from one who simply writes well, and the Personal Project is where that shows up most visibly. Content matters too, but mainly the content the Diploma will assume: algebraic fluency, a habit of writing a conclusion that refers to evidence, and enough laboratory discipline to design a fair test unaided.

DP1 is where subject choices stop being reversible in practice. Six subjects, three at Higher Level, locked in a window that closes early in the first term, and the decision interacts with university plans a family may not have made yet. The work in DP1 is foundations, plus getting the internal assessment started early enough that it can be rescued if the first idea fails. Most families who arrive in DP2 in trouble were fine in DP1 and simply left the internal assessment late.

DP2 is a triage year. There is not enough time to re-teach two years of content, so expert help in DP2 means choosing what not to do: finishing the internal assessment to a criterion rather than to a feeling, drilling the two question types that carry the most marks, and leaving a weak topic alone when marks are cheaper elsewhere. Starting in the final term is still worth doing, but what it can achieve is narrower, and a tutor should say so before taking the booking.

sections.heading: The university endgame: equivalency, Qudurat and Tahsili
paragraphs: An IB Diploma is not automatically a certificate a Saudi university treats as equivalent to the Saudi secondary certificate. It becomes one through an equivalency decision - mu'adalah - issued by the Ministry of Education, and the same requirement applies to A Levels and to an American high school diploma. Families consistently discover this late, in the final school year, when documents take longer than anyone expected. The school's Diploma coordinator and the Ministry's own published guidance are the two places to start.

Most Saudi universities also use the Qiyas tests run by ETEC's National Center for Assessment. Qudurat, the General Aptitude Test, measures verbal and quantitative reasoning rather than syllabus content, and can be sat in Arabic or in English. Tahsili, the Achievement Test, covers the science-stream subjects - mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology and English - and its content follows the Saudi national curriculum. That last clause is the whole of the problem for an international-curriculum student.

The material overlaps what a Diploma student has studied; the framing does not. A student who can write a strong Higher Level Chemistry paper can still meet Tahsili questions phrased in an order and a vocabulary nobody has ever taught them in. The honest preparation is exposure to the national-curriculum framing, started early rather than in the final weeks. No tutor can promise an admission outcome, and no page should publish a score threshold or a weighting formula: a university's own published criteria is the only reliable source.

sections.heading: What an expert tutor will not do, and what to do when none is free
paragraphs: The line on assessed work is not a technicality. An internal assessment, an Extended Essay, a Theory of Knowledge essay and a Personal Project must be the student's own work, and a school is required to act on a suspicion that it is not. A tutor teaches the skill, reads what the student has written, names the criterion that is not yet met and asks questions. A tutor does not produce the text, and a provider offering to is selling a family a malpractice investigation.

Keep a record. Dated drafts in the student's own account, a note of what each session covered, and feedback written as questions rather than as replacement sentences will all stand up if anyone ever asks. This is also the practical test of a provider: ask how they handle a draft, and listen for whether the answer contains a limit. The essay mills competing for this search do not volunteer one, and that absence is the clearest signal a parent gets.

The honest last point. Sometimes there is no specialist free for a scarce component at the hour a family needs, and the right answer is to say so rather than to put a willing generalist in the slot. Where that happens the options are a different weekly time, a short wait for the right person, or a narrower brief - examination technique now and content later. A trial lesson is free and happens first, which is the point at which both sides find out.

faqs.question: At what point in the Middle Years Programme does an expert subject tutor actually change anything?
faqs.answer: Usually in Year 9 or Year 10, when the criteria stop being generous and the Diploma's assumptions start being made. Before that, a strong class teacher and reading at home do most of the work. What a specialist adds is criterion literacy: reading criterion B or C and saying what it rewards, which changes how a student writes long before it changes what they know. The Personal Project is the second moment worth paying for.

faqs.question: What should a student have in place by the end of DP1 before an expert tutor is worth adding?
faqs.answer: Three things. A real internal assessment idea in each subject that needs one, not a title. A set of marked papers you can look at together, because a mark pattern is diagnosable and a single bad test is not. And an honest view of which Higher Level is weakest. A student without those three spends the first month of DP2 paying a tutor to build them, which works but costs time that was free earlier.

faqs.question: Is it too late to bring in an expert IB tutor in the final term of DP2?
faqs.answer: No, but what it can do is narrower, and a tutor should say so before taking the booking. There is no time to re-teach two years, so the work becomes selection: the two question types that carry the most marks, the internal assessment finished properly against its criteria, and the technique that converts knowledge the student already has. Families asking for two grade-bearing habits and a finished internal assessment are rarely disappointed.

faqs.question: Does a strong IGCSE grade mean a student can skip outside help in the first Diploma year?
faqs.answer: Often it does, and that is the honest answer. The exception is the jump into a Higher Level science or Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches, where a top IGCSE grade establishes fluency but not the habit of justifying each step. Watch the first set of Higher Level papers rather than the certificate. If the marks hold, do nothing. If they drop two grades and stay there for a term, the gap is usually technique.

faqs.question: How early do Higher Level choices have to be right, and can an expert tutor fix a wrong one?
faqs.answer: The window closes early in DP1, and after that a change is a school decision with timetable consequences, so the choice has to be close to right first time. A tutor can make a difficult Higher Level survivable, and can sometimes build the evidence a school will accept for a drop to Standard Level. Where the choice was made for a university course nobody has checked the prerequisites for, check them before paying for lessons.

faqs.question: What does an expert tutor do with a command term that a textbook does not?
faqs.answer: A textbook explains the content; a mark scheme pays for a particular shape of answer. A specialist takes one past-paper question, puts the published scheme beside it, and makes the student rewrite their own answer until the shape matches - an explain answer with a mechanism, an evaluate answer with a judgement rather than a list. This is the fastest-moving work in any subject, because the student already knows the material.

faqs.question: How much of a Diploma science grade sits outside the written papers?
faqs.answer: In the Diploma sciences the internal assessment carries a fifth of the final grade, and it is the one component a student controls completely: the question, the method, the data, the analysis and the write-up. That makes it the first place to look when a predicted grade disappoints, and the cheapest place to recover marks. It also makes a late start expensive. Confirm the exact weighting for your child's subject with their teacher.

faqs.question: Why does Paper 3 exist in Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Paper 3 is a shorter paper of extended problem-solving questions, sat only at Higher Level, and it tests something the other two papers cannot reach: whether a student can be led through unfamiliar mathematics and keep their reasoning intact. Students who revise by topic are often surprised by it, because the questions do not announce which topic they belong to. Preparation is different too - fewer questions, more time on each.

faqs.question: How do grade boundaries move, and what should a parent read into a predicted grade?
faqs.answer: Boundaries are set after papers are marked, against how the cohort performed on that particular version of the paper, which is why a raw mark means little until a session is graded. A harder paper moves the boundary down. A predicted grade is separate: a teacher's professional judgement built from work already seen. It is not a promise and it can be revised. The useful response to a disappointing prediction is better evidence.

faqs.question: What is Ministry of Education equivalency, and when should a Diploma family start it?
faqs.answer: Equivalency, or mu'adalah, is the decision by the Ministry of Education that treats a foreign or international certificate as equivalent to the Saudi secondary certificate. Without it, a Saudi university does not read an IB Diploma as a school-leaving qualification. Start asking in the first Diploma year rather than after results, because the process runs on documents - certified transcripts, attestations, school letters - and documents take longer than families expect.

faqs.question: Why does Tahsili catch out a student who has only ever studied the IB?
faqs.answer: Because Tahsili, the Achievement Test, follows the Saudi national curriculum. The subject matter overlaps an IB science and mathematics education heavily, so content is rarely the obstacle. The framing is: question order, vocabulary, the expected method, and an emphasis that differs from the one a Diploma student has trained on for two years. The fix is exposure rather than teaching, early enough that the format stops being a surprise.

faqs.question: Can a student sit Qudurat in English, and does an IB student need it at all?
faqs.answer: Qudurat, the General Aptitude Test, runs through ETEC's National Center for Assessment and is available in Arabic or in English, which matters for a student schooled entirely in English. Whether it is required depends on where the student applies: most Saudi universities use the Qiyas tests in admission, while overseas universities do not ask for them. Check the specific universities on the shortlist, because programmes inside one university can differ.

faqs.question: Where should a family check what a Saudi university actually weighs?
faqs.answer: On that university's own admission pages, for that specific programme, in the cycle they are applying in. Universities publish their own formulas combining school results with the Qiyas tests, the weightings differ between institutions and between programmes, and competitive engineering, medicine and science programmes lean hardest on Tahsili. Some universities also set a maximum age for the secondary certificate they accept, which is worth checking before a gap year.

faqs.question: Does an expert tutor help with a university application, or only with the subject?
faqs.answer: Subject teaching is the service, and it is worth being clear about that boundary. A subject specialist can tell you what a Higher Level prerequisite means in practice, and whether a chosen Mathematics route fits an engineering application. Equivalency paperwork, Qiyas registration and the application itself belong with the school's counsellor and the universities' own criteria. No tutor can promise an admission outcome, and anyone implying one is describing a decision that is not theirs.

expert-ib-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the component that is costing the marks
expert-ib-tutor.closingBody: If you take one thing from this page, make it the question: which component is losing the marks, and who has taught that component before? Ask your child's subject teacher first, because the answer is free and better informed than anybody else's. Then, if the school cannot staff it, book a free trial lesson with a specialist who can name the syllabus points before they name an hourly rate. Lessons are one-to-one and delivered online, on the Kingdom's own clock.

intro.heading: Start with the evening, then the teacher
paragraphs: Families looking for a female IB tutor in Saudi Arabia are usually solving two problems at once. One is preference about who teaches their child, which is theirs to make and needs no justification. The other is logistics, and it is the one that quietly decides everything: what time the student is actually home, which evenings are usable, and whether the person teaching them keeps a working week that overlaps with a Saudi school week at all. Get the second right and the first becomes a straightforward filter.

The school week here runs Sunday to Thursday, with Friday and Saturday as the weekend. That single fact invalidates most scheduling advice written elsewhere. Sunday evening is the start of the student's week and they are tired by it. Thursday evening is the start of a weekend and the worst time to introduce new material, though a good time for a long paper nobody has to recover from in the morning. The working core of the week is Sunday through Wednesday.

Then there is the school run. Riyadh is roughly an hour across in traffic, and a family in Al Malqa or Al Narjis in the north whose child attends a school nearer Al Olaya is not home when the bell rings. Jeddah stretches as a long coastal spine from the historic centre north to Obhur. In the Eastern Province, families live in one of Dammam, Al Khobar or Dhahran and attend school in another. The earliest workable lesson time follows arrival, not dismissal.

Because lessons are delivered online, one to one, over live video, none of that has to be negotiated against a tutor's driving distance. Nobody is sent to a Saudi address — in-home teaching is a service we run only in India — and for this particular search that format is the direct answer rather than a substitute. A family that wants a female specialist in Higher Level Chemistry is choosing from everyone who teaches it, not from whoever lives nearby and happens to be free.

Around all of this sits a system worth reading correctly. Private and international schools in the Kingdom operate under a licence from the Ministry of Education, school evaluation and accreditation runs through the Education and Training Evaluation Commission, and at the end of the school years an international certificate needs an equivalency decision before a Saudi university treats it as equivalent to the national one. Those facts shape subject choices and timing more than most families expect.

So the page runs in that order. It settles the week, the school run and the clock first, then deals directly with choosing the tutor's gender and what the online format makes possible. After that come the school-system facts a family has to read correctly: licences, the two different calendars running in the same city, and the equivalency route. It closes on switching curriculum, on employer communities, and on the four questions that tell you whether a tutor has actually taught the course.

female-ib-tutor.programmesIntro: Three IB programmes, and what each one asks of a family here.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary inquiry rather than subject teaching, with no external examinations. Progress is reported against learning outcomes, and the exhibition closes the programme in the final year.
programmes.countryNote: Support at this stage is mostly about literacy, number fluency and English where it is not the home language. Short, frequent sessions work better than long ones, and a parent sitting nearby is usually a help rather than a distraction.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Criterion-referenced assessment across eight subject groups, ending in the Personal Project. A grade from 1 to 7 is assembled from strand descriptors, so content knowledge alone does not produce a high mark.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Internal assessment carries weight in every subject and the core contributes points.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Paper 3 at Higher Level sets one long structured problem on unfamiliar ground. It rewards sustained reasoning rather than a remembered procedure.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics, with heavy use of technology. The interpretation marks are where procedurally taught students lose ground.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics and organic mechanisms carry the Higher Level extension, and the internal assessment needs a question that is measurable with school equipment.

subjects.name: Physics

subjects.name: Biology

subjects.name: Economics

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature

subjects.name: Arabic B

sections.heading: The week, the school run, and the hour a lesson can start
paragraphs: Begin with the timetable rather than the teacher, because the timetable is what fails first. The Saudi school week runs Sunday to Thursday and the weekend is Friday and Saturday. That shifts the whole shape of a tutoring week away from the Monday-to-Friday pattern most advice assumes. Sunday evening sits at the start of the student's week and carries the most fatigue. Wednesday evening is usually the strongest slot of the week, and Thursday evening belongs to long papers rather than new content.

The second constraint is the journey home. A northern Riyadh family in Al Malqa or Al Narjis whose child attends a school closer to Al Olaya is often not home until well after five, and a four o'clock slot that looked reasonable on paper collapses in the first week of term. Jeddah has the same problem along its coastal spine. In the Eastern Province, where families routinely live in one of Dammam, Al Khobar or Dhahran and attend school in another, the crossing at dismissal is far slower than the same crossing mid-morning.

The third is Arabia Standard Time, which is UTC+3 and never changes. A tutor in a country that adjusts its clocks twice a year will drift against a Saudi family unless the slot is written down in Saudi local time from the start. Settle all three before discussing anything else: the evenings that work, the hour the student is genuinely home and able to think, and the slot expressed in local time. An arrangement built on those holds for a whole term.

sections.heading: Choosing the tutor's gender, and what one-to-one online makes possible
paragraphs: This is the practical heart of the query, so it deserves a direct answer. Because every lesson is one to one over live video, the tutor is chosen rather than allocated. A family states the subject, the level and the tutor's gender in the first message, and the shortlist is built against all three. No explanation is asked for and none is needed. The same applies to language: a family can ask for a tutor comfortable teaching a subject in English to a student whose first language is Arabic.

The format matters because it widens the pool rather than narrowing it. An in-home arrangement limits a family to people who live within a workable drive, which in most Saudi cities is a small number of people and, once gender and subject and level are all specified, sometimes nobody at all. Teaching over video removes the geography from the problem. The constraint that remains is the one that should remain: who has actually taught this component, and are they free at a Saudi evening hour.

It is worth being honest about where a preference does cost something. In very scarce combinations — a female specialist in Higher Level Physics with marking experience, free at six in the evening — the shortlist can be short, and the choice may be between waiting a few weeks for a slot and starting with somebody who meets three of the four criteria. We will say which it is rather than quietly substituting. The table below sets out what each format actually offers.

sections.heading: Gender-segregated schooling, and what it changes for outside teaching
paragraphs: Gender-segregated schooling exists in parts of the education system in the Kingdom, and international schools vary in how they are organised. For a family arranging outside teaching, the practical consequences are narrow and worth stating plainly rather than left for the reader to infer. A student's school day, timetable structure and the staff they are used to may differ from what a tutor elsewhere assumes, and a tutor worth having asks about it in the first conversation rather than guessing.

The second consequence is about subject staffing. A smaller cohort within a school means fewer teachers per subject, and where a school is organised into separate sections the number of specialists available to any one group of students can be smaller again. That is arithmetic rather than policy, and it is one of the ordinary reasons a family ends up looking outside the school for a Higher Level subject that the school nominally offers.

The third is simply that preference is allowed to be preference. A family may want a female tutor because their daughter works better that way, because of how the household runs, or for no stated reason at all. Online one-to-one teaching makes that a filter in a list rather than a negotiation. What a tutor is judged on afterwards does not change: component knowledge, whether they can read a marked paper correctly, and whether they are free at an hour that works. Those three tests apply identically whoever the family has chosen, and they are the only ones that predict how the next six months will go.

sections.heading: Licences, calendars and equivalency: the system a family works inside
paragraphs: Private and international schools in the Kingdom operate under a licence from the Ministry of Education. Separately, school evaluation and accreditation runs through the Education and Training Evaluation Commission, usually called ETEC, which operates e-services covering national school accreditation and the approval of international accreditation bodies. A school may also be authorised to run IB programmes, which is a decision taken by the IB organisation rather than by a Saudi body. None of these processes covers private tutoring, which is unregulated.

Calendars are the part that catches relocating families. Ministry schools run a two-semester year that opens in late August and closes in late June, with an autumn break, a midyear break and an Eid Al Fitr break. International and British-curriculum schools set their own calendars and most run three terms, with dates that differ school by school inside the same city. Never plan around a calendar copied from another school: ask your own school for its published dates and work from those.

At the far end sits equivalency. A foreign or international certificate needs an equivalency decision — mu'adalah — from the Ministry of Education before a Saudi university treats it as equivalent to the national secondary certificate, and that applies to an IB Diploma, A Levels and an American high school diploma alike. Alongside it are Qudurat and Tahsili, delivered by the National Center for Assessment, Qiyas. Universities publish their own criteria; check the figures with the university rather than a third-party summary.

sections.heading: Switching into the Diploma from a national, British or American school
paragraphs: Each route arrives with a different gap, and knowing which one saves a term. A student from a Saudi national-curriculum school usually brings solid mathematics and science content but meets an assessment culture that pays for command terms, structured reasoning and a written register rather than recall. The first weeks are better spent on how answers are built than on revisiting content the student already holds, and the English demand of the subject papers is often the real obstacle rather than the subject itself.

A student arriving from a British Year 11 has the paper habit already and usually adapts quickly to the written components. What is new is the volume: six subjects rather than three or four, an internal assessment in every one of them, plus Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay. The failure mode here is time management rather than ability, and it shows up in the second term when several internal assessment deadlines land together and nothing was started early.

An American-curriculum student generally brings strong breadth, confident writing and weaker depth in the sciences and mathematics, which is exactly where Higher Level bites. Chemistry and Physics at Higher Level assume more than a general course covers, and the gap appears within weeks rather than months. Whichever route a student comes from, the useful first step is the same: map the previous syllabus against this one, including option topics, and put the internal assessment timeline on paper before any teaching starts.

sections.heading: Compound and camp communities, and the study week inside them
paragraphs: A sizeable number of families in the Kingdom live in employer communities — compounds and camps attached to a company, a university or an industrial city — and the study week inside one works differently from a city household's. The school is often on site or a short ride away, which removes the traffic problem entirely and makes an earlier lesson slot realistic. In Thuwal, Jubail and parts of the Eastern Province that is the ordinary arrangement rather than the exception.

What it adds instead is a schedule shaped by one employer. Term dates, holiday patterns and even the working day follow the organisation rather than the city, so a tutoring slot has to be agreed against the community's rhythm, including the long breaks when much of it empties out. Families who keep a single fortnightly session running through a long break come back without having lost the thread; families who stop entirely usually pay for it in the first weeks of the new term.

The subject question is sharper in these communities too. A school serving one employer's population has a small cohort, which means fewer Higher Level options actually run and fewer specialists per subject. That is the honest reason outside teaching is common here, and it has nothing to do with the quality of the school. Ask which Higher Level subjects ran with the last cohort, how many teachers cover each science, and what happens when an option does not fill.

sections.heading: What to ask a prospective IB tutor, and what a good answer sounds like
paragraphs: Four questions separate a specialist from a subject graduate, and all four can be asked before paying anything. Which syllabus components does my child sit, and what does the Higher Level extension add that Standard Level does not have? Here is a marked answer — why did it score what it scored? What would you work on first, and what will you not be able to fix in the time we have? The last one is the most revealing, because an honest answer exists and a salesperson will not give it.

A good answer is specific within a sentence. A tutor who teaches the course names the components without looking, describes the extension material concretely, and reads a marked answer in the language of the mark scheme rather than in generalities about confidence. On the internal assessment they will say clearly what they will and will not do: teaching the criteria, testing a research question for feasibility and commenting on the student's own draft, but not writing or completing any part of it.

Treat unverifiable numbers as noise. Success percentages, star ratings and headcounts cannot be checked by a parent and are published by the party they flatter. Advertised rates are different, because they are at least attributable: a tutoring-company listing puts IB subject tutoring in Riyadh from about SAR 180, rising to roughly SAR 200 to 220 for Higher Level tracks, which is one provider's advertised figure rather than an average or our price. No tutor can promise a grade.

faqs.question: Can we ask for a female tutor for a specific IB subject, and how is that handled?
faqs.answer: Yes. Put it in the first message alongside the subject, the level and the evenings that work, and the shortlist is built against all of those rather than filtered afterwards. No reason needs giving. If the combination of gender, subject, level and slot has nobody free, you will be told that plainly, with the options, rather than offered somebody who meets some of the criteria and not the rest.

faqs.question: Does asking for a female tutor narrow the pool for a Higher Level science?
faqs.answer: It can, because Higher Level Physics and Chemistry specialists are scarce before any other filter is applied. Teaching over video widens the pool from a driving radius to a national and international one, which usually absorbs the constraint. Where it does not, the realistic choice is between waiting a few weeks for a slot to open and starting at a less convenient hour. Both are better than an unqualified substitute.

faqs.question: Our daughter's school runs separate sections — will an online tutor understand how her timetable works?
faqs.answer: A tutor worth having asks about it in the first conversation instead of assuming. What matters practically is when lessons at school happen, which teacher sets the pace, how homework is issued, and when assessments fall. Send the timetable and the scheme of work if the school publishes one. A tutor who never asks how the student's school week is structured will keep setting work that collides with it.

faqs.question: What transfers when a student moves from a Saudi national-curriculum school into the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: Mathematics and science content transfers better than families expect. What does not transfer is the assessment culture: the Diploma pays for command terms, structured reasoning and a written register rather than accurate recall. The English demand of the subject papers is often the real obstacle rather than the subject matter. Spend the first weeks on how answers are built, and treat content revision as the second priority rather than the first.

faqs.question: How hard is the move from a British Year 11 into the first Diploma year?
faqs.answer: Academically it is usually manageable, because the written-paper habit is already there. The difficulty is volume: six subjects instead of three or four, an internal assessment in every one, plus Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay. Students fail on time management rather than ability, and it shows in the second term when several internal assessment deadlines arrive together. Build the timeline in the first month, not the fifth.

faqs.question: Our son is moving from an American high school into Higher Level Chemistry here — what has to be rebuilt first?
faqs.answer: Depth, mostly. A general science course covers breadth well and leaves the quantitative and mechanism-level work thinner than Higher Level assumes, so the difficulty appears within weeks rather than months. The specific gaps are usually stoichiometry and energetics, followed by the mechanism-level treatment of organic reactions. Map the previous course against the syllabus first, including the option topic his school has chosen, then teach the gaps in order of weight rather than in textbook order.

faqs.question: Which Diploma subjects are hardest to pick up after switching school mid-year?
faqs.answer: The ones with a long dependency chain: Mathematics at Higher Level, where each topic assumes the last, and the sciences, where a missed practical sequence cannot simply be read up. Subjects assessed largely through extended writing transfer more easily, because the thinking is already in place and only the conventions are new. Option topics are the hidden problem, since schools choose different ones and nobody mentions it until a mock.

faqs.question: Which curricula do schools in the Kingdom actually offer, and how do we check before enrolling?
faqs.answer: Provision is mixed. Ministry schools follow the national curriculum, while private and international schools offer IB programmes, Cambridge and Edexcel qualifications, American high school diplomas and others, sometimes more than one in the same building. Ask the school directly which qualification each year group is entered for, which stages of the IB it is authorised to run, and which Higher Level options ran with the last cohort. Written answers are worth asking for.

faqs.question: What happens if a school offers the Middle Years Programme but not the Diploma?
faqs.answer: The student reaches Year 11 and then has to move, which is a decision better made in Year 9 than discovered in Year 10. Some families transfer to a school running the Diploma, some switch to IGCSE and then A Levels, and some commute to another city in the same cluster. The Middle Years Programme prepares well for the Diploma, so the question is availability and logistics rather than readiness.

faqs.question: How do compound and camp schools differ from city schools for IB subject choice?
faqs.answer: The journey problem disappears, because the school is usually on site or minutes away, which makes an earlier evening slot realistic. The subject problem sharpens: a school serving one employer's community has a small cohort, so fewer Higher Level options run and fewer specialists cover each science. That is arithmetic rather than a reflection on the school, and it is the ordinary reason outside teaching is common in these communities.

faqs.question: How does an international school's three-term year differ from the Ministry's two semesters?
faqs.answer: Ministry schools run two semesters from late August to late June, with an autumn break, a midyear break and an Eid Al Fitr break. Most international and British-curriculum schools set their own three-term calendars, and the dates differ school by school within one city. Families with children in both systems end up managing two calendars. Always work from your own school's published dates rather than a general pattern.

faqs.question: How late can an evening IB lesson start after a northern Riyadh school run?
faqs.answer: For a family in Al Malqa or Al Narjis attending a school nearer the centre, five or six in the evening is usually the earliest realistic start, not four. Add fifteen minutes of margin, because a bad run otherwise eats the first exercise every time. Later than about eight is a poor weekly habit on a school night, though it works occasionally for a long paper before a weekend.

faqs.question: Can lessons move to a shorter, more frequent pattern when the school day is shortened?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it often works better than keeping the original hour. Three forty-minute sessions covering one component each can achieve more than two long ones when the student's day has compressed and evening routines have shifted. Agree the revised pattern before the change rather than during it, and agree the date it reverts, so the original slot is still held when the normal timetable returns.

faqs.question: What happens to a weekly IB slot during the long summer break?
faqs.answer: Three options, and the choice matters more in the Diploma than earlier. Keeping the weekly slot preserves it but is hard to sustain. Pausing entirely is cheapest and usually costs a few weeks of ground in the new term, particularly on internal assessment work. A single fortnightly session through the break is the compromise most families settle on. Ask in advance whether the slot is held if you pause.

female-ib-tutor.closingHeading: Send the subject, the level, the evenings and the preference
female-ib-tutor.closingBody: Four things in one message are enough to start: the subject and level, which evenings work once the school run is done, and whether you want a female tutor. We will come back with who teaches that component and is free at a Saudi evening hour, or tell you plainly that nobody is and what the alternatives are. The trial lesson costs nothing and should run on a piece of work the student has already lost marks on, because that is the only thing that shows how a tutor actually teaches.

intro.heading: Choosing the teacher, not just the subject
paragraphs: The phrase a female IGCSE tutor in Saudi Arabia is typed by parents in Riyadh, Jeddah, Al Khobar and a dozen smaller places, and it rarely means what a tutoring agency assumes it means. It is not a complaint about male teachers. It is a practical request: a teenage daughter working one-to-one for two hours a week, often in the evening, often on a subject she has started to dread, and a parent who would rather that hour felt straightforward for her. Gender-segregated schooling exists in parts of the system here, so for many students a woman teaching them is the normal arrangement they already know.

In an in-home market that request is hard to fill. A visiting tutor has to be a subject specialist, free in the evening, and willing to cross a city at the hour the traffic is worst. Add a specific gender to those three and the pool in any one district shrinks to whoever happens to live nearby. That is the real reason families end up with a general science graduate teaching Physics 0625 rather than somebody who has marked it. Online one-to-one takes the geography out of the problem: the tutor has to match the syllabus and the slot, and nothing else about where they live matters.

This page is about what the request costs and what it buys. Advertised rates in the Kingdom run from roughly SAR 35 an hour on budget online platforms to SAR 200 and above for senior-school examination subjects, and the figures below are other providers' published numbers rather than ours. What moves a rate is scarcity and marking experience, not the tutor's gender: asking for a woman narrows a list, it does not add a surcharge. Where it genuinely narrows the list is the handful of subjects thin in both genders, which is Additional Mathematics 0606, Physics 0625 and Computer Science 0478.

Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a Saudi address, and home visits are a service offered only in India. We say that plainly because the honest answer beats the one a parent hopes for: an online specialist who has taught the exact component outperforms a nearby generalist, and your daughter keeps the same teacher if you move from Jeddah to Dammam next term.

What follows is ordered the way a family actually decides. The week and the clock come first, because a lesson nobody can attend is worth nothing. Then the money, with the published bands and what moves them. Then how to check that the tutor in front of your daughter knows the syllabus and not merely the subject, and what she is allowed to do with coursework when it arrives.

female-igcse-tutor.programmesIntro: IGCSE sits inside a longer run. These three stages have to be thought about together, because the subject list chosen at fourteen decides what is still available at sixteen.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary and Checkpoint
programmes.description: The years before IGCSE entry, ending in Checkpoint tests in English, mathematics and science. Checkpoint is diagnostic rather than a certificate, and a weak science score is the earliest honest warning that Extended tier will be hard work.
programmes.countryNote: Schools in the Kingdom use these years to sort students into Core and Extended groups. Ask what evidence the school is using.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Two years, examined by syllabus code, with many subjects tiered. Core is graded C to G and Extended A* to E, so a student entered for Core cannot be awarded above a C however well the papers go.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge schools here enter candidates for the June series, with November used for resits. Confirm the component list and tier in writing.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The same two years on a different scale: Edexcel reports 9 to 1 and splits mathematics entry into Foundation and Higher. Papers, formula sheets and question styles differ from Cambridge even where the content looks identical.
programmes.countryNote: Some schools here run both boards in different departments, so a daughter can sit Cambridge sciences and an Edexcel mathematics paper.

female-igcse-tutor.subjectsIntro: A tutor is matched to a syllabus code, not a subject name. These are the codes families in the Kingdom ask about most, with where the marks go missing in each.

subjects.name: Mathematics 0580
subjects.description: Two written papers, no coursework. Extended candidates lose most marks on algebraic manipulation under time pressure and on unstructured multi-step questions in Paper 4.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics 0606
subjects.description: Taken alongside 0580 by students heading for A Level mathematics. The jump is calculus and trigonometric identities.

subjects.name: Physics 0625
subjects.description: Includes an alternative-to-practical paper rewarding experimental reasoning rather than recall. Describing a method precisely is where marks go.

subjects.name: Chemistry 0620
subjects.description: Organic chemistry and the mole calculations carry the heaviest losses. Definitions are examined close to word for word.

subjects.name: Biology 0610
subjects.description: The most memory-dense of the sciences. Marks disappear where a student writes everything known about a topic instead of answering the command term.

subjects.name: English First Language 0500
subjects.description: Paper 2 asks for directed writing and close analysis of language. A school essay rewards opinion; this paper rewards evidence explained.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language 0510
subjects.description: Reading and writing under a strict word count, plus listening. Marks go on answering more than the question asked.

subjects.name: Computer Science 0478
subjects.description: Paper 1 is theory and Paper 2 is algorithms and pseudocode. Schools here often staff this from the IT department.

sections.heading: What a family means by a female IGCSE tutor, and the straight answer
paragraphs: The straight answer is yes, you can specify it, and it is a normal request rather than an awkward one. When a family asks for a woman to teach a fifteen-year-old daughter Chemistry 0620, the matching brief carries three things: the board and syllabus code, the tier the school has entered her for, and the tutor's gender. None of the three is treated as optional. What the request cannot do is conjure a specialist where none exists, which is what the section on subject scarcity further down is for.

The reasons families give are practical and they vary. Some students have been taught in single-sex classes for years and work better in the pattern they know. Some are talking about a subject they are frightened of, and would rather do that with a woman. Some parents want one more adult in their daughter's week whom they have chosen deliberately. Commentary on any of that is unnecessary: it is a preference, you state it, and the matching works around it.

Where the answer gets more interesting is what the request costs. In an in-home market a narrower brief means a smaller local pool, and a smaller pool means a higher quoted rate, because that is how in-home pricing works everywhere. Online, the pool is not local, so a gender preference costs nothing by itself. The thing that still moves the number is subject scarcity, and that is worth understanding before you read any advertised rate anywhere.

sections.heading: The week and the clock come before everything else
paragraphs: Schools in the Kingdom run Sunday to Thursday, and Friday and Saturday are the weekend. That single fact invalidates most tutoring copy written for a British or Indian audience, because a tutor whose own week is Monday to Friday is being asked to teach on their Sunday and to take Friday off. It is workable, and a tutor who has taught Gulf families for years expects it, but it has to be agreed at the start rather than discovered in week three.

Arabia Standard Time is UTC+3 and the Kingdom does not change its clocks. A tutor in a country that does will drift an hour away from your daughter's slot twice a year unless the appointment is pinned to Saudi local time and their own calendar converts around it. Pin it to the Kingdom. The table below shows what a seven-in-the-evening slot here looks like from the places tutors most often sit in.

Then there is the school run. A finish at half past two or three, plus a drive across Riyadh or up the Jeddah coast, puts a realistic start somewhere between five and eight in the evening. Younger students do better at the earlier end; a Year 11 candidate working towards the June series often takes the later slot and is sharper for it. During Ramadan the school day shortens and study moves late, so the slot moves with it rather than disappearing. A Friday or Saturday session is possible and some families prefer it, though a weekend slot competes with everything else in the week.

sections.heading: What the market charges, and what actually moves the number
paragraphs: Rates in this market sit mostly behind a contact form, which is why a parent cannot calibrate. The bands in the table are other providers' advertised figures, taken from platform marketing pages, tutor-marketplace guides and tutoring-company listings. They are not a market average, and none of them is what IB Gram charges: our fee depends on the subject, the level and the length of the arrangement, and is quoted to you before anything is booked.

Read the spread as a ladder of specialism rather than a ladder of quality. The low end buys a graduate who knows the subject and will work through textbook exercises with a student who mostly needs company and structure. The upper end buys somebody who has taught the specific syllabus code for years, or marked it, and can say why a technically correct answer scored two out of four. For a Core-tier student shoring up basics, the low end is often the honest choice.

What drives the number, roughly in order: how scarce the subject specialism is, whether the tutor has marking or examining experience, the level, whether they travel, and how long the arrangement runs. A tutor's gender is not on that list and should not appear on an invoice. If a provider quotes a premium for a woman without naming a subject scarcity behind it, ask what the premium is for. The answer is usually that their local pool is small, which is an in-home problem rather than yours.

sections.heading: Where the request genuinely narrows the pool
paragraphs: Three or four IGCSE subjects are thin everywhere, in both genders, and a family asking for a woman will feel that thinness first. Additional Mathematics 0606 is the clearest case. It is taken by a small number of students in any school, it is examined at a level closer to the first year of A Level, and the people who teach it well are usually already teaching A Level somewhere else. A specific gender on top of that is a waiting list rather than an impossibility.

Computer Science 0478 is the second, for a different reason. Many schools in the Kingdom staff it from the IT department, so the student meets a competent teacher who has never sat the examination's pseudocode conventions. The theory paper is learnable from a textbook. The algorithms paper is not, and that gap is the most common reason a family goes looking outside the school for one subject rather than for a whole programme.

English First Language 0500 is thin in a quieter way. There are plenty of English teachers; there are far fewer who will mark a directed-writing task against the published criteria instead of responding to it as a reader. For the three sciences at Core tier, for 0580 Mathematics and for English as a Second Language 0510, the pool is wide enough that a gender preference changes the waiting time by days rather than weeks. Ask what the realistic start date is before you commit to a plan; a straight answer tells you how deep that provider's list actually goes.

sections.heading: Checking that a tutor knows the syllabus, not just the subject
paragraphs: A subject degree says what somebody studied. It says nothing about whether they know that Chemistry 0620 examines definitions close to word for word, that Physics 0625 carries an alternative-to-practical paper, or what the Extended tier adds to the 0580 Paper 4. Those are syllabus facts, and a tutor who does not have them to hand has not taught the course recently. The free trial lesson exists to find that out before any money moves.

Three questions do most of the work. Which paper does my daughter lose most marks on, and what is in it? What does the mark scheme for a six-mark question in this subject want that a good textbook answer does not give? What has the school entered her for, Core or Extended, and does that ceiling match what she is aiming at? A specialist answers all three in a sentence each, without reaching for the syllabus document.

Marking experience is worth asking about and worth checking rather than believing. Boards appoint examiners for a series at a time, so the honest version of the claim is specific: which board, which paper, which role. A tutor who says they have marked the subject generally, with no component named, is describing an impression. Ask for the component. Nobody is offended by the question, and it filters the field quickly. The same applies to a claim about teaching in a school: ask which school, and which board it entered candidates with.

sections.heading: Coursework, and the line a tutor does not cross
paragraphs: A tutor may teach, explain, question, model a technique on a different example and give feedback on what the student has produced. A tutor may not produce it. On an IGCSE coursework component or an MYP Personal Project, the submitted work has to be the student's own, and a school that suspects otherwise has a malpractice process it is obliged to run. No reputable tutor goes near that line, and the providers advertising essay help in this market are selling a risk the family carries, not one they carry.

The distinction is easy to hold once it is named. Reading a draft and saying which criterion is underserved is teaching; rewriting the paragraph is not. Asking why a conclusion does not follow from the data is teaching; supplying the conclusion is not. Working through a past-paper question of the same type is teaching, and working through the live coursework task is not. Sessions here run on that side of the line, and the student keeps every version of the file.

Keep a record, because it protects your daughter rather than the tutor. Dated drafts, a short note of what each session covered, and feedback kept in writing give a school everything it needs if a question is ever raised. A tutor who resists leaving a written trail of their own feedback is telling you something. The whole value of the component is that the work is hers, and the mark goes to the work that is.

sections.heading: What schools here staff, what they do not, and what a family arranges itself
paragraphs: Private and international schools in the Kingdom are licensed by the Ministry of Education, and school evaluation and accreditation runs through the Education and Training Evaluation Commission, ETEC, which operates e-services for national school accreditation and for the approval of international accreditation bodies. What none of that tells a parent is whether one particular Year 10 class has a specialist in front of it. Licensing is about the institution; staffing a minority subject is about a timetable and a recruitment market.

The pattern is consistent across the cities. Core subjects with large cohorts are staffed properly because they have to be. The subjects taken by six students in a year group get covered by whoever has a free period and the nearest qualification, or they get dropped from the option block entirely. When a school tells a family that Additional Mathematics 0606 is not running, that is a staffing decision, and the family either changes the plan or arranges the subject itself.

So the question to ask a school before enrolling, or before option forms go in, is not which subjects appear in the prospectus. It is which of them actually ran, who taught them, and what tier the cohort was entered for. If a subject on your daughter's list is one the school is quietly covering with a non-specialist, you want to know that in the autumn term rather than eight weeks before the June series. That gap is what an outside tutor is for.

faqs.question: Can I ask for a female IGCSE tutor without explaining why?
faqs.answer: Yes. The matching brief has a field for it and nobody asks for a reason. It sits alongside the board, the syllabus code and the tier as something you specify rather than hope for. The one honest caveat is availability in the scarcest subjects: for Additional Mathematics 0606 or Computer Science 0478, a specific gender can mean waiting days for the right specialist rather than starting this week. You will be told that, not quietly matched with somebody else.

faqs.question: Does asking for a female IGCSE tutor change the hourly rate?
faqs.answer: Not by itself. What moves a rate here is how scarce the subject specialism is, whether the tutor has marking experience, the level, whether they travel, and how long the arrangement runs. Gender is not on that list and should not appear on an invoice. In an in-home market a narrow brief does push the quoted figure up, because the local pool shrinks, but that is a geography problem. Ask any provider quoting a gender premium what the premium pays for.

faqs.question: My daughter is in a single-sex class at school, so is an online female tutor the obvious match?
faqs.answer: It is often the comfortable one, and comfort counts in a subject she has started to dread. It is not automatically the right one: a woman who has never taught Chemistry 0620 is still the wrong tutor. The order that works is specialism first, then gender inside that pool, then the slot. If both are available, take both. If the only 0606 specialist free this term is a man, that is a conversation rather than a refusal.

faqs.question: What may a tutor do with my daughter's IGCSE coursework, and what must she do herself?
faqs.answer: A tutor may explain the criteria, ask why a section does not follow, model the technique on a different example, and give feedback on what she has already produced. A tutor may not write, rewrite or supply any part of it. The submitted piece has to be hers, and a school that suspects otherwise runs a malpractice process. Keep dated drafts and the written feedback, because that record protects her if anyone asks how the work was made.

faqs.question: How is an MYP Personal Project supervised when a tutor is involved from outside the school?
faqs.answer: The school supervisor owns the process: they approve the goal, hold the meetings and sign the academic-honesty record. An outside tutor sits beside that, never inside it. The useful work is teaching the research skill the project needs, reading the process journal and asking the questions the criteria ask. The tutor does not choose the goal, build the product or write it up. Tell the school a tutor is involved, because a clean paper trail is easier to defend.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE Physics 0625 topics most often need teaching outside school hours?
faqs.answer: Three recur. Moments and equilibrium, where students can state the principle and still cannot set the calculation up. Circuits with more than one branch, where the method breaks before the arithmetic does. And the alternative-to-practical paper as a whole, because it asks for experimental reasoning, control variables and how to improve a method, none of which a textbook chapter drills. Thermal physics also goes missing late, usually because it was taught in the week before a holiday.

faqs.question: Why does Additional Mathematics 0606 catch out a student who was comfortable with 0580?
faqs.answer: Because it is not an extension of 0580, it is the start of a different course. Calculus arrives properly: differentiation, stationary points and integration as area. Trigonometric identities have to be manipulated rather than recognised. The questions run longer and give fewer scaffolding steps, so a student used to being led through a 0580 Paper 4 question finds nothing to hold on to. A comfortable 0580 grade predicts very little here, which is why families discover the gap a term in.

faqs.question: Where do marks go missing in the IGCSE Chemistry 0620 written papers?
faqs.answer: Definitions first. They are examined close to word for word and a near-miss earns nothing, so isotopes, oxidation and the difference between a mixture and a compound cost marks every series. Then the mole calculations, where students lose method marks by not showing the steps. Then organic chemistry, learnt as a list of names rather than as reaction types, so an unfamiliar molecule stops everything. Finally the command terms: describe, explain and suggest want different answers.

faqs.question: What does IGCSE English First Language 0500 Paper 2 reward that a school essay does not?
faqs.answer: Evidence, quoted and then explained. A school essay often rewards a confident opinion; this paper rewards a short quotation followed by what the writer's word choice does to a reader. The directed-writing task also wants a register, whether a letter, a report or a speech, held consistently for the whole answer, and students lose marks drifting back into essay voice. Reading the criteria with somebody beats writing more practice pieces.

faqs.question: If my daughter's school covers Computer Science 0478 from the IT department, what is actually missing?
faqs.answer: Usually the examination conventions rather than the content. An IT teacher can explain how a loop works; Paper 2 asks for pseudocode written the way the board writes it, trace tables filled in correctly, and an algorithm designed to a specification under time pressure. Paper 1 theory is learnable from the textbook. The algorithms paper is where the mark loss sits, and it is the most common reason a family in Riyadh or Dhahran looks outside the school.

faqs.question: Can a school in the Kingdom tell us who will teach a subject before we commit to the option block?
faqs.answer: It can tell you what ran previously and who taught it, and that is the question worth asking. Ask which subjects on the option list actually ran, who taught each one, what tier the cohort was entered for, and how many students took it. A subject that ran with six students and a non-specialist will probably do the same again. Schools answer this honestly when asked directly; a prospectus lists what is possible rather than what is staffed.

faqs.question: What does ETEC do, and what does it not tell us about a subject teacher?
faqs.answer: The Education and Training Evaluation Commission handles school evaluation and accreditation in the Kingdom, including e-services for national school accreditation and for approving international accreditation bodies. The Ministry of Education licenses private and international schools. Both work at the level of the institution. Neither publishes who stands in front of a particular Year 10 class, what tier that class was entered for, or whether the teacher has taught the syllabus before. Those are questions for the school.

faqs.question: Why is a female IGCSE specialist harder to find in Jubail or Yanbu than in Riyadh?
faqs.answer: Because the whole cohort is smaller. An industrial city has a handful of international classes per year group, so the number of local teachers who have taught Extended-tier sciences recently is in single figures before any other preference is applied. Riyadh has the deepest pool in the Kingdom and is still an hour across in traffic. Online matching ignores both facts: a family in Yanbu gets the same list as a family in Al Olaya.

faqs.question: If we move from Jeddah to Al Khobar mid-course, does my daughter keep the same tutor?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that is one of the practical arguments for teaching this way. The lesson is a video call pinned to Arabia Standard Time, so a move inside the Kingdom changes nothing except possibly the school run and therefore the start time. What does change is the school: a new scheme of work, maybe a different board, sometimes a different tier. Send the new component list over and the plan is rebuilt around it.

female-igcse-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the trial lesson, not the search
female-igcse-tutor.closingBody: The useful next step is a free trial lesson on the subject that is actually costing marks, with the tutor you asked for. Send the board, the syllabus codes, the tier the school has entered her for, and the evenings that work in Arabia Standard Time. You will get a diagnostic session, a written note of where the marks went, and a fee for that subject and level before anything is booked. If the match is not right, say so after two lessons. Lessons run online, one-to-one, over live video, anywhere in the Kingdom.

hail.heroEyebrow: ONLINE IB AND IGCSE TEACHING FOR HA'IL
hail.heroSubtitle: IB and IGCSE tutors in Ha'il are not usually hired because a student cannot understand the subject. They are hired because marks are leaking somewhere specific — a command term read loosely, a graph drawn without units, an investigation that answers a question nobody asked. Ha'il has a university and a growing private-school sector, but Diploma-level international provision sits in Riyadh, Jeddah and the Eastern Province. Lessons here run one-to-one over live video, on Arabia Standard Time, in the hours the school run and the evening actually leave free.
