sections.heading: Why a group hour and a one-to-one hour are not interchangeable
paragraphs: The per-head arithmetic makes a group look obviously better and the comparison is unsound, because the two formats deliver different quantities of the thing that actually moves marks. In an individual session the teaching is addressed to one diagnosis and the marking covers one student's work. In a group of five the exposition is shared, which is efficient, but the marking either does not happen or happens at a fifth of the depth. The hour costs less and produces less evidence, and evidence is what the money is for.

The condition under which a group genuinely wins is narrow and worth stating precisely: the gap has to be identical across the students. That happens, particularly where a whole teaching set was taught a topic badly or where nobody has been shown how a command term works. It happens far less often than families assume. Three students failing the same paper usually fail it in three different ways: one has not covered two topics, one cannot pace a paper, one writes answers that never address the verb. One lesson cannot fix three problems.

There is a second-order effect in a group that families underestimate. The weakest student in a group sets the pace the teacher must respect, and the strongest sets the pace the group perceives. In a set of five with mixed gaps, the student who most needs individual attention is the one least likely to ask for it, and a Diploma candidate eight weeks from the May session cannot afford to be the quiet one. Group formats work best where the students are genuinely matched, which requires diagnosis before the group is formed.

In the Kingdom there is also a hard logistical limit. A group needs one hour that survives several different school runs, and in Riyadh the city is roughly an hour across in traffic, while in the Eastern Province families live in one of three cities and attend school in another. In Jubail a parent's rotation roster moves a session for everybody rather than for one household. Groups form most easily on a compound, where the cohort is dense and the commute is short, and least easily everywhere else.

sections.heading: Class size in a school, and the gap an individual hour fills
paragraphs: The reason outside classes exist at all is arithmetic inside the school. A subject teacher with a set of twenty-two Diploma candidates and a scheme of work to deliver cannot mark every student's every answer to a question-type breakdown, and would not be expected to. They mark to keep the set moving, they report at the school's reporting intervals, and they teach the median of the room. That is the job, and it is done well in a great many schools in the Kingdom.

What it cannot produce is the granular individual evidence described at the top of this page. A student who loses marks on extended responses in a way specific to how they personally write will not be identified by set-level marking, because the loss looks like an average performance. The school sees a mid-band student. An individual diagnosis sees a student who knows the content and has one trainable habit costing them several marks a paper. Those are the same child and different problems.

This is also why the useful conversation with a school is narrow rather than evaluative. Do not ask whether a student is doing well; the answer will be a band. Ask what the marked breakdown by question type shows, whether the Higher Level extension topics have been covered yet, and which of the internally assessed components have been drafted. Schools answer specific questions specifically, and those three answers tell a family whether they need coverage teaching, technique teaching or nothing at all.

The honest corollary is that outside classes should be narrower than most families buy. If the school is delivering content competently and the loss is in technique on two question types, the purchase is a short block of marked technique work, not a year of parallel teaching. Parallel teaching also carries a risk: a second method introduced alongside the school's leaves a student arbitrating between two adults, and that costs marks in exactly the paper the family was trying to protect.

sections.heading: The plateau, and what the evidence says to do about it
paragraphs: Most arrangements that fail do not fail dramatically. They plateau: the first few weeks produce visible movement, then the number stops going up, and because everybody is working hard the arrangement continues for another two months on momentum. Recognising a plateau quickly is the single most valuable use of a measurement system, and it is the reason the question-type score matters more than an overall mark.

There are four common causes and they need different responses. The first is that the easy technique gains have been taken and what remains is content, which is slower; the response is a coverage checklist and a longer horizon rather than a change of tutor. The second is that the work set between sessions has stopped being done, which turns every session into a diagnosis of the same gap; the response is a smaller quantity of work that actually gets completed.

The third cause is a mismatch between what is being taught and where the marks are. This shows up as a rising score on the thing being drilled and a flat overall mark, which is a genuinely useful signal: the drilling worked and the wrong thing was drilled. The response is to re-score a recent timed paper and reallocate. The fourth is a mismatch between tutor and student, which is usually visible by the second or third session rather than at the plateau, and the response is to re-match early rather than to work harder at a pairing that is not landing.

What should not happen is the response this market defaults to, which is more hours. Adding a second weekly session to a plateau usually doubles the cost and reproduces the plateau, because the limiting factor was never contact time. The review at the end of a block exists to force this decision, and it has to be able to produce 'change the plan' or 'stop' as outcomes. A family who cannot imagine the review concluding 'stop' is not running a review.

sections.heading: The last eight weeks before the May session, measured
paragraphs: The run-in to the May session is where measurement earns its keep, because the available decisions get narrower every week and the cost of guessing rises. By eight weeks out the syllabus is either covered or it is not, and the honest first act is a full paper under timed conditions in each subject that matters. That score, broken down by question type, is what the plan should be written from. Writing it from the term's notes instead is the most common mistake in this period.

The middle of the run-in is about restraint. Two question types, drilled properly, will move a grade more reliably than broad revision across a syllabus, and the evidence has already named which two. Leaving the rest alone feels wrong to students and parents alike, and it is correct: a candidate who tries to revise everything in six weeks revises nothing to the depth that changes a mark. A second timed paper at around four weeks out tests whether the drilling transferred.

The final fortnight has one rule, and it is the hardest to keep. Nothing new is introduced. New content at this point displaces the paper practice that actually moves marks and reliably raises anxiety at the moment it matters most. Sessions become short, mixed question sets marked in the same session, on question types the student can already do, plus whatever the formula or data booklet requires. The last week is retrieval, sleep and no testing that could leave a candidate rattled.

The table below sets the cadence out as a shape rather than a calendar, which is deliberate: entry deadlines, mock dates and the series itself are administered by the school and the board and they move. Your school's Diploma Programme coordinator holds the dates that apply to your child. What does not change from one year to the next is the order of operations, and the order is what families get wrong.

sections.heading: Cost against evidence: what each riyal is actually buying
paragraphs: A family deciding between formats is really deciding how much evidence they need, and that is a cheaper question to answer than it looks. Where the problem is a topic nobody taught properly, exposition is what is needed and exposition is divisible: a cohort class or a recorded course delivers it at a fraction of the individual rate, and the school's own revision club may deliver it free. Paying an individual rate for exposition is the most common overspend in this market.

Where the problem is specific to how one student writes answers, evidence is indivisible and so is the cost. Nobody can mark one student's extended responses at a fifth of the depth and produce a fifth of the insight; it produces none. This is the purchase that justifies the upper end of the advertised range, and it is also the purchase that should be narrow. A short block of marked technique work on two question types is a defined piece of work with a measurable output, not a standing arrangement.

The figures worth holding in mind are published rather than ours. IB subject tuition is advertised from about SAR 180 an hour on tutoring-company listings, Higher Level and Advanced Placement routes at roughly SAR 200 to 220, general non-specialist online tutoring from about SAR 55, and budget platform IGCSE support from as little as SAR 35 per head. Those are provider-published advertised rates, not a market average and not a price list of ours, and they are useful only as a reference range against which to read a quote.

The discipline that keeps spending honest is the review. Agree the block, agree what will be measured, agree the date it gets looked at, and agree that 'stop' is one of the available answers. A family doing that will sometimes spend more in a term than one buying the cheapest per-head option, and will know what it bought. No fee guarantees a grade, boundaries are set after papers are marked, and the only thing a family can genuinely purchase is better-informed work.

sections.heading: Starting: baseline, plan, review, and the honest version of 'it is not working'
paragraphs: The first useful message is specific: subject, level, year group, and what the most recent marked work actually shows. If you do not know what it shows, that is the first thing to establish and it takes one session rather than a term. Include two or three windows that genuinely work after your city's school run, because a slot set optimistically gets rescheduled twice and then abandoned, and an abandoned slot produces no evidence at all.

Then a free trial lesson with the tutor who would actually teach, working on a recent piece of marked schoolwork rather than a prepared showcase. The useful question to ask inside the hour is where candidates lose marks in the paper your child is weakest at. An answer naming question types and command terms means this person has taught the course; an answer about confidence and foundations means they have not, however pleasantly it is delivered.

After that, a written baseline from marked questions, a plan with the measurement cadence in it, a fixed slot in Arabia Standard Time, and a review date. Two subjects go on separate evenings rather than back to back after a Sunday-to-Thursday school day, because the second hour produces attendance rather than work. All of it is agreed before a block starts, which is what makes the review meaningful instead of ceremonial.

And the honest version of the awkward part. Sometimes the evidence says the arrangement should stop, and we will say so rather than sell another block: the gains have been taken, the remaining gap is the school's to close, or the student does not want this and is attending for a parent's benefit. Sometimes no specialist is free in the subject and window you need, particularly for scarce Higher Level sciences near a series, and we will tell you that instead of putting a generalist in front of a Higher Level candidate. And on assessed work the line does not move: a tutor teaches the criteria and gives feedback on the student's own drafts, and never writes, redrafts or supplies text for an Internal Assessment, an Extended Essay, a Theory of Knowledge essay or a Personal Project.

process.title: Say what the marked work shows
process.description: Subject, level, year group, and what the most recent marked work actually says: missing topics, lost technique, or a core deadline. If nobody knows, that is one session to establish rather than a term to guess at. Online IB classes are matched from this, not from a subject name and a year group.

process.title: A free trial lesson on real work
process.description: An hour with the proposed tutor, working on a recent piece of marked schoolwork rather than a showcase exercise. Ask where candidates lose marks in the paper your child is weakest at. Question types and command terms in the answer mean the course has been taught; generalities mean it has not.

process.title: A written baseline and a measurement cadence
process.description: A baseline from marked questions, separating coverage from technique, plus the cadence: weekly question-type scores and a full timed paper every three to four weeks. The cadence is written down because it is the thing that silently disappears first when a term gets busy.

process.title: A fixed slot, and two subjects on separate evenings
process.description: The slot is written in Arabia Standard Time and held for the term, so a tutor abroad changing their clocks does not move it. Set it against your worst school-run week. Where two subjects need work they go on different days, never back to back after a Sunday-to-Thursday school day.

process.title: A review with three possible answers
process.description: At the end of each block, a review against the baseline using annotated work, with continue, change the plan and stop all genuinely on the table. A review that can only conclude 'continue' is a renewal notice. If a match is wrong we re-match early rather than extend it.

whyPoints.title: The evidence is named before the money
whyPoints.description: Marks by question type weekly, a timed paper every three to four weeks, criterion bands on the student's own drafts, and a coverage checklist. Those four, with what each cannot show written beside it. A family who agrees that list first can audit the spending afterwards, which is unusual in this market.

whyPoints.title: The format follows the diagnosis
whyPoints.description: A shared gap is a group job, exposition is divisible and often free at school, and a problem specific to one student's written answers needs individual marking. We will tell you when a cohort class or your school's own revision club is the better buy, because the alternative is selling you the wrong format.

whyPoints.title: Plateaus get named, not out-waited
whyPoints.description: Four causes, four different responses, and none of them is 'add another hour'. Adding contact time to a plateau usually doubles the cost and reproduces the plateau, because contact time was not the limiting factor. The review exists to force that decision while there is still a term to use.

whyPoints.title: Rates quoted with their sources
whyPoints.description: Advertised IB subject tuition from about SAR 180 an hour, Higher Level routes about SAR 200 to 220, general tutoring from about SAR 55, budget platforms from about SAR 35 per head. All provider-published figures, none a market average, and none presented as our own price.

whyPoints.title: Slots built for the Kingdom's week
whyPoints.description: Sunday to Thursday is the school week and Friday and Saturday are the weekend, which makes a Friday morning the easiest long block in the week to fill with a busy specialist. Everything is written in Arabia Standard Time, so a clock change abroad never moves a lesson here.

whyPoints.title: No outcome claims and no written coursework
whyPoints.description: No fee guarantees a grade, since boundaries are set after papers are marked. No percentages, ratings or headcounts we cannot evidence. A tutor teaches criteria and gives feedback on the student's own drafts, and never writes, redrafts or supplies text for assessed work.

faqs.question: How is an internally assessed component moderated, and can a class format help with it?
faqs.answer: The school marks the component against the published criteria and the board moderates a sample to check the school applied them as intended, which can move the whole cohort's marks up or down. That means two things for a family. A class cannot influence moderation, and anyone implying otherwise is misdescribing the process. What outside teaching can legitimately do is improve the work itself before submission, by teaching what each criterion strand asks for and giving feedback on the student's own drafts. That is individual work, so a group format is a poor fit for it.

faqs.question: What does an IB mark scheme reward that a well-written textbook answer does not?
faqs.answer: Specificity against the command term, and the particular links the scheme lists. A textbook answer explains a topic; a mark scheme pays for a defined number of points, each of which has to be recognisable. A candidate can write a fluent, accurate paragraph and score two of six marks because four of the listed points are absent. This is why marked practice beats reading: the student sees which of their sentences earned something and which earned nothing, and that distinction is almost impossible to infer from a textbook.

faqs.question: How many Diploma points come from the Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay matrix?
faqs.answer: The two core written components are graded separately and then combined through a published matrix that contributes points on top of the six subject grades, with the subject grades themselves carrying up to seven each. The exact matrix is published by the IB and your school's Diploma Programme coordinator holds the current version. The planning point is that the core is small enough to be neglected and large enough to decide an offer, and it is the part of the Diploma most often left until the deadline is close.

faqs.question: How is the Extended Essay graded, and does a group class ever suit it?
faqs.answer: Against published criteria covering the research question, the knowledge and understanding shown, the critical argument, the presentation and the student's own reflections. It is marked on how the essay works as a piece of research, not on how interesting the topic is, which is why a strong subject performer can score poorly. A group class suits the generic parts: what the criteria mean, how to frame a question, what a reflection is for. Everything after the first draft is individual, because the feedback has to be on this student's own argument.

faqs.question: What happens if a Diploma candidate misses a written paper?
faqs.answer: It is handled by the school with the board under their published arrangements, and the outcome depends on the reason, the evidence and how much of the subject's assessment is already complete. This is not something a family negotiates directly or a tutor can influence, so the first call is always to the school's Diploma Programme coordinator rather than anywhere else. What a family can control is the preparation around it: candidates sitting several papers in one period benefit from pacing and sleep planning far more than from extra content in those weeks.

faqs.question: How is a baseline measured in the first two weeks of classes?
faqs.answer: From marked questions rather than conversation. The student works through material chosen so the tutor can diagnose, and the output is a short written document with three parts: which topics are covered and secure, which are covered and shaky, and which lost marks are technique rather than content. Those are different problems with different timelines, and no amount of discussion separates them. The baseline is also the document every later review compares against, so it is worth reading properly rather than filing. It usually takes one session to produce.

faqs.question: What does progress look like week by week in a Higher Level science class?
faqs.answer: Two numbers moving at different speeds. The technique number, usually the score on extended-response and command-term handling, moves within three to five sessions because it is a habit. The content number moves across a term because topics have to be taught and then practised. A family watching only an overall mark sees a flat line for weeks and concludes nothing is happening, when the technique score has in fact doubled. Score the two separately from the start and the picture becomes legible, and the decision at the review becomes straightforward.

faqs.question: Who owns the study plan: the class, the school or the family?
faqs.answer: The school owns the course and its sequence, the tutor owns the intervention, and the family owns the decision about whether the intervention continues. Confusion here is expensive. A tutor who tries to own the course ends up teaching a parallel syllabus, which leaves the student arbitrating between two methods. A family who hands over the decision stops reviewing. Write down who is responsible for what at the start, including who contacts the school and how often, and most of the friction in the arrangement disappears before it appears.

faqs.question: What should a family do when a student plateaus halfway through a block of classes?
faqs.answer: Diagnose the plateau before changing anything, because there are four common causes with four different answers. The easy technique gains may simply be taken, leaving slower content work. The work set between sessions may have stopped being done. The drilling may be aimed at the wrong question types, which shows as a rising drilled score and a flat overall mark. Or the tutor and student may not be a fit. Adding a second weekly hour is the default response in this market and it usually doubles the cost while reproducing the plateau.

faqs.question: How do we decide whether to continue after one term of classes?
faqs.answer: By comparing the current evidence with the written baseline, not by asking whether the sessions have been good. Three questions settle it. Has the question-type score moved on the things that were drilled? Has the timed-paper score moved, which tells you whether the gains survive the clock? And is the remaining gap one that outside teaching can close, or is it the school's to close? If the answers are no, no and the school's, the honest conclusion is to stop, and a review that cannot reach that conclusion is not a review.

faqs.question: How is examination technique taught separately from content in a class?
faqs.answer: By scoring it separately and then teaching it directly from marked work. Technique teaching looks unlike content teaching: the student has a script in front of them, the tutor asks what the command term demanded, how many marks were available, how long the answer should have taken, and which sentence earned nothing. There is no new material in the session. Most students have never had this taught explicitly, which is why it produces faster movement than content work and why it is the right purchase close to a series.

faqs.question: What does a student entering the first Diploma year need from classes in the autumn term?
faqs.answer: Foundations and habits rather than content support, because the content has barely started. Algebraic fluency if a science or the analysis route in mathematics is coming. Command-term literacy, since the first assessments mark it and nobody teaches it. And an early, unhurried look at two or three possible Extended Essay areas so the research question is not invented under pressure later. Buying subject-content classes in the first weeks of the Diploma usually means paying to pre-teach material the school is about to deliver competently.

faqs.question: When is it worth moving a Higher Level subject down to Standard Level?
faqs.answer: When the evidence says the Higher Level marks are not reachable and the subject is not required at Higher Level for what the student intends to study. Both halves matter. A Higher Level course runs on roughly 240 recommended teaching hours against about 150 at Standard Level and carries components Standard Level does not sit, so the saving in effort is real. But where a university course requires a subject it usually requires it at Higher Level, so check the published prerequisites before the change rather than after, and make the decision with the school.

faqs.question: How much notice does a November-series resit candidate need before classes start?
faqs.answer: Less than a full-year candidate, and the work is sharper, because the diagnosis already exists in a marked script. The useful sequence is to get the script or the statement of results analysed by question type first, then decide what actually needs teaching, then book. The constraint is supply rather than time: tutors who know a specific paper fill their schedules in the weeks immediately after results, so the decision to resit is worth making as soon as results arrive rather than a term later.

faqs.question: Is it too late to join classes in the final term of the Diploma?
faqs.answer: No, but only one kind of work is worth buying. In the final term the syllabus is either covered or it is not, and the available marks sit in technique: command terms, time allocation against the mark tariff, deciding when to abandon a question, and writing the method line rather than the answer. A timed paper in the first session should set the whole plan. What has the worst return of anything available is new content in the last fortnight, which displaces paper practice and raises anxiety precisely when neither helps.

faqs.question: What should a family do if the student does not want to attend classes at all?
faqs.answer: Treat it as information rather than resistance, and find out which of three things it is. Some students object to the format, in which case a different cadence or a different tutor fixes it. Some object to being the problem in the household, which a diagnosis framed in marks rather than in character usually defuses. And some genuinely do not want the subject or the course, which is a conversation with the school and not something tutoring solves. Paying for attendance against a student's will reliably produces attendance and no measurable movement.

ib-classes.closingHeading: Agree the measurement before the hours
ib-classes.closingBody: Send the subject, the level, the year group and what the most recent marked work shows. We will propose a named tutor who has taught that course, arrange a free trial lesson with that person on real work, and produce a written baseline from marked questions before any block is agreed. The cadence gets written down with it: weekly question-type scores, a full paper under timed conditions every three to four weeks, and a review date where continue, change and stop are all available answers. Teaching runs one-to-one over live video on Arabia Standard Time, Sunday to Thursday, with Friday or Saturday paper clinics where a timed paper needs two uninterrupted hours.

ib-coaching.tutorsIntro: Each coach below holds one subject at one level and a working week that can carry a Saudi evening for two years. Both halves matter: a Chemistry HL specialist who is only free at midnight Arabia Standard Time is not a match, however good their subject background looks on paper.

intro.heading: Start with the points arithmetic, then look at the calendar
paragraphs: The Diploma is a two-year machine with a published specification, and almost every decision a family makes about support becomes obvious once the arithmetic is on the table. Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, each graded one to seven, giving a maximum of 42. The core adds up to three more points from the Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay matrix, for 45 in total. Inside each subject, internally assessed work typically carries around a fifth of the grade and the written papers carry the rest. Higher Level mathematics adds a third paper worth a fifth on its own.

Read that again and notice what it implies. A fifth of every subject grade is decided by work produced over months under supervision, not in an examination hall. Three points — the difference between a conditional offer met and missed — come from two pieces of writing that no subject teacher owns. And in several subjects the Higher Level component that most often drags a grade is the one testing unfamiliar extended problems, which routine homework does not touch. Support aimed at the papers alone leaves most of the available movement on the floor.

That is what IB coaching should mean in practice, and the word is worth defining because this market uses it loosely. Subject teaching closes content gaps. Coaching works on everything that converts what a student knows into marks the scheme can pay for: command-term discipline, paper structure, timing, criterion literacy on internally assessed work, and the management of a two-year workload that nobody in the house has seen before. Most families need both, in a proportion that changes between the first Diploma year and the second.

Which brings in the second organising fact, and the reason this page is built the way it is. None of that happens without a slot that survives two years. The school week in the Kingdom runs Sunday to Thursday. Arabia Standard Time is UTC+3 and the clocks here never change. A coach's own working week — their school day, their time zone, their weekend — decides whether a stable weekly hour exists at all, and a mismatch there ends an arrangement faster than any disagreement about teaching. We check it before we offer a match, and we write the slot down in Saudi local time so the drift lands on the coach rather than on your evening.

Everything we arrange is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not send coaches to homes anywhere in the Kingdom; in-home visits are a service we run only in India. IB Gram holds no accreditation from the IB and claims none — we are an independent matching platform, and a page that implied otherwise would be lying about something a parent can check. What we do claim is specific: a specialist in your child's subject and level, on a slot that holds, with a written note after every session.

ib-coaching.programmesIntro: Four things a Saudi family deals with under the IB label, listed in the order they consume a week. The Diploma and its core together are a larger time commitment than most families budget for, which is the practical reason a weekly rhythm has to be designed rather than improvised.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across the subject groups, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, with externally examined papers sat in the May session by schools on a northern-hemisphere year. Each subject carries internally assessed work the school marks and the IB moderates. Higher Level is not Standard Level with extra chapters: in several subjects it changes how shared content is examined, and in mathematics it adds a whole paper. Grades run one to seven per subject, for a maximum of 42 before the core is counted.
programmes.countryNote: In the Kingdom the Diploma is sat by a spread of international schools across Riyadh, Jeddah, the Eastern Province and a handful of smaller centres, each on its own calendar. Two consequences follow for coaching: the term structure a family is working to differs from their neighbour's, and the subject a school cannot staff with a specialist in a given cohort differs city by city. Both are reasons to plan from your own school's published calendar and subject list.

programmes.name: The Diploma core
programmes.description: Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. The first two together contribute up to three points through a published matrix, and a failing condition in the core can prevent the award of the Diploma regardless of subject grades. The Extended Essay is an independent piece of around four thousand words with a supervisor and a required reflection process. Theory of Knowledge is assessed through an essay on a prescribed title and an exhibition of objects.
programmes.countryNote: The core is where Saudi families most often lose points they could have had, because no subject teacher owns it and it has no weekly homework to anchor it. It is also where coaching is most clearly distinct from subject teaching: a coach can teach the Theory of Knowledge essay's argumentative form and test whether an Extended Essay research question is answerable, without touching a word of the student's own writing.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four published criteria per subject, each marked out of eight, with descriptors a parent can read directly. The Personal Project in the final year is assessed on its process journal as much as its product. Mathematics splits into standard and extended routes, and the extended route is what makes Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level realistic later. Nothing here appears on an external certificate, which is exactly why it is the cheapest place to fix habits.
programmes.countryNote: For families in the Kingdom the useful MYP question is not whether a child is doing well but whether they are building the two things the Diploma will demand: criterion literacy and the ability to carry a long task without being chased. A term of work in the final MYP years costs less and achieves more than the same term bought in the second Diploma year, and almost nobody buys it then.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary units of inquiry with no external examinations and reporting against conceptual understanding and the learner profile. What is worth tracking at this stage is narrow: reading fluency, written structure, number sense and whether a child can explain a method aloud. The exhibition in the final year is a first long independent task and a useful early read on how a child handles one.
programmes.countryNote: Primary cohorts in the Kingdom's international schools are mobile, with children arriving from several systems at once, so the commonest issue is a method taught twice in two different ways rather than a gap. That is a short piece of work — usually a term — and it is best done before the Middle Years Programme starts layering criteria on top of shaky arithmetic.

ib-coaching.subjectsIntro: The Diploma subjects Saudi families most often ask us to coach, described by what they demand of a week and where their marks are decided. Weekly time is the scarce resource in a Sunday-to-Thursday school week, so it is worth knowing which subjects eat it.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The heaviest weekly load in the Diploma at Higher Level, because Paper 3 rewards extended unfamiliar problems that cannot be prepared by repetition. Two long papers, Paper 3 at a fifth of the grade, and the exploration. Proof, series and calculus technique take the autumn; Paper 3 argument-building takes the spring. A student who can only do questions that resemble the ones they have seen is the standard failure case here.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Lighter week by week than Analysis and Approaches but unforgiving on interpretation: a technically correct model with no sentence explaining what it means scores poorly. The graphic display calculator is assumed as a reasoning tool. Many engineering courses expect Analysis and Approaches instead, so the route choice belongs in the Middle Years Programme, not in the first Diploma year.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Two written papers plus a scientific investigation carrying around a fifth of the grade. Uncertainty treatment is examined more tightly than students expect, and extended-response marks go to answers that follow the scheme's structure rather than to the most insightful explanation. Higher Level depth changes how shared topics are questioned, which is why a Standard Level coach cannot simply go slower.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The data booklet is permitted and chronically underused. Calculations are marked for method as much as for answer, and organic mechanisms respond to drilled practice rather than to re-reading. The investigation is where most of the recoverable grade sits, and it is lost at the research-question stage far more often than in the write-up.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content-heavy with a vocabulary that is marked strictly: a nearly-right term earns nothing and 'explain' answered as a description loses the mechanism marks. Weekly time goes on precise definitions and process sequencing. The investigation needs a variable the student can genuinely control, which is a feasibility question best settled a term before data collection.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Studies, evaluation and research methods, with an internally assessed experimental replication. Students arrive able to recall studies and unable to evaluate them, which is where the grade is decided. Higher Level extensions demand a sharper grasp of methodology, and the replication fails on design rather than on writing.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: A pre-released case study for the examined paper plus an internally assessed research project on a real organisation. Tools applied generically score badly; tools applied to the evidence in front of the student score well. The research project's access to real data is the practical constraint, and it has to be solved early rather than assumed.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Source work, essays and a historical investigation the student designs. Paper 1's source questions are a technique rather than a knowledge test, and students who treat them as comprehension forfeit the provenance and cross-referencing marks. Essay practice is the single highest-yield weekly habit in this subject and the one most often skipped.

subjects.name: Language B: French, Spanish and others
subjects.description: Reading, writing to a specified text type, listening, and an individual oral built on course themes. Text-type convention is the recoverable loss: a blog, a formal letter and a report are marked on features that can be learned in a couple of sessions. Weekly contact matters more here than in any other group, because a fortnight's gap is visibly audible in the oral.

subjects.name: Visual Arts
subjects.description: A comparative study, a process portfolio and an exhibition, all internally produced and externally assessed. Almost the entire grade is coursework, which makes it the subject where a two-year rhythm matters most and where a student who works in bursts suffers. Coaching here is about documentation discipline and curatorial reasoning, never about making the work.

ib-coaching.regionsTitle: The Kingdom's cities, seen through the evening they leave for a lesson
ib-coaching.regionsIntro: Where a family lives changes the hour a weekly session can actually start, which is the thing that decides whether a two-year arrangement survives. These are the markets we coach into, read through the school run rather than through the map.

regions.name: Riyadh
regions.note: Roughly an hour across in traffic, so two families at the same school can have school runs ninety minutes apart. Al Olaya and Al Malqa yield different workable start times, and the practical ceiling is two weekday evenings rather than four for anyone crossing the city twice a day.

regions.name: Jeddah
regions.note: A long coastal spine from the historic centre north to Obhur. Families at the northern end absorb a substantial daily run, which pushes the realistic start past 6.30pm and makes a stacked double evening more attractive than spreading sessions across the week.

regions.name: Dhahran, Al Khobar and Dammam
regions.note: A single school and labour market where families live in one city and school in another, often with a compound gate and a company bus in the chain. Session times here are unusually stable once set, because the commute itself is predictable in a way Riyadh's is not.

regions.name: Jubail
regions.note: Industrial shift patterns rather than distance are the scheduling constraint. Where a parent works a rotating roster, the sensible design is a slot that does not depend on their presence plus a written note after each session, agreed at the outset instead of discovered later.

regions.name: Al Ahsa
regions.note: About an hour and a half inland from the Eastern Province cluster, so families schooling children in Khobar or Dhahran lose the early evening to the road. A later start and a longer single session usually beats two short ones here.

regions.name: Makkah and Madinah
regions.note: Both run calendars that bend around Hajj and Umrah seasons, when regional travel slows and school rhythms shift. A fixed online slot is easier to protect through those weeks than anything requiring a journey, and families plan the pause in advance rather than week by week.

regions.name: Abha and Khamis Mushait
regions.note: Twenty-five kilometres apart at altitude in 'Asir, sharing a catchment and a thin local specialist pool. Evening slots are straightforward; it is the supply of a Higher Level specialist that is the binding constraint, which is precisely what a video slot solves.

regions.name: Tabuk, AlUla and NEOM
regions.note: The north-west, with the newest international provision in the Kingdom and small resident cohorts. Families here often coach one or two Higher Level subjects their school cannot staff, which makes the weekly commitment narrow and the matching requirement precise.

regions.name: Thuwal and the Red Sea coast
regions.note: Campus and company towns north of Jeddah where the school is minutes away, which produces the widest evening window in the Kingdom. A 4.30pm start is genuinely available here and is worth using, because an earlier session leaves the rest of the evening intact.

schoolClusters.note: The widest set of IB World Schools in the Kingdom, running the Primary Years, Middle Years and Diploma Programmes in various combinations, each on a calendar it publishes itself. Because term dates and mock-examination weeks differ between schools in the same city, a coaching plan built on a city-wide assumption will be wrong for most families. Students we support attend schools of this kind; no relationship with any of them is implied.

schoolClusters.city: The Eastern Province and the Gulf coast
schoolClusters.note: The International Schools Group operates several campuses across the conurbation, and the Diploma runs at some of them rather than all. British and Cambridge curricula are also long established here, so a family moving between campuses can change board and programme without changing city. Check which programme a campus actually offers in the year of entry rather than in general.

schoolClusters.city: Jeddah, Thuwal and the Red Sea coast
schoolClusters.note: A mixed market where some schools run the Diploma, some Cambridge courses and several both, stretched along the coast from the historic centre north past Obhur to the campus communities beyond. Term structures vary from the Ministry of Education school year and from each other, which matters when planning the eight weeks before a series.

ib-coaching.schoolDisclaimer: Schools are named as ecosystem context for families arranging IB support in the Kingdom. No affiliation, endorsement or relationship with any named school or group is implied.
ib-coaching.modesIntro: Four weekly patterns, described by what each does to an evening rather than by what it costs. Pick on the shape of your week first; the subject matching is easier to solve than the calendar is.

modes.title: One fixed hour, same evening, two years
modes.description: The pattern that produces the most durable movement in the Diploma, because it allows a two-year arc: foundations and command terms in the first year, internally assessed work in the middle, paper technique at the end. It needs a coach whose own working week can carry the same hour for two years, which is a harder matching problem than subject expertise and the one families underestimate.

Sunday to Wednesday evenings are the most stable; Thursday is the weekend here

modes.title: A stacked double evening
modes.description: Two subjects back to back on one evening with a break between, rather than two separate nights. In Riyadh or northern Jeddah, where a school run can consume ninety minutes, buying one evening instead of two is often the difference between a plan that holds and one that collapses in week five. It suits students for whom starting is harder than continuing.
bullets: Two different specialists, not one coach stretching across two subjects

modes.title: A weekend morning with a coach in the Americas
modes.description: Friday and Saturday are the weekend in the Kingdom, and a Friday morning here is a weekday evening or an early start for a coach in Europe or the Americas. That opens a pool of specialists who cannot touch a Saudi school night at all. For a scarce Higher Level subject it is frequently the only route to a genuine specialist, and it costs a weekend morning rather than an evening.

Keeps all five school evenings clear for school work

modes.title: A study-leave intensive
modes.description: During study leave the school day disappears and mornings become available, which changes what is possible: full papers under timed conditions in the morning, marked and taught from in the afternoon. This is the only point in the year when a compressed block makes sense, and it is useless for a student who is behind on content rather than on technique.
bullets: Morning sessions while the student is fresh, not after a school day

sections.heading: What a Diploma grade is actually built from
paragraphs: Coaching decisions get easier once the specification is on the table. Each of the six subjects produces a grade from one to seven, giving 42 points. Up to three further points come from the Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay matrix, which combines the grades awarded for those two pieces, for a maximum of 45. Inside a subject, internally assessed work carries around a fifth of the grade in most cases, marked by the school against published criteria and moderated by the IB. The written papers carry the rest, split between a shorter paper rewarding precision and recall and a longer one rewarding structured explanation.

Two structural facts follow, and they govern where coaching time should go. The first is that a fifth of every subject grade is produced over months rather than in an examination hall, under conditions a family can influence: a feasible research question, an early start, criterion literacy, honest feedback on a draft the student wrote. The second is that the three core points are decided by two pieces of writing no subject teacher owns, which is why they are the most commonly conceded points in the whole Diploma.

The third fact is specific to Higher Level. In mathematics, Paper 3 is a fifth of the grade on its own and tests extended problems in unfamiliar contexts. In the sciences, the Higher Level content changes how shared topics are examined rather than simply adding more of them. A coach who treats Higher Level as Standard Level at a slower pace will produce a student who is comfortable with the familiar and lost on the paper that decides the grade.

The table sets out the arithmetic. It is worth reading with your child's six subjects in mind, because it usually reveals that the cheapest available points are not in the subject the family is worried about.

sections.heading: Coaching or tutoring: what the word means here, and what we actually do
paragraphs: Families use the two words interchangeably and providers encourage it, but the distinction is useful and it changes what you should buy. Subject teaching closes content gaps: the student does not know oxidation states, or cannot differentiate implicitly, or has never understood the second-order effects in a demand diagram. That is a teaching job with a measurable endpoint, and it is usually the right purchase in the first Diploma year.

Coaching is everything that converts knowledge into marks. Command-term discipline, so an 'evaluate' question gets a judgement and a 'describe' question does not get an argument. Paper structure and timing, so the last two questions are not sacrificed. Criterion literacy, so a student reads the descriptors for their own internally assessed work before writing rather than after being marked. And workload management across two years, which no fourteen-year-old arrives equipped for and which the Diploma punishes harder than any single subject does.

Most students need a blend, and the blend shifts. The first Diploma year is usually two-thirds teaching and a third coaching: build the foundations, establish command terms, choose and narrow the internally assessed questions. The second year inverts: content is largely delivered, and the available movement is in technique, timing, coursework quality and the core. A provider who sells the same hour in both years is not reading the course.

What we will not do, in either mode, is produce assessed work. A coach teaches content, explains criteria and their mark allocations, tests whether a research question is answerable, asks the questions a supervisor or examiner will ask, and names where a paragraph fails to evidence its claim. A coach never writes, drafts, rewrites or completes any part of an Internal Assessment, an Extended Essay, a Theory of Knowledge essay or a Personal Project, and never supplies text to be pasted in. Several providers in this market blur that line, and a parent is entitled to ask the question in one sentence: will anything you produce end up in my child's document?
bullets: Teaching closes content gaps; coaching converts knowledge into marks the scheme pays for
Roughly two-thirds teaching in the first Diploma year, inverting in the second

sections.heading: The Sunday-to-Thursday week is the organising fact, not a footnote
paragraphs: The school week in the Kingdom runs Sunday to Thursday. Friday and Saturday are the weekend. Almost every piece of tutoring copy a Saudi parent reads was written for a Monday-to-Friday audience and quietly assumes that Sunday is a rest day, which is why so many proposed timetables feel subtly wrong. Sunday evening here is the equivalent of a Monday night: the week's work is starting and a student has least slack. Thursday evening is the equivalent of a Friday: nothing set then gets done.

That has concrete consequences for how a week is designed. The most reliable weekday slots sit Sunday to Wednesday, with Sunday best used for the subject that needs the week's momentum and Wednesday best for the subject with a Thursday deadline. Thursday evening sessions look fine on paper and are the first to be cancelled. Friday and Saturday open up coaches in time zones that cannot touch a school night, which is a genuine advantage and not a consolation prize.

The second consequence concerns how many evenings a family can actually spend. In Riyadh, where the city is an hour across in traffic, two weekday evenings is a realistic ceiling for most families and four is a fantasy that collapses by week five. In a campus or compound town where the school is minutes away, three or four are genuinely available. Designing for the ceiling rather than the ambition is the single biggest predictor of whether an arrangement survives to the second Diploma year.

The third is Ramadan, which moves roughly eleven days earlier each year against the Gregorian calendar and therefore drifts across the academic year rather than sitting in one place. School days shorten and study moves later into the evening. Most families keep their sessions and shift them later, sometimes shortening ninety minutes to sixty; some pause for the month. Either works. Deciding in advance works; cancelling week by week loses the slot.

sections.heading: Arabia Standard Time, and why a coach's own working week decides this
paragraphs: Arabia Standard Time is UTC+3 and the Kingdom does not observe daylight saving, so the clocks here never move. Most of the countries our coaches live in do move theirs. An unpinned slot therefore drifts by an hour twice a year, and families discover it when a coach appears an hour early in the autumn and an hour late in the spring. The fix is trivial and most providers skip it: write the slot down in Saudi local time, and let the coach's own clock absorb the change.

The deeper point is that a time zone is only half the problem. What decides whether a slot holds for two years is the coach's own working week: when their school day ends, which days are their weekend, and whether they are marking their own classes' work on the evening you need them. A classroom teacher in Europe finishing at 4pm their time is comfortable in your early evening and awkward in your late one. A coach in India at UTC+5:30 can take almost any Saudi evening, which is why that pool is the largest. A coach in East Asia is asleep. A coach in North America is at breakfast, which is useless on a school night here and excellent on a Friday morning.

There is also a weekend mismatch worth naming. A coach in a Monday-to-Friday country has their weekend on Saturday and Sunday. Your school week starts on Sunday. That means your most valuable weekday slot sits inside their weekend, and a coach who agrees to it in September may resent it by February. We ask the question directly before offering a match, because an arrangement that depends on somebody's goodwill against their own weekend is not a two-year arrangement.

The table maps the pools we actually draw from. Read the last column, because it is the one that determines what slot you will really be offered rather than what the time difference suggests is possible.

sections.heading: The core: Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay, and the three points nobody plans for
paragraphs: The core is where Saudi families most reliably lose points they could have had. Three points sit in the Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay matrix — enough to turn a 34 into a 37 and a missed conditional offer into a met one — and they are attached to two pieces of work with no weekly homework, no obvious owner and no immediate consequence for neglect. Students who are conscientious in six subjects routinely treat both as administration until the term they are due.

Theory of Knowledge is assessed through an essay on a prescribed title and an exhibition of objects, and its difficulty is formal rather than intellectual. Students have opinions; the assessment wants a structured argument about how knowledge is produced in specified areas, with counter-argument handled rather than mentioned. That form is teachable in a handful of sessions and is almost never taught explicitly, because the subject sits outside the subject-teaching structure of a school.

The Extended Essay is about four thousand words of independent research with a school supervisor and a required reflection process that is itself assessed. It fails at the research-question stage: a question too broad to answer in the word count, or one with no accessible sources or data, cannot be rescued by good writing in the final month. A coach reading a proposed question in the first weeks and saying plainly that it cannot be answered has done more for the grade than one polishing a doomed draft later.

Creativity, Activity, Service carries no points and can still cost the Diploma, because it is a completion requirement with documentation and reflection attached. The pattern we see is a student who has genuinely done the activities and has not written them up. That is a workload-management problem, which is exactly what coaching is for, and it is the cheapest intervention in the entire Diploma.
bullets: Three matrix points are the most commonly conceded points in the Diploma
The Theory of Knowledge essay's difficulty is formal — argument structure, not opinion
An Extended Essay is lost at the research question, not in the writing

sections.heading: Where Diploma marks are lost, component by component
paragraphs: The losses in the Diploma are different from the losses at IGCSE, because the Diploma asks for extended reasoning and sustained independent work rather than short dense answers. Five patterns account for most of what we see across Saudi schools, and each has a different fix and a different cost in weeks.

First, command terms in extended response. A student writes what is true instead of what the term requires, and an examiner cannot award marks for insight that does not meet the instruction. Second, Paper 3 and the Higher Level extension components, where routine practice produces a student who is fluent on familiar question shapes and stranded on unfamiliar ones. Third, internally assessed work that was lost at the question stage: too broad, no controllable variable, no accessible data. Fourth, the core, left until the term it is due. Fifth, timing — the last two questions of a long paper surrendered because the earlier ones were over-answered.

Notice that only the second of those five is really about subject knowledge. The rest are technique, planning and workload, which is both encouraging and uncomfortable: encouraging because they move faster than content gaps, uncomfortable because they require a student to change how they work rather than to learn more. That is the actual work of coaching, and it is why a first session should end with a named list rather than a general impression.

One honest limit. We do not promise a grade, a point total or an improvement, and no coach can. What a well-matched specialist changes is the proportion of what a student already knows that the mark scheme is able to pay for. In our experience that proportion is larger than families expect, and it is still not a certainty. Any provider converting it into a guaranteed number is selling something they cannot deliver.
bullets: Four of the five commonest Diploma losses are technique, planning or workload
Paper 3 and Higher Level extensions need unfamiliar problems, not more revision
Internally assessed work fails at the question stage more than in the write-up
No coach can promise a grade; what moves is how much of what is known gets paid for

sections.heading: What IB coaching costs in the Kingdom, and what moves the number
paragraphs: Rates published in this market are advertised rates set by providers, not measured averages, and they should be read as the band a family will meet rather than as a benchmark. Tutoring companies advertising IB subject support in the Kingdom quote from roughly SAR 180 an hour, with Higher Level and premium tracks around SAR 200 to 220. Tutor marketplaces put general private tuition in senior-school examination subjects at SAR 200 and above, and general private tuition at primary level around SAR 50. Broader platforms advertise general online tutoring from around SAR 55 and budget IGCSE one-to-one from around SAR 35. International providers quoting in dollars sit near sixty dollars an hour.

We publish no price on this page because a single figure covering a Mathematics AA HL specialist with examining experience and a Standard Level language coach would be misleading for both. What is worth publishing is the order in which the drivers act, because it tells a parent whether a quote is reasonable. Scarcity of the specialism comes first and dominates everything else. Then examining or marking experience. Then level: Higher Level above Standard Level, Standard Level above the Middle Years Programme. Then whether travel is priced in, which is one reason a video slot usually compares well on a like-for-like basis. Then the length of the commitment.

The under-asked question is what the hour includes. Marking turnaround on written work, who supplies past papers and mark schemes, what note the parent receives, what happens to a cancelled session, and whether the coach has read the school's scheme of work. Those items, not the headline number, are the real difference between the bottom and the top of the advertised range, and they are worth agreeing in writing before the first paid session. Families who feel badly served by tutoring have almost always bought the hour and expected the attachments.

On the shape of a commitment: weekly support for one Higher Level subject across a full Diploma year is a real financial decision and deserves to be treated as one. Price it per term rather than per hour, compare it with what a study-leave intensive would cost, and ask what the money buys that free school subject clinics do not. Sometimes the honest answer is that the clinic covers it, and a coach worth paying will say so.

sections.heading: How an online session runs across two Diploma years
paragraphs: The mechanics are unremarkable and the pattern across two years is the part worth describing. A session runs in a browser-based video room with a shared whiteboard, so the coach writes and the student writes on the same page. Past papers and mark schemes are loaded as documents and annotated live, which means a student watches a question being unpacked in the order an examiner reads it rather than watching a finished solution appear. Written work is photographed or uploaded between sessions, marked against the published scheme and returned annotated.

In the first Diploma year the sessions look like teaching. Content is built in sequence, command terms are drilled, and towards the end of the year the internally assessed question in at least one subject is chosen and narrowed. In the middle of the course, sessions shift to coursework: a draft the student wrote, read against the criterion descriptors, with the questions a supervisor will ask. In the final year, sessions become timed papers marked to the real standard, then teaching from the errors, then repeating with a different paper.

Parents can sit in on any session, and most do for the first one and then stop, which is the right pattern: a teenager who is being watched performs rather than struggles, and struggling visibly is what the hour is for. What replaces it is a short written note after each session — the component worked on, what the student got wrong, what has been set — so nobody depends on a teenager's account of their own lesson. Across two years those notes become the honest record of whether the arrangement is working.

Equipment is simple and worth getting right once. A laptop beats a tablet for a ninety-minute mathematics or science session, mostly because a paper and a whiteboard have to be visible together. A stylus helps for diagrams; paper held to the camera is a perfectly legitimate way to show working. A headset matters more than bandwidth beyond a basic threshold, and a quiet room with a door matters more than any of it. Sessions can be recorded at the family's choice, and students use recordings to revisit a method rather than to re-watch a whole hour.
bullets: First year teaching, middle coursework, final year timed papers marked to the scheme
Parents sit in on the first session and then stop; the written note replaces it
Laptop over tablet for ninety minutes; paper to camera is fine for working
