faqs.question: What time does a Diploma online lesson usually start for a student in Riyadh?
faqs.answer: Between six and eight in the evening for most families, with the northern districts at the later end because the run home takes longer. Earlier than six is rarely realistic once school and travel are counted, and later than eight costs concentration on a school night. The start time matters because it filters tutor time zones: an eight o'clock Riyadh start is late evening in India and still mid-afternoon in the United Kingdom.

faqs.question: Our tutor is in a country that changes its clocks - how is a Saudi slot kept stable?
faqs.answer: By writing the slot down in Arabia Standard Time rather than in the tutor's local time. The Kingdom has no daylight saving, so the Saudi hour never moves; when the tutor's country shifts, their own local time for the session changes and yours does not. Agree this when the slot is set, and confirm it in writing before their change. Families who define the slot in the tutor's time end up renegotiating it twice a year.

faqs.question: Can a Diploma lesson run on a Friday or a Saturday in the Kingdom?
faqs.answer: Yes, and a weekend morning is often the better answer where the school week is already full. Friday and Saturday are the Saudi weekend, so a morning block leaves the student fresher than a weekday evening session at eight. It can also solve a tutor-side problem: someone whose own working week makes a Saudi weekday impossible may be free on a Saturday morning. Two hours with a break works better than one long run.

faqs.question: What happens to a weekly Diploma slot when school days shorten during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: The slot usually moves later or shifts to a weekend morning for those weeks, and that is agreed in advance rather than improvised. School days shorten and evening patterns change, so the autumn hour may not work. Because it moves about eleven days earlier each year, it falls at a different point in the course each time. Ask the tutor to plan around it when the slot is first set.

faqs.question: How do we keep a Diploma slot through the long summer break?
faqs.answer: Two options work. Pause and hold the slot, agreeing the restart date before the break so the hour is still yours in the autumn. Or convert it into a short block of sessions aimed at one thing - the internal assessment design, or the topics the school rushed at the end of the year. Dropping the arrangement entirely and rebooking in the autumn usually means a different tutor and a different hour, which costs more than it saves.

faqs.question: What does a Saudi school typically fail to staff at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Higher Level Physics and Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches most often, with Economics at Higher Level and second modern languages close behind. The cause is arithmetic rather than ambition: a small cohort cannot justify a specialist for every Higher Level, so a school runs the subject with a non-specialist, offers it at Standard Level only, or withdraws it for a year. Ask which Higher Levels ran last year and who taught them, because the answer repeats.

faqs.question: How does a Ministry of Education school calendar differ from our international school's?
faqs.answer: Ministry of Education schools run a two-semester year starting in late August and finishing in late June, with an autumn break, a midyear break and an Eid Al Fitr break. Most international and British-curriculum schools run three terms and set their own dates, which differ school by school inside one city. The practical effect is that siblings at different schools break in different weeks, so a shared tutoring slot has to be planned around two calendars rather than one.

faqs.question: Why does a Diploma family in the Eastern Province drive to a school in another city?
faqs.answer: Because provision is uneven and the Diploma is not offered everywhere. In the Dammam, Al Khobar and Dhahran conurbation the three cities behave as one school market, and families routinely live in one and attend school in another. Elsewhere the drive exists because the nearest school running the Diploma is simply not local. That commute is the hidden constraint on an evening slot, and it is the number a tutor should be told before a time is agreed.

faqs.question: What should we ask a school about Diploma subject availability before enrolling?
faqs.answer: Four questions, in writing. Which subjects are offered at Higher Level this year, and which ran last year? Who teaches each one and what is their subject background? Is anything delivered online or through a third party? And what happens to a group that is too small to run? The answers predict exactly which subject a family will need outside support for, which is more useful than any prospectus and takes one email.

faqs.question: What are the options where there is no local school offering the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Three, in practice. Commute to a school in a neighbouring city, which is normal in the Eastern Province and heavy everywhere else. Choose a different curriculum locally, usually a British or Cambridge route, and accept that the pathway changes. Or board or relocate. Where the family stays and the subject support is the gap rather than the school, one-to-one online teaching covers the specific Higher Level the local school cannot run.

faqs.question: What does an American-curriculum student need to catch up for a Higher Level science?
faqs.answer: Usually depth rather than breadth. A general high-school science course covers a wide range at a level the Diploma treats as assumed, so the gap appears in quantitative work: the algebra behind the equations, the precision expected in a definition, and the uncertainties analysis in practical work. Add command terms, which are new as a system rather than as vocabulary. One term of focused work closes this for one subject, and two subjects at once rarely goes well.

faqs.question: Can a student join the Diploma a term late and still sit the May session?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is the school's decision rather than a tutor's. Content can be caught up in one subject, occasionally two. The harder problem is assessed work already in motion: internal assessments with school deadlines, an Extended Essay needing a supervisor and reflection sessions, a Theory of Knowledge title, and a CAS record. Ask the Diploma coordinator what is already past, then decide. Joining late and sitting a later session is often the better plan.

faqs.question: What transfers from a British school into the IB Diploma, and what does not?
faqs.answer: IGCSE content transfers well and is roughly what the Diploma assumes at the start. What does not transfer is the habit of justifying each step, which Higher Level papers reward and IGCSE rarely demands, and the breadth: a student used to three or four subjects now carries six plus the core. A student partway through A Levels faces the bigger gap, because subjects already dropped have to be picked up again from the beginning.

faqs.question: What is realistic to recover in one term after switching into the Diploma?
faqs.answer: One subject brought to a secure footing, and the assessed work for it started properly. That is a genuine outcome and worth paying for. Two weak subjects plus a late internal assessment is not a one-term job, and a tutor who accepts that brief without saying so is taking the booking rather than solving the problem. The honest sequence is to stabilise the subject with the nearest school deadline first, then reassess at four weeks.

intro.heading: The decision you are actually making, and the three ways it goes wrong
paragraphs: A parent looking for Diploma support is making four decisions at once, and they usually get presented as one. Whether to add outside teaching at all. Which subject, if the answer is yes. Whether this is a first-year problem that needs building or a final-year problem that needs converting. And when, inside a week that is already full, the lesson is going to happen. The fourth decision looks like administration and is the one that determines whether the other three ever produce anything.

Start with the week, because it is the hardest constraint and the one nobody writes about. The school week in the Kingdom runs Sunday to Thursday. Friday and Saturday are the weekend. A Diploma student is carrying six subjects, an Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and a Creativity, Activity, Service record, and the school day is followed by homework in several subjects at once. What is left is a handful of evenings, two of which are usually already committed to something. That is the real supply of lesson slots, and it is small.

Now add the tutor's week. A tutor in the United Kingdom or Europe works Monday to Friday, so a Sunday evening lesson for your child is a weekend evening for them. A tutor in India or Pakistan works into Saturday, so your Sunday is an ordinary working day and the problem is the hour rather than the day. A tutor inside the Kingdom shares your week exactly and has their own teaching day to finish first. None of these is disqualifying. All of them change which slots will still exist in the second year of the Diploma.

Three failures follow from getting this wrong, and they are the three we see most. The first is the arrangement that works for a term and quietly dies, because the tutor was giving up a weekend evening and goodwill is not a schedule. The second is the slot that drifts twice a year, because it was agreed in the tutor's local time rather than in Arabia Standard Time, and a clock change in another country moved a Diploma lesson into the middle of dinner. The third is the student taking support in three subjects at once, with no evening left in which to do the work any of them set.

The recommendation that follows from all of this is unglamorous. Fix the hour first, in Arabia Standard Time, against your household's real week. Then match a specialist inside the pool genuinely working at that hour, for one subject, chosen because it is the one where the gap is widest or the stakes are highest. Add a second subject only once the first has a rhythm, and expect to protect the slot rather than to move it. A Diploma arrangement that survives two years beats a better-credentialed one that lasts a term.

The rest of this page does the Diploma properly, because the decision is not really answerable without it: the six subject groups and what each one signals, how the 45 points are assembled, what the core demands, what changes at Higher Level, and how a Diploma becomes a certificate a Saudi university will accept. Then it returns to the week and the time zone, which is where the decision is won or lost.

ib-diploma-tutor.programmesIntro: The Diploma is the final two years of a longer continuum, and where a student entered it changes what they need now. These are the stages either side of it, with a note on how each behaves for a family in the Kingdom rather than in the country the school's curriculum came from.

programmes.name: The first Diploma year
programmes.description: Content is laid down, subject choices become real, and the internal assessment work starts whether or not it feels urgent. There is no external examination at the end, which is exactly why the year is dangerous: a student can drift for two terms with nothing to show it, and the drift becomes visible only when the second year arrives with no margin. The Extended Essay question is usually chosen here too.
programmes.countryNote: In the Kingdom this is also the year families discover which Higher Level options their school actually runs rather than lists. A student taking a Higher Level subject the school covers alongside another course is not in trouble, but they are carrying more of it themselves, and the first year is when that becomes fixable rather than terminal.

programmes.name: The second Diploma year
programmes.description: Internal assessment deadlines, the Extended Essay, the Theory of Knowledge essay and university applications all land in the same months, and then the examination session follows. The work shifts from learning content to converting it into marks: command terms, timing, mark schemes and the specific question types that cost this student marks. Predicted grades are issued during this year and shape every application made from it.
programmes.countryNote: Saudi families applying inside the Kingdom are simultaneously starting an administrative process that overseas-bound families are not: documentation, equivalency and the Qiyas tests. That is a second workload in the same term as the first. Families who map it early build time for it; families who do not find both halves compressed into a final few weeks.

programmes.name: What comes before, inside the IB continuum
programmes.description: The Middle Years Programme assesses against four lettered criteria per subject and ends with the Personal Project. It builds extended inquiry and criterion-referenced writing. What it does not build is timed examination technique, because it does not assess by external paper, so students arriving into the Diploma from it are often strong writers who have never written to a clock.
programmes.countryNote: Schools in the Kingdom run this route and the IGCSE route into the Diploma, sometimes within the same city. Neither is a deficit. The useful question at enrolment is which route the school's own leaving cohort took and how its Diploma results looked afterwards, because that answers more than a curriculum comparison does.

programmes.name: The other route in
programmes.description: Cambridge or Edexcel IGCSE, examined externally at sixteen, with tiering in many Cambridge subjects. Students arriving from this route into the Diploma bring strong examination habits and meet a different problem: the Diploma rewards sustained argument and independent investigation, where IGCSE rewarded precise short answers. Mathematics is the usual pressure point, because the step into a Higher Level course assumes fluency IGCSE did not require.
programmes.countryNote: An IGCSE grade in the Kingdom frequently decides whether a school will allow a Higher Level subject, and the decision is made quickly after results. Families who treat the final IGCSE term as a Diploma entry requirement rather than as an end point keep more options open at a point where options are cheap.

ib-diploma-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma subjects families in the Kingdom most often ask for, usually because a school runs them at one level only or covers a Higher Level option alongside another course. Each note says what the subject assesses and where the marks are actually lost.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic fluency is the whole foundation, and gaps in it surface in calculus rather than in algebra. The Higher Level course adds proof and further calculus with no Standard Level counterpart, and the additional paper carries its own weighting. Most lost marks are method marks: a correct answer with the working held in the student's head earns a fraction of what an honest flawed method earns.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology-assisted work, assessed on interpretation as much as on calculation. Students lose marks by giving a number with no units, no context and no comment. The choice between this and Analysis and Approaches is a university decision first: engineering and many physical science courses expect the latter, and the choice is made in the first Diploma year.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Extended-response questions reward a stated principle before any algebra appears, and students who begin with the equation lose the reasoning marks. Unit errors and significant figures drain marks across every paper. The Higher Level extension topics are the ones a thinly staffed school covers last, and the internal investigation is where strong paper candidates most often underperform.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics carry the difficulty, and the data booklet helps only a student who has practised finding things in it under time. Examiners pay for the precise term, not the paraphrase. The internal assessment stands or falls on a research question narrow enough to generate real data, which is a design problem rather than a writing one.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Breadth is the difficulty and definitions are marked strictly, so a near-miss definition earns nothing. Command terms divide this subject sharply: outline, explain and distinguish demand different structures, and a student who writes the same shape of answer for all three loses marks in every one. Statistical handling in the internal investigation is routinely its weakest section.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: The labelled diagram carries the marks and the labels are what get dropped. Evaluation is where able writers stall, surveying both sides without reaching a judgement a mark scheme can credit. The Higher Level quantitative work is treated as arithmetic by students who then lose the interpretation marks that were the point of including it.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Source work is a skill with its own criteria: origin, purpose, value and limitation, applied to the source rather than recited. Essay questions reward a sustained argument with a line of reasoning, and narrative chronology scores in the lower bands however accurate it is. The internal assessment is a historical investigation with a methodological section students consistently under-write.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tools are easy to name and hard to apply, and the marks sit in applying one to the specific organisation with the figures supplied. Higher Level answers need a recommendation defended against a rejected alternative. Listing advantages and disadvantages without choosing stops an otherwise competent answer short of the top band every time.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Not a comprehension exercise. The paper asks for an argument about how a text produces its effect, supported by close reference, and students trained on content-recall subjects write summary instead. The individual oral needs a global issue chosen early and two texts that genuinely speak to it, which is a planning problem long before it is a speaking one.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pseudocode under examination conditions is a separate skill from writing code that runs, and students who have only done the second lose marks on the first. The Higher Level extension covers abstract data structures and resource management, which reward diagrams. The internal assessment solves a real client's problem, and projects fail the criteria when client and success criteria were invented late.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Studies are evidence, not content to be recalled, and an answer that describes a study without using it to support a claim earns little. Command terms separate describe, contrast and evaluate sharply here. The internal assessment is an experimental replication where the statistical reasoning, rather than the write-up, is what distinguishes the bands.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Assessed by an essay on a prescribed title and an exhibition of objects with a written commentary, and marked on the quality of knowledge argument rather than on subject content. Students who write an opinion piece score poorly; students who interrogate how a claim could be known score well. Word limits are strict and are published in the current subject guide the coordinator holds.

ib-diploma-tutor.regionsIntro: Where a family lives in the Kingdom changes the evening that is actually available, which is why a Diploma arrangement should be built around the household's week before it is built around a tutor. These are the places Diploma families write in from, with the scheduling reality in each.

regions.name: Riyadh
regions.note: Roughly an hour across in traffic, which means the school run, not the school day, sets the earliest workable start. A family in the north and a family in the south of the city can be an hour apart on the same timetable, and that hour decides whether a European tutor is reachable at all.

regions.name: Jeddah
regions.note: A long coastal spine from the historic centre north to Obhur, so travel time rather than distance governs the evening. Families at the northern end routinely start later than the city's school timings alone would suggest, which narrows the pool of tutors whose own day is already ending.

regions.name: Dammam, Al Khobar and Dhahran
regions.note: One conurbation acting as a single school market, with families living in one city and attending school in another. Cross-city school runs push the realistic start later. The King Fahd Causeway to Bahrain adds a weekend pattern that occasionally collides with a Thursday evening slot.

regions.name: Jubail and Yanbu
regions.note: Industrial cities where household routines bend around shift rotations, so a fixed weekly hour is worth more than a flexible one. A slot that works for one rotation block may not work for the next, which is an argument for agreeing the time against the student's week rather than the parent's.

regions.name: Al Ahsa
regions.note: About an hour and a half inland from the Eastern Province cluster. Families commuting to coastal schooling have the latest effective start of anyone in that region, and for them the tutors whose own working day ends early are the practical pool rather than the preferred one.

regions.name: Makkah and Madinah
regions.note: Established school markets where the year also bends around Hajj and Umrah seasons, which affects travel and attendance in ways a tutor based elsewhere needs to be told rather than left to infer. A Diploma plan made here should name those weeks in advance.

regions.name: Thuwal and the KAUST campus
regions.note: A campus community north of Jeddah whose intake turns over with research contracts, so mid-course arrivals into DP1 and DP2 are normal. Continuity through a relocation matters more here than the identity of any one tutor, and online delivery is what makes that continuity possible.

regions.name: Tabuk, AlUla and NEOM
regions.note: The north-west, where provision is catching up with an arriving workforce and there is often no local specialist in a Higher Level subject at any price. Connectivity is the question worth checking before the first session rather than the supply of tutors, which is already settled.

schoolClusters.note: Students we support attend schools including these, which between them run the IB continuum alongside Cambridge and American provision. Ask any school which Higher Level options actually ran in the last intake rather than which appear in the subject list, because in a small cohort those are different documents.

schoolClusters.city: Jeddah and the Red Sea coast
schoolClusters.note: The British International School of Jeddah is an IB World School and a Cambridge school; Deutsche Internationale Schule Jeddah runs to Grade 12. Term dates and mock timings differ between schools in the same city, so a Diploma plan has to be built from your own school's calendar.

schoolClusters.city: Dhahran, Jubail and the Eastern Province
schoolClusters.note: The International Schools Group operates several campuses here and the Diploma is offered at some of them rather than all, so programme availability is a per-campus question. British and Cambridge curricula sit alongside the IB provision across the conurbation.

ib-diploma-tutor.modesIntro: Three ways of working cover nearly every Diploma request, and the difference between them is how much of the two years remains. All three are one-to-one over live video, with the hour fixed in Arabia Standard Time rather than in the tutor's local time.

modes.title: A protected weekly slot across both Diploma years
modes.description: One subject, one tutor, one hour a week held for the duration. The value is cumulative: a tutor who has seen the same error twice can name it, and a two-year relationship covers internal assessment design, the paper technique and the final conversion without a handover. This is the mode that justifies choosing the tutor whose week genuinely contains your hour.
bullets: The hour agreed in Arabia Standard Time and not renegotiated seasonally
Internal assessment milestones mapped against the school's own deadlines
Written feedback to the parent after every session
A pause available across a long break without losing the slot

modes.title: Internal assessment and core support
modes.description: Shorter, denser work on the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge or a subject's internal assessment, at the points in the year where those collide. The tutor teaches the criteria, discusses the question, reads what the student has written and says where it falls short of a descriptor. The student does the writing and the revising, always.
bullets: Criteria explained in the language the examiner uses
A research question tested for scope before any work is done
Feedback against descriptors, on the student's own draft
Timelines set from the school's internal deadlines, not ours

modes.title: Conversion work before the examination session
modes.description: Past papers under time, marked against published mark schemes, with command terms and answer length drilled directly. This assumes the content is largely in place and turns it into marks. For a student with real content gaps it is the wrong purchase, and the diagnostic will say so rather than taking the booking.
bullets: Diagnosed from the student's own marked mock scripts

sections.heading: What a Diploma actually is: six groups, three at Higher Level
paragraphs: A Diploma student takes six subjects, one from each of six groups, normally three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level. Some students take four at Higher Level and two at Standard. The sixth group is the arts, and a student may replace it with a second subject from groups one to five instead, which is the commonest substitution among science-directed students in the Kingdom. The structure matters because it constrains the choices: a student cannot drop a language to take a third science, and a university prerequisite in a group four subject has to be met inside that group.

Each group signals something different to a university, and parents frequently misjudge which signals carry weight. Group four and group five do most of the work for science, engineering and medicine applications, and the mathematics course chosen matters as much as the level. Group three subjects supply the essay writing and evaluation that social science degrees expect. Group two, the second language, is rarely a prerequisite for anything and is often where a student spends disproportionate anxiety.

The level decision inside each group is where most of the real consequence sits. Three Higher Level subjects is a workload decision as well as an academic one, and a student who takes the wrong three carries two years of unnecessary difficulty for no gain in their application. The right three are the ones a destination programme actually expects, which is knowable in the first Diploma year if a family looks. Universities publish their prerequisites; that document is more useful than any amount of general advice.

The table below sets out the groups and what each choice reads as. It is written for the Kingdom specifically: the typical Higher Level choices listed are the ones schools here run most reliably, which is not the same as the ones they advertise. A family whose school cannot staff a Higher Level option in the group a degree requires has a real problem, and it is better identified in the first Diploma year than in the second.

sections.heading: Where the 45 points come from
paragraphs: The arithmetic is simple and badly explained almost everywhere. Six subjects, each graded from 1 to 7 by the IB, give a maximum of 42 points. Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay are each awarded a letter grade, and the two letters are combined in a published matrix worth up to three further points. Forty-two plus three is 45, and nothing else contributes. Creativity, Activity, Service earns no points at all and is a completion requirement, which is a distinction worth making to a student who has decided it does not matter.

The failing conditions are the part families do not hear about until they matter. A Diploma is not awarded on total alone: the IB publishes a minimum total and a list of conditions that prevent an award regardless of it, including the effect of a very low grade in any single subject and a failing letter on either core component. A student with a respectable total and one unaddressed failure does not receive the Diploma. Your child's Diploma Programme coordinator holds the current version of those conditions, and they are the person to ask rather than a forum.

Inside each subject grade sits an internally assessed component, marked by the teacher against IB criteria and then moderated by the IB. In most subjects it is around a fifth of the final grade, and the exact figure is published in the subject guide the teacher works from. Its significance is out of proportion to its weighting, for two reasons: it is the only part of the grade produced under no time pressure, and it is the part a student can still influence when the papers are months away.

The practical consequence for a family choosing where to spend money is clear enough. Points gained in internal assessment and in the core are gained in work done over weeks, with feedback, in the student's own time. Points gained on papers depend on technique under time, which also responds to teaching but on a longer timescale. A family starting in the first Diploma year should think about the first category. A family starting in the final months is working almost entirely in the second.

sections.heading: The core: Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS
paragraphs: The core is the part of the Diploma that has no equivalent in any other school qualification, and it is the part students treat as optional until it is too late to treat it that way. Theory of Knowledge is assessed by an essay on a prescribed title and by an exhibition of objects with a written commentary. It is marked on the quality of the knowledge argument rather than on any subject content, which is why strong subject students sometimes score poorly: they write what they know instead of interrogating how it could be known.

The Extended Essay is an independent research piece on a question of the student's own choosing, capped at four thousand words, supervised inside the school with a required reflection process. The commonest failure is not writing quality. It is scope: a question too broad to answer in four thousand words, or too narrow to sustain them, chosen before the student had read enough to know which. A supervisor will push on this, and a student who chooses carefully in the first Diploma year has removed most of the risk already. Word limits and reflection requirements are published in the current guide the coordinator holds.

Creativity, Activity, Service carries no points and cannot be skipped, which is a combination students find confusing and parents find irritating. It needs a record of engagement across the three strands with reflection, signed off by the school's coordinator. The practical advice is to keep the record as you go, because reconstructing eighteen months of activity in a final term is both unpleasant and visibly thin. It also competes for exactly the evenings a tutoring slot wants, which is a scheduling fact rather than a complaint.

On what a tutor may do with any of this, the line is firm and it is worth stating in plain terms. A tutor may teach the criteria, explain what a descriptor asks for, discuss whether a research question is answerable, and read a draft the student wrote and say where it falls short. No tutor may write the Extended Essay, part-write it, supply text for it or redraft a student's paragraph into better prose. The same applies to the Theory of Knowledge essay and to every internal assessment. We give feedback; the student writes; the draft trail stays theirs.

sections.heading: Higher Level against Standard Level: what actually changes
paragraphs: Parents often read Higher Level as harder and leave it there, which under-describes the difference in a way that leads to poor choices. The content differs: Higher Level courses carry additional topics with no Standard Level counterpart, and those topics are examined. The assessment differs: most subjects add a paper or a component at Higher Level, carrying its own weighting. The expectation in extended responses differs: Standard Level rewards a correct explanation, Higher Level rewards a reasoned argument applied to an unfamiliar context.

The IB publishes recommended teaching hours for each, around two hundred and forty for a Higher Level course and around one hundred and fifty for Standard Level. That ratio is the honest measure of the commitment, and it explains the pattern we see in thinly staffed schools: the Higher Level extension topics are the ones taught last, taught quickly, or set as reading, because they are the hours a school is shortest of. A student in that position is not behind through any fault of their own and is the single most common Diploma tutoring request in the Kingdom.

The choice of which three to take at Higher Level should be made against destination prerequisites rather than against enthusiasm or current grades. A university that requires a group four subject at Higher Level will not accept it at Standard Level, and that requirement is published. Conversely, taking a fourth Higher Level subject because a student can is a decision to spend ninety extra recommended hours on something no application asked for, in a two-year programme that is already full.

Dropping from Higher Level to Standard Level mid-course is possible, is sometimes right, and is a conversation to have with the school early rather than in a panic. It is right when a student is losing marks across their other five subjects because one is consuming all their time. It is wrong when it closes a prerequisite the student still intends to use. The table sets out what the level decision actually governs, so the conversation can be had on evidence.

sections.heading: The Sunday-to-Thursday week, and the tutor's own working week
paragraphs: This is the section that decides whether any of the rest of this page turns into teaching. The school week in the Kingdom runs Sunday to Thursday, and almost every page about online tutoring assumes Monday to Friday, because it was written for another market and lightly edited. The practical consequence is specific: your child's Sunday evening is a school night and, for a tutor in most of Europe or the Americas, a weekend evening. Your Thursday evening is the start of your weekend and the middle of their working week.

Match on that honestly and the arrangement lasts two years. Ignore it and you get the failure that looks like nothing in particular: a tutor who is reliable for a term, then starts proposing alternative times, then becomes hard to book. Nobody did anything wrong. A person giving up a weekend evening for somebody else's school night is drawing on goodwill, and goodwill is a budget rather than a schedule. Asking directly, before matching, which days are inside a tutor's own working week is the cheapest insurance available.

The second variable is the hour. A Diploma session is more demanding than an IGCSE one and runs longer, so the slot has to fall where both sides are capable of ninety minutes of real work. For a family whose school run ends late, in northern Jeddah or inland from the Eastern Province cluster, the realistic start is later than the school timetable suggests, and each half-hour later removes a set of countries from the pool. That is worth knowing before you fall in love with a profile.

The table converts a six in the evening slot in the Kingdom into the tutor's own clock and sets it beside their working week. Read the final column rather than the second: availability and sustainability are different properties, and a Diploma needs the second. Within the region, a tutor whose own week also runs Sunday to Thursday is the most structurally stable match there is, and that is a genuine reason to ask where a tutor is rather than treating location as irrelevant.

sections.heading: Arabia Standard Time does not move; the tutor's clock does
paragraphs: The Kingdom runs on Arabia Standard Time, three hours ahead of Coordinated Universal Time, and does not observe daylight saving. That single fact prevents the most common avoidable disruption in cross-border tutoring, provided somebody acts on it. A slot agreed as seven in the evening in the Kingdom is seven in the evening in the Kingdom permanently. A slot agreed as four in the afternoon in the tutor's country moves by an hour twice a year, in opposite directions, and lands somewhere in your family's dinner.

Write the time down in Arabia Standard Time, in the confirmation, and say explicitly that it does not change when the tutor's clock does. This sounds trivial and is responsible for a surprising share of the arrangements that quietly fail in the second year, because the drift happens in the middle of a term when nobody has the appetite to renegotiate and the lesson gradually becomes inconvenient for everybody. The tutor absorbs the change; the family keeps the hour.

Two further scheduling realities are specific to the Kingdom and worth naming in a plan rather than discovering. During Ramadan the school day shortens and household routines shift to later in the evening, so Diploma sessions commonly move rather than pausing. The dates move against the Gregorian calendar each year and are confirmed by moon sighting, so the right approach is to agree with the tutor in advance that the slot will move for those weeks and then fix the replacement hour when the pattern is known locally.

The second is the long summer break and the autumn and midyear breaks, which differ between international schools in the same city because each school sets its own calendar. A plan built on one school's published dates does not transfer to another school across the road. Send your own school's calendar to the tutor at the start rather than relying on a general assumption, and decide in advance which breaks are pauses and which are working weeks.

sections.heading: Command terms, mark schemes and what a predicted grade is worth
paragraphs: Diploma marks are awarded against mark schemes written around command terms, and the command term is an instruction rather than a courtesy. Evaluate wants a judgement supported by weighed evidence. Justify wants a conclusion with reasons attached. Analyse wants a structure broken into parts and the relationship between them. Discuss wants more than one position genuinely considered. A student who answers all four with the same shape of essay loses marks in three of them, and the marked script shows exactly where.

Mark schemes also reward things textbook answers do not contain. In the sciences that means the stated principle before the algebra and the correct unit after it. In the essay subjects it means a line of argument rather than coverage, and an explicit judgement where one is asked for. In mathematics it means visible method, which is where able students are most profligate. None of this is secret; the schemes are published and the single most useful hour a Diploma student can spend is marking their own paper against one.

Grade boundaries move between series, which unsettles families who expect a fixed scale. They move because the IB sets them after examiner judgement on the difficulty of that particular paper, so a slightly harder paper carries slightly lower boundaries. The useful consequence is that a raw mark is not a grade until boundaries are published, and the unhelpful consequence is that a student who was two marks under a boundary in a mock learns nothing durable from the gap. Work on the error pattern rather than on the margin.

A predicted grade is the school's professional judgement of what a student is likely to achieve, issued for university applications, and it is not a promise from anybody. Teachers base it on the evidence they have, which is internal assessment and mock performance. It can be discussed with the school, with evidence, and a family that wants to discuss one should bring marked work rather than an opinion. No tutor can issue a predicted grade, change one, or guarantee that a final grade will match it.

sections.heading: From a Diploma to a Saudi university: how equivalency works
paragraphs: This is the biggest gap in the material written about Diploma tutoring in the Kingdom, and it is a mechanism rather than a mystery. A foreign or international school certificate is not automatically treated as equivalent to the Saudi secondary certificate. It needs an equivalency decision, the mu'adalah, from the Ministry of Education, and that applies to an IB Diploma, to A Levels and to an American high school diploma in the same way. Until that decision exists, a Saudi university has nothing it can process.

Alongside it, Saudi universities read the national testing system. Qudurat, the General Aptitude Test, is run by the Education and Training Evaluation Commission through its National Center for Assessment, Qiyas, and tests verbal and quantitative reasoning rather than taught syllabus content; it is sat in Arabic or in English. Tahsili, the Achievement Test, covers the science-stream subjects: mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology and English. Its content follows the Saudi national curriculum, which is precisely why Diploma students find its framing unfamiliar even where the underlying material is not.

Each university then publishes its own admission criteria, combining school results with those scores, and the weightings differ by university and by programme. Competitive engineering, medicine and science programmes lean hardest on the Achievement Test. We publish no threshold for either test and no university's formula, because they differ by institution, programme and intake, and a number copied from a forum is worse than no number at all, since a family plans around it. Some universities also state a maximum age for the certificate they will accept, which matters to a student taking a gap year.

What a Diploma tutor can usefully do inside this is narrow and real. Subject teaching makes the Achievement Test's underlying material secure rather than approximate, and mapping a Diploma syllabus against national-curriculum framing tells a family which topics need teaching rather than revision. Subject and level choices can be checked against a destination programme's published prerequisites while those choices are still open. The administrative route is the family's and the Ministry's, and no platform can promise an admission outcome.

sections.heading: Starting, reporting, and the point where you stop
paragraphs: The first conversation is a diagnosis rather than a booking. We want the subject, the level, where the student is in the Diploma, the school's term structure and internal deadlines, and a marked piece of recent work. A mock script with the examiner's annotations is worth more than any description, because it shows whether the marks went to content, to command terms, to method or to the clock, and those four need different teaching.

A free trial lesson follows and it is diagnostic in both directions. The tutor works a real problem with the student and then says what the difficulty looks like from inside the subject and what the first four weeks should achieve. Sometimes that recommendation is to buy less: a student who understands the content and loses marks on technique needs a short block, not two years of weekly lessons. A trial that never disagrees with the parent has not assessed anything.

Reporting after that is written and goes to you, after every session: what was covered, what was set, and what is still wrong. The review point is at four sessions, where there is enough evidence to judge whether the same errors are still appearing and whether the student is doing the work between lessons. Either side can stop or change tutor at that point. If the slot works and the person does not, we keep the slot and change the person, briefed with what the first tutor found so your child does not repeat a diagnostic.

Occasionally no specialist is free at your hour, particularly for a scarce Higher Level subject in the months before the examination session, when every family wants the same evening. We will say so and offer the alternatives rather than putting a generalist in the slot and letting you work out the difference later. Stopping is also a legitimate outcome: a student who has the technique and is doing the work does not need to keep paying for company, and we would rather say that than keep a slot filled.

process.title: Name the subject, the level and the year
process.description: Chemistry at Higher Level in the second Diploma year with the internal assessment due this term is a brief. Chemistry is not. The level, the position in the two years and the school's internal deadlines decide whether the work is content, internal assessment or conversion, and those three need different tutors and different session lengths.

process.title: Fix the hour before the tutor
process.description: Work out which evenings genuinely exist in your Sunday-to-Thursday week once the school run, the core and homework are accounted for, and set the time in Arabia Standard Time. Then we match inside the pool actually working at that hour. Choosing the person first and the time afterwards is how a two-year arrangement becomes a two-term one.

process.title: Send a marked script and the school calendar
process.description: The script shows where marks are being lost; the calendar shows when the pressure arrives. Together they produce a plan rather than a schedule. International schools in the same city run different terms and different mock timings, so a general assumption about the year is worse than the document your school already published.

process.title: Treat the trial as the test
process.description: Ask which components the tutor has taught and marked, what a named mark scheme pays for, and what they see in your child's script. Watch whether your child is writing or listening. The trial should produce a specific plan for four weeks, and sometimes the honest plan is smaller than the one you arrived intending to buy.

process.title: Review at four sessions, then protect the slot
process.description: Four lessons is enough evidence. We look at whether the same errors persist, what the school has noticed, and whether work is happening between sessions. After that, the single most valuable thing a family can do is defend the hour: a Diploma arrangement that holds its slot for two years outperforms a better-credentialed one that keeps moving.

whyPoints.title: The tutor's working week checked before matching
whyPoints.description: We ask where a tutor is and which days are inside their own working week, because a Sunday school night that falls on somebody's weekend is an arrangement running on goodwill. Availability and sustainability are different properties, and a Diploma needs the second one for two years rather than one term.

whyPoints.title: Slots pinned to Arabia Standard Time
whyPoints.description: The Kingdom does not observe daylight saving, so a time agreed in Arabia Standard Time stays where it was put and the tutor's clock is what moves. That is written into the confirmation. It removes the most common avoidable disruption in cross-border tutoring, and it costs nothing to do properly at the start.

whyPoints.title: Matched by group, level and component
whyPoints.description: A Higher Level extension topic a school covered last is a different request from internal assessment design or from paper technique in the final term. We match on the component that is actually costing marks, which is why the diagnosis comes before the booking rather than after it.

whyPoints.title: The core taken as seriously as the subjects
whyPoints.description: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay are worth up to three points and can prevent an award outright, and they are the parts a student can still influence when papers are months away. Support covers the criteria, the scope of a research question and feedback on the student's own drafts.

whyPoints.title: Nothing written on a student's behalf
whyPoints.description: A tutor explains a descriptor, discusses a research question and says where a draft falls short. No Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge essay or internal assessment is written, part-written or redrafted for a student, in any subject. The draft trail stays with the student, which is also what protects them if a school ever asks.

whyPoints.title: Honest about the limits
whyPoints.description: No grade, point total, predicted grade or university place is promised here, and no threshold for Qudurat or Tahsili is published, because those differ by university and programme. When no specialist is free at your hour we say so rather than substituting a generalist, and stopping is a legitimate recommendation.

faqs.question: What does a first diagnostic session look for in a student who is already partway through DP2?
faqs.answer: Three things, in order. Whether the content is in place, which a few targeted questions establish faster than any test. Whether the marks being lost are technique rather than knowledge, which the student's marked mock script shows directly. And what is still movable in the time remaining, since internal assessment and core work respond over weeks while paper technique responds faster. The output is a four-week plan with one priority rather than a list of everything that could be improved. For a student this far in, deciding what not to work on matters as much as deciding what to teach.

faqs.question: Who owns the plan when the school already has its own approach to a Diploma subject?
faqs.answer: The school does, and an outside tutor works inside it rather than running a parallel course. That means knowing the school's scheme of work, its internal deadlines and what the subject teacher has already said about a draft. Where the tutor disagrees with the school's method, the student is told that two valid approaches exist and shown the one their teacher will be marking against, because a student caught between two notations for the same topic ends up confident in neither. Tell the school that subject support is in place; a teacher who knows will usually share the internal timeline.

faqs.question: What does a Diploma tutor report to a parent, and how often?
faqs.answer: After every session, in writing: what was covered, what was set, what the student is still getting wrong and what you can expect to see next week. Monthly, something broader, covering whether the error pattern is shifting and whether the work between sessions is happening. What a report should not contain is a predicted grade, because a tutor is not in a position to issue one, or a percentage improvement figure, because a single student is not a sample. Specific and unflattering is more useful than encouraging, and if a report reads like reassurance it is not telling you anything.

faqs.question: What do we do if the Diploma student does not want a tutor at all?
faqs.answer: Take it seriously rather than overriding it, because a resentful student in a one-to-one session wastes the hour efficiently. Usually the objection is to being treated as a problem, and it dissolves when the work is specific: a student who sees their own marked script and the three marks they left on the table engages with that. Start with a single diagnostic session framed as a second opinion rather than a commitment, let the student set the first agenda, and give them a veto on continuing. A student who chose the arrangement works in it.

faqs.question: How do we decide to stop outside support partway through the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Stop when the student is reliably doing the thing the tutoring taught without the tutoring. The signals are concrete: the same error has stopped appearing in marked work, the student is marking their own papers against mark schemes, and the sessions have started to feel like company rather than teaching. That last one is worth taking seriously. A tutor who cannot name what the next four weeks will change should be told to stop, and an honest one will say it first. Paying for presence is common in the final year and is mostly a response to parental anxiety rather than to a subject problem.

faqs.question: How many Diploma subjects can realistically be supported in one Sunday-to-Thursday week?
faqs.answer: One, in most cases, and two only where the student is genuinely not using their evenings. Six subjects, the core and school homework already consume the week, and a tutored session generates work of its own that has to land somewhere. A student taking support in three subjects has the sessions and none of the time to act on any of them, which converts teaching into attendance. Choose the subject where the gap is widest or where a published prerequisite makes the stakes highest, establish a rhythm, and only then consider adding a second.

faqs.question: Why do Diploma sessions in the Kingdom usually start later than families first propose?
faqs.answer: Because the school run, not the school day, sets the earliest workable time, and in cities that are an hour across that gap is substantial. A family in northern Jeddah or commuting inland from the Eastern Province cluster is often an hour behind the school timetable before anyone opens a book. A Diploma session also needs a student capable of sustained work rather than one who has just walked in, so a short gap after arriving home is worth protecting. Each half-hour later removes a set of tutor time zones from the pool, which is why the hour is worth settling first.

faqs.question: Can a Diploma session run on a Friday or a Saturday when the school week is full?
faqs.answer: It can, and for some households it is the better answer, particularly where weekday evenings are consumed by the core and by homework in several subjects. The trade-off is that a Saudi weekend day is a working day for tutors in much of the world and a weekend day for others, so the pool is differently shaped rather than smaller. What works least well is treating the weekend as overflow for lessons missed during the week, because the student needs at least one day with nothing scheduled in a programme this long.

faqs.question: What happens to a Diploma slot when the school day shortens during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Sessions usually move rather than stop. School hours shorten and household routines shift later in the evening, so the sensible approach is to agree in advance with the tutor that the slot will change for those weeks, then fix the replacement hour once the local pattern is known. The timing moves against the Gregorian calendar each year and is confirmed by moon sighting, so it is not something to pin down months ahead. For a student with an internal assessment deadline in the same period, agreeing which weeks are working weeks is worth doing before it arrives.

faqs.question: Our Diploma tutor is in the United Kingdom. What happens to our hour when their clocks change?
faqs.answer: Nothing, provided the slot was agreed in Arabia Standard Time and recorded that way. The Kingdom does not observe daylight saving, so your six in the evening stays at six in the evening, and the tutor's local time moves by an hour twice a year. They absorb it. Where this goes wrong is an arrangement agreed in the tutor's local time, which then drifts into your dinner in one direction and into the school run in the other. Ask for the confirmation to state the time in Arabia Standard Time explicitly, once, at the start.

faqs.question: How much of a Higher Level Diploma grade is decided by internal assessment rather than by the papers?
faqs.answer: In most subjects the internally assessed component sits at around a fifth of the final grade, and the exact figure is published in the subject guide your child's teacher works from, so that is the number to ask for rather than a general one. Its importance is larger than its weighting suggests, for two reasons. It is the only part of the grade produced without time pressure, over weeks, with feedback available. And it is the part a student can still influence when the examination session is months away, which makes it the highest-value work available early in the programme.

faqs.question: What exactly is a Diploma predicted grade, who decides it, and can it be challenged?
faqs.answer: It is the school's professional judgement of the grade a student is likely to achieve, issued for university applications, and it comes from the subject teacher and the coordinator rather than from any tutor. Teachers base it on the evidence available: internal assessment, mock performance and classwork. It can be discussed, and a family that wants to discuss one should bring marked work rather than an opinion, early rather than after applications are submitted. A predicted grade is not a promise from the school, from the IB or from anyone else, and no tutor can issue one or alter one.

faqs.question: Why do Diploma grade boundaries move from one examination session to the next?
faqs.answer: Because they are set after the papers have been sat, using examiner judgement about how demanding that particular paper turned out to be. A harder paper carries slightly lower boundaries, which is the mechanism that keeps a grade meaning roughly the same thing across sessions. Two consequences follow for a family. A raw mark is not a grade until boundaries are published, so a mock percentage is an indication rather than a result. And a student who missed a boundary by two marks has learned nothing durable from the margin; the error pattern is the thing to work on.

faqs.question: What do Diploma command terms like evaluate, justify and analyse actually require?
faqs.answer: Different structures, which is why the same essay answering all three loses marks in two of them. Evaluate wants a judgement reached by weighing evidence on both sides. Justify wants a stated conclusion with the reasons attached to it. Analyse wants something broken into its parts with the relationship between them made explicit. Discuss wants more than one position genuinely considered rather than listed. The fastest way to fix this is mechanical: sort twenty past-paper questions by command term and answer them in sets, which produces the right shape by habit rather than by effort.

faqs.question: How does the Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay matrix change a Diploma total?
faqs.answer: Each of the two is awarded a letter grade, and the published matrix combines them into up to three additional points on top of the forty-two available from six subjects. That is the whole of their arithmetic contribution. Their larger significance is the other direction: a failing letter on either can prevent a Diploma being awarded whatever the subject total, which makes the core a risk to manage rather than an optional extra. Your child's Diploma Programme coordinator holds the current matrix and the current failing conditions, and those are the authoritative versions.

ib-diploma-tutor.closingHeading: Settle the hour, then the specialist
ib-diploma-tutor.closingBody: A Diploma arrangement succeeds or fails on whether the slot survives two years, so start there. Work out which evenings genuinely exist in your Sunday-to-Thursday week, set the time in Arabia Standard Time, and tell us the subject, the level and where your child is in the programme. Send one marked script and your school's own calendar. A free trial lesson follows, and it is a diagnosis rather than a sales call: the tutor will say what the real difficulty is and what four weeks should achieve, including when the honest answer is less than you planned to buy. Lessons are one-to-one over live video; IB Gram does not send tutors to Saudi addresses. No grade, point total or university place is ever promised.

intro.heading: Why a Higher Level Biology search usually starts mid-course
paragraphs: Biology at Higher Level is the subject families most often underestimate. It reads as a memorising course, and for a term it behaves like one. Then the extended-response questions arrive, the data-based questions start asking candidates to evaluate someone else's experiment rather than recall a definition, and the scientific investigation lands on top of everything else. Most parents who search for an IB DP Biology HL home tutor in Saudi Arabia are not looking for a crammer. They are looking for someone who can see which of the four themes has gone soft, and how much of the remaining year is still available to fix it.

The honest answer depends on where the student is in the year, which is why this page runs backwards from the May session rather than forwards from today. A DP1 student in the autumn term has time to rebuild the molecular and cellular foundations properly. A DP2 student in the spring term does not, and pretending otherwise wastes the money. Between those two points sits the scientific investigation, which carries a fifth of the grade on its own and has school-set deadlines that almost never move. Counting backwards also tells you when not to buy: a student with secure themes and a working investigation plan may need six lessons rather than sixty.

A word on the phrase itself. In-home Biology tutoring in the Kingdom is a thin market, and it thins further the moment Higher Level is specified. Agencies in Riyadh and Jeddah price travel into their hourly rates, and a family in Abha, Tabuk or Ras Tanura may find nobody within driving distance who has taught the current guide at all. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a Saudi address: lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, and in-home teaching is a service we offer only in India. For Higher Level Biology that is also the better arrangement, because it decides the match on specialism instead of on distance.

What a specialist actually does is unglamorous. The first session diagnoses — a short set of past-paper questions sampled across the four themes, a look at any investigation work that exists, and a direct question about which command terms the student cannot tell apart. Out of that comes a plan with a date-free spine: what has to be true by the end of this term, what by the end of the next, and what the last eight weeks before the session are reserved for. Progress is written down and sent to you, not described in a phone call, and it names the theme and the paper rather than reporting that the session went well. If the match is wrong, say so after two lessons and we change it without an argument.

sections.heading: What Higher Level Biology is actually made of
paragraphs: Start with the shape of the grade, because every sensible plan is built from it. Higher Level Biology is assessed by two written papers and one internally assessed investigation. Paper 1 carries 36% and comes in two parts sat together: Paper 1A is multiple choice across all four themes, and Paper 1B is a set of data-based questions built around experiments the candidate has never seen. Paper 2 carries 44%, runs longer at Higher Level than at Standard Level, and mixes short answers with extended responses worth several marks each. The investigation carries the remaining 20%.

The content sits in four themes — unity and diversity, form and function, interaction and interdependence, continuity and change — each examined at four levels of organisation, from molecules to ecosystems. Higher Level candidates meet additional material inside every theme rather than in a separate unit bolted on at the end. That design matters for tutoring. There is no block of HL-only content to leave until last, so a student shaky on Standard Level cell biology is shaky on the Higher Level extension of it too.

Parents who did the Diploma themselves, or who have read an older guide, often ask about Paper 3. The current Biology course does not have one: the experimental and data-handling material that used to sit there now lives inside Paper 1B and Paper 2. Checking which guide a tutor teaches from is a fair first question, and a tutor who cannot answer it cleanly is not right for a Higher Level candidate. Your child's Diploma Programme coordinator can confirm the components the school has entered for.

sections.heading: The Higher Level Biology year, counted backwards
paragraphs: Diploma schools in the Kingdom enter candidates for the May session, so the useful way to plan is to count back from it. Work forwards from today and the plan drifts; work backwards and every term is given a job. The last eight weeks belong to timed papers and command-term technique, which means the content has to be broadly in place before they begin. The term before that belongs to whichever themes the diagnostic found weakest, taught properly rather than revised quickly.

Further back sits the scientific investigation. Schools set their own internal deadlines for it, usually with a draft submission some months ahead of the final one, and those are the hardest constraints in the year: a fifth of the grade depends on them and the school controls them. A student who leaves the investigation until content revision has started loses marks on both at once. The Diploma Programme coordinator holds the actual dates, so ask for them in writing at the start of DP2.

The Kingdom's calendar adds two wrinkles. International schools set their own term dates and most run three terms, while Ministry of Education schools run two semesters, so two children in the same compound can sit on different timetables all year. Ramadan shortens the school day and moves earlier each year against the Gregorian calendar, so it drifts across the Diploma course rather than landing twice in the same place. Both are reasons to agree the weekly slot in Saudi local time and review it each term.

sections.heading: Where Higher Level Biology marks are actually lost
paragraphs: The gap between a 5 and a 7 at Higher Level is rarely content. It is the difference between answering the question asked and answering the question recognised. Outline, describe and explain are not synonyms: outline wants the bare points, describe wants an account without reasons, explain wants the reasons themselves. Distinguish wants differences stated as pairs. Compare and contrast wants similarities as well as differences, and a candidate who supplies only differences has given away half the marks already.

Paper 1B is where candidates who revise by rereading notes come unstuck. The questions are built on experiments nobody has seen, and the marks go to students who can read an axis, spot a control, name a confounding variable and say plainly what the data do not show. Practising that is a separate activity from learning the themes, and most school schemes of work have no room for enough of it. A tutor can set one unfamiliar dataset a week and mark it to the published criteria.

In Paper 2 the extended responses carry the most recoverable marks on the paper. Candidates lose them by writing everything they know about a topic instead of building an argument the mark scheme can find. Strong answers are organised, use the right terminology once rather than circling it, and answer the command term in the opening sentence. This is teachable inside a few weeks, which is why it belongs at the end of the plan rather than the beginning.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation, and what a tutor may not touch
paragraphs: The scientific investigation is one independent investigation, up to 3,000 words, marked out of 24 against four criteria: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Each criterion is worth six marks, and the four are not equally easy to pick up. Research design marks are won before any data exist, in the quality of the question and the control of the variables. Evaluation marks are lost at the very end, when a tired candidate writes that the experiment went well.

What an outside tutor may do is narrow, and worth stating plainly. A tutor can teach the criteria, discuss a research question, ask why a variable is being controlled, show what a worked treatment of uncertainty looks like, and give feedback on a draft the student has already written. A tutor never writes, edits or redrafts assessed work, and anyone offering to is offering something the board treats as malpractice.

Schools supervise this work, and the supervision is part of the assessment. Your child's teacher signs that the work is the student's own, which is why a tutor's role has to be visible rather than hidden. Tell the school that an outside tutor is reading drafts; no honest school objects, and it protects the student if a question is ever raised. Keep the student's own drafts and raw data, dated, in one place. A trail showing that the investigation grew week by week is the simplest defence a family can hold, and it costs nothing to build while the work is happening rather than afterwards.

sections.heading: What in-home Higher Level Biology costs here, and what online changes
paragraphs: Rates in the Kingdom are advertised rather than published, and every figure below is somebody else's advertised rate. Tutoring platforms list general online tutoring from around SAR 55 an hour, and budget platforms advertise IGCSE one-to-one from around SAR 35. Tutor-marketplace guides to Riyadh put general private tuition for senior-school examination subjects above SAR 200 an hour. Tutoring-company listings for IB subjects start from around SAR 180, with Higher Level and premium tracks advertised nearer SAR 200 to 220.

What moves the number, roughly in order of weight: scarcity of the subject at the level asked for, marking or examining experience, the level itself, whether the tutor travels, and the length of the package. Higher Level Biology sits at the scarce end in most Saudi cities, because the pool of people who have taught the current guide to Higher Level is small and unevenly spread. In-home delivery adds travel to every hour, and in Riyadh or Jeddah traffic that cost is priced in.

Teaching online removes that travel line and replaces a local pool with a national one. The practical gain for a Biology family is not a discount, it is access to someone who has marked the extended responses their child keeps losing marks on. IB Gram quotes per family after the free trial lesson, because a DP2 candidate eight weeks out and a DP1 student in the autumn term need very different amounts of work. Home visits in the Kingdom are not something we sell; in-home teaching is a service we offer only in India.

sections.heading: What Saudi schools can and cannot staff at Higher Level
paragraphs: Private and international schools in the Kingdom hold licences from the Ministry of Education, and school evaluation and accreditation runs through the Education and Training Evaluation Commission, ETEC, which operates e-services for national school accreditation and for the approval of international accreditation bodies. None of that tells a parent whether a particular school can staff Higher Level Biology this year. A licence is permission to operate a school; it says nothing about how many Biology specialists the department has.

The practical picture is uneven. Diploma provision concentrates in Riyadh, Jeddah and the Dammam-Khobar-Dhahran cluster, with The KAUST School serving the Thuwal campus community and the International Schools Group running several Eastern Province campuses, not all of which offer the Diploma. Outside those centres a school may run the Diploma with a single Biology teacher covering Standard and Higher Level in one room. That teacher may be excellent. They are still one person with a timetable, and when they leave the Higher Level group is hardest to replace.

This is the real reason families here buy outside teaching, and it is worth asking the school directly rather than guessing. Ask how Higher Level Biology is staffed, whether the current guide is being taught, what happens to the group if a teacher leaves, and how many past papers the course plans to sit under timing. The answers are usually honest and occasionally uncomfortable. A school that cannot answer the last question has not planned its final term.

sections.heading: Moving into Higher Level Biology from another curriculum
paragraphs: Families in the Kingdom change schools more often than most, and Biology is one of the subjects where a switch shows. A student arriving from a British school with IGCSE Biology behind them usually has the content vocabulary and not the command terms. A student arriving from an American high school has often met more breadth and less depth, and finds the data-based questions unfamiliar. A student from a national-curriculum or CBSE background may be ahead on recall and behind on evaluating somebody else's method.

Timing decides what is recoverable. A move into DP1 during the autumn term is manageable with a term of targeted work on Theme A and Theme B. A move during DP2 is a different problem, because the scientific investigation travels badly: data collected under one school's supervision may not be accepted, and the new school's internal deadline may already have passed. Ask the receiving school, in writing, what it will take before the move is final.

What we do in the first month after a switch is diagnose rather than teach. A short set of questions across the four themes, one unfamiliar dataset, and a look at whatever investigation work exists. The output is a list of gaps, not a reassurance. Some of them close in a fortnight and some are a term's work. Telling the difference early lets a family decide whether to carry Higher Level Biology or ask the school about Standard Level while that choice is still open.
