sections.heading: Why two quotes for the same Higher Level hour differ by a factor of three
paragraphs: Ask three providers for Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level and the quotes will not cluster. The first thing separating them is what the word tutor means in each case. A university student who scored well in the subject three years ago, a current Diploma teacher, and somebody who has marked for a board are all sold under the same noun at wildly different prices, and only the third can tell you with authority what a mark scheme rewards.

The second separator is the component list. A tutor who has taught the Higher Level extensions, supervised explorations through to submission and worked Paper 3 under timing is doing four jobs. A tutor who covers the shared Standard Level content well is doing one of them, competently. Both can honestly advertise as a Higher Level tutor. Only one of them can take the hour that actually decides the grade, and the way to find out is to hand over a Paper 3 part and watch.

The third is overhead and travel. An agency loads its margin, an in-home tutor loads the journey, and a platform loads its payment and matching costs. None of that is improper, but none of it reaches the student either. A family deciding between a cheap quote and an expensive one is usually choosing between less specialism and more overhead rather than between two grades of teaching, which is why the component question is the one worth asking first.

sections.heading: What one Higher Level hour should contain before you buy a second
paragraphs: A first hour that produces nothing you can read afterwards was not a diagnostic, it was a conversation. The useful version samples across all four assessed pieces: a short non-calculator algebra run for Paper 1, a calculator question where method must still be shown for Paper 2, a Paper 3 opening to see whether the student can read a scaffold, and a look at whatever exploration work exists. That takes under an hour and it names the weak component instead of guessing.

The second thing an hour should produce is a correction the student can reuse without the tutor present. Marking in mark-scheme language does that: not a tick, but a note that the shape of the graph earned the method mark while the missing asymptote lost the accuracy one. A student who learns to read their own script that way buys fewer hours later, which is the opposite of what an hourly business is incentivised to deliver and the reason it is worth asking for.

The third is a plan with dates against it. Exploration milestones, the Paper 3 block, and the point in the second Diploma year where content coverage stops being the priority. None of that requires a long document. It requires somebody to have thought about the whole two years rather than next Tuesday, and it is a fair thing to expect from the top of the advertised range rather than from the bottom of it.

sections.heading: A Saudi evening slot against the tutor's own working week
paragraphs: The Kingdom's school week runs Sunday to Thursday. A tutor in London, Toronto or Mumbai works Monday to Friday or Monday to Saturday. The overlap is narrower than it looks, and it is where most weekly arrangements quietly fail: the family thinks they have bought fifty-two lessons and the tutor has agreed to a slot that sits at the dead end of their own day. Checking this before the first payment is cheaper than renegotiating it in the autumn term.

The second complication is that Arabia Standard Time never moves. The Kingdom sits at UTC+3 all year with no daylight saving, so a slot agreed in a tutor's local time will shift twice a year by an hour without anybody deciding to shift it. Book in Saudi local time and the problem is designed out. A tutor in a country that does change its clocks absorbs the drift instead, which is a small ask and worth making explicitly at the start.

The table below reads a 7.30pm Saudi slot from several common tutor locations, with their own working week beside it. It is not a ranking. A tutor in Amman or Cairo shares the Sunday-to-Thursday rhythm and will treat a Wednesday evening as a school night exactly as your child does. A tutor in India is reliably available at that hour but reaching the end of a long day. Knowing which you have changes what you ask for in week one.

sections.heading: Group set, small class or one-to-one: where the money goes
paragraphs: Group teaching is cheaper per hour and sometimes better. For content a whole set is meeting for the first time, four students and a good teacher is a defensible purchase, and the discussion adds something a single student talking to one adult does not get. Revision lectures on a named topic work the same way. If the thing being bought is exposition, splitting the cost across a group is sensible and the per-hour saving is real.

For everything diagnostic it inverts. The reason a student is losing marks in Paper 2 is specific to their script: they trust the calculator where method is required, or they round early, or they never label a sketch. None of that is visible in a group, and none of it is fixable by exposition. An hour spent reading one student's own working is the single highest-yield purchase at Higher Level, and it cannot be shared without becoming something else.

The practical answer for most Saudi families is a mixture, bought deliberately rather than by accident. Use the school for exposition, because it is already paid for. Use group revision for a topic the whole set finds hard. Buy one-to-one time for the weak component, the exploration and Paper 3, where the work is individual by definition. That spends the most money where the marks actually are instead of spreading it evenly across a syllabus the student mostly knows. Spread evenly is how most families spend, because it is the default.

sections.heading: Three ways Higher Level mathematics budgets get wasted here
paragraphs: The first is buying hours before buying a diagnosis. A family who feels behind books two lessons a week in the autumn term, and both lessons track whatever the class did that week. Six months later the spending is substantial and the weak component is untouched, because nobody ever asked which of the four pieces was failing. One well-constructed hour at the start redirects everything that follows, and it is the cheapest hour in the sequence.

The second is paying a specialist rate for generalist work. Higher Level pricing exists because the extensions are scarce. If the hour is spent on quadratics, trigonometric basics and homework supervision, the family is funding scarcity it is not consuming. That is sometimes the right call for a student whose foundations genuinely need rebuilding, but it should be a decision taken openly, with a cheaper tutor doing the foundation work and the specialist kept for the Higher Level content.

The third is leaving Paper 3 and the exploration to the last term. Together they are 40% of the grade, both are improvable, and both need lead time. Exploration work started late loses marks on presentation and reflection no amount of final-term spending recovers, and Paper 3 technique bought in the last six weeks competes with revision for every other subject. Spending the same money earlier buys more marks, which is the whole of the argument. Earlier is cheaper in a way that is unusual in education, and it is worth acting on.

sections.heading: What no fee buys at any price
paragraphs: Some things are not for sale and a provider offering them is telling you something. No tutor can promise a grade, a point total or a specific improvement, because the papers, the boundaries and the student's own performance on one morning are outside anyone's control. A tutor who quotes a guaranteed outcome against a fee is selling certainty that does not exist, and the price of that reassurance is usually the quality of the teaching beneath it.

Assessed work is the harder boundary. The exploration is marked in school as the student's own, and the school signs a declaration to that effect. A tutor may discuss whether a research question carries enough mathematics, may read a draft and name which criterion is weak, and may teach a technique the student has decided to use. No tutor may draft or supply text for assessed work, at any rate, and we decline that request when it is made.

Nor does any fee buy standing we do not have. IB Gram holds no accreditation, licence or partnership from the Ministry of Education, from the Education and Training Evaluation Commission, or from the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. There is no office in the Kingdom. What a fee buys is a specialist's hour, marked work between sessions, and a slot held in your own time zone. Anybody claiming more than that in this market is worth reading twice. Ask in writing what exactly the fee covers, and keep the answer.

faqs.question: How is the exploration weighted against the three written papers in Mathematics AA HL?
faqs.answer: The exploration carries 20% of the Higher Level grade against 30% for Paper 1, 30% for Paper 2 and 20% for Paper 3. It is marked in school from 20 marks across five criteria and then moderated externally, which makes it the equal of the third paper. It is also the only component whose timetable a student controls, so starting it early is the cheapest mark on the course.

faqs.question: What is the real difference between Paper 1 and Paper 2 in Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Both run two hours for 110 marks and both carry 30% of the grade, so the difference is technology rather than weight. Paper 1 permits none, which turns it into a test of exact algebra, identities, surds and hand-drawn sketches. Paper 2 allows a graphic display calculator throughout, which moves the difficulty to judgement: deciding which questions want a numerical answer and which still require method on the page to earn anything at all.

faqs.question: How many marks does each exploration criterion carry in Mathematics AA HL?
faqs.answer: Twenty marks are split across five criteria: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and the use of mathematics, with the last carrying the largest share. That distribution is the reason a beautifully written piece containing Standard Level statistics scores badly at Higher Level, while a rougher piece doing genuine Higher Level mathematics scores well. Reading a draft against each criterion separately, rather than as a whole, is how the gaps become visible.

faqs.question: Does a Higher Level Analysis and Approaches student sit a different Paper 1 from a Standard Level one?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Higher Level and Standard Level papers are separate examinations with different durations, mark totals and content coverage. Standard Level sits two papers of ninety minutes and eighty marks, each worth 40% of the grade, with no third paper. Higher Level sits two-hour papers for 110 marks apiece plus the Paper 3 investigation. A tutor who has only prepared students for the Standard Level papers has not prepared anyone for these.

faqs.question: What does commensurate with the level of the course mean for an AA HL exploration?
faqs.answer: It means the mathematics has to sit at the standard of the Higher Level syllabus rather than below it. A correlation coefficient and a scatter graph are Standard Level tools at best, and a Higher Level piece built on them loses marks in the criterion that carries the most. Work that uses calculus, complex numbers, vectors or a genuine proof clears the bar. Testing a research question against this before writing anything saves the most time of any single check.

faqs.question: How do Mathematics AA HL points combine with Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay in the Diploma total?
faqs.answer: Each of the six subjects is graded from one to seven, giving a maximum of 42, and up to three further points come from the combination of Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay. Mathematics therefore contributes at most seven points directly. Its wider effect is indirect: a student whose mathematics is unstable tends to lose time from every other subject, and a Higher Level grade that collapses can put a conditional offer out of reach.

faqs.question: What does the first hour with an online AA HL tutor need to establish?
faqs.answer: Which of the four assessed pieces is weakest, and on what evidence. That means sampling questions from all three papers and looking at whatever exploration work exists, rather than discussing how the student feels about mathematics. The hour should end with something written: a named weak component, one or two topics to repair, and a view on whether exploration work is on schedule. Without that, the second hour starts from the same guesswork as the first.

faqs.question: How many Higher Level mathematics lessons a week does a struggling first-year Diploma student need?
faqs.answer: Usually one, sometimes two short ones, and almost never more. One hour of specialist teaching plus marked work between sessions changes more than three hours of supervised practice, because the limiting factor at Higher Level is usually technique and notation rather than exposure. Two shorter sessions suit fluency repair, where practice between contacts matters. A student needing more than two hours a week of mathematics is usually in the wrong course rather than short of tuition.

faqs.question: How soon should a parent expect to see movement in Higher Level mathematics?
faqs.answer: Measurable movement on a specific component inside six to eight weeks is reasonable; a shift in the overall grade is not. Early progress shows up as questions the student can now finish unaided, fewer accuracy marks dropped, and sketches that carry their labels. Ask for that evidence rather than a predicted grade. Anybody offering a grade projection after a handful of hours is describing a sales position rather than a professional judgement about the May session.

faqs.question: What should an AA HL tutor's written feedback look like after a mock paper?
faqs.answer: Marks attributed to the scheme rather than a total: which method marks were earned, which accuracy marks were lost, and where a command term was misread. It should name two or three things to change, not twenty. It should also separate content failures from technique failures, because they need different work. Feedback that says revise calculus is not feedback; feedback that says you chose substitution where parts was faster, twice, is.

faqs.question: What happens when a student plateaus at a 5 in Analysis and Approaches HL?
faqs.answer: A plateau at that level is usually a technique ceiling rather than a content gap. The student knows the syllabus and keeps dropping accuracy marks, misreading command terms, or running out of time because routine algebra is slow. The work is timed practice on the specific failure, not another pass through the topics. Paper 3 is often the fastest lever here, because almost nobody practises it and twenty per cent of the grade sits inside it.

faqs.question: When in the first Diploma year should a student decide to move from AA HL to AA SL?
faqs.answer: The decision belongs to the school and has an internal deadline, so ask for that date in the autumn term rather than assuming it is late. The honest test is whether the Higher Level extensions are reachable with support or merely survivable, and whether holding the subject is costing marks in two others. Moving down is not a failure; carrying a Higher Level subject that absorbs every evening until the final term usually costs more than it earns.

faqs.question: What should a Year 11 student do in the months before the Higher Level course starts?
faqs.answer: Algebraic fluency, done without a calculator, and nothing else. Indices, surds, algebraic fractions, rearrangement, function notation and factorising at speed are what the first Higher Level term assumes and never revisits. Previewing calculus is the common instinct and the weaker investment, because the course teaches it properly anyway. Cheap pre-Diploma hours spent on manipulation reduce the number of expensive Higher Level hours needed later, which is the best return on this page.

faqs.question: How does Higher Level mathematics support change between the first and second Diploma years?
faqs.answer: In the first year the work is foundations and new content, and there is room to rebuild something older. In the second year that room is gone, so support becomes triage: secure the topics carrying the most marks, finish the exploration, and spend the remainder on paper technique. The spending profile changes too, because the final-term hours are the scarcest and least flexible, and they buy fewer marks than the same money spent a year earlier.

ib-dp-math-aa-sl-online-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Analysis and Approaches at Standard Level as their own subject, not as a sideline to a general maths timetable. Each has worked Paper 1 and Paper 2 question by question and marked an exploration against the criteria.

intro.heading: An AA SL tutor here is a scheduling problem before a teaching one
paragraphs: Families in Riyadh, Jeddah and the Eastern Province rarely begin this search because the mathematics is a mystery. They begin it because the week does not fit. The school day ends, the drive home takes what it takes, and by the time a Standard Level student opens Analysis and Approaches it is already evening. Add a tutor living in a country with a different working week and the lesson that looked obvious on paper never happens twice in a row. So this page opens with the clock, because an IB DP math AA SL online tutor in Saudi Arabia who cannot hold a stable slot teaches nothing.

The second discovery is that Analysis and Approaches at Standard Level is not the Higher Level course with the hard parts removed. It is a full syllabus built around five topics: number and algebra, functions, geometry and trigonometry, statistics and probability, and calculus, taught across roughly one hundred and fifty hours. Paper 1 is sat without a calculator and carries forty per cent of the grade. Paper 2 assumes a graphic display calculator and carries another forty. The mathematical exploration, produced by the student and marked at school, carries the remaining twenty.

The third discovery is that almost nobody plans the Diploma backwards. A family books help when a report card arrives, which is usually the wrong moment, because by then the content gap and the technique gap have merged into one problem that looks bigger than either. Counting backwards from the May session gives each stretch of the course a job. The first Diploma year secures algebra and functions. The summer break fixes an exploration question. The autumn term finishes calculus. The spring term belongs to whole papers under time, and none of that needs a year written on it.

What follows is mechanics rather than persuasion. Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, with a shared whiteboard so working stays visible line by line. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a Saudi address, and home visits are a service we offer only in India. A family in the Kingdom gets a specialist in this single course, free at a Sunday evening slot in Arabia Standard Time, rather than whoever happens to teach maths within a twenty-minute drive. That is the honest argument for online teaching, and it is the only one this page makes.

Read the sections in order if the week is your problem, or skip to the exploration if the draft is. Both lead to the same place: a Standard Level grade is built from two timed papers and one piece of coursework, and the thing that moves all three is regular contact with somebody who knows the mark schemes.

sections.heading: What this search is actually hiring for
paragraphs: Answer the literal query first. A family searching this phrase wants a named specialist in one Diploma course, available at a usable hour in the Kingdom, who knows what Paper 1 rewards and what the exploration criteria say. They are not looking for a general maths teacher. The phrase carries AA and SL for a reason: the parent has already found out that Analysis and Approaches is a different subject from Applications and Interpretation, and that comfort with one does not transfer to the other.

The job has four parts and they are not equally weighted. Keep class content from drifting out of reach, which means staying a fortnight ahead of the school's sequence rather than repairing it later. Build non-calculator fluency, because Paper 1 is where a Standard Level student most often loses marks to arithmetic rather than to ignorance. Teach the graphic display calculator as examined content in its own right. Support the exploration without ever becoming its author.

That fourth part is where a parent should listen hardest in a trial lesson. Internal assessment is twenty per cent of the grade and it is marked at school, which makes it the easiest component for a dishonest provider to promise and the hardest for a family to police. A tutor who answers by describing criteria, drafts and feedback is describing legitimate teaching. One who offers a finished piece is offering malpractice, and the school is obliged to act on it.

sections.heading: Arabia Standard Time and the Sunday-to-Thursday week
paragraphs: The Kingdom runs on Arabia Standard Time, UTC+3, and does not change its clocks. That single fact decides whether a weekly slot survives a full Diploma year. A tutor in a country that does change its clocks will drift by an hour twice a year unless the agreement is written in Saudi local time from the first lesson. Families who agree a slot in the tutor's time discover this in the week the tutor's clocks move, which is rarely a convenient week to lose.

The second factor is the tutor's own working week. School here runs Sunday to Thursday, with Friday and Saturday as the weekend. A tutor whose week runs Monday to Friday has a free Sunday, which is one of your prime teaching evenings, and a busy Thursday evening that you may also want. A tutor in India sits two and a half hours ahead, so a six o'clock Riyadh lesson lands at half past eight for them: late, but sustainable on a weekday.

A tutor in the United Kingdom sits two or three hours behind depending on their summer clock, so the same lesson falls inside their own school day in term time. A tutor on the eastern coast of the United States is seven or eight hours behind, which looks easy until you notice that your Sunday is their working Sunday. Elsewhere in the Gulf the week and the weekend match yours exactly, with no seasonal drift at all. Ask about the working week before the rate.

sections.heading: The AA SL year counted backwards from the May session
paragraphs: Saudi IB schools sit the May session. Working forwards from today produces a plan that runs out of road; working backwards from the session gives every stretch of the course a job. Almost nobody in this market publishes that plan, which is odd, because it is what a parent most wants and what a tutor can be held to. Your school's Diploma Programme coordinator holds the internal deadlines, and those matter more than any generic calendar because the exploration deadline is set by the school.

The sequencing logic is simple. Algebra and functions must be secure before calculus is taught, because most differentiation errors at Standard Level are algebra errors wearing a calculus hat. Statistics can be learned late without damage; calculus cannot. The exploration needs a question fixed before the second year begins, because a question chosen in the autumn term competes with content teaching for the same hours and usually loses. Timed papers need a clear run at the end, which only exists if content finished earlier.

One warning about terms. International and British-curriculum schools in the Kingdom set their own calendars and most run three terms, while Ministry of Education schools run two semesters from late August to late June. Two families in the same district can be on different schedules, and both will see their study pattern change during Ramadan as school days shorten. Use your own school's published calendar for dates, and use the table below for sequence.

sections.heading: Five topics, two papers, one exploration
paragraphs: Standard Level Analysis and Approaches is built from five topics. Number and algebra covers sequences, series, exponents, logarithms and the binomial theorem. Functions covers transformations, quadratics, rational functions and inverses. Geometry and trigonometry covers triangle work, radians, identities and equations. Statistics and probability covers data presentation, correlation and distributions. Calculus covers limits informally, differentiation, integration and kinematics. The course is designed for about one hundred and fifty teaching hours, so a school that loses half a term to staffing creates a real gap rather than an inconvenience.

Assessment is two written papers and one piece of internal assessment. Paper 1 is sat without a calculator and carries forty per cent. Paper 2 assumes a graphic display calculator and carries another forty. Both run ninety minutes at Standard Level, both move from short questions to longer structured ones, and both supply the formula booklet. The remaining twenty per cent is the mathematical exploration, individual written work marked by the teacher against published criteria and then moderated by the board.

There is no third paper at Standard Level. Paper 3 belongs to the Higher Level courses, so a tutor who mentions it while discussing an SL student has not read the syllabus they are being paid to teach. That is a fair thing to test in a trial lesson, alongside asking which formula booklet pages a student should know without looking, and which calculator functions are expected rather than optional on Paper 2. The answers are quick and they tell you a great deal.

sections.heading: Where Standard Level marks actually go missing
paragraphs: The most common Paper 1 loss is not a topic. It is exact-value work. A question asking for a surd, a fraction or an answer in terms of a logarithm is checking that a student can finish without a screen. Students who practised everything with a calculator reach the right method, then round, and the mark scheme pays nothing for that. This is trainable in weeks rather than months, which makes it the highest-return thing a tutor can do in the autumn term.

The second loss is notation in calculus. A derivative written without its variable, an integral without the constant, a chain rule applied without stating the inner function: each is a method mark the scheme awards and the student fails to claim. The fix is mechanical and slightly tedious, which is exactly why a student will not do it alone. The third loss is Paper 2 treated as the easy one, when it rewards choosing the right calculator function and quoting an answer to the required accuracy.

The fourth loss sits in statistics, where students read too quickly. Correlation described as causation, a regression line used outside its data range, a conditional probability answered as a joint one: all comprehension failures rather than mathematical ones. A tutor who marks past-paper work line by line finds these patterns inside three sessions, which is why a diagnostic built on the student's own scripts beats a generic placement test. Exam technique is a separate skill from content and has to be taught separately.

sections.heading: The exploration: what a tutor may do, and what no tutor may do
paragraphs: The mathematical exploration is twenty per cent of the AA SL grade and it is assessed work. It is marked by the teacher against five published criteria covering presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and the use of mathematics, with the mathematics criterion carrying the largest share. Students lose most marks in the middle criteria rather than the last, because they pick a question that is mathematically thin and then write about it well. A good tutor intervenes at the question stage, while help is still cheap.

Legitimate support looks like this: teaching the mathematics the chosen question requires, challenging whether that question is answerable in the page allowance, marking a draft against each criterion, and naming which criterion the draft is currently failing. A frank conversation about scale helps too. An exploration about something the student genuinely cares about scores better on personal engagement, and that criterion is close to impossible to fake convincingly.

What no tutor may do is produce the piece. No tutor should supply a finished write-up, insert their own calculations as the student's, or rewrite paragraphs until the voice is no longer the student's. The board treats that as malpractice and the school is obliged to act. Providers advertising completed coursework are selling a risk the family carries rather than a service. Keep your own record of what was discussed at each stage; it costs nothing and answers the only question that matters if the work is queried.

sections.heading: What AA SL tuition costs here, and what moves the number
paragraphs: Rates in this market are published by vendors rather than collected independently, so read every figure below as an advertised rate and not as an average. The table lists what providers in the Kingdom put on their own pages. None of it is IB Gram's price, and none of it predicts what a family ends up paying, because session frequency and package length move the final figure more than the headline rate does.

What drives the number, in rough order of weight: subject scarcity first, because a specialist in a course schools struggle to staff costs more everywhere; then examining or marking experience; then level, since Higher Level work is quoted above Standard Level and both above IGCSE; then whether the tutor travels, which loads an in-home rate with time nobody is teaching in; and finally package length. Analysis and Approaches at Standard Level sits mid-range rather than at the top of that spread.

One honest note on value. Two sessions a week across a whole Diploma year is a large commitment and often the wrong shape. A term of weekly work to secure algebra and functions, a lighter summer on the exploration question, then a dense block of timed papers before the May session usually costs less in total and matches how the course is examined. A provider recommending the same weekly pattern for every student, wherever they are in the course, is selling a subscription rather than teaching a syllabus.

faqs.question: Our child moved from a British school into Mathematics AA SL after a term of AS Mathematics - what actually carries over?
faqs.answer: Most of the pure content carries over intact, because AS Mathematics and AA SL overlap heavily on differentiation, integration of standard functions, trigonometric identities and sequences. What does not carry over is the exploration, which has no A-level equivalent, and the command-term style of the IB mark schemes. Expect four to six sessions on exploration method and paper technique, and far fewer on content. Ask the school which topics the set has already covered, because Diploma teaching order varies.

faqs.question: What does a student arriving from CBSE Class 10 need to close before Mathematics AA SL feels manageable?
faqs.answer: Usually less content than the family fears and more presentation than they expect. CBSE Class 10 algebra and trigonometry map onto AA SL well, so the gap sits in three places: working shown as a justified method rather than a result, exact-value answers without a calculator, and the written style the exploration needs. A term of weekly work normally clears all three. The harder adjustment is that an IB mark scheme pays for the route taken.

faqs.question: Can a student move down from Mathematics AA HL to AA SL partway through the Diploma, and what is lost?
faqs.answer: Schools do allow it, usually with a deadline tied to their own reporting rather than to the board. Content-wise little is lost, because SL is a subset of the HL syllabus, so the student is normally ahead rather than behind. What is lost is Higher Level mathematics on the transcript, which some overseas engineering and mathematics courses ask for at Higher Level specifically. Check the university requirements before the school's deadline, not after it.

faqs.question: Which Mathematics AA SL topic bites first for a student arriving from an American Algebra 2 course?
faqs.answer: Trigonometry in radians, almost every time. An Algebra 2 background usually gives solid function work and reasonable algebra, but degrees-first teaching leaves radian measure, identities and trigonometric equations feeling foreign just as calculus starts to need them. Logarithm manipulation is a close second. Both are short, teachable gaps rather than year-long deficits, and a diagnostic on the student's own class test shows which of the two is the real problem.

faqs.question: Is it better to switch from Mathematics AI SL to AA SL, or to stay with AI and strengthen the exploration instead?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on where the student is going. If a course they want asks for Analysis and Approaches, switching early is worth the disruption. If the destination accepts either route, staying put and spending the same hours on the exploration and on exam technique usually produces a better grade, because the switch costs a term of catch-up on algebraic manipulation. Decide against a written university requirement rather than an impression.

faqs.question: Why do so few schools in the Kingdom run Mathematics AA at Standard Level alongside AI in the same block?
faqs.answer: Staffing and class size. Running both routes at both levels needs four separate sets and specialists for each, which only works where the Diploma cohort is large. Smaller cohorts here usually offer one route at both levels and the other at one level, and some offer AI alone because it timetables more easily against science options. Ask which combinations the school has actually run in recent cohorts.

faqs.question: What happens to a Mathematics AA SL set when a school loses its only specialist mid-course?
faqs.answer: The usual sequence is cover teaching from inside the department, then a recruitment process that takes a term or longer. Content delivery often continues, but two things slip: the pace through calculus, and exploration supervision, because a cover teacher is reluctant to advise on a draft they did not set up. That is the situation where outside support pays for itself. Tell the tutor what happened so the plan attacks the gap.

faqs.question: How do I check whether my child's school actually enters candidates for Mathematics AA SL rather than AI?
faqs.answer: Ask the Diploma Programme coordinator for the subject sets running in the current cohort, in writing, and for the mathematics routes that appeared in the previous two cohorts. A school can be authorised to run the Diploma and still not timetable every route every year. Course selection documents sometimes list all four mathematics options as available in principle while the timetable supports two.

faqs.question: Does an ETEC evaluation tell me anything useful about how well a school teaches Mathematics AA SL?
faqs.answer: Only indirectly. Private and international schools in the Kingdom are licensed by the Ministry of Education, and school evaluation and accreditation processes run through the Education and Training Evaluation Commission. Those processes look at the school as an institution rather than at one Diploma set, so they say little about who stands in front of your child. For that, ask about the teacher's own subject degree.

faqs.question: Before we enrol, what should we ask a Saudi school about who teaches its Mathematics AA SL set?
faqs.answer: Four questions. Who teaches the set, and is mathematics their degree subject? Has anyone in the department examined or moderated for the board? How many students are in the set, since a set of six and a set of twenty-six are different courses in practice? And what is the internal deadline structure for the exploration? The last answer tells you most about how organised the department is.

faqs.question: What time does a Mathematics AA SL lesson usually run for a student on a Sunday-to-Thursday school week?
faqs.answer: Most families settle between five and eight in the evening, Sunday to Wednesday, with Thursday kept lighter because the weekend starts that night. Riyadh families in the outer districts often push to seven because of the drive. Earlier slots work better for compound and camp families, where activities sit close to home. Two shorter sessions usually beat one long one, because non-calculator fluency responds to frequency.

faqs.question: Our tutor is in the United Kingdom - how does a Mathematics AA SL slot survive their clock change?
faqs.answer: By writing the slot in Arabia Standard Time from the first lesson and never in the tutor's time. The Kingdom is UTC+3 and does not change its clocks, so when the United Kingdom moves theirs the gap shifts from three hours to two and back again. If the agreement says six in the evening Riyadh time, nothing moves for you and the tutor adjusts their diary instead.

faqs.question: Do Mathematics AA SL lessons continue through the shortened school days of Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, usually with the slot moved rather than paused. School days shorten and evening routines change, so many families switch to a later start or to two shorter sessions instead of one. Because the dates move against the Gregorian calendar each year, agree the revised pattern a few weeks ahead with the tutor rather than assuming the previous arrangement still fits. Content teaching normally slows while past-paper marking holds up.

faqs.question: How many weeks before the May session should Mathematics AA SL past-paper work move to two sessions a week?
faqs.answer: Around eight to ten weeks out, and only once content teaching has genuinely finished. Moving earlier means sitting papers on material the class has not covered, which teaches a student that they cannot do the subject rather than teaching them the subject. The useful pattern is one Paper 1 and one Paper 2 a week, each marked and returned with a written fault list.

ib-dp-math-ai-hl-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors listed below teach Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level, which is not the same job as teaching Analysis and Approaches. Each has taken students through Paper 3 and has marked an exploration against the five published criteria.

intro.heading: A capable AI HL student can still finish on a grade nobody expected
paragraphs: The pattern is familiar to anyone who has taught this course. A student follows every lesson, does the homework, understands the statistics and then produces a mock result two grades below what the class work suggested. Almost always the cause is not understanding. It is four specific failures: a conclusion written in the wrong register after a hypothesis test, graph theory and matrix content met once and never revisited, Paper 3 treated as a longer Paper 2, and an exploration that answers a thin question beautifully. An IB DP math AI HL tutor in Saudi Arabia who starts anywhere else is guessing.

Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level runs on four assessed components. Paper 1 is two hours of shorter questions and carries thirty per cent. Paper 2 is two hours of extended response and carries another thirty. Paper 3 is a single hour containing two long problem-solving questions and carries twenty. The mathematical exploration, written by the student and marked at school, carries the final twenty. Every paper assumes a graphic display calculator, which is why calculator technique is examined content here rather than a convenience.

The content that separates Higher Level from Standard Level in this course is unusually concentrated. Matrices, eigenvalues and transition matrices, graph theory with adjacency matrices and spanning trees, complex numbers in polar form, non-linear regression, formal hypothesis testing and differential equations solved with Euler's method all sit above the Standard Level line. None of them appear in a student's earlier schooling, so there is no prior fluency to fall back on when a paper applies two of them at once.

Repair has an order, and the order is set by the May session that Saudi IB schools sit. Hypothesis-test write-up is a two-session fix and should happen first because it recurs on every paper. Graph theory and matrices need a block of teaching rather than revision. Paper 3 technique only works once the content behind it exists. The exploration question has to be settled before the second year starts, because after that it competes with content teaching for the same evenings.

Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, timed to Arabia Standard Time so the slot does not drift when a tutor's own country changes its clocks. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in the Kingdom; home visits are a service we offer only in India. What a family gets instead is somebody who has taught this specific course, which matters more in AI HL than in almost any other Diploma subject. A capable mathematician who has never marked an AI Paper 3 will teach the content accurately and still miss the register the mark scheme pays for, and that distinction is the whole argument for choosing a specialist rather than the nearest available graduate.

sections.heading: The four places AI HL marks actually go
paragraphs: Start with the hypothesis test, because it recurs on every paper. A student runs a chi-squared test or a two-sample t-test on the calculator, reads off the p-value, and writes that the result is significant. The mark scheme wants the comparison stated, the null hypothesis named, and the conclusion returned to the context of the question. Three marks are available and most students claim one. This is a register problem rather than a statistics problem, and it is fixable in two sessions.

Second, the Higher Level content that appears once. Graph theory, matrices and eigenvalues, and complex numbers in polar form are usually taught in a single run and then not revisited until revision. By then the vocabulary has gone: a student who can invert a matrix cannot say what an eigenvector is for. Papers apply these topics in combination, so partial recall produces partial answers and the method marks go unclaimed.

Third, Paper 3 treated as a longer Paper 2. It is not: two extended problems in sixty minutes, each building through parts that depend on earlier answers, usually around an unfamiliar context. Fourth, the exploration, where students answer a thin question well instead of a reasonable question adequately. Each of these four has a different fix and a different place in the year, which is what the rest of this page sets out. Treating them as one problem called revision is why a term of extra lessons sometimes moves nothing at all.

sections.heading: Paper 3, component by component
paragraphs: The table below sets out the four components, what each one weighs, and the loss each one is known for. Read the final column first. A student who recognises their own pattern there has already saved a term of general revision, because the repair for a carried-forward arithmetic slip looks nothing like the repair for missing content.

Paper 3 deserves particular attention because it is the component where class ranking and examination ranking diverge most. Sixty minutes for two long problems means a student who spends twenty-five minutes on the first part of question one has lost the paper before reading question two. The questions are deliberately set in contexts nobody has taught: a traffic model, a disease spread, a network of pipelines. The mathematics is on the syllabus; the setting is not meant to be familiar.

The technique is teachable and it is specific. Read the whole question before starting, because the later parts tell you what the earlier ones are for. Write down what each symbol in the stem means. Expect to carry a result forward, and expect to be asked to comment on whether the model is reasonable. That last instruction is worth marks, and it is the one students leave blank when time runs short. Practice under a real clock is the only thing that fixes it, and six or seven timed attempts across a term is usually enough to change the habit. Marking them together afterwards matters more than sitting them, because the useful information is where the clock ran out rather than what the final total was.

sections.heading: Hypothesis tests: the write-up is the mark scheme
paragraphs: Formal hypothesis testing is Higher Level content in this course and it is where the gap between calculator fluency and examination credit is widest. The calculator does the arithmetic in seconds. What earns marks is everything around it: stating the null and alternative hypotheses in the language of the context, naming the test and the significance level, comparing the p-value to that level explicitly, and then writing a conclusion that mentions the thing being tested rather than the statistics.

The chi-squared test attracts particular trouble. Students confuse the goodness-of-fit test with the test for independence, use the wrong degrees of freedom, or quote an expected frequency below five without comment. Each is a one-mark habit rather than a misunderstanding. The two-sample t-test brings its own: a one-tailed alternative written as two-tailed, or a conclusion claiming the means are equal when the test can only fail to find a difference.

The fix is mechanical. Write the same five lines every time, in the same order, until the shape is automatic, and have them marked against a real mark scheme rather than against a textbook answer. Three sessions of this across a term typically recovers more marks than three weeks of new content, which is why it sits first in the repair order rather than last. It also improves the exploration, where the same write-up discipline is assessed under the mathematical communication criterion. A student who has learned to state hypotheses properly on a paper writes a far more defensible statistical section in their own project, so the two pieces of work stop competing for the same effort.

sections.heading: Graph theory, matrices and the content with no SL equivalent
paragraphs: Several Higher Level topics in this course have no Standard Level version at all, which means a student cannot lean on half-remembered earlier work. Graph theory covers adjacency matrices, walks and paths, minimum spanning trees, the Chinese postman problem and the travelling salesman problem with its upper and lower bounds. Matrices cover multiplication, inverses, determinants, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, and transition matrices used to model systems that settle towards a steady state.

These topics share two features. They are vocabulary-heavy, so a student who half-remembers the definitions cannot start the question, and they are algorithmically precise, so a method applied almost correctly earns almost nothing. A spanning tree built by eye rather than by a stated algorithm is marked as a guess. An eigenvector quoted without showing the equation it satisfies loses the method marks even when the numbers are right.

In a small Higher Level set these are also the topics most likely to be taught thinly, because they come late and because a teacher covering both AI levels at once is under real pressure. That is the specific reason families in smaller Saudi cities reach for outside help here. A block of teaching rather than revision is what these need: new content properly taught, then revisited twice before the spring term so the vocabulary survives. A useful test for a parent is to ask the student to define an adjacency matrix and a spanning tree without notes. If either definition is vague, the topic has been met rather than learned, and no amount of past-paper practice will close that on its own.

sections.heading: Differential equations, Euler's method and arithmetic discipline
paragraphs: The calculus strand at Higher Level in this course ends somewhere students rarely expect: coupled differential equations, phase portraits, and numerical solutions by Euler's method. Conceptually none of it is beyond a capable student. Procedurally it is unforgiving, because Euler's method is an iterative calculation where an error in the second step quietly corrupts every line after it and the final answer looks plausible.

Marks here are lost to layout rather than to mathematics. A student who works down a tidy table of steps, with the step size written at the top and each column labelled, can check their own arithmetic and can show an examiner the method even when a value is wrong. A student working across a page in loose lines cannot. The same applies to slope fields, where a sketch drawn without reference to the stationary behaviour earns little however neat it looks.

Phase portraits for coupled systems reward one specific habit: finding the eigenvalues first and saying what they imply about the trajectories before drawing anything. Students who draw first and justify afterwards tend to produce a picture that cannot be defended. These are all teachable routines, and they are the reason a tutor who has actually taught this strand is worth more than one who knows the mathematics but has never marked it. A graduate who studied differential equations at university solved them analytically and may never have met a numerical table at all, so ask directly whether they have taught Euler's method to a Diploma class rather than whether they know what it is.

sections.heading: The exploration at Higher Level, and what no tutor may do
paragraphs: The exploration carries twenty per cent of the AI HL grade and is marked at school against five published criteria: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection, and the use of mathematics. The last criterion carries the largest share and is where Higher Level students are judged hardest, because mathematics judged commensurate with the course has to be genuinely at Higher Level. A well-written statistical summary that any Standard Level student could have produced will not score there.

Legitimate support is specific. A tutor may teach the mathematics the chosen question requires, press on whether the question is answerable within the page allowance, mark a draft against each criterion in turn, and name which criterion the draft is currently failing. Suggesting that a student look for a richer data set, or that a model needs a second variable, is teaching. Writing the analysis is not.

What no tutor may do is produce the piece. No tutor should supply a finished write-up, insert their own calculations as the student's, or edit the prose until the voice has changed. The board treats that as malpractice and a school is obliged to act on it, with consequences that fall on the candidate rather than on the provider who sold it. Keep a simple record of what each session covered; it costs nothing and settles the question if the work is ever queried. Providers in this market advertising finished coursework are selling a risk the candidate carries alone.

sections.heading: The repair order, counted back from the May session
paragraphs: Saudi IB schools sit the May session, so the repair plan runs backwards from there rather than forwards from today. The order is set by how often each fault recurs and by how long it takes to fix. Hypothesis-test write-up is first because it appears on every paper and takes two or three sessions. Graph theory and matrices come second because they need teaching rather than revision and the teaching has to happen while there is still time to revisit it.

Paper 3 technique comes third, and only once the content behind it exists, because practising problem solving on topics a student has not learned teaches them that they cannot do the subject. The exploration runs on its own track, governed by the school's internal deadlines rather than by the board, and the question should be fixed before the second year starts. Your school's Diploma Programme coordinator holds those dates and they differ between schools in the same city.

Calendar practicalities matter too. International and British-curriculum schools here mostly run three terms and set their own dates, while Ministry of Education schools run two semesters from late August to late June. Study patterns shift during Ramadan as school days shorten, so the sensible move is to agree a revised lesson pattern a few weeks ahead rather than to lose a month. In the final eight weeks nothing new is taught: two timed papers a week, marked, with the fault list driving what gets reviewed.

faqs.question: Which Mathematics AI HL topics have no Standard Level equivalent at all?
faqs.answer: Graph theory, matrices with eigenvalues and eigenvectors, complex numbers in polar and exponential form, non-linear regression, formal hypothesis testing, and differential equations solved by Euler's method or treated as coupled systems. None has a Standard Level counterpart, so a student cannot fall back on earlier work when a question combines two of them. These are also the topics most often taught thinly in a small Higher Level set, which is why they dominate requests for outside teaching.

faqs.question: Why do strong AI HL students score worst on Paper 3?
faqs.answer: Because it rewards a skill the other papers do not test. Paper 3 is sixty minutes for two long problems set in unfamiliar contexts, each building through parts that depend on earlier answers. A student used to recognising question types finds nothing to recognise, spends too long on the first part, and leaves the second question unstarted. Classroom strength does not transfer without timed practice on the real thing.

faqs.question: Where does weak algebra still cost marks in Mathematics AI HL when every paper allows a calculator?
faqs.answer: In rearrangement and substitution, mostly. A calculator solves an equation you can state; it does not help you form one from a worded model, change the subject of a formula with three variables, or simplify before substituting into an iterative method. Weak algebra also shows up in matrix work, where showing the equation an eigenvector satisfies earns the method marks. The calculator removes arithmetic, not structure.

faqs.question: What does an AI HL mark scheme want in the conclusion to a chi-squared test?
faqs.answer: Four things, all short. Name the test and the significance level. State the null hypothesis in the language of the context, not in symbols alone. Compare the p-value to the significance level explicitly, with the direction stated. Then write a conclusion about the thing being tested, saying there is or is not sufficient evidence of an association. Writing that the result is significant, and stopping, claims one of the available marks.

faqs.question: Which AI HL topic is most often rushed at the end of the course?
faqs.answer: Differential equations, and particularly coupled systems and phase portraits. They sit at the end of the calculus strand, they arrive when mock examinations are competing for teaching time, and they are the hardest strand to self-teach from a textbook. Graph theory runs a close second for the same reason. Both reward a proper block of teaching rather than revision, which means starting them earlier than the scheme of work suggests.

faqs.question: How much of Mathematics AI HL is memory and how much is calculator technique?
faqs.answer: Less memory than students assume, because the formula booklet carries most of what they try to learn. The real load is knowing which calculator function answers which question, entering a model without transcription errors, and interpreting the output in a sentence. Definitions are the exception: graph theory and matrix vocabulary has to be known cold, because a student who cannot say what an eigenvector represents cannot begin the question.

faqs.question: What qualification should I look for in a Mathematics AI HL tutor rather than an AA one?
faqs.answer: A mathematics or statistics degree is the baseline, but the discriminating question is teaching history. Ask how many AI Higher Level cohorts they have taken through Paper 3, and ask them to describe the difference between the goodness-of-fit and independence versions of the chi-squared test. An AA specialist may be a stronger mathematician and still be unfamiliar with the modelling and statistics this course is assessed on.

faqs.question: How do I verify that a tutor has actually taught AI HL Paper 3 rather than AI SL?
faqs.answer: Ask what Paper 3 contains, in detail. The honest answer names two extended problems, sixty minutes, twenty per cent of the grade, and unfamiliar contexts. Then ask how they prepare a student for a question part that depends on a previous answer the student got wrong. Somebody who has taught it will talk about carried-forward marks immediately. Somebody who has not will talk about revision in general terms.

faqs.question: Should a Mathematics AI HL student have a tutor who has examined for the board?
faqs.answer: It helps more in this course than in most, because so many AI HL marks sit in how an answer is written rather than in whether it is right. Somebody who has marked knows what a conclusion needs, how carried-forward credit works, and what an examiner does with a correct answer and no method. It is not essential, and it is worth checking rather than assuming: ask which component and which level they marked.

faqs.question: Our AI HL tutor is strong on statistics but weak on graph theory - what do we do?
faqs.answer: Say so early, and treat it as a scope problem rather than a competence problem. The practical options are to add a short block with a second tutor for the discrete topics, or to change tutor if the gap covers more than one strand. Either is better than hoping it resolves, because graph theory and matrices carry real weight across Papers 1 and 2 and the vocabulary cannot be learned in revision week.

faqs.question: What should we ask in a trial lesson to test an AI HL tutor's grasp of matrices?
faqs.answer: Hand them a transition matrix question and watch what they do first. A tutor who sets up the steady-state equation and explains what the eigenvector means in context is teaching the examined content. One who reaches straight for the calculator and reads off a number is showing you the thing your child already does. Ask them to mark one of your child's attempts aloud, which reveals more than any explanation.

faqs.question: What may a tutor do with a Mathematics AI HL exploration draft, and what may they never do?
faqs.answer: A tutor may teach the mathematics the question needs, question whether it is answerable in the page allowance, mark the draft against each of the five criteria, and name which criterion is currently failing. A tutor may not supply a finished write-up, insert their own calculations as the student's, or edit the prose until the voice has changed. The board treats that as malpractice and the consequences fall on the candidate.

faqs.question: Which exploration criterion do AI HL students most often lose marks on?
faqs.answer: The use of mathematics, because at Higher Level the mathematics has to be commensurate with the course. A clean statistical summary that a Standard Level student could have produced scores poorly there however well it is written. Reflection is the second weak point: students describe what they did instead of evaluating what the result means and where the model breaks. Both are decided by the question chosen, which is why the question stage matters most.

faqs.question: Can a tutor suggest the data set for a Mathematics AI HL exploration?
faqs.answer: Suggesting where to look is teaching; choosing on the student's behalf is not. A tutor can reasonably say that a data set is too small for the test being planned, that a published source would be more defensible than a survey of friends, or that a second variable would allow Higher Level techniques. The student makes the choice and should be able to explain why, because personal engagement is assessed and cannot be borrowed.

intro.heading: Where your child sits in the Diploma year decides what to buy
paragraphs: A home tutor is a mode of delivery, not a diagnosis. Before the question of who comes to the house, there is a more useful question: what point in the two-year Diploma has your child reached, and what does AI SL demand at that point? A student eight weeks into the first year needs the algebra and number work the course assumes and skips. A student in the second autumn is holding new content and an exploration at once. A student in the spring term has a mock result and a short run of weeks to act on it.

Those three students need different tutors, different session lengths and different numbers of hours. Buying a generic weekly hour because it was available locally is the most common way a Saudi family spends money on Diploma mathematics without changing a grade. Buying the right eight weeks is often cheaper and always more effective. That is the argument this page makes before it says anything about delivery. It is also the question most providers skip, because an open-ended weekly booking is easier to sell than a defined block with an end date in it. Ask any tutor how many sessions they expect to need and what they will have fixed by the end of them.

On delivery, IB Gram is plain. Teaching is one-to-one and happens over live video, pinned to Arabia Standard Time. No IB Gram tutor will travel to a Saudi address; in-home visits are a service we offer only in India. What that buys a family here is the pool: instead of choosing from the people who can reach your compound before seven, you choose from people who teach Applications and Interpretation as their subject, wherever they live. In a country where Diploma mathematics teaching clusters in three cities, that is the whole difference.

It also matters because families in the Kingdom move. A posting changes from Jubail to Riyadh, a campus contract ends, a parent transfers from Al Khobar to Jeddah. A tutor attached to a neighbourhood is lost in that move, usually in the middle of a term. A tutor attached to a timetable is not. The same person carries on through the second Diploma year, which matters most for the exploration, where continuity of supervision is worth more than any single lesson.

We are an independent tutoring platform. IB Gram holds no licence, accreditation or partnership from the IB, from Cambridge, from Pearson, or from the Ministry of Education, and no school named on this page has any connection with us. No tutor can promise a grade or a university place. What a specialist can do is tell you which part of AI SL is costing marks, and roughly how long it takes to fix.

sections.heading: Start from the stage, not from the search term
paragraphs: AI SL runs over two years and is examined once, so the same subject needs three different kinds of teaching depending on when you start. In the first two terms the useful work is foundational: a student who cannot rearrange a formula confidently will meet that weakness again in functions, then in calculus, then in the exploration. Fixing it early costs a handful of sessions. Ignoring it means paying for the same gap four times in different disguises.

By the second autumn the picture changes. New content arrives while the exploration is being drafted and the school is collecting evidence for predicted grades, which is the heaviest term of the Diploma for most students. A tutor here is doing two jobs at once, and a family that books a single weekly hour usually finds it absorbed entirely by whatever is due that week. Two shorter sessions, one for content and one for the exploration, works better than one long one.

From the spring term onwards the job is narrow and measurable. A marked mock script says exactly which topics and which command terms cost marks, and a short block aimed only at those is the best-value tutoring a Diploma family ever buys. The test of a tutor at this stage is whether they ask for the script before quoting. Anyone who proposes a full syllabus recap in the final term has not looked at the evidence and is selling hours rather than teaching.

sections.heading: What an in-home AI SL tutor in the Kingdom actually involves
paragraphs: The in-home market is real and worth describing honestly. A tutor who drives to a family is paid for the travel as well as the teaching, whether that is stated as a higher hourly rate or billed separately, and tutor-marketplace guides put general Riyadh private tuition for senior-school examination subjects at SAR 200 and above, with travel loading on top. Evening traffic across a city an hour wide turns a sixty-minute lesson into a three-hour commitment for the tutor, and that is priced in.

The harder constraint is the pool. A family hiring within a drive radius is choosing from the people who happen to live nearby and happen to teach mathematics. The chance that one of them teaches Applications and Interpretation specifically, knows the difference between its two papers, and has marked explorations against the criteria is low in Riyadh and lower everywhere else. Outside the three main population centres, there is often nobody to choose from at all.

So IB Gram does this differently. Teaching is one-to-one over live video, pinned to Saudi local time, and home visits are a service we offer only in India. The honest case for that is not convenience: it is that a student in Najran or Yanbu gets the same named AI SL teacher a student in Al Olaya does, past papers and mark schemes are shared on screen as they are worked through, and nothing is lost to a commute at either end of the lesson.

sections.heading: Three terms, two semesters, one city
paragraphs: Two schools on the same Riyadh road can run different years. Ministry of Education schools follow a two-semester calendar that opens in late August and closes in late June, with an autumn break, a midyear break and a break for Eid Al Fitr. International and British-curriculum schools set their own calendars and most run three terms, which means different half-terms, different mock weeks and different exploration deadlines from the school next door.

For a family with children in two systems, that is a scheduling problem rather than a curiosity. One child's break week is the other's assessment week, and a single weekly slot cannot serve both. It also means no page on the internet can tell you when your child's exploration draft is due. The only reliable source is the calendar your own school publishes, and the Diploma Programme coordinator who maintains it.

The practical approach is to collect three dates at the start of each term: the mock window, the internal exploration deadlines, and the week the school breaks. Everything else can be planned around them. A tutor who asks for those three dates in the first conversation is thinking about the year; one who offers a package of hours without asking is selling a product that may sit entirely inside a holiday. Two further details are worth having early: whether the school runs its mock before or after the long midyear break, since that decides whether revision happens in term time or in a holiday, and whether the exploration draft deadline sits before or after the mock. Schools in the same city routinely answer those two questions differently, and the order changes which piece of work a family should pay for first.

sections.heading: Moving into AI SL from another curriculum
paragraphs: Mathematics transfers worse than any other subject on a mid-course move, because the order differs even where the content matches. A student arriving from an Extended IGCSE course has most of the algebra AI SL assumes and almost none of its statistical reasoning: chi-squared testing, regression, confidence intervals and the judgement about which to use are new, and they arrive quickly. A Core-tier candidate has a larger gap and needs it named rather than discovered in a test.

A student from an American high school usually brings strong graphical and calculator work and a looser habit with algebraic form, which is a good fit for AI SL and a poor one for Analysis and Approaches. A student from a British A-level start brings the opposite. A student arriving from India meets two changes at once: Cambridge's February and March series is an India-only sitting, so the entry pattern shifts to June and November, and the command-term discipline of IB marking is unfamiliar.

In every case the first job is a written gap list, not a course recap. One diagnostic session across number, functions and data handling will show which strands are missing, and a short sequence closes them while the class carries on. Three or four weeks of targeted work is usually enough for a transfer into the first Diploma year. A move during the second year needs the school's topic list as well, because what matters is what the class has already covered.

sections.heading: What a Saudi school can and cannot staff in Diploma mathematics
paragraphs: Private and international schools in the Kingdom are licensed by the Ministry of Education, and school evaluation and accreditation runs through the Education and Training Evaluation Commission, which operates e-services for national school accreditation and for the approval of international accreditation bodies. A school authorised to run the Diploma has satisfied those processes. None of it guarantees that the school can put a specialist in front of every mathematics class every year.

Staffing is the gap families notice. A school may list four mathematics routes and run two. Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level is the one most reliably offered, because it carries the largest numbers; the Higher Level version and Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level are the ones that quietly disappear when a teacher leaves mid-contract. Combined classes are the usual response, with two courses taught in one room by one teacher at two levels.

Before enrolling, or before accepting a course allocation, ask three questions in writing. Which mathematics courses actually ran last year, not which are listed in the prospectus. Will this course be taught as a separate class or combined with another. And who will supervise the exploration. The answers tell you more about your child's likely grade than any inspection summary does, and they tell you whether outside teaching is a convenience or a necessity. There is no shame in a school admitting it cannot run a course this year; the schools that handle it well say so early and help families plan around it. The ones to worry about are those that list a course, allocate students to it, and then teach it inside another class without telling anybody what has changed.

sections.heading: Repairing the mathematics AI SL assumes and never reteaches
paragraphs: AI SL has a prior-knowledge list the course expects and does not cover. Index laws, rearranging a formula with the unknown in two places, percentage change compounded over several periods, right-angled trigonometry, reading function notation as a machine rather than as decoration, and arithmetic with standard form. None of it is difficult. All of it is assumed from the first week, and a student who is shaky on two or three items spends the year half a step behind without ever failing a topic outright.

The symptoms are recognisable. A student who understands the model but cannot make the algebra give up the value they need. A student whose answers are right to three significant figures and wrong to two. A student who can read a graph on the calculator screen and cannot say what the gradient means in the units of the question. These read as carelessness on a report card and they are not; they are missing foundations.

Repair work is cheap and fast when it is targeted. A diagnostic across those six areas takes twenty minutes, and most students need two or three of them rather than all six. Two or three sessions close them, after which the weekly slot can go back to current content. The mistake is treating the whole of IGCSE mathematics as the revision target, which wastes a term and tells the student their problem is much bigger than it actually happens to be.

sections.heading: Fitting an AI SL slot around Ramadan, breaks and the school day
paragraphs: Ramadan drifts roughly eleven days earlier each year against the Gregorian calendar, so it lands in a different part of the academic year each time and cannot be planned for once. School days shorten, evenings reorganise, and the useful move is to keep the slot and change its shape: a shorter session, later in the evening, aimed at review rather than new content. Dropping the slot entirely for the month is what costs momentum.

The breaks need the same treatment. A two-semester school has an autumn break and a midyear break; a three-term school has half-terms that fall elsewhere. Pausing a weekly slot across a break is reasonable, but say so in advance, because a slot abandoned without notice is usually gone. Where a break lands shortly before a mock, the better use is a short block inside it rather than a pause.

On notice, be concrete with whoever you book. Agree how much warning a permanent change of slot needs, what happens to a single cancelled lesson, and how a clash with a school trip or an internal examination is handled. These are the arrangements that decide whether a year of tutoring is twenty-eight lessons or nineteen, and the difference is far larger than any hourly rate negotiation. One more point is worth settling at the start: who tells whom when a lesson will not happen, and by what route. A message to a tutor's phone the hour before is not a cancellation policy, and a family that has agreed the route in writing never has the argument about a lesson nobody attended.
