faqs.question: What transfers into AI SL from a national-curriculum mathematics course?
faqs.answer: Arithmetic, basic algebra and right-angled trigonometry transfer well. What rarely transfers is the statistical reasoning AI SL leans on, and the habit of using a graphic display calculator as a working tool rather than a checker. Students also meet assessment language they have not seen, where the command term decides how much working is expected. A diagnostic across data handling and function notation finds the real gap in one session.

faqs.question: Is a move from Extended IGCSE mathematics into AI SL or into AA SL the easier one?
faqs.answer: AI SL is usually the gentler transfer, because Extended IGCSE already covers much of the algebra it assumes, and the new material is statistical rather than abstract. Analysis and Approaches asks for proof and non-calculator fluency that IGCSE touches lightly. The exception is a student who enjoys manipulation and dislikes data work, for whom the statistics strand of AI SL is the harder adjustment despite the easier reputation.

faqs.question: Our child joins a Saudi IB school partway through the first Diploma year, so what does catching up in AI SL involve?
faqs.answer: First, the school's topic list for the year so far, because the order differs between schools even where the syllabus does not. Then a diagnostic to separate what was taught elsewhere from what was missed entirely. Most mid-year arrivals need three or four targeted sessions on one or two strands rather than a general recap. The exploration is the part to settle early, since timelines are already running.

faqs.question: An American-curriculum student is moving into AI SL, so what is usually missing?
faqs.answer: Less than families fear. Graphical and calculator work tends to be strong, which suits a course where technology is assumed in both papers. The gaps are usually algebraic form, the discipline of showing method for method marks, and the specific statistical tests the syllabus names. Two or three weeks of deliberate command-term practice closes most of the rest, because the content is familiar and the marking conventions are not.

faqs.question: Can a student change from Analysis and Approaches to Applications and Interpretation after the first term?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it depends entirely on the school: the change needs a staffing slot, a registration amendment and a view on how much has been missed. Ask the Diploma Programme coordinator for the deadline in writing before deciding. Academically the move is manageable, because the algebra already covered is more than enough; the work is catching the statistics strand the other course does not teach.

faqs.question: What happens to statistics work already done when a family relocates inside the Kingdom?
faqs.answer: The content stands, but the sequence usually does not, so a student arrives having covered regression and not probability distributions while the new class has done the reverse. Ask both schools for their topic lists and compare them directly. One session is normally enough to map the overlap, after which only the genuinely missing material needs teaching. Exploration progress should be discussed with the new supervising teacher immediately.

faqs.question: Why do some Saudi schools run AI SL but not AI HL?
faqs.answer: Numbers and staffing. Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level attracts the largest cohort in most schools, so it is the route that always runs. The Higher Level version needs enough students to justify a separate class and a teacher who can take it, and when either is missing the course quietly disappears from the timetable. Ask which mathematics classes actually ran last year rather than which appear in the prospectus.

faqs.question: What should a family ask a Saudi school about Diploma mathematics before enrolling?
faqs.answer: Four things, in writing. Which mathematics courses ran last year and with how many classes. Whether the course your child wants will be taught separately or combined with another level. Who supervises the exploration and how many drafts they review. And when the internal deadlines fall. The answers predict your child's experience far better than a prospectus page or an inspection summary does.

faqs.question: Who licenses the private and international schools teaching AI SL in the Kingdom?
faqs.answer: The Ministry of Education licenses private and international schools. School evaluation and accreditation runs through the Education and Training Evaluation Commission, which operates e-services for national school accreditation and for approving international accreditation bodies. A school authorised to run the Diploma has cleared those processes. None of that speaks to whether a particular class has a subject specialist this year, which is the question that affects a grade.

faqs.question: Our school teaches AI SL and AA SL in one combined class, so what should we buy?
faqs.answer: Targeted outside teaching for whichever course is getting less of the teacher's attention, which is usually the smaller group. A combined class tends to converge on shared content and rush the parts that differ, so ask the teacher which topics are being taught to both and which separately. Then buy sessions aimed only at the separate material. That is a short, specific commitment rather than a weekly hour all year.

faqs.question: Does an AI SL slot need to move when the school day shortens during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Usually it moves later and gets shorter rather than disappearing. The month lands in a different part of the academic year each time, so plan it when you can see it coming rather than in advance. A forty-five minute review session in the late evening keeps the habit and the slot; cancelling the month loses both, and families who cancel often find the slot has gone when they come back.

faqs.question: When in the Diploma year is it realistic to start AI SL support from scratch?
faqs.answer: Any point up to the spring term of the second year can produce real movement, because technique and command terms respond quickly. What changes is the ambition. Starting in the first year allows foundations to be rebuilt; starting after the mock allows the specific topics the script names to be fixed. Starting in the final fortnight buys exam-hall tactics and little else, and should be sold to you as that.

faqs.question: How much notice does changing a regular AI SL slot need?
faqs.answer: Agree it at the start rather than when you need it. A permanent change usually needs a week or two, because the tutor's other students hold the surrounding times. A single rescheduled lesson for a school trip or an internal examination is normally fine with a few days' notice. Write down what happens to a lesson cancelled on the day, since that is the case that causes arguments later.

faqs.question: What happens to AI SL lessons during the autumn break and the midyear break?
faqs.answer: That depends which calendar your school follows. A two-semester school breaks in the autumn and again at midyear; a three-term school has half-terms in different weeks. Pausing is reasonable if you say so in advance so the slot is held. Where a break falls shortly before a mock, a short block inside the break is better value than a pause, because the student is rested and the content is current.

ib-dp-math-ai-sl-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level as their own subject. Each works from the published assessment criteria, the formula booklet and real past papers rather than a general maths syllabus, and each has taught students sitting the May session from inside the Kingdom's school week.

intro.heading: What a Saudi family is really buying when they search for an AI SL tutor
paragraphs: A parent searches for an IB DP Math AI SL tutor at a particular moment: the first real Paper 1 comes back, the mark is lower than the classwork suggested, and the teacher's comment says the method was right but the working was not shown. Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level is not a soft option. It is a different course from Analysis and Approaches, with its own papers, its own calculator expectations and its own ways of losing marks. The search is for someone who knows that course, not someone who is good at maths.

AI SL is the statistics-and-modelling branch of Diploma mathematics. Its five topics — number and algebra, functions, geometry and trigonometry, statistics and probability, and calculus — lean towards data handling, and a graphic display calculator is assumed in both written papers rather than banned from one of them. Students arriving from an IGCSE course where the calculator was a checking tool often underuse it for a year. Students arriving from a national-curriculum school meet statistical tests they have never been asked to choose between. Both gaps are teachable, and both are invisible on a report card.

Then there is the week. Saudi schools teach Sunday to Thursday, so the pressure points are Sunday evening and Wednesday evening, not the Monday-to-Friday rhythm most tutoring copy assumes. The Kingdom sits on Arabia Standard Time at UTC+3 and does not change its clocks, so any drift in a weekly slot comes from the tutor's country rather than yours. Add a school run that can take forty minutes across Riyadh at the wrong hour and a four o'clock lesson is a fiction. These are logistics, and they decide whether the teaching happens at all.

The second organising fact is the calendar, counted backwards. Diploma mathematics is examined once, in the May session, and the exploration that carries a fifth of the grade falls due inside the school's own calendar well before that. Work out which stage your child has reached and the tutoring question answers itself: repairing algebra early in the first year is a different job from paper technique in the final weeks, and an exploration draft in the autumn term is a third one. No student needs the same hours all year.

What IB Gram offers is narrow and worth stating plainly. Lessons are one-to-one and delivered online over live video, pinned to Saudi local time. We do not send anyone to a Saudi address — home visits are a service offered only in India — and we are an independent tutoring platform with no affiliation to the IB, to any examination board, or to any school named here. No tutor can promise a grade. What a specialist does is name the marks your child is losing and show the method that earns them back.

sections.heading: Where an AI SL lesson fits a Sunday-to-Thursday week
paragraphs: Saudi schools run a Sunday-to-Thursday week, with Friday and Saturday as the weekend. That single fact reorganises a tutoring plan. Sunday evening carries the load a British family associates with Monday, Wednesday is the mid-week dip, and Thursday evening is already the weekend in a teenager's head. A weekly AI SL slot placed on a Thursday gets cancelled by half-term; the same slot on a Monday or Tuesday evening tends to survive the whole year intact.

The school run decides the earliest workable start. Riyadh is roughly an hour across in traffic, Jeddah runs as a long coastal spine, and the Dammam, Al Khobar and Dhahran cluster means a family can live in one city and attend school in another. A four o'clock lesson assumes the student is home, fed and settled by four, which is rarely true on a school night. Most AI SL slots that hold their shape start between half past six and eight in the evening.

Length matters as much as timing. Two sixty-minute sessions in a week beat one ninety-minute session for AI SL, because the subject is practice-shaped: a calculator technique taught on Sunday needs testing on Wednesday while it is still fresh in the hand. In the final term that inverts, and a longer single block becomes useful for sitting a complete paper under timing. The slot is worth reviewing at the start of each term rather than fixing once and then defending it.

sections.heading: Arabia Standard Time against the tutor's own working day
paragraphs: Arabia Standard Time is UTC+3 and the Kingdom does not observe daylight saving. A slot agreed in Saudi local time therefore never moves on your side of the call. It moves on the tutor's side, twice a year, if their country changes its clocks. A family that agreed seven in the evening Saudi time, in writing, is protected; a family that agreed a time on the tutor's clock quietly loses an hour of the evening when that clock goes forward.

India sits two and a half hours ahead of the Kingdom and does not change its clocks either, which makes an Indian-based AI SL specialist an unusually stable match for a Saudi evening: half past six in Riyadh is nine o'clock in Delhi, late but workable for a tutor who teaches evenings. The United Kingdom sits three hours behind in their winter and two in their summer, so an early-evening Saudi slot lands in a British afternoon and survives the change only if it is pinned here.

The practical rule is to write the slot down in Saudi local time, name the day, and agree in advance what happens when a clock change makes it awkward on the tutor's side. Ask that question before the first lesson rather than in the week the change happens. A tutor who already teaches across several Gulf time zones will have an answer ready; one who has only ever taught locally very often does not, and the slot drifts.

sections.heading: The AI SL year, counted backwards from the May session
paragraphs: Diploma mathematics is a two-year course with one set of written papers at the end, sat in the May session by almost every IB school in the Kingdom. That makes the calendar easier to plan than an IGCSE year with two series, and harder to recover from: there is no second sitting inside the Diploma for a student who drifted through the first twelve months. Planning backwards from the session is the only version of this that holds together.

The exploration is the piece families underestimate. It carries a fifth of the AI SL grade, it is marked against five published criteria, and the school sets its own internal dates for the proposal, the draft and the final submission — usually in the autumn term of the second year, months before the papers. A student who leaves the idea until the spring term is choosing between a rushed piece of work and lost teaching time, and most choose badly.

Each stage needs a different kind of help. The first year is repair work: the algebraic manipulation from Year 11 that AI SL assumes and does not reteach. The second autumn is exploration supervision alongside new content. The spring is mock review. The final weeks are paper technique, timing and command terms. Confirm every date with your child's Diploma Programme coordinator, because entries and internal deadlines differ by school and nothing written on this page replaces the calendar your own school publishes at the start of each term.

sections.heading: How Applications and Interpretation SL is assessed
paragraphs: Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level is assessed through two written papers and one piece of internally assessed work. Paper 1 runs ninety minutes and carries forty per cent of the grade: short-response questions across the whole syllabus, answered in the question booklet itself. Paper 2 also runs ninety minutes and also carries forty per cent, built from a smaller number of extended-response questions that run through several linked parts and reward sustained, readable working.

The remaining fifth is the mathematical exploration, a written investigation of the student's own choosing, submitted through the school. Both papers assume technology: a graphic display calculator is required throughout AI SL, and there is no non-calculator paper of the kind Analysis and Approaches candidates sit. A formula booklet is provided in the examination, which changes what is worth memorising and what is worth knowing how to find quickly under pressure in the hall.

Those three components pull in different directions, and a tutor should be able to say which one is costing your child marks. A student who scores well on Paper 1 and poorly on Paper 2 has a stamina and structure problem rather than a content problem. A student whose exploration marks are low on reflection has a writing problem inside a mathematics subject. Ask the school's teacher for the component breakdown in writing before you buy any hours at all, because a tutor aiming at the wrong component will work hard and change nothing.

sections.heading: Where AI SL marks are actually lost
paragraphs: Statistics is where AI SL marks go first. The course asks students to choose a test rather than apply one they have been handed: a chi-squared test for independence or for goodness of fit, a correlation coefficient and the regression line that may or may not be appropriate, a confidence interval that has to be read in context. Candidates who can compute all of it still lose marks for picking the wrong tool, or for treating a correlation as proof of a cause.

Calculator discipline is the second leak. Degrees left in radian mode, intermediate values rounded and then reused, a sketch of a graph with no window or axis labels, an answer written down with none of the method that earned it — each costs method marks the student had already done the work for. AI SL rewards a candidate who shows the calculator was used deliberately, and penalises one who shows only the final number on the answer line.

Interpretation is the third. Many AI SL questions end by asking what the answer means for the situation described, and a numerically correct response with no sentence in context earns less than it should. Command terms do real work here: write down, find, determine, hence, justify and interpret each ask for something different, and a student who treats them as synonyms for answer leaves marks on the table in every single paper they sit. Teaching the terms takes one session and pays for itself.

sections.heading: The exploration, and what a tutor may and may not do
paragraphs: The mathematical exploration is twelve to twenty pages of the student's own investigation, marked against five criteria: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection, and use of mathematics. Use of mathematics carries the largest share of the twenty marks available, which is why an exploration built on a safe idea with thin mathematics scores badly however neatly it is typed. Choosing the idea well is most of the grade, and it happens before any data is collected.

Legitimate help looks like this. A tutor can ask whether an idea has enough mathematics in it to reach the top band, point out that a data set is too small to support a regression, explain what the reflection criterion actually rewards, and mark a draft the student has written against the published descriptors. A tutor can teach a statistical technique the student has chosen to use, as a technique, in the way a class teacher would.

The line is simple and worth saying out loud, because the pages competing for this search will not say it. No tutor should produce a single line of the mathematics that is handed in, choose the topic on a student's behalf, or supply text to be pasted. The school sets how many drafts may be formally reviewed and records the supervision, so a family that keeps the tutor's feedback alongside the student's own dated versions has the evidence ready if a question is ever raised about whose work it is.

sections.heading: What AI SL tuition costs in the Kingdom, and what moves it
paragraphs: Advertised rates in Saudi Arabia span a wide range, and every published number comes from a vendor rather than from a survey. Tutoring-platform listings start general online tutoring from around SAR 55 an hour. Tutor-marketplace guides put general Riyadh private tuition for senior-school examination subjects at SAR 200 and above. Tutoring-company pages list IB subject tutoring in Riyadh from roughly SAR 180, with Higher Level tracks quoted near SAR 200 to SAR 220 an hour.

Those are advertised rates, not a market average, and none of them is IB Gram's price — a rate is agreed with the family after the free diagnostic lesson. What moves the number is scarcity first: an Analysis and Approaches HL specialist costs more than an AI SL one everywhere, because fewer teachers can do it. Then marking or examiner experience, then level, then whether the tutor travels to a home, then the length of package booked.

AI SL sits in the middle of that spread, which is reasonable news for a family buying a year of weekly support. To compare quotes honestly, ask three questions: is this person teaching AI SL specifically or Diploma mathematics generally, what happens to unused lessons, and is written feedback included or billed separately. Some international providers quote in US dollars at around sixty dollars an hour, which is a different budget once converted into riyals, and a currency risk a family carries for the length of the booking.

faqs.question: What does a free first lesson in Applications and Interpretation SL actually test?
faqs.answer: It is a diagnostic rather than a sales call. The tutor sets a short mixed group of questions — one statistics item, one function item, one calculator-heavy modelling task — and watches the method rather than the answers. The output is a written note naming the topics needing reteaching, the calculator habits costing method marks, and a suggested weekly shape. You receive that note whether or not you book anything further.

faqs.question: How soon after starting AI SL support should a parent expect a mark to move?
faqs.answer: Technique gaps move fastest. Calculator discipline, showing method and reading command terms correctly can lift a paper score inside three or four sessions, because the content was already there. Topic gaps take longer: a statistics unit never properly taught needs five or six weeks before it shows in a test. If nothing has changed after a full term of weekly lessons, the match is wrong and should be changed.

faqs.question: What should an AI SL tutor's written note after each session contain?
faqs.answer: Three things: what was covered, what the student got wrong and why, and what they are practising before the next lesson. A useful note names the component — lost the method marks in a Paper 2 part — rather than reporting that the session went well. Over a term those notes become a record you can compare against the school's own account of the same topics.

faqs.question: What happens if our AI SL tutor and the school teach the same topic differently?
faqs.answer: The school's approach wins, because the school marks the exploration and sets the predicted grade. A good tutor asks for the scheme of work or the textbook early and teaches inside it, flagging a genuine difference instead of overwriting it. Where a method is a matter of preference — which regression to run, how to lay out a chi-squared table — the student learns the school's version first.

faqs.question: How do we decide whether to keep AI SL lessons once the exploration is submitted?
faqs.answer: The exploration is a fifth of the grade and it is finished; the papers are the other four fifths and they are not. Most families keep a weekly slot and change its purpose, moving from supervision to past papers and timing. If the student already scores consistently on both papers, dropping to a fortnightly session through the spring term and returning to weekly for the final weeks is reasonable.

faqs.question: Can an AI SL lesson and a second subject run on the same evening in a Sunday-to-Thursday week?
faqs.answer: They can, and it usually works badly. A ninety-minute mathematics session followed by physics on a school night produces one good hour and one wasted one. Spreading two subjects across Sunday and Tuesday, or Monday and Wednesday, keeps both fresh and leaves Thursday clear. Where a double evening cannot be avoided, put mathematics first, while the student can still hold a method in their head.

faqs.question: How late can an AI SL slot start when the school run finishes after six?
faqs.answer: A start between half past six and eight in the evening is normal across Riyadh, Jeddah and the Eastern Province cluster, and some families run a half past eight slot in the second Diploma year. Later than that and the session stops being teaching. If the commute makes every weekday evening tight, one longer weekend session plus a short midweek review is more honest.

faqs.question: What happens to a weekly AI SL slot across the long summer break?
faqs.answer: Three options, and families choose differently. Pause and reserve the slot for the autumn term, which keeps the tutor but loses momentum. Drop to a fortnightly session that keeps calculator work and statistics ticking over. Or use the break for a short block on the exploration idea, the one piece of AI SL work that can move forward without the school timetable. Say which you want before term ends.

faqs.question: Our AI SL tutor is abroad, so how is the slot kept stable when their clocks change?
faqs.answer: Write the slot down in Saudi local time from the first lesson, because Arabia Standard Time does not move. Then ask what the tutor intends to do when their own country changes its clocks: hold the Saudi time and shift their day, or move the lesson. Either answer works if it is agreed in advance. The failure case is a slot recorded in the tutor's local time.

faqs.question: Why does Applications and Interpretation SL have no non-calculator paper?
faqs.answer: Because the course is built around using technology rather than around manipulation by hand. AI SL asks students to model real situations, run statistical tests and read graphs, all of which assume a graphic display calculator. Analysis and Approaches keeps a non-calculator paper because its purpose includes algebraic fluency. So calculator competence is examinable in AI SL, not incidental, and treating the device as a checking tool costs marks in both papers.

faqs.question: What is AI SL Paper 2 asking for that Paper 1 does not?
faqs.answer: Paper 1 samples the whole syllabus through short questions, each standing alone, so one weak topic costs a few marks. Paper 2 uses a smaller number of extended questions whose parts build on each other, so an early slip can cost the rest of the question. It rewards sustained, legible working and punishes a candidate who abandons a part-finished answer. Practising only Paper 1 flatters a student badly.

faqs.question: Which command terms carry the marks in an AI SL extended-response question?
faqs.answer: Write down expects an answer with no working and gives no credit for method. Find and determine both want the working shown, with determine usually implying a fuller argument. Hence means the previous part must be used, and ignoring it loses marks even when the answer is right. Justify and interpret want a sentence about the situation, not another number. Reading these correctly beats any single topic.

faqs.question: How do grade boundaries work for Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level?
faqs.answer: Boundaries are set after each session, once the papers have been marked and the difficulty of that particular set is known, so they shift a little from one session to the next. That is why a raw score from a past paper means nothing until it is read against that paper's own boundaries. A tutor should mark practice papers with the matching scheme and report the grade.

faqs.question: Is an AI SL predicted grade based on the mock paper or on the exploration as well?
faqs.answer: The school decides, and most weigh everything they hold: internal tests, the mock, classwork and the exploration mark if it is finished. A predicted grade is a professional judgement submitted by the school, not a forecast a tutor can issue or change. What tutoring can do is give the school more recent evidence, and a complete paper sat under timing in the spring often reads better than an autumn mock.

intro.heading: What you are actually choosing between, and what each option costs
paragraphs: A parent looking for Diploma teaching in the Kingdom is rarely short of options. The school offers an after-school clinic. A tutoring centre advertises a group revision course for the May session. A neighbour recommends someone who drives out to the compound on Tuesdays. A platform quotes an hourly rate from SAR 55 and a provider abroad quotes in dollars. The prices differ by a factor of six, the words used to describe them are nearly identical, and none of those pages explains what the difference buys.

The Diploma makes that comparison harder than it looks, because the thing being bought is narrow. A family is not buying maths. They are buying somebody who knows what Paper 3 asks of a Higher Level candidate, what a mark scheme pays for a method line, and how an internal assessment criterion is applied by a moderator. Content teaching is the cheap part, and a school usually does it adequately. The scarce, expensive part is a person who has taught and marked the exact component where the marks are going missing.

Every riyal figure on this page is a rate somebody else advertises, attached to the type of source that publishes it. None of them is our price, none is a market average, and a vendor's own number is marketing rather than evidence. They are useful anyway: read together they show what this market charges for scarcity, and that is the one pattern a family can plan around.

Lessons from IB Gram are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, with the paper or the draft on a shared screen. We do not send a tutor to an address in the Kingdom; home visits are a service we offer only in India. For a Diploma family that is a smaller constraint than it sounds, because the pool of people who have taught a given Higher Level subject here is small and concentrated in Riyadh, Jeddah and the Eastern Province cluster. A family in Tabuk, Jazan or AlUla is not choosing between an online specialist and a local one. They are choosing between an online specialist and nobody.

So this page runs in the order the decision runs. First the four ways Diploma teaching is bought in this market, with the advertised prices attached to each. Then what moves an hourly figure, so two quotes for the same subject can be compared honestly. Then online against in-home once travel across a Saudi city is counted, what a single hour should contain before a family pays for a second, and the three ways money is routinely wasted on Diploma support. The last two sections cover the week lessons have to fit into and the things a fee cannot buy at any price.

sections.heading: The four ways a Saudi family buys Diploma teaching
paragraphs: Almost every enquiry starts with a price comparison that is not comparing like with like. A school's own after-school clinic is inside the fee or close to it, and it is taught by the same teacher whose lesson the student already did not follow. A group revision course charges per seat and runs to a fixed syllabus order, which suits a student broadly on track and wastes the money of one who is not. An in-home tutor charges for travel whether the quote itemises it or not.

The useful question is not which is cheapest per hour but which one can act on the specific thing going wrong. A Higher Level Chemistry candidate losing marks on the evaluation criterion of an internal assessment does not need eight more hours of content. They need one hour on that criterion with somebody who has applied it to real work. A group course cannot deliver that hour, and the school may lack the staffing to give it one-to-one.

So the ranking changes with the problem, which is why one recommendation for every family is dishonest. For a student drifting across a whole subject, the school clinic plus a weekly hour is usually enough and is the cheapest route that works. For a scarce component - Paper 3, a Higher Level internal assessment, Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at the top of the course - the specialist hour is the only option that changes anything, and it is worth paying more for fewer of them.

sections.heading: Why two quotes for the same Higher Level subject differ by a factor of three
paragraphs: The figures advertised here run from roughly SAR 35 an hour on a budget online platform to over SAR 200 for a senior-school examination subject in Riyadh, with international providers quoting around sixty dollars. All of them describe the same product in almost the same words. Three things explain nearly the whole spread, and only one of them is about how well anybody teaches.

Subject scarcity does most of the work. A Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches teacher who has marked Paper 3 is rare everywhere and rarer inside the Kingdom; a Standard Level Mathematics tutor is not. The second factor is marking or examiner experience, worth paying for in exactly one way: that tutor can say what the mark scheme pays for rather than what the textbook says. The third is level - Higher Level above Standard Level, above the Middle Years Programme, above IGCSE - because the content ceiling is higher and fewer people are comfortable at the top of it.

What does not explain the spread is marketing. A rate quoted in dollars by a provider abroad shows a different cost base, not better teaching. A rate advertised from a low number is the starting point for the cheapest subject at the lowest level, and the Higher Level figure on the same site is usually double it. Two questions settle most quotes: which component of this subject have you taught most recently, and have you ever marked it.

sections.heading: Online one-to-one against an in-home tutor, once Saudi distances are counted
paragraphs: An in-home quote carries a travel decision the family pays for twice. Riyadh is about an hour across in traffic, so a tutor living in the north and teaching in the centre either prices the journey in or restricts the hours they offer. Jeddah behaves the same way along its coastal spine. In the Dammam, Al Khobar and Dhahran conurbation families live in one city and attend school in another, so an in-home tutor's catchment and the school's catchment are different shapes on the map.

The second cost never appears on an invoice: the pool. An in-home tutor has to live within driving distance, which shrinks the choice from everyone who teaches the subject to everyone who teaches it nearby. For Standard Level Mathematics in Riyadh that still leaves a reasonable choice. For Higher Level Physics in Al Ahsa, Jazan or AlUla it often leaves none, and the family pays a specialist-sounding rate for generalist teaching because the alternative is nothing at all.

Teaching over video removes travel from the price and geography from the pool. It adds three requirements instead: a reliable connection, a quiet room for the hour, and a slot the family genuinely defends each week. The Diploma suits the format, because the work is documents - past papers, mark schemes, internal assessment drafts, graphs, annotated scripts - and documents are easier to work on together on a shared screen than across a kitchen table. IB Gram does not send tutors to Saudi addresses; home visits are a service offered only in India.

sections.heading: What one Diploma hour should contain before you pay for a second
paragraphs: A first paid hour should produce something a parent can read. Not a comment on attitude - a specific diagnosis: which paper, which topic, which command term, and what the next four weeks will do about it. If the hour produces only an agreement that the student is finding mathematics difficult, the money bought nothing the last school report did not already say for free.

The free trial lesson exists for that reason, and it is a working session rather than a sales call. The tutor takes a recent piece of the student's own marked work, asks them to attempt two questions aloud, and watches for the point where the reasoning actually stops. A student who can state an equation but cannot select it has a different problem from one who selects it correctly and then drops the method marks. Those two need different teaching in different amounts, and guessing between them is what makes support expensive.

After that, an hour should be auditable. Work set and checked between sessions. A short written note naming what was covered and what comes next. Marked scripts returned with the mark scheme beside them, so the student sees what a six-mark answer was supposed to contain rather than being told the answer was thin. Families who ask for those three things in the first fortnight rarely argue about value in the third month, because the evidence accumulates where both sides can see it.

sections.heading: Three ways Diploma families waste money here
paragraphs: The first is paying for content when the loss is technique. A student who understands the topic and still scores five out of ten is being marked down for how the answer is written: the command term ignored, the evaluation missing, the working unexplained. More content hours produce a better-informed student with the same mark. An hour spent reading two of their own answers against the mark scheme usually moves more marks than four hours of revision, at a quarter of the cost.

The second is buying in the final term what was needed in the first year. Internal assessment work is chosen, drafted and finalised across the two years, and those deadlines sit well before the written papers. A family starting support eight weeks before the May session can still improve examination technique, but it cannot change an assessment already submitted, and that component is a fixed share of every subject grade. The late block is the dearest hour in this market and the one with the least leverage in it.

The third is paying the wrong rate for the wrong scarcity. A generalist charged at a specialist rate for a Higher Level component is one error; a specialist bought at a premium to teach foundations the school already covers is its mirror image. Decide which component is costing marks, then buy the narrowest person who can fix it. Asking a tutor what they have marked is how you tell the two apart before paying.

sections.heading: The Sunday-to-Thursday week, and what an evening slot really costs
paragraphs: The school week here runs Sunday to Thursday, with Friday and Saturday as the weekend. That single fact rearranges any schedule copied from a British or Indian page. The heaviest homework lands on a Wednesday or Thursday evening, and the two free days sit where another country's week is still running. A tutor whose own students are mostly on a Monday-to-Friday timetable has to hold a Sunday evening deliberately, so a family should confirm the slot is a standing commitment rather than an experiment.

The Kingdom keeps Arabia Standard Time at UTC+3 and does not change its clocks. A tutor in India is two and a half hours ahead, so a 6pm lesson in Riyadh falls in their mid-evening. A tutor in the United Kingdom is three hours behind during their winter and two in their summer, which means an hour agreed in local time there drifts twice a year unless the booking is pinned to Saudi local time instead.

Two calendar facts change when support is worth buying. Public schools in the Kingdom run two semesters from late August to late June, with an autumn break, a midyear break and an Eid Al Fitr break, while most international and British-curriculum schools set their own three-term years, so term dates differ school by school inside one city. School days also shorten during Ramadan and evening study patterns shift with them. Build the slot around the family's actual week and it survives all of that.

sections.heading: What the fee does not buy at any price
paragraphs: A tutor teaches, reviews and gives feedback on work the student has written. No student may hand any part of the drafting of an internal assessment, an Extended Essay, a Theory of Knowledge essay or a Personal Project to somebody else, and a provider offering to help with that paperwork is selling a route to a malpractice investigation rather than a grade. The legitimate version is narrow: pressure-test the research question, read the method for holes, mark a draft against the published criteria, hand it back to be rewritten.

A fee does not buy a predicted grade either. Predicted grades are set by the school from the student's own evidence, and an outside tutor contributes nothing beyond better evidence to look at. No tutor can promise a grade, a points total or an improvement, and anyone who does should be treated with real scepticism, because there is no mechanism by which an hour a week produces a number. What tutoring can honestly offer is more marks available from the same understanding, which is a different and far more checkable claim.

The university endgame sits outside the fee as well. A foreign or international certificate needs an equivalency decision from the Ministry of Education before a Saudi university treats it as equivalent to the national secondary certificate. Qudurat, run through ETEC's national assessment centre, tests reasoning rather than syllabus content. Tahsili follows the Saudi national curriculum, which is exactly why international-curriculum students find it unfamiliar. Universities publish their own criteria and they differ by programme, so read the university's own page rather than a tutoring company's summary.

faqs.question: We are moving from a CBSE school into the first Diploma year - which two subjects need paid support first?
faqs.answer: Mathematics and the English A course, in that order, more often than the sciences. A student arriving from CBSE usually has strong procedural mathematics and meets a course wanting proof, modelling and a written justification of method. The English demand is the bigger surprise, because Diploma marks come from analysis under time rather than content recall. Buy one weekly hour in each for a term, then review before adding a third.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to repeat the first Diploma year than to buy catch-up teaching across three subjects?
faqs.answer: Repeating costs a year of school fees and a year of the student's life, so it is rarely cheaper in money or time. Catch-up teaching in three subjects at once is also the most expensive way to buy support: three weekly hours plus marking is a large bill for a student already tired. The honest answer is usually two subjects, chosen by which components carry the most marks, leaving the third with the school.

faqs.question: Our child switched from A Levels into Standard Level mathematics - how many weeks of one-to-one does that take?
faqs.answer: Expect a term rather than a month. The content overlap is large and the assessment overlap is small: the Diploma wants modelling, a graphical calculator used deliberately, and an internal assessment with no A Level equivalent. A realistic block is eight to twelve weekly hours, front-loaded onto the assessment and calculator technique, after which most students drop to fortnightly. Ask the tutor to name the topics each week, so the block has a visible end.

faqs.question: What happens to money we spent on a subject the student drops at the end of the first Diploma year?
faqs.answer: The teaching is not wasted if it went into technique. Command-term discipline, mark-scheme reading and timed-paper practice transfer to every other subject on the timetable. Content hours in a dropped subject are gone. That is the argument for spending the first year's budget on what generalises, and for waiting until subject choices are genuinely settled before buying heavy content support in a subject the student is unsure about.

faqs.question: If our school teaches Higher Level and Standard Level Physics in one combined class, what should we buy?
faqs.answer: Buy the Higher Level extension rather than the whole subject. A combined class usually covers the shared core competently and runs short of time on Higher Level-only material and on Paper 3, which is where such a cohort loses marks. One weekly hour on extension topics and past Paper 3 questions is a smaller bill than general support and targets what the school cannot reach. Ask which extension topics get separate timetabled time.

faqs.question: Does a school's own paid revision programme cost less than an outside Diploma specialist, and is it the same thing?
faqs.answer: It usually costs less per hour and it is not the same thing. A school programme is taught by the same staff to a group from the same scheme of work, which is useful for coverage and weak for diagnosis: the explanation that did not land in class is the one being repeated. Run both where the budget allows, and spend the outside hour on the component the school cannot staff.

faqs.question: Our school will not run Higher Level Economics next year - what are the options and what do they cost?
faqs.answer: Three, in rising order of disruption. Take the subject at Standard Level and keep the Higher Level ambition for university elsewhere. Move to a school in the city that runs it, which costs a place and a commute. Or ask whether the school will support it as a self-taught option alongside outside teaching, which the Diploma coordinator must agree first. The third route needs more hours than a normal subject, priced accordingly.

faqs.question: What does an ETEC evaluation actually tell us about the Diploma teaching inside a school?
faqs.answer: Less than parents hope. The Education and Training Evaluation Commission runs school evaluation services, and licensing of private and international schools sits with the Ministry of Education. Neither process reports whether one Higher Level subject is taught by a specialist this year. For that, ask the school: who teaches it, how long they have taught it, and whether the Higher Level material is timetabled separately. A school's standing and a subject's staffing are different questions.

faqs.question: How does a two-semester school calendar change when we should buy Diploma support, compared with a three-term school?
faqs.answer: It moves the review points rather than the total. Public schools here run two semesters from late August to late June with an autumn break, a midyear break and an Eid Al Fitr break; most international schools set their own three-term years. On a two-semester calendar the first useful evidence arrives later, so a family starting in the autumn works from one reporting cycle instead of two. Start from the school's published calendar.

faqs.question: Is a slot right after the school run worth more or less than a late-evening one for a Diploma student?
faqs.answer: For most Diploma students the late-afternoon hour is worth more per riyal, because concentration is better and the session can end with work the student actually does that night. The exception is a second-year student carrying three Higher Levels whose afternoons are committed; for them a late slot that happens reliably beats an earlier one that keeps getting cancelled. Choose the hour the family can defend every week.

faqs.question: How many evenings a week can a Diploma student in the Kingdom realistically give to paid lessons?
faqs.answer: Two for most families, and three only for a short block before the May session. The school week runs Sunday to Thursday with homework and internal assessment work on top, and a student who gives four evenings to tutoring stops doing the independent practice the tutoring is meant to make possible. Two evenings plus marked work between sessions is the pattern that survives a whole term.

faqs.question: Which week of the autumn term is the worst one to start paid Diploma support in?
faqs.answer: The week the school issues its first full reports. Every family in the cohort reaches the same conclusion on the same evening, and the specialists with capacity are taken within days. The second-year autumn is already the tightest part of the two years, with university applications and internal assessment deadlines in the same weeks. Starting a fortnight before reports go out costs the same per hour and offers a choice of tutors.

faqs.question: If our family relocates from Jeddah to Riyadh mid-Diploma, does anything about the lessons or the fee change?
faqs.answer: Nothing about the lessons. The tutor, the slot and the plan are unchanged, because teaching is over live video and Arabia Standard Time applies in both cities. What changes is the school, and that deserves a session of its own: a new scheme of work, a different order of topics, sometimes a different internal assessment timetable. Send the new school's subject outlines to the tutor before the first lesson.

faqs.question: Does a tutor working from India suit a Saudi Diploma student's evening, given the two-and-a-half-hour difference?
faqs.answer: It fits well, which is why much of this market is staffed that way. Arabia Standard Time is UTC+3 and India is two and a half hours ahead, so a 6pm lesson in Riyadh is mid-evening for the tutor: late, but inside a normal teaching day. The real constraint is the week rather than the clock, because a tutor whose other students sit on a Monday-to-Friday timetable must hold a Sunday hour deliberately.

From there the decision can be priced honestly: how many hours, in which subject, against which component. Tell us the subject, the level and the two evenings that work.

intro.heading: A Physics HL search in the Kingdom usually starts with a dropped grade
paragraphs: The query that brings families here is a home-tutor query, and the reason behind it is almost always a specific script. A student who held a 6 through the first Diploma year comes back from a mock with a 4, the school's comment says revise more thoroughly, and nobody has said which component lost the marks. Higher Level Physics punishes that vagueness more than most Diploma subjects, because the content is wide, the mathematics is unforgiving and the marks are spread across three places that fail for three different reasons.

Physics at Higher Level runs to about 240 teaching hours against 150 at Standard Level, and the extra time is not padding. It buys rigid body mechanics, special relativity, thermodynamics and entropy, electromagnetic induction, gravitational and electric potential, and the radioactive decay law. A student who treats those as extra reading rather than examined content will meet them cold in Paper 2, where the extended-response questions carry the heaviest single share of the grade.

The second thing a parent is buying is diagnosis. Paper 1 at Higher Level splits into 1A, which is multiple choice, and 1B, which is data analysis and experimental work, and together they carry 36 per cent. Paper 2 carries 44 per cent. The scientific investigation, written up by the student from their own data, carries 20 per cent. Confirm that component list in writing with your school's Diploma Programme coordinator, because the shape of the course decides where an hour of tutoring should be spent.

The money question deserves an answer up front, because it is the reason most families hesitate. Vendors here publish rates rather than negotiating them privately, so the spread is visible before anyone makes a call: general online tutoring with no subject specialism is advertised from around SAR 55 an hour, IB subject tutoring in Riyadh from around SAR 180, and Higher Level premium tracks at roughly SAR 200 to 220. Those are advertised figures taken from vendor listings. None of them is our price, and none is a market average. What a listing never shows is whether that tutor has worked from a mark scheme for this subject, which is the difference between an hour that recovers marks in Paper 1B and an hour of pleasant revision.

On delivery, we are direct about it. In-home tutoring exists in Riyadh, Jeddah and the Eastern Province cluster, and the market publishes rates for it. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a Saudi address; home visits are a service we offer only in India. Saudi families are taught one-to-one over live video on Arabia Standard Time, which is also what makes a genuine Higher Level Physics specialist reachable from Abha, AlUla or a Jubail compound rather than only from a central Riyadh postcode.

subjects.name: Theme A: Space, time and motion

subjects.name: Theme E: Nuclear and quantum physics

subjects.name: The scientific investigation
subjects.description: The student's own investigation, written to a word limit and marked on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation.

subjects.name: Experimental and practical skills
subjects.description: Uncertainty, error bars, lines of best fit and gradients with units. The most teachable component in the course.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches

sections.heading: Where Higher Level Physics marks actually go missing
paragraphs: Start with the script, not the syllabus. In a mock pack that has been properly marked, the lost marks in Higher Level Physics cluster in four places, and three of them have nothing to do with how much content the student knows. The first is Paper 1A, where a candidate who understands the physics still loses marks by answering from memory instead of eliminating options, particularly on vector resolution and on graph interpretation where two distractors are deliberately close.

The second is Paper 1B. This is the data-analysis half of Paper 1, and it rewards a set of habits rather than recall: quoting an uncertainty to a sensible precision, matching significant figures to the raw data, drawing a line of best fit that respects error bars, and reading a gradient with its units attached. A student who has never been taught these as examined skills treats them as tidiness and loses marks steadily across every question.

The third is Paper 2, which carries the largest share of the grade and the longest answers. Here the command term decides the mark. Outline, explain, determine, deduce and show that each demand a different shape of response, and a six-mark explanation that describes instead of explaining caps itself at two or three. The fourth place is the scientific investigation, where evaluation is almost always the weakest of the four criteria. Diagnosis is the first hour of work rather than an optional extra, and it is far cheaper than a term of general revision aimed at nothing in particular.

sections.heading: Uncertainty and significant figures: the cheapest marks in the course
paragraphs: Of everything a Higher Level Physics tutor can fix, the Paper 1B skill set returns the most marks per hour. It is narrow, it is mechanical, and it is examined the same way every series. A student needs to know when an absolute uncertainty becomes a percentage one, how uncertainties combine through a product, a quotient and a power, and how to carry that through to a final answer quoted to a defensible precision rather than to whatever the calculator displayed.

Then come the graph skills, which are where the longer data questions live. Error bars have to be plotted from the uncertainties, not sketched. The line of best fit has to pass within the bars, and the steepest and shallowest acceptable lines give the uncertainty in the gradient. The gradient itself has to be read with units and then connected back to the physical relationship the question is testing, which is the step that separates a mark of two from a mark of five.

Schools rarely have time for this. Practical lessons are spent collecting data because the experimental programme has hours to log, and the analysis is set as homework and marked lightly. A tutor working one-to-one over live video has the student's own graph on screen, can see where the pencil went, and can insist on the same routine until it is automatic. Advertised rates do not distinguish between a tutor who teaches this and one who does not, so a family has to ask directly.

sections.heading: The Higher Level extensions, and why they have no Standard Level fallback
paragraphs: The structural difference between the two levels is often misread. Higher Level Physics is not the Standard Level course plus a separate options book; the extensions sit inside the same five themes, which means a student who is weak on the Standard Level core meets the harder material on an unstable foundation rather than in a separate module they could choose to leave late. That is why a mid-course drop in grade so often traces back a year.

In practice the extensions that cause the most trouble are concentrated. Rigid body mechanics and special relativity extend Theme A and assume confident vector work. Thermodynamics and entropy extend Theme B and arrive late in most schemes of work. Theme D grows the most: gravitational and electric potential, escape speed, orbital energy and electromagnetic induction, each of which requires holding a field and an energy argument in the same answer. The decay law extends Theme E and is examined mathematically.

The teaching consequence is that a Higher Level tutor has to work two layers at once, repairing the core while the school pushes on through the extension. A tutor who only knows the Standard Level material can keep a student busy and still leave the examined extension untouched, which is the most expensive version of cheap tutoring. Ask a prospective tutor which Theme D extension they taught most recently and what the usual error in it is; the answer is diagnostic in a minute.

sections.heading: What the market advertises for a Higher Level Physics hour
paragraphs: Rates in the Kingdom are published by vendors, not by any central body, so every figure here is an advertised rate from a named type of source and none of it is our price or a market average. The spread is wide. General online tutoring with no subject specialism is advertised from around SAR 55 an hour on tutoring platforms, and budget platforms advertise IGCSE one-to-one from around SAR 35. Those numbers are not describing the same product as a Higher Level Physics specialist.

At the senior end, tutor-marketplace guides describe Riyadh private tuition for senior examination subjects at SAR 200 and above, tutoring companies list IB subject tutoring in Riyadh from around SAR 180, and Higher Level and AP premium tracks appear at roughly SAR 200 to 220. International providers quoting in dollars sit near sixty dollars an hour, which a Saudi family should convert before comparing. In-home quotes load travel into the hour, and in a city an hour across that loading is real.

What moves the number, in order of weight: subject scarcity first, because a Higher Level Physics teacher is harder to find than a Standard Level biologist anywhere; then marking or examining experience; then level, with Higher Level above Standard Level above Middle Years work; then whether the tutor travels; then package length. A rate that is high because the subject is scarce is not the same as a rate that is high because the tutor is good, and the only way to tell is to put them in front of a marked script.

sections.heading: Home tutoring for Physics HL in the Kingdom, and how we deliver it instead
paragraphs: The home-tutor question deserves a straight answer rather than a redirect. In-home private tuition is a real market in Riyadh, Jeddah and the Dammam cluster, agencies quote for it, and for younger children it has obvious merits: a parent in the next room, no device to manage, a tutor who sees the kitchen table where the work gets done. Families asking for a Higher Level Physics home tutor are usually asking for that reliability rather than for a particular technology.

The problem is arithmetic rather than principle. A weekly visit restricts the search to specialists who live within a practical drive, and the number of people in any one Saudi city who have taught Higher Level Physics recently and can travel on a Tuesday evening is small. Travel is priced into the hour, a late school run pushes the slot back, and traffic cancels lessons that the family has already paid for. The scarcer the subject, the worse that trade becomes.

So we do not pretend to offer it. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a Saudi address and makes no home visits in the Kingdom; home visits are a service we offer only in India. Saudi families are taught one-to-one over live video, with the student's own script, graph or spreadsheet shared on screen. That is what lets a family in Abha, AlUla or a Jubail compound work with a Higher Level Physics specialist rather than with whoever is nearest.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation: what a tutor may do, and what may not be touched
paragraphs: The investigation is worth a fifth of the grade and is the single place where tutoring can cross into malpractice, so the boundary needs saying plainly. The work must be the student's own: their research question, their method, their data, their analysis and their words. A tutor who produces any part of it has not helped; they have put the student's Diploma at risk, and schools are required to report suspected malpractice to the IB rather than deal with it quietly.

What a tutor may legitimately do is still substantial. They can teach the four assessment criteria and what each one rewards, so that research design is read as a question about controlled variables and range rather than as a tidy introduction. They can work through published exemplars. They can question a research question until the student can defend it, point out that a chosen range will not produce a gradient worth analysing, and teach uncertainty propagation on practice data that is not the student's own.

They can also read a draft and give feedback in the form the IB expects: comments on what the criteria ask for, not corrections written into the document. Evaluation is the criterion that usually carries the fewest marks, because students apologise for their experiment rather than analysing its limitations against their own results. That is teachable without anyone writing a sentence for the student, and it is the conversation to have with a prospective tutor before any money changes hands.

sections.heading: Arriving into Higher Level Physics from another system
paragraphs: A large share of Higher Level Physics students in the Kingdom did not start the course where they are finishing it. Families relocate into Riyadh, the Eastern Province, NEOM and AlUla mid-course, and students switch schools between the first and second Diploma year. Physics is one of the hardest subjects to pick up late, because the experimental hours and the investigation are logged against a specific school's programme and cannot simply be carried in from elsewhere.

The gaps are predictable by origin. A student from a British A-level course usually has strong mechanics and electricity but has met no command-term structure of the IB kind and no internal assessment with these four criteria. A student from an American programme often arrives with good conceptual coverage and little algebraic density, and has never written to a word limit. A student from the national curriculum meets both a language shift and a change in what a question is asking for.

The practical answer is a timed diagnostic rather than a syllabus audit. Give the student a past Paper 1B and one Paper 2 extended-response question, mark them against the real scheme, and the gap announces itself in forty minutes. Then ask the receiving school three questions in writing: how many practical hours are already logged, when the investigation is due, and whether the Higher Level extensions in Theme D have been taught yet. Those three answers decide what the first term of tutoring is for.

faqs.question: Why can a Saudi school teach Standard Level physics but not run the Higher Level class?
faqs.answer: Because the two levels are timetabled separately and Higher Level needs about 240 hours against 150. A small cohort makes that uneconomic, so the Higher Level option is withdrawn or merged. Ask the school, in writing, how many students are entered at Higher Level, who teaches the extension content, and whether the two levels share lessons. The answers tell you whether an outside specialist is a convenience or a necessity.

faqs.question: Our school teaches Higher and Standard Level physics in one combined class - what does that cost our son?
faqs.answer: Usually the extensions. A combined class is paced for the larger group, so rigid body mechanics, special relativity, thermodynamics, potential and induction get compressed into the last weeks or set as reading. The Standard Level students are fine; the Higher Level ones meet examined content cold in Paper 2. Ask for the scheme of work, check when the extension topics are scheduled, and target tutoring there.

faqs.question: Which Higher Level physics topics do schools in the Dammam, Khobar and Dhahran cluster most often leave until last?
faqs.answer: The pattern across the Eastern Province mirrors the Kingdom: Theme E nuclear and quantum work and the Theme B thermodynamics extension are taught last and revised least, because the earlier mechanics and fields content eats the timetable. Compound schools also lose teaching days to shift patterns. If your child is in the second Diploma year and has not met entropy or the decay law, start there.

faqs.question: Does a private school's operating licence from the Ministry of Education say anything about Higher Level Physics?
faqs.answer: No. The Ministry licenses private and international schools to operate, and school evaluation and accreditation run through the Education and Training Evaluation Commission, which also approves international accreditation bodies. Neither process guarantees that a particular subject is offered at a particular level in a particular year. Subject availability is a staffing decision inside the school, so ask the school directly and get the answer in writing before you enrol.

faqs.question: What does an evaluation report tell us about the physics teaching our daughter actually gets?
faqs.answer: It tells you about the school as an institution: governance, safeguarding, provision and improvement planning. It does not tell you who is teaching Higher Level Physics this year, whether that teacher has marked for the board, or how many periods the extension content receives. Read the report for the institution and then ask subject-level questions separately: who teaches it, what they taught before, and what last year's Higher Level entry looked like.

faqs.question: What may a tutor do with a Higher Level Physics investigation draft, and what must stay the student's own?
faqs.answer: A tutor may teach the four criteria, work through published exemplars, question the research question until the student can defend it, and comment on a draft by pointing at what a criterion asks for. The student's research question, method, data, analysis and sentences must be theirs. A tutor who edits text into the document has created a malpractice problem rather than a better grade.

faqs.question: How are the four investigation criteria marked, and which one costs Higher Level Physics students most?
faqs.answer: Research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation are each marked out of six, giving twenty-four marks that convert to a fifth of the final grade. Evaluation is consistently the weakest. Students write an apology for their experiment rather than analysing specific limitations against their own data and proposing realistic improvements. That is teachable without anyone touching the writing, and it is usually the cheapest improvement available on the whole component.

faqs.question: Can a tutor suggest the research question for a Higher Level Physics investigation?
faqs.answer: A tutor should not hand one over. What they can do is teach what makes a question workable: a measurable independent variable, a range wide enough to produce a gradient worth analysing, controllable confounders and equipment the school owns. Then they interrogate the student's own proposals until one survives, so the student arrives at a question they can defend to their supervisor.

faqs.question: What does a Physics Extended Essay need that a strong investigation report does not?
faqs.answer: A genuine research argument and much more independent reading. The investigation is a controlled piece of experimental work with four criteria. The Extended Essay is longer, supervised at school, and judged on how well a focused question is researched, argued and reflected on, with formal reflection sessions recorded. A tutor can teach structure, sourcing and how to narrow a question, and can give feedback on drafts; the research and the writing remain the student's.

faqs.question: How does a tutor give feedback on uncertainty analysis without touching the student's own data?
faqs.answer: By teaching the method on other data. Practice sets, past Paper 1B questions and published exemplars all carry uncertainties to propagate, error bars to plot and gradients to read with units. The student then applies the routine to their own results unaided. On their draft, the tutor comments on whether the analysis criterion has been met rather than recalculating anything, which keeps the work demonstrably the student's.

faqs.question: What does a student arriving from a British A-level physics course need to add for Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Three things, usually. First, command-term discipline: outline, explain, determine, deduce and show that each demand a particular shape of answer and a mark scheme pays for that shape. Second, the internal assessment, which has four criteria and a word limit and no A-level equivalent. Third, the parts of Theme E and the Theme B extension that an A-level specification may have covered differently. Mechanics and electricity usually transfer well.

faqs.question: Our son is moving from an American school's physics course into Higher Level - what is missing?
faqs.answer: Typically algebraic density and written precision. Conceptual coverage is often good, but the course may have been taught with lighter mathematics, so logarithmic plotting, small-angle work and multi-step derivations feel new. Writing to a word limit is also new. Set a timed Paper 1B and one Paper 2 extended-response question, mark them against the real scheme, and the gap is visible in forty minutes rather than after a term.

faqs.question: How much of IGCSE Physics 0625 actually transfers into the Higher Level course?
faqs.answer: The vocabulary and roughly the first layer of each theme. What does not transfer is the mathematical treatment: the Diploma expects algebraic manipulation, graph linearisation and uncertainty work that 0625 only gestures at. Students entered for the Core tier, which is capped at a C, usually have the largest gap. Confirm the tier and component list with the school in writing, because tier entry is reversible only before the entry deadline.

faqs.question: What should a family relocating into the Kingdom mid-course ask the new school about physics?
faqs.answer: Three questions, in writing. How many of the required experimental hours are already logged and will any transfer. When is the scientific investigation due and has a research question been approved. Which Higher Level extension topics have already been taught, particularly in Theme D. Those answers decide whether the first term of outside support is catching up on content, rebuilding practical evidence, or both at once.

It is a free trial lesson spent on a recent piece of your child's own marked physics work, with a tutor who teaches Higher Level Physics rather than science in general, and a written starting point naming the component that is costing marks. From there the decision can be priced against the advertised rates above: how many hours, against which paper. intro.heading: The question behind this search is who, not whether
paragraphs: A parent typing this phrase has usually already decided that outside teaching is needed. What they cannot judge is whether the person on the other end of the video call knows Higher Level Physics as an examined course or merely knows physics. Those are different competencies and they produce different lessons. One explains the content again, more patiently and at the student's pace. The other reads a marked script, names the component that is leaking, and teaches the thing a mark scheme pays for.

The distinction is easy to see once you know where Higher Level marks go. Paper 1 splits into 1A, which is multiple choice, and 1B, which is data analysis, and together they carry 36 per cent of the grade. Paper 2 carries 44 per cent in short and extended responses. The scientific investigation, written by the student from their own data and marked on four criteria worth 24 marks in total, carries 20 per cent. Confirm that list in writing with your school's Diploma Programme coordinator.

Each of those three places fails for its own reason, and each reason implies a different competency in the tutor. Paper 1A rewards elimination under time pressure. Paper 1B rewards a mechanical routine with uncertainties, error bars and gradients. Paper 2 rewards obedience to command terms. The investigation rewards an evaluation that analyses rather than apologises. A tutor who can only do the first of those will still fill an hour pleasantly, and the grade will not move.

So this page is built for checking. It says what each component demands, which claims on a tutor profile carry information and which are decoration, how examining or marking experience actually helps, and what a Higher Level Physics lesson looks like on screen when it is being done properly. There is a table of the usual claims with a single verifying question against each, meant to be used in a trial lesson rather than admired. It also says what a qualification in this subject is worth: a physics degree settles the content and says nothing about assessment, while recent teaching of this course at this level settles rather more. Both are worth asking about, and both are easy to ask about badly.

On delivery we are plain. Lessons for families in the Kingdom are one-to-one over live video, on Arabia Standard Time, with the student's own script, graph or spreadsheet shared on screen. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a Saudi address and makes no home visits in Riyadh, Jeddah or the Eastern Province; home visits are a service we offer only in India. The gain is reach: a verified Higher Level Physics specialist is as available in Abha or Jubail as in central Riyadh.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Physics
programmes.description: Five themes at both levels with Higher Level extensions inside each, examined by Paper 1 and Paper 2, plus an experimental programme of around 60 hours containing the scientific investigation and the collaborative sciences project.
programmes.countryNote: In the Kingdom this is the scarcest teaching competency in the sciences. Ask a prospective tutor which Higher Level extension they taught most recently and what the usual error in it is.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme sciences
programmes.description: Integrated sciences marked on four criteria rather than papers. A good Middle Years teacher is not automatically a Higher Level Physics teacher, because nothing in that course is examined by a written paper against a published mark scheme.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools here run the Middle Years Programme without the Diploma above it, so families often need a tutor who can bridge the two rather than one who knows only the destination.

programmes.name: Pre-Diploma IGCSE physics
programmes.description: Cambridge 0625 or Edexcel 4PH1 as separate physics, or physics inside a combined award. A Cambridge Core entry is capped at a C, so tier choice decides whether Higher Level is realistic later.
programmes.countryNote: Most Saudi Higher Level candidates arrive from this route. A tutor who has taught both 0625 and the Diploma can see which gaps are habits from the earlier course rather than new weaknesses.

ib-dp-physics-hl-online-tutor.subjectsIntro: Ask which of these a tutor has taught in the last year. The answers map directly onto what your child is about to meet, and vagueness here is the most useful warning sign a family gets.

subjects.name: Theme A: Space, time and motion
subjects.description: Kinematics, forces, momentum, energy, and at Higher Level rigid body mechanics and special relativity. Ask how they teach angular acceleration.

subjects.name: Theme B: The particulate nature of matter
subjects.description: Thermal transfers, gas laws, the greenhouse effect, current, and at Higher Level thermodynamics and entropy. Usually taught last, so often taught badly.

subjects.name: Theme C: Wave behaviour
subjects.description: Simple harmonic motion, superposition, standing waves, the Doppler effect. Ask how they get a student to argue from a sketched graph.

subjects.name: Theme D: Fields
subjects.description: Gravitational and electric fields, magnetism, and at Higher Level potential, escape speed, orbital energy and induction. The densest extension block in the course.

subjects.name: Theme E: Nuclear and quantum physics
subjects.description: Atomic structure, radioactivity, fission, fusion, stellar processes and the Higher Level decay law. Examined mathematically, revised least.

subjects.name: Paper 1B and practical skills
subjects.description: Uncertainty propagation, error bars, best-fit lines, gradients with units. The clearest test of whether a tutor teaches marks or content.

subjects.name: The scientific investigation
subjects.description: Research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, six marks each. Ask what they will and will not do with a draft.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The co-requisite. A physics tutor who cannot teach logarithmic plotting will stall in Theme E and in half of Paper 1B.
