sections.heading: What a Higher Level Physics mark scheme pays for
paragraphs: Begin with the failure rather than the credentials, because the failure tells you which credential matters. In a properly marked Higher Level mock, the lost marks are rarely spread evenly. They sit in Paper 1A, where a student who understands the physics answers from memory instead of eliminating distractors on vectors and graphs. They sit in Paper 1B, where uncertainty and significant figures are treated as tidiness. They sit in Paper 2, where a six-mark explanation describes instead of explaining and caps itself at two or three.

Each of those is a mark-scheme problem rather than a content problem, and that is the key to hiring. A mark scheme does not award credit for knowing; it awards credit for a named step appearing in a named place. Show that requires the working shown. Determine requires a value with a unit. Explain requires a causal chain, not a description of the outcome. Deduce requires a conclusion drawn from something stated earlier in the answer. The vocabulary is the assessment.

So the competency a family is buying is the ability to read a script against the scheme and say which of those steps was missing. A tutor who has done this will ask for marked work before quoting anything, and will talk about components rather than topics. A tutor who has not will offer to go through the syllabus from the beginning, which is the most expensive way to teach a student who already knows most of it. The first conversation usually settles which one you are talking to.

sections.heading: Which claims on a tutor profile actually carry information
paragraphs: Profiles in this market are written to reassure rather than to inform, so most of what they say needs translating. A physics degree proves the content is secure at a level far above the Diploma; it proves nothing about mark schemes, command terms or the four investigation criteria. Years of experience may mean fifteen years of teaching the same national curriculum. A statement that a tutor covers all sciences usually means the Higher Level extensions in Theme D are not their home ground.

Two claims do carry real information. The first is recent teaching of the course at the level you need, which is checkable by asking which extension topic they taught most recently and what the standard error in it is. The second is marking or examining experience for the board, which is checkable by asking what a particular command term is worth in a six-mark answer and where candidates habitually lose the final two marks. Vague answers to narrow questions are the answer.

Everything else should be treated as decoration until tested. A regulator or board does not approve, accredit or endorse private tutors, and neither does IB Gram claim any such status; the Ministry of Education licenses schools and school evaluation runs through the Education and Training Evaluation Commission. If a listing implies a board relationship, that is a reason for scepticism rather than confidence. Unverifiable success statistics, star ratings without a method and promises about grades belong in the same category.

sections.heading: Five questions for a trial lesson, and what a good answer sounds like
paragraphs: A trial lesson is an interview conducted on real work, so take a recently marked script into it. The first question is simple: looking at this script, which component is costing the most marks and why. A specialist answers with a component and a mechanism within a few minutes. A generalist answers with a topic list. The second question is what they would do in the first four lessons, which should produce a sequence aimed at one or two named weaknesses.

The third question is about Paper 1B. Ask them to talk the student through propagating an uncertainty into a final answer and reading a gradient with its units. This is the fastest discriminator in physics, because the routine is narrow enough that either a tutor owns it or they do not. The fourth is about Paper 2: ask what the difference is between outline, explain and deduce in a mark scheme, and listen for whether the answer is about structure rather than length.

The fifth question is the honesty question, and it is the one families skip. Ask directly what the tutor will not do with an investigation draft or an Extended Essay. The right answer sets a boundary without being asked twice: they will teach the criteria, question the research question, work on exemplars and comment on what a criterion requires, and they will not write, edit or supply any part of the work. Hesitation here is more informative than any certificate.

sections.heading: Examining and marking experience: what it is worth, and what it is not
paragraphs: Examining experience is the most over-sold claim in this market and still the most useful one when it is real. Someone who has marked a component has sat with a mark scheme and hundreds of scripts and knows exactly where candidates stop earning credit. That knowledge transfers directly to Paper 2, where the gap between a competent answer and a credited one is structural, and to the investigation, where the criteria descriptors are read far more literally than students expect.

It transfers less well elsewhere. Marking does not teach anyone how to explain induction to a sixteen-year-old who is frightened of it, and it does not make a tutor patient. Nor is it a proxy for currency: a person who marked a component some years ago may not have taught the current guide, with its five themes, its two-paper structure and its scientific investigation. Both things need asking about separately, and a good tutor will distinguish between them without prompting.

What the claim is never worth is a guarantee. No tutor can promise a grade, a point gain or an admission outcome, and anyone who does is telling a family something false about how boundaries and moderation work. Grade boundaries move between series because they are set against the demand of the papers actually sat, so a tutor who talks in terms of securing specific marks on specific components is describing something real, while one who talks in terms of promised grades is not.

sections.heading: What a Higher Level Physics lesson looks like over live video
paragraphs: Parents reasonably ask whether a subject this diagram-heavy survives a screen. In practice the format suits it, provided the tutor works the way a physics teacher works. The student's own script is shared, not retyped. A shared annotation surface carries free-body diagrams, circuit sketches and graphs, and both parties draw on it. Working is written out in full rather than described, because a derivation that is spoken instead of written is exactly the habit that loses marks in Paper 2.

Data work is where the screen is better than paper. A spreadsheet of the student's own results can be plotted live, error bars added from the uncertainties, and the steepest and shallowest acceptable lines drawn in front of them to show how the gradient uncertainty is obtained. The same file goes home at the end of the lesson. That is awkward to do over a kitchen table with a pencil and far quicker with the file open between two cursors.

A family should expect a few concrete things rather than a promise of engagement: a shared drawing surface in use every lesson, work marked and returned between sessions, past papers and mark schemes provided rather than asked for, and a short written note saying what was covered and what the student owes before next time. Ask whether lessons are recorded and who is able to see them, and settle that answer in writing before the first session rather than discovering it afterwards.

sections.heading: Vetting a tutor on the investigation, where the boundary is strict
paragraphs: The scientific investigation is worth a fifth of the grade and is the place where tutoring can quietly turn into malpractice, so the vetting here is different in kind. It is not about ability but about practice: what this tutor does when a student arrives with a draft two days before the deadline and a weak evaluation. The answer should be an offer to teach the criterion and interrogate the student's own analysis, with no suggestion of supplying sentences, calculations or a conclusion.

The legitimate space is wide and worth knowing in detail, because it lets a family recognise a good answer. A tutor may teach what the four criteria reward, work through published exemplars, question a research question until the student can defend it, point out that a chosen range will not yield a usable gradient, and teach uncertainty propagation on practice data that is not the student's own. They may read a draft and comment on whether a criterion has been met.

What they may never do is write, redraft, edit or produce any part of it, supply the analysis, or hand over a research question. Schools are obliged to report suspected malpractice to the IB rather than settle it internally, and the consequence falls on the student. Keeping dated drafts, the student's own raw data and a short note of what outside help was given is sensible practice, and a tutor who suggests that before being asked has told you something useful.

sections.heading: Checking a tutor against your own school's reality
paragraphs: The last piece of verification is local. A tutor can be excellent and still be working against a scheme of work they have never seen, and in the Kingdom the variation between schools is wide. International and British-curriculum schools set their own calendars and most run three terms, while Ministry schools run two semesters, so the point in the course at which a topic arrives differs between two schools in the same city. The tutor needs the school's sequence, not a generic one.

Staffing matters too. Higher Level Physics is among the first classes affected when a cohort is small, which is why a number of schools here teach the two levels together or hand the subject to a teacher carrying two sciences. A tutor who asks early whether the levels share lessons, which extension topics have been taught, how many experimental hours are logged and when the investigation is due is building a plan. One who does not ask will teach a syllabus instead of a student.

Give a new tutor three documents in the first week: the school's scheme of work or topic sequence, the most recent marked assessment with the mark scheme if the school released it, and the internal assessment timeline. Then agree how often the tutor writes to you rather than to the student. The point of the briefing is not supervision for its own sake; it is so that the first paid hour starts where your child actually is.

faqs.question: How do we brief an outside physics tutor on our school's own scheme of work?
faqs.answer: Send three things in the first week: the topic sequence or scheme of work, the most recent marked assessment with its mark scheme if the school released it, and the internal assessment timeline. Then agree how often the tutor writes to you. Schools here set their own calendars, so the order topics arrive in differs between two schools in the same city, and a tutor working from a generic sequence will teach the wrong fortnight.

faqs.question: Why do schools in the Kingdom often give Higher Level Physics to a teacher carrying two sciences?
faqs.answer: Cohort size. Higher Level Physics needs roughly 240 timetabled hours against 150 at Standard Level, and a small entry makes a dedicated specialist hard to justify. The subject is then combined, shared or added to a teacher already carrying chemistry or biology. That teacher may be excellent, but the extension content in Theme D and the Theme B thermodynamics work usually get the least preparation time.

faqs.question: Our school's physics teacher changes most years - how does an online tutor keep continuity?
faqs.answer: By holding the record the school keeps losing. A tutor who stays across both Diploma years accumulates the marked scripts, the topics covered, the practical hours logged and the investigation timeline, and can brief themselves against a new teacher's sequence in one conversation. Ask for a written note after each lesson and a termly summary; those documents are what survive a staffing change.

faqs.question: What should we ask a school about laboratory time before committing to Higher Level Physics?
faqs.answer: Four questions. How many of the required experimental hours are timetabled rather than aspirational. Who supervises the scientific investigation and how many students they supervise. Whether the collaborative sciences project is scheduled or squeezed. And whether Higher and Standard Level students share practical sessions. The answers predict how much data-analysis teaching your child is likely to need from somewhere outside the school itself.

faqs.question: Which parts of Higher Level Physics do Saudi schools most often leave families to arrange themselves?
faqs.answer: Three recur. Paper 1B data-analysis technique, because practical lessons are spent collecting data and the analysis is set as lightly marked homework. Command-term discipline for Paper 2, which needs one-to-one marking time. And evaluation on the investigation, which is coached in a group when it needs individual attention. None of the three is a school failing; they are the parts that do not fit a class of twenty.

faqs.question: How do we check that a physics tutor understands where supervision ends and tutoring begins?
faqs.answer: Ask what they will not do with a draft. A tutor who understands the boundary answers immediately and specifically: they will teach the criteria, question the research question, work on exemplars and comment on whether a criterion is met, and they will not write, edit or supply any part of the work. A vague or reassuring answer to that question is the warning. Ask it before any payment.

faqs.question: What should a tutor's written feedback on an investigation draft look like?
faqs.answer: Comments about the criteria, not corrections inside the document. Useful feedback reads like this: the evaluation names no specific limitation tied to your own results; the analysis quotes an uncertainty the raw data cannot support; the conclusion does not refer back to the research question. The student then decides what to change and writes it. Feedback that arrives as edited text has crossed a line the school is obliged to report.

faqs.question: Can a tutor be present while a student collects their own experimental data?
faqs.answer: Data collection happens in the school laboratory under the supervisor's arrangements, so in practice a tutor is not present. What a tutor can do is rehearse the method beforehand on practice data, check the student has thought about range, control and repeats, and afterwards teach the analysis routine on the results the student brings. The data, the method and the write-up remain the student's own throughout.

faqs.question: How do we keep a record that our daughter's physics investigation is her own work?
faqs.answer: Keep the dated drafts, her raw data in the form it was recorded, and a short note of what outside help was given and when. Most schools also require reflection or progress meetings with the supervisor, and those notes serve the same purpose. The record is not about suspicion; it means a question about authorship can be answered in minutes with documents rather than with assertions.

faqs.question: What happens if a school questions the outside help a physics student received?
faqs.answer: The school investigates first, and if it suspects malpractice it is obliged to report the case to the IB rather than resolve it quietly. The student carries the consequence, which can reach the whole Diploma rather than one subject. This is why the boundary is worth settling in writing at the start: a tutor who teaches criteria and comments on drafts is defensible, and one who supplied text is not.

faqs.question: How do we verify a tutor can teach both an American approach to mechanics and the IB one?
faqs.answer: Ask them to describe the difference in what is examined rather than in what is taught. A good answer talks about algebraic density, multi-step derivations, writing to a word limit and command-term structure, and gives an example of a question that would be scored differently. A tutor who says the content is the same has answered the easy half of the question and missed the half your child is losing marks on.

faqs.question: Our son changed schools between the Diploma years - can one tutor cover two schemes of work?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is where an outside tutor earns their place, provided they are given both sequences. Ask the new school which extension topics have been taught, how many experimental hours transfer and whether the investigation has an approved research question. Then the tutor maps what the previous school covered against the new one and works the gap. Without those documents the tutor is guessing, however good they are.

faqs.question: What should be checked first when a student moves into another school's Higher Level Physics class?
faqs.answer: The practical record and the investigation. Content gaps are visible in a timed Paper 1B and one Paper 2 extended response, and can be closed in weeks. Missing experimental hours and an unapproved research question cannot be closed by tutoring at all; they need the school's agreement. Ask for both in writing in the first week, then let the diagnostic decide what the teaching should target.

faqs.question: Does a tutor who taught A-level physics need anything extra to teach the Higher Level course?
faqs.answer: Usually two things. The internal assessment, with its four criteria, word limit and strict authorship rules, has no A-level equivalent and is a fifth of the grade. And the command-term structure that a Diploma mark scheme rewards differs from the phrasing an A-level specification uses. Subject content transfers well, particularly mechanics and fields, so the question to ask is about assessment rather than physics.

intro.heading: The same search, asked in four different terms, has four answers
paragraphs: Families type this phrase at very different moments, and the moment changes what a good tutor looks like. In the autumn term of the first Diploma year the useful tutor is the one who rebuilds method: rearrangement, units, how a physics answer is written down. In the spring the useful tutor knows the four investigation criteria. In the second year the useful tutor marks Paper 2 answers against the published scheme. Eight weeks before the May session the useful tutor is the one who says no to several things.

Nobody in this market writes about it that way. Vendor pages describe a general service and leave the family to guess whether it fits the week they are actually in, which is why so many arrangements are bought in the wrong month and judged to have failed. So this page runs forwards through the course, naming at each stage what the course is doing, what usually goes wrong, and the single question that tells you whether the person in front of you can help with that stage rather than with some other one.

The shape of the course sets the rhythm. Standard Level Physics is around 150 teaching hours across two years, covering five themes, with an experimental programme of roughly 40 hours that includes the collaborative sciences project and the scientific investigation. Paper 1, split into 1A multiple choice and 1B data analysis, carries 36 per cent. Paper 2 carries 44 per cent. The investigation carries 20 per cent and is written by the student from their own data. Confirm the components and the internal deadline with your school's coordinator.

On the home-tutor question, a straight answer. In-home private tuition genuinely exists in Riyadh, Jeddah and the Dammam, Al Khobar and Dhahran cluster, agencies quote for it, and for a younger child it has real merits. Judged across a two-year Diploma course it has one structural weakness: a travelling tutor is a local tutor, so the pool is whoever lives within a practical drive, and a cancelled journey in the mock season costs a week nobody gets back.

IB Gram does not send a tutor to a Saudi address and makes no home visits in the Kingdom; home visits are a service we offer only in India. Saudi families are taught one-to-one over live video, on Arabia Standard Time, with the student's own script, graph or spreadsheet shared on screen. That is what lets the tutor be chosen for the stage your child is in rather than for their postcode, and it is why a family in Al Ahsa or Tabuk can be as well served as one in central Riyadh. It also means the slot survives a sandstorm, a traffic jam and a school trip, because nobody has to drive anywhere to teach it.

subjects.name: Theme D: Fields

subjects.name: Theme E: Nuclear and quantum physics

subjects.name: Paper 1B and practical skills

sections.heading: Start from where your child is in the course
paragraphs: Physics support is bought in a particular week of a particular term, and that fact decides more than any claim on a tutor profile. A student in the first autumn term has time and a method problem. A student in the spring of the first year has an investigation to design. A student in the second autumn has mocks arriving and two themes still untaught. A student in the final term has technique to fix and nothing left to learn. The same tutor is not equally good at all four.

Working forwards rather than backwards also changes the conversation with a prospective tutor. Instead of asking whether they teach physics, a parent can ask what they would do in this term, with this much of the course covered, and listen for whether the answer is specific to the stage. A tutor who proposes starting at Theme A in the second autumn has not understood the question. One who asks which themes remain and when the mocks fall has.

The table below sets the course out in order with the question worth asking at each point. It is deliberately short on adjectives and long on timing, because timing is the thing families get wrong. The commonest version of that mistake is waiting: the first year feels like the year there is room to wait, and it is the year in which an hour a week is cheapest and buys the most weeks of effect.

sections.heading: The first Diploma year: the habits that decide the final grade
paragraphs: Most Standard Level physics grades are lost quietly in the first year, in ways that do not show up in a report until much later. The first habit is algebraic: a student who rearranges slowly or by trial will lose marks in every theme, because a physics question asks for a quantity and the route to it runs through manipulation. The second is notational. Units dropped, substitutions not shown and answers quoted to whatever precision the calculator offered are all marks the scheme simply does not award.

The third habit is practical. The experimental programme begins in this year, and a student who records data loosely now will struggle with the investigation later, because the analysis depends on having an uncertainty for every measurement and a range wide enough to be worth plotting. None of these is difficult to teach. All of them take months of repetition, which is exactly what a weekly hour in a year with no examinations at the end of it is good for.

So the tutor you want in this term is not the most impressive examiner in the market. It is someone who will insist on the same small disciplines every week, mark short pieces of work and hand them back, and resist the temptation to lecture on content the school is covering adequately. The test question is the one in the table: can they fix rearrangement inside a physics lesson rather than scheduling a separate mathematics course the family did not ask for?

sections.heading: The investigation window, and the boundary a tutor must not cross
paragraphs: Somewhere in the middle of the course the scientific investigation arrives, and it is worth a fifth of the grade. It is also the one stage where outside help can quietly become malpractice, so the boundary needs to be agreed before the work starts rather than argued about afterwards. The work must be the student's own: their research question, their method, their data, their analysis and their sentences. A school that suspects otherwise is obliged to report the case to the IB rather than settle it internally.

Inside that boundary a tutor can do a great deal. They can teach what each of the four criteria rewards, which is more specific than students expect: research design is largely about controlled variables and a usable range, and evaluation is about limitations tied to the student's own results rather than general apologies. They can work through published exemplars, interrogate a proposed research question until the student can defend it, and teach uncertainty propagation on practice data that is not the student's own.

They can also read a draft and comment on whether a criterion has been met, in the form of comments rather than corrections written into the document. What they cannot do is write, redraft, edit or supply any part of it, hand over a research question, or produce the analysis. A tutor who sets that boundary out before being asked has told you something useful about how they work, and in this market that is a genuine differentiator rather than a formality.

sections.heading: The late themes: fields and nuclear physics arrive when time has gone
paragraphs: Ask any Standard Level physics teacher which themes get squeezed and the answer is consistent: Theme D fields and Theme E nuclear and quantum physics. They sit at the end of most schemes of work, they arrive in the second year alongside mocks and internal assessment deadlines in five other subjects, and the teaching time left for them is whatever the earlier themes did not consume. Students then meet them properly for the first time in revision, which is the worst moment to meet anything.

The content itself is not the hardest in the course at this level, which is what makes the loss avoidable. Theme D at Standard Level is largely conceptual: field patterns, the behaviour of a charge or mass in a field, and the distinction between field strength and force. Theme E is structural: atomic models, decay types, half-life reasoning, and the energy accounting behind fission, fusion and stellar processes. Both reward precise definitions and both appear in Paper 2 in question styles that are easy to rehearse.

The practical consequence for a family is a timing decision. If your child is entering the second year with these themes untaught, the sensible brief for a tutor is to run slightly ahead of the school on them rather than behind, so the class lesson becomes consolidation rather than first contact. Ask a prospective tutor how they would sequence that against the school's own plan; a specific answer means they have done it, and a vague one means they have not.

sections.heading: The final term, and what a good tutor will refuse
paragraphs: In the last stretch before the May session the work changes character. Content teaching stops paying, because there is not enough time to secure anything new, and technique starts paying heavily. The useful sequence is timed papers under real conditions, marking against the published scheme, and then targeted repair of the two or three components where marks are going: usually the Paper 1B data routine, command-term structure in Paper 2, and whichever theme the school taught last.

What a family should expect is evidence rather than reassurance. Scripts marked and returned with the scheme alongside, a short written statement of which components the block is targeting, and a willingness to say that a particular weakness will not be fixed in the time available. A tutor who promises to cover the whole syllabus again in eight weeks is selling comfort. Grade boundaries are set against the demand of the papers actually sat, so no tutor can promise a grade at any point in the year.

Equally important is what a good tutor refuses. This is the term when requests to rescue coursework appear, and the right answer is a plain no, with an explanation of what can be done instead. It is also the term to decline the request to add three more subjects in the final fortnight, because spreading an hour across everything weak is how a family ends up with no component fixed. Pick the two that move the most marks and finish them properly.

sections.heading: What the school staffs, and what it hands back to the family
paragraphs: Private and international schools in the Kingdom are licensed by the Ministry of Education, and school evaluation and accreditation run through the Education and Training Evaluation Commission, which also approves international accreditation bodies. Neither process decides which subjects a particular school offers at which level in a given year. That is a staffing decision taken inside the school, and it is the thing a family actually needs to know before choosing a Diploma science.

In practice three gaps recur. Physics is often taught by someone carrying a second science, which thins preparation time for the themes that arrive late. Standard and Higher Level students are sometimes taught in one class, which paces the lesson for the larger group. And the data-analysis half of the course gets least lesson time, because practical periods are spent collecting results and the analysis is set as homework and marked lightly. None of these is a scandal; all three are predictable.

What follows is a brief rather than a complaint. Ask the school in writing which themes have been taught, how many experimental hours are logged, who supervises the investigation and when it is due, and whether the two levels share lessons. Hand those answers to the tutor in the first week along with the most recent marked assessment. The point is that the first paid hour starts where your child actually is, rather than where a generic syllabus plan assumes they are, and four of those five answers take a single email to obtain.

sections.heading: Checking the person: questions that change with the term
paragraphs: Verification in this market has to be done by the parent, because no regulator or board approves private tutors and nobody should imply otherwise. The good news is that one well-aimed question does more than any certificate. In the first year, ask how they would fix rearrangement inside a physics lesson. In the investigation window, ask what they will not do with a draft. In the second autumn, ask how they mark against a published scheme. In the final term, ask which components they would target and why.

Two general claims are worth probing whenever they appear. The first is subject currency: ask which theme they taught most recently at this level and what the standard error in it is, and listen for a specific error rather than a general comment about understanding. The second is marking experience: ask what a six-mark explain question loses its last two marks on. Someone who has marked for a board answers that immediately, and the answer is about structure.

Then judge the arrangement on evidence after four weeks: has marked work come back, has a written note named what moved, and can the student describe the routine they are supposed to be using. If the answer to all three is no, change the tutor rather than adding hours. A family that treats the first month as a trial rather than a commitment loses a month at worst, which is far cheaper than discovering the mismatch in the final term.

faqs.question: Our daughter's investigation is due next week and the evaluation is thin - what can a tutor legitimately do now?
faqs.answer: Teach the criterion and nothing else. A tutor can explain what evaluation rewards, show it in a published exemplar, and ask her questions about her own results until she can name a specific limitation and a realistic improvement. She then writes it. What a tutor must not do is draft the paragraph, supply the limitation or edit her text, and a deadline does not change that. Plan the window earlier next time.

faqs.question: Is it acceptable for a tutor to teach the investigation criteria from another student's marked exemplar?
faqs.answer: Published exemplars exist for exactly this purpose, and working through one is legitimate and useful. What is not legitimate is a classmate's live or recent work, which raises both a collusion question and a privacy one. Ask where an exemplar came from. A tutor using published material with the marks and examiner comments attached is teaching the standard; one circulating current student work is creating a problem for two families.

faqs.question: Can a physics tutor help with a Theory of Knowledge essay that uses a physics example?
faqs.answer: They can help with the physics and should stop there. A tutor can check that a scientific claim in the essay is accurate and that the example is described correctly, which is genuinely useful. The knowledge argument, the structure and the writing belong to the student and to their Theory of Knowledge teacher. As with any assessed work, feedback is comment rather than correction, and nothing is written into the document.

faqs.question: Who confirms that a Standard Level physics investigation is the student's own work?
faqs.answer: The school does, through the supervising teacher, as part of the internal assessment process, and the student is expected to be able to account for their own data and decisions. Keeping dated drafts, raw data in the form it was recorded and a short note of outside help given makes that straightforward. The record is not about suspicion; it means an authorship question can be answered with documents in minutes.

faqs.question: Do we have to tell the school that our child has a physics tutor?
faqs.answer: Schools differ, so ask rather than assume. Many want to know, both to avoid duplicating support and because the supervisor of an internal assessment is entitled to understand what help a student has had. Telling them has a practical benefit too: a teacher who knows about the tutor will often share the scheme of work and the marked assessments, which makes the tutoring better aimed than it would otherwise be.

faqs.question: Which Standard Level physics themes most often need teaching from outside our school?
faqs.answer: Theme D fields and Theme E nuclear and quantum physics, because both sit at the end of most schemes of work and are taught in the second year against mock papers and other deadlines. The Paper 1B data-analysis skills come a close third, since practical lesson time goes on collecting results. Those three account for most of the outside teaching Saudi families buy for this course.

faqs.question: Why does Theme B thermal physics catch out students who are strong in mechanics?
faqs.answer: Because it is examined on definitions and reasoning rather than on manipulation. A student who is quick with equations can describe heating and temperature loosely, confuse specific heat capacity with latent heat in a two-stage problem, or argue about energy transfer without mentioning the particles. The marks sit in precise statements, which is a different skill from solving for an unknown and needs rehearsing separately.

faqs.question: Where does weak rearrangement first show up in Standard Level physics?
faqs.answer: In Theme A, usually within the first term, and it looks like slowness rather than error. A student who rearranges by trial still arrives at answers, so nothing appears wrong until the questions need two steps under time pressure. It then reappears in Theme C with the wave relationships and in every gradient question in Paper 1B. Fixing it early is cheap; fixing it in the second year costs lesson time that technique needs.

faqs.question: What goes wrong in a Standard Level answer about simple harmonic motion?
faqs.answer: Phase. Students learn the equations and then describe displacement, velocity and acceleration as if they peak together, or sketch a graph without noting where each quantity is zero. Examiners ask for the relationship rather than the formula, so the answer has to say what happens at the extremes and at the midpoint. A sketched graph with the key points labelled earns marks that a paragraph of description does not.

faqs.question: How much of Standard Level physics is memory, and how much is examination technique?
faqs.answer: Less memory than students assume. The relationships are provided in the booklet issued for the examinations, so recall matters mainly for definitions and for the standard explanations in Themes B and E. Most of the recoverable marks sit in technique: answering in the shape the command term sets, showing substitutions, quoting units and handling uncertainties. That is why marked scripts are a better diagnostic than a topic checklist.

faqs.question: Our school runs two semesters and a friend's school runs three terms - does that change when we start?
faqs.answer: It changes the sequencing rather than the principle. Ministry schools run a two-semester year and international and British-curriculum schools set their own calendars, most of them in three terms, so two schools in the same city reach Theme D at different points. Start from your own school's published calendar and scheme of work, and have the tutor plan against that rather than against a general Diploma timeline.

faqs.question: What does it mean for us if the school's physics teacher also teaches chemistry?
faqs.answer: It usually means preparation time is split, and the themes taught last get the least of it. It does not mean the teaching is poor; plenty of excellent science teachers carry two subjects in schools with small cohorts, which is common across the Kingdom. The practical implication is to watch the late themes and the data-analysis work, and to ask early which parts of the course the department expects families to support.

faqs.question: How do compound and camp schools in the Eastern Province differ for physics practical work?
faqs.answer: The timetable is shaped by the employer's rhythm as much as the school's, so laboratory sessions can be blocked rather than weekly and travel days remove teaching time. Families in the Dammam, Al Khobar and Dhahran cluster also commonly live in one city and attend school in another. Both facts affect when experimental hours are logged, which is worth checking before the investigation window arrives.

faqs.question: Our school offers the Middle Years Programme but not the Diploma - how should we plan for physics?
faqs.answer: Plan for a transfer and for a mathematics gap. A number of schools in the Kingdom run the Middle Years Programme without the Diploma above it, so students move at sixteen into a new school, a new scheme of work and a sharper algebraic expectation in the same term. The useful preparation in the final Middle Years year is rearrangement, graph work and precise method writing rather than Diploma physics content.

ib-dp-physics-sl-home-tutor.closingHeading: Tell us which week of the course you are in
ib-dp-physics-sl-home-tutor.closingBody: The most useful thing a family can say at the start is not the grade they want but where the course has reached: which themes have been taught, whether the investigation has an approved research question, and when the mocks fall. From there the brief writes itself, and the trial lesson can be spent on a recently marked script rather than on introductions. Send the school's scheme of work, the latest marked assessment and the two evenings that work on Arabia Standard Time, and we will say plainly what the first four weeks should target.

ib-dp-physics-sl-online-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB Diploma Programme Physics at Standard Level as their main subject, not as an add-on to a general science timetable. Each works from the current Physics guide, the published mark schemes and the data booklet the student will actually be handed in the examination hall.

intro.heading: Four options, one decision, and a series to count backwards from
paragraphs: Most families searching for this do not want a general science tutor. They want somebody who knows that Physics SL now sits in two written papers and one internally assessed investigation, and who can say which of the five themes a student can still afford to be weak in. That is a narrow brief, and it is the reason the search happens at all: the school has one physicist, the physicist has a full timetable, and the student has a mock paper coming back with a grade nobody in the house expected. The honest answer is that the choice is between four things, and only one of them is a tutor. Setting them side by side first saves a term of guessing.

The organising fact on this page is the examination series, and everything useful runs backwards from it. Saudi IB schools sit the May session; Cambridge and Pearson candidates in the Kingdom sit the June series and the November series. Counting backwards from whichever applies gives a family a plan instead of a panic: the investigation is finished and moderated long before the papers, the second year's content lands late, and the last eight teaching weeks are worth more in marks than any three months earlier in the course. Working the plan forwards from today instead produces a reading list; working it backwards produces a timetable. A tutor who cannot tell you where the student sits on that timeline is guessing too.

Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, and that is not a compromise forced by geography. It is what makes a Standard Level Physics specialist available to a family in Tabuk on the same terms as a family in Riyadh. IB Gram does not send tutors to a Saudi address; home visits are a service we offer only in India. What a Saudi family gets instead is a tutor chosen for the subject rather than for the postcode, a slot pinned to Arabia Standard Time, and a shared screen both people write on at the same time, which matters more in Physics than in almost any other subject.

The rest of the page is specific on purpose. There is a backwards calendar with what each stage of the course should have produced, the paper weightings written out so revision time can be allocated against marks rather than against anxiety, the themes where Standard Level candidates lose most of their marks, what the in-home and online markets in the Kingdom advertise per hour and why the numbers differ, and the line a tutor must not cross on the scientific investigation. Nothing on it is a promise about a grade, because a grade is not something any tutor can promise. Everything on it can be checked against a published document.

ib-dp-physics-sl-online-tutor.programmesIntro: Physics SL does not start in the Diploma. The three programmes below are the ones a Saudi family actually moves through, and each one hands the next a specific set of skills, or a specific gap that shows up two years later.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Physics at Standard Level runs across both Diploma years. Two written papers carry the external grade and a scientific investigation carries the rest. Students pick Physics inside Group 4, usually alongside a Mathematics course that decides how comfortable the algebra feels.
programmes.countryNote: Saudi IB schools sit the May session, and a Diploma certificate needs a Ministry of Education equivalency decision before a Saudi university treats it as equivalent to the national secondary certificate.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Sciences in the Middle Years Programme are assessed against criteria rather than papers, which builds investigation skill but not examination stamina. A student arriving in Physics SL from MYP usually knows how to design an experiment and has never written a timed six-mark answer.
programmes.countryNote: Several Riyadh and Jeddah schools run the Middle Years Programme without the Diploma above it, so families change school between Year 11 and Year 12.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: Cambridge IGCSE Physics is tiered at entry: Core is graded C to G, Extended A* to E. A Core entry caps the grade at C however well the papers go. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE grades 9 to 1 instead.
programmes.countryNote: Saudi candidates sit the June and November series. Cambridge's February and March series is available in India only, so pages copied from Indian sites get this wrong.

ib-dp-physics-sl-online-tutor.subjectsIntro: Physics SL is this page's subject, but a Diploma is six subjects and a core, and a weak one drags the total. These are the courses families most often add once the Physics is steady, with the thing each one is actually marked on.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Two papers and a scientific investigation. Paper 1A is multiple choice, Paper 1B is data analysis, Paper 2 is structured and extended response. Most Standard Level marks go missing in Paper 2.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The same two-paper shape. Standard Level candidates lose marks on bonding explanations and on the arithmetic of moles under time pressure.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Heavy on precise terminology and command terms. A correct idea written with the wrong verb scores nothing.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The algebra behind Physics SL. Weakness here shows up as lost method marks in kinematics and circuit questions.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation

sections.heading: The four options a Saudi family is choosing between
paragraphs: The first option is to do nothing extra and let the school carry it. That is the right answer more often than a tutoring page will admit, and it is testable: ask the Physics teacher for the student's last two paper marks broken down by question, not as a single grade. If the teacher can supply that breakdown and has a plan for the weak questions, a tutor adds little beyond reassurance, and the money is better spent elsewhere.

The second is group revision, usually a weekend course close to the series. It is cheap per hour and it works for a student whose problem is coverage rather than technique. It does not work for the much commoner case: a student who understands the physics and keeps writing answers the mark scheme cannot reward. Nobody diagnoses that in a room of fifteen. The third option is an in-home tutor, and in Riyadh, Jeddah and the Eastern Province cluster that pool genuinely exists.

Elsewhere it thins out fast, and even where it exists it is a pool of people who teach Physics, not necessarily people who teach Physics SL. The fourth option is an online specialist, which is what IB Gram provides: one-to-one lessons over live video, chosen for the course rather than the commute. The decision between the third and the fourth is not really about convenience. It is about whether the family wants the strongest Physics SL teacher it can reach, or the strongest one inside a twenty-minute drive.

sections.heading: Physics SL counted backwards from the examination series
paragraphs: Work from the series, not from today. Every Saudi family's version of this timeline is slightly different, because international schools in the Kingdom set their own calendars and most run three terms while Ministry of Education schools run two semesters, but the order of events does not move. The investigation is done before the papers. The second Diploma year carries the harder half of the content. The final eight weeks are technique, not teaching. Everything else is a local variation.

The table below is the version worth printing. Read it right to left if the student is already late: it tells you which stage was skipped, and skipped stages are what a diagnostic lesson is for. A student in the spring term of the first Diploma year who has not started thinking about the investigation is normal. A student in the spring term of the second year in the same position has a problem that eats revision time.

Two dates sit outside the school's control and inside the examinations officer's. Entries for the Cambridge and Pearson June series close several months ahead of the papers, and once the tier or the component list is fixed it is fixed. Ask for both in writing. For the Diploma, the registration and investigation submission windows belong to the Diploma Programme coordinator, and no tutor should be guessing at them on a family's behalf. That is not a disclaimer; it is the one piece of administration that cannot be recovered after the deadline.

sections.heading: What each Physics SL paper is worth, and what that means for revision
paragraphs: Physics at Standard Level is assessed by two written papers and one internally assessed scientific investigation. Paper 1 comes in two parts sat together: Paper 1A is multiple choice, Paper 1B is a set of data-analysis questions built around unfamiliar experimental results. Together they carry 36% of the grade. Paper 2 is structured and extended-response and carries 44%. The investigation carries the remaining 20% and is marked by the teacher and moderated externally.

Those three numbers should decide how a term's revision hours are split, and usually they do not. Families default to re-reading theory, which is Paper 1A work, and Paper 1A is the smallest slice of the smallest paper. The 44% sitting in Paper 2 is won by writing: picking the command term apart, showing the substitution before the answer, drawing the graph the question asked for. Hours moved from re-reading to writing under timing are the cheapest marks on this course.

The data booklet changes how content should be learned. Equations the student will be handed in the examination hall do not need memorising; knowing which one applies, and what each symbol means in the question's own words, does. Standard Level and Higher Level sit different papers of different lengths, so a Higher Level past paper is useful for practice and misleading for timing. Grade boundaries are published after each session and move with how the cohort found the papers, which is why a raw mark means nothing until the boundary is set.

sections.heading: Where Standard Level candidates actually lose the marks
paragraphs: The losses are predictable and they are not evenly spread across the five themes. Space, time and motion goes wrong at the point where a problem needs two equations and a sign convention rather than one equation. Students who can state Newton's laws still drop marks on an inclined plane because the component is resolved the wrong way and nothing after that can be awarded. The marks are lost in the setup, not in the physics.

The particulate nature of matter is where arithmetic goes missing: specific heat capacity and latent heat questions are generous with method marks and unforgiving about units and powers of ten. Wave behaviour punishes vague language, because path difference, phase difference and optical path are three different things and a mark scheme treats them as three different things. Fields is where Standard Level candidates most often confuse a potential with a field strength, and a graph with a gradient.

Nuclear and quantum physics arrives last, is taught fastest, and is the theme most likely to be half-learned when the papers come. It is also the theme with the highest ratio of definitions to calculations, which makes it the cheapest to repair late. The single commonest loss across all five, though, is not a topic at all: it is answering a four-mark question with one sentence. A tutor's first job in Physics SL is usually to make the student write more, not know more, and that is a technique problem with a short fix.

sections.heading: The Sunday-to-Thursday week, and a slot that survives a term
paragraphs: The school week in the Kingdom runs Sunday to Thursday. Friday and Saturday are the weekend. That single fact invalidates most tutoring copy written for a Monday-to-Friday country, and it has a practical consequence: the usable weekday slots are Sunday through Wednesday evenings, because a Thursday evening lesson competes with the start of the weekend and loses.

Arabia Standard Time is UTC+3 and the Kingdom does not change its clocks. A tutor in a country that does will drift by an hour twice a year unless the slot is agreed in Saudi local time and left there. The arithmetic matters when choosing where a tutor sits: India is two and a half hours ahead, so a 7pm lesson in Riyadh is a 9.30pm lesson for the tutor. The United Kingdom is two or three hours behind depending on their own clocks, which makes a Saudi evening a comfortable British afternoon.

Then there is the school run. Riyadh is about an hour across in traffic, so a family in Al Narjis collecting from a school in the north is not starting a lesson at four. The same is true of the Dammam, Al Khobar and Dhahran cluster, where living in one city and schooling in another is routine. During Ramadan school days shorten and study moves later into the evening; the sensible move is to agree the shifted slot before the term starts rather than renegotiating it weekly. Lessons also pause cleanly through the long summer break without losing the slot.

sections.heading: What Physics tutoring is advertised at in the Kingdom
paragraphs: Nobody in this market publishes a clean price, so what follows are other providers' advertised rates with the kind of source each comes from. They are not IB Gram's prices and they are not a market average. Tutoring-platform listings start general online tutoring from around SAR 55 an hour, and budget platforms advertise IGCSE one-to-one from around SAR 35. A tutor-marketplace guide puts general Riyadh private tuition at about SAR 50 an hour for primary and over SAR 200 for senior-school examination subjects.

Tutoring-company listings for IB subject tutoring in Riyadh advertise from around SAR 180, with Higher Level and Advanced Placement premium tracks at roughly SAR 200 to 220. International providers quoting in dollars sit near sixty dollars an hour, which is a different budget once a currency conversion and a package length are applied. The spread between SAR 35 and SAR 220 is not a quality ladder; it is mostly a measure of how specialised the person on the other end is.

Four things move the number, in order of weight. Subject scarcity comes first: a Physics specialist costs more than a general science tutor everywhere, and a Higher Level one costs more again. Marking or examining experience comes second, and it is worth paying for because it buys mark-scheme fluency rather than content. Level comes third, with Higher Level above Standard Level above Middle Years Programme above IGCSE. Travel comes fourth, and it is the one a Saudi family can simply remove: an in-home rate carries the tutor's journey across Riyadh inside the price, and an online rate does not.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation, and the line a tutor must not cross
paragraphs: The internally assessed scientific investigation is 20% of the Physics SL grade and the only part of it the student controls entirely. It is marked by the school against four criteria, research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, and then moderated externally, which means a generous school mark can be pulled back if the written work does not support it.

What a tutor may do with it is narrow and worth stating plainly, because this market contains providers who will not state it. A tutor may teach the physics the investigation rests on. A tutor may explain what each criterion rewards, and may react to a draft the student has already written, pointing at an uncertainty that has not been propagated, a graph with no error bars, a conclusion that restates the data instead of evaluating it. A tutor may also teach a student how to frame a research question narrow enough to answer inside the word limit.

What a tutor must never do is produce any of it. No part of the investigation may be drafted, rewritten or edited by anyone other than the student, not a paragraph, not a caption, not a recalculated table. The same line applies to the Extended Essay, the Theory of Knowledge essay and the Middle Years Programme personal project. A provider who offers anything else is offering academic misconduct, and the consequence lands on the student, not on the provider. Ask any prospective tutor the question directly; the answer tells you what you are buying.

faqs.question: What does the first diagnostic lesson for IB DP Physics SL actually cover?
faqs.answer: It starts with a past-paper question rather than a conversation. The tutor watches the student work through one structured Paper 2 item and one data-analysis item, then probes two or three themes. The output is a written note: which themes are secure, where marks are lost in the writing rather than the physics, and whether the scientific investigation is on schedule. The plan is built from that note.

faqs.question: How soon should a parent expect Physics SL paper marks to move?
faqs.answer: Technique marks move faster than content marks. A student losing marks because four-mark questions are answered in one sentence can gain inside three or four weeks; the fix is a habit, not knowledge. A student missing half of Themes D and E needs a full term, because content has to be taught before it can be examined. Ask the tutor which of the two your child is.

faqs.question: What should a Physics SL tutor's written note after each lesson contain?
faqs.answer: Three things and not much else: what was covered, what the student got wrong and why, and what has been set before the next session. A note saying the lesson went well is worthless. A note saying the student resolved forces along the wrong axis twice, and has been set four inclined-plane questions, is something you can check next week. Ask for the first one in that form.

faqs.question: What happens if my child and the Physics SL tutor do not get on?
faqs.answer: Tell us after the second or third lesson, not after the term. A mismatch is usually not about competence; it is pace, or a tutor who explains in words for a student who needs a diagram. We change the tutor and pass the diagnostic note across, so the second tutor starts where the first left off. There is no charge for the change itself.

faqs.question: Which evening slots work for Physics SL inside a Sunday-to-Thursday school week?
faqs.answer: Sunday through Wednesday evenings, in practice. Thursday evening is the start of the weekend in the Kingdom and attendance drops, and a Friday lesson competes with family time. Most families settle between 5pm and 8pm Arabia Standard Time, after the school run and before homework collapses. In Riyadh, where the drive across the city can take an hour, a 4pm start usually fails.

faqs.question: Our Physics tutor is abroad, so how does the slot survive their clock change?
faqs.answer: By agreeing it in Saudi local time and never in theirs. The Kingdom sits on Arabia Standard Time, UTC+3, and does not observe daylight saving, so a slot written as 7pm Riyadh time is 7pm Riyadh time every week of the year. A tutor in the United Kingdom will find it shifts for them twice a year, and that is theirs to absorb. Get it in writing.

faqs.question: Can a Physics SL lesson be scheduled on a Friday or Saturday in the Kingdom?
faqs.answer: It can, and for some families a weekend morning when nobody is tired beats a Tuesday evening after a long school day. The trade-off is that weekend lessons are easier to cancel, so they suit an intensive block better than a term-long weekly rhythm. If the student is taking two subjects, one Saturday morning and one midweek beats stacking both into a single evening.

faqs.question: Do Physics lessons continue through the shortened school days of Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, with the slot moved rather than cancelled. School days shorten during Ramadan and the family's whole rhythm moves later, so the sensible approach is to agree a shifted time before the month begins and keep the same weekly frequency. Dropping lessons entirely for a month costs more than it saves when the series is close. Where the month overlaps a mock period, a lighter fortnight is realistic.

faqs.question: What percentage of the Physics SL grade does each component carry?
faqs.answer: Paper 1 carries 36%, split between the multiple-choice Paper 1A and the data-analysis Paper 1B, which are sat together. Paper 2 carries 44% and holds the structured and extended-response questions. The scientific investigation carries the remaining 20%, marked by the school and moderated externally. Those three numbers are the only honest guide to how revision hours should be divided, and they usually point at Paper 2.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Paper 1A and Paper 1B in Physics SL?
faqs.answer: Paper 1A is multiple choice across the whole course: fast, broad, and punishing of half-learned definitions. Paper 1B is a data-analysis exercise built on an unfamiliar experiment, and it tests the same skills the scientific investigation tests, including uncertainties, gradients, error bars and whether a conclusion is supported. They are sat in the same session. Students who prepare only for 1A get no practice at 1B.

faqs.question: Which command terms decide marks in Physics SL extended-response questions?
faqs.answer: State, outline, describe, explain, deduce, determine and suggest, and each one buys a different length of answer. State wants a single clause with no justification. Explain wants a causal chain. Deduce and determine want the working shown, because the method carries marks the final number does not. Reading the verb before writing is worth more marks here than any single topic.

faqs.question: Why do Physics SL grade boundaries move from one session to the next?
faqs.answer: Because boundaries are set after the papers are marked, not before they are sat. If a Paper 2 turns out harder than intended, the mark needed for each grade comes down; if it was gentle, it goes up. The consequence is that a raw mark on a past paper means nothing until it is read against that session's own boundary. Use the boundary published with the paper being practised.

faqs.question: How is a predicted grade for Physics SL decided, and can a tutor change it?
faqs.answer: The school decides it, using the student's own work: mocks, class assessments, the investigation draft. An outside tutor has no part in issuing it and should never imply otherwise. What a tutor can do is make the evidence better before the prediction is made, which usually means a well-timed mock and a cleaner investigation. If a prediction looks wrong, that conversation belongs with the subject teacher.

faqs.question: Is the Physics data booklet allowed in both Physics SL written papers?
faqs.answer: The data booklet is available in the written papers, which changes what is worth memorising. Equations handed to a student do not need learning; recognising which equation a question is describing does, and so does knowing what every symbol means. Standard Level candidates lose marks hunting for the right formula under time pressure more often than they lose them not knowing it.

ib-dp-physics-sl-online-tutor.closingHeading: Start where the student actually is
ib-dp-physics-sl-online-tutor.closingBody: If the series is a long way off, a weekly slot alongside the school's scheme of work is the cheapest version of this and the one that moves a Physics SL grade furthest. If the series is close, a shorter intensive block aimed at Paper 2 writing and timed papers is the honest answer. Either way the first step is the same: a free trial lesson, a written diagnostic, and a plan counted backwards from the session the student sits.

ib-dp-physics-sl-tutor.tutorsIntro: Matching for Standard Level Physics starts with two facts: which themes the school has reached, and which evenings are genuinely free after the school run. A tutor who cannot hold the second reliably is the wrong match however good the first looks.

intro.heading: The decision is which option survives a Saudi school week
paragraphs: A family looking for Standard Level physics support is usually choosing between four things, not one. There is the school's own clinic or subject surgery, which is already paid for inside the fee. There is a group revision course, bought per seat and per block. There is a private tutor who travels to the house, which is a real market in Riyadh, Jeddah and the Dammam cluster. And there is one-to-one teaching over live video. All four can teach physics. They do not all survive a Saudi term.

The thing that kills most arrangements is the calendar rather than the teaching. The school week here runs Sunday to Thursday, with Friday and Saturday as the weekend, so the usable slots are Sunday through Wednesday evenings and the weekend proper. The Kingdom runs on Arabia Standard Time, three hours ahead of Coordinated Universal Time, and it does not observe daylight saving. A tutor based in a country that does will see the same lesson land an hour differently in their own day twice a year, and the family is the one who notices.

Standard Level Physics itself is a two-year, 150-hour course covering five themes: space, time and motion; the particulate nature of matter; wave behaviour; fields; and nuclear and quantum physics. It is examined by Paper 1, which splits into 1A multiple choice and 1B data analysis and carries 36 per cent, and Paper 2, which carries 44 per cent in short and extended responses. The scientific investigation, which the student designs and writes from their own data, carries the remaining 20 per cent. Confirm that component list with your school's Diploma Programme coordinator.

What that structure means for scheduling is that the work is continuous rather than seasonal. The investigation sits in the middle of the course, the experimental programme accumulates across both years, and the data-analysis skills in Paper 1B only become automatic through repetition. An hour a week across two years does more for a Standard Level student than a block of twenty hours bought in the final term, and it is usually cheaper spread out than compressed, because advertised rates in this market tend to rise as a series approaches.

So the recommendation this page builds towards is a single defended weekly hour, pinned to Arabia Standard Time, with a tutor whose own working week makes a Saudi school evening normal rather than heroic. Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a Saudi address and makes no home visits in the Kingdom; home visits are a service we offer only in India. That is also what frees the search from a twenty-minute driving radius around your own district.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Physics at Standard Level
programmes.description: Around 150 teaching hours over two years, five themes, an experimental programme of roughly 40 hours that includes the scientific investigation and the collaborative sciences project, and two written papers in the May session.
programmes.countryNote: Most Saudi IB schools sit the May session, so the second Diploma year runs short. A weekly slot started in the first year has twice as many weeks to work with as one started after the winter.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme sciences
programmes.description: Integrated sciences marked on four criteria rather than papers, with inquiry and practical work at the centre. It builds investigation habits, but not the algebra or graph work that Standard Level physics assumes from the start.
programmes.countryNote: A fortnightly slot is usually enough at this stage, and the useful target is algebraic fluency rather than physics content. Several schools here run this programme without the Diploma above it.

programmes.name: Pre-Diploma IGCSE physics
programmes.description: Cambridge 0625 or Edexcel 4PH1 as separate physics, or physics inside a combined award. Tier choice matters: a Cambridge Core entry is capped at a C, which closes the door on a comfortable start to Standard Level later.
programmes.countryNote: British-curriculum schools outnumber IB ones across the Kingdom, so the IGCSE year is where most Saudi Standard Level physics students are made or lost. Confirm the tier with the school in writing.

ib-dp-physics-sl-tutor.subjectsIntro: Standard Level Physics is one timetable line and five teaching blocks underneath, plus two assessment skills that sit outside the content. These are what a weekly hour gets spent on across the two years.

subjects.name: Theme A: Space, time and motion
subjects.description: Kinematics, forces, momentum and energy. Taught first, which is why a weak algebra start shows up here before it shows up anywhere else.

subjects.name: Theme B: The particulate nature of matter
subjects.description: Thermal energy transfers, the gas laws, the greenhouse effect and electric current. Definitions in this theme are examined strictly.

subjects.name: Theme C: Wave behaviour
subjects.description: Simple harmonic motion, wave models, superposition, standing waves and the Doppler effect. Graph and phase reasoning carry the marks.

subjects.name: Theme D: Fields
subjects.description: Gravitational and electric fields, magnetic effects and motion in a field. The Higher Level extensions are absent, so the Standard Level treatment is conceptual.

subjects.name: Theme E: Nuclear and quantum physics
subjects.description: Atomic structure, radioactivity, fission, fusion and stellar processes. Taught last in most schemes, so the easiest theme to meet unprepared.

subjects.name: Paper 1B and practical skills
subjects.description: Uncertainties, error bars, lines of best fit and gradients with units. Narrow, mechanical and the quickest marks to recover.

subjects.name: The scientific investigation
subjects.description: The student's own investigation, marked on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation at six marks each.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The usual mathematics partner for Standard Level physics. Where it is weak, physics marks go first, particularly on gradients and rearrangement.

sections.heading: The four options a Standard Level physics family is choosing between
paragraphs: Start with what is already paid for. Most international schools in the Kingdom run some form of subject clinic, and a Standard Level student who is merely behind on one theme often needs nothing more than to attend it with specific questions. It costs nothing extra and it is taught by the person who sets the internal assessments. Its limit is that it repeats the class explanation at the class pace, which does not help a student whose problem is a component rather than a topic.

The second option is a group revision course, sold per seat in blocks before a series. These give structure and coverage and are reasonable value for a student who has drifted across several themes. What they cannot do is target one weak component, because the content is fixed before anyone has seen your child's marked work. The third option is a private tutor who travels to the house. Agencies quote for this, and for younger students it has obvious merit, but the pool is whoever lives within a practical drive.

The fourth is one-to-one teaching over live video, which removes the driving radius from the problem and leaves scheduling as the only real constraint. For Standard Level physics the honest recommendation is the school clinic plus one defended weekly hour online, with a group course only if the student is behind in several subjects at once. The rest of this page explains the scheduling arithmetic that decides whether the weekly hour survives, because an arrangement that collapses in the second month has cost more than it bought.

sections.heading: The Sunday-to-Thursday week, and the slots that actually survive
paragraphs: Saudi school weeks run Sunday to Thursday. Friday and Saturday are the weekend, which means the teaching evenings are Sunday through Wednesday, Thursday is the start of the weekend and already loose, and Friday and Saturday behave like a British Saturday and Sunday. Almost every piece of tutoring copy written for an Indian or British audience assumes the opposite, which is how families end up with a Monday-to-Friday timetable that fits nobody and a tutor who disappears on the wrong two days.

Within that week, the workable window is narrower than it looks. The school day ends early, but the run home in Riyadh or along the Jeddah coastal spine can absorb an hour, sports and Arabic or Quran classes occupy the early evening in many families, and a sixteen-year-old is not learning Theme C phase relationships at ten at night. In practice the usable band is the early to mid evening, which is also when every other family in the Kingdom wants the same tutor.

That congestion is the argument for fixing a slot early and defending it. A Standard Level physics student needs the hour to be boring and automatic: the same evening, the same time, the same tutor, booked for the term rather than negotiated weekly. The table below sets out what that Saudi evening looks like in the tutor's own country, because a slot that is a normal working evening at both ends is the one that is still running in the final term.
