sections.heading: Arabia Standard Time does not move, and other clocks do
paragraphs: The Kingdom sits at Coordinated Universal Time plus three hours and does not observe daylight saving, so Saudi local time is the same all year. That sounds like a simplification and it creates the single most common scheduling failure in cross-border tutoring. A slot agreed in a tutor's own time zone will shift by an hour against the Saudi clock when that country changes its clocks, which happens twice a year in Europe and North America and not at all here.

The fix is mechanical: agree the lesson in Saudi local time and write it down that way. Six o'clock on a Sunday evening in Riyadh is six o'clock whatever Europe is doing. Tutors working across borders are used to this, and a good one will raise it before the first lesson. If the arrangement is instead recorded in the tutor's own time, somebody has to remember to move it, and the lesson that gets missed is usually the one in the week the clocks changed.

The same logic applies to the parts of the year that move. The autumn break, the midyear break and the long summer all interrupt a weekly slot, Ramadan shortens school days and shifts evening study patterns because it moves earlier against the Gregorian calendar each year, and school calendars differ between two schools in the same city. None of that is a reason to abandon the slot. It is a reason to agree in advance what happens to it during each break, and to book it as a term rather than as a string of single lessons.

sections.heading: What Standard Level Physics asks for, paper by paper
paragraphs: Paper 1 is the shorter examination and carries 36 per cent of the grade. It comes in two parts. Paper 1A is multiple choice, and it rewards elimination under time pressure rather than recall: the distractors are built from the errors students actually make, particularly in resolving vectors and reading graphs. Paper 1B is data analysis and experimental work, and it rewards a mechanical routine with uncertainties, error bars, best-fit lines and gradients quoted with their units.

Paper 2 carries 44 per cent and is where most Standard Level grades are decided. The questions run from short answers to extended responses, and the command term controls the mark. Outline, describe, explain, determine, deduce and show that each demand a particular shape of response, and a mark scheme awards credit for named steps appearing in named places rather than for general understanding. A student who describes when the paper says explain has written a reasonable paragraph and earned half the marks available.

The scientific investigation carries the final 20 per cent. The student designs it, collects their own data and writes it up to a word limit, and it is marked on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation at six marks each. Standard Level students are not examined on the Higher Level extensions, so the content load is lighter, but the assessment demands are identical in kind. Confirm the component list and the internal assessment deadline in writing with the school, because both decide what a weekly hour should be spent on.

sections.heading: Where Standard Level students lose marks, and what a weekly hour fixes
paragraphs: The pattern in marked Standard Level scripts is consistent enough to plan around. The first loss is algebraic rather than physical: a student who cannot rearrange confidently will lose marks in every theme, because physics questions ask for a quantity and the route to it runs through manipulation. The second is definitional. Theme B in particular examines definitions strictly, and an approximate definition earns nothing even when the surrounding understanding is sound.

The third loss is the data question, and it is the most recoverable. Uncertainty propagation, plotting error bars, drawing a credible line of best fit and reading a gradient with units are narrow skills that respond quickly to repetition. The fourth is command-term discipline in Paper 2, which also responds to practice, but only if someone marks the answers against the real scheme and insists on the structure rather than praising the content.

That ordering is what makes a weekly hour the right purchase rather than a block. Algebra and definitions need repetition over months. The data routine needs a short, intense burst and then maintenance. Command-term work needs marked scripts coming back week after week. None of those is satisfied by twenty hours in the final term, and all of them are satisfied by one hour a week with marked work in between. The grade follows the habits, which is why the calendar matters as much as the teaching does. A slot that runs for two years quietly beats a dramatic rescue in the final weeks.

sections.heading: When to start, from the Middle Years Programme to the final term
paragraphs: In the Middle Years Programme the useful work is not physics at all. A fortnightly slot aimed at algebraic fluency, graph reading and writing a method precisely will do more for a future Standard Level grade than early exposure to content, because the Middle Years sciences are marked on criteria rather than on papers and the gap that opens later is mathematical. Students arriving into the Diploma from this route are usually comfortable with investigation and uncomfortable with rearrangement.

The IGCSE years are where the decision is made. Tier choice on a Cambridge entry is a hard constraint, since Core is capped at a C and Extended is the realistic route into a Diploma science, and tier entry is reversible only before the entry deadline. Support here should target the Extended paper and the mathematics behind it rather than the physics syllabus, and the question to ask the school in writing is which tier your child is entered for and why.

In the first Diploma year a weekly hour is cheap insurance and buys the most weeks. In the second it is triage, and the first job is a timed diagnostic rather than a syllabus sweep. Starting in the final term before the May session is not pointless, but what it can realistically deliver is examination technique, the data routine and command-term discipline rather than two years of content. Advertised rates also tend to firm up as a series approaches, which is one more argument for booking early.

sections.heading: After the Diploma: equivalency, Qudurat and Tahsili
paragraphs: This is the part of the pathway that almost no vendor page in this market covers, and physics sits in the middle of it. A foreign or international school certificate, including an IB Diploma, needs an equivalency decision from the Ministry of Education before a Saudi university treats it as equivalent to the Saudi secondary certificate. The same applies to A Levels and to an American high school diploma. It is an administrative step with its own documentation, and families who discover it late lose weeks they did not budget.

Alongside it sit the Qiyas tests, run by the National Center for Assessment under the Education and Training Evaluation Commission. Qudurat, the General Aptitude Test, measures verbal and quantitative reasoning rather than syllabus content and can be sat in Arabic or English. Tahsili, the Achievement Test, covers the science-stream subjects including physics, and its content follows the Saudi national curriculum. That last detail is the one that matters: the material overlaps a Diploma physics course, but the framing and the expected approach do not.

Which is why international-curriculum students often find Tahsili harder than their own examinations, and why a Standard Level physics student planning to apply within the Kingdom should look at the Tahsili syllabus rather than assume their course covers it. Universities publish their own admission criteria combining school results with these tests, and those criteria differ by university and by programme. We publish no thresholds and no weighting formulas here; read the university's own published criteria, because that is the only version that governs.

faqs.question: Should Standard Level physics support start in the first Diploma year or the second?
faqs.answer: The first, if the choice is open. A slot started early has roughly twice the number of teaching weeks before the May session, and it catches the algebra and definition problems while they are still cheap to fix. Starting in the second year is triage: useful, but the first job becomes a timed diagnostic and the plan narrows to technique and the data routine rather than content.

faqs.question: What should a Middle Years Programme student build before Standard Level physics?
faqs.answer: Algebraic fluency, graph reading and precise method writing. Middle Years sciences are marked on criteria rather than papers, so students usually arrive confident with investigation and shaky with rearrangement, and physics asks for rearrangement in every theme. A fortnightly slot aimed at the mathematics does far more for a future physics grade at this stage than early exposure to Diploma content ever does.

faqs.question: Is it worth starting Standard Level physics lessons in the final term before the May session?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided the expectation is honest. What a final term can deliver is examination technique, the Paper 1B data routine and command-term discipline, all of which move marks. What it cannot deliver is two years of content. Book early, because the weeks before a series are the ones every family wants, and advertised rates in this market tend to firm up as a series approaches.

faqs.question: What should a Standard Level physics student do in the break between the two Diploma years?
faqs.answer: Three things, and none of them is a syllabus sweep. Finish or consolidate the scientific investigation while there is time to think rather than to rush. Secure the data-analysis routine, which is narrow enough to learn properly in a few sessions. And rebuild whichever theme the first year left weakest, usually Theme A mechanics or Theme B definitions. Two sessions a week for a few weeks is plenty.

faqs.question: When is it worth adding a second subject alongside Standard Level physics?
faqs.answer: When the physics slot has stopped being the thing that worries you and the marked work shows the routine holding. Adding a subject earlier usually splits attention and both move slowly. If two subjects are weak at once, a longer weekend session covering both in one sitting is easier to sustain than four separate weekday evenings in a Sunday-to-Thursday week.

faqs.question: How is Standard Level Physics assessed, paper by paper?
faqs.answer: Paper 1 carries 36 per cent and has two parts: 1A multiple choice and 1B data analysis and experimental work. Paper 2 carries 44 per cent in short and extended responses. The scientific investigation, designed and written by the student from their own data, carries 20 per cent and is marked on four criteria worth six marks each. Confirm the component list with your school's coordinator.

faqs.question: What does Standard Level physics Paper 2 ask for that Paper 1 does not?
faqs.answer: Structure. Paper 1 asks for a correct selection or a correct value; Paper 2 asks for a written answer whose shape matches the command term. Explain wants a causal chain, determine wants a value with a unit and the working shown, deduce wants a conclusion drawn from something stated earlier. The physics may be identical to a Paper 1 item and the marking entirely different.

faqs.question: Why do Standard Level Physics grade boundaries move between examination series?
faqs.answer: Because boundaries are set against the demand of the papers actually sat, after the scripts have been marked. A harder paper produces lower boundaries and an easier one higher boundaries, so a raw mark does not map to a fixed grade across series. This is also why no tutor can promise a grade: what can be promised is work on named components, which is what moves a raw mark.

faqs.question: How is a predicted grade for Standard Level Physics decided, and what is it used for?
faqs.answer: The school decides it, usually from internal assessments, mock papers and the teacher's professional judgement of likely performance in the May session. It is sent to universities as part of an application and is not a promise to the student or from the student. If a predicted grade looks wrong, ask the school which evidence it rests on; the answer is a list of marked work, and that list is where tutoring can change something.

faqs.question: What does a Standard Level physics mark scheme reward that a good textbook answer does not?
faqs.answer: Named steps in named places. A textbook explanation can be complete, elegant and earn three of six marks because it never states the relationship the scheme was looking for or never shows a substitution. Mark schemes award credit point by point, which means answering in the structure the command term sets is worth more than writing more. This is learnable in a term with marked scripts coming back weekly.

faqs.question: Why does a Diploma with Standard Level physics still need Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: Because equivalency is about the certificate, not the subjects. A foreign or international school qualification, including the IB Diploma, needs an equivalency decision from the Ministry before a Saudi university treats it as equal to the Saudi secondary certificate. A Levels and American high school diplomas go through the same step. It is administrative rather than academic, and families who leave it late lose weeks in an application cycle.

faqs.question: Does Tahsili cover physics a Standard Level student has not actually studied?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and that is the useful warning. Tahsili covers the science-stream subjects including physics, and its content follows the Saudi national curriculum rather than the Diploma. The topics overlap, but the framing, the expected method and the emphasis differ, which is why international-curriculum students often find it harder than their own papers. Read the published Tahsili syllabus against your child's course rather than assuming coverage.

faqs.question: Does taking physics at Standard Level rather than Higher Level limit an engineering application?
faqs.answer: It can, and the constraint comes from the university rather than from the IB. Competitive engineering and science programmes often state subject prerequisites at Higher Level, and mathematics choice matters at least as much as physics. The honest answer is to read the published entry criteria of the specific universities and programmes under consideration, in the year of application, rather than relying on any general rule a tutoring page could give.

faqs.question: How early should a Standard Level physics student start preparing for the Qiyas tests?
faqs.answer: Early enough that it does not collide with the final term of the Diploma. Qudurat tests verbal and quantitative reasoning rather than syllabus content, so it is prepared for differently from a physics paper, and Tahsili needs reading against the national curriculum. Families who plan both into the first Diploma year avoid a clash with internal assessment deadlines. Check the registration arrangements with the National Center for Assessment directly.

ib-dp-physics-sl-tutor.closingHeading: Pick the evening first, then the tutor
ib-dp-physics-sl-tutor.closingBody: For Standard Level physics the arrangement that survives a Saudi term is simple: one hour a week, the same evening, written down in Arabia Standard Time, with a tutor whose own working week makes that hour ordinary. Start with a free trial lesson on a recently marked script, take the written starting point it produces, and then fix the slot for the term rather than negotiating it weekly. Tell us which themes the school has covered, which evenings are genuinely free after the school run, and whether the weekend suits you better.

ib-dp-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Diploma subjects at both levels and are listed against the year of the course they are strongest in. A DP1 student who needs the foundations rebuilt and a DP2 student eight weeks from the May session are different jobs, and matching them to the same person is how a weekly hour gets wasted.

intro.heading: The Diploma is twenty-four months long, and support has to be planned that way
paragraphs: Most families hire a Diploma tutor in a hurry, in the second year, after a mock paper comes back badly. That is understandable and it is late. The Diploma is a single two-year course with a shape: content front-loaded into the first year, internal assessment work started in the first year and finished early in the second, predicted grades produced in the second year from evidence gathered before them, and a final term that is almost entirely technique. Where a student sits in that shape determines what a weekly hour should be used for, and the answer in DP1 is not the answer in DP2.

The logistics come first on this page because they decide everything after them. A Diploma arrangement has to survive two academic years, which means roughly seventy to eighty weekly sessions, two long summers, two Ramadan periods that fall in different parts of the course, school trips, mock weeks and at least one family travel disruption. A slot that works brilliantly for six weeks and then becomes negotiable every third week is not support; it is a series of appointments. The families who get the most out of a DP tutor are the ones who treat the slot like a timetabled lesson.

The second logistical fact is the week itself. Schools here run Sunday to Thursday, with Friday and Saturday as the weekend. Sunday and Monday evenings are the two most valuable slots in a Saudi Diploma week, because teaching lands before the week's work is written rather than after it has been handed in. They are also the two evenings a tutor on a Monday-to-Friday school timetable somewhere else cannot hold. Asking about a tutor's own working week, not only their time zone, is the single most useful question at booking.

The third is Arabia Standard Time, UTC+3, which does not change. That is an advantage. Pin the slot in Saudi local time, write it that way in the confirmation, and let the tutor absorb any clock change in their own country. Do the opposite — agree the slot in the tutor's time — and it will drift twice a year, and in a two-year arrangement that means four unannounced shifts, each of which costs a lesson while somebody works out what happened.

What follows is the Diploma counted through: what DP1 is for, what the gap between the two years decides, what arrives all at once in the DP2 autumn term, how predicted grades are produced, and what the final weeks before the May session should actually contain. No calendar year is named anywhere on this page, because your child's school sets its own dates and the examinations officer and the Diploma Programme coordinator hold the real ones.

Lessons are delivered online, one to one, over live video. IB Gram does not send a tutor to an address in the Kingdom; home visits are a service we run only in India. Tutors teach, review and give feedback on the student's own Internal Assessment, Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge work, and produce no part of it.

ib-dp-tutor.programmesIntro: The Diploma is one course, but it is four different jobs for a tutor depending on where the student is standing in it. These are the four, with what each stage demands of a weekly slot.

programmes.name: The year before the Diploma starts
programmes.description: The most cost-effective point to buy teaching and the one almost nobody uses. What matters here is algebraic fluency, writing at length under time, and the independent research habit that Internal Assessment will demand. A student who arrives in DP1 slow at manipulating expressions will be slow in every mathematics and science paper for two years, and that is not a Diploma problem; it is an earlier one carried forward.
programmes.countryNote: In the Kingdom this stage is complicated by route. Students reach the Diploma from MYP 5, from Cambridge IGCSE, from an American middle route and from MoE schooling, and each arrives missing something different. The single most useful thing a Saudi family can do in the break before DP1 is find out which of those gaps applies to their child, rather than assuming the school's offer letter means the student is ready.

programmes.name: The first Diploma year
programmes.description: Content-heavy and deceptively quiet. The papers are two years away, school assessments are frequent but low-stakes, and a student can coast through the first two terms without the gap showing. Internal Assessment work starts in most subjects during this year, Theory of Knowledge teaching begins, and the Extended Essay is chosen and supervised from the spring term onwards. Support here is foundational: fluency, note discipline, and writing to command terms early.
programmes.countryNote: DP1 is also when subject choices turn out to be wrong, and the window for changing them is short and school-specific. A student who took Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level because the application said so, and is drowning in it by the spring term, has a decision to make with their coordinator. A tutor's honest read on whether the level is recoverable is worth more at that moment than any amount of extra practice.

programmes.name: The second Diploma year
programmes.description: Crowded from the first week. Internal Assessment deadlines in several subjects arrive within weeks of each other, the Extended Essay reaches final submission, the Theory of Knowledge essay runs alongside, university applications are live, and mock papers are sat in the middle of all of it. Teaching in DP2 is triage: deciding what to work on, in what order, with how much time, and accepting that not everything can be first.
programmes.countryNote: DP2 is when a weekly slot proves whether it was properly set up. A family that pinned the hour in Arabia Standard Time, chose a tutor whose own week leaves Sunday and Monday free, and kept the slot through the summer arrives in this year with a working arrangement. A family that books in the DP2 autumn term is competing for the same evenings as everybody else in the Gulf, which is why late requests are the hardest ones to fill well.

programmes.name: Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS
programmes.description: The core runs in parallel with everything else and contributes points through the matrix combining Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay. Both are marked against published criteria, both are supervised at school, and both are where students lose points they could have kept. CAS is not graded but is a completion requirement, and an incomplete CAS record is a problem a tutor cannot solve in the final term.
programmes.countryNote: Core work is where the academic-honesty boundary matters most and where this market behaves worst. A tutor may teach research method, explain the criteria, challenge an argument and give feedback on a student's own draft. A tutor may not write or restructure any part of it. Saudi families are offered the other thing routinely; a school that detects it is handling a malpractice case, which is not something a better grade elsewhere repairs.

ib-dp-tutor.subjectsIntro: Each Diploma subject has its own two-year rhythm: when the internal work starts, what the second year adds, and which term quietly decides the grade. These are the subjects Saudi families most often hire for, read that way.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The DP1 content decides the DP2 outcome more than in any other subject. Students who leave the first year without fast algebra and confident calculus spend the second year slow on every question. At Higher Level the extension material and the extended-reasoning paper arrive late in the course, which is exactly when there is least time to absorb them.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The exploration is the piece students most often start late, and a weak dataset chosen in the DP1 summer cannot be rescued in the DP2 spring. The course rewards interpretation of output over mechanics, so the useful DP2 work is writing about results rather than producing more of them.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The internal investigation is usually designed and run in DP1, which means the uncertainty and data-handling teaching has to happen then. Higher Level extension topics land in the second year, and the recurring DP2 problem is mathematical rather than conceptual: logarithmic scales, gradients with units, and reasoning written out in full.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms are the DP2 pressure point and energetics the DP1 one. The internal investigation needs a measurable variable chosen early, because a topic selected in haste produces data nothing can be concluded from. Data booklet fluency is a two-year habit, not a revision task.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content volume makes DP2 feel impossible if DP1 notes were never organised. The statistical treatment of the investigation is where Higher Level candidates lose marks earned in the laboratory, and it is taught once in the first year and then assumed. Command-term discipline separates a four-mark answer from a seven-mark one throughout.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: The internal portfolio commentaries are written across both years and are the most controllable marks in the subject. Diagrams carry credit on their own. Evaluation is the component students run out of time to teach themselves, so it belongs in the DP1 spring term rather than in the final eight weeks.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The research project at Higher Level needs a real organisation and real material, chosen in DP1 and worked through the summer. Students who delay it into the DP2 autumn term collide with every other internal deadline at once. Written answers are capped by failure to anchor a framework to the stimulus.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The individual oral is prepared in the second year from works studied across both, so DP1 note-taking determines how much there is to work with. Paper 1 is unseen analysis and improves slowly with weekly practice rather than quickly with revision. The Higher Level essay rewards a planned argument over a complete work.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: The historical investigation is a DP1 or early-DP2 piece, and the prescribed subject and regional option chosen by the school decide what reading is relevant. Source work in the first paper is a separate skill from essay writing and is best taught early, while there is still time for it to become a habit.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The exhibition comes in the first year and the essay in the second, and both are marked against published criteria. Students who treat TOK as opinion score badly in both. The prescribed title has to be answered as written, which sounds obvious and is the single most common reason a competent essay loses points.

ib-dp-tutor.regionsTitle: Where DP students are, and what their week looks like
ib-dp-tutor.regionsIntro: Diploma provision is spread unevenly across the Kingdom, and the practical question in each place is the same: what time can a lesson actually start, and will that hold for two years? These are the cities and regions this request comes from, read as a scheduling problem.

regions.name: Riyadh
regions.note: The deepest Diploma provision in the Kingdom and an hour across in traffic. The school run, not the school day, sets the earliest workable slot, so DP families here usually settle on a slot from six o'clock onwards and keep it for both years.

regions.name: Jeddah
regions.note: Schooling spread along a coastal spine from the historic centre north to Obhur. A student at a school at one end and a family home at the other loses real time daily, which pushes the realistic DP slot later and makes a fixed hour worth more than a flexible one.

regions.name: Dhahran, Al Khobar and Dammam
regions.note: One conurbation and one school market, with Diploma provision in some campuses and not others. Compound and camp routines here produce early evenings and settled timetables, which is why two-year slots hold unusually well in this cluster.

regions.name: Jubail
regions.note: An industrial city with shift patterns in many households. A parent's rotation can decide which evening is reliable, so DP families here benefit most from agreeing the slot against the rotation rather than against the school day.

regions.name: Makkah and Madinah
regions.note: Limited senior international provision, with Makkah roughly 80km east of Jeddah. Pilgrimage seasons shape the local calendar and the practical availability of evenings, so DP slots here are worth agreeing a term at a time rather than week by week.

regions.name: Abha and Khamis Mushait
regions.note: Twin cities about 25km apart in 'Asir at altitude, sharing a catchment. A Diploma student here may be one of very few in their subject combination, which makes the weekly outside hour the main source of subject-specific teaching rather than a supplement to it.

regions.name: Tabuk, NEOM and AlUla
regions.note: Growing fast with newly arriving professional families and mid-course transfers into DP1 and even DP2. The first job is usually a diagnostic rather than a weekly slot, because nobody yet knows which topics the student has covered.

regions.name: Al Ahsa and the inland Eastern Province
regions.note: An hour and a half from the coastal cluster, so a daily school run into Diploma provision is out of reach for most families. DP students here are often boarding, commuting weekly or studying at a school with one specialist per subject.

regions.name: Thuwal and the KAUST community
regions.note: A campus community north of Jeddah, academically dense and internationally mobile. Diploma students here are frequently strong and short of one extension topic rather than a whole subject, which makes for a narrow brief and a short arrangement.

schoolClusters.note: The city's IB World Schools between them run the Primary Years, Middle Years and Diploma Programmes, so a student can in principle stay inside one framework from primary to Year 13. Whether a given Higher Level subject runs in a given year still depends on how many students choose it.

schoolClusters.city: Eastern Province and Jeddah Diploma provision
schoolClusters.note: Diploma teaching sits in some campuses and not others, which catches families who assume a school group runs one curriculum everywhere. British-curriculum schools in the same cities run to A Level instead, so a move between them is a change of qualification rather than of address.

modes.title: DP1 weekly foundation slot
modes.description: One subject, one fixed hour a week, through the first year. The work is unglamorous: fluency, note discipline, writing to command terms, and early internal assessment method. It is the cheapest version of Diploma support and the one that prevents the expensive version, because almost everything families pay heavily for in DP2 is a DP1 gap that was left alone.

sections.heading: A weekly slot that has to survive two years
paragraphs: The failure mode of Diploma tutoring is not a bad tutor. It is a good tutor in a slot that quietly stops happening. Two academic years is roughly seventy to eighty weekly sessions across two long summers, mock weeks, school trips, travel and two Ramadan periods falling in different parts of the course. An arrangement that depends on being renegotiated each week does not last that long, and it usually fails in the DP2 autumn term, which is the worst possible moment.

Two things make a slot durable, and neither is about the subject. The first is that it is written in Arabia Standard Time. The Kingdom is UTC+3 and does not change its clocks, so the slot is fixed here by definition; it is the tutor's country that moves. Agree it in the tutor's local time and it drifts twice a year, which over two years is four unannounced shifts. Each one costs at least one lesson and some goodwill.

The second is the tutor's own working week, which parents rarely ask about and which matters more than the time difference. A tutor who teaches in a school on a Monday-to-Friday timetable somewhere else is at work during your Sunday and Monday, and those are the two most valuable evenings in a Saudi Diploma week: teaching lands before the week's work is written. A tutor based in the Gulf, or tutoring full time, has those evenings available. The same question applies to Thursday, which in this market behaves the way a Friday night does elsewhere — a student will attend and absorb very little.

The practical advice is to settle the slot once, before the first lesson, with three questions answered: what time zone the tutor is in, what their own working week looks like, and whether they can commit to the same hour for an academic year rather than a term. A tutor who hesitates on the third question is telling you something useful. Better to know in the DP1 autumn term than to find out when the Internal Assessment deadlines arrive.

sections.heading: DP1: the year that decides the second year
paragraphs: The first Diploma year is quiet in a way that misleads families. Papers are two years away, school assessments are frequent and low-stakes, and a student can get through two terms on competence and goodwill without anybody noticing that the foundations are slow. The gap shows up in DP2, when there is no time to fix it, and that is why most expensive second-year tutoring is really unpaid first-year work with interest.

What DP1 is actually for breaks into four things. Fluency, which in mathematics and the sciences means algebraic manipulation fast enough that the thinking has room to happen. Note discipline, because DP2 revision is only as good as the DP1 notes it draws on, and a student revising from a textbook in the final term has lost the year. Writing to command terms, which is a habit that takes months rather than a technique that takes an afternoon. And internal assessment method, taught before the piece is chosen rather than after a weak topic has been committed to.

The spring term of DP1 is also when the Extended Essay subject is chosen and a supervisor allocated, and when internal assessment work begins in several subjects at once. A student who treats that term as the calm before the storm arrives in the summer with two half-started pieces. A student who uses it properly arrives in DP2 with a research question that works and a method that will produce data.

There is one more DP1 job, and it is uncomfortable. This is the year a subject choice turns out to be wrong. A student who picked Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level on application and cannot keep up by the spring term has a real decision to make with their coordinator, and the window for making it is short and school-specific. An honest read from a subject specialist — recoverable with work, or not recoverable at this level — is worth more at that moment than another term of practice papers.

sections.heading: The break between DP1 and DP2, and what it quietly decides
paragraphs: The long break between the two Diploma years is the most under-used asset a family has. It is the only period in the whole course with time and no deadlines, and most students spend it recovering from a year that did not actually exhaust them. Two or three things done in that break change the whole of the second year, and none of them requires a heavy schedule.

The first is the internal assessment work. A student who returns in the DP2 autumn term with data collected, a method written up and a draft in progress has removed the single biggest source of second-year panic. One who returns with a topic idea is about to meet three internal deadlines, the Extended Essay, the Theory of Knowledge essay and university applications in the same eight weeks. Nothing in DP2 is as cheap to fix in advance as this.

The second is the one subject that went badly. Not all of them — a student who tries to repair three subjects over a summer repairs none and starts the year tired. One subject, two sessions a week, aimed at the specific thing that was weak, is realistic and it holds. The third is reading for the Extended Essay, which is the only point in the course where a student can read widely without something else being due.

Families often ask whether to keep the weekly slot running through the break at all. For most Diploma students the honest answer is to keep the slot and reduce the frequency, because the alternative is losing the hour to somebody else and competing for it again in the autumn, when every family in the Gulf is looking. A paused slot that is formally held and a paused slot that is simply abandoned are different things, and it is worth asking which one is being offered.

sections.heading: The DP2 autumn term, when everything arrives at once
paragraphs: The second Diploma year does not build gradually. Internal assessment deadlines in several subjects land within weeks of each other, the Extended Essay reaches final submission, the Theory of Knowledge essay runs in parallel, mock papers are sat, and university applications are live — all inside one term. Students who were coping in DP1 stop coping here, and the reason is almost never the subject content. It is that four things are due and nobody has decided what order to do them in.

That makes the DP2 autumn term a triage problem, and triage is a teachable skill. The order is set by two rules: what is marked externally or counts toward the Diploma soonest goes first, and what has a hard submission date beats what has a soft one. An internal assessment with a school deadline in three weeks outranks revision for a paper five months away, even though the paper is worth more. A student who revises instead of submitting has chosen the comfortable task.

The second thing a tutor does in this term is protect the evidence base for predicted grades. Mock papers and school assessments sat in this term are the main material from which the school forms its judgement, and that judgement is used in university applications. A student who treats the autumn mock as a practice run has misunderstood what it is for. This is the term where marked written work matters most, and where the weekly hour is best spent on producing it rather than on covering new content.

The third is honesty about what will not be fixed. Not every weak subject can be brought up in one term while three others are being submitted. A good DP2 plan names what is being prioritised and what is being held at its current level until the spring, and says so to the parent in writing. A plan that implies everything can improve at once produces a student who works constantly and moves on nothing.

sections.heading: Predicted grades: what they are, when they are set, what moves them
paragraphs: A predicted grade is the school's professional judgement of what a student is likely to achieve, formed from the evidence it holds — class assessments, mock papers, internal assessment progress, and the teacher's read of the student's trajectory. Universities use it during the application cycle, which is why it carries weight well before any paper is sat. It is not a promise in either direction, and it is not a negotiation.

Two things follow from that, and both are about timing. First, the evidence is produced before the judgement, which means the useful moment to intervene is the DP1 spring and the DP2 autumn, not the week the predictions are issued. A family that hires a tutor after a disappointing prediction is asking for something a tutor cannot deliver: the judgement has already been made from work that has already been marked. Second, the way to influence a prediction is to produce better marked work, in the subject, before the judgement is formed. There is no other route.

Parents sometimes ask whether a tutor can challenge a prediction. No. The grade belongs to the school, the teacher has the evidence, and a tutor who offers to argue the case on a family's behalf is offering something improper and ineffective. What a tutor can legitimately do is tell you, from marked work, where the student currently stands against the demands of the paper, and whether the prediction looks consistent with that. If there is a genuine mismatch, the conversation is between the family and the school, with the marked work in hand.

The related thing worth understanding is grade boundaries, because they explain why a mock mark and a final grade are not the same currency. Boundaries are set after a session, from how candidates actually performed on that paper, so a mark that was a low grade on one paper can sit differently on another. A mock percentage is therefore a position, not a prediction, and treating it as a guaranteed outcome in either direction misreads what it is. No tutor can promise a grade, and anybody offering one is selling marketing rather than teaching.

sections.heading: The final term before the May session
paragraphs: In the last stretch the job changes completely. Content teaching largely stops, not because content stops mattering but because the marginal hour is worth more somewhere else. What is taught instead is examination behaviour: which questions to attempt and in what order, how long to spend on each, how to read a command term correctly under pressure, and how to write what the mark scheme rewards instead of everything the student knows about the topic.

The method is whole papers under timed conditions, marked properly afterwards against the real scheme, with the marking read line by line with the student. Not topic exercises, not question banks, not watching somebody else solve problems. A student who has never sat the full paper to time does not know whether their problem is knowledge or pacing, and those two problems have opposite fixes. Most students discover in the first timed paper that they lose more to timing and question choice than to gaps.

The common mistake in this term is starting new content. A Higher Level extension topic never properly taught cannot be learned to examination standard in the last weeks while four other subjects are also being revised, and attempting it usually costs marks elsewhere. The honest plan triages: secure what is nearly secure, protect the components with the most available marks, and accept a weak topic as weak rather than spending the term on it. That decision is uncomfortable and it is almost always correct.

Two practical notes. School revision timetables and outside sessions should complement each other rather than compete, so a tutor should know what the school is running before setting work. And entries are an administrative matter with real deadlines: a student sitting a resit, a November-session paper, or a Cambridge or Pearson entry alongside the Diploma needs the examinations officer involved months ahead rather than weeks. Cambridge and Pearson both run June and November series for candidates here, and the February and March series is available only to candidates in India, which is a mistake families are told surprisingly often.

sections.heading: The first month with a new DP tutor
paragraphs: A Diploma arrangement should start with a diagnostic rather than a lesson. The tutor's first job is to find out what the student can actually do, which is rarely what their school marks suggest and almost never what the student reports. That means working through real questions and watching the attempts rather than asking what they find hard, because students are poor witnesses to their own errors: the error is nearly always earlier in the working than they think it is.

What comes out of the diagnostic is a short plan with three or four checkable items and a date for reviewing it. Checkable means stated as something a parent can verify at the end of the month without understanding the subject: writes uncertainty correctly in the investigation, draws a correctly labelled diagram without prompting, finishes the paper with time to check, stops losing method marks by working mentally. Not "improve in physics", which cannot be checked and therefore cannot be missed.

Reporting should be short and frequent rather than long and quarterly. A note after each session saying what was covered, what was set and what the tutor is watching takes two minutes to write and tells a parent more than a termly report. At the end of the first month the review looks at school marks and marked written work, with the tutor's annotations next to the school's, which is the single most revealing document a Diploma parent can read.

If it is not working after a month, there are three honest explanations and it is worth naming which. The plan was wrong, the match was wrong, or the student is not doing the work between sessions. Only the second is fixed by changing tutor, and two or three lessons is usually enough to tell. The third is the most common and the least discussed, and no tutor can solve it alone; it needs a conversation at home about what the weekly hour is actually for.

sections.heading: Where the two years go wrong, term by term
paragraphs: Diploma failures are patterned, and the pattern is predictable enough to plan against. In the DP1 autumn term the error is assuming the course is a continuation of IGCSE or MYP: the content looks familiar and the writing demand is not, and students get good marks for answers that would score badly in two years' time. In the DP1 spring term the error is leaving internal assessment topics unchosen while the term feels calm.

In the DP1 summer term and the break, the error is total rest. In the DP2 autumn term it is order: four things due, no decision about sequence, and a student who works every evening and submits late anyway. In the DP2 spring term the two errors are starting new content and revising passively — rereading notes, watching explanations, highlighting — rather than writing answers and marking them against a real scheme.

Across both years, three further failures recur regardless of term. Theory of Knowledge treated as unimportant until the essay is due, which costs points in the matrix that were cheap to keep. CAS left unrecorded, which is a completion problem rather than a grade problem and cannot be fixed in the final weeks. And a weekly slot that slid from a fixed timetabled hour into something negotiated each week, which is how support stops without anyone deciding to stop it.

None of this is an argument that every Diploma student needs a tutor for two years. Plenty do not. It is an argument that the decision should be made against where the student is in the course rather than against how a recent mock paper felt, because the two years have a shape, and buying the wrong kind of help at the wrong point in it is the most common way this money is wasted.

process.title: Say which Diploma year, not which year group
process.description: A brief that can be matched says DP1 or DP2, the subject, the level, the option or extension topic, and what the next deadline is. A DP1 student rebuilding algebra and a DP2 student eight weeks from the papers need different tutors and a different use of the hour, and the word that distinguishes them is the one families most often leave out.

process.title: Match on the subject guide and the year of the course
process.description: We shortlist tutors who have taught that subject guide at that level, and we check marking experience the way a parent would: board, subject, component, number of series. Where the brief is a second-year triage problem, we favour tutors who have taken students through the final term before rather than the strongest content specialist.

process.title: Use the free trial hour as a diagnostic
process.description: One hour, no charge. The tutor works through real questions and watches the attempts rather than asking the student what they find hard, because the error is almost always earlier in the working than the student thinks. You get a plain statement of where the student actually stands afterwards, including if the answer is that little help is needed.

process.title: Fix the slot for the academic year
process.description: The hour is written in Arabia Standard Time and the tutor absorbs any clock change in their own country. We check that their working week leaves your Sunday and Monday evenings free and ask them to commit to the same hour for the year rather than the term, because a Diploma arrangement that is renegotiated weekly does not reach DP2.

process.title: Agree three or four checkable things
process.description: The first month's plan is written so a parent can verify it without knowing the subject. Writes uncertainty correctly. Finishes the paper with time to check. Stops losing method marks to mental arithmetic. A plan nobody can check is a plan nobody can be held to, and it is how a Diploma term disappears without a decision being made.

process.title: Review against marked work, not against mood
process.description: At the end of the first month and each term after it, we look at school assessment marks and at marked written work with the tutor's annotations beside the school's. Confidence is a pleasant side effect and a useless measure. If the plan was met we usually narrow the arrangement rather than widen it.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the year of the course, not just the subject
whyPoints.description: DP1 foundation work and DP2 triage are different jobs. Tutors are listed against both the subject guide and the stage they are strongest at, so a second-year student under four deadlines does not get a tutor whose instinct is to start the syllabus again from the beginning.

whyPoints.title: A slot built to last two years
whyPoints.description: Every slot is pinned to Arabia Standard Time, checked against the tutor's own working week, and agreed for an academic year rather than a term. That is unglamorous and it is the difference between an arrangement that reaches the final term and one that quietly lapses in the DP2 autumn.

whyPoints.title: Honest about what the final term can and cannot do
whyPoints.description: In the last weeks the useful work is technique, triage and timed papers. A tutor who promises to teach an untaught Higher Level extension topic from scratch in that window is selling optimism. We will say which components are worth the remaining hours and which are not.

whyPoints.title: The assessed-work line, stated to the student first
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach method, explain the published criteria and give feedback on the student's own Internal Assessment, Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge drafts. They write no part of them. The student hears that in the first session, and a record of what each session covered is available if the school asks.

whyPoints.title: No grade promises and no invented numbers
whyPoints.description: Grade boundaries are set after a session from how candidates actually performed, so nobody can promise a grade before one is sat. There is no success rate, star rating or tutor count on this page either, because a figure without a sample, a date and a method tells a parent nothing.

whyPoints.title: Independent, online, and clear about both
whyPoints.description: IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform with no affiliation to any board, school or regulator. Diploma lessons for Saudi families are delivered one to one over live video; we do not send a tutor to an address in the Kingdom, and in-home visits are a service we run only in India.

faqs.question: What should the first month with a DP tutor cover for a student halfway through DP1?
faqs.answer: A diagnostic first, then foundations. The tutor works through real questions and watches the attempts, because a mid-DP1 student's problem is usually earlier in the working than they believe: slow algebra, notes that cannot be revised from, or answers written without reference to the command term. The month should end with three or four checkable changes and a short written plan. Content coverage matters less at this point than fluency and writing habits, because those compound over the eighteen months still to run and cannot be installed later in a hurry.

faqs.question: How is a starting point diagnosed for a DP2 student who is already behind?
faqs.answer: With a timed paper rather than a conversation. A second-year student sits a whole past paper under proper conditions, and the tutor marks it against the real scheme and reads it back with them line by line. That single exercise separates three different problems that feel identical to the student: missing content, poor question choice and bad pacing. They have opposite fixes, and a term spent on the wrong one is a term lost. The outcome is a priority order by deadline, not a plan to revisit the whole course.

faqs.question: What should a parent expect to see after four weeks of DP support?
faqs.answer: Three things, none of which is a grade. Marked written work with the tutor's annotations beside the school's, which is the most revealing document a Diploma parent can read. Movement on the specific items in the first month's plan, stated plainly enough to verify. And a clear statement of what has not moved and why. A tutor who reports only that your child is more confident has not reported anything; confidence rises long before technique does, and in DP2 there is not time to wait for the rest.

faqs.question: How often should a DP tutor report, and what belongs in the note?
faqs.answer: After every session, in a few lines: what was covered, what was set, what the tutor is watching, and anything the school should know. Short and frequent beats long and termly, because a Diploma year moves too fast for a report that arrives after the term it describes. At the end of each term something fuller is reasonable — progress against the plan, what is being prioritised next, what is deliberately being held at its current level. Anything longer than a page is usually padding.

faqs.question: What happens if a DP tutor teaches a topic in a different order from the school?
faqs.answer: The tutor follows the school. The student has to sit the school's assessments, meet the school's internal deadlines and be judged on the school's evidence, so an outside tutor who runs their own sequence creates two courses instead of one. The tutor should ask for the scheme of work in the first week and set work against it. Where the school's order genuinely leaves a gap — an extension topic rushed at the end, say — the tutor should name that explicitly to the parent rather than quietly teaching around it.

faqs.question: How do we decide whether to continue DP support after one term?
faqs.answer: Look at the plan, the marked work and the school marks, and then choose between three options rather than two. Continue as is, narrow it, or stop. Narrowing is the most under-used: keep the slot, drop to a session every other week, or move the focus to the next assessment. If nothing moved, name which of the three causes applies — wrong plan, wrong match, or work not done between sessions — because only the middle one is solved by changing tutor and the last one is the most common.

faqs.question: Which evenings work best for a DP student carrying three Higher Levels?
faqs.answer: Sunday and Monday, almost always. Teaching lands before the week's work is written rather than after it has been handed in, and a student still has four school days in which to use what was taught. Wednesday works for marking back written work. Thursday should be avoided where there is any choice: the weekend starts that night and a student will attend politely and absorb very little. For a second subject, Tuesday with a gap after the first session is more productive than stacking both on one evening.

faqs.question: How does a DP slot survive a tutor's clock change in another country?
faqs.answer: By being written in Arabia Standard Time from the start and never in the tutor's local time. The Kingdom is UTC+3 and does not change its clocks, so the hour is fixed here; it is the tutor's offset that moves, twice a year, in any country that uses daylight saving. Over a two-year Diploma that is four shifts. If the slot is pinned in Saudi time, the tutor absorbs each one and the student notices nothing. If it is not, a lesson is lost each time while somebody works out what happened.

faqs.question: What happens to a weekly Diploma slot during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: It moves once, deliberately, and stays moved for the month. School days shorten, household routines change and late-evening study becomes normal rather than exceptional, so the sensible approach is to agree the shifted hour a fortnight in advance and keep it fixed until the month ends. Families who reschedule week by week typically lose two sessions to confusion. Because Ramadan drifts earlier each year against the Gregorian calendar, it falls at a different point of the Diploma for each cohort, which is another reason to plan it rather than assume last year's pattern.

faqs.question: Should a DP1 student keep lessons running through the long summer break?
faqs.answer: Keep the slot, reduce the frequency, and use it for specific work rather than general revision. The break is the only stretch in the Diploma with time and no deadlines, so it is where internal assessment data gets collected, where the one subject that went badly gets repaired, and where Extended Essay reading actually happens. Trying to fix three subjects over a summer repairs none and starts DP2 tired. Ask also whether a paused slot is formally held, because reclaiming a good evening in the autumn is harder than keeping it.

faqs.question: Can a DP2 student take two Higher Level subjects in one evening?
faqs.answer: Yes, with two conditions. Different specialists for each subject, because one tutor covering two Higher Levels is the exact generalist problem the hire was meant to solve. And a break between the sessions, with the combined homework load agreed between both tutors so it does not silently double. It is a term-long measure for a student who is behind in two subjects, not a permanent arrangement, and it should drop back to one slot as soon as the weaker subject holds.

faqs.question: How much notice is needed to move a regular Diploma slot permanently?
faqs.answer: A couple of weeks is usually enough, and it is worth doing properly rather than informally. A tutor holding a weekly hour for two years has built a timetable around it, and a slot vacated at short notice is often filled by somebody else. Where the change is driven by the school — a new club, a shifted bus, a term-time timetable change — say so, because a tutor can sometimes offer an adjacent hour rather than a different day. Single lessons are a separate matter and need far less notice.

faqs.question: Why do strong DP students lose marks on command terms rather than on content?
faqs.answer: Because the command term tells the examiner which answer is being marked, and students read the topic instead. Explain, describe, outline, evaluate, justify and discuss each require a different structure and a different amount of reasoning, and a candidate who writes an excellent description where the paper asked for an evaluation has written the wrong answer well. The fix is mechanical and takes weeks rather than months: underline the command term, state what it requires, then write. It is also the cheapest mark recovery available in the final term.

faqs.question: How do grade boundaries move between sessions, and what does a mock mark actually mean?
faqs.answer: Boundaries are set after each session, from how candidates performed on that particular paper, which is why the same raw mark can sit in different grades across sessions. A mock mark is therefore a position rather than a prediction: it tells you where a student stands against the demands of the paper, not what they will be awarded. It is still the most useful instrument available, because the error pattern inside it is stable even when the boundary is not. Nobody can promise a final grade before a paper is sat.

faqs.question: What share of a Diploma subject grade is internally assessed, and who decides it?
faqs.answer: The share is set in each subject guide and differs by subject and level, so the precise figure for your child's course should come from their teacher or Diploma Programme coordinator rather than from a tutoring page. What is consistent is the mechanism: the work is marked at school against published criteria and then moderated externally, which means the criteria are knowable in advance and the marks are earned over months rather than in one sitting. That makes it the most controllable part of the Diploma and the part most often left late.

faqs.question: What does the examinations officer need from a DP2 family, and when?
faqs.answer: Earlier than families expect. Entries for any qualification sat alongside the Diploma — a Cambridge or Pearson paper, a resit, a November-series entry — close months ahead of the series, and a private candidate has to arrange a centre themselves. Cambridge and Pearson both run June and November series for candidates in the Kingdom, and the February and March series is for candidates in India only, which families are wrongly told often enough that it is worth checking. Your school's examinations officer holds every actual date.

faqs.question: How does a November-session candidate's two years differ from a May one?
faqs.answer: The whole calendar shifts, and almost every piece of generic Diploma advice is written for the other cohort. Internal assessment deadlines, the Extended Essay submission and the mock programme all move with it, which means a November candidate reading a May timeline will plan against the wrong term. The practical effect is that their summer break falls in the middle of the final run rather than before it. A tutor working with a November candidate should be asked directly whether they have taken that cohort through before.

ib-dp-tutor.closingHeading: Start from where your child is in the two years
ib-dp-tutor.closingBody: Tell us the Diploma year, the subject, the level and the next deadline. We will match a tutor to that stage of the course rather than to the subject alone, put them in a free trial hour used as a diagnostic, and come back with a plain statement of where your child stands — including if the honest answer is that not much help is needed. If it goes ahead, the slot is pinned to Arabia Standard Time, checked against the tutor's own working week, and agreed for the academic year rather than the term. Everything is taught one to one over live video.

intro.heading: Five options, one decision, and almost no comparable information
paragraphs: A Saudi family looking for IB examination preparation is rarely choosing between tutors. They are choosing between kinds of help, and the five kinds are not priced, delivered or measured in comparable ways. The school's own revision programme is already paid for through fees. A group revision course sells a fixed number of hours to a room. An in-home tutor hired locally charges for travel inside the price. Self-study costs nothing but the student's attention. One-to-one online teaching charges by the hour and competes with all four.

Nobody in this market publishes that comparison, which is why families end up buying the first option that answers the phone. The useful way to decide is not which is best in general but which fills the specific gap the student has. A candidate who knows the content and loses marks to timing needs something very different from one who never understood the Higher Level option. One of those gaps is solved cheaply by past papers and a clock; the other is not solved by any amount of them.

Cost is worth stating in the open, with sources attached. A tutor-marketplace guide puts general private tuition for senior-school examination subjects in Riyadh at around SAR 200 an hour and primary tuition nearer SAR 50. A tutoring-company listing advertises IB subject tutoring in Riyadh from roughly SAR 180, with Higher Level premium tracks at about SAR 200 to 220. Budget online platforms advertise general tutoring from around SAR 55. Those are other providers' advertised rates, not ours and not a market average. What moves any of those numbers is the same everywhere: subject scarcity first, then marking experience, then level, then whether the tutor travels.

The constraint that quietly eliminates options is the week. Schools in the Kingdom run Sunday to Thursday, with Friday and Saturday as the weekend, and a Diploma candidate in their final year already has mocks, internal assessment deadlines and the Extended Essay inside that week. A group course running four afternoons is competing with homework. An in-home tutor is competing with traffic. Arabia Standard Time is UTC+3 with no clock change, so an overseas tutor's own working day decides whether their hour is even available.

What follows compares the five options directly, then looks at the three that families most often get wrong: what the school already does and the gap it genuinely leaves, when a group course is better value than one to one, and what in-home tuition in a Saudi city actually involves. After that, the subjects a school cannot always staff, and the scheduling arithmetic that decides which plan survives a term. Our own teaching is delivered online, one to one; home visits are a service we offer only in India.

ib-exam-preparation.programmesIntro: Examination preparation means something different at each stage of an IB education, and the earlier stages are where the habits that later papers reward are either built or missed entirely.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: No external examinations at all. What matters here is reading stamina and number fluency, both of which show up a decade later in paper timing.
programmes.countryNote: Families arriving in the Kingdom from examination-heavy systems sometimes read the absence of tests as an absence of rigour. The useful response is to watch reading volume rather than to add testing.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Criterion-referenced assessment across eight subject groups, with the Personal Project in the final year. There are criteria to learn but no external papers to rehearse.
programmes.countryNote: This is where command-term discipline can be built cheaply. A student who learns the difference between describe and explain here does not need to learn it under pressure in the Diploma.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects at Higher or Standard Level with written papers, plus internally assessed components, Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay.
programmes.countryNote: Almost every Saudi IB school sits the written papers in the May session, and this is where all five preparation options are actually competing for the same hours.

ib-exam-preparation.subjectsIntro: Examination preparation is only comparable subject by subject, because the component that decides the grade differs. These are the Diploma subjects Saudi families most often seek outside help with.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof and calculus depth at Higher Level, with an optional investigation paper. Marks are won through shown working rather than final answers.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics with assumed calculator fluency. Interpretation written in words the mark scheme accepts is the usual gap.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Explanation chains and uncertainty handling decide the grade more often than the mathematics does.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Mechanisms, energetics and fluent use of the data booklet. Definitions are marked to the letter.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The widest content load in the sciences, where the real losses come from command terms rather than recall.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Source work and essay structure, with the Higher Level regional option adding a separate paper to prepare.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and earned evaluation. The commentaries remain the student's own work throughout.

subjects.name: English A: Literature
subjects.description: Unseen analysis under time pressure, plus the comparative essay. The oral belongs to the student and the school.

ib-exam-preparation.regionsIntro: Which options are genuinely available depends on where a family lives, and the gap between Riyadh and a smaller city is larger than any difference in teaching quality.

regions.name: Riyadh
regions.note: The only city where all five options realistically exist. Group courses and in-home tutors are both available, and both are priced against heavy traffic.

regions.name: Jeddah
regions.note: A long coastal city where a group course convenient for one end of it is impractical for the other, which pushes families towards one-to-one arrangements.

regions.name: Dhahran and Al Khobar
regions.note: Compound and camp schedules shape the evening, and a well-established international sector means school revision provision is often genuinely good.

regions.name: Al Ahsa
regions.note: About an hour and a half inland from the Eastern Province cluster, far enough that a weekly in-home arrangement collapses on travel alone.

regions.name: Buraidah and the Qassim region
regions.note: Few international entries, so a Diploma candidate here is usually preparing without any local subject specialist to call on.

regions.name: Jazan and Najran
regions.note: The thinnest provision in the Kingdom. Distance is the real constraint, and remote teaching is the only option that behaves the same here as in Riyadh.

schoolClusters.note: Diploma provision sits in a small number of schools, and the Higher Level combination a student wants is not always one their school can timetable in a given year.

schoolClusters.city: Jeddah, Thuwal and the Eastern Province
schoolClusters.note: The Diploma runs at some campuses and not others within the same group, so two families in one city can face very different school provision.

sections.heading: Five ways to prepare for IB examinations, set side by side
paragraphs: The five options are not variations on one product, and comparing them on price alone produces a bad decision. The school's revision programme is included in fees and taught by someone who knows the cohort, but it runs at the pace of a class. A group course sells a syllabus to a room, which is efficient for content coverage and useless for a student whose specific gap nobody in the room shares. Self-study from past papers is close to free and genuinely effective for timing, provided somebody marks the output honestly.

An in-home tutor hired locally has the advantage of presence and the disadvantage of arithmetic. The pool is limited to specialists within a reasonable drive, and in a city an hour across that is a small pool in a narrow subject. Travel is priced into the hour whether it is itemised or not. One-to-one online teaching removes the travel and widens the pool to anyone who can hold a slot in Saudi time, which is why a family in Jazan gets the same access as one in Riyadh.

The practical answer for most families is a combination rather than a winner. School provision plus self-study covers more than parents expect, and the paid hours are then aimed narrowly at whatever those two cannot reach. That is a cheaper plan than any single option bought at full scale, and it is the plan a specialist should propose if the evidence supports it. A provider who recommends their own option for every gap is not comparing anything.
